issues.body:
Currently we have many different ways that we do maintenance on the product catalog.

Many different events can trigger the need for us to do maintenance including: 
- purchases/deliveries
- repricing
- errors discovered
- promos
- market dynamics changes
- time

Once we have determined _what_ to change to describe the desired new state of the world there are multiple possible ways to implement the desired change including:
- new catalog entries, variants, strains, effects, flavors, etc
- new categories, subcategories, product types, etc
- new prices at global, local, or promo level
- new promos that achieve interesting bundle or pricing effects

Connecting those two ends is a part in the middle that needs to be reviewer interactive. We have built several iterations of this middle part over the last few weeks depending upon the particular pair of cause and destination. However they all share the same core purpose. So far the best version of this by far in my opinion has been the most recent set of mass repricing pages and detail sub pages, followed by the delivered / pending purchases.

Generally these need to describe what the current state is for each item, what helios proposes the new state to be, and for particular types of changes price in particular, useful interactive price ladder controls and data summary presentations, along with clicked new tab details pages, giving the reviewer a chance to make changes and approve at each level of organization and hierarchy for efficiency. 

These tend to be organized in a logical and reviewer-friendly fashion that allows for individual and efficient family pricing based on market price pressures and data. 

It also shows proposal changes in other attributes besides price such as catalog image, attributes such as flavor effect and strain information, and product description. For each the details page will have additional alternative options, justification for the proposal, and further click to source descriptions of where things came from. The attributes proposed here are editable and removable. 

Individual change line items, as well as each layer above in the organizational hierarchy can be approved disapproved or mass changed or mass edited. 

Brands (and distributors, as collections of brands) can be annotated as MSO brands, what's going to have policy implications on the nature of proposals for pricing or promos, and this brand attribute should be prominently displayed when present on a brand or SKU from that brand. This attribute should also be toggleable every time a brand chip appears, however toggling it should definitely require confirmation and be logged. 

A task here is to design and implement this middle section such that it can be mostly agnostic to what triggered it and what is consuming its output. Carefully architect and design this system in a modular fashion given the description of the many use cases involved.  Wire The implementation together for the first use cases of "new purchases" and "full catalog repricing review into catalog pricing" and "full catalog review into promos for brands".

Completion of a task linked to an issue should update the issue.  All CLI-tool-handled commits that relate to a github issue should mention the issue at the bottom of the commit message to ensure the issue is updated.  The final commit that closes the issue epic needs to actually UPDATE the issue, or have a github runner that knows how to do so.  Either way, this needs to be automated and the full feedback loop closed.

Finally, we need a repo-agnostic watcher shell script that can cycle through repos fetching the latest tasks horizon, looking for unclaimed / unstarted work, then upon finding one, "claiming" it somehow (perhaps a meta-only task commit or something?) and launching a new tmux window where we pipe "echo $AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS | amp-smart" in the new tmux window, where AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS tells the agent which repo and task number to begin, and to continue until permanently stuck or complete; either way paging dave with the results (<p5 unless it's an emergency).

This script / tooling needs to be available for use for all repos.  Modifications to this idea are fine if they are better design, but something like this needs to be  in place as our development methodology.

...that we will be using in the MSS repo for landing pages on FB.US site, to optimize and hill climb performance, also into this repo to do the same on our google ads (`gads`) themselves.  We can interact with gads programmatically in **EXTREMELY** rate limited fashion (for now) via API, or with almost unlimited capacity via sequenced CSV imports through ads editor (although that requires synchronous user action, so should be batched where possible).

Ensure that the entirety of the philosophy and strategy and approach from that repo is clearly understood both locally by the agent and the agent's oracle before attempting to pull and create an equivalent version i this repo to live in ads/google and handle the hill-climbing of the gads *content*, whereas the mss repo handles hill-climbing of the gads *landing pages*.

For now, communication and data transport is strictly unidirectional; data flows from the gads through helios and this repo and eventually into the MSS repo for analysis for landing pages.  It doesn't flow back up currently.

The first task of the new system will be to ingest via API the current state of the system, and backfill an "assumed prior state" (if one cannot query historical performance and state) of "yesterday, we reset most of our disapproved or limited assets, and now we're seeing the results after a day+ of gads policy processing and applied limitations or disapprovals.  

Have the agents architect the system and involve both oracle and private LLMs to ensure the top quality and performance of the architecture and design.  We really need this system to evolve rapidly onto a high-performance ad and asset set.  It should do so via aggressive speculative testing of the policy engine on intra-gads stuff (what THIS repo controls, not the extra-gads landing page stuff).  We should aggressively create temporary "*-trial-00N" asset groups or ad groups, where we attempt to isolate specific causes of limitation or disapproval and how to hill-climb and anneal (or other method) our way around them to hill-climb so we simultaneously achieve stellar performance (meaning users are being well served by our ads, which both we want AND gads wants, and is Google's thesis for what makes users' lives better) and learn rapidly the policy enforcement landscape for intra-gads assets.

The first major milestone after design is complete will be to have ingested our current gads state and produce an HTML summary of next steps:
 - A repair or replace disapproved or limited assets so we start serving again ASAP
 - B In conjunction with L2, identify candidate experiments to run in miniature, $1-budget groups, to probe the policy engine for smaller pieces in isolation, and create them
 - C Remove entirely any items created in a previous B step that are no longer needed, so they do not clutter UIs and reporting.
The HTML must summarize in a human-reviewer-efficient fashion what is being done, and what the proposed experiments are, and how the prior experiments' results (if available) have been assessed, and what is being done now as a result, etc.
The HTML must be served via the mss-one-offs service for 24 hours, with link to the HTML included in a page to dave at P3.  We should be able to download the "CSVs numbered for sequential import into Ads Editor" as a single ZIP file from a button at the top and bottom of the page

If there are other significant concerns I'm likely to have missed, please update the github issue with questions or comments.

Document the design carefully and post a markdown version in the github issue comments if possible as well, for convenience.

issues.body:
as a reminder, new issues are intended to automatically trigger epic-level task-dag tasks whose initial instructions for the agents are to use all sophistication needed to understand the issue and recursively plan its solution.  That task should be picked up be an agent, who then begins to decompose the epic into tasks.  Each task requiring further breakdown should ALSO generate a new "finish breaking this down" initial task, which will then be picked up by an agent and continued.  These are supposed to be quickly picked up by workers and broken down recursively into a plan, with each step producing either "a thing that needs to be broken down further, and an executable task referencing it to break it down further", or a leaf-level task which, depending on the initial instructions, may then be a stopping point, or if instructed to just implement instead of plan, would be accompanied by an executable task to "implement that [leaf-level] task" which would be immediately picked up and implemented recursively until the epic is closed.

Either way:
1) that should happen automatically at new Issue creation
2) If the epic was closed, the issue should be commented and closed as well.  All commits related to the epic should include a mention of the issue by URL.
3) Reopening an issue should be treated the same as a new comment on an open issue
4) A new comment on an open or closed issue should be treated as a new sub-epic task associated after-the-fact with the original issue epic.  This, like all such issue- or comment- based task-dag creation, should happen on every issue create/update automatically.
5) When a comment's task-dag task is closed, if the comment's issue's epic task is completed, the issue needs to be (re-)closed if open.
6) The Agent-->Issue channel needs to be dramatically hardened and improved.  Agents need to be able to submit task-dag issue-related commits that reliably trigger a github job that migrates data from the meta commit into the issue.  This has been done successfully more than once (various markdown files posted as comments, for instance, in the genesis issue itself!!), but it needs to be done **reliably**, so produce a canonical implementation and pseudo-force agents to use it.
7) Have both Oracle and our private LLM confer to assess the dramatic reliability improvements required for v1, just to be usable.  Implement these immediately don't want for approval of design once there's LLM consensus.  

This task will not be considered complete until comments placed in the Comms Genesis issue (https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/9) are reliably responded to, and the state changes to the issue follow the rules above over time.

In addition to the whole-catalog actions ("handle pending purchases", "reprice items", "promo items", etc), there are various one-off actions we'll want to be able to easily do:
- Find all in-stock items without catalog images and make it trivial to take and upload photos from mobile website
- Find all in-stock items with "bad" barcodes or missing barcodes of a particular type and allow uploading a photo of the barcode, which is then parsed prior to updating the package's barcode.
- Create a new catalog entry (or small number of entries / variants), given an english description of what we need and upload of zero or more product or variant photos.  This will be especially useful for non-cannabis items like 510 batteries, rolling papers, blunt wraps, etc.  The proposal should end up going through the review process just like other catalog modification/curation flows do

...and probably more, but let's prepare to support at least these initial one-off catalog activities in a first-class way in Helios' "product catalog flows" UI section.

# Customer-Sentiment Capture — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#3](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/3).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/customer-sentiment/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo; this child epic scope is **strictly the
> `automation` / Helios slice of that design**.  Every implementation
> commit that lands on `automation` master and satisfies any part of
> this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#3
> ```
>
> so the top-level coordinator's
> `cross-repo-completion-sync.yml` ingests it as a completion ref.

## Scope owned by this repo

- HTTP submission API (`POST /v1/reviews/submit` and
  `POST /v1/reviews/<submission_id>/drawing-entry`).
- DB schema (`review_submissions`, `review_contact_info`,
  `review_drawing_entries`, `review_emails`) + migrations.
- LLM sentiment-and-suitability gate (re-uses Helios's existing
  private-LLM gateway client; no new provider).
- Email pipeline + templates under `helios/email_templates/reviews/`,
  using `reviews@freshlybaked.us` as `From:` (mailbox provisioning
  belongs to `nixos-sbc`).
- Helios admin UI: `/reviews` list, `/reviews/<id>` detail with
  acknowledge / resend-email / re-run-llm / force-add-or-remove-segment
  / mark-fraudulent actions, plus `/reviews/drawing` exportable list.
- Per-site config table fields:
  `review_provider_kind`, `review_provider_url_template`,
  `review_email_dave|support|ops`, `review_drawing_enabled`,
  `review_free_preroll_enabled`, `review_llm_gate_enabled`,
  `sweed_free_preroll_segment_id`, `sweed_drawing_segment_id`.
- Sweed client method additions: `customers.find_by_phone_or_email`,
  `customers.create_minimal`, `segments.add_member`,
  `segments.remove_member`.
- For Midtown pilot:
  - `sweed_free_preroll_segment_id = 8666`
    ([segment URL](https://prime.sweedpos.com/marketing/segments/segment/8666))
    — added only on `strong-with-text` LLM-pass + customer-accepted-
    offer path.
  - `sweed_drawing_segment_id = 8669`
    ([segment URL](https://prime.sweedpos.com/marketing/segments/segment/8669))
    — added on **every** drawing-form submission (both
    `strong-no-text` and `strong-with-text` paths).

## Out of scope

- The public landing page UI — owned by `mostly-static-sites`.
- DNS, TLS, mailbox / DKIM / SPF setup — owned by `nixos-sbc`.
- Sweed-side segment / promo *definitions* — operator-manual,
  prerequisite.

## Phases

- **A1.** DB migration + skeleton submission API (no LLM, no email, no
  Sweed).  Behind feature flag `reviews_capture_v1`.  Helios
  `/reviews` read-only list shipped in same phase so operators can
  observe captured submissions.
- **A2.** LLM gate integration (sentiment + safe-to-post-publicly
  contract from parent design §"Sentiment + suitability LLM gate"),
  including the operator-settled degraded heuristic on `llm_verdict=
  error` (`len(text)>=50 AND word_count(text)>=10` → `degraded_pass=
  true` → treat as `passed` UX; otherwise fall back to
  `strong-no-text`), AND a P3 page to Dave on every error event
  linking to `/reviews/<submission_id>`.  Surface the historical
  per-site PlaceID source already in this repo's history as the
  `review_provider_url_template` substitution source rather than
  building a new PlaceID store.
- **A3.** Email pipeline + templates for negative / lukewarm /
  strong-with-text buckets.
- **A4.** Sweed integration (find / create / segment add) for **both**
  per-site segment ids: `sweed_drawing_segment_id` (Midtown `8669`,
  always added on drawing-form submit) and `sweed_free_preroll_segment_id`
  (Midtown `8666`, added only when the customer accepted the
  paste-text offer).  Both segment-add results land on the
  `review_drawing_entries` row independently; either may end up
  `skipped` (per-site id NULL), `failed`, or `added`.  Bronx ids
  left NULL until that site rolls out.  Helios detail page gains
  the force-add/remove (per-segment) and mark-fraudulent actions.
- **A5.** `/reviews/drawing` exportable list + acknowledge workflow.

Phases A1–A2 are the minimum useful set (we capture + LLM-gate).
A3–A5 are the customer-facing reactive set.

## Cross-repo dependencies

- Needs DNS / mailboxes from `nixos-sbc` child epic before A3 emails
  can actually deliver.  A1/A2 can proceed without.
- Needs the public landing page from `mostly-static-sites` for any
  real customer submissions.  A1/A2 can be exercised manually with
  curl against `/v1/reviews/submit` until then.

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. All five A-phases have landing commits on `automation`'s master
   carrying `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#3`.
2. The Helios `/reviews` and `/reviews/drawing` routes are accessible.
3. Midtown-site submissions flow end-to-end in a smoke test:
   - 5★ + text → LLM pass → drawing entry submitted → membership in
     **both** Sweed segments id `8669` (drawing) and id `8666`
     (free preroll) after the customer accepts the paste-text offer.
   - 5★ no text → drawing entry submitted → membership in segment id
     `8669` only.

# Gemini-Seeded Strategic-Cluster Campaigns — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#5](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/5)
> (the coordinating epic; folded in from the original Batch-1
> Gemini-clusters scope previously tracked in
> [virusdave/top-level#2](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/2)
> conversations).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/gemini-clusters/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo; this child epic scope is **strictly the
> `automation` / Helios slice of that design**, covering both
> Batch-1 (cluster-sweep + helios cluster-proposals page) AND
> Batch-2 (four new clusters + asset-gen worker + per-variant
> leaderboard + Lane-C approval toggle).
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `automation` master and
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#5
> ```
>
> so the top-level coordinator's
> `cross-repo-completion-sync.yml` ingests it as a completion ref.

## Configuration format policy (settled)

**All configuration in this epic is [JSONC](https://github.com/microsoft/node-jsonc-parser)**
(strict-JSON value payload with `//` and `/* */` comments, trailing
commas allowed) per the operator-mandated house style applied to
fuzzy-SKU (#4). The one carved-out exception remains GitHub Actions
workflow files (`.github/workflows/*.yml`), which GitHub Actions
mandates be YAML.

`strategic-clusters` is therefore a JSONC file
(`config/gads/strategic-clusters.jsonc`), not YAML, even though the
parent-epic plan illustrates the schema in YAML form for readability.

## Scope owned by this repo

### A. Strategic-clusters config + cluster-sweep (Batch 1 baseline)

- **`config/gads/strategic-clusters.jsonc`** — the twelve-cluster
  seed (eight Batch-1 + four Batch-2) with per-cluster target-query
  seeds, suggested headlines, frozen `Trust_Anchor_Cash_Debit`
  reference, per-family component-stack references, and parameter
  axes (Batch 2 only).
- **`gads-cluster-sweep` L2 job** under
  `services/gads/cluster_sweep/`:
  - reads `strategic-clusters.jsonc` + most-recent daily L2 repair
    queue;
  - reconciles each cluster against current ad campaigns
    (`extend-existing | merge-into-existing | create-new |
    pause-and-replace`) with rationale + existing-campaign-id
    references;
  - emits per-lane actions (Lane A CSV + Lane C operator checklist;
    Lane B deferred);
  - assembles a ZIP bundle per the parent design §"ZIP bundle
    contents".
- **CLI entry point** `bin/gads-cluster-sweep` invoked by the
  `nixos-sbc` systemd timer (P4 in the parent design) and by the
  helios on-demand button.

### B. Helios `/ads/cluster-proposals` page + bundle endpoint

- New helios route + Tailwind/HTMX page rendering per-cluster cards
  (verdict, per-lane action breakdown, "Download bundle" button).
- Bundle endpoints: `/ads/cluster-proposals/bundle.zip` (top-level)
  and `/ads/cluster-proposals/<cluster-slug>/bundle.zip` (per-cluster).
- "Run on demand" POST that enqueues a `gads-cluster-sweep` job and
  returns a polling URL.
- **Per-variant leaderboard view** (Batch-2 addition) under
  `/ads/cluster-proposals/<cluster-slug>/leaderboard` showing
  per-(family × variant) conversion deltas keyed by UTM. The
  leaderboard reads from the conversion-event store fed by the
  `mostly-static-sites` route handler; it is read-only.
- **Lane-C "Approve for production" toggle** per variant. Toggling a
  variant to "approved" updates an `asset_approvals` table; the
  asset-gen worker and the `mostly-static-sites` route handler both
  consult that table when picking a winning variant. Promotion is a
  one-click operator action (no auto-cron) per parent design
  §"Out of scope".

### C. Asset-gen worker (Batch-2 addition)

- New service under `services/asset-gen/`:
  - **Private-LLM wrapper** — reuses the existing helios private-LLM
    gateway client (no new provider) to produce H1 / subhead / CTA /
    bullet-list / utility-block text variants per family, observing
    the per-family caps in the parent design §"Asset generation
    pipeline (private LLM + Painter)".
  - **Painter wrapper** — invokes the existing Painter client to
    produce `Hero_*` variants per family (≤4 per family, ≤48 total).
    Per-`<parameter-tuple>` overrides are allowed but each consumes
    one of the family's image-variant slots.
  - **Existing-asset-preference manifest resolver** — walks
    `mostly-static-sites/assets/lp/<family>/manifest.json` to find
    pre-existing assets that satisfy a brief; only invokes Painter /
    LLM when no existing asset matches. Emits a per-run
    `painter_calls_saved` counter that surfaces in the cluster-sweep
    bundle README.
  - **Lane-C review gate** — generated text + image variants land
    in `asset_drafts` (NOT directly into `mostly-static-sites`); the
    helios `/ads/cluster-proposals/<cluster>/leaderboard` page
    surfaces them for operator approval. Only approved variants are
    promoted to the manifest committed in `mostly-static-sites`.
  - **Commit producer** — on operator approval, opens a
    `mostly-static-sites` PR / commit that lands the chosen variant
    under `assets/lp/<family>/<variant>.png` (Painter heroes) or
    updates `assets/lp/<family>/copy.jsonc` (LLM text), with
    `chmod g+w` and the `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#5` trailer.

### D. DB additions

- `cluster_sweep_runs` (run_id, started_at, finished_at, snapshot_sha,
  bundle_url, repair_counts JSON, painter_calls_saved INT).
- `cluster_actions` (run_id FK, cluster_slug, lane, verdict, action,
  evidence JSON, status).
- `asset_drafts` (draft_id, family_slug, asset_type, variant_idx,
  prompt_template_id, llm_or_painter_response_id, blob_url,
  generated_at, status ∈ {pending, approved, rejected, promoted}).
- `asset_approvals` (draft_id FK, approved_by, approved_at,
  promoted_commit_sha, promoted_at).
- `conversion_events` (variant_id, utm JSON, event_type ∈
  {add_to_cart, cart_abandon}, occurred_at, site_slug, family_slug).

### E. UTM schema + helios ingestion endpoint

- `POST /v1/conversion-events` consuming a tiny payload from the
  `mostly-static-sites` route handler when a tracked UTM-decorated
  page emits an Add-to-Cart or Cart-Abandonment client event.
- UTM contract: `utm_source=gads`, `utm_medium=cpc`,
  `utm_campaign=<cluster-slug>`, `utm_content=<family>:<variant_id>`.

## Out of scope

- **Lane B (auto-API mutate).** Deferred to a follow-on epic per the
  parent design.
- **Multivariate auto-promotion.** Hill-climbing leaderboard records
  conversion deltas + surfaces them; promotion is a one-click
  operator action.
- **Public landing-page HTML / JS bundle.** Owned by
  `mostly-static-sites`.
- **systemd units + nightly timers + DNS.** Owned by `nixos-sbc`.
- **Sweed integration / customer-sentiment flows.** Out of this
  epic entirely.

## Phases

Phase tags mirror the parent design §"Phase plan" so the
coordinating progress comments (top-level#5 leaf task 2) can group
them cleanly. `automation` owns P0/P1/P3/P5 plus the Batch-2 asset-gen
sub-phases B1..B4 that hang off P3.

- **P0 (`automation`).** `strategic-clusters.jsonc` lands with all
  twelve seeded clusters + per-cluster query seeds + per-family
  component-stack references. Loader stub registers the config;
  no sweep job yet.
- **P1 (`automation`).** `gads-cluster-sweep` L2 job — reconciliation,
  per-lane action emission, ZIP-bundle assembly. CLI invocation
  works end-to-end against a recorded daily L2 repair queue.
- **P3 (`automation`).** Helios `/ads/cluster-proposals` page +
  bundle endpoint + on-demand run button. P3 is a parallel-with-P2
  phase: helios renders even before `mostly-static-sites` has the
  landing-page side wired up (cluster cards just show empty
  per-family asset lists).
- **B1 (`automation`, Batch-2).** Asset-gen worker skeleton +
  private-LLM wrapper + Painter wrapper + manifest resolver. No
  generation yet; just dry-run mode that logs what it *would*
  generate so the per-family caps can be eyeballed before any
  Painter spend.
- **B2 (`automation`, Batch-2).** Live asset generation under per-
  family caps, landing into `asset_drafts`. No promotion yet.
  Includes the `painter_calls_saved` accounting from the
  existing-asset preference path.
- **B3 (`automation`, Batch-2).** Helios per-variant leaderboard +
  Lane-C "Approve for production" toggle + `asset_approvals`
  table. Operator-driven UI; promotion still manual.
- **B4 (`automation`, Batch-2).** Commit-producer path that opens
  the `mostly-static-sites` commit on operator approval, with the
  required trailer.
- **P5 (`automation`).** Wire-up + e2e + runbook
  (`docs/runbooks/gads-cluster-sweep.md`). Includes the operator
  walk-through for the asset-gen approval loop.

P3 / B1 are parallel after P1 lands. B2..B4 are sequential.

## Cross-repo dependencies

- Needs `nixos-sbc` N1 (`gads-cluster-sweep.service` + timer) before
  the scheduled weekly run happens in production. CLI works
  standalone for development.
- Needs `nixos-sbc` N2 (`asset-gen.service` + timer) before nightly
  manifest rebuilds. Live operator-triggered runs work via helios
  in B2.
- B4 needs `mostly-static-sites` M2 (asset-manifest consumer + route
  handler) before promoted variants can actually render.

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. All listed phases (P0/P1/P3/B1/B2/B3/B4/P5) have landing commits
   on `automation` master carrying `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#5`.
2. `gads-cluster-sweep` has produced at least one successful

5. The asset-gen pipeline has produced at least one Painter hero per

6. Operator runbook (`docs/runbooks/gads-cluster-sweep.md`) walks
   through (a) editing `strategic-clusters.jsonc`, (b) triggering an

# Catalog → Review Queue: rebuild around the canonical product-review row

The current `/catalog/review` page (`ReviewPage.tsx`, the "Compact Approval Queue")
is decision-first cards with no structured data, no pricing ladder, and no family
grouping. It does not consume `src/catalogUpdateEngine/` and is operationally
useless for the actual review workflow.

We have **repeatedly** described the canonical "here's what a product being
reviewed" row: structured data clearly called out, a canonical pricing ladder
control PREPOPULATED with LitAlerts pricing data, optional MSO chip on the
brand, expandable detail drill-in, and reviewer-friendly family hierarchy.
The bones of this exist in:

- `src/shared/ui/pricing-ladder/` (canonical ladder, supports a static
  visual mode or an interactive slider via `attachPricingLadderSlider`).
- `src/catalogUpdateEngine/` (PricingLadder, CatalogProposalRow,
  MSOBrandAnnotation, CatalogChangeLineItemPersisted).

…but the `/catalog/review` UI consumes none of it.

## Required outcome

1. A new `docs/helios/canonical-review-row/` design doc describing the
   structural + visual contract of a "product being reviewed" row, so all
   future review surfaces (purchases, repricing, market-data matches,
   promos) can render the same row.
2. `/catalog/review` rebuilt as a family-grouped queue, where "family" =
   `(brand × category × subcategory × size)`. Each family panel:
   - Header with brand chip (MSO toggle), family identity, family-level
     approve/reject.
   - One canonical product-review row per family member, each with:
     - Live state + proposed state side-by-side, structured.
     - Canonical pricing ladder, prepopulated from the latest LitAlerts
       market evidence cached for that catalog entry.
     - Slider attached to the ladder for edit-proposed-price, snap-to-quarter.
     - Inline approve / reject / edit / note.
3. Server: a family-grouped review-queue endpoint that joins
   `proposal_line_items` to their latest cached LitAlerts market-evidence
   row, ordered for reviewer efficiency (drift first, MSO first, larger
   spreads first).
4. The OLD `/catalog/review` (ReviewPage) is REPLACED, not coexisting.

## Out of scope

- Touching the pricing-ladder package itself (use it as-is via its public
  API).
- Promos. Pricing + descriptions only for v1.

# Pricing → New Run: multiselect filters + family-expansion scope + multi-site

The current Pricing → New Run filters (`PricingGeneratePage.tsx`) accept
brand / category / subcategory as **plain text inputs** — operators must
type names exactly. Site inventory scoping is two independent checkboxes
("Bronx" / "Midtown"). There is no scope mode that says "include the
whole family for every brand that has stock at the location".

## Required outcome

1. **Multiselect filters** (brand / category / subcategory) backed by a
   `/api/pricing/facets` endpoint that lists candidate values with row
   counts. The picker must support multi-select and free-text quick
   search.
2. **Site selection** as a first-class control:
   - Multi-select chip control with at least `midtown`, `bronx`. The
     stock / pending-purchase checks resolve against the chosen sites.
3. **New default scope mode** —
   `family_expansion_from_stock_or_pending`:
   - For every catalog entry currently in stock at a selected site OR
     present on a non-cancelled pending purchase, identify its family
     `(brand × category × subcategory × size)`. Include EVERY catalog
     entry in that family in the run, even if itself out of stock.
   - This is the new default; `full_catalog` and `filtered_catalog`
     remain available.
4. **Strict toggle**: when on, the scope collapses back to only the
   in-stock / pending entries themselves — no family expansion.
5. Scope preview + run-create wire through all the new filter shape.

## Implementation notes

- The existing `liveBronxInventory` / `liveMidtownInventory` /
  `midtownEverReceived` booleans get superseded by `sites: string[]` +
  `stockOnly: boolean` + `includePending: boolean`. Migrate the
  scope-preview + queue-run contracts atomically.
- `pricing_scope_preview` and the queue-run job both need to compute
  the family expansion in one SQL pass — do not iterate in JS.

issues.body:
# Catalog → Market Data: persisted FuzzySku records + catalog ↔ LitAlerts match review

We pull market evidence from LitAlerts but we don't persist a structured
"this LitAlerts row, parsed into a FuzzySku, maps to this catalog entry
with this verdict" record. The catalog ↔ LitAlerts mapping is
re-computed inside each pricing run as fuzzy match heuristics —
expensive, opaque, and not human-curatable.

## Required outcome

1. **Persisted, timestamped FuzzySku records** —
   `fuzzy_skus(id, created_at, source_kind, source_listing_id,
   raw_input_json, parser_id, parser_rule_id, parsed_json, brand_norm,
   category_norm, subcategory_norm, size_g_norm, ...)`. Each LitAlerts
   product, after passing through its tenant's parser config (see
   epic E), produces or updates one row here.
2. **Match table** —
   `catalog_market_matches(id, catalog_group_id, catalog_product_id,
   fuzzy_sku_id, verdict, verdict_set_at, verdict_set_by_user_id,
   confidence, ...)`. `verdict` ∈ `{exact, brand_family, no_match}`.
3. **Confidence scoring** — a deterministic scorer that, given a catalog
   entry, finds all candidate `fuzzy_skus` with `verdict ∈ {exact,
   brand_family}` and emits a confidence in [0, 1]. The same scorer
   ranks unverdicted candidates for human triage.
4. **Catalog → Market Data page** — list catalog entries with proposed
   matches; for each candidate, the reviewer marks
   exact / brand_family / no_match. Verdicts are persisted with
   actor + timestamp; future pricing runs trust them as the source of
   truth.
5. Pricing runs read this table instead of re-fuzzying from scratch:
   - `exact` and `brand_family` rows feed the canonical pricing ladder.
   - `no_match` rows are blacklisted; the scorer must not re-propose
     them.

## Non-goals

- The parser-config UX for LitAlerts is epic E, not this one.

The Config module already has a Parsing branch (see
`ConfigParsingPendingPurchasesPage.tsx` and `configParsing.ts`) backed
by the parsekit runtime registry. LitAlerts is listed in the
helios-parser-configs README as a planned sibling use-case but has

## Pivot

LitAlerts already exposes pre-parsed structured product data via:
- `GET /v1/retailers/{retailerId}/products`
- `GET /v1/brands/{brandId}/products?state=NY&includeOOS=true`

Each `LAProduct` carries `brand`, `brandId`, `category`, and `configs[]` (with `amount`, `units`, `normalPrice`, `salePrice`, `currentStock`, `recreational/medical` flags, plus `medicalURL`/`recreationalURL`).

This is essentially a pre-built FuzzySku for 95% of fields. The per-retailer text-parser substrate from #19 is the wrong altitude for this scale — we should consume structured data directly and only fall back to text parsing for the residuals (`strainNorm`, `packCountNorm`, `subcategoryNorm` which is oddly only on `LAInventoryChange`).

## Scope

1. **Schema** — `litalerts_brands`, `litalerts_products` tables keyed by upstream IDs, snapshot-style upserts with `observed_at`.
2. **Ingest worker** — daily `/v1/brands?state=NY` crawl → upsert brands; then for each brand, `/v1/brands/{brandId}/products?state=NY&includeOOS=true` → upsert products. Pull *all* retailers in NY (filter to pricing distance bands post-hoc in the consumer).
3. **One-off HTML sanity check** for catalog-brand ↔ LitAlerts-brand mapping (interactive UI for manual override comes later).
4. **Cutover** Market Data review surface (issue #18) and pricing comp queries to consume the structured table; rip the search-term observation flow once parity is verified.
5. **TF-IDF residual matcher** within `(brandId, category, size)` tuples for picking the right LAProduct when multiple competitors carry multiple strains/SKUs of the same family.
6. **Park** issue #19's per-tenant parsekit parser work with documented notes — substrate stays but per-competitor configs are paused.

## Non-goals (yet)

- MA/NJ states (NY only for now)
- Bespoke per-retailer ecom scrapers (only if/when LitAlerts structured data proves insufficient)

issues.title: Structured LitAlerts ingest — pivot away from per-tenant text parsing

# Helios "Business & Performance Metrics" page tree — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/business-metrics/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo; this child epic scope is **strictly the
> `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` slice of that design**, which is the
> whole thing in v1 — no other peer repo is on the critical path.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation` master that
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>`
> trailer so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post the
> per-phase progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

Everything described in the parent EPIC_PLAN.md, broken out by phase
below. Re-read the parent before starting — the section here is
deliberately a thin index over the parent rather than a re-statement
of the design (the parent is the single source of truth).

### P0 — schema + API contract

- DB migration adding `metric_annotations` per the schema in the
  parent plan (postgres; uses `gen_random_uuid()` and `timestamptz`).
- TypeScript `MetricDef` type + auto-discovering registry under
  `server/src/metrics/**`.
- HTTP endpoints:
  - `GET  /api/metrics`                          → list of `MetricDef` (sans `query`)
  - `GET  /api/metrics/<id>`                     → execute the metric's query
                                                  (query params: `sites`, `from`, `to`, `agg`)
  - `GET    /api/metric-annotations?from=&to=&scope=` → list visible annotations
  - `POST   /api/metric-annotations`              → create (returns full row)
  - `PATCH  /api/metric-annotations/<id>`         → update title/body/tag/scope/t_*
  - `DELETE /api/metric-annotations/<id>`         → soft delete
- Two trivial `MetricDef`s checked in (e.g. `_demo.flat_line` and
  `_demo.random_walk`) so P0 can be exercised end-to-end without
  waiting on real-data SQL.

### P1 — shared chart wrapper + page shell

- React `<MetricChart/>` per the parent design:
  - subscribes to a page-level `TimeAxisContext` (locked by default);
  - 🔒/🔓 toggle to opt the chart out of the shared axis;
  - pan + wheel-zoom that round-trip through the context when locked;
  - "annotate mode" toggle → click (point) or click-drag (range) to
    author a `metric_annotations` row via the P0 API;
  - renders existing annotations in the visible window as 4-px
    vertical ticks at the bottom of the plot, colour-coded by
    `tag`, with hover tooltip;
  - inline edit/delete on the tooltip.
- `/metrics` layout page:
  - left-nav grouped by `metric.group` (auto-built from the registry);
  - global controls bar across the top: **site filter** (multi-select),
    **aggregation** dropdown, **time range / zoom** picker;
  - renders the P0 demo metrics through `<MetricChart/>` end-to-end.

### P2 — Customer acquisition + Margins

Implements these four `MetricDef`s exactly per the parent plan:

- `acquisition.first_vs_returning`
- `margins.effective_gm_pct`
- `margins.gross_margin_dollars`
- `margins.stack_new_vs_returning`

This phase validates the SQL aggregation pattern against real Sweed
order data. Pin the "first-time vs returning" definition to: a
customer is "first-time on order O" iff there is no prior completed
order in our system for the same `customer_id` (Sweed identity). If
Sweed identity isn't stable across the time window, the child-epic
owner documents the fallback in the runbook (P7) and pages the
parent issue with the chosen definition for sign-off **before**
shipping P2.

### P3 — Basket / category / fulfillment / payment

Implements the eight `MetricDef`s in the parent plan's "Basket size",
"Category distribution", and "Fulfillment & payment breakdown"
groups. Includes the category-expand interaction (click a category
in the stack → re-render with the clicked category split into
subcategories).

### P4 — Inventory / slow movers / running low

Implements `inventory.cost_distribution`, `inventory.misalignment`,
`slowmovers.cost_at_risk`, `lowstock.upcoming_outs`. The two
"as-table" panels (slow movers, running low) ship inside the same
`<MetricChart/>` wrapper rendered in table mode — same site filter,
same aggregation (where meaningful), same annotation support — so
that the operator never has to context-switch between table and
chart UX. Expected-margin-loss column for running-low uses the
trailing-21-day daily-margin run-rate for the SKU.

### P5 — Cashier throughput + weather correlation + delivery sub-line

- `cashier.transactions_per_hour` — joins order timestamps against
  the Sweed Shifts RPC's Cashier-role logins; non-manager filter
  applied at the role level.
- `weather.scatter_margin_vs_{high_temp,low_temp,precip}` — adds a
  daily NOAA-pull ingest. Station list lives in a per-site config
  (default mappings: NYC sites → KLGA primary / KJFK fallback;
  child-epic owner picks defaults for other sites and documents them
  in the runbook). If station-selection ergonomics turn out to need
  operator-level edits without a redeploy, the owner files a
  follow-on child epic against `helios-parser-configs` — do **not**
  pre-emptively move it there in v1.
- `delivery.order_count_by_zone` + `delivery.margin_pct`.

### P6 — Customer origin map (static v1)

- OSM-tile base layer (use Helios's existing map tile provider /
  config — do not add a new dependency on a tile vendor for this
  epic).
- Choropleth + heatmap per delivery zip, intensity = order count in
  the selected window. "First-time customers only" toggle. Diff
  overlay vs. a user-selectable prior window ("change since 6 months
  ago"). **No playback.** The playback v2 follow-on is filed as a
  separate issue at the end of this phase but is explicitly not part
  of #7's acceptance criteria.

### P7 — Operator runbook

`docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md` covering:

- "I want a new metric X" — file path, `MetricDef` template,
  picking `defaultAggregation`, registering the metric group, SQL
  idioms (when to use `time_bucket()`, when to fall back to
  DuckDB, how to keep the site filter param SQL-injection-safe).
- Annotation model (point vs range, `scope=global|metric:<id>`,
  soft-delete semantics).
- Sanity checks to run after a Sweed backfill (cross-check totals
  against the existing Helios `/pricing` daily summary).
- Closure-comment template: at P7 land time, post the comment per
  the parent epic's acceptance criteria #6 on `virusdave/top-level#7`.

## Out of scope for v1 (filed as follow-ons at P7 close)

- `cashier.upsell_lift` (statistical-significance per-cashier).
- `promos.{summary,detail}`.
- `customers.origin_playback` (animated timeline scrub of the map).
- Threshold-based alerting on any metric.
- Mobile-optimised layout.

## Validation per phase

Each phase MUST:

1. Land green on `automation`'s existing CI (typecheck, unit, e2e
   if applicable).
2. Be visible on `vps-nixos-3` after the standard
   `systemctl restart helios-{prep,server,worker}` bounce
   (per `AGENTS.md` of `automation`).
3. Carry both `Phase: P<n>` and `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7`
   trailers on the master-landing commit (or the final commit of a
   multi-commit phase).
4. For P2 and beyond: include at least one screenshot link (in the
   commit message or a docs PR) demonstrating the new panel
   rendering against live data on `vps-nixos-3`. Helios is
   operator-only so the screenshot link is for the operator's
   review, not for the public.

## Completion signal for the child

This child epic is done when:

- P0–P7 are landed per the trailer convention above.
- The acceptance criteria 1–6 in the parent epic plan are
  demonstrated on `vps-nixos-3`.
- A closure comment is posted on `virusdave/top-level#7` per the
  P7 runbook section above, including:
  - the live `/metrics` URL on `vps-nixos-3`;
  - the per-phase commit links;
  - a one-line note for each deferred v2 item with the follow-on
    issue number(s) filed against this repo.

# Sweed orders ingest worker — periodic poll + highwater mark

> Sibling / unblocker for [#21](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21)
> (Helios "Business & Performance Metrics" page tree, child of
> [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)).
>
> This epic exists because every `MetricDef` in P2-P6 of #21 currently
> ships as a STUB returning synthetic data — they cannot return real
> numbers until completed Sweed sales live in helios postgres. This
> issue ships the pipeline that makes them real.

## Problem

`/metrics` ships the full v1 IA (left-nav, chart frame, annotation
surface) backed by `_stub` MetricDefs whose `query` functions emit
deterministic random walks. The real-data SQL is intentionally absent
because helios does not yet have a place to query completed Sweed
sales from. Every P2-P6 metric (acquisition, margins, basket size,
category, fulfillment, payment, inventory, slow-movers, low-stock,
cashier throughput, delivery, customer origin) is bottlenecked on
this.

## Approach

Pull completed sales from Sweed's existing
[`store.sale.invoice.list`](../../helios/src/worker/sweed/sales.ts#L218-L261)
RPC on a 5-minute cadence, materialise them into a helios-owned
postgres table, and crash-tolerantly resume via a per-dealer
highwater mark.

```diagram
╭───────────────────────╮   every 5 min   ╭──────────────────────────╮
│ helios worker         │  per-dealer     │ Sweed                    │
│ ingestSweedOrdersJob  │────────────────▶│ store.sale.invoice.list  │
╰───────────┬───────────╯  fromDate=hw    ╰──────────────────────────╯
            │  paginate (pageSize=50)
            ▼
╭───────────────────────╮   upsert by      ╭──────────────────────────╮
│ helios postgres       │   (dealer, inv)  │ sweed_orders             │
│                       │◀─────────────────│ sweed_order_line_items   │
│                       │                  ╰──────────────────────────╯
│                       │   advance        ╭──────────────────────────╮
│                       │◀─────────────────│ sweed_orders_ingest_     │
│                       │   highwater      │ highwater (per dealer)   │
╰───────────────────────╯                  ╰──────────────────────────╯
```

### Highwater mark — crash-safe ingest

A single row per dealer holds the **largest `payTime` we have ever
inserted into `sweed_orders` for that dealer**. The next poll asks
Sweed for invoices with `fromDate = highwater - <overlap>` so we
never miss a row even when the worker crashes between fetching and
committing.

```sql
create table sweed_orders_ingest_highwater (
  dealer_id           bigint primary key,
  highwater_pay_time  timestamptz not null,
  last_polled_at      timestamptz not null default now(),
  last_seen_count     int not null default 0,        -- rows in last poll
  last_inserted_count int not null default 0,        -- rows newly inserted in last poll
  consecutive_empty_polls int not null default 0,    -- backoff signal
  notes               text                            -- operator-readable free-form
);
```

#### Why an overlap, not a strict `> highwater` cursor?

Two reasons:

1. **`payTime` precision is seconds; Sweed can emit multiple invoices
   at the same `payTime`.** A strict `>` cursor misses the second
   invoice in the same second; an overlap + upsert by
   `(dealer_id, invoice_id)` is safe under any RPC ordering and the
   redundant rows are simply no-ops via `on conflict do nothing`.
2. **Clock skew + late-arriving rows.** If a kiosk is offline and the
   ticket lands in Sweed 90 seconds after the operator paid, a
   strict cursor permanently loses it. The overlap window guarantees
   we re-poll the last 5 minutes of `payTime` until we have proof
   the rows are stable.

Suggested overlap: **`max(5 minutes, 1.5 × poll_interval)`** so a
single missed poll cycle doesn't widen the gap beyond the overlap
window. A constant `15 minutes` is the simplest correct first cut.

#### Cold-start backfill

On first run for a dealer (no row in
`sweed_orders_ingest_highwater`), the worker walks the dealer's full
history **day-by-day, working backwards from `now()` toward the
dealer's known store-opening date**, advancing a separate
"backfill cursor" after each day commits so a crash resumes on the
same day rather than restarting from scratch. The routine forward
5-minute poll runs concurrently from `now()`; the two meet in the
middle.

Hard floors (do not poll earlier than this):

| Dealer | Site             | Opened in Sweed | Earliest `payTime` we will request |
|--------|------------------|-----------------|-------------------------------------|
| TBD    | Bronx            | **2025-07-15**  | 2025-07-15 00:00 America/New_York   |
| TBD    | Midtown          | **2026-04-01**  | 2026-04-01 00:00 America/New_York   |

(Dealer ids resolved at first poll from
[`getStoreInfo`](../../helios/src/worker/sweed/sales.ts) /
`/config/sweed` once this lands; the floors are stored alongside
the highwater row as `min_pay_time` so the worker doesn't keep
hammering Sweed for pre-opening dates.)

Backfill order is **newest-day first** (today, yesterday, day before,
…) so the `/metrics` default trailing-90-day window fills in fastest
and the dashboard becomes useful before the multi-month tail
finishes. Each day is one queued job; the operator can pause /
prioritise / rerun individual days from `/config/workers`. Surfaces
backfill progress on the existing `/config/workers` page via the
standard job-queue progress fields so the operator can watch the
catch-up complete.

### Schema

```sql
-- Migration NNN: sweed_orders ingest

create table sweed_orders (
  -- Composite primary key keeps upserts idempotent and is the only
  -- key we need to maintain (no surrogate id).
  dealer_id          bigint not null,
  invoice_id         text not null,
  primary key (dealer_id, invoice_id),

  -- Time fields — both indexed because metrics filter on pay_time
  -- and the dashboard hover-tooltip surfaces ingested_at for
  -- "freshness" badges.
  pay_time           timestamptz not null,
  ingested_at        timestamptz not null default now(),

  -- Customer denormalised onto the order so the
  -- first-vs-returning aggregation can be done without a customer
  -- table. customer_id is null for guests; first_time_for_customer
  -- is computed at ingest as `not exists (select 1 from sweed_orders
  -- where customer_id = $1 and pay_time < $2)` so a single index
  -- query at metric-time gives the answer.
  customer_id        bigint,
  is_guest           boolean not null default false,
  first_time_for_customer boolean,

  -- Cash-side aggregates from the RPC envelope.
  grand_total_dollars  numeric(12, 2) not null,
  subtotal_dollars     numeric(12, 2),
  tax_dollars          numeric(12, 2),
  discount_dollars     numeric(12, 2),

  -- Computed at ingest from sweed_order_line_items so
  -- margins.* metrics don't have to join. Recomputed if a row's
  -- line-items are ever back-edited (Sweed allows post-pay edits
  -- under some configurations).
  cost_dollars         numeric(12, 2),   -- sum(line.wholesale_cost * qty)
  margin_dollars       numeric(12, 2),   -- grand_total - cost
  margin_known         boolean not null default false,  -- true iff every line had a known wholesale cost

  -- Fulfillment + payment denormalised from the RPC envelope. Free
  -- string today because Sweed's taxonomy is operator-editable;
  -- metrics derive their stack labels from `distinct fulfillment_type`
  -- queried at request time.
  fulfillment_type   text,
  payment_method     text,

  -- For the customer-origin map (P6 of #21). Coalesces the
  -- delivery_address.zip field on the invoice envelope; null when
  -- there is no delivery address (kiosk / pickup / in-store).
  delivery_zip       text,

  -- Provenance: keep the raw RPC payload so we can re-derive any
  -- field we forgot to normalise without re-fetching from Sweed.
  raw_json           jsonb not null
);

create index on sweed_orders (pay_time);
create index on sweed_orders (dealer_id, pay_time);
create index on sweed_orders (customer_id, pay_time) where customer_id is not null;
create index on sweed_orders (fulfillment_type);
create index on sweed_orders (payment_method);
create index on sweed_orders (delivery_zip) where delivery_zip is not null;

-- Hypertable if pg_timescale is available — drop into a plain table
-- if not (the metric SQL falls back to date_trunc()).
-- select create_hypertable('sweed_orders', 'pay_time', if_not_exists => true);

create table sweed_order_line_items (
  dealer_id          bigint not null,
  invoice_id         text not null,
  line_seq           int not null,           -- position within the invoice
  primary key (dealer_id, invoice_id, line_seq),
  foreign key (dealer_id, invoice_id) references sweed_orders(dealer_id, invoice_id) on delete cascade,

  sku_id             text,
  sku_name           text,
  category_id        text,                   -- Sweed top-level category id
  category_name      text,
  subcategory_id     text,
  subcategory_name   text,
  brand_name         text,
  qty                numeric(12, 3) not null,
  unit_price_dollars numeric(12, 2) not null,
  line_total_dollars numeric(12, 2) not null,
  unit_cost_dollars  numeric(12, 4),         -- nullable: unknown-cost SKUs exist
  line_cost_dollars  numeric(12, 4),
  cost_known         boolean not null default false
);

create index on sweed_order_line_items (sku_id);
create index on sweed_order_line_items (category_id);
create index on sweed_order_line_items (brand_name);
```

### Worker

```
helios/src/worker/jobs/ingestSweedOrdersJob.ts
```

- Enqueued every 5 minutes by the existing scheduler (see
  [`configWorkersStockRefreshJob`](../../helios/src/worker/jobs/configWorkersStockRefreshJob.ts)
  for the pattern — same job-queue, same per-dealer fan-out, same
  `withSweedSession` wrapper).
- One job per dealer per tick (so a single sick dealer can't stall
  the others; the existing job_queue.priority gives the operator a
  knob to expedite manual catch-up enqueues).
- Inside the job:
  1. `select highwater_pay_time from sweed_orders_ingest_highwater where dealer_id = $1 for update skip locked`
     — `for update skip locked` so two workers racing on the same
     dealer simply no-op the loser.
  2. If no row exists, insert sentinel `now() - 30 days` AND queue a
     backfill job (see "cold-start backfill" above).
  3. Call `listSaleInvoices({ dealerId, fromDate: highwater - 15min, toDate: now() })`
     wrapped in `withSweedSession` (Sweed token pool — see
     [`docs/sweed/getting-a-token-for-one-offs.md`](../../docs/sweed/getting-a-token-for-one-offs.md)).
  4. For each invoice:
     - `insert into sweed_orders (...) on conflict (dealer_id, invoice_id) do nothing`.
     - On real insert, fetch line items if the list response doesn't
       carry them (TBD — confirm against staging; if list omits
       line items, add a follow-up `store.sale.invoice.get` per row
       or use a bulk `store.sale.invoice.list.detailed` variant).
     - Compute `first_time_for_customer` and the cost/margin
       aggregates inside the same transaction.
  5. Advance the highwater to `max(pay_time)` over the inserted
     batch (NOT `now()` — late-arriving rows would be lost).
  6. Bump `last_polled_at` + `last_seen_count` + `last_inserted_count`
     + reset `consecutive_empty_polls` (or increment it if no new
     rows landed).

### Operator-visible surfaces

- **`/config/workers` page**: new row "Sweed orders ingest", with
  per-dealer highwater age, last poll outcome, and a "force backfill
  from <date>" button (re-enqueues the backfill job).
- **Pending-migrations banner**: sentinel entries for the new
  schema migration so an unmigrated deploy is flagged before any
  metric query trips on it.
- **Audit log entry** on every backfill-window override (the
  routine 5-min polls don't audit — they'd flood — but any manual
  re-enqueue does).

### Wire-up to #21

Once this lands:

1. Replace each P2-P6 stub `query` function in
   [`helios/src/server/metrics/_stub/`](../../helios/src/server/metrics/_stub/)
   with the real SQL against `sweed_orders` + `sweed_order_line_items`.
   The MetricDef metadata (id, group, title, series, defaultAggregation)
   stays untouched.
2. Drop the `STUB: synthetic data — real-data SQL pending` prefix
   from each metric's description (the stub-prefix gate in
   `stubMetric.test.ts` becomes a per-metric assertion only for
   metrics still labelled as stubs).
3. File the [P7 runbook](../../docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md)'s
   closure comment on `virusdave/top-level#7`.

## Non-goals for v1 of this epic

- **No mirroring writes back to Sweed.** This ingest is read-only.
- **No real-time CDC.** 5-minute poll cadence is plenty for an
  operator dashboard; sub-minute latency is a v2 conversation.
- **No de-duplication across dealer-merges.** If Sweed merges two
  dealer ids, helios keeps both rows; operator handles per-incident.
- **No replay-on-edit.** Sweed allows post-pay invoice edits under
  some configurations; v1 simply ignores edits (the first poll that
  saw the invoice wins). The "replay edits" follow-on is filed
  separately at this issue's close if operator-observed drift is
  material.

## Phases

- **R0 — schema + highwater table + migration sentinel.** No worker
  yet; just the place to put the data.
- **R1 — read-only worker behind a feature flag.** Polls every 5
  min, inserts rows, advances highwater. Disabled by default in
  prod until R2.
- **R2 — `/config/workers` operator surface + alarm-on-stale
  highwater.** Enable the worker by default.
- **R3 — replace P2 stubs in [`helios/src/server/metrics/_stub/p2_*`](../../helios/src/server/metrics/_stub/)
  with real SQL.** Repeat for R4 = P3, R5 = P4, R6 = P5, R7 = P6.

Each Rn carries the trailers:

```
Phase: R<n>
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7
```

## Acceptance criteria

This epic is done when:

1. The 5-minute poll has been running for ≥ 24h on `vps-nixos-3`
   without operator intervention, with `consecutive_empty_polls = 0`
   on at least one dealer.
2. `select count(*) from sweed_orders` matches the daily totals on
   the existing `/pricing` daily summary to within rounding for at
   least one trailing 7-day window.
3. Every P2-P6 metric on `/metrics` no longer carries the
   `STUB:` description prefix.
4. The closure comment on `virusdave/top-level#7` per the P7
   runbook is posted.

# Per-product wholesale-cost cache — unblocks margin / COGS metrics on `/metrics`

> Follow-on under [#22](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/22)'s
> umbrella; final blocker for the COGS-dependent stubs in
> [#21](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21).

## Problem

`store.sale.invoice.list` returns `wholesaleCost: 0` on every line item
(verified across 1,252 items observed live on 2026-05-26), so
`sweed_orders.cost_dollars` / `margin_dollars` are never populated by
the ingest worker. The COGS-dependent stubs on `/metrics` therefore
cannot be flipped from stub to real:

- `margins.effective_gm_pct`
- `margins.gross_margin_dollars`
- `margins.stack_new_vs_returning`
- `category.margin_dollars_stack`
- `fulfillment.margin_dollars`
- `fulfillment.effective_gm_pct`
- `delivery.margin_pct` (also depends on #25 delivery-zip)

## Approach — option (b) from #21's status comment

Stand up a **per-product wholesale-cost cache** keyed by
`inventoryItemId` (NOT per-invoice `store.sale.invoice.get`, which
multiplies Sweed RPC traffic by basket size and would dominate the
ingest budget).

```diagram
╭───────────────────────╮   daily 03:00 ET  ╭──────────────────────────╮
│ helios worker         │  per-dealer       │ Sweed                    │
│ refreshProductCost-   │──────────────────▶│ store.product.list       │
│ CacheJob              │                   ╰──────────────────────────╯
╰───────────┬───────────╯
            │  upsert by (dealer_id, inventory_item_id)
            ▼
╭─────────────────────────────╮
│ helios postgres             │
│ sweed_product_cost_cache    │
╰─────────────┬───────────────╯
              │  read at metric query time
              ▼
╭─────────────────────────────╮
│ /metrics SQL — join         │
│ sweed_order_line_items      │
│   on inventory_item_id      │
│ → cost_dollars, margin_*    │
╰─────────────────────────────╯
```

### Schema

```sql
create table sweed_product_cost_cache (
  dealer_id           bigint not null,
  inventory_item_id   text   not null,
  wholesale_cost_dollars numeric(12, 4) not null,
  refreshed_at        timestamptz not null default now(),
  product_name        text,   -- denormalised for ops-friendly debug
  primary key (dealer_id, inventory_item_id)
);
```

### Worker

`helios/src/worker/jobs/refreshProductCostCacheJob.ts` — daily, per
dealer, full-list refresh (~one Sweed RPC paginated). Operator-visible
on `/config/workers` with last-refresh age + a manual rerun button.

### Wire-up

1. At `sweed_orders` ingest time (job from #22), look up each
   line item's `inventory_item_id` against this cache and populate
   `sweed_order_line_items.unit_cost_dollars` + `cost_known = true`
   when a row exists. Leave `cost_known = false` when missing (no
   silent-zero fallback).
2. Recompute `sweed_orders.cost_dollars` / `margin_dollars` /
   `margin_known` at the same time.
3. Backfill: after the first cost-cache refresh succeeds for a
   dealer, enqueue a one-off `recomputeSweedOrderCostsJob` that walks
   the existing `sweed_orders` history for that dealer and rewrites
   the cost / margin columns.
4. Replace the 6 stub `query` functions for the affected metrics
   with real SQL against `sweed_orders` / `sweed_order_line_items`.
   Filter to `margin_known = true` when computing GM% so half-known
   baskets don't pollute the chart.

## Non-goals

- **No per-invoice cost fetch.** That's option (a) and is rejected
  on cost grounds (see #21 status comment 2026-05-26).
- **No real-time cache refresh** — daily is enough for an operator
  dashboard; v2 if needed.
- **No historical cost replay** — when an operator edits a product
  cost in Sweed, all *prior* `sweed_orders` rows keep their
  as-of-ingest cost (otherwise yesterday's GM% silently changes
  whenever inventory bookkeeping moves).

## Acceptance criteria

- `sweed_product_cost_cache` has ≥ 1 row per active dealer.
- ≥ 90% of `sweed_order_line_items` rows in the trailing 30 days
  have `cost_known = true`.
- All 6 listed margin/COGS metrics on `/metrics` no longer carry
  the `STUB:` description prefix.
- `select sum(margin_dollars) from sweed_orders where pay_time >= now() - '7 day'`
  matches the equivalent total from a Sweed-side report to within
  1%.
issues.creator: virusdave

# Sweed per-package snapshot ingest — unblocks inventory.* + COGS/margin metrics on `/metrics`

> Follow-on under [#22](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/22)'s
> umbrella; supersedes the originally-separate
> [#23](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/23) (per-product
> cost cache) because per the operator clarification (2026-05-26),
> **wholesale cost is a per-PACKAGE (inventoryItemId) attribute, not
> per-SKU** — different packages for the same SKU can have different
> costs. One ingest pipeline therefore covers both "current on-hand
> stock per package" and "historical cost per package".

## Problem

Two groups of `/metrics` stubs share the same blocker — helios has no
per-package record of cost, on-hand qty, or lab data:

**COGS / margin** (currently zero-cost):
- `margins.effective_gm_pct`
- `margins.gross_margin_dollars`
- `margins.stack_new_vs_returning`
- `category.margin_dollars_stack`
- `fulfillment.margin_dollars`
- `fulfillment.effective_gm_pct`
- `delivery.margin_pct` (also depends on [#25](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/25))

**Inventory** (currently stubs):
- `inventory.cost_distribution`
- `inventory.misalignment`
- `slowmovers.cost_at_risk`
- `lowstock.upcoming_outs`

## Approach — operator-directed RPC

Use Sweed's **`store.inventory.item.list.grouped`** with `isOnStock: false`
so the response includes packages that have already sold-through (we
need historical cost for `sweed_order_line_items` joins, not just
on-hand). Page through (`pageSize: 50` per the operator's example) per
dealer.

> The existing
> [`configWorkersStockRefreshJob`](../../helios/src/worker/jobs/configWorkersStockRefreshJob.ts)
> already pulls this exact RPC for METRC-tag enumeration — that
> worker is the right place to fork the snapshot path from, NOT a
> greenfield `store.product.list`-based worker. Extend the existing
> `StockInventoryItemSchema` to also pull cost / lab / expiration
> fields, and persist them to a new versioned snapshot table.

Per-package endpoints `store.inventory.item.get` (with
`inventoryItemId`) and `store.product.list` are available as
single-row fallbacks for the `enrichOnePackage` retry path.

### Cadence

**Every 5 minutes, 08:00–02:00 ET** (per operator). Quiet 02:00–08:00
ET because no orders are being rung up — saves Sweed RPC budget for
night-time backfill jobs (#22).

### Versioning — per-package history table

Every poll **inserts** a new row whenever the observed package shape
changes (cost / qty / lab / expiration / location), so we have a
full audit trail. Identical-to-previous polls do NOT insert (saves
storage; the existing-row `observed_at_max` is just bumped).

```sql
create table sweed_package_snapshots (
  dealer_id          bigint not null,
  inventory_item_id  text not null,
  observed_at_min    timestamptz not null,        -- when this row's shape first observed
  observed_at_max    timestamptz not null,        -- bumped every poll where shape unchanged
  primary key (dealer_id, inventory_item_id, observed_at_min),

  product_id         bigint,                      -- Sweed product (SKU) id
  product_name       text,
  category_id        text,
  subcategory_id     text,
  brand_name         text,

  -- Quantity
  current_qty        numeric(12, 3),
  available_qty      numeric(12, 3),              -- nets out holds
  hold_qty           numeric(12, 3),

  -- Cost — operator-confirmed this is per-PACKAGE
  wholesale_cost_dollars numeric(12, 4),

  -- Lab / package metadata
  metrc_tag          text,                        -- externalTrackCode
  lab_result_thc_pct numeric(6, 3),
  lab_result_cbd_pct numeric(6, 3),
  expiration_date    date,
  received_at        timestamptz,                 -- when this package landed in the store
  stock_location     text,

  raw_json           jsonb not null
);

create index on sweed_package_snapshots (dealer_id, observed_at_max desc);
create index on sweed_package_snapshots (inventory_item_id);
create index on sweed_package_snapshots (product_id);

-- "Current" view — latest snapshot per package per dealer
create view sweed_package_current as
select distinct on (dealer_id, inventory_item_id) *
from sweed_package_snapshots
order by dealer_id, inventory_item_id, observed_at_max desc;

-- "As-of" helper — cost at a given timestamp, used by COGS joins
create function sweed_package_cost_as_of(p_dealer bigint, p_item text, p_ts timestamptz)
returns numeric language sql stable as $$
  select wholesale_cost_dollars
  from sweed_package_snapshots
  where dealer_id = p_dealer
    and inventory_item_id = p_item
    and observed_at_min <= p_ts
  order by observed_at_min desc
  limit 1
$$;
```

### Wire-up to #22 line items

`sweed_orders` is currently header-only. To compute COGS we need a
sibling `sweed_order_line_items` table populated from
`raw_json.items[]` on ingest, with `inventory_item_id` as the join
key into `sweed_package_snapshots`. Add migration + an
`extractLineItemsJob` that backfills from existing `raw_json` once,
then ingest writes them inline going forward.

```sql
create table sweed_order_line_items (
  dealer_id          bigint not null,
  invoice_id         text not null,
  line_seq           int not null,
  primary key (dealer_id, invoice_id, line_seq),
  foreign key (dealer_id, invoice_id) references sweed_orders(dealer_id, invoice_id) on delete cascade,

  inventory_item_id  text,        -- package id (joins to sweed_package_snapshots)
  product_id         bigint,
  product_name       text,
  category_name      text,
  subcategory_name   text,
  qty                numeric(12, 3) not null,
  unit_price_dollars numeric(12, 2) not null,
  subtotal_dollars   numeric(12, 2) not null
);

create index on sweed_order_line_items (inventory_item_id);
create index on sweed_order_line_items (product_id);
```

### COGS metric SQL pattern

```sql
select
  time_bucket($agg, so.pay_time) as bucket,
  sum(li.subtotal_dollars) as revenue,
  sum(li.qty * sweed_package_cost_as_of(so.dealer_id, li.inventory_item_id, so.pay_time)) as cogs
from sweed_orders so
join sweed_order_line_items li
  on (so.dealer_id, so.invoice_id) = (li.dealer_id, li.invoice_id)
where so.pay_time between $from and $to
group by 1;
```

`as_of` semantics ensure historical orders use the package cost as it
was on the order date, not whatever it is today — important when a
restock changes the wholesale cost.

## Non-goals

- **No write-back** to Sweed (helios never edits package data).
- **No real-time CDC.** 5-min poll, plus 6-hour quiet window
  overnight, is plenty for an operator dashboard.
- **No replay-on-edit of `sweed_orders`.** Snapshot rows are append-
  only; if a Sweed product moves category later, prior snapshots
  keep the old category (audit-honest).

## Acceptance criteria

- `sweed_package_snapshots` has ≥ 1 row per active package per
  dealer, polled every 5 min during 08:00–02:00 ET.
- `sweed_order_line_items` populated for every `sweed_orders` row
  (backfill complete).
- ≥ 90% of trailing-30-day line items have a non-null cost via
  `sweed_package_cost_as_of`.
- All 6 listed margin/COGS metrics + all 4 inventory metrics on
  `/metrics` no longer carry the `STUB:` description prefix.

# Sweed per-invoice detail fetch — unblocks delivery-zip metrics + customer origin map

> Follow-on under [#22](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/22)'s
> umbrella; remaining blocker for the delivery-zip-dependent stubs in
> [#21](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21).

## Problem

`store.sale.invoice.list` (the RPC the #22 ingest worker uses) does
**not** return a delivery address on the invoice envelope, so
`sweed_orders.delivery_zip` is always null. Every delivery-routed
order therefore lands in the `other` bucket on the customer-origin
map and on the delivery-zone count chart, making both useless.

Affected stubs / shimmed-real metrics on `/metrics`:

- `customers.origin_map` (currently real-shim that buckets
  everything into `other`)
- `delivery.order_count_by_zone`
- `delivery.margin_pct` (also depends on #23 COGS cache)

## Approach

Augment the #22 ingest worker with a **deferred per-invoice
`store.sale.invoice.get` enrichment pass**, scoped to delivery-typed
orders only (`fulfillment_type LIKE 'delivery%'`). That keeps RPC
volume to ~30-40% of total invoices instead of 100%.

```diagram
╭───────────────────────╮
│ ingestSweedOrdersJob  │   inserts envelope-only rows (no zip yet)
│  (from #22)           │
╰───────────┬───────────╯
            │  for each new row with fulfillment_type ~ 'delivery%'
            ▼
╭───────────────────────╮   ╭──────────────────────────╮
│ enrichDeliveryZipJob  │──▶│ store.sale.invoice.get   │
│  (this issue)         │   ╰──────────────────────────╯
╰───────────┬───────────╯
            │  update sweed_orders set delivery_zip = ...
            ▼
╭───────────────────────╮
│ /metrics SQL: filter  │
│  + group by zip       │
╰───────────────────────╯
```

### Worker

`helios/src/worker/jobs/enrichSweedOrderDeliveryZipJob.ts`:

1. Selects up to N orders matching
   `fulfillment_type ~ '^delivery' and delivery_zip is null and
   ingested_at < now() - '60 seconds'` (the 60s grace lets the routine
   ingest finish before we double-pull).
2. Calls `store.sale.invoice.get(invoiceId)` per row, wrapped in
   `withSweedSession` per the Sweed token pool convention.
3. `update sweed_orders set delivery_zip = coalesce(get-response.deliveryAddress.zip, '')`
   — empty-string sentinel for "we checked and there was no zip" so
   we don't keep re-pulling.
4. Batch-rate-limited (start at 60 RPC/min/dealer) and
   crash-resumable (the where-clause re-picks any row we didn't
   finish on the next tick).

### Backfill

Same one-shot pattern as #23: after this lands, enqueue a one-time
`backfillDeliveryZipJob` that walks the existing delivery-typed
`sweed_orders` rows oldest-first; surfaced on `/config/workers` so
the operator can throttle / pause.

### Privacy

`delivery_zip` is a 5-digit US ZIP, not a street address — safe to
keep indefinitely. We deliberately do NOT pull or persist the rest
of `deliveryAddress` (line1, line2, name). If a future map view
needs higher resolution, file a separate issue with operator + Dave
sign-off.

## Non-goals

- **No backfill of non-delivery orders.** Kiosk / pickup / in-store
  invoices stay envelope-only.
- **No per-invoice cost / line-item refresh.** Use #23's per-product
  cost cache for COGS; don't conflate.
- **No real-time enrichment.** The 60s grace + batched poll is fine;
  the map view is not real-time.

## Acceptance criteria

- ≥ 95% of trailing-30-day delivery orders on `vps-nixos-3` have a
  non-null `delivery_zip`.
- `delivery.order_count_by_zone` and `customers.origin_map` render
  with the actual delivery zip distribution, not the `other`
  catch-all bucket.
- No `STUB:` prefix remains on the affected metric descriptions.

# Daily weather ingest for sites 10019 / 10458 — unblocks `weather.scatter_*` metrics

> Follow-on under [#22](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/22)'s
> umbrella; remaining blocker for the weather-correlation stubs in
> [#21](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21) (P5).

## Problem

`weather.scatter_*` ships as stubs because helios has no weather data
source. Per operator direction (2026-05-26), use whichever **free
historical daily source** is reliable, scoped to the two operating
sites: **ZIP 10019** (Midtown Manhattan) and **ZIP 10458** (Bronx /
Fordham).

Affected stubs:

- `weather.scatter_margin_vs_high_temp`
- `weather.scatter_margin_vs_low_temp`
- `weather.scatter_margin_vs_precip`

## Source — Open-Meteo Historical (recommended over NOAA CDO)

[Open-Meteo Historical Weather API](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-weather-api):

- **No API key, no rate limits for non-commercial / low-volume use**
  (free tier; their public good is free up to 10k calls/day per IP).
- Single HTTPS GET per (site, day-range), JSON response, ECMWF /
  ERA5 reanalysis as the underlying dataset.
- `https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=40.7647&longitude=-73.9842&start_date=2024-01-01&end_date=2026-05-26&daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum&timezone=America%2FNew_York&temperature_unit=fahrenheit&precipitation_unit=inch`
  returns daily highs, lows, and precip for Midtown.

| Site label | ZIP   | Latitude  | Longitude  | Sweed dealer |
|------------|-------|-----------|------------|--------------|
| Midtown    | 10019 | 40.7647   | -73.9842   | 210705       |
| Bronx      | 10458 | 40.8623   | -73.8870   | 210249       |

Fallback path: if Open-Meteo is down or returns no data for a day,
re-fetch from NOAA NCEI CDO v2 (`station=GHCND:USW00014732` for
LGA, `GHCND:USW00094789` for JFK) on the next cadence. NOAA CDO
needs a free token cached at `/home/amp-local/.secret/noaa/token` —
defer setting that up until Open-Meteo actually fails in prod.

## Schema

```sql
create table weather_daily (
  site_zip       text not null,          -- '10019' or '10458'
  date           date not null,          -- ET calendar date
  high_temp_f    numeric(5, 1),
  low_temp_f     numeric(5, 1),
  precip_in      numeric(6, 3),
  source         text not null default 'open-meteo',
  ingested_at    timestamptz not null default now(),
  raw_json       jsonb not null,
  primary key (site_zip, date)
);

create index on weather_daily (date);
```

No separate `weather_stations` / `site_weather_stations` config —
two zips, one worker, no operator-edit surface needed for v1.

## Worker

`helios/src/worker/jobs/ingestWeatherDailyJob.ts`:

- Daily at 06:00 ET (one job per zip), idempotent by
  `(site_zip, date)`.
- Pulls trailing 7 days each tick (cheap; lets us absorb late
  corrections from Open-Meteo's reanalysis pipeline without a
  bespoke backfill job).
- Cold-start backfill on first run: pull start_date = the earlier
  of `(min(pay_time)::date, '2024-01-01')` from `sweed_orders`
  → end_date = today. One-shot, one Open-Meteo call per zip.
- Surfaced on `/config/workers` like other helios scheduled jobs.

## Wire-up

Replace the 3 stub `query` functions in
[`helios/src/server/metrics/_stub/p5_cashier_weather_delivery.ts`](../../helios/src/server/metrics/_stub/p5_cashier_weather_delivery.ts)
with real SQL: per (site_zip, day), daily margin from `sweed_orders`
(using dealer→zip lookup) joined to `weather_daily` on date. Each
scatter point = one (site, day) pair. Bucket selector lets the
operator collapse to weekly / monthly averages.

Dealer ↔ zip mapping lives as a small helios constant for v1:

```ts
export const SITE_ZIP_BY_DEALER: Record<number, string> = {
  210705: '10019',  // Midtown
  210249: '10458',  // Bronx
}
```

## Non-goals

- **No hourly weather.** Daily summary only.
- **No forecasts.** Past observations only.
- **No multi-station blending.** One zip → one ERA5 cell.
- **No per-operator station config UI** — two sites, hard-coded
  mapping, fine for v1. If we open a third site this becomes an
  operator surface.

## Acceptance criteria

- `weather_daily` has ≥ 1 row per zip per day for the trailing 90
  days on `vps-nixos-3`.
- The 3 listed weather metrics on `/metrics` no longer carry the
  `STUB:` description prefix and render a real scatter.
issues.creator: virusdave
issues.title: Daily weather ingest (Open-Meteo) for sites 10019 / 10458 — unblocks weather.scatter_*
