# Sweed Shifts ingest — unblocks `cashier.transactions_per_hour`

> Follow-on under [#22](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/22)'s
> umbrella; remaining blocker for the cashier-throughput stub in
> [#21](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21) (P5).

## Problem

`cashier.transactions_per_hour` ships as a stub because helios has no
record of when each cashier was clocked-in. Sweed exposes shift data
through its `store.shift.*` family of RPCs but helios does not yet
ingest it. Without a clocked-in-hours denominator there is no way to
compute per-hour throughput per cashier — only per-day totals, which
hide schedule efficiency.

Affected stub:

- `cashier.transactions_per_hour`

## Approach

Periodic per-dealer pull of `store.shift.list` (or whichever verb
returns historical closed shifts — confirm at implementation time
against staging; the live RPC family is poorly documented). Store
one row per `(dealer, employee, shift_open, shift_close, role)` and
join against `sweed_orders` at metric-query time.

```diagram
╭───────────────────────╮   every 15 min     ╭──────────────────────────╮
│ helios worker         │  per-dealer        │ Sweed                    │
│ ingestSweedShiftsJob  │───────────────────▶│ store.shift.list         │
╰───────────┬───────────╯                    ╰──────────────────────────╯
            │  upsert by (dealer_id, shift_id)
            ▼
╭───────────────────────╮     join          ╭──────────────────────────╮
│ helios postgres       │   on user_id +    │ /metrics SQL             │
│ sweed_shifts          │   pay_time within │ tx_count / cashier_hours │
│                       │   shift window    │ per hour-of-day          │
╰───────────────────────╯                   ╰──────────────────────────╯
```

### Schema

```sql
create table sweed_shifts (
  dealer_id      bigint not null,
  shift_id       text not null,
  primary key (dealer_id, shift_id),

  employee_id    bigint not null,
  employee_name  text,
  role           text not null,            -- 'Cashier', 'Manager', 'Driver', etc.
  is_cashier     boolean generated always as (role = 'Cashier') stored,
  is_manager     boolean generated always as (role ilike 'manager%') stored,

  shift_open     timestamptz not null,
  shift_close    timestamptz,              -- null = currently open
  shift_minutes  int generated always as (
    extract(epoch from coalesce(shift_close, now()) - shift_open)::int / 60
  ) stored,

  ingested_at    timestamptz not null default now(),
  raw_json       jsonb not null
);

create index on sweed_shifts (dealer_id, shift_open);
create index on sweed_shifts (employee_id, shift_open);
create index on sweed_shifts (dealer_id, is_cashier, shift_open) where is_cashier;
```

The `sweed_orders` row also needs to record which Sweed user
processed each invoice (`cashier_user_id`) — that's a free field on
the existing invoice envelope (`createdById`), add a column + ingest
fill in this issue.

### Worker

`helios/src/worker/jobs/ingestSweedShiftsJob.ts`:

1. Highwater table per dealer (same pattern as #22 — last
   `shift_open` seen).
2. 15-minute cadence; cold-start backfill walks history same way
   #22's ingest does.
3. Upsert by `(dealer_id, shift_id)`; reopen-close transitions land
   as `update sweed_shifts set shift_close = ...`.

### Cashier-role filter

Per the parent epic plan, "non-manager filter applied at the role
level". The `is_cashier` / `is_manager` generated columns make this
trivial — the metric SQL filters `is_cashier = true` so floor leads,
managers, drivers, etc. don't pollute the throughput numerator.

### Wire-up

Replace the stub for `cashier.transactions_per_hour` in
[`helios/src/server/metrics/_stub/p5_cashier_weather_delivery.ts`](../../helios/src/server/metrics/_stub/p5_cashier_weather_delivery.ts).
SQL sketch:

```sql
with cashier_hours as (
  select
    time_bucket('1 hour', shift_open) as bucket,
    sum(shift_minutes) / 60.0 as hours
  from sweed_shifts
  where is_cashier and shift_open between $from and $to
  group by 1
),
tx_per_hour as (
  select
    time_bucket('1 hour', pay_time) as bucket,
    count(*) as transactions
  from sweed_orders so
  join sweed_shifts s
    on so.cashier_user_id = s.employee_id
   and so.pay_time between s.shift_open and coalesce(s.shift_close, now())
   and s.is_cashier
  where pay_time between $from and $to
  group by 1
)
select
  c.bucket, t.transactions::numeric / nullif(c.hours, 0) as tx_per_hour
from cashier_hours c
left join tx_per_hour t using (bucket);
```

## Non-goals

- **No write-back** to Sweed shift records (helios never edits
  shifts).
- **No payroll computation.** This is for the dashboard
  denominator only.
- **No per-cashier upsell-lift** — explicitly deferred in the parent
  epic's "out of scope for v1" list.

## Acceptance criteria

- `sweed_shifts` has ≥ 1 row per active cashier per day on
  `vps-nixos-3` for the trailing 30 days.
- `cashier.transactions_per_hour` on `/metrics` no longer carries
  the `STUB:` prefix and renders a real time series.
- Spot-check: hours sum from `sweed_shifts` for one trailing day
  matches Sweed's payroll export to within 1%.
issues.creator: virusdave
issues.title: Sweed Shifts ingest — unblocks cashier.transactions_per_hour

# Helios `/metrics` v1.1 rework — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
> (reopened after v1 shipped as a single-chart picker with stubbed
> data). The authoritative design for this rework is
> [`docs/epics/business-metrics/EPIC_PLAN_v1_1_REWORK.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN_v1_1_REWORK.md)
> in the top-level repo; the original v1 design at
> [`docs/epics/business-metrics/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> remains authoritative for the bits v1.1 does **not** rework
> (schema, API contract, `MetricDef` shape, v2 deferrals).
>
> The corresponding v1 child epic is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#21`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21);
> this issue tracks the v1.1 rework only — please do not reopen the
> v1 child.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation` master that
> satisfies any part of this rework MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: R<n>`
> trailer (note `R`, not `P`, to distinguish from v1 phases) so the
> cross-repo-completion-sync workflow posts a per-phase progress
> comment on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

Everything described in the parent rework addendum, broken out by
phase below. **Re-read the parent rework addendum before starting
any phase** — this child plan is deliberately a thin index over
the parent, not a re-statement of the design. The parent is the
single source of truth for both UX and data-contract decisions.

The original v1 codebase under `server/src/metrics/**`,
`server/src/api/metrics.ts`, `server/src/api/metric-annotations.ts`,
and the `MetricChart` / `/metrics` React tree is the **starting
point**, not the throw-away — v1.1 is a re-shaping, not a rewrite.

### R0 — Reality audit + v1.1 scope freeze

- Inventory every `MetricDef` currently registered under
  `server/src/metrics/**`. For each entry record:
  - whether it is real-data backed or backed by a synthetic stub
    today (this is already partly visible from the existing
    `STUB:` description prefix; the audit should be authoritative
    and machine-readable, not based on the description string);
  - which `sweed_orders` / `sweed_*` / external table(s) it reads;
  - what would be required to flip it to real data (which ingest
    follow-on it depends on; how big the SQL is).
- Reconcile this list against the v1 metric enumeration in
  [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) §"v1 metric panels".
  Resolve any orphans (registered but not in spec) and any holes
  (in spec but never registered).
- Produce the **canonical v1.1 panel list** as a checked-in
  artefact: `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics-v1_1-canonical.md` (or
  equivalent location consistent with the existing runbook). Each
  row: metric id, dashboard section, chart type, current data
  status, required source, planned R4 tranche, "in v1.1"
  yes/no/deferred.
- For any panel proposed to be **deferred from v1.1**, post a
  comment on [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
  listing the proposed deferrals + rationale and wait for explicit
  operator sign-off **before** removing them from the registry.
- Extend the `MetricDef` type with the `dataQuality` block from
  the parent rework addendum (`status: 'real' | 'experimental'`,
  `sources: string[]`, optional `freshnessSla`). Add a
  pre-deploy / CI check that rejects a build where any
  production-visible `MetricDef` is missing `dataQuality` or has
  `dataQuality.status !== 'real'`. (Permit `'experimental'` only
  for entries explicitly marked `dashboard.defaultVisible: false`.)
- Hide / remove demo metrics (`_demo.flat_line`,
  `_demo.random_walk` — and any other v1-era placeholders) from
  the production registry.

**Exit criteria**: a single authoritative list answers "what
ships in v1.1", every entry has a status + source-table mapping,
the build refuses to ship a stub-as-real, demo metrics are gone
from production.

### R1 — Dashboard shell rework

- Replace the existing single-chart picker layout at `/metrics`
  with a **sectioned multi-panel grid**. Sections per the parent
  addendum suggestion (Executive health / Revenue mix / Inventory
  risk / Operations / Context) — the precise grouping is owned by
  this phase and may be retuned, but the result must be a
  dashboard, not a picker.
- Extend `MetricDef` with a `dashboard: { section, order, size,
  defaultVisible }` block. R0's canonical list drives where each
  metric lands in the grid.
- Refactor the existing left-nav into a **table-of-contents**:
  sticky, jumps to dashboard sections / metrics, shows a status
  dot (real / fresh / stale / error) per metric. Clicking a TOC
  entry **scrolls to** the dashboard panel; it must not replace
  the dashboard with a single chart.
- Preserve all v1 global controls (site filter, time range,
  aggregation, axis lock state) at the top of the dashboard, and
  ensure global state is encoded in URL query params so the page
  is shareable / reload-safe.
- All existing real-data panels render as dashboard tiles using
  the existing `<MetricChart/>` component, scaled down to tile
  density.

**Exit criteria**: `/metrics` on a desktop browser shows multiple
charts simultaneously without the operator interacting with the
nav; the left-nav no longer hides every chart except one;
URL-encoded global state is restored on reload.

### R2 — Synchronized crosshair / hover-readout

- Extend `TimeAxisContext` (or add a sibling `TimeHoverContext` —
  implementer's choice; the existing context wiring may make a
  sibling cleaner) with the `TimeHoverBus` contract from the
  parent rework addendum:

  ```ts
  type TimeHoverEvent = {
    t: string;
    sourcePanelId: string;
    bucket?: string;
  };

  type TimeHoverBus = {
    publish(event: TimeHoverEvent): void;
    clear(sourcePanelId: string): void;
    subscribe(listener: (event: TimeHoverEvent | null) => void): () => void;
  };
  ```

- Implement the publish path inside `<MetricChart/>` mousemove,
  `requestAnimationFrame`-throttled. No React state updates on
  every pixel.
- Implement the subscribe path: on subscription update, render a
  vertical crosshair at the nearest bucket boundary + a per-series
  readout pane (panel-local, no shared layout shift).
- Only locked, time-compatible panels (line / area / stacked-area
  / bar) participate in cross-panel hover. Scatter / map / table
  panels are free to ignore the bus or publish their own
  underlying timestamp on hover-over-element if useful (weather
  scatter dot → publish that day so other panels can show the
  corresponding day's values).
- Explicit "no data at hovered `t`" rendering — do not silently
  show the last available value, that misleads the operator.
- Verify zero network traffic on hover (devtools network tab
  empty while mousing across the dashboard).

**Exit criteria**: hovering one locked time-series panel updates
every other compatible locked panel; readouts are accurate at the
hovered bucket; performance is smooth (no visible jank on a
~10-panel dashboard); detail route inherits the same behaviour.

### R3 — Routable expansion + drill-down UX

- Add a `/metrics/<metricId>` detail route. Use the same React
  shell + `TimeAxisContext` as the dashboard so global state
  persists when expanding / collapsing.
- Add an expand affordance to every dashboard tile (title-bar
  icon at minimum; whole-tile click on the chart title is also
  acceptable). Clicking routes to the detail view, carrying the
  current global state in the URL.
- Detail view renders the same `<MetricChart/>` larger, with a
  richer legend / readout pane and annotation controls. The
  detail view's "back to dashboard" preserves dashboard scroll
  position.
- Extend `MetricDef` with a `drilldowns?: DrillDef[]` array:

  ```ts
  type DrillDef = {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    appliesTo: 'series' | 'category' | 'point' | 'row';
    queryParam: string;
  };
  ```

- Implement, at minimum, these v1.1-required drilldowns:
  - **`category.*`** stacks: click a category band → reload the
    panel split by that category's subcategories.
  - **`fulfillment.*`** panels: click a fulfillment-type band /
    legend entry → detail view filtered to that fulfillment.
  - **`delivery.*`** panels: click a zone band → detail view
    filtered to that delivery zone.
  - **`slowmovers.cost_at_risk`** and **`lowstock.upcoming_outs`**
    table rows: row click → SKU-focused detail (filter /
    highlight is acceptable if a per-SKU detail route is out of
    v1.1 scope).
- Encode drill state in the URL (`?drill=<drillId>&value=<...>`)
  so detail views are shareable / reload-safe.

**Exit criteria**: every dashboard panel can be expanded into a
real route; the four required drilldowns above are implemented
and reload-safe; share-link of an expanded panel reproduces the
exact view (site filter + range + agg + drill).

### R4 — Real-data wiring, by source tranche

The dominant work of the rework. Broken into source-grouped
sub-phases so each tranche is independently shippable and
reviewable. Each sub-phase commit carries `Phase: R4a` / `R4b` /
etc. so the parent issue gets fine-grained progress updates.

#### R4a — orders / cost / margin-backed metrics

Depends on the existing `sweed_orders` ingest + closed
[#23](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/23)
wholesale-cost cache. Wires real data for:

- `acquisition.first_vs_returning` (verify the v1 "first-time"
  definition pin: `customer_id` with no prior completed order in
  our system — document in the runbook if Sweed identity is
  unstable in the chosen window);
- `margins.effective_gm_pct`, `margins.gross_margin_dollars`,
  `margins.stack_new_vs_returning`;
- `basket.size_by_fulfillment`, `basket.size_by_customer_type`;
- `category.sales_stack_dollars`, `category.sales_stack_fraction`,
  `category.margin_dollars_stack` (and the
  category → subcategory drill from R3);
- `fulfillment.order_count`, `fulfillment.sales_dollars`,
  `fulfillment.margin_dollars`, `fulfillment.effective_gm_pct`;
- `payment.order_count`, `payment.sales_dollars`.

Each metric's response includes the `meta` block from the parent
rework addendum (sources, lastUpdatedAt, coverage). Sanity-check
total sales $ and total margin $ against the existing Helios
operational reports where one exists; note any discrepancy in the
phase's commit message + parent-issue comment.

#### R4b — inventory / SKU-risk metrics

Depends on
[#24](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/24)
Sweed per-package snapshot ingest. Wires:

- `inventory.cost_distribution` (with category → subcategory
  drill);
- `inventory.misalignment` (diverging bar at latest `t` ranked by
  `(on_hand_cost / 30d_cogs_run_rate) - target_ratio`);
- `slowmovers.cost_at_risk` (table-as-chart with the columns from
  v1 spec, plus the row-click → SKU drill from R3);
- `lowstock.upcoming_outs` (table-as-chart including the
  "expected margin loss $" column = `days_out × daily_margin_run_rate`).

R4b lands the ingest work in
[#24](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/24) as
its first commit if not already complete, then the SQL on top.

#### R4c — delivery / customer-geography metrics

Depends on
[#25](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/25)
Sweed per-invoice detail fetch. Wires:

- `delivery.order_count_by_zone` (with zone drill from R3);
- `delivery.margin_pct`;
- `customers.origin_map` (OSM-tile choropleth + heatmap; static
  date-range selector + diff-vs-prior overlay; playback remains
  v2 per the v1 plan).

#### R4d — external / operational context

Depends on
[#26](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/26)
daily-weather ingest and
[#27](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/27)
Sweed Shifts ingest. Wires:

- `weather.scatter_margin_vs_high_temp`,
  `weather.scatter_margin_vs_low_temp`,
  `weather.scatter_margin_vs_precip`;
- `cashier.transactions_per_hour`.

**Exit criteria for each R4 sub-phase**: every metric in the
sub-phase reports `dataQuality.status = 'real'` and renders real
production values on the live `/metrics` page; the CI guardrail
passes; the sanity-check note (where one applies) is committed
into the phase's commit message; no synthetic fallback remains in
production.

**Net exit criterion for R4**: zero production-visible panels are
backed by stubs.

### R5 — Data-quality hardening + dashboard usefulness pass

- Loading / empty / stale / error states for every panel (no
  silent blank tiles, no infinite spinners on a single source
  outage).
- Source / freshness badges in panel headers (small badge that
  reads e.g. `sweed_orders · 14 min ago`; hover for full
  source-list tooltip).
- Performance review: measure dashboard cold-load on
  `vps-nixos-3`; first useful panel within ~3 s, full settle
  within ~8–10 s absent source outages. Add server-side caching /
  concurrency limits where a single panel's query dominates.
- Stub-leak guardrail: a CI / pre-deploy test that walks the
  production registry and fails the build if any visible metric
  has `dataQuality.status !== 'real'` (matches R0's contract;
  this phase tightens it to a hard gate).
- Visual polish: tile density, readable typography, sensible
  default chart sizes. Not a redesign — just enough that the
  dashboard is comfortable to leave open on an operator screen.
- Verify global controls (site filter, aggregation, range) apply
  cleanly to every locked panel within one round-trip; verify
  per-panel lock / unlock interacts correctly with global
  changes.

**Exit criteria**: the operator can tell at a glance whether
every panel is fresh and trustworthy; cold-load meets the latency
budget; the build refuses to ship a stub.

### R6 — Runbook, validation evidence, closure package

- Refresh `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md` for the v1.1 reality:
  - dashboard model (sections, panel placement, drill contract,
    hover bus);
  - how to add a new metric (now includes `dashboard`,
    `dataQuality`, optional `drilldowns` blocks);
  - how the stub-leak guardrail works and how to disable a
    metric temporarily;
  - how to verify the synchronized crosshair after a change;
  - how to bring up `/metrics` locally and confirm real-data
    metadata.
- Validation evidence (committed under the runbook):
  - dashboard-overview screenshot;
  - synchronized-hover screenshot (or short GIF) showing two
    panels' crosshairs synced;
  - expand / detail route screenshot showing URL + drill state;
  - real-data badges screenshot (source + freshness visible);
  - one representative drill screenshot (e.g. category →
    subcategory).
- Parent closure package: a single comment on
  [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
  containing the live URL, the R0–R6 per-phase commit table, the
  canonical metric list with per-panel data-source mapping, the
  validation-evidence screenshots, and the oracle review note
  (see below).
- **Oracle review**: before R6 closure, the rework owner runs an
  oracle review pass against the live `/metrics` page and the
  canonical metric list, captures the oracle's "fit for purpose"
  assessment, addresses any blocking feedback, and includes the
  final oracle note in the closure package. This is the operator's
  stated bar; do not skip it.

**Exit criteria**: parent can close based on evidence, not trust.

## Cross-repo dependencies

Same as v1 — none hard. The ingest follow-ons
([#22](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/22),
[#24](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/24),
[#25](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/25),
[#26](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/26),
[#27](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/27))
all live in this repo and are picked up by the R4 sub-phases.

If during R4 a new external ingest stream is discovered to be
needed (e.g. a different NOAA station list owned by
`helios-parser-configs`), file an additional child epic against
the appropriate peer per the
[cross-repo task-dag driver](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/cross-repo-task-dag-driver.md)
model and link it from the parent issue.

## Acceptance criteria (delegated from parent)

The full v1.1 acceptance criteria live in the parent rework
addendum §"Refreshed acceptance criteria". Reproduced here as a
checklist for the R6 owner:

- [ ] (1) Dashboard, not picker — `/metrics` shows multiple charts
      at once by default; left-nav is TOC only.
- [ ] (2) Routable expansion — `/metrics/<metricId>` route exists,
      preserves global state in URL, supports browser back.
- [ ] (3) Useful drilldowns — minimum four implemented (category,
      fulfillment, delivery zone, SKU); drill state in URL.
- [ ] (4) Synchronized crosshair + readouts — hover on one locked
      panel drives all compatible locked panels; no network
      traffic on hover; explicit no-data state.
- [ ] (5) Real data only — zero stub / synthetic / demo metrics
      visible on production `/metrics`; all deferrals removed
      from registry with operator sign-off on #7.
- [ ] (6) Data transparency — source / freshness badges on every
      panel; stale / error / empty states explicit; key totals
      sanity-checked against Helios reports.
- [ ] (7) Global controls coherent — site / aggregation / range
      apply across locked panels within one round-trip.
- [ ] (8) Annotations integrated — CRUD works in tile + detail
      modes; annotations cross-render on other panels covering
      the annotated `t`.
- [ ] (9) Performance — first paint ~3 s, full settle ~8–10 s on
      `vps-nixos-3`; skeleton states for slow panels.
- [ ] (10) Oracle-approved evidence package — live URL, commit
      table, screenshots, canonical metric list, oracle note.

issues.body:
## Problem

Comments posted on GitHub issues by autonomous Amp agents (via
`gh issue comment` from `vps-nixos-3` etc.) currently carry the
authoring user's identity — for example `virusdave (Dave Nicponski)`
on agent-driven hosts where Dave's `gh auth login` token is the
backing credential. This is misleading: readers (and Dave himself)
cannot distinguish at-a-glance between

  * a comment Dave actually wrote, and
  * a comment a long-running agent wrote on his behalf.

This came up on [#25](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/25):
> The issue comment was hallucinated by an agent, not a directive of mine.
> Speaking of which, I'd really like system-generated comments to NOT be
> made as `virusdave` user if possible, or at minimum to be prefaced
> loudly in bold at top "SYSTEM-GENERATED".

## Proposed remediation (in preference order)

1. **Separate machine identity (preferred).** Provision a dedicated
   GitHub bot account (`fbnyc-amp-bot`, GitHub App, or fine-grained
   PAT under a different login) and have `gh` invocations made by
   agents — `page-dave`, `scripts/task-dag`, the github-worker
   harness, ad-hoc `gh issue comment` calls — authenticate as the
   bot identity. Then `author: virusdave` only ever appears on
   comments Dave physically typed. Mechanically the simplest way is
   one of:

     * a separate per-host `GH_TOKEN` env var pointing at the bot
       PAT, exported on the agent shells but not on Dave's
       interactive shell; or
     * `gh auth switch` between two named hosts (`github.com` vs
       `github.com/fbnyc-amp-bot`) on agent shells.

2. **Mandatory header (fallback).** If a bot identity isn't worth
   provisioning, every agent-authored comment MUST begin with a
   loud, bold first line — e.g.

   ```
   > **🤖 SYSTEM-GENERATED — written by Amp agent on `vps-nixos-3`**
   ```

   so the reader's eye catches it before they engage with the
   substance. This is brittle (relies on every code path
   remembering to prepend) but cheap.

## Implementation surface to audit

Anything that calls `gh issue comment`, `gh pr comment`, `gh issue
create` from agent contexts. Quick grep targets:

- `scripts/task-dag` (posts a comment on `complete`)
- `scripts/upload-to-mss` (does NOT post comments, but reviewer)
- `page-dave` (out-of-band; uses ntfy, not GitHub — fine)
- ad-hoc `gh issue comment` calls in `helios/scripts/*`
- the github-worker harness (`/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/`)

If we go with option 2, the cleanest implementation is a thin
`scripts/gh-bot-comment` wrapper that prepends the header and
delegates to `gh issue comment` so every agent flow uses one entry
point.

## Acceptance criteria

- Comments posted by autonomous agents are immediately visually
  distinguishable from comments Dave wrote, on every issue and PR.
- No code path posts an unannotated agent comment under Dave's
  identity.

## Context

Filed by an Amp agent (vps-nixos-3) after Dave flagged the gap on
[#25](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/25#issuecomment-4548352805).

issues.body:
# Helios `/metrics` v1.2 rework — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
> for the v1.2 iteration. Authoritative design:
> [`docs/epics/business-metrics/EPIC_PLAN_v1_2_REWORK.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN_v1_2_REWORK.md)
> in the top-level repo.
>
> The v1 child epic is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#21`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21)
> (closed); the v1.1 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#28`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/28)
> (closed at the R6 closure commit). This issue tracks the v1.2
> rework only — please do not reopen the v1 or v1.1 children.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation` master that
> satisfies any part of this rework MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: V2<n>`
> trailer (e.g. `Phase: V2'3`) — distinct from v1's `P<n>` and
> v1.1's `R<n>` — so per-phase progress comments on the parent
> issue are visually grouped per rework iteration.

## Scope owned by this repo

v1.2 closes the six oracle-flagged gaps captured in the parent
addendum:

1. Prior-period comparison & variance as the default render of
   every time-series panel.
2. Tabular drilldown renderer (per-SKU / per-(category,
   subcategory) tables behind slow-mover, low-stock, inventory
   misalignment).
3. CSV / PNG / SVG export from every panel.
4. Aggregation parity — `dow` / `dom` / `dofortnight` either work
   end-to-end or are removed from the global control set.
5. On-tile annotation drill (annotation popover available without
   first expanding the panel).
6. `inventory.cost_distribution` perf refactor (single all-snapshots
   fetch + JS as-of fold).

Re-read the parent addendum before starting any phase. This child
plan is intentionally a thin index over the parent.

### R'0 — Scope freeze + agg-parity decision + canonical update

- Re-confirm the v1.2-in-scope panel set against the canonical
  v1.1 panel list landed in R6 of the v1.1 rework. Any panel
  added or removed from the registry since v1.1 closure is
  reconciled here.
- Pick `dow` / `dom` / `dofortnight`'s fate:
  - default position is "implement them generically across every
    time-series metric via a client-side reduce over already-fetched
    bucketed data";
  - fall-back position is "remove them from the global agg
    dropdown until per-metric opt-in lands" — fall back **only**
    with explicit operator sign-off on the parent issue.
- Extend `MetricDef` types:
  - `supports?: { priorPeriod?: boolean; yearOverYear?: boolean; ... }`
  - `desirableDirection?: 'up' | 'down' | 'neutral'`
    (drives variance-readout colour; default `'up'`).
  - `drilldowns[].tableMode?: TableModeDef` (see parent §"Tabular
    drilldown contract").
- Add a CI guardrail that fails the build if any visible
  time-series metric is missing `supports.priorPeriod: true` after
  R'1 lands.
- Refresh `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics-v1_1-canonical.md` to a
  `…-v1_2-canonical.md` superset that adds `supports.priorPeriod`
  / `desirableDirection` / `tableMode` columns, and update the
  runbook anchor on the parent issue's body.

**Exit criteria**: single authoritative v1.2 panel list,
aggregation-parity decision recorded, `MetricDef` types
extended (no behavioural change yet — types are additive),
guardrail wired (currently passing because nothing declares
`supports.priorPeriod` yet — flips to enforcement in R'1).

### R'1 — `compareTo` API + reference series rendering

- Server side:
  - Every time-series metric's `GET /api/metrics/<id>` accepts a
    new optional `compareTo` query param:
    `prior-period` (default), `year-over-year`, `none`.
  - When `compareTo !== 'none'` the response includes a parallel
    `series` entry with `kind: 'reference'`, `baselineRange:
    { from, to }`, sampled at the **same** bucket boundaries as
    the primary series (zero-fill explicit; missing data
    explicit, not silently zero).
  - Variance readout for the latest visible bucket (and totals
    across the visible window) computed server-side:
    `meta.variance: { absolute, fraction, baselineRange }`
    per primary series.
  - All work done in the same SQL pass where possible; if a
    second SQL is required, batched in the same handler so each
    request is one round-trip from the client's perspective.
- Client side:
  - `<MetricChart/>` renders `kind: 'reference'` series as a
    dimmed (e.g. 38% opacity) version of the primary's stroke
    colour, behind the primary, with no `×` markers; keeps
    primary stroke + markers identical to v1.1.
  - Hover-readout tooltip shows current bucket value, reference
    value, and variance per series; the synchronized crosshair
    from v1.1 R2 includes reference values in its readout.
  - Per-panel `compareTo` toggle in the panel header (chevron menu:
    `Prior period` / `Year over year` / `Off`). Per-page default
    is `prior-period`; per-panel choice persists in the URL via
    `compareTo[<metricId>]=…` so share-links reproduce.

**Exit criteria**: every visible time-series panel renders a
prior-period reference series by default; toggling per-panel
between prior-period / YoY / off works and persists in the URL;
the R'0 guardrail is in enforcement.

### R'2 — Variance readouts + optional shading

- Panel header readout: small chip rendering
  `Δ <sign> <abs> (<pct>)` for the visible-window totals, with
  colour driven by `MetricDef.desirableDirection` (up = green-on-pos,
  down = green-on-neg, neutral = no colour). On hover/focus, expand
  to a small popover with `current = X`, `reference (prior period)
  = Y`, `Δ = X−Y`, `Δ% = (X−Y)/Y`.
- Hover-readout tooltip (the crosshair tooltip from v1.1 R2) gains
  a per-series variance row (`Δ = X−Y (Δ%)`) under each existing
  value row.
- Variance shading: optional faint shaded band between primary
  and reference, gated by a page-level toggle (off by default for
  dashboard density; on by default in detail / expanded mode).
- Verify the panel header readout doesn't cause layout shift when
  the value loads (reserve space with a skeleton placeholder).

**Exit criteria**: variance is readable at a glance from the
dashboard without clicking; colour direction respects
`desirableDirection`; expanded mode shows the shaded band.

### R'3 — `TableModeDef` + per-metric `/rows` endpoint + table tab

- Server side:
  - New endpoint family `GET /api/metrics/<id>/rows?<global filters>
    & sort=<col>:<dir> & page=<n> & pageSize=<m>`. Implemented per
    metric; default `pageSize` from `TableModeDef.pageSize ?? 50`,
    server-clamps `pageSize ≤ 200`.
  - Response shape:
    ```ts
    {
      columns: TableColumnDef[];           // mirror of MetricDef
      rows: Record<string, unknown>[];     // server-formatted values for export honesty
      totalRows: number;
      page: number;
      pageSize: number;
      sort: { column: string; direction: 'asc' | 'desc' };
      meta: { sources, lastUpdatedAt, coverageFrom, coverageTo, warnings };
    }
    ```
  - Sort + page implemented in SQL (no JS-side reshuffle on
    pagination — pagination is the whole point).
- Client side:
  - `MetricDef.drilldowns[].tableMode` declared → detail route
    (`/metrics/<metricId>`) shows a tab strip `Chart | Table`.
    Default tab when arrived via row-click drill is `Table`; via
    a regular expand affordance, `Chart`.
  - `<MetricTable/>` component: column headers click to sort
    (multi-cycle: asc → desc → off), page controls at the
    bottom, per-row action button when
    `tableMode.rowAction` is declared.
- Land the three required tables:
  - `slowmovers.cost_at_risk` rows: `{ sku, name, on_hand_cost,
    retail_value, last_sold_date, days_since_sold }`.
  - `lowstock.upcoming_outs` rows: `{ sku, name, days_of_cover,
    expected_margin_loss, daily_margin_run_rate, next_reorder_date }`.
  - `inventory.misalignment` rows: `{ category, subcategory,
    on_hand_cost, cogs_30d, observed_ratio, target_ratio,
    divergence }`.
- The R'4 CSV export builds on the same `/rows` endpoint with a
  capped unpaginated mode (see R'4); land that hook in this phase
  even if the export menu wiring happens in R'4.

**Exit criteria**: three required tables render with server-side
sort + pagination on the detail route; row-click drills (where
declared) link out; CI smoke confirms each declared
`tableMode.endpoint` returns 200 on a representative window.

### R'4 — Export (CSV / PNG / SVG)

- Server side:
  - `GET /api/metrics/<id>/export?fmt=csv` — long-form CSV. In
    chart mode: `metric_id,series_id,bucket_start,value,kind`
    (`kind` is `'primary'` or `'reference'`). In table mode:
    columns mirror `TableColumnDef.key` order; rows are
    unpaginated, server-clamped at `max=10000`. Response carries
    `X-Export-Clipped: true` + a leading `# clipped at 10000
    rows` comment line when clamp hits.
  - `GET /api/metrics/<id>/export?fmt=png` and `fmt=svg` —
    server-side render of the panel SVG via a headless render of
    `<MetricChart/>` (use `satori` or the existing SSR path if
    one is wired; otherwise `node-canvas` over a hand-built SVG
    string is acceptable). Width / height / DPR fixed
    (`w=1200,h=600,dpr=2` default; overridable via query).
    Output preserves current global state from the request query
    (site / range / agg / compareTo / drill).
- Client side:
  - Panel header (dashboard tile + detail view) exposes an export
    chevron menu with `CSV` / `PNG` / `SVG` actions. Selecting an
    action issues a normal download via a hidden `<a download>`
    so the browser handles it natively.
  - In table mode, the same export menu emits a rows-based CSV
    (the server endpoint switches mode automatically based on
    the `mode=table` flag the client adds).
- Smoke tests:
  - CSV round-trip: render a panel, export, re-parse, assert
    bucket count + first/last bucket match the rendered chart.
  - PNG smoke: response is `image/png`, byte length > 1KB, magic
    bytes `\x89PNG`.
  - SVG smoke: response is `image/svg+xml`, contains the metric
    id in a `data-metric` attribute on the root `<svg>`.

**Exit criteria**: every panel exports cleanly to all three
formats from both dashboard tile and detail view; exports honour
current global state; clip notices appear when row cap is hit.

### R'5 — Aggregation parity + on-tile annotation drill

- Aggregation parity (per R'0 decision):
  - Path (1) **implement**: add a generic client-side reducer
    that takes the bucketed `series` response and folds it to
    `dow` (Mon..Sun, ISO weekday), `dom` (1..31), and
    `dofortnight` (1..14, anchored on a configurable epoch).
    Stacked / percent / area chart types share the reducer.
    Scatter / map / table panels declare
    `supportsAggregations: ['total','month','week','date','hour']`
    only and the global agg dropdown disables non-supported
    options when only such panels are visible (rare).
  - Path (2) **remove**: drop `dow` / `dom` / `dofortnight` from
    the global agg dropdown; document in the runbook how a
    metric opts in per-metric (would be a v1.3+ thing).
- On-tile annotation drill:
  - Reuse the expanded-mode annotation popover component for
    on-tile pip hover/focus/tap; pip hit area is the rendered
    indicator + a small invisible padding (8px) for touch.
  - Popover shows: annotation title, author, ISO timestamp, an
    excerpt of the comment body, and a `Open panel detail`
    button that routes to the owning panel's detail view scrolled
    to the annotated `t`.
  - Crosshair (from v1.1 R2) does not fire while the annotation
    popover is open over the pip — popover takes precedence.
  - Keyboard: annotation pips are reachable via Tab, popover
    opens on Enter / Space, closes on Escape, never traps focus.

**Exit criteria**: agg dropdown advertises only options that all
visible time-series metrics support (or implements them
generically); on-tile annotations are inspectable without first
expanding the panel; touch / keyboard parity verified.

### R'6 — `inventory.cost_distribution` perf + closure package

- Perf refactor:
  - Replace the per-bucket DISTINCT-ON snapshot scan with a
    single window-scoped pull: `SELECT … FROM inventory_snapshots
    WHERE snapshot_ts BETWEEN window_start - max_lookback AND
    window_end` (and any filter that already narrows the read).
  - JS-side as-of fold: for each requested bucket boundary
    (already produced by `walkBuckets`), pick the most recent
    snapshot row per (sku, location) with `snapshot_ts ≤ boundary`.
    Reduce to per-(category[, subcategory]) cost totals.
  - Server-side cache: snapshot stream is roughly append-only,
    so cache the window pull with a 60s TTL keyed on
    `(start, end, max_lookback)`. Cache layer is the existing
    in-process LRU; no Redis required.
  - Measurement: produce a `before` / `after` timing table for
    P50 / P95 cold / P95 warm on the live `vps-nixos-3` against
    typical dashboard windows (1d / 7d / 28d / 12wk). Target:
    P50 < 250 ms warm, P95 < 600 ms cold.
- Runbook refresh: `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md` extended
  with the v1.2 surface (compareTo, table mode, export, agg
  parity, annotation tile drill, snapshot-fold).
- Validation evidence committed under the runbook:
  - prior-period overlay screenshot (default render);
  - variance readout in header + tooltip screenshots;
  - table-mode tab screenshot on a real slow-mover row;
  - CSV / PNG / SVG export sample (CSV first 20 lines; PNG
    thumbnail; SVG embed-able snippet);
  - annotation popover on a dashboard tile screenshot;
  - `inventory.cost_distribution` before/after timing table.
- Oracle review pass: re-run an oracle review on the live
  `/metrics` page + the new v1.2 surfaces + the canonical metric
  list. Capture the oracle's "fit for purpose — world class for
  this operator's stated needs?" verdict. If the oracle flags new
  gaps, address them in this phase before the closure commit, or
  file an explicit follow-on epic and call it out in the closure
  package.
- Closure package: a single comment on
  [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
  containing the live URL, the R'0–R'6 per-phase commit table,
  the AC §1–8 sign-off (with one-line evidence per criterion),
  the refreshed canonical metric list, the validation evidence,
  and the oracle note. The close commit MUST carry
  `Closes-Epic: #7` per #8's policy so
  `close-completed-issues.yml` closes the issue.

**Exit criteria**: parent can close based on evidence, not trust;
all v1.2 AC §1–8 demonstrably hold on production; v1.1 AC §1–10
continue to hold (no regressions); the oracle confirms the
dashboard is fit for the operator's stated "world-class business
performance metrics dashboard" purpose.

## Cross-repo dependencies

None hard. v1.2's data needs are entirely covered by the ingest
streams already wired in v1.1 (orders / cost / inventory snapshots
/ delivery / weather / shifts). If a v1.2 phase discovers a
missing column or a stream-shape problem, file an additional child
epic against the appropriate peer per the
[cross-repo task-dag driver](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/cross-repo-task-dag-driver.md)
model and link it from the parent issue.

## Acceptance criteria (delegated from parent)

The full v1.2 acceptance criteria live in the parent rework
addendum §"Refreshed acceptance criteria". Reproduced here as a
checklist for the R'6 owner:

- [ ] (1) Prior-period comparable by default; per-panel
      compareTo toggle (prior-period / YoY / off); variance in
      header + hover; reference fetched in same round-trip.
- [ ] (2) Table tab on detail route for slow-movers,
      low-stock, inventory-misalignment; server-side sort +
      paging; CSV export of unpaginated rows with clip notice.
- [ ] (3) CSV / PNG / SVG export from every panel (tile +
      detail); preserves global state; CSV is canonical machine
      format.
- [ ] (4) Aggregation parity — `dow` / `dom` / `dofortnight`
      either work on every visible time-series metric or are
      removed from the global control set.
- [ ] (5) On-tile annotation drill — popover on pip hover /
      focus / tap with title / author / timestamp / excerpt;
      `Open panel detail` button routes correctly.
- [ ] (6) `inventory.cost_distribution` P50 < 250 ms warm,
      P95 < 600 ms cold on `vps-nixos-3` 12-week window;
      timing note in R'6 commit.
- [ ] (7) v1.1 AC §1–10 continue to hold on production; no
      regressions in the dashboard / crosshair / expand+drill /
      stub-leak guardrail.
- [ ] (8) Oracle-approved closure evidence package — live URL,
      commit table, screenshots, canonical metric list, oracle
      note; close commit carries `Closes-Epic: #7`.

# Customer / Visitor Address Ingestion — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/visitor-address-ingestion/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in the top-level repo; this child epic scope is **strictly the
> `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (Helios + ingest monorepo) slice of
> that design**.  Every implementation commit landing on `automation`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: A<n>`
> trailer so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post the
> per-phase progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

Everything described in the parent EPIC_PLAN.md, broken out by phase
below.  Re-read the parent before starting — the section here is a
thin index over the parent rather than a re-statement of the design.

### A1 — DB migration + webhook handler + bearer-token auth

- Alembic / golang-migrate / whatever-helios-uses migration adding
  the `visitor_scans` table with **exactly** the columns, indices,
  and unique constraint defined in the parent design.
- Two routes, mounted on the existing helios-server HTTP router:
  - `POST /wh/bx/veriscan/checkin`
  - `POST /wh/mh/veriscan/checkin`
- Both routes share a single handler whose only per-route input is
  the literal `site_slug` (`'bx'` or `'mh'`) passed by the route
  binding.  Unknown slugs MUST be impossible by construction
  (whitelist at mount time, not at runtime).
- Bearer-token auth middleware that:
  - reads `VERISCAN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` from env at process start;
  - rejects requests with no `Authorization` header (401);
  - parses `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (case-insensitive scheme);
  - compares constant-time against the env value;
  - on mismatch: 401 with no body and a `warn`-level structured
    log including remote IP + path (no token material).
- Envelope validation per parent design (Type, EventId, WebHookId,
  Data.HashId presence).  400 on missing.
- Insert with `ON CONFLICT (provider, hash_id) DO NOTHING`.
- `info`-level structured log of every accepted body keyed by
  `hash_id` (so we have a full audit trail outside the DB).
- Smoke-test: a `curl` example committed under `docs/runbooks/`
  that POSTs a synthetic VeriScan envelope at the local helios-server
  binary and asserts a 200 + row insert.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: A1`.

### A2 — Backfill CLI

- New subcommand on the existing `helios-prep` binary:

  ```
  helios-prep visitor-scans backfill \
      --site=<bx|mh> --provider=veriscan \
      --file=<path> [--dry-run]
  ```

- Accepts JSON array, NDJSON, or CSV (sniffed from extension first,
  content second).
- For each input record, reshapes columns into the VeriScan-envelope
  `Data` schema (the operator-supplied Drive export is a flat row
  dump, not a wire envelope), synthesises an envelope with:
  - `Type='CreateCard'`,
  - `WebHookId=0` and `EventId=<stable hash of HashId>` (so re-runs
    are idempotent and not just "no-op via unique constraint" but
    also produce identical `raw_envelope` JSONB),
  - `Created`/`Sent` set to the file's mtime,
- Calls into the **exact same** insert helper used by A1.
- Reports `inserted=`, `skipped_duplicate=`, `errored=` counts at
  the end; `--dry-run` prints the would-be inserts as JSON Lines.
- Unit tests cover: round-trip with the same file twice yields
  `inserted=N` then `skipped_duplicate=N`; malformed row yields
  `errored=1` and does not abort the run.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: A2`.

### A3 — Admin page

- `/admin/visitors/scans` per parent design.  Sits behind the
  existing helios admin auth (oauth-reverse-proxy).
- Paginated table newest-first, columns + filters per parent.
- Row click → drawer with the full normalised row + a syntax-highlit
  JSON view of `raw_envelope`.
- CSV export of the current filter view (uses the same query the
  table renders, no second source of truth).

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: A3`.

## Out of scope

- DNS / TLS / nginx / agenix / systemd unit changes —
  `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`.
- VeriScan-side webhook configuration — operator.
- Downloading the Drive backfill file — operator hands the file to
  the backfill CLI via `--file=`.
- Any consumer of `visitor_scans` (marketing, segmentation,
  loyalty, geo-analyses).  Later epics will read this table.

## Phase dependencies

- A1 depends on `nixos-sbc` N1 (env var present at runtime).  A1
  code itself can be written and unit-tested without N1; only the
  deployed-to-prod step blocks.
- A2 depends on A1 landing (shared insert helper).
- A3 depends on A1 landing (table must exist).
- A2 and A3 can proceed in parallel.

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. A1, A2, A3 each have at least one commit on `automation` master
   carrying `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9` and the matching
   `Phase:` trailer.
2. The A1 smoke-test (`docs/runbooks/`) runs green against the
   deployed helios-server on `vps-nixos-3`.
3. The operator confirms (via a comment on
   [#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9)) that
   VeriScan webhook configuration on bx + mh points at the
   correct URLs with the correct bearer token, and that at least
   one live check-in has produced a row visible in
   `/admin/visitors/scans`.

# Customers UX v2: export customer-origin replay to MP4

> **Status: PAUSED** — placeholder for v2 work requested by the operator on
> [virusdave/top-level#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9)
> ("Export to mp4 on demand of the replay movie would be a plus for v2;
> leave an open todo and paused github issue for this.").
>
> This issue is intentionally not on the critical path of the
> Customers UX child epic (C1–C5). Do **not** start work on this until:
>
> 1. The Customers UX child epic C5 (in-browser replay playback at
>    `/admin/customers/map`) has landed and been operator-accepted.
> 2. The operator explicitly un-pauses this issue.

## Background

Parent design:
[`docs/epics/visitor-address-ingestion/CUSTOMERS_UX_EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/visitor-address-ingestion/CUSTOMERS_UX_EPIC_PLAN.md)
in `virusdave/top-level`.

C5 ships a "weather-radar-style" replay of customer-origin check-ins on
`/admin/customers/map`, fully driven by URL state (`from`, `to`,
`bucket`, `speed`, `lifetime`, `fade`, `loop`, `tail`, `enc`,
`viewport`, plus shared Check-ins filters).

The operator wants to be able to export a given replay configuration as
a deterministic MP4 for offline review / sharing with non-Helios
stakeholders.

## Scope (when un-paused)

- Accept a shareable replay config from `/admin/customers/map`
  (the same URL state set documented in parent design §9.2).
- Render a deterministic 1080p / 30fps MP4 that visually matches the
  in-browser replay for that URL.
- Burned-in overlays:
  - title;
  - time range;
  - current domain timestamp;
  - encoding legend;
  - site/filter summary.
- Progress UI in the admin page while rendering.
- Actionable error UI on failure (no silent timeouts).
- Privacy guardrails:
  - no raw PII;
  - no exact addresses beyond the map config's allowed aggregation
    (parent design §13);
  - exact-point mode disallowed for MP4 export unless explicit
    operator-confirmed flag is set on the export request.

## Likely implementation shape (subject to design when un-paused)

- Headless browser (or offscreen MapLibre canvas) renders frames at
  the replay's logical timestamps.
- Frame sequence piped to `ffmpeg` for MP4 muxing.
- Render runs server-side on `helios.freshlybaked.us` and streams the
  result to the operator's browser; or generates a downloadable file
  in a known location with a notification.
- Design before implementation — do not start coding the renderer
  before the design step is reviewed.

## Acceptance criteria (when un-paused)

- Exported MP4 visually matches the in-browser replay for the same
  URL config (same buckets, same encoding, same lifetime/fade math).
- Output includes title, time range, timestamp, legend, and
  site/filter summary as burned-in overlays.
- Long exports either succeed end-to-end or fail with an actionable
  error message; no silent timeouts.
- No MP4 work blocks or destabilises C1–C5.
- Privacy guardrails enforced server-side, not just client-side.

## Out of scope

- Sharing/publishing the resulting MP4 outside Helios.
- Live streaming (this is render-on-demand only).
- Audio.
- Per-frame interactive controls in the MP4 (it is a passive video).

## Coordination

When un-paused, this issue should be re-delegated from
`virusdave/top-level` as a fresh child epic if the operator wants the
cross-repo task-dag tracking, or simply worked on directly with a
`Satisfies:` trailer pointing back at #9 (or a new parent issue) at the
operator's preference.

# Customers UX — `automation` child epic

> Second child epic of
> [virusdave/top-level#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9),
> sibling to the ingestion child epic at
> [`./EPIC_PLAN.md`](./EPIC_PLAN.md).
>
> Authoritative design:
> [`docs/epics/visitor-address-ingestion/CUSTOMERS_UX_EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../CUSTOMERS_UX_EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in the top-level repo.  This file is the thin per-repo scope index;
> read the parent design before starting.
>
> Implementation commits landing on `automation` master that satisfy
> any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9
> ```
>
> and SHOULD also carry:
>
> ```
> Phase: C<n>
> ```
>
> so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post the per-phase
> progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

The Helios admin UI + helios-server API + DB compatibility views that
make `visitor_scans` operationally useful, plus the IA reorganisation
that puts CRM and Segments under a new top-level "Customers" item.

Phased as C1..C5; C6 is explicitly deferred to a separate **paused**
follow-on issue (operator's request: "Export to mp4 on demand of the
replay movie would be a plus for v2; leave an open todo and paused
github issue for this.").

### C1 — Live scans table — PAGE-BACK TRIGGER

**Operator-stated stop-the-line trigger.** Ship this first. The
operator's exact words: "Page me as soon as the 'recent / live scans'
part is complete, as i want to enable this *now*."

- Canonical route `/admin/customers/check-ins`.
- Alias `/admin/visitors/scans` (the route the ingestion epic A3
  originally planned) so it remains valid.
- Server endpoint `GET /api/admin/customers/check-ins` per parent
  design §6.6 (subset for C1: scan rows + basic filters + facets;
  purchase summary fields can return `null`/`unknown`).
- Detail endpoint `GET /api/admin/customers/check-ins/:scan_id`
  with raw payload permission gating per parent design §13.
- Canonical `checked_in_at = COALESCE(scanned_at, created_at,
  ingested_at)`; if a normalized column was added in the ingestion
  epic, use it; otherwise use the expression + matching index per
  parent design §11 "Indexes to add or verify".
- Newest-first paginated/virtualised table with the C1 columns in
  parent design §6.3.
- Basic filters (server-side SQL, NOT client-only): site,
  checked-in date range, ingest source, document type, scan status,
  authentication status, state, postal prefix.
- Row drawer with normalized fields + address/geocode panel + raw
  JSON panel (permission-gated; if Helios lacks the permission
  infrastructure, hide the raw panel rather than expose unguarded).
- Lightweight auto-refresh (every 15–30s) plus manual refresh; live
  status chip showing latest `checked_in_at` / `ingested_at`.
- No purchase joins, no map, no IA changes in C1.
- After deploy, post the C1 status comment on parent issue #9 per
  parent design §16.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C1`.

### C2 — Purchase-history facets + matching layer + CSV export

- New compatibility views over the existing CRM/orders source:
  `customer_order_facts` and `customer_order_line_facts` per parent
  design §5.3. Use the same business definitions the existing CRM
  page already uses.
- `visitor_scan_customer_matches` match layer per parent design §5.4
  with the precedence table (default purchase-history filters use
  `confidence >= 85`).
- Extend `/api/admin/customers/check-ins` to compute and return:
  `purchase.match_*`, `purchase.history_at_checkin`,
  `purchase.prior_order_count`, `purchase.last_purchase_at`,
  `purchase.converted_after_checkin`, `purchase.visit_*`,
  `purchase.lifetime_*` per parent design §6.6 sample response.
- Add purchase filters (parent §6.4.4):
  - purchase history at check-in (repeat/no-prior/unknown);
  - visit conversion (yes/no/unknown);
  - first-time purchaser conversion;
  - prior order count bands;
  - lifetime spend bands;
  - average basket bands;
  - last purchase recency bands;
  - products / product categories (via line-item facts);
  - site of prior purchases.
- Visit window (default 12h) operator-controllable per parent
  design §6.4.4.
- Add summary strip + facet counts per parent §6.5.
- Data-quality chips: unmatched scans, missing geocode,
  low-confidence matches.
- CSV export of current filter view; raw VeriScan payload
  **excluded** by default per parent §13.
- Definitions tooltip on every purchase metric.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C2`.

### C3 — Customers IA + CRM/Segments move

- New top-level Customers nav with children Check-ins, Map, CRM,
  Segments per parent §4.1.
- Move existing CRM page to `/admin/customers/crm`.
- Move existing Segments page to `/admin/customers/segments`.
- Add backwards-compatible aliases for old CRM/Segments routes per
  parent §4.2; query params must be preserved.
- No functional change to CRM or Segments behaviour; this is IA only.
- Consistent CustomersLayout / breadcrumbs across the four pages.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C3`.

### C4 — Static customer-origin map

- Route `/admin/customers/map` per parent §7.
- MapLibre GL; default NYC-focused viewport; site pins for `bx`
  and `mh` from site metadata (add if not present).
- Server endpoint `GET /api/admin/customers/map` per parent §7.4;
  reference SQL shape in parent §7.5; default `origin=id_address`,
  `agg=grid`, `grid=250m`.
- Server coarsens grid / warns when payload would exceed budget
  (parent §11 perf budgets).
- Shared filters with Check-ins (date, site, purchase history,
  conversion, document/age).
- Encoding panel (Vega-Lite-style) per parent §8.3 with channels
  `color`, `size`, `opacity`, `strokeColor`, `strokeWidth`; always-
  visible legend; colorblind-safe defaults; default preset
  "purchase-repeat-basket" per parent §8.2; encoding config
  serialised in URL state.
- Marker click → inspect drawer with aggregate metrics +
  representative scan IDs + "open matching Check-ins" deep link
  carrying the equivalent filter set.
- No exact home-address pin display by default; exact-point mode
  is gated per parent §7.3 and §13.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C4`.

### C5 — Replay playback

- New endpoint `GET /api/admin/customers/map/timeline` per parent
  §9.3; finite bucketed event series (NOT streaming) per parent
  §9.1; default bucket size per parent §9.4; server coarsens to
  meet feature-count budget (parent §11).
- Playback URL state (`bucket`, `play`, `speed`, `lifetime`,
  `fade`, `loop`, `tail`, `enc`, `viewport`) per parent §9.2;
  share URL restores the full replay configuration.
- Client lifetime/fade math per parent §9.5; default loop behaviour
  `tail=clear` per parent §9.6; small visual pause at reset.
- Controls per parent §9.7: play/pause, scrubber + current
  timestamp, speed/lifetime/fade selectors, loop toggle, reset,
  "open current frame in Check-ins" action.
- Marker rendering uses MapLibre/WebGL layers (NOT thousands of
  DOM markers) so we hit the 30–60fps target on real data
  volumes.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` → loads paused, controls remain
  available; tabular "events in current frame" fallback.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C5`.

### C6 — DEFERRED to separate paused issue

C6 (MP4 export of the replay) is **NOT** in this child epic. It is
filed as a separate paused issue in this repo titled "Customers UX
v2: export customer-origin replay to MP4". That issue is paused on
creation and only un-pauses after C5 lands and the operator
explicitly asks for it. Do not start C6 work as part of this epic.

## Out of scope

- VeriScan webhook ingestion + `visitor_scans` table + backfill CLI
  + ingestion admin page — owned by the sibling
  [`./EPIC_PLAN.md`](./EPIC_PLAN.md) child epic.
- agenix / nginx / systemd / DNS changes — `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`.
- Customer-facing UI of any kind. Helios is operator-only.
- Edit / delete of `visitor_scans`. Append-only ground truth.
- External geocoding / reverse-geocoding.
- Marketing automation, campaign sending, loyalty mutation,
  segment-membership mutation.
- Websocket / Kafka / event-bus realtime architecture.
- MP4 export (C6 — separate paused issue).

## Data-model coordination with the ingestion child epic

The Customers UX needs the following from `visitor_scans` (parent
design §14). Most are already present in the ingestion design; the
items below are coordination points to confirm with the sibling
ingestion epic before C2 lands:

1. Canonical `checked_in_at` — either a normalized column added by
   ingestion or the documented `COALESCE(scanned_at, created_at,
   ingested_at)` contract + matching index per parent §11.
2. `issuing_state` distinct from address `state` (operator
   explicitly listed this as a filter facet).
3. Raw normalized columns for `phone`, `email`, `first_name`,
   `last_name`, `birth_date` for the match layer.
4. Coordinate validity surfacing (zero/null guarded out of the map).
5. Per-row `site_slug` correctness for backfilled rows.
6. Site metadata (display name, store lat/lon, timezone, address)
   reused or added for the map's site pins and distance-from-site
   filter.

If any of these is missing when C2 / C4 start, file a focused
change request against the ingestion child epic before proceeding.

## Phase dependencies

- C1 depends on the ingestion child epic's A1 having landed (table
  + at least one row from webhook or backfill). C1 code can be
  written and unit-tested against the schema in parallel; the
  page-back trigger requires a real live row.
- C2 depends on C1 (shared endpoint + drawer) and on
  CRM/orders being readable from helios-server (already true; the
  existing CRM page reads it).
- C3 depends on C2's CRM/Segments not being broken by the
  move; can land in parallel with C2 if the routes are wired
  carefully.
- C4 depends on C2's match layer + facts views (for purchase
  encodings) and on coordinate-validity guards in `visitor_scans`.
- C5 depends on C4.
- C6 is deferred; do not start.

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. C1..C5 each have at least one commit on `automation` master
   carrying `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9` and the matching
   `Phase: C<n>` trailer.
2. The C1 page-back STATUS comment has been posted on
   [#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9) and the
   operator has confirmed live visibility.
3. At least one live VeriScan check-in is visible end-to-end:
   webhook → row → Check-ins table → matched customer →
   purchase summary → map marker → replay frame.
4. C6 has been filed as a separate paused issue in this repo and
   linked from the C5 completion comment.
