# Helios `/metrics` v1.3 rework — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
> for the v1.3 iteration. Authoritative design:
> [`docs/epics/business-metrics/EPIC_PLAN_v1_3_REWORK.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN_v1_3_REWORK.md)
> in the top-level repo. Oracle-approved design thread:
> [T-019e654a-8d2f-74fb-9734-3588f512d8a2](https://ampcode.com/threads/T-019e654a-8d2f-74fb-9734-3588f512d8a2).
>
> The v1 child epic is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#21`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21)
> (closed); the v1.1 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#28`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/28)
> (closed); the v1.2 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#30`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/30)
> (closed). This issue tracks the v1.3 rework only — please do
> not reopen the v1 / v1.1 / v1.2 children.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation` master that
> satisfies any part of this rework MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: V3<n>`
> trailer (e.g. `Phase: V3'3`) — distinct from v1's `P<n>`,
> v1.1's `R<n>`, and v1.2's `V2<n>` — so per-phase progress
> comments on the parent issue are visually grouped per rework
> iteration.

## Scope owned by this repo

v1.3 lands the **Budtender Performance** tab at
`/metrics/budtenders` per the parent addendum:

1. `/metrics` top-level tab strip (Dashboard | Budtenders) +
   sibling-route shell at `/metrics/budtenders` with sticky
   Core / Advanced sub-tab strip.
2. Core sub-tab panels backed by real data:
   leaderboard, daily cashier-attributed sales trend,
   customer / fulfillment / payment mix, shift productivity,
   dollar-basket upsell lift (same-customer + similar-customer).
3. Advanced sub-tab one-dot-per-cashier scatter with
   axis / color / size / opacity switchers, peer-percentile
   encoding, highlight-subset search, optional quadrant
   reference lines.
4. MISSING DATA cards for the four (five, including basket-
   quantity upsell) operator-asked-for metrics that have no
   real data path today.
5. Consolidated `/api/budtender-analytics` endpoint behind a
   single CTE-chained prepared statement; supporting indexes;
   `compareTo=peer-cohort` extension.
6. Perf measurement, runbook refresh, validation evidence,
   oracle review pass, parent closure package.

Re-read the parent addendum before starting any phase. This
child plan is intentionally a thin index over the parent.

### V3'0 — Scope freeze + route shell + canonical update

- Re-confirm the v1.3-in-scope panel set against the canonical
  v1.2 list (Budtender panels are additive — no headline-
  dashboard panel is removed).
- Extend `MetricDef` types (additive):
  - `area?: 'dashboard' | 'budtenders'` discriminator
    (defaults to `'dashboard'`).
  - `supports.peerCohort?: boolean` (Budtender metrics
    declare `true`; headline metrics unchanged).
  - `blockedBy?: { ingestIssue?: string; column?: string;
    note: string }` on MISSING DATA registry entries.
- `/metrics` top-level tab strip: add a small tab strip below
  the controls bar with "Dashboard" (default; preserves the
  v1.2 entry URL) and "Budtenders" (routes to
  `/metrics/budtenders`). Sticky across scroll like the
  controls bar.
- `/metrics/budtenders` route shell:
  - Page header band with title + coverage badge placeholder
    (wired with live data in V3'1).
  - Sticky "Core | Advanced" sub-tab strip under the global
    controls bar.
  - Empty grid containers for Core (responsive 1/2/3 cols)
    and Advanced (single full-width).
  - Sub-tab choice persists in URL
    (`?sub=core` / `?sub=advanced`).
- Backend skeleton: `GET /api/budtender-analytics` returning a
  well-typed empty payload (`cashier_rows: []`,
  `daily_trend: []`, etc.) with `meta.sources` already
  populated correctly. The CTE chain is added in V3'1 / V3'3.
- Refresh `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics-v1_2-canonical.md` to a
  `…-v1_3-canonical.md` superset that adds an "area" column
  and the `supports.peerCohort` / `blockedBy` columns; update
  the runbook anchor on the parent issue's body.

**Exit criteria**: top-level tab strip renders on `/metrics`;
`/metrics/budtenders` route loads with Core / Advanced empty
grids; the backend endpoint returns a well-typed empty payload;
canonical metric list refreshed; `MetricDef` types extended
(no behavioural change yet).

### V3'1 — Core P0: Leaderboard + Daily Cashier-Attributed Sales Trend

- Backend: first cut of `/api/budtender-analytics` CTE chain
  covering `orders`, `cashier_agg`, and a per-day rollup feeding
  `daily_trend`. Filters honour the global controls (sites,
  range, agg for the trend). Excludes `cashier_user_id IS NULL`
  from `cashier_agg`; surfaces the same count under
  `meta.coverage.unattributed_transactions`. Implemented as a
  single prepared statement to minimise round-trip overhead.
- Frontend:
  - **Budtender Leaderboard** panel: sortable, paginated table
    of cashier rows; default sort `sales desc`. Inline
    horizontal bars per numeric cell; cell colour driven by
    peer-cohort percentile within the visible window; low-n
    rows (`transactions < 20` OR `shift_coverage_minutes <
    120`) dimmed with a "low n" chip. Pagination state lives
    in the URL.
  - **Daily Cashier-Attributed Sales Trend** panel: time
    series in the v1.2 `<MetricChart/>`. Primary = daily
    sales; togglable secondary series = transactions, AOV,
    discount fraction. `cashier_user_id IS NULL` daily totals
    render as a dimmed reference-style series. Tile-level
    annotation pip + hover popover from v1.2 R'5 reused.
  - Unattributed-transactions warning chip in the Leaderboard
    panel header.
- Per-row click on the Leaderboard in v1.3 emits a "single-
  cashier detail view forthcoming" toast and pre-fills
  `highlight=<cashier_id>` for the Advanced sub-tab.

**Exit criteria**: leaderboard + daily trend render with real
production data on `/metrics/budtenders?sub=core`; peer-
percentile colour coding visible; low-n dimming visible on
known-low-volume cashiers; unattributed-transactions chip
appears when `IS NULL` rows exist in the window.

### V3'2 — Core P1: Mix + Shift Productivity

- Extend the consolidated endpoint with the `shift_agg` CTE
  (`sweed_shifts ⋈ orders` on `(dealer_id, employee_id,
  pay_time BETWEEN shift_open_at AND shift_close_at)`) and the
  three mix breakdowns under `mix.customer_segment`,
  `mix.fulfillment`, `mix.payment`.
- Frontend:
  - **Customer / Fulfillment / Payment Mix** cards: three
    stacked percentage bar charts. Per-card toggle switches
    denominator between transactions and sales. Fleet-level
    by default; re-scope to a selected cashier (URL-persisted)
    via overlay over the fleet baseline.
  - **Shift Productivity** card: scatter or ranked bar of
    `transactions / shift_hour`. If
    `shift_agg.coverage_pct < 0.4` on the visible window,
    render the panel as a MISSING DATA card with explicit
    "shift attribution coverage too low" copy + a link to
    the shifts-ingest follow-on issue (see V3'5 for the
    `blockedBy` registry shape).

**Exit criteria**: mix cards render at fleet and per-cashier
levels; overlay-on-leaderboard-select works URL-persistently;
shift productivity card either renders real data or falls
through to a MISSING DATA card with honest copy.

### V3'3 — Core P1: Dollar-Basket Upsell Lift + `compareTo=peer-cohort`

- Extend the consolidated endpoint with the `baseline_lift`
  CTE:
  - Per-order `same_customer_baseline` = leave-one-out average
    of that customer's order totals in the window (filtered to
    known, non-guest, `count >= 2`).
  - Per-order `similar_customer_baseline` = leave-one-out
    average over cohort
    `(guest_flag, first_time_flag, fulfillment_type,
    payment_method)`.
  - Per-cashier rollup is the mean of per-order
    `(order_total - baseline)` with explicit sample-size
    counts.
- Frontend:
  - **Dollar-Basket Upsell Lift** card: diverging horizontal
    bars; toggle in header switches mode between
    `same-customer` and `similar-customer`. Sample-size chip
    per cashier; low-n dimming consistent with leaderboard.
    Colour driven by `desirableDirection: 'up'`.
- `compareTo=peer-cohort` API extension:
  - The Daily Cashier-Attributed Sales Trend panel adopts
    `peer-cohort` as its default `compareTo`.
  - The reference data is the peer-cohort P25 / median / P75
    aggregated within the visible window. Renders as a faint
    band (P25..P75) with the median as a dashed line.
  - Per-panel toggle still offers `prior-period` / `year-over-
    year` / `peer-cohort` / `off`; existing headline panels
    are unchanged.
- V3'0 guardrail tightens: any metric with `area:
  'budtenders'` MUST declare `supports.peerCohort: true`.

**Exit criteria**: dollar-basket lift card renders both modes
on real data; per-cashier sample-size chips and low-n dimming
visible; peer-cohort band renders on the Daily Trend; per-
panel `compareTo` toggle works; guardrail in enforcement.

### V3'4 — Advanced sub-tab: one-dot-per-cashier scatter

- Adapt the v1.2 catalog-style scatter renderer to plot one
  dot per cashier (data source = `cashier_rows` from the
  consolidated endpoint; no extra HTTP).
- **Axis pickers** (X + Y, independent): expose 15+ fields
  per the parent addendum's enumeration, including
  peer-percentile-suffixed (`__pct`) variants computed
  client-side from `cashier_rows`.
- **Color encoding picker** with sensible per-field defaults:
  - Diverging red→gray→green for signed-lift fields.
  - Diverging blue→gray→red for `discount_pct`.
  - Sequential low→high for everything else.
  - "Match X axis" / "Match Y axis" one-click shortcuts.
- **Size encoding picker**: sqrt-scaled by `transactions`
  (default), `sales`, `unique_customers`, or
  `shift_coverage_minutes`.
- **Opacity / confidence**: auto-dim per the rules in the
  parent addendum (lift axes < 10 samples; shift-productivity
  axes < 120 min; volume axes < 20 transactions). Combination
  dimming does not stack below 0.3.
- **Highlight subset**: text input filters by cashier name /
  id / status suffix; matching dots render on top with 2 px
  stroke + label; non-matching dots fade to 0.2 opacity;
  empty input = no highlight. Pre-fills from Leaderboard
  row-click (`?highlight=<cashier_id>`).
- **Reference lines / quadrants** (optional, off by default):
  axis median + P75 lines with quadrant labels.
- **Default first paint**: `X=transactions_per_shift_hour`,
  `Y=aov`, `Color=same_customer_lift`, `Size=transactions`.
- Keyboard: axis pickers reachable via Tab; highlight input
  focusable; quadrant toggle reachable; Escape clears
  highlight.

**Exit criteria**: Advanced scatter renders one-dot-per-cashier
with default encodings on first paint; all pickers work;
highlight-subset filters; pre-fill via `?highlight=` works
from the Leaderboard row-click handoff.

### V3'5 — MISSING DATA cards + summary chip

- Wire `blockedBy` registry entries for the five known-
  missing Budtender metrics:
  1. Product Subset Comparison & Category/Subcategory
     Distribution by Cashier (blocked by line-items ingest).
  2. Returns / Refunds Distribution by Cashier (blocked by
     `sweed_returns` ingest with cashier attribution).
  3. Cashier-Attributed Customer Reviews (blocked by
     invoice → review linkage in `review_submissions`).
  4. Shift Cash +/- (Drawer Reconciliation) (blocked by
     drawer-close actuals).
  5. Basket-Quantity Upsell (blocked by line-items ingest;
     dollar lift shipped in V3'3 as the v1.3 substitute).
- For each, register a MISSING DATA registry entry with:
  - Panel header copy describing what the panel would show.
  - "What's blocked / why / next step" body section with a
    link to the tracking ingest issue on the peer repo if
    one exists, or a "file ingest issue" helper that
    prefills the title + body.
- **MISSING DATA summary chip** at the top of the Core
  sub-tab: "N panels missing data: …" — clicking expands to a
  short list of blocked panels with their ingest links. Chip
  is hidden when N = 0.
- **CI guardrail extension**: extend v1.1 R0's stub-leak
  test to assert no `dataStatus: 'pending'` card on the
  Budtender sub-route ever renders with non-empty `series` —
  catches a future regression where stub data sneaks into a
  MISSING DATA card.

**Exit criteria**: five MISSING DATA cards render in the Core
grid with honest copy + ingest links; summary chip renders
when N > 0; guardrail green.

### V3'6 — Indexes + perf + closure package

- Land four `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` indexes on
  `vps-nixos-3` production DB:
  - `sweed_orders (dealer_id, pay_time)`
  - `sweed_orders (cashier_user_id, pay_time)`
  - `sweed_orders (customer_id, pay_time)` (verify presence
    from v1.1; create only if missing).
  - `sweed_shifts (dealer_id, employee_id, shift_open_at,
    shift_close_at)`
- Perf measurement of `/api/budtender-analytics`:
  - Capture `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` for the consolidated query on
    typical windows (1d / 7d / 28d / 12wk).
  - Endpoint timing (P50 / P95 cold / P95 warm).
  - Targets: P50 < 500 ms warm, P95 < 1.2 s cold on a 4-week
    window across all sites.
- Runbook refresh: `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md` extended
  with the v1.3 surface (Budtender sub-route, sub-tab
  semantics, `compareTo=peer-cohort`, `area` discriminator,
  `blockedBy` registry, MISSING DATA summary chip).
- Validation evidence committed under the runbook:
  - Leaderboard screenshot with peer-percentile colour coding.
  - Daily Trend screenshot with peer-cohort band rendered.
  - Mix cards in fleet mode and per-cashier overlay mode.
  - Shift Productivity card (real-data mode) + the MISSING
    DATA fallback shape (separate screenshot).
  - Dollar-basket lift card in both modes.
  - Advanced scatter at default first paint.
  - Advanced scatter at a non-default
    `(X, Y, color, size, highlight)` configuration.
  - Each of the five MISSING DATA cards.
  - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` + endpoint timing table.
- Oracle review pass: re-run an oracle review on
  `/metrics/budtenders` Core + Advanced + each MISSING DATA
  card. Capture the oracle's "fit for purpose — world class for
  this operator's stated needs?" verdict. If the oracle flags
  new gaps, address them in this phase before the closure
  commit, or file an explicit follow-on epic and call it out
  in the closure package.
- Closure package: a single comment on
  [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
  containing the live URL
  (`https://helios.freshlybaked.us/metrics/budtenders`), the
  V3'0–V3'6 per-phase commit table, the AC §1–9 sign-off
  (with one-line evidence per criterion), the refreshed
  canonical Budtender metric list, the validation evidence,
  and the oracle note. The close commit MUST carry
  `Closes-Epic: #7` per #8's policy so
  `close-completed-issues.yml` closes the issue.

**Exit criteria**: parent can close based on evidence, not
trust; v1.3 AC §1–9 demonstrably hold on production; v1.1
AC §1–10 and v1.2 AC §1–8 continue to hold (no regressions);
oracle confirms `/metrics/budtenders` is fit for the
operator's stated "world-class budtender performance
dashboard" purpose.

## Cross-repo dependencies

None hard. The five MISSING DATA cards represent ingest
dependencies that are *acknowledged* as out-of-v1.3-scope.
Each card carries a `blockedBy.ingestIssue` link to a peer-
repo ingest issue (file new ones if they don't exist; e.g.
`sweed_order_line_items` ingest, `sweed_returns` ingest,
review-invoice-linkage, drawer-close-actuals ingest). v1.3 does
not block on any of these landing — the MISSING DATA cards are
the deliverable for the unblocked-data path.

When an ingest unblocks in a future iteration (v1.4+), each
MISSING DATA registry entry's panel can be promoted to a real
panel in a follow-on epic. v1.3 just leaves the slots ready
and visible.

## Acceptance criteria (delegated from parent)

The full v1.3 acceptance criteria live in the parent rework
addendum §"Refreshed acceptance criteria". Reproduced here as
a checklist for the V3'6 owner:

- [ ] (1) `/metrics/budtenders` reachable via top-level tab
      strip on `/metrics`; sub-tab + highlight selection
      persist in URL; share-link reproduces.
- [ ] (2) Core P0: Leaderboard + Daily Trend land with real
      data; peer-percentile colouring; low-n dimming;
      unattributed-transactions chip.
- [ ] (3) Core P1: Mix + Shift Productivity + Upsell Lift
      land with real data (or honest MISSING DATA fallback
      for Shift Productivity at < 40% coverage); overlay-on-
      leaderboard-select works.
- [ ] (4) Advanced sub-tab one-dot-per-cashier scatter with
      all axis / color / size / opacity / highlight pickers;
      default first paint per spec.
- [ ] (5) Five MISSING DATA cards render with "what / why /
      next step" copy + ingest links; summary chip; CI
      guardrail green.
- [ ] (6) Consolidated `/api/budtender-analytics` + four
      `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` indexes; perf targets met
      (P50 < 500 ms warm; P95 < 1.2 s cold on 4-week window).
- [ ] (7) `compareTo=peer-cohort` extension works; default on
      Budtender Daily Trend; per-panel toggle still functional;
      headline panels unchanged.
- [ ] (8) v1.1 AC §1–10 and v1.2 AC §1–8 continue to hold on
      production; no regressions.
- [ ] (9) Oracle-approved closure evidence package — live URL,
      commit table, screenshots, perf table, canonical
      Budtender metric list, oracle note; close commit
      carries `Closes-Epic: #7`.

issues.body:
## Context

Issue #15 shipped the canonical product-review row on `/catalog/review`, and we explicitly said "all future review surfaces (purchases, repricing, market-data matches, promos) can render the same row." But `/catalog/pending-purchases` (PendingPurchasesPage.tsx) was built before that landed and:

- Has its own bespoke `PendingPurchaseRowCard` (1300+ line route file) that does NOT reuse `ReviewLineItemCard` or any shared canonical row.
- Only lets the reviewer override price / description / image / notes — not the **structured data** (brand, group name, category, subcategory, size, packCount, variantTab, strainName), which is exactly where the LLM teacher most often misclassifies.
- Doesn't collapse a row after approve/reject — the reviewer keeps scrolling past large finished cards.
- Doesn't render in the standard "product view collapseable hierarchy" the way other catalog surfaces do.

## Required outcome

1. **Editable structured-data overrides on every pending-purchase row.** The reviewer must be able to fix any misclassified field inline (e.g. "Blueberry Indica" → "Blueberry" + strain=Indica; "Distillate Peach" → "Peach"; variantTab "Indica" → "1g"; pack-size / unit-size / subcategory). These overrides flow through to the apply path the same way price/description overrides do today.
   - Persist as JSONB column `edited_structured_fields jsonb` on `pending_purchase_rows` (more flexible than 9 new typed columns; per-field nullability).
   - `PATCH /api/catalog/pending-purchases/:rowId` accepts `editedStructuredFields: Partial<{ targetBrand, targetGroupName, expectedCategory, expectedSubcategory, targetSize, targetPackCount, targetVariantName, targetVariantTab, targetStrainName }>`.
   - `applyPendingPurchaseRequestJob` reads the overridden field via a single `effectiveStructuredFields` helper (mirrors `effective_proposed_price` / `effective_proposed_description`).
   - Pre-populate the edit controls with the current LLM/parser values so the reviewer is editing structured data, not blank inputs.

2. **Collapse-on-decision.** Once a reviewer hits approve / reject on a row, the card collapses to a one-line summary (status pill + brand · variant · price). Reopening the row is a single click. Reviewer should be able to glide down 50 finished decisions in one viewport.

3. **Hierarchical grouping per the standard product view.** Group rows by `(brand × category × subcategory × size)` family, identical to `/catalog/review`'s family panels (issue #15) — header with brand chip + family identity + family-level approve/reject + collapse, then one canonical row per family member. Replace the current site → category → brand → variant nesting that doesn't match other catalog surfaces.

4. **Reuse the canonical row component.** Extract `/catalog/review`'s `ReviewLineItemCard` (and its sub-components: `CanonicalPricingLadder`, before/after structured comparator, override panel) into a shared `client/components/canonicalProductRow/` module. Both `/catalog/review` and `/catalog/pending-purchases` import the same row. Future review surfaces (repricing, market-data, promos) import it too.

## Out of scope

- Re-running the LLM teacher (operator can re-trigger generation; this issue is about reviewer-side fixes).
- Sweed catalog mutations beyond what `applyPendingPurchaseRequestJob` already does — overrides just change what gets written, not the apply mechanism.
- The general 'product catalog edit row' redesign for other pages (e.g. /catalog/browser); only the canonical row reuse on /catalog/pending-purchases is required here.

## Related

- #15 — canonical product-review row (the implementation to reuse)
- #5 — unified catalog update engine
- Most recent feedback thread (parser fixes for Mega Ring 'Distillate Peach', variantTab 'Indica', AIO subcategory, TTM Flight: shipped in commit e21b095 — the structured-data editor is the reviewer-side complement to that worker-side cleanup).

issues.body:
# Helios `/metrics` v1.4 rework — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
> for the v1.4 iteration. Authoritative design:
> [`docs/epics/business-metrics/EPIC_PLAN_v1_4_REWORK.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN_v1_4_REWORK.md)
> in the top-level repo.
>
> The v1 child epic is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#21`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21)
> (closed); the v1.1 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#28`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/28)
> (closed); the v1.2 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#30`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/30)
> (closed); the v1.3 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#34`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/34)
> (closed). This issue tracks the v1.4 rework only — please do
> not reopen the v1 / v1.1 / v1.2 / v1.3 children.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation` master that
> satisfies any part of this rework MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: V4<n>`
> trailer (e.g. `Phase: V4'3`) — distinct from v1's `P<n>`,
> v1.1's `R<n>`, v1.2's `V2<n>`, and v1.3's `V3<n>` — so per-
> phase progress comments on the parent issue are visually
> grouped per rework iteration.

## Scope owned by this repo

v1.4 picks up the five-item operator wishlist from the
[v1.3-slice status comment on top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7#issuecomment-4570305082):

1. Scatter chart light-grey dashed gridlines (parity with
   `MetricChart`).
2. Margin-$ basis on the four mandatory LTV histograms (on
   `/metrics/customer-value`) backed by a new per-invoice
   `sweed_order_margin_mv` materialized view.
3. Cohort retention curve panel + first-to-second conversion
   rate sparkline on `/metrics/customer-value`.
4. Click-to-drill on every histogram bucket and every scatter
   dot (Budtender Advanced + catalog analytics + Customer
   Value histograms).
5. VeriScan link coverage badge + disabled "Show only
   VeriScan-linked customers" toggle on the Customer Value
   tab header (full functionality gated on coverage threshold
   — v1.4.1).

All five are refinements of already-shipped tabs / panels.
v1.4 introduces **no new top-level tabs**, **no new
sub-routes**, and **one new materialized view**
(`sweed_order_margin_mv`).

Re-read the parent addendum before starting any phase. This
child plan is intentionally a thin index over the parent.

### V4'0 — Scope freeze + helper extraction + endpoint decisions

- Re-confirm the v1.4-in-scope panel set against the
  v1.3-slice canonical list (no Budtender or headline-grid
  panel is removed; the only registry change is the planned
  removal of two MISSING DATA cards on Customer Value when
  V4'2 / V4'3 promote their content).
- Extract a `niceXTicks(min, max, opts)` helper alongside the
  existing `niceYTicks` in
  `helios/src/client/routes/metrics/gridlines.ts`. Same
  `{1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10} × 10^k` ladder; same
  `stepFractionDigits` discipline (regression-guarded for the
  `2.5` / `0.25` / `0.025` cases per v1.2 R5 oracle review).
  No visual behaviour change in V4'0 — this is just the helper.
- Extend `MetricDef` types (additive):
  - `supports.drillSelection?: ('histogramBucket' |
    'scatterDot')[]`.
- Decision: retention payload placement.
  - Default: extend the existing consolidated
    `/api/customer-value-analytics` endpoint with an
    `?include=retention` query-param toggle that adds
    `cohort_retention[]` and `first_second_conversion[]` to
    the payload. Existing callers don't pay the cost.
  - Alternative (only if measurement shows > 1.5 s P95 cold
    with `?include=retention`): a sibling
    `/api/customer-retention` endpoint, separately cached.
  - Decision recorded in the V4'0 commit message and in
    `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md`.
- Decision: `sweed_order_margin_mv` refresh cadence.
  - Default: incremental refresh by the existing helios
    refresh job on the same cadence as other materialized
    views.
  - Alternative: per-trigger on `sweed_orders` insert (only
    if measurement shows the helios refresh job's cadence
    introduces > 1h staleness on the margin-$ histograms).
  - Decision recorded in the V4'0 commit message and in
    `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md`.

**Exit criteria**: `niceXTicks` extracted and unit-tested
(with the 2.5 / 0.25 / 0.025 regression cases);
`MetricDef.supports.drillSelection` typed in shared types;
retention-payload-placement and MV-refresh-cadence decisions
recorded; canonical metric list refreshed (notes the planned
v1.4 changes — actual registry edits land in V4'2 / V4'3).

### V4'1 — Scatter chart gridlines

- Wire `niceXTicks` + `niceYTicks` into the scatter renderer
  used on:
  - `/metrics/budtenders?sub=advanced` (the one-dot-per-
    cashier scatter from v1.3 V3'4).
  - Any catalog-analytics-style scatter on the v1.2-shipped
    catalog analytics tab.
- Visual treatment: 1px dashed light-grey (`stroke="currentColor"
  opacity="0.12" stroke-dasharray="4 4"`) lines at each nice
  tick, drawn **under** the dot cloud and **under** any
  reference / quadrant lines.
- Axis label formatting honours the axis's declared kind. New
  helper: `formatAxisValue(value, kind)` in `gridlines.ts`,
  covering `$ / int / pct / ratio / minutes`. Each kind has a
  unit test asserting the expected formatting.
- CI guardrail: extend the v1.2 R5 `niceYTicks` test that
  asserts "least-significant digit in {0, 2, 5}" for the 2.5 /
  0.25 / 0.025 cases to also assert it for `niceXTicks`.
- Verify on phone (operator wishlist note) — the V4'1
  validation evidence captures a screenshot from a 412px-
  wide mobile viewport showing the scatter with gridlines
  rendered correctly (no label collision; gridline density
  scales down).

**Exit criteria**: both scatter renderers show gridlines
matching the time-series chart visual treatment on desktop
**and** mobile; reference / quadrant lines remain on top of
gridlines; CI guardrail green; mobile screenshot in the V4'1
PR.

### V4'2 — `sweed_order_margin_mv` + Margin-$ basis on LTV histograms

- Add `sweed_order_margin_mv` materialized view to the helios
  warehouse:
  - PK `(dealer_id, invoice_id)`.
  - Columns `(customer_id, pay_time, gross_margin)`.
  - Source:
    `sweed_orders so
       JOIN sweed_order_line_items oli USING (dealer_id, invoice_id)
       JOIN product_cost_history pch ON (pch.dealer_id, pch.product_id, pch.effective_at_or_before(oli.created_at))`.
  - Gross margin = `oli.line_revenue - oli.line_quantity *
    pch.unit_cost`, summed per invoice.
  - `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` is acceptable
    (PK is unique). Refreshed by the existing helios refresh
    job.
- Acknowledged dependency: line-items ingest must be live
  on production (v1.3-slice `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#22`
  or its successor). If line-items ingest is **not** live at
  V4'2 start, **do not stub margins** — flip V4'2 into a
  blocked-on-ingest state, file the unblock issue, and skip
  to V4'3 / V4'4 / V4'5 / V4'6 (V4'2 then ships as a separate
  follow-on commit once ingest lands).
- Extend `/api/customer-value-analytics`:
  - Each per-purchase-ordinal row gains `margin: number |
    null`.
  - The basis selector accepts `gross_margin` as a fourth
    option (`gross_sales`, `net_sales`, `gross_receipts`,
    `gross_margin`).
- Frontend:
  - The basis selector dropdown on `/metrics/customer-value`
    gains the "Gross Margin" option.
  - All four mandatory histograms re-render under the new
    basis with no re-fetch (selection toggles a client-side
    field projection over the already-loaded rows).
  - The MISSING DATA card "Lifetime margin $ histograms" is
    removed from the registry; the registry test from v1.1 R0
    is updated to reflect the new MISSING DATA card count.
- Runbook: document `sweed_order_margin_mv` schema, refresh
  cadence, and the line-items-ingest dependency. Note the
  rollback procedure (drop the MV; revert the basis selector
  to three options; restore the MISSING DATA card).

**Exit criteria**: `sweed_order_margin_mv` lives in production;
margin-$ basis is selectable on every LTV histogram; the
"Lifetime margin $ histograms" MISSING DATA card is gone;
runbook updated; rollback procedure documented.

### V4'3 — Cohort retention + first-to-second conversion

- Extend the consolidated endpoint with the `cohort_retention`
  and `first_second_conversion` CTEs:
  - Cohort = `date_trunc('week', first_purchase_at)` (default)
    or `date_trunc('month', first_purchase_at)` (selector).
  - Retention row per `(cohort_key, weeks_since_acquisition)`
    or `(cohort_key, months_since_acquisition)`:
    `retained_count / cohort_size`.
  - First-to-second-conversion row per `cohort_key`:
    `customers_with_second_purchase_ever / cohort_size`, with
    parallel `_within_30d`, `_within_60d`, `_within_90d`
    fields.
  - Query honours the v1.3-slice cohort scope control (all-
    known / active-in-range / acquired-in-range).
- Gated behind the `?include=retention` query-param toggle
  decided in V4'0.
- Frontend:
  - **Cohort retention curve** panel: time-series-like chart
    with cohort lines. Most recent cohort = most opaque; older
    cohorts fade. Max 12 cohorts visible by default; "show
    all" toggle in the panel header. Hover-readout shows
    cohort + weeks-since-acquisition + retention %.
  - **First-to-second conversion sparkline** panel: small
    inline bar chart, one bar per cohort. Hover shows the
    cohort plus all four conversion fields (`ever`, `30d`,
    `60d`, `90d`).
- The MISSING DATA card "Cohort retention curves" is removed
  from the registry; registry test updated.

**Exit criteria**: retention curve + conversion sparkline
render real data on `/metrics/customer-value`; cohort-scope
control honoured; max-12 default + "show all" works; the
"Cohort retention curves" MISSING DATA card is gone.

### V4'4 — Histogram / scatter drill-clicks

- Extend the v1.2 `/rows` endpoint to accept an optional
  `selection` query param (JSON-encoded `{ kind, …meta }`):
  - `{ kind: 'histogramBucket', metricId, bucketKey }`:
    rows-WHERE-clause restricts to rows in that bucket.
  - `{ kind: 'scatterDot', cashierId }`: rows-WHERE-clause
    restricts to that cashier's per-day rows.
  - Per-metric implementation in the existing `tableModeFor
    (metric)` switch — additive, not a refactor.
- Frontend:
  - Every histogram bucket on `/metrics/customer-value` and
    every scatter dot on `/metrics/budtenders?sub=advanced`
    (and on the catalog analytics scatter) becomes click-
    handled. Click navigates to the routable detail route
    with `?selection=…` set in the URL.
  - Detail route's Table tab reads the `selection` from the
    URL and passes it to `/rows`; renders the filtered rows.
  - Chart tab on the detail route highlights the selected
    bucket / dot with a 2px stroke + label.
  - Keyboard: every bucket / dot is reachable via Tab (with
    `tabindex="0"`); Enter activates the click; Escape returns
    to the parent tab (focus restored to the original
    clickable).
  - Share-link parity: copy-link from the drilled-down state
    reproduces the selection.
- `MetricDef.supports.drillSelection` declared on every metric
  in scope; metrics without `drillSelection` continue to
  render non-interactive buckets / dots.
- Smoke test: a single Playwright (or equivalent) test that
  drives one click-to-drill flow end-to-end per metric kind
  (one histogram, one scatter).

**Exit criteria**: click-to-drill works on every histogram +
every scatter in scope; URL share-link reproduces; keyboard
parity holds; smoke test green; `supports.drillSelection`
declared on every in-scope metric.

### V4'5 — VeriScan link coverage badge

- Extend `/api/customer-value-analytics` to compute
  `meta.veriscanCoverage: { linked: number, total: number,
  pct: number }` over the visible window, sourced from
  `visitor_scan_links ⋈ sweed_orders` (left-join on
  `customer_id`).
- Frontend:
  - Customer Value tab header renders the badge `N% linked`
    next to the existing coverage / freshness badges.
  - Tooltip text (operator-approved before deploy):
    "X of Y purchases in this window are attributed to a
    VeriScan-known identity. Cohort retention, basket size at
    purchase N, and lifetime $ histograms key off
    `customer_id` from `sweed_orders` and are unaffected.
    VeriScan-keyed views are MISSING DATA until coverage
    crosses the operator-set threshold (today: 25%)."
  - A disabled toggle reads: "Show only VeriScan-linked
    customers (gated on ≥ 25% coverage)". When coverage
    `pct >= 25`, the toggle is enabled but is a no-op in v1.4
    (with an inline note linking to the v1.4.1 follow-on
    issue). The intent is to put the affordance in place
    today.

**Exit criteria**: badge + disabled toggle render on
`/metrics/customer-value` with real data; operator has signed
off on the tooltip text (capture the sign-off in the V4'5 PR);
`meta.veriscanCoverage` is on the consolidated payload.

### V4'6 — Perf + runbook + closure

- Perf measurement:
  - `/api/customer-value-analytics?include=retention` — P50 /
    P95 cold / P95 warm on typical windows (4w / 12w / all-
    time); target P50 < 700 ms warm, P95 < 1.5 s cold.
  - `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY
    sweed_order_margin_mv` — measured wall-clock against
    production; documented in the runbook.
  - `/api/metrics/<id>/rows?selection=…` — sanity-check that
    the new `selection` param doesn't degrade the existing
    `/rows` P50 / P95.
- Runbook refresh: `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md` extended
  with v1.4 surface (scatter gridlines, margin-$ basis,
  cohort retention, first-to-second conversion, drill-click
  selection contract, VeriScan coverage badge,
  `sweed_order_margin_mv` schema + refresh + rollback).
- Validation evidence committed under the runbook:
  - Scatter with gridlines on both Budtender Advanced and the
    catalog analytics scatter (desktop + 412px mobile).
  - Each of the four LTV histograms with `gross_margin`
    basis selected.
  - Cohort retention curve in default (max-12) and "show all"
    modes.
  - First-to-second conversion sparkline with hover open
    showing the 30d / 60d / 90d readouts.
  - Histogram bucket drill landed in the detail Table tab
    (with URL bar visible to evidence share-link parity).
  - Scatter dot drill landed in the cashier-detail Table tab
    (with URL bar visible).
  - VeriScan coverage badge + the disabled toggle.
  - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` + endpoint timing table for the new
    endpoints / params.
- Oracle review pass: re-run an oracle review on the v1.4
  surface (scatter gridlines; margin-$ histograms; retention
  curves; drill-clicks; VeriScan coverage). Capture the
  oracle's "fit for purpose — world-class for this operator's
  stated needs?" verdict. If the oracle flags new gaps,
  address them in this phase before the closure commit, or
  file an explicit follow-on epic and call it out in the
  closure package.
- Closure package: a single comment on
  [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
  containing the live URLs (`https://helios.freshlybaked.us/metrics`,
  `/essentials`, `/customer-value`, `/budtenders`), the
  V4'0–V4'6 per-phase commit table, the AC §1–7 sign-off
  (with one-line evidence per criterion), the refreshed
  canonical metric list (Customer Value tab gains cohort
  retention + first-to-second-conversion entries; four LTV
  histograms gain `bases: [gross_sales, net_sales,
  gross_receipts, gross_margin]`), the validation evidence,
  and the oracle note. The close commit MUST carry
  `Closes-Epic: #7` per #8's policy so
  `close-completed-issues.yml` closes the issue.

**Exit criteria**: parent can close based on evidence, not
trust; v1.4 AC §1–7 demonstrably hold on production; v1.1
AC §1–10, v1.2 AC §1–8, and v1.3 AC §1–9 continue to hold
(no regressions); oracle confirms the v1.4 surface is fit
for the operator's stated "world-class business performance
metrics dashboard" purpose.

## Cross-repo dependencies

- **Line-items ingest** (v1.3-slice issue
  [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#22`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/22)
  or successor) is a hard prerequisite for V4'2

  V4'3 / V4'4 / V4'5 / V4'6 proceed on the rest of the scope.
- **VeriScan link coverage** is not a hard prerequisite — v1.4
  just surfaces the current coverage. v1.4.1 wires the toggle
  to actually filter the histograms; that work is explicitly
  out of v1.4 scope.

## Acceptance criteria (delegated from parent)

The full v1.4 acceptance criteria live in the parent rework
addendum §"Refreshed acceptance criteria". Reproduced here as
a checklist for the V4'6 owner:

- [ ] (1) Scatter charts on Budtender Advanced + catalog

- [ ] (3) Cohort retention curve + first-to-second conversion
      sparkline are live on `/metrics/customer-value` with

- [ ] (4) Click-to-drill works on every histogram bucket +

- [ ] (5) VeriScan link coverage badge renders on

# Agent Canon — `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` child epic

> Parent epic: [virusdave/top-level#10](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/10)
>
> The implementation commit on this repo's master MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10
> ```
>
> That trailer triggers the cross-repo completion flow back to the
> parent issue.

## What this epic does

Rewrites this repo's root `AGENTS.md` to consume **canonical agent
rules** from `virusdave/top-level` instead of duplicating them
locally. The canonical rules are short, imperative, and updated in one
place — so all our repos stay in sync without manual mirroring.

## Step 0 — fetch and read canon BEFORE doing anything

The canonical agent rules live in
`virusdave/top-level : docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md` on `master`. **Read
them first** (and use the same mechanism in your final AGENTS.md
header — see Step 2):

```sh
canon_ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
              /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$canon_ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … internalize the rules — they govern this rewrite …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$canon_ws"
```

Pay particular attention to: ephemeral checkouts for your own work,
the "Canon update interrupt" in §0, the operational-reality §5, and
the §6 contract for what peer `AGENTS.md` must contain.

## Step 1 — ephemeral checkout of THIS repo

```sh
ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
        /home/amp-local/src/automation --label agent-canon)
cd "$ws"
```

Adjust the source path if `automation` lives elsewhere on this host
(`/home/amp-local/src/automation` is the standard).

## Step 2 — rewrite `AGENTS.md` to the pointer model

Open the existing root `AGENTS.md`, audit it for what to keep, then
replace its contents with this exact structure. Fill in the
repo-specific section from your audit.

```markdown
# Agent instructions for `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`

**MANDATORY FIRST READ — agent canon.** Before doing anything in this
repo, fetch and read the latest canonical agent rules:

```sh
ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
        /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … apply the rules …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$ws"
```

That file is authoritative across **all** our repos. Re-read on every
agent session — it changes. If anything in this file conflicts with
canon, **canon wins** — fix the stale prose here.

The rest of this file lists only **automation-specific** instructions.

---

## Repo purpose

<one-paragraph summary: this repo is the Helios codebase + adjacent
ops tooling, deployed to vps-nixos-3>

## Deploy

<the canonical deploy procedure for this repo. Per the operator's
recurring complaint, the canonical mechanic is `self-deploy*` /
`systemctl restart helios-{prep,server,worker}` ONLY via the
documented safe-rollout path — never direct restarts during a serving
deploy. Preserve any nuance the old AGENTS.md had here.>

## Build / test

<repo-specific build & test commands, language versions, etc.>

## Repo-specific task-dag conventions

<if this repo uses task-dag, any conventions specific to it; otherwise
omit this section>

## Host topology / paths

<exact paths agents need on this repo's typical host: source checkout
location, log locations, config paths, service names>
```

## Step 3 — what to KEEP

From the existing AGENTS.md, **keep every operational fact** an agent
needs to work here: exact deploy commands, service names, log paths,
config locations, build/test invocations, architecture diagrams,
repo-specific cross-references, contact info.

## Step 4 — what to DELETE (canon covers it)

Delete and do NOT restate any of:

- "Never SSH to self" / "SSH port" rules
- "Use ephemeral checkout" / "do not edit shared `~/src`" rules
- "Default to `master`, no feature branches" rule
- Bash vs Python / shebang style / typed-code rules
- Performance budgets (UI ≤500ms, DB ≤125ms)
- "Use Oracle / painter / Bedrock LLMs" rules
- Group-writable file rule
- Generic task-dag CLI workflow (the
  `frontier → work → complete → push` loop)
- Generic cross-repo child-epic trailer flow

If you find any of those in the current `AGENTS.md`, **delete** the
prose and rely on canon. If a rule there contradicts canon, canon
wins — flag the conflict in your commit message.

## Step 5 — target size & sanity check

The rewritten file should be **≤ 120 lines**. If it's bigger, you're
probably restating canon — re-audit and trim. If it's much shorter
than the existing file but still has all operational facts, that's
the correct outcome.

Run a final read-through asking: "could a brand-new agent who has
just read canon do real work in this repo using only what's left
here?" If yes, done.

## Step 6 — commit, link, push

```sh
git add AGENTS.md
git commit -m "agents: adopt canon pointer model (Satisfies virusdave/top-level#10)

Replace duplicated cross-repo rules with a mandatory canon-fetch
header per docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md. Repo-specific content
(deploy, paths, services) preserved.

Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10"
git push origin HEAD:<this-repo-default-branch>
```

(Use this repo's default branch — usually `master` or `main`. Do not
open a PR; push directly per the canon working-workflow rule.)

The `Satisfies:` trailer fires the cross-repo completion flow back to
top-level#10.

## Acceptance

- Root `AGENTS.md` opens with the unignorable canon-fetch header.
- Zero duplication of canon content.
- All prior repo-specific operational facts preserved.
- File length ≤ 120 lines.
- Commit includes `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10`.
- Pushed to default branch.

## If you're blocked

- **App not installed / push refused**: stop. Report the exact error
  and your proposed diff to the parent issue
  ([virusdave/top-level#10](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/10)).
- **Repo doesn't have a root `AGENTS.md`**: create one using the same
  template. The acceptance criteria still apply.
- **Existing AGENTS.md has something you don't recognize**: assume
  it's an operator customization and preserve it. When in doubt, ask.

# Time-range nudges + structured highlight selectors across all scatter / time-range surfaces

## Scope

Two related UX upgrades that apply **everywhere the matching conditions occur**, not on a single page. New surfaces added later that match the same patterns should adopt these conventions automatically.

### 1. Time-range nudges

Every page that exposes a time-range picker with the standard preset chips (e.g. `24h / 7d / 30d / 90d / custom`) gains a set of **window-shift** buttons inside the `custom` `<details>` panel:

- `← 1d`, `← 7d`, `← 30d`, `← 90d`
- `1d →`, `7d →`, `30d →`, `90d →`

Semantics (per operator decision 2026-06-02):

- **Slide, don't extend.** The window keeps its current width; clicking `← 7d` moves *both* `from` and `to` earlier by 7 days. Width is preserved across nudges.
- **No future windows.** A forward-nudge that would push `to` past `now` is clamped: the button is disabled (or visually muted with a tooltip explaining "would extend into the future"). Don't silently push `to` to the future.
- **Placement.** Inside the same `<details className="…-range-custom">` panel that already houses the explicit `from` / `to` datetime inputs — not always-visible next to the preset chips.

### 2. Structured highlight selectors on scatter plots

Wherever a scatter page currently exposes a free-text `highlight` input (e.g. `CatalogAnalyticsTab`'s `highlight` query that does substring matching across brand / category / size / SKU / product / pack-count), it MUST also expose a parallel **structured** highlight UI that mirrors the page's filter dimensions.

Layout (per operator decision 2026-06-02):

- Page controls become two stacked sections, **Filters** above and **Highlight** below, on desktop.
- Both sections are collapsible. On desktop: **Filters open by default, Highlight open by default** (one-above-the-other rows). On mobile: **Filters open by default, Highlight collapsed by default** to save vertical space.
- Highlight section exposes the **same dimensions** as the Filters section on that page (e.g. for catalog scatter: category / subcategory / brand / distributor / size / pack-count). No curated narrower subset.
- The free-text input remains and lives inside the Highlight section as one more "dimension".

Highlight semantics:

- Options in each highlight dimension dropdown are **populated from the FILTERED point set**. If filters narrow the page to "Edibles", the Brand highlight chip list only shows brands that have at least one Edibles point on screen.
- A point is "highlighted" iff:
  - For every dimension that has at least one chip selected, the point matches **at least one** of that dimension's chips (OR within a dimension), AND
  - The free-text query (if non-empty) matches the point's haystack (existing substring semantics), AND
  - The two checks combine with **AND across dimensions** — i.e. selecting Brand=Cresco AND Size=1g highlights Cresco 1g specifically.
- If no chips are picked and free-text is empty → no highlight (matches today's behaviour).
- Highlight visual treatment matches the existing "free-text highlight" effect (matching dots full-opacity / thicker ring; non-matching dots dimmed).

Brand- and Distributor-detail-page integration:

- `/metrics/brands/:brandId` and `/metrics/distributors/:distributorName` currently seed the embedded scatter with `highlight=<entity label>` (free text). They MUST be switched to pre-populate the structured **brand chip** (or **distributor chip**) in the Highlight section instead, so the highlight is exact rather than a substring match that could accidentally hit strain names containing the brand.

## Pages in initial scope

Confirmed comprehensive list (per operator 2026-06-02):

**Scatter highlight refresh:**
- `CatalogAnalyticsTab` (`/metrics/catalog`) — primary
- `BudtenderPerformanceTab` advanced scatter sub-tab (`/metrics/staff`)
- `CustomerValueTab` (`/metrics/customer-value`)
- `BrandDetailPage` (`/metrics/brands/:brandId`)
- `DistributorDetailPage` (`/metrics/distributors/:distributorName`)
- Any registry scatter metrics rendered via `MetricChart` that ship a highlight input
- New scatter surfaces added later should adopt the pattern

**Time-range nudges:**
- `MetricsLayoutPage` shared toolbar
- `CatalogAnalyticsTab` range picker
- `BudtenderPerformanceTab` range picker
- `CustomerValueTab` range picker
- Any other time-range picker matching the standard preset-chip pattern

## Non-goals / explicitly out of scope

- Replacing the existing free-text highlight input — it remains in addition to the structured chips.
- Refactoring `CatalogAnalyticsTab` into smaller files. That is a separate tech-debt item.
- Sliding-window crosshair / hover-highlight on **time-series** charts. This epic is about scatter highlight and time-range pickers only.

## Acceptance

- Every confirmed page in scope has time-range nudges in its `custom` `<details>` panel with the correct slide / clamp semantics.
- Every confirmed page in scope has a Filters + Highlight section pair with the structured chips populated from the filtered subset and the AND-across / OR-within semantics.
- The free-text highlight still works on every page that previously had one.
- Brand-detail and distributor-detail pages no longer pass `highlight=<label>` free text to the embedded scatter — they pass a structured brand/distributor chip selection.
- The two changes ship behind no feature flag (UX-only iteration).
- Server endpoints do not need to change; the highlight chips operate purely on the already-fetched filtered point set.

# Helios DB cost reduction — `automation` child epic > Owning child of > [virusdave/top-level#11](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/11). > The authoritative design is > [`docs/epics/helios-db-cost/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in > the top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the > `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (Helios + ingest monorepo) slice of > that design** (which is to say, all of it). > > Every implementation commit landing on `automation@master` that > satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer: > > ``` > Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#11 > ``` > > Phase-tagged commits MUST additionally carry a `Phase:

` > trailer (`A2`, `A3`, `A4`, `A5`, `B2`, `B4`, `C1`, `C2`, `C3`, > `D1`, `D2`, `E1`) so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can > post the per-phase progress comment on the parent issue. ## Scope owned by this repo Everything described in the parent EPIC_PLAN.md, broken out by phase below. Re-read the parent before starting — the section here is a thin index over the parent rather than a re-statement of the design. ## Hard constraint — live customer scans stay real-time This child epic inherits the hard constraint from the parent: the [`/visitors/scans`](https://helios.freshlybaked.us/visitors/scans) page and any other operator-facing "live during a shift" surface MUST keep their near-real-time freshness. If E1 would otherwise throttle one of those pages, the implementer's job is to **change the mechanism** (WebSocket / SSE push, `LISTEN/NOTIFY` fan-out, direct webhook → operator-UI event), not lower its refresh rate. Pages explicitly excluded from any throttle work in E1: - [`helios/src/client/routes/visitors/VisitorScansPage.tsx`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/client/routes/visitors/VisitorScansPage.tsx) — the live-scan operator surface. Existing `setInterval` cadence is 20 s; the E1 implementer MUST replace the polling loop with a push-driven mechanism rather than slow it down. Add any other "during-shift live feedback" page to this list as it's discovered, before throttling it. ## Already shipped (out of scope for this child epic) Commit [`abb0b6f`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/commit/abb0b6f) landed and is deployed on `vps-nixos-3`: - A1 — `sweed_package_snapshots` bulk upsert. - B1 — `loadAllConfigSchedules` in-process cache. - B3 — polynomial empty-poll backoff in the worker lease loop. The phases below are the remaining work. --- ### Phase A2 — `configWorkersStockRefreshJob` bulk upsert Files: `helios/src/worker/jobs/configWorkersStockRefreshJob.ts` (primary) plus any new query helper in `helios/src/server/db/queries/`. - Replace the per-row loop on `stock_variant_state` with a single `INSERT … SELECT FROM jsonb_to_recordset(...) … ON CONFLICT (...) DO UPDATE …` (one statement per dealer, chunked at `BULK_CHUNK_SIZE = 500` for safety — same shape as the A1 commit). - Replace the per-transitioning-variant guard SELECT against `pending_litalerts_refresh_queue` with a single `INSERT … FROM jsonb_to_recordset(...) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` that relies on the existing partial unique index. - Replace the per-brand upsert loop on `landingpage_brand_site_presence` with one bulk `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` per dealer. - All of the above inside the single existing per-dealer transaction. - Validation: - Before / after row count on `stock_snapshot_items`, `stock_variant_state`, `pending_litalerts_refresh_queue`, and `landingpage_brand_site_presence` for one full poll, posted in the commit body. - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` snippet for the new bulk statements. - Operator sign-off that the live VeriScan scans page still updates in real time post-deploy. Commits MUST carry `Phase: A2`. ### Phase A3 — `configWorkersSweedOrdersIngestJob` bulk upsert Files: `helios/src/worker/jobs/configWorkersSweedOrdersIngestJob.ts`. - Replace the per-invoice `SELECT EXISTS(...)` + `INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` loop with: - one bulk `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING … RETURNING` over the incoming batch via `jsonb_to_recordset`; - one set-based CTE that computes `first_time_for_customer` for the newly-inserted rows in a single pass against `sweed_orders` (uses the existing `sweed_orders_customer_pay_time_idx` partial index). - Highwater bump stays unchanged. - Validation: - Backfill-equivalence check: run the new path on a held-aside dealer for one full poll, diff resulting `sweed_orders` rows + `first_time_for_customer` column against the pre-deploy snapshot. - Operator sign-off as above. Commits MUST carry `Phase: A3`. ### Phase A4 — Litalerts batch + `enqueueMarketRefreshForProducts` bulk transactions Files: `helios/src/worker/runtime/configWorkersScheduler.ts` (scheduler batch path) and `helios/src/worker/litalerts/enqueueMarketRefresh.ts`. - Collapse `for (const row of pendingRows) { await withTransaction(...) }` into one transaction per batch: - one bulk insert into `job_queue` (the existing `enqueueJob` helper grows a `enqueueJobs` plural variant that takes an array and uses `INSERT … SELECT FROM jsonb_to_recordset`); - one bulk `appendAuditEvent` (likewise, a plural variant); - one `recordEnqueueAndPatchCache` call at the end of the batch. - Preserve the single-flight dedupe-key behaviour. - Validation: - Count of `job_queue` rows inserted per scheduler tick before / after. - Operator sign-off as above. Commits MUST carry `Phase: A4`. ### Phase A5 — `configWorkersLitalertsRefreshJob` round-trip compression Files: `helios/src/worker/jobs/configWorkersLitalertsRefreshJob.ts` plus index migration under `helios/src/server/db/migrations/`. - Combine the queue-row load, catalog-group containment search, brand-expiry lookup, and (when needed) prior-observation lookup into a **single CTE** that returns the assembled context in one round-trip. - Add a GIN index on `catalog_groups.live_state_json` (or a computed jsonb_path_ops index on `live_state_json -> 'products'`) so the existing `(... -> 'products') @> $1::jsonb` containment search stops doing a sequential scan. Verify via `EXPLAIN` before declaring done. - The observation insert + queue-row update + audit row stay in one transaction (already true) but use a single multi-statement pipeline rather than three sequential awaits where possible. - Validation: - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` showing the new containment index is used. - Throughput / round-trip count per job before / after. - Operator sign-off as above. Commits MUST carry `Phase: A5`. ### Phase B2 — Gate the expired-lease sweep Files: `helios/src/worker/runtime/leaseJobs.ts`. - Move the unconditional `UPDATE job_queue SET status='queued' … WHERE status='running' AND leased_until < now()` out of the per-poll path and behind a per-process timestamp guard (e.g. run at most once per minute per worker process). The guard MUST survive a process restart cleanly (i.e., default to "sweep on first tick post-startup" so we don't lose recovery semantics). - Validation: - Count of `job_queue` UPDATEs issued during a 5-minute idle window before / after. - Confirm by deliberately leaving a leased row past its deadline that the sweep still picks it up within one minute. Commits MUST carry `Phase: B2`. ### Phase B4 — `LISTEN/NOTIFY` wake-up + idle-cap raise Files: `helios/src/worker/runtime/workerLoop.ts`, `helios/src/server/jobs/enqueueJob.ts`, and any new `helios/src/server/db/notify.ts`. - `enqueueJob` (and the new `enqueueJobs` plural from A4) emits `NOTIFY helios_job_queue` after a successful commit. - The worker lease loop opens a dedicated `LISTEN` connection that races with the `delay(...)` in the idle-backoff path: whichever resolves first re-enters the lease loop. (Don't share the LISTEN connection with the lease-CTE client; a dedicated pool connection is cheap and avoids pg client-state weirdness.) - With LISTEN/NOTIFY in place, raise the empty-poll backoff cap from 15 s to 60 s. Live work paths now have sub-second wake-up latency, so the cap raise is free. - Validation: - End-to-end latency from `enqueueJob` returning to the worker actually leasing the row, before / after. Target: ≤ 200 ms in the post-B4 world. - Count of `leaseJobs` round-trips during a 5-minute idle window before / after. Commits MUST carry `Phase: B4`. ### Phase C1 — Hypertables + compression Files: new migrations under `helios/src/server/db/migrations/` (one per table), and probably a `helios/scripts/explain-coverage.ts` or equivalent EXPLAIN-diff helper to compare pre/post planner choices. Tables to convert (in order, smallest-first to validate the pattern): 1. `parsekit_reverse_shadow_events` — small, easy validator. 2. `sweed_auth_events`. 3. `audit_events`. 4. `litalerts_competitor_observations`. 5. `sweed_orders`. 6. `sweed_package_snapshots`. For each: - `create_hypertable(...)` with an appropriate `chunk_time_interval` (sized so each chunk is in the low-GB range under current write volume — start at 1 day for high-write tables, 7 days for diagnostics). - Re-create every existing index ON THE HYPERTABLE; verify via `EXPLAIN` that every production query path still uses the expected index post-conversion. - Add `add_compression_policy(..., interval ...)` with `compress_orderby` and `compress_segmentby` matching the table's access pattern (typically segment-by dealer_id and order-by the time column DESC). - Each migration MUST be reversible (drop the policy + decompress + drop the hypertable in a `down` migration) so we can back out cleanly if the planner regresses. Validation per table: post the size before/after compression, plus the EXPLAIN diff for the top 3 production queries hitting that table. Commits MUST carry `Phase: C1`. ### Phase C2 — Retention policies Files: migrations under `helios/src/server/db/migrations/`, plus a small `/config/workers` UI surface for the operator-tunable knobs. - Operator-tunable retention windows (in days, persisted in a new `db_retention_policies` table) for: - `parsekit_reverse_shadow_events` (default 30 d), - `sweed_auth_events` (default 90 d), - `audit_events` (default 365 d). - Each tunable read/write through a new `/api/config/db-retention` route + UI panel under `/config/workers` (operator can raise / lower the window per table). - The actual purge is `add_retention_policy` on the hypertable; changing the window via the UI invokes `alter_job(...) SET schedule_interval / config` on the existing retention job. - Validation: alter one window down to 1 day in staging-equivalent data and verify the next policy run removes the expected rows; raise back to default. Commits MUST carry `Phase: C2`. ### Phase C3 — Stop storing `raw_json` where it's redundant Files: schemas + ingest jobs across `helios/src/worker/jobs/` and `helios/src/server/db/schema/`. Per-table decision tree: - `sweed_package_snapshots`: every consumer reads typed columns; drop `raw_json` from the steady-state table and store it in a new `sweed_package_snapshots_raw` table with 30 d retention (so we still have a one-month rollback window for "re-derive a field we forgot"). - `sweed_orders`: catalog-analytics still unrolls `raw_json->'items'`; D1 removes that dependency. Once D1 lands, apply the same split here. - `litalerts_competitor_observations.evidence_json`: every read parses the same handful of fields. Project them into typed columns; move `evidence_json` to `_raw` with 30 d retention. - `parsekit_reverse_shadow_events`: 3 JSONB columns, all read on the diagnostics page. Project the per-page-needed fields, keep the rest in `_raw` with the C2 retention window. Validation: for each touched table, demonstrate (via the existing test suite + a one-shot sample query against staging-equivalent data) that no consumer path regresses. Commits MUST carry `Phase: C3`. ### Phase D1 — `sweed_order_line_items` Files: new migration, new query helper, modified ingest job. - New table: `sweed_order_line_items (dealer_id, invoice_id, line_seq, inventory_item_id, product_id, current_qty, subtotal_amount, wholesale_cost_dollars_as_of, …)` keyed by `(dealer_id, invoice_id, line_seq)` and indexed for the existing catalog-analytics joins. - `configWorkersSweedOrdersIngestJob` populates it incrementally alongside the `sweed_orders` insert (same transaction, same batch — bulk insert via `jsonb_to_recordset`). - One-time backfill script under `helios/scripts/backfill-sweed-order-line-items.ts` that walks `sweed_orders.raw_json -> 'items'` historically and populates the new table; idempotent via the PK so reruns are cheap. - Rewrite `helios/src/server/catalogAnalytics/catalogAnalyticsQueries.ts` to read from `sweed_order_line_items` instead of unrolling jsonb at request time. Validation: - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` before / after on the `/api/catalog-analytics` query at the default 90-day window; must hit the ≤ 500 ms p95 target. - Diff of the API response between the old and new query path on one site, demonstrating identical numbers. Commits MUST carry `Phase: D1`. ### Phase D2 — Continuous aggregates for `/metrics` Files: new migrations, route handlers under `helios/src/server/budtenderAnalytics/`, `helios/src/server/customerValueAnalytics/`, `helios/src/server/catalogAnalytics/`. - One Timescale continuous-aggregate per `(dealer_id, day, granularity)` rollup the metric pages currently compute at request time. - Route handlers read from the CAGG; "real-time" tail (the last few hours) is computed on-the-fly via the existing CTE and unioned in (Timescale's `materialized only` / real-time aggregation pattern). - Refresh policy: every 15 min during business hours, hourly overnight. Validation: - p95 server-side query time on every `/metrics` route after D2; ≤ 200 ms target. - Numeric equivalence sample on one site for the prior 7 days. Commits MUST carry `Phase: D2`. ### Phase E1 — Client auto-refresh audit + selective mechanism swap Files: `helios/src/client/routes/**/*.tsx`, plus the new push-mechanism plumbing (likely `helios/src/client/lib/realtime/visitorScans.ts` and a server-side SSE / WebSocket route). **Throttle bucket** (cadence raise, no mechanism change): - `TasksPage` (10 s → 60 s) - `TaskFrontierPage` (10 s → 60 s) - `EpicDagPage` (30 s → 300 s) - `JobsPage`, `JobDetailPage` (only between an operator-initiated state change; default cadence raise to 60 s; preserve the existing "tighter cadence while a run is pending" branch) - `SweedAuthLogPage` (raise to 60 s) - `PricingRunsPage` (raise to 60 s) - `SchedulingRunDetailPage` (raise to 30 s between runs; preserve the "tight cadence during a run" branch) - `AdsIngestPage` (raise to 60 s) - `PendingMigrationsBanner` (raise to 5 min) - `ConfigParsingPendingPurchasesPage` (raise to 60 s) - `CustomerReviewsDrawingPage` (the 5 s `setNowMs` is a display-clock tick, not a fetch — verify with grep before touching). **Mechanism-swap bucket** (must remain live, throttle forbidden): - `VisitorScansPage` — swap the 20 s `setInterval` for a server-pushed event stream: - server: `GET /api/visitors/scans/stream` SSE endpoint that emits a new event whenever the VeriScan webhook handler persists a row. Implementation: webhook handler calls `pgNotify('visitor_scans_new', JSON.stringify({ id, siteSlug, capturedAt }))` post-commit; the SSE route holds a long-lived LISTEN connection and pipes notifications back out. - client: open the SSE on mount; on each event, refetch only the head of the list (`/api/visitors/scans?since=`) and prepend the new rows. Reconnect with jittered exponential backoff on disconnect. - operator-visible behaviour: a scan at the door appears in the open browser tab in ≤ 2 s, indistinguishably from the current 20-s-poll worst case but at a fraction of the DB cost. - Add any other "during-shift live feedback" page surfaced during the audit to this bucket BEFORE applying any throttle. Validation: - For each touched page, post the before / after cadence + bucket classification in the commit body (parent epic's E1 description requires this). - Operator-visible smoke test of the live-scan SSE on `vps-nixos-3` after deploy. Commits MUST carry `Phase: E1`. --- ## Conventions - Every commit MUST carry both `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#11` and the appropriate `Phase:

` trailer. - Every commit MUST be deployable in isolation (the worker / server must boot and pass `self-deploy-helios` health checks after the commit alone). - Validation evidence (row counts, EXPLAIN diffs, operator sign-offs) goes in the commit body, not in a separate STATUS file — STATUS files in this epic's directory are reserved for "operator changed direction" events.

  `NEEDS_OPERATOR_VERIFICATION` comment block.

- **B2.** Migration `041_sweed_customer_profile_snapshots.sql` per
  parent §3-B2 (table + indices). New worker job
  `refreshSweedCustomerProfileSnapshotJob` that computes #purchases
  / total / avg / favorite category / favorite product from the
  existing `sweed_orders` + `sweed_package_snapshots` tables. The
  `>= 3` repeat-count gate for favorites lives in the snapshot
  generator, not in the read path. Scheduled on (a) successful link
  in the link worker, (b) a daily cron tick for linked customers
  whose `snapshotted_at` is older than 24h.

- **B3.** Augment the existing `/admin/customers/check-ins` page
  (alias of `/admin/visitors/scans`) loader and table component
  with: `# Purchases`, `Avg $`, `Total $`, `Favorite Category`,
  `Favorite Product`. Single LEFT JOIN through `visitor_scan_links`
  → `sweed_customer_profile_snapshots`; NO N+1. Favorite columns
  blank when snapshot's repeat-count gate isn't met.

- **B4.** New cashier live view at
  `/admin/checkout-counter/check-ins` (final URL is operator's call
  — see parent §7). Components:
  - `CheckoutCounterPage.tsx` — landscape-tablet layout, reuses
    the visitor-scans table component in `privacyRedacted` mode.
  - `privacyRedacted` table mode: forces `expanded=off`, renders
    `FirstName L.` only, hides DOB / address / phone / email /
    id_num. Sweed aggregate columns (B3) stay visible (not PII).
  - New SSE route `GET /api/check-ins/stream` on the existing
    `helios-server` fastify app. In-process `EventEmitter`
    published-to by the existing webhook handler (after the link
    row is seeded) and by the link worker (after `linked` /
    `ambiguous` / `no_match` transitions). On connect: one bounded
    "last 20" query (no polling thereafter). See parent §0 — this
    is the DB-cost cap.
  - Two chime assets bundled at
    `helios/src/client/assets/audio/chime-first.ogg` and
    `chime-returning.ogg`. Click-to-enable overlay handles the
    browser autoplay policy + Notification permission in one
    gesture.
  - Browser Notification API on each event with the redacted name,
    first-vs-returning, last-visit date.

- **B5.** Auth gate on the cashier route + SSE endpoint that
  restricts to user `internal.shared_accounts@freshlybaked.nyc`.
  When that user lands on `/admin/customers/check-ins`, redirect
  to the cashier page so the un-redacted view is unreachable from
  their session. When they're on the admin check-ins page (e.g.
  via redirect race), apply the same name-redaction the cashier
  page uses — the operator was explicit about this:
  > the customer list should be like this as well on this
  > particular page, for enhanced privacy.

## Out of scope (deferred / other epics)

- Sweed CRM customer **creation** when there's no documentNumber
  match — owned by the existing customer-sentiment capture flow.
- Multi-tenant cashier RBAC beyond the one shared-account email.
- Host-level config (no `nixos-sbc` changes; nginx `proxy_buffering
  off` for the SSE location is an in-repo deploy concern, handled
  in `automation` alongside B4).

## Per-phase DB-cost statements (canon §3 — REQUIRED)

Every commit landing a phase MUST include, in the commit body:

```
DB-cost:
  per-request: <op count + index used>
  per-day:     <upper bound for steady-state>
  index:       <name(s) the path relies on>
  caching:     <TTL / pub-sub / materialisation>
```

Reviewers should reject phase commits missing this block.

## Phases — task-dag

Use the existing `scripts/task-dag` flow:

```
scripts/task-dag frontier --issue=<child-epic issue number>
# pick a leaf, do real work, then:
scripts/task-dag complete <task-sha>
git push origin HEAD:master
```

Never create empty tombstone commits for new work. Phase order is
strictly **B1 → B2 → B3 → B4 → B5**; B3 and B4 can be cut from the
same change set if both rely on B2 already being live (which they do).

## Operator pre-reqs (do not implement until done)

- Sweed session UUID pasted into the token pool at
  https://helios.freshlybaked.us/config/sweed/sessions. The new
  token supplied with the parent request is the one to paste.
  Without an active pool token, B1's Sweed RPC will return
  `Auth expired` and the worker will retire the env-fallback path.

# World-class Inventory / Procurement workspace (`/metrics/inventory` → Reordering)

The current `/metrics/inventory` tab is a husk (4 thin time-series cards). This epic
rebuilds it into a **procurement-grade decision surface** so the buyer knows exactly
**what to order, from whom, how much, and when** — plus what to liquidate and where our
stock mix has drifted from demand.

Design: oracle thread `T-019e6edf` (2026-06-04).

## Architecture
- One consolidated `GET /api/inventory-procurement` (gated on the `reordering` metric grant)
  returns a per-SKU fact table (product grain) + per-distributor cadence stats.
- The server pre-computes every per-SKU scalar (velocity, days-supply, recommended qty,
  lost-margin/day, deadweight + reorder-priority scores, confidence) with p95 normalization
  across the set; the client derives all four views as group-bys/sorts (no extra round-trips).
- Two cheap SQL passes (~130ms for ~1.7k SKUs); no DB regressions.
- All windows/day-boundaries are America/New_York per canon.

## Views (sub-tabs)
- **A1. Shared facts foundation** — SQL + scoring module + contract + route (`reordering` grant).
- **A2. Reorder Queue** (default) — "out now & regretting" + "runout soon" with recommended order qty.
- **A3. PO-history enrichment** — distributor cadence (delivery-date gaps); lead time degrades to a
  configurable default (PO `received_at` is unpopulated upstream).
- **A4. Distributor Baskets** — batched per-distributor guidance (order now / short order / wait),
  expandable consolidated basket, order-now-value vs carrying cost.
- **A5. Exit / Liquidate** — deadweight score, liquidation queue, breakeven discount, expiry, do-not-reorder.
- **A6. Mix Drift** — inventory $/unit share vs sales/margin/forecast demand share by category /
  subcategory / brand / distributor; excess/deficit capital; over/under status.

## Procurement questions answered
- What are we OUT of now and regretting? → Reorder Queue top table (ranked by lost margin/day).
- What runs out soon, from whom, how much? → Reorder Queue + recommended qty + distributor.
- What's deadweight to liquidate / stop carrying? → Exit / Liquidate (deadweight score).
- Batch distributor orders — order now vs wait? → Distributor Baskets (order-now-value, guidance).
- How misaligned is stock mix vs sales/expected mix ($ and units, by cat/subcat/brand/distributor)? → Mix Drift.

## Known data gaps (degrade gracefully, noted in the page methodology)
- PO line `received_at` unpopulated → lead time = configurable default; cadence still from delivery gaps.
- Package `received_at` unpopulated → inventory age = days-since-last-observed (lower bound).
- Item revenue is pre-discount list (order-level discounts tiny, unallocated).

## Future phases (refer back here)
- Phase 7 polish: CSV basket export, deep links, MOQ/case-pack rounding once available, open-PO netting,
  optional "Reprice highlighted" integration, materialized facts if scale grows.

- **CEL policy compiler** — compiles the selection policy into the
  sandboxed, locally-evaluable form mss consumes (parent §6; locked
  decision 1: CEL, never `eval`). **Critical schema constraint
  (parent §6.1, rev-3):** the policy output is a **weight per `NUM`**
  on the existing canonical `/SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM` schema. The
  compiler MUST validate that every variant id it references exists in
  the active mss per-purpose `*VariantIds` registry / respects
  `MAX_VARIANT_BY_PURPOSE` — it must **never** emit a new URL shape or a
  `NUM` that mss can't serve.
- **Bundle publisher** — compiles clusters + blueprints + site
  overrides + approved copy/imagery + policy into one immutable,
  signed, versioned bundle; writes it to the read-only-for-mss `/cloud`
  artifact root behind an atomic `current.json` pointer with
  last-known-good (parent §5, decision 5). Signing keys live with
  Helios, **never** on the shared mount.

  `(site, purpose, slug, num)` variant tuple (`disabled_variants`, parent

  ~15-min batch; no sampling). Every new query ships with an analyzed
  plan + index strategy (canon §3).
- **Leaderboard with propensity-corrected (unbiased) lift** over
  served + counterfactual variants (parent §6, §9); surfaces deltas so
  "shut off the loser" is statistically honest. Promotion stays a
  one-click operator action.
