## Where the code lives

- Slow endpoint query:
  `helios/src/server/db/queries/reviewFamilyQueueQueries.ts`
  (`listReviewFamilyQueue`).
- Route: `helios/src/server/routes/review.ts`
  (`GET /api/review/family-queue`).
- Contract: `helios/src/shared/contracts/api/review.ts`
  (`ReviewFamilyQueueQuerySchema`, `ReviewFamilyQueueResponseSchema`).
- Live-state writer (Phase B projection hook):
  `helios/src/worker/jobs/catalogGroupPersistence.ts`
  (`updateCatalogGroupLiveState`).
- Migration sentinels: `helios/src/server/db/pendingMigrations.ts`.
- Migrations: `helios/src/server/db/migrations/NNN_*.sql` (applied
  manually by an operator; idempotent `IF NOT EXISTS`).
- Client review page + the canonical pending-purchases review layout to
  reuse: `helios/src/client/routes/...` (pending-purchases review is the
  UI parity target — find and extend it, do not fork).

## Constraints (apply to every slice)

- **Typed TS only.** No untyped query/response shapes.
- **Measure before/after with a real full fetch**, not just
  `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` (canon: plans hide payload/detoast/serialization
  cost). Record server `exec_time`, wall time, payload bytes, and
  executor memory in the commit/issue.
- **Idempotent migrations** (`CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`,
  `CONCURRENTLY` where applicable) so they no-op on prod and stay
  recreate-safe. Add a matching sentinel to `pendingMigrations.ts`.
- **Do NOT add btree indexes to the join/filter path** — measured fast
  already.
- **Do not regress competitor-match correctness** (separate epic).
- **Reuse canonical UI** (pending-purchases review layout); no forked
  components.

## Slices

### R-A — Server family-aware pagination + minimal client paging *(ship together)*

Two-phase query in `listReviewFamilyQueue`:

1. Narrow family-page CTE/query over the indexed join only
   (`proposal_line_items ⋈ proposal_rows ⋈ proposal_batches ⋈
   catalog_groups`, projecting `brand/category/subcategory` columns
   only) → group → deterministic order → `LIMIT familyLimit+1`. **No**
   `jsonb_array_elements`, `regexp_replace`, `evidence_json`, or full
   `live_state_json` here.
2. Fetch full line items + reduced live state for the selected
   families' proposal rows, and observations only for that page's
   product ids.

- Add to `ReviewFamilyQueueQuerySchema`: `limit` (default 10, max 25)
  and `cursor`. Add `pageInfo { hasNextPage, endCursor }` to the
  response. Cursor encodes the sort tuple + filter state +
  `familyKeyVersion: 1`.
- Interim family key = `(brand, category, subcategory)`; multi-size
  families render `Mixed`/blank size. Keep individual actions.
- `maxItemsPerPage` safety cap; oversized family returned alone +
  logged.
- Minimal client change: request a single page; stop fetching/rendering
  the whole queue.
- **Acceptance:** payload ≪ 2.4 MB, no whole-queue
  `jsonb_array_elements`, executor memory ≪ 600 MB, DB interaction
  ≤125 ms; before/after numbers posted. Ships before R-B/R-C.

### R-B — `catalog_group_products` projection table

- Migration: `catalog_group_products(catalog_group_id, product_id,
  ordinal, name, tab, size_name, price numeric, updated_at, primary key
  (catalog_group_id, product_id))`; indexes `(product_id)`,
  `(catalog_group_id, ordinal)`. Idempotent + sentinel + idempotent
  backfill from `live_state_json`.
- Populate in `updateCatalogGroupLiveState`, write-on-change only
  (`WHERE … IS DISTINCT FROM`), inside the same transaction as the
  existing column projection.
- Size semantics: product-targeted → that product's `size_name`;
  single-size group → that size; multi-size group → `NULL`/`"Mixed"`.
- Rewrite R-A's narrow query to read `size_name` from the projection
  table (drop the lateral blob crack); upgrade the family key to
  include size; bump `familyKeyVersion → 2`.
- **Acceptance:** narrow page query has zero JSON cracking; multi-size
  groups grouped correctly; plan + timings posted.

### R-C — Client UX parity with pending-purchases review

- Lazy/virtualized mount of pricing ladders (mount on demand, not all
  at once).
- Reuse the pending-purchases review hierarchical layout: family groups
  with **group-level actions** + per-item actions.
- Group-aware pagination UI: never split a normal family across a page;
  massive family handled per R-A's guard.
- **Acceptance:** page interactive ≤500 ms after data; no all-ladders
  mount; layout matches pending-purchases review.

### R-D — Resolve dead MSO filter

- `msoOnly` is hardcoded `{ isMSOBrand: false }` → returns nothing.
  Either wire to a real brand-annotation source or remove the dead
  filter from contract + UI. Prefer removal if no source is ready.

### R-E — *(stretch)* precomputed preview columns

- Only if `regexp_replace` previews still measure material after R-A.
  Add `*_preview_text` (+ truncation flag) columns on
  `proposal_line_items`, maintained on insert/edit paths. Do not do
  pre-emptively.

# FBUS FAQ — `automation` (Helios control plane) child epic

> **MATERIALISED 2026-06-15.** The four operator decisions are resolved
> in the parent
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md` §1](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#1-operator-decisions-resolved-2026-06-15)
> and folded into the phases below.
> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md). **Re-read the parent (and the
> parent epic #15) before starting any phase** — this child epic is a
> **thin index** over the parent's design, not a re-statement of it. The
> parent wins on any drift.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#17
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>` trailer
> so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post per-phase progress
> on the parent issue.

## Role in the epic

Helios (`automation`) is the **FAQ brain**: it owns the FAQ content
source-of-truth, generation + the editorial review/approve workflow, the
sanitized-host denylist, the change-detection/sync loop, governance
checks, and the signed SEO-bundle publisher. mss stays a thin, zero-DB
renderer (peer child epic at `../mostly-static-sites/EPIC_PLAN.md`).

This builds **directly on the FB-NYC SEO FAQ control plane already
shipped under epic #15** (`helios/src/server/seo/faqGenerate.ts`,
`faqContent.ts`, signed bundle publisher). This child epic **extends**,
it does not rebuild.

## ⚠️ Binding constraints (parent §5–§6, canon §1)

- **IRONCLAD human-approval gate (canon §1).** No FAQ draft, sanitized
  variant, family content, or sync-detected change becomes publicly
  visible without a human approving that **specific** content first.
  Generation and the sync loop only ever produce **drafts**
  (`source='generated', approval_id=null`) + fire `page-dave`; they
  **never auto-publish**.
- **Zero `.nyc` / brand / cannabis-meta-term leak in sanitized content.**
  The FBUS sanitized-host denylist must be **stricter than the current
  `RAW_ONLY_TERMS`** (include `flower(s)`, `strain(s)`, etc. if the rule
  is truly zero meta-terms). Approval and bundle publish must both fail
  closed on any leak.
- **`content_sha256` must match the approval ledger** before publish.
- **No invented facts.** Generated answers are drafts; verify against real
  store data (hours, areas, payment, policies) before approval.
- **DB-cost discipline (canon §3).** The sync/change-detection job is a
  recurring background DB workload → written cost budget + Oracle
  DB-efficiency review recorded on the peer issue **before deploy**.

## Subtasks (authoritative list in parent §4 / issue Phases 1 & 5)

**P1 — FAQ source migration + sync loop:**
- One-time import the hardcoded FB-NYC FAQ
  (`mostly-static-sites: apps/freshlybaked-site/app/sites/all/loyalty-faq/page.tsx`)
  into Helios; generate sanitized variants; human review/approve; publish
  the bundle with FAQ sets + widgets.
- Add a **source-key** model (`fbus-global-faq`, `fbus-deliverance-faq`,
  … `fbus-dedicated-faq`).
- Add a **sync/change-detection job** with the **hybrid cadence the
  operator chose** (parent §1 Q3): **(a)** an *approval* of FAQ content
  (FB-NYC / Helios) **drives the bundle push** (event-driven publish of
  already-approved content); **(b)** an *observed* upstream/source change
  — or **creation/modification of content** such as a newly added or
  modified LP family — recomputes `content_sha256`, creates/updates a
  Helios **draft**, and fires **`page-dave`** for review. Path (b)
  **never auto-publishes**; only path (a)'s human approval does. **Guard:**
  path (a) may publish **only** the exact `content_sha256` / sanitized
  content that was approved — a raw/upstream approval that would change the
  FBUS *sanitized* output routes through path (b) (new draft + page), never
  an implicit sanitized publish.
- Coordinate with mss to remove/neutralize the hardcoded FB-NYC FAQ page
  (+ CI guard against reintroduction). FB-NYC then renders raw from the
  bundle.

**P5 — family-contextual generation + governance:**
- Generate per-family drafts (deliverance, conquest, tours, recurse,
  branding, compare — the operator-confirmed current set, parent §1 Q1)
  via the private Bedrock LLM, scoped via widget `route_patterns` that
  **consume the machine-readable LP-family registry artifact** mss P0
  exports (family id, canonical representative route, route patterns,
  sample routes, indexability policy, source SHA) — or, if a generated
  copy is unavoidable, record the exact mss source SHA for provenance.
  Do **not** maintain a second hand-edited family list here.
- Governance before review: item-count cap, answer-length cap,
  forbidden-term scan, duplicate-question check, near-duplicate-answer
  check (token/Jaccard/shingle overlap is fine to start).
- Review page shows: raw + sanitized + rendered FBUS preview + route
  patterns + approx impacted route count + diff vs previous + leak/dup
  warnings.

**P6 — rollout support / monitoring:**
- Provide approved-content status, disabled-content rollback, `page-dave`
  alerts, and any ads-policy lint / reporting needed for rollout
  decisions.
- Coordinate with the operator on the ads-disapproval baseline + window.

## CI gates owned here (parent §7)

(1) sanitized-content leak unit tests; (2) approval rejects any leaked
sanitized answer / shared question / `.nyc` URL; (3) bundle-validation
tests (`content_sha256` must match approval); (9) ads-policy lint.

## Phasing

P1 (source migration + sync) is the unblocking control-plane slice and
goes first; P5 (family content + governance) follows once mss can render.
Tag commits with `Phase: P<n>`.

# GAds → Landing-pages analytics (V1) — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#18](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/18).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/gads-landing-analytics/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in the top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the
> `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (Helios) slice of that design**, which in
> V1 is the whole thing — no other peer repo is on the critical path.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation@master` that
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#18
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>` trailer
> (`P0`..`P5`) so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post the
> per-phase progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

Everything in the parent `EPIC_PLAN.md`, broken out by phase below.
**Re-read the parent before starting** — the parent is the single source
of truth; this file is a thin phase index over it.

## Binding constraints (from the parent, do not weaken)

- **Confidential, per-site access.** Three grants `gads-bronx`,
  `gads-midtown`, `gads-all`. `gads-all` is its own grant, never
  synthesised from the per-site grants. The server derives the site
  predicate from the authenticated route/grant and MUST NOT accept a
  client `site`/`sites` param that widens scope.
- **Cheap DB, by operator decree.** One small rollup table refreshed
  out-of-band; **no** per-assignment fact table, **no** hourly+daily
  rollup pair, **no** always-on derivation worker, **no** CAGGs /
  hypertable conversion / compression / HLL in V1. Each of those, if
  ever proposed, needs its own Oracle DB review. Do not fight epic #11.
- **Serving never touches raw `lp_events`.** Dashboard reads hit only
  `gads_lp_rollup` (+ the refresh-state row). A test asserts this.
- **Observed performance, not accounting.** No causal claims. Revenue
  and ROAS render "Unavailable" (no fake numbers). Cost is allocated and
  badged. Hide variant rows < 25 assignments behind a toggle.
- **Canon gates at implementation time:** the DB migration + refresh
  query ship with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` plans and a payload
  byte-size measurement (canon DB gate); the UI gets the mandatory
  Oracle UI review before it ships; record the Agent Gate Record on each
  commit / issue update.

---

### P0 — Audit + lock semantics (do this first)

No schema change yet; produce a short design note (committed or linked).

- Verify the live `lp_events` columns + existing indexes match the
  parent's assumptions (`assignment_id`, event types, `site`, `family`,
  `cluster_slug`, `experiment_id`, `policy_id`, `policy_rule_id`,
  `branch_id`, `served_probability_bps`, `assignment_key_type`,
  `gclid_hash`, `traffic_flags`, `event_ts`). Confirm `assignment_id`
  presence per stage and whether `branch_id` is whole-page vs per-slot.
- **Define + test the GAds traffic predicate** (biggest correctness
  risk): which `assignment_key_type` / `traffic_flags` count as paid.
  Decide handling of `cookie`/`session`/`default` (default: exclude
  from cost/CPA, badge "GAds-detected traffic only").
- Pick the **reporting timezone** (America/New_York / Ads business
  zone) for `assignment_day`; document it.
- Lock the exact metric formulas: assignment-level-unique funnel counts;
  `conversions_7d/30d/90d` semantics; right-censoring of immature
  cohorts; sample threshold (25); allocated-cost basis (must sum back to
  the aggregate snapshot total per day/site/campaign bucket).
- `EXPLAIN` the candidate refresh query over a realistic date range on
  current data volume; decide whether the one partial `lp_events` index
  is needed.
- Pick the initial refresh cadence (30-60 min; default to the slower
  end).

Deliverable: design note + the confirmed predicate/timezone/formulas.

### P1 — Grants, routes, access enforcement

Files: `shared/contracts/domain/auth.ts` (grant enum),
`helios/src/client/routes/metrics/MetricsLayoutPage.tsx`
(`MetricsTabId`, `METRICS_TABS`, `METRICS_TAB_ALIASES`), server auth
middleware/route guard.

- Add `MetricGrantKey` values `gads-bronx`, `gads-midtown`, `gads-all`.
- Add the three tab ids + aliases so
  `/metrics/gads-<site>` -> `/metrics/gads-<site>/landing-pages`.
- Add the typed `GADS_METRIC_SCOPES` registry (grant -> site scope).
- Server-side grant + scope enforcement; `gads-all` requires its own
  grant explicitly.
- Regression tests: Bronx user cannot read Midtown or all; Midtown
  cannot read Bronx or all; holding both site grants does **not** grant
  all; unauthorized responses leak no site list / no cross-site data.

### P2 — Rollup storage + refresh job

Files: new migration under `helios/...migrations`, new worker job under
`helios/src/worker/jobs/`, query helper under
`helios/src/server/db/queries/`.

- Migration: `gads_lp_rollup` (grain + measures per parent §3),
  `gads_lp_rollup_refresh_state`, and (only if P0 proved it needed) the
  one partial `lp_events` index.
- Idempotent refresh job on the P0 cadence: recompute a **bounded 90-day
  assignment-day horizon** (so late `lp_conversion`s update the correct
  older bucket), dedupe duplicate event posts, apply the GAds traffic
  predicate, compute counts in the reporting timezone, join allocated
  GAds cost conservatively, write the refresh-state row.
- Ship `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` for the refresh query in the commit
  body.
- Tests/fixtures: duplicate events deduped; late conversion updates the
  right assignment-day bucket; 7/30/90d counts correct; allocated cost
  sums back to the snapshot total.

### P3 — Serving endpoint

Files: `shared/contracts/api/gadsLandingPages.ts`,
`server/db/queries/gadsLandingPagesQueries.ts`, the route handler.

- `GET /api/gads/<site-scope>/landing-pages` returns hero KPIs + funnel
  + variant table (top N, 25-50) + per-site breakdown (for `gads-all`) +
  freshness/badging metadata, in **one** compact payload.
- Site predicate derived from the grant, never widened by client input.
- Reads **only** `gads_lp_rollup` + the refresh-state row; a test
  asserts no raw `lp_events` query on the serving path.
- Ship the full-fetch payload byte-size measurement (canon DB gate).

### P4 — UI (Landing pages sub-page)

Files: `helios/src/client/routes/metrics/gads/` (new `GAdsTab`,
`GAdsLandingPagesTab`), reuse `MetricsAccessGate`, range presets +
`RangeNudgeRow`, `ControlsSection`, metrics CSS; extract shared
`MetricRangeControls`.

- Sub-page nav: Landing pages active; Campaigns / Creative / Keywords /
  Policy health / Experiments / Evolution / Iteration as disabled
  "Coming soon" stubs.
- First screen order per parent §5: freshness+attribution strip -> KPI
  strip -> next-action card (top 3 review candidates, each with a direct
  action) -> funnel waterfall (biggest drop-off inline) -> variant table
  (mobile-first, sticky action column, low-sample toggle).
- Revenue/ROAS rendered "Unavailable" with explanatory copy; cost
  badged "allocated"; right-censored cohorts badged. No em-dashes.
- **Mandatory canon Oracle UI review before it ships** (record the link
  on the peer issue).

### P5 — Docs, observability, rollout

- Runbook notes: refresh cadence, how to inspect the last refresh, how
  to manually rebuild the rollup.
- Lightweight job logging/metrics for the refresh.
- Document the deferred V2 items (mss enrichment, revenue/ROAS, Timescale
  features, future sub-pages).
- Deploy via the canonical `self-deploy-helios` path (no manual service
  surgery).

---

## Out of scope (V2 / later epics)

mss event-schema enrichment (order id / revenue / device class /
page-load-failure event on `lp_conversion`); exact Sweed revenue
attribution + ROAS/CPA + cancellation/refund handling; gclid-level cost;
bandit-aware off-policy stats; the reserved sub-pages; Timescale
CAGGs/hypertable/HLL. Each gets its own design + Oracle review when it
lands.

# Opaque `branding/` slugs — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Thin index over the authoritative parent plan
> [`docs/epics/branding-opaque-slugs/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in `virusdave/top-level`. Where this and the parent disagree, the parent
> wins — fix this doc. Tracking issue:
> [virusdave/top-level#19](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/19)
> (split from #15).
> **Operator-approved (2026-06-15); parent §6 decisions are RESOLVED and
> folded in below.** This peer issue materialises under top-level **#19**
> via the `Materialise-Child-Epic:` trailer flow — the work scope here is
> final.

## Scope (Helios control plane)

Make Helios speak the **same opaque `branding` ref** that
`mostly-static-sites` consumes, so the bandit/`NUM` emission, the signed
bundle, and any ad-URL producer reference branding rows **without the
literal brand name**.

**BINDING:** Helios still only decides **`NUM`** (the variant) and
publishes weights/kill-lists evaluated locally by the existing mss
middleware (parent §0, [#13 §6](../../../unified-landing-engine/EPIC_PLAN.md)).
This epic changes only the **`SLUG` representation** Helios emits for
`branding` — literal → opaque. No new route shapes, no schema change.

## First task: confirm the in-repo facts

The top-level repo cannot read automation source. Locate (parent names the
likely area, `helios/src/server/ads/…`):

- where the bandit / `NUM` emission and the signed bundle reference a
  branding row's `SLUG` (currently the literal brand id);
- any ad-final-URL / ValueTrack producer that builds `branding/` `/0`
  URLs;
- how `compare/`/`conquest/` already emit their opaque refs (reuse that
  exact path/helper-equivalent for parity with mss).

## Phase (parent §5)

- **P3 — emit the opaque branding ref.** Only after mss prod serves opaque
  and protects literal URLs (parent P0–P2). The bandit/`NUM` emission, the
  bundle, and any new-ad-URL producer reference branding rows by the
  **same** opaque ref mss uses. Add a **bundle-compile parity check**:
  every emitted branding ref must resolve in the mss registry (same spirit
  as the existing `MAX_VARIANT_BY_PURPOSE` / variant-id drift guard) so
  Helios can never publish an opaque ref mss cannot decode. The operator
  chose **migrate** (parent §6.2), so Helios additionally emits the
  **literal→opaque mapping** for every affected `branding/` `/0` final URL
  — the input the operator's one-off Ads-Editor CSV migration consumes.
  Agents do **not** touch the Ads account.
- **P4 (with operator/mss).** Staged rollout + deploy via
  `self-deploy-helios` under operator approval. The operator runs the
  one-off Ads-Editor CSV final-URL **migrate** (parent §6.2 — export →
  rewrite literal finals to opaque → re-import) using the mapping above
  for the already-approved ad final URLs; absorb the Google re-review on
  migrated ads. mss P1 `308` back-compat stays in place throughout.

## Verification

- Bundle-compile parity test: every emitted branding ref resolves in the
  mss registry; build/test green.
- Prove identical `brand-id → opaque-ref` output against the **shared
  contract** mss publishes (checked-in test vectors / generated manifest /
  importable package — parent §7), in CI.
- Each landing commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#19`.

## Coordination

P3 depends on the mss opaque scheme (parent P0–P2) landing first — agree
the shared output **contract** (not just "same code") before Helios emits
opaque branding refs.

# Eliminate broken-codebase debt — `automation` child epic (helios + ads)

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#20](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/20).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/fleet-green/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in the
> top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the
> `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (Helios monorepo) slice** of that design,
> covering both the `helios/` and `ads/` packages.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation@master` that
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#20
> ```
>
> **Re-read the parent `EPIC_PLAN.md` before starting** — it is the
> single source of truth; this file is a thin index over it.

## Binding standards (from the parent, do not weaken)

- Required gates (lint, typecheck, test, build) green on `master`.
- No first-party TypeScript `any` (`as any`, `: any`, `any[]`, `<any>`).
- Tests deterministic; tests never touch prod serving resources; force
  test-only config (no `??=` fallback to ambient prod env).
- No disabled/weakened gates (`--no-verify`, `ts-ignore`, `.skip` /
  `.only`, commented-out checks) without an equal-or-stronger replacement.
- Verify in a fresh ephemeral checkout; heavy commands under
  `large-action-lock`. Attach an Agent Gate Record per commit / issue
  update.

## Scope owned by this repo

### Phase A — `helios/` client typecheck debt

1. **Fix the ~13 real client type errors** so
   `tsc -p tsconfig.client.json --noEmit` passes:
   - `Pill` `children` typed `string` but passed `string[]`;
   - `number` → `string` prop mismatches;
   - maplibre `Geometry` / `LngLatLike` casts.
2. **`tsconfig.client.json` hygiene** — stop pulling `*.test.ts` and
   node-using `shared/` modules into the *client* typecheck; they belong
   to the server/node typecheck, not the browser bundle. (Doing this
   first may shrink the error list in step 1.)
3. **Re-enable the client typecheck** in `.githooks/pre-commit`
   (`tsc -p tsconfig.client.json --noEmit`) and remove the
   "disabled, ~9 errors" note. The re-enabled hook must match CI.

### Phase B — `helios/` `any` + test-config debt

4. **Remove the ~31 first-party `any`** in `helios/src` (give each a
   real type; no blanket `unknown` cast-through that re-hides it).
5. **Force test-only config** in smoke/tests — replace
   `DATABASE_URL ??= ...` and any sibling ambient-prod fallbacks with an
   explicit ephemeral test resource, GC'd on every exit path. No test
   may reach a prod DB / live server / prod credential.

### Phase C — `ads/`

6. **Remove first-party `any`** (≈14 files).
7. **Ensure a typecheck/test gate exists for `ads/`** and is green
   (if `ads/` has no gate wired today, add one).

### Phase D — scaffolding to stay green (do once for this repo)

8. **Required-status CI** on `master` / PRs running the full gate set
   (lint, typecheck — server *and* client, test, build).
9. **no-explicit-`any` scanner** — ESLint
   `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: error` where ESLint exists, else
   a grep gate over first-party `src`.
10. **disabled-gate scanner** — flag `--no-verify` recipes,
    commented-out checks, `ts-ignore`, and `.skip` / `.only` in
    committed tests.
11. **test-resource scanner** — flag prod URLs / credentials and
    ambient-env `??=` fallbacks in tests.
12. **Pre-commit hooks installed and matching CI** — no client-typecheck
    carve-out.

## Acceptance

Fresh ephemeral checkout; full gate set (server + client typecheck,
lint, test, build) run and **recorded green** under `large-action-lock`;
scanners (Phase D) added and passing; pre-commit hooks match CI with no
carve-outs; Agent Gate Record attached. Sole exception to green is an
active prod incident, repaired to green immediately after.

# Helios build hygiene — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#22](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/22)
> ("codebase cleanup & hygiene"). The authoritative design is
> [`docs/designs/codebase-cleanup-and-hygiene.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/codebase-cleanup-and-hygiene.md)
> in the top-level repo (§1 verified findings, §3.2 build design, §4
> Phase 3, §6 resolved decisions 4 & 5).
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`
> `master` and satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#22
> ```
>
> This is **Phase 3** only: small, low-risk build-setup changes that help
> even on the current shared production build box and need no off-prod
> infrastructure. The heavier "move build off prod / off-prod CI"
> work is **Phase 4**, tracked separately and parked in
> [virusdave/top-level#23](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/23).

## Verified starting state (read directly from `automation`)

- Helios build = plain `tsc` + `vite` over npm (`helios/package.json`):
  `build` = `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` (+ asset copy) then `vite
  build`. No turbo/nx, no build cache, no build/test CI.
- `helios/package.json` has **no** `typecheck` / `test` / `lint` scripts
  (so "build & test always pass on master" is currently unenforceable).
  `vitest` is a dependency but unscripted.
- `tsconfig.server.json` names a `tsBuildInfoFile` but does **not** set
  `incremental` / `composite`, so the file is inert and every server
  build re-typechecks from scratch. `skipLibCheck: true` is already set.
- No `flake.nix` / devShell — toolchain (node/tsc/vite) is whatever the
  host provides.

> Re-verify all of the above in a **fresh ephemeral checkout** before
> editing; do not trust this snapshot blindly. Run any heavy command
> (`npm ci`, `tsc`, `vite build`, `vitest`) under `large-action-lock` —
> the build host is the 2 vCPU / ~2 GiB production box.

## Scope owned by this repo (Helios) — Phase 3

### H1 — Turn on incremental TypeScript (near-zero risk, behavior-preserving)
- Set `"incremental": true` in `tsconfig.server.json` so the existing
  `tsBuildInfoFile` actually caches and warm `build:server` stops
  re-typechecking from scratch. Consider `composite` + project
  references for the client/server split if it's a clean win; don't
  force it.
- Persist the `.tsbuildinfo` between runs (on-box now; graduates to
  `actions/*` cache when an off-prod builder exists — that's Phase 4 / #23).
- Ensure `tsc` `include` does **not** pick up `dist`/build outputs as
  source (`exclude` them) so outputs are never re-consumed as input.

### H2 — Add the missing check scripts + make `check` the required pre-push gate
- Add to `helios/package.json`:
  - `typecheck` → `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit` (and the client
    tsconfig if applicable),
  - `test` → `vitest run`,
  - `check` → runs `typecheck` + `test` (+ a fast build sanity if cheap).
- Wire `check` as the **required pre-push gate** each agent runs before
  `git push` (the decided "master always green" mechanism for now;
  design decision 5). A GitHub-hosted/self-hosted CI backstop +
  branch-protection is Phase 4 (#23), not this epic.

### H3 — Idempotent, self-prerequisite build env (#22 problem 1)
- Add an `ensure-build-env` step the build owns and that is safe cold or
  warm:
  - `npm ci` (lockfile-pinned) when `node_modules` is absent/stale,
    using the on-box `~/.npm` cache;
  - `mkdir -p` every output dir the scripts assume (generalise the
    existing `mkdir -p dist/server/...` so no step fails on a
    missing-or-already-present dir);
  - never assume — and never fail merely because — `node_modules`/`dist`
    already exist.
- Wire `build` / `test` / `check` to call `ensure-build-env` first.
- Add an **idempotence matrix** test (cold checkout; warm `node_modules`;
  stale `dist`; post `git clean -xfd`; run `check` twice) so artifact
  flakiness can't regress.

### H4 — Reproducible toolchain via Nix devShell (operator suggestion D)
- Add a `flake.nix` (or `shell.nix`) devShell pinning node + npm (+ any
  system libs) so `nix develop` / `nix-shell` gives an identical,
  declarative build environment locally and on the box. Additive; pairs
  with `ensure-build-env` (devShell = toolchain, script = project
  prereqs).

## Out of scope (Phase 4 — see #23)
- Moving heavy build/test off the production box onto a builder host.
- Off-prod build/test CI + `actions/*` caches + branch-protection
  required checks.
- Nix **binary cache** / Nix-closure deploy.

## Acceptance
- `helios` has working `typecheck` / `test` / `check` scripts; `check`
  is green on `master` and is the documented required pre-push gate.
- Server build is incremental (warm builds measurably faster) and never
  consumes build outputs as source.
- A cold checkout and a warm checkout both `check` successfully (the
  idempotence matrix passes); the build sets up its own prerequisites.
- A `flake.nix` devShell pins the toolchain.
- Every satisfying commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#22`.

# Helios GAds evolver introspection dashboard — automation child epic

> **Child epic of** [`virusdave/top-level#24`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/24)
> (`gads-evolver-introspection`). The **parent epic plan is authoritative**
> for design, philosophy, IA, data sources, and page content:
> [`virusdave/top-level:docs/epics/gads-evolver-introspection/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/gads-evolver-introspection/EPIC_PLAN.md).
> This child holds the Helios (`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`) implementation
> scope only.
>
> **Every implementation commit** that satisfies any part of this epic MUST
> carry the trailer `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#24`, and SHOULD also
> carry `Phase: P<n>` (`P1`..`P7`) so the cross-repo-completion-sync
> workflow posts a per-phase progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope (one-line)

Build the reserved **`Evolution`** and **`Iteration`** sub-pages under the
existing per-site, grant-gated `/metrics/gads-<site>/` GAds tab system
(IA + grants from [#18](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/18)),
reading the evolver's own decision/outcome data already in the Helios DB /
filesystem. An **introspection surface for how Helios reacted**, not a
re-implementation of Google's ad dashboards. Rapid hill-climb, **not**
audit-grade (decision
[0003](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-kb/decisions/0003-joint-gads-lp-optimization-not-audit-grade.md)).

## Binding constraints

- **Reuse #18's IA, grants (`gads-bronx` / `gads-midtown` / `gads-all`),
  scope registry, and serving model verbatim.** No new route shapes, no
  forked access model. `gads-all` is its own grant, never synthesised.
- **Server-derived site predicate.** Never trust a client-supplied
  site-widening param. Per-site pages must not leak cross-site rows.
- **Cheapest defensible DB use.** Bounded aggregate queries over the
  existing small purpose-built tables. **No** per-event fact table, no
  always-on derivation worker, no rollup/hypertable/CAGG/HLL in V1.
- **Honest approximations.** Every estimate badged; never a fabricated
  precise-looking number. Honest empty states where a write path is not
  yet confirmed.
- **Migrations do not auto-apply on deploy.** Any schema change is applied
  on prod by the agent only after Oracle DB review **and** explicit
  operator approval, then verified live (canon §3).

## Phases (detail in the parent plan §5–§7)

| Phase | Deliverable | Closure criteria |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Data audit + site-scope semantics | Confirm prod population of `gads_ad_attempts`, `landingpage_ad_outcomes`, bundle/L2/L3 artifacts. Decide per-attempt site-scope policy (preferred: add `site text null`, backfill best-effort, hide unknown-scope per-site, show under `gads-all` badged). No per-site page ships until scoping is safe. |
| **P2** | Minimal schema/index support | Add `site` to `gads_ad_attempts` if P1 confirms; cheap indexes only if justified; optional tiny `gads_evolver_runs` run-index table (no large JSON/prompts in DB). No rollup/hypertable/CAGG/HLL. Migration gated on Oracle DB review + operator approval. |
| **P3** | Backend contracts + grant-gated endpoints | Typed `GadsEvolutionResponse` / `GadsIterationRunsResponse` / `GadsIterationRunDetailResponse`; `GET /api/gads/evolution`, `/api/gads/iterations`, `/api/gads/iterations/:runId`; server-derived site predicate; per-site access tests (Bronx user cannot read Midtown/all; `gads-all` explicit; unknown-scope hidden per-site; payload bounded). |
| **P4** | Evolution UI | `/metrics/gads-<site>/evolution` (reserved stub → implemented): learning heartbeat, loop-health KPI strip, action/outcome matrix, hotspots, L3 adoption + LP-reaction panels. Honest empty states + badges. **Mandatory Oracle UI review before ship.** |
| **P5** | Iteration run browser | `/metrics/gads-<site>/iteration`: bounded run timeline + run-detail drilldown (DB-derived + badge when L2 JSON missing). No unbounded historical-file loads. |
| **P6** | L3 + LP enrichment | Latest L3 evaluation summaries; `l3-addenda.md` freshness/hash; whether a later L2 run consumed addenda; `landingpage_ad_outcomes` summary if populated. No approval-workflow / prompt-diff persistence invented here. |
| **P7** | Docs, tests, rollout readiness | Operator runbook; tests pass; UI reviewed; payload/query-cost notes recorded; epics updated; ready for **gated `self-deploy-helios`** (no deploy from the planning worker). |

## Out of scope (V1)

Causal lift / off-policy estimates, win probability, credible intervals,
regret; prompt/rule approval workflow + prompt-diff persistence; trial
monitoring until the trial check tables are real; per-click cost / revenue
/ ROAS; anomaly detection; heatmaps; any Timescale CAGG/hypertable/HLL.

# Dev-loop optimization — `automation` child epic (helios + ads)

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#26](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/26).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/dev-loop-optimization/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the
> `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (Helios monorepo) slice** of that design,
> covering both the `helios/` and `ads/` packages.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation@master` that
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#26
> ```
>
> **Re-read the parent `EPIC_PLAN.md` before starting** — it is the
> single source of truth; this file is a thin index over it.

## Goal

Make the everyday Helios dev loop fast: agents iterate with
**light/targeted** checks scoped to the package/service/files they
touched, while the **full** lint/typecheck/test/build/smoke suite is
owned by CI / the final gate and is no longer hand-run repeatedly under
`large-action-lock` before every commit.

## Binding standards (from the parent, do not weaken)

- Two-gate green tree: fast local + final presubmit. Location split, not
  a waiver — full required CI coverage stays enforced.
- A check leaves pre-commit/local iteration only with equal-or-stronger
  coverage remaining in CI.
- No first-party `any`, no disabled/weakened gates, no `--no-verify`,
  tests deterministic and prod-resource-free (inherited from fleet-green
  [#20](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/20); keep green).

## Scope owned by this repo

1. **Inventory + time** every check in `helios/` and `ads/`: lint,
   server typecheck, client typecheck, unit tests, build, smoke, and the
   fleet-green scanners (no-any, disabled-gate, test-resource). Record
   each command's wall-clock from a fresh ephemeral checkout with a warm
   cache.
2. **Provide light/targeted commands** for every >~30s check. Likely
   splits:
   - per-package lint (`helios/` vs `ads/`) and changed-file lint;
   - server-vs-client typecheck run independently, scoped to the package
     touched, instead of the whole monorepo;
   - focused test runs (single file / pattern / changed behavior) rather
     than the full suite;
   - keep the full `next build` / full test suite / smoke as CI-only.
3. **Document a dev-loop table in `automation`'s `AGENTS.md`**: touched
   area (`helios/` server, `helios/` client, `ads/`) → light local
   command → final presubmit CI status → when an agent may hand-run a
   heavy command (debug a CI failure, harness change, operator ask).
4. **Lighten `.githooks/pre-commit`** from the full-CI mirror to
   fast/targeted checks (changed-file lint + scoped typecheck of the
   touched package), **after** confirming the full gate is a required CI
   status. Do not reintroduce the client-typecheck carve-out fleet-green
   removed — keep it enforced in CI; just don't run the *whole* monorepo
   typecheck in the hook.
5. **Confirm the broken-master window is closed**: the full gate must
   validate the exact commit before it publishes/deploys (required PR
   check / branch protection), or deploy promotion waits for CI green.

## Acceptance

From a fresh ephemeral checkout:

1. `AGENTS.md` dev-loop table present; every >~30s `helios/`/`ads/` check
   has a light/targeted command or a documented heavy-final-only
   exception.
2. Pre-commit hook is fast/targeted; full lint/typecheck (server +
   client)/test/build remains a required CI status, recorded green for a
   sample commit.
3. No coverage deleted; broken-master window closed or interim exception
   documented.
4. Agent Gate Record (two-gate template) attached.

# Helios LP evolution inspection pages — automation child epic

> **Child epic of** [`virusdave/top-level#25`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/25)
> (`lp-evolution-inspection`). The **parent epic plan is authoritative**
> for design, philosophy, IA, data sources, page content, and the
> boundary vs #24:
> [`virusdave/top-level:docs/epics/lp-evolution-inspection/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/lp-evolution-inspection/EPIC_PLAN.md).
> This child holds the Helios (`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`) implementation
> scope only.
>
> **Every implementation commit** that satisfies any part of this epic MUST
> carry the trailer `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#25`, and SHOULD also
> carry `Phase: P<n>` (`P1`..`P7`) so the cross-repo-completion-sync
> workflow posts a per-phase progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope (one-line)

Implement the **LP-system companion** to the GAds evolver introspection
dashboard ([#24](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/24)) under
the existing per-site, grant-gated `/metrics/gads-<site>/` GAds tab system
(IA + grants from [#18](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/18)):
an **LP Evolution** overview with **inferred disapproval attribution**
(LP-related vs ad-related — Google gives only a coarse signal, so this is a
**cross-entity LP/family correlation** engine, not a field lookup),
**suspect-LP / suspect-family** steering, and a **slop-vs-signal**
copy-quality lens, plus an **LP Iteration** per-run / per-candidate
drilldown. It reads the evolver's own
LP decision/outcome data already in the Helios DB / filesystem. An
**introspection surface for how Helios reacted on landing pages and joint
ad/LP decisions**, not a re-implementation of Google's ad dashboards.
Rapid hill-climb, **not** audit-grade (decision
[0003](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-kb/decisions/0003-joint-gads-lp-optimization-not-audit-grade.md)).

## Binding constraints

- **Reuse #18's IA, grants (`gads-bronx` / `gads-midtown` / `gads-all`),
  scope registry, and serving model verbatim.** No new route shapes, no
  forked access model. `gads-all` is its own grant, never synthesised.
- **Coordinate with #24 — do not duplicate its ad-evolver pages.** Keep
  #24's `/evolution` + `/iteration` for ad-evolver loop health; #25 owns
  LP + joint-decision inspection. Cross-link both ways (parent plan §3);
  do not move #24's LP-reaction panel.
- **Server-derived site predicate.** Never trust a client-supplied
  site-widening param. Per-site pages must not leak cross-site rows.
- **Cheapest defensible DB use.** Bounded aggregate queries over the
  existing small tables (`landingpage_ad_outcomes`, `gads_ad_attempts`,
  `gads_lp_rollup`) + bounded reads of recent L2/L3/morning-bundle
  artifacts. **No** per-event fact table, no always-on derivation worker,
  no rollup/hypertable/CAGG/HLL in V1.
- **Honest approximations + first-class `unknown`.** Every estimate badged;
  never a fabricated precise-looking number; **never force an
  attribution** — `unknown` is a real answer. Honest empty states where a
  write path / data field is not yet confirmed.
- **Migrations do not auto-apply on deploy.** Any schema change is applied
  on prod by the agent only after Oracle DB review **and** explicit
  operator approval, then verified live (canon §3).

## Attribution is inference, not a lookup (binding — parent §0.1)

Google **deliberately withholds** the precise reason for a policy limit /
disapproval. The only signal it gives is **which hierarchy level**
(campaign / asset group / ad group / asset / ad) was limited and **which
policy topic** fired. There is **no ad-text-vs-LP source field** to read.
So the LP-vs-ad verdict is **inferred** by **correlating per-entity policy
state over the shared-final-URL/LP and page-family dimensions** (e.g. all
ad groups on a given LP limited while same-family siblings on other LPs
stay clean → that LP is suspect; the pattern may span a whole family). The
fix for a suspect LP must repair the *right* page — **never** flatten the
ad copy **or** the landing page into generic slop.

## Attribution criteria are hill-climbable, not constant (binding — parent §0.2)

The operator approved on the explicit condition that **the attribution
criteria themselves must be hill-climbable** — a simple fixed heuristic
(e.g. "95% of ads pointing at the LP are rejected") will be too crude once
the low-hanging fruit is gone. Binding on the Helios implementation:

- **No magic numbers in code.** Every verdict-deciding threshold, weight,
  and minimum (contrast minimums, suspicion-score weighting, topic→lever
  priors, confidence cutoffs) lives in **one named, versioned criteria
  set**, not scattered literals. V1 may be a deliberately simple ruleset,
  but it must be swappable without rewriting the engine.
- **Versioned + traceable verdicts.** Each attribution result records the
  **criteria version** that produced it plus the raw inputs it saw
  (implicated/clean contrast counts, topics, hierarchy level, outcome
  sequence). Responses carry the active criteria version; the UI badges it
  on every verdict/suspect row and exposes a "how this verdict was decided"
  trace so the operator can tune the *criteria*, not just read output.
- **V1 = explicit substrate for tuning, not a learned model.** An
  automated/learned attribution model is out of scope for V1; making the
  criteria explicit, parameterised, versioned, and auditable is in scope.
  See parent §0.2 / §7.2.2.

## Data + capability gates (P1 must resolve before the engine claims a verdict)

- Confirm prod population/scoping of `landingpage_ad_outcomes`,
  `gads_ad_attempts`, `gads_lp_rollup`, L2/morning-bundle artifacts, L3
  outputs.
- **Confirm whether candidate copy + rejected candidates are recorded** in
  artifacts (the slop-vs-signal "why rejected" view depends on it).
- **Confirm the inference substrate** (the centerpiece depends on it, not
  on a Google source field — there isn't one): (a) we capture **per-entity
  policy state over time + hierarchy level + policy topic**; (b) we can
  **join each entity to its final-URL/LP and to its page family** (likely
  via `landingpage_ad_outcomes` / `gads_lp_rollup` / the cluster registry).
  Without the LP/family join the correlation engine cannot run.
- Confirm whether any cheap LP text snapshot exists (LP-promise match); do
  **not** crawl live pages in V1.
- Emit a **capability matrix** mapping every parent-plan panel (§7–§8) to
  `wired` / `partially wired` / `not wired yet`; missing fields become UI
  badges, not guessed data.

## Phases (detail in the parent plan §6–§8)

| Phase | Deliverable | Closure criteria |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Data audit + capability matrix | Confirm prod population/scoping of the tables/artifacts above; confirm candidate/rejected-candidate presence; **confirm the inference substrate** — per-entity policy state + hierarchy level + policy topic, **and** the entity→final-URL/LP and entity→family join the correlation engine needs (no Google ad-vs-LP source field exists); produce the panel→capability matrix. No per-site page ships until site scoping is safe; the engine must have the LP/family join before claiming a suspect. |
| **P2** | Minimal schema/index support | Reuse #24's `site` fix for `gads_ad_attempts` if landed; else add `site text null` + best-effort backfill; hide unknown-scope per-site, show under `gads-all` badged. Optional tiny artifact/run-index table **only if** P1 proves scans are expensive (no large JSON/prompts in DB). Cheap indexes only if justified by plans. No rollup/hypertable/CAGG/HLL. Migration gated on Oracle DB review + operator approval. |
| **P3** | Backend contracts + **correlation/inference engine** | Typed `GadsLpEvolutionResponse` / `GadsLpIterationRunsResponse` / `GadsLpIterationRunDetailResponse` (capability flags in every response); grant-gated `GET /api/gads/lp-evolution`, `/api/gads/lp-iterations`, `/api/gads/lp-iterations/:runId`; server-derived site predicate; bounded ranges. **Cross-entity correlation engine (parent §7.2):** group per-entity policy state by shared final-URL/LP and family; emit `lp_related`/`ad_related`/`mixed`/`undetermined` with evidence grade, confidence bucket, and implicated-vs-clean contrast counts (anti-coincidence guard); never force a verdict. **Criteria are a single named, versioned set (parent §0.2): no magic numbers in code; each verdict records its criteria version + raw inputs; the response carries the active criteria version.** Tests cover correlation logic (suspect LP when siblings clean; no false suspect on thin contrast) + access (Bronx cannot read Midtown/all; `gads-all` explicit; unknown-scope hidden per-site; payload bounded). |
| **P4** | LP Evolution UI (overview + attribution + suspect LP/family) | `/metrics/gads-<site>/lp-evolution` (parent §7): scope/freshness/capability strip, LP heartbeat, attribution snapshot + `?panel=attribution` detail, **suspect-LP / suspect-family ranked list (parent §7.2.1)**, planned-action×outcome matrix, hotspots, funnel guardrail, recent decision log. Honest empty/low-confidence states + contrast counts; no fake attribution. **Mandatory Oracle UI review before ship.** |
| **P5** | Slop-vs-signal lens | Quality triage on overview + `?panel=slop-signal` (parent §7.3): deterministic context-token preservation, generic-phrase + reuse detector, intent specificity, hook preservation, optional LP-promise match (badged if unwired), chosen-vs-rejected comparison, context-loss watchlist, **positive-examples table**. Deterministic/explainable V1 lens; candidate/rejected absence handled honestly; no opaque LLM score required. |
| **P6** | LP Iteration browser | `/metrics/gads-<site>/lp-iteration` (parent §8): bounded run timeline + run detail (decision flow + attempt/candidate table), candidate detail drawer, bounded artifact links, DB-only fallback + badge when L2 JSON missing. No unbounded historical-file loads. Run-detail links from #24 can target this page. |
| **P7** | Docs, tests, rollout readiness | Operator runbook (read attribution + evidence grades; interpret slop risk; interpret `unknown`; debug missing site scope; #24 vs #25); access + classifier tests; query-cost notes; UI reviewed; epics updated; ready for **gated `self-deploy-helios`** (no deploy from the planning worker). |

## Backend contract sketch (P3)

```ts
GadsLpEvolutionResponse          // overview + attribution + slop/signal summaries + capability flags
GadsLpIterationRunsResponse      // bounded run timeline
GadsLpIterationRunDetailResponse // single run: decision flow + attempt/candidate rows + artifact links
```

Each response carries `capabilities` flags (`siteScopedAttempts`,
`entityPolicyState`, `policyTopics`, `entityLpJoin`, `familyMapping`,
`candidateText`, `rejectedCandidates`, `lpTextSnapshot`, `lpRollup`) so the
UI badges exactly what is / isn't wired. (Note: there is **no**
`explicitPolicySource` flag — Google does not expose an ad-vs-LP cause;
the verdict comes from the correlation engine, gated on `entityLpJoin` /
`familyMapping`.) Site scope is derived server-side from the
authenticated GAds metrics tab context, never from a widening query param;
follow Helios's existing route/site-encoding convention (the binding rule
is the access model, not the literal endpoint strings).

The attribution payload also carries the **active criteria version** (e.g.
`attributionCriteriaVersion`) and, per verdict/suspect row, the criteria
version + raw inputs that produced it (parent §0.2 / §7.2.2), so the UI can
badge which ruleset decided each call and the operator can hill-climb the
criteria rather than just read their current output.

## Out of scope (V1)

Causal lift / off-policy estimates, win probability, credible intervals,
regret; prompt/rule approval workflow + prompt-diff persistence; opaque LLM
copy-quality score; live LP crawling for promise-match; per-click cost /
revenue / ROAS; anomaly detection; heatmaps; any Timescale
CAGG/hypertable/HLL.

# Prospective Pending-Purchase Classifier — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#33](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/33).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md`](../../../../designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md)
> and the staged plan + the 8 operator decisions live in
> [`docs/epics/prospective-pending-purchase/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md),
> both in the top-level repo. This child epic exists because **all
> implementation lands in `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (the Helios app
> under `helios/`)**: the worker classifier, server routes, DB schema,
> review UI, and the inventory lifecycle are all Helios surfaces.
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `automation` master and
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#33
> ```

## Scope owned by this repo (Helios)

Two parallel tracks. The **classifier track** replaces the reactive
pending-purchase generator with a prospective Bedrock-driven one behind a
deterministic validator. The **pricing-safety lifecycle track** closes the
first-sale mispricing race for brand-new SKUs. They are independent and
meet only where catalog-apply creates the live product the lifecycle then
prices.

### Classifier track

- **C0 — Amp → `import_json` bridge runbook** (already operational; no
  code). Purchase 151113 packet #53 was built this way. Documents the
  manual escalation path that stays as the human-triggered escape hatch.
- **C1 — Refactor the generator into seams.** Carve
  `collectPendingPurchaseContext`, `buildPendingPurchasePacket`,
  `persistGeneratedPendingPurchasePacket` out of
  `worker/jobs/generatePendingPurchasePacketJob.ts`; no behavior change
  yet. Isolate the legacy rule-based row-builder behind ONE seam **so it
  can be deleted at cutover (C8)** — it is not a preserved path
  (decision 4: go direct).
- **C2 — Hint bundle storage + admin API.** New
  `pending_purchase_hint_bundles` / `pending_purchase_hint_documents`
  tables; admin endpoints; `hintBundleId` on the generate job + route.
  v1 = pasted arbitrary hint text only (decision 2).
- **C3 — Hint fact extraction + intent classification.**
  `extractPendingPurchaseHintFacts` (Bedrock JSON for menus; deterministic
  for Sweed PO JSON). First LLM-classify the hint for *how* it helps
  (canonical SKU list / ordered-items expectation / free-text description /
  line-item list — decision 2), then extract inert cited facts.
- **C4 — Prospective LLM classifier.**
  `classifyPendingPurchasePacketWithLlm`; event-level prompt over the full
  order + live catalog + hint facts; `PendingPurchaseLlmDraftRow` output
  contract (model proposes a reuse link, never authorizes it). Default
  model = the current "standard, most capable general reasoning model,"
  chosen dynamically + a below-the-fold Bedrock config page for rare
  per-context overrides (decision 1).
- **C5 — Deterministic validator / reconciler (the safety layer).**
  Validate every reuse candidate vs the live product; taxonomy/size/pack/
  house-brand guards; duplicate detection; Helios (not the model) computes
  deterministic fields + price + inline market evidence.
- **C6 — Review-UI surfacing.** Show confidence, rationale, hint
  citations, reuse candidates, and new-brand/new-group/no-comps warnings
  (all from the passthrough `raw_row_json`).
- **C7 — Apply-time drift guard + optional post-apply refresh.**
  Generated-reuse drift guard in the apply job; optional enqueue of created
  product ids after apply.
- **C8 — Direct cutover + legacy deletion.** Switch
  `catalog.pending_purchases.generate` to the LLM-prospective path and
  **delete the legacy rule-based classifier** (decision 4). A short
  dev-only shadow comparison during validation is fine, but it ships as the
  single path — no permanent `generationMode` toggle, no legacy fallback.

### Pricing-safety lifecycle track (independent; can ship first)

- **L1 — Lifecycle record + gates (no reverse move).**
  `purchase_inventory_lifecycle_runs` / `_items` tables keyed by
  `(dealer_id, po_id)`; start / verify-quarantine / purchase-market-refresh
  / purchase-reprice routes; market-completion (timestamp-based) +
  price-applied (live-price-equality) verifiers; reuse the existing pricing
  review UI. No release route yet.
- **L2 — Bulk quarantine repair + gated release.** Extract a shared
  stock-transfer service from the one-way move-to-inspection; purchase-
  scoped bulk move-to-inspection (repair); reverse + bulk **release** to a
  chosen FOR SALE room (dropdown, default "FOR SALE - Sales Floor" —
  decision 6) with immediate-before-transfer preflight (live price + live
  quarantine re-verify), post-transfer verification, and partial-failure
  recovery. Quarantine is **optional, not enforced** (decision 5): the UI
  offers bulk move-to-quarantine + full lifecycle OR reprice-in-place
  skipping the release/move-back. Repricing is SKU-level with a small badge
  when a SKU already has on-floor stock (decision 8).
- **L3 — Automation + monitoring.** `inventory.lifecycle.advance` job to
  poll/advance async gates; quarantine-breach monitor; alerts (lot in FOR
  SALE before priced, market timeout, price-apply failure, release partial
  failure).

## Dependency order (for task breakdown)

```
C0 (done) ─▶ C1 ─▶ C4 ─▶ C5 ─▶ (C6, C7) ─▶ C8
              C2 ─▶ C3 ─────────▲
L1 ─▶ L2 ─▶ L3        (lifecycle track, parallel to the classifier track)
```

- C1 unblocks C4; C2 unblocks C3; C3 feeds C4; C5 depends on C4; C6 & C7
  depend on C5; C8 depends on C5+C6+C7.
- L-track is fully parallel and independent of the classifier track.

## Out of scope (explicit)

- **FT-1** hint file uploads (CSV/PDF/manifests/POs/catalogs/scrapings) —
  near-term follow-up, separate task.
- **FT-2** auto-generated proposal packets — gated on FT-3.
- **FT-3** LitAlerts competitor-data redesign — its own future top-level
  epic (decision 7); not created here.
- **FT-4** broader pricing process/engine redesign — its own future epic.
- Any change to the human review + apply approval gate (kept as-is).

## Required gates (per canon)

- **Oracle critical-infra / DB review** for the validator (C5), the apply
  drift guard (C7), the hint tables + generate-job changes (C2), and the
  lifecycle tables + release safety (L1/L2). DB migrations apply on prod
  only after Oracle blessing **and** explicit operator approval, then
  live-sentinel verification.
- **Green tree** — repo-documented light/targeted lint/typecheck/test for
  touched Helios areas in the dev loop; full presubmit before merge. No
  first-party `any`; no bug-masking fallbacks.
- **Oracle UI review** for C6 review-UI changes, the L1 lifecycle panel,
  and any operator-facing copy.

## Completion signal

This child epic is complete when both tracks have landed on `automation`
master with `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#33` trailers: the legacy
classifier is deleted and `catalog.pending_purchases.generate` runs the
validated prospective path (C8), and the quarantine→reprice→release
lifecycle is operator-usable end-to-end with its hard release gates (L3).

# Helios catalog-pricing overhaul — step 1 — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#35](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/35).
> The authoritative umbrella is
> [`docs/epics/catalog-pricing-overhaul/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo. This child epic covers **only step 1** of that umbrella
> (the operator's first #35 comment); later steps are separate child epics.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation` master that satisfies
> any part of this child epic MUST carry a cross-repo completion trailer
> linking back to the parent epic — but see the **Caution** in *Validation*
> below: because #35 is a long-lived multi-step umbrella, confirm the exact
> `Satisfies:` target with the operator before landing so a single completed
> child does not prematurely close #35.

## Step-1 operator ask (verbatim intent)

> Our first step will be a temporary page to let the operator request to see
> the categorical family groups described, and see which product variants
> would be included. We'll use this temporary page to iterate until this part
> works correctly.
>
> Also, verify that our use of LitAlerts now includes geographic limits in the
> request, so we can limit to (a) close competitors and (b) near-mid market
> data without timing out the server requests constantly.

This step is deliberately a **scaffold for iteration**: get family grouping
provably correct and confirm market pulls are geographically bounded, before
building the richer per-family pricing/market UX in later steps.

## Scope owned by this child epic

### T1 — Temporary "Categorical Family Explorer" page

An operator-only, clearly-temporary Helios page (e.g. route
`catalog/family-explorer`, labelled TEMPORARY in-page) that lets the operator:

- Pick the grouping mode: **[nonbrand] categorical family** or **brand
  categorical family** (vendor family is out of scope until the vendor→brand
  mapping exists — say so in the UI).
- Choose the source subset to group over. The operator's step-1 comment does
  not ask for subsets, so the **minimal** deliverable is the whole variant
  catalog (umbrella A-i). "Currently in stock at site" (A-ii) is an optional
  stretch for this step; the richer A-iii/iv/v subsets are later steps. Ship
  the whole-catalog case first; do not block step 1 on any subset.
- See, for the chosen mode/subset, the **resolved family groups** and, for
  each group, **exactly which variants/SKUs are included** (name, SKU,
  brand, category, subcategory, pack qty, unit size, and the size "group" it
  resolved to). The point is auditable membership so the operator can confirm
  the grouping is right.

Reuse, do not rebuild:
- `helios/src/shared/domain/catalogCohort.ts`
  (`buildCatalogCohortKey`, `parseUnitSize`, `CatalogCohortInput`) for the
  non-brand key; extend the key with `brandNorm` for brand families.
- Catalog variant data from `catalog_groups` / catalog snapshots as used by
  `helios/src/server/db/queries/catalogMarketMatchQueries.ts` (`CatalogVariant`).
- Standard page/route wiring: component+loader under
  `helios/src/client/routes/`, registered in
  `helios/src/client/app/router.tsx`; a `registerXRoutes` server module
  registered in `helios/src/server/app/buildServer.ts`; `loadJson` client
  helper; `requireSessionUser(...,'viewer')` on read endpoints.

### T2 — Unit-size "group" equivalency (the operator's core correctness bar)

The family grouping MUST expose a **unit-size group** that implements the
operator's "morally equivalent" size buckets, because plain numeric size is
not what he means:

- Prerolls: roll novelty/marketing sizes into standard ones — 0.6 g → 0.5 g,
  1.1 g → 1.0 g — with **candidate** standard buckets around 0.35, 0.5, 1.0,
  1.5, 2.0 g (boundaries to be confirmed with the operator, see below).
- Other categories keep their natural sizes (edibles ~10 mg; flower 3.5/7/14/28
  g; vapes by size + all-in-one/disposable attribute).

Investigation found this is **not** currently implemented: `catalogCohort.ts`
keys on exact parsed size and `marketMatch/listingParse.ts`'s `sameSizeFamily`
uses numeric tolerance (`max(0.05, size*0.08)`) that does **not** group
0.5/0.6 or 1.0/1.1. Implement a small, well-tested, category-aware size-group
normalizer as a **single-source shared module** (unit-tested with the
operator's examples), and in step 1 wire it **only into the explorer
grouping** so the operator can validate it in isolation. Do **not** rewire
`catalogCohort.ts`'s cohort keys or `sameSizeFamily`'s market matching in this
step — changing those alters the semantics of existing pricing runs and
belongs to the later step that actually touches the pricing/market path. The
bucket table must be easy to review and adjust as the operator iterates.
**Post a representative sample of the prerolls' structured data on #35 and
confirm the bucket boundaries with the operator before hard-coding them** (the
operator explicitly invited follow-up questions here).

### T3 — Verify (and, if needed, enforce) geographic limiting of LitAlerts pulls

This task is **independent of the T1 explorer page**, which pulls no market
data (per-family market pricing is out of scope for step 1). It verifies the
operator's actual ask — that *our use of LitAlerts* in the shared
pricing/market-evidence code is geographically bounded and does not fall back
to unbounded statewide pulls that time out.

Wording reconciliation (must be stated in the closure comment): the operator
says "geographic limits **in the request**", but the LitAlerts partner client
(`helios/src/worker/litalerts/partnerClient.ts`) exposes **no** lat/lng/radius
request parameter — its params are `state`, `includeOOS`, `categoryFilter`,
`subcategoryFilter`, `brandIds`. Helios instead implements the geographic
limit **client-side by retailer selection**: it picks the nearest retailers
(from geocoded `litalerts_retailer_locations`) and issues per-retailer pulls.
The child epic's job is to confirm this selection actually achieves the
intent (bounded, non-timing-out pulls limited to close + near-mid retailers)
and to surface, in the closure comment, that the limit is done by retailer
selection rather than a request param — asking the operator to confirm that
satisfies him, or to say if he specifically wants a request-level radius
(in which case checking whether the LitAlerts API even offers one becomes a
follow-up, not step-1 work).

- The live-evidence path in `helios/src/worker/pricing/litAlertsMarket.ts`
  already fans out over the ~50 nearest retailers
  (`PRICING_NEARBY_RETAILER_FETCH_LIMIT`) via
  `/v1/retailers/:id/products?brandIds=` rather than the statewide
  `/v1/brands/:id/products` "that routinely times out". Distance banding
  (near/mid/far) is in `helios/src/shared/domain/pricingGeneration.ts`.
- **Fan-out count is not the same as a band limit.** The ~50-nearest cap
  bounds request *volume*; it does not by itself guarantee those retailers
  fall within the operator's "(a) close competitors" (near band) or "(b)
  near-mid market" (near + mid bands). The verification MUST establish where
  (if anywhere) evidence is actually filtered to near / near+mid before
  aggregation, and whether the fan-out can currently include far-band
  retailers. Map the operator's (a)/(b) explicitly onto the near / near+mid
  bands and confirm that mapping is enforced, not just assumed.
- Deliverable: a focused test/assertion over the shared market-evidence code
  that any live LitAlerts pull is geographically bounded (nearest-retailer
  fan-out with the near/near+mid band limit applied) and **never** issues the
  unbounded statewide brand call. If any relied-upon path can still issue an
  unbounded statewide pull, or can pull far-band retailers into the "market"
  aggregate, fix it.
- Also confirm the partner client's timeout/retry behavior
  (`helios/src/worker/litalerts/partnerClient.ts`) is unchanged and adequate;
  the fix is bounding request scope, not lengthening timeouts.

This step verifies existing behavior and closes any gap; it is explicitly
**not** a rewrite of the LitAlerts subsystem.

## Explicitly out of scope for step 1 (later child epics)

- The full A subset picker (ever-in-stock / recent-receive / family-superset).
- Per-family market pricing view, mismatch bulk-tagging + re-run, price/promo
  application, and the detailed click-through market-data page (umbrella D).
- Vendor categorical families.
- Making the temporary page permanent/polished — it is a throwaway iteration
  surface; the durable UX comes in later steps.

## Validation

Each landing commit MUST:

1. Land green on `automation` CI: `cd helios && npm run check` (server + client
   typecheck + `vitest run`) and `npm run build`. Add unit tests for the
   size-group normalizer (T2) covering the operator's preroll examples and for
   the geographic-bounding assertion (T3). No first-party `any`; no
   bug-masking fallbacks; deterministic, prod-resource-free tests.
2. Be visible on `vps-nixos-3` after the sanctioned `self-deploy-helios`
   (never manual `systemctl restart` of the helios units).
3. Carry the cross-repo completion trailer on the master-landing commit (or
   the final commit of a multi-commit change). **Caution — #35 is a
   long-lived, multi-step umbrella.** A `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#35`
   trailer feeds `cross-repo-completion-sync` / `close-completed-issues`,
   which close the top-level epic once *every delegated child* has a
   completion. If this step-1 child is the only delegated child when it
   completes, that trailer could **prematurely close #35** before later steps
   are materialised. Before landing, the automation fleet MUST confirm the
   intended trailer target with the operator on #35 — reference the
   materialised step-1 child issue (and rely on the delegation link back to
   #35) rather than blindly closing #35 — so the umbrella stays open across
   steps. Do not assume `Satisfies: #35` is correct here without that check.
4. Honor canon gates: Oracle design review (before implementing) and diff
   review (before landing) for this operator-facing surface; Oracle UI review
   of the page's mobile layout / signal-to-noise / next-action; a recorded
   DB cost/plan for any new catalog query (reuse existing indexed catalog
   reads where possible). Record the Agent Gate Record on each landing.

## Completion signal for the child

This child epic is done when:

- The temporary Categorical Family Explorer renders correct non-brand and
  brand family groups with auditable per-group variant membership, using the
  reviewed size-group equivalency (T1 + T2), demonstrated on `vps-nixos-3`.
- The geographic-limiting verification (T3) is landed with a passing
  assertion/test and a short written confirmation.
- An operator-facing closure/status comment is posted on
  `virusdave/top-level#35` prefixed `<!-- task-dag:status -->` (the automated
  `<!-- task-dag:completion -->` cross-repo signal is emitted by the peer
  repo's completion-sync workflow from the `Satisfies:` trailer — do not
  hand-post it), including the live page URL on `vps-nixos-3`, the commit
  links, the confirmed size-bucket table, and the geographic-band mapping
  with the request-param-vs-retailer-selection reconciliation from T3, so the
  operator can iterate from a concrete baseline into step 2.

issues.body:
## Why

Follow-up from issue #55 competitor-pricing coverage work. The pricing/market-evidence path picks nearby competitors from the geocoded [`litalerts_retailer_locations`](helios/src/server/db/migrations/027_litalerts_retailer_geo.sql) table. That table is only refreshed when someone runs the one-off [`helios/scripts/backfill-litalerts-retailer-geo.mts`](helios/scripts/backfill-litalerts-retailer-geo.mts) by hand.

When it goes stale, newly-opened dispensaries are absent (distance = unknown, weight 0) and silently cannot drive price. This exact rot was observed: the table was ~6 weeks stale (555 rows vs 588 live), and refreshing it added **13 more near+mid (<=3mi) competitors** (79 -> 92) that were previously invisible.

New dispensaries open rarely, so a weekly refresh is ample.

## What

Add a periodic (weekly) worker job that does what the one-off backfill does: pull `/v1/retailers?state=NY`, upsert into `litalerts_retailer_locations`, geocode any missing/changed coords via the Census geocoder, refresh `last_seen_at`.

Design notes (from Oracle review):
- Do NOT shell out to the `.mts` one-off. Lift its upsert+geocode logic into a worker-importable module and reuse the existing [`helios/src/worker/geocoder/census.ts`](helios/src/worker/geocoder/census.ts) client, which already centralizes the 1-RPS Census rate limiter (the one-off's 200ms sleep is looser than the shared limiter).
- Register via the existing `configWorkersScheduler` pattern: job type + payload in `shared/contracts/domain/jobs.ts`, handler in `worker/jobs/`, registration in `jobRegistry.ts`/`jobPools.ts`, a scheduler hook in `configWorkersScheduler.ts`, and a `config_worker_schedules` row (weekly window). Idempotent dedupe key (week bucket).
- Keep it read-only w.r.t. everything except `litalerts_retailer_locations`; it must not touch `sales_reconciliation`.

## Acceptance
- Weekly job refreshes the table without manual intervention; verified enqueue + one successful run on prod.
- Deterministic, prod-resource-free unit test for the lifted upsert/geocode module (mock the partner + Census clients).
- `cd helios && npm run check` green.

## Helios: agent-waste review-queue UI + admin navbar entry + escalating review reminder

**Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
— "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality" (design
[`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md) §5, Lever D).
**Backend already landed:** the `agent-waste` observation store + reviewed-advisory
selector/injection shipped in `Nicponskis/github-worker`
([issue #3](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/issues/3), closed; see
[`docs/AGENT_WASTE.md`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/docs/AGENT_WASTE.md)).
This issue is the **Helios (this repo, `helios/`) UI half** the operator asked
for, deliberately split out because it is production-frontend work in a
different repo than the dispatcher.

### Background (self-contained)

Agents record **structured observations** of wasted effort (footguns, repeated
startup work, etc.) to a local store. A human reviews that backlog and, when a
pattern is worth acting on, promotes it to the reviewed **advisory catalog**
([`advisories.yaml`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml)
in top-level) or to a guardrail. Nothing agent-authored is ever auto-injected;
the human review step is the safety gate. Today that backlog has **no UI** — it
is only reachable via a CLI. This issue adds the operator-facing surface.

### Asks (from the operator on github-worker#3)

1. **Review-queue page(s)** listing the observations awaiting human review
   (each row: time, severity, kind, id, repo, and any free-form note). An admin
   should be able to triage from here (at minimum view/dismiss; ideally a link
   toward "promote to advisory"). Free-form notes are shown for humans and are
   **never** injected into agents.
2. **Navbar entry** in a sensible, discoverable location, **admin-gated**, so an
   admin can find the review queue. Reuse the canonical Helios nav rather than a
   new pattern — see `helios/src/client/components/TreeNav.tsx` /
   `SidebarNavContext.tsx`, route registration in
   `helios/src/client/app/router.tsx`, and the admin/permission gating in
   `helios/src/shared/domain/permissions.ts` (do a reuse-search-before-build
   pass per canon).
3. **Escalating, dismissable review reminder:** a notice reminding the admin to
   review the queue that becomes **progressively more frequent** the more
   backlogged the queue is / the more wasteful agents have been, and re-escalates
   on re-engagement until the backlog is handled. Dismissable, not modal-nagging.

### Data contract (ready today)

The github-worker CLI exposes the backlog as machine-readable JSON:

```
agent-waste backlog --format json      # array of observation events for review
agent-waste list --format json         # all raw events (debug/admin)
```

Store: append-only NDJSON at
`${GITHUB_WORKER_STATE_DIR:-~/.local/state/github-worker}/agent-waste.ndjson`
on the github-worker host (see `docs/AGENT_WASTE.md` for the exact schema and
path precedence). Event fields: `time, kind, id, severity, repo, task_sha,
estimated_wasted_tokens, estimated_wasted_seconds, note, host`.

### Open question for the implementer (flag, don't guess)

Helios and the github-worker dispatcher may run on **different hosts**. Decide
how Helios reads the backlog: same-host read of the NDJSON / shelling out to
`agent-waste backlog --json`, versus a small read-only bridge/endpoint. Confirm
the deployment topology with the operator before wiring it. (Design §5/§12: the
store is intentionally single-host local today.)

### Acceptance

- Admin can reach a review-queue page from the Helios navbar; page renders the
  current backlog from the `agent-waste backlog --json` contract.
- The review reminder escalates with backlog size/recency and is dismissable.
- Admin-gated; mobile-friendly; canonical nav reused (not re-invented).
- Canon gates for UI work apply (Oracle UI review for layout/nav/copy;
  reuse-search recorded; Agent Gate Record).

_Filed as a tracked follow-up to github-worker#3 under parent epic
virusdave/top-level#34._
