# Helios catalog-pricing overhaul — step 2 — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#35](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/35).
> The authoritative umbrella is
> [`docs/epics/catalog-pricing-overhaul/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo. This child epic covers **step 2** of that umbrella; step 1
> ([#55](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/55)) shipped the
> temporary Categorical Family Explorer + the T2 size-group normalizer + the
> LitAlerts geographic-limit verification.
>
> **Do not close #35** on completion, and do not put `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#35`
> on any landing commit without operator confirmation — #35 is a long-lived,
> multi-step umbrella (same caution as #55).

## What this is (operator clarification — read first)

**This is NOT the final pricing view.** It is a simple, DIAGNOSTIC enhancement
to the existing TEMPORARY Family Explorer page (route `catalog/family-explorer`)
so the operator can **see the LitAlerts listing-data matching happening against
the brand-categorical-families, and judge how well that matching + scoring
works.** The expectation is that match/data quality is currently poor (prior
selected subsets of pricing data have been terrible in general), and that we
will likely tweak the matcher substantially before any of this is good enough to
feed a real pricing page.

So the deliverable is **matching visibility, warts and all** — the same
"auditable membership" philosophy the step-1 page already uses for catalog
variants, extended to the market-listing side. It is a tool to reveal and
iterate on matcher quality, NOT to produce clean prices for repricing.

Consequences for scope:
- **Show the matcher's actual output** (candidate listings + the real
  per-candidate scores/factors), so what the operator audits is the same
  matching that would eventually feed pricing — not a new bespoke aggregate.
- **Do not hide bad matches or awkward data.** Stale data, unrecorded pack
  counts, weak brand mappings, low scores — these are exactly what the operator
  wants to SEE. Label them; don't gate them out.
- Price is shown as one context column, not the point. No polished price
  aggregate / repricing math in this step.

### Verbatim operator asks

Iteration request:
> the groupings look sane for non-brand categorical families. When ACTUALLY
> doing the repricing, the operator will likely want to navigate by
> brand-category-family, often pricing all peers within that family at the same
> price point. Subdivide each categorical family by brand on the next iteration
> of this review page, and let's start attaching "Litalerts pricing data from
> the brand-categorical-family" to the per-brand categorical family groupings.
> It can start collapsed, and i can expand on that page or click-to-new-tab
> details page.

Clarification:
> What i asked for is not the final pricing view. It's a simple enhancement to
> the last page to see the listing data matching happening to the brand
> categorical families and see how well that matching and scoring works. We may
> need to tweak it substantially before the data quality is good enough to
> actually feed a real pricing page. Prior selected subsets of pricing data have
> been terrible, in general.

## Scope

### T1 — Brand-subdivided Family Explorer (client-only)

Restructure the temp page to a hierarchy: **non-brand categorical family →
per-brand sub-family → variants**. Implement in the pure shared module
`helios/src/shared/domain/familyExplorer.ts`: compute the non-brand family key,
then subdivide members by `familyBrandKey`. Render non-brand family header +
total count → per-brand sub-rows (count) → variant table. Unit-test the nesting
(a non-brand family with multiple brands subdivides correctly; deterministic
order). No new server data. Size: **S**.

### T2 — Attach LitAlerts match candidates + scores per brand-categorical-family (diagnostic)

Per brand-categorical-family (brand + category + subcategory + size-group +
pack), show the LitAlerts listings the matcher associates with it AND how it
scored them, collapsed by default, expandable in-page (a click-through details
route is optional for v1).

**Reuse the REAL matcher/scorer** so the audit reflects production matching:
- `scoreCatalogFuzzy` / `scoreCatalogFuzzyFactors` +
  `applyVerdictPostFilter` in `helios/src/shared/marketMatch/confidence.ts`
  (the same scorer `loadGroupReview` uses per catalog group).
- The override-aware brand resolution + category-alias + fuzzy fetch in
  `helios/src/server/db/queries/catalogMarketMatchQueries.ts`. A
  brand-categorical-family may span several catalog groups; surface the
  candidate listings scored against the family's dimensions (extract the
  override-expansion + fuzzy-fetch into a shared helper — it becomes its third
  caller).

For each family, the collapsed summary + expanded detail should make matcher
quality legible, e.g.:
- candidate count, and how many score above / below the usual threshold,
- per-candidate: listingName, brand (raw + normalized), category_norm, parsed
  size + folded size-group, price (context), retailer, and the **score + factor
  breakdown** (brand / category / size / name-token) so the operator can see
  WHY a listing did or didn't match,
- honest mapping state: `mapped` / `operator-says-none` (explicit-null override)
  / `unmapped` (no override → `lower(trim(brand))` fallback, labeled),
- caveats surfaced inline, not hidden (see below).

Fetch lazily per family on expand. Size: **M** (composition of existing pieces).

## Data facts (Oracle-reviewed, prod-verified 2026-07-06) — caveats to SURFACE, not gate

These are real properties of the current data. Because this is a matching-quality
audit, **display/label them; do not filter them out.**

- **Prices**: `fuzzy_skus.raw_input_jsonb` has no `preTaxPrice`/`postTaxPrice`.
  Derive as the existing code does: `preTax = salePrice ?? normalPrice`,
  `postTax = preTax × 1.13`. Keys present: `normalPrice`, `salePrice`,
  `currentStock`, `retailerId`, `productId`, `listingName`, `brand`, `category`,
  `url`, `configIdx`.
- **Stale snapshot**: all 693,464 partner-product rows were captured
  **2026-05-25 → 2026-05-27** (~6 weeks old), a one-shot snapshot, not a feed.
  Label "as of 2026-05-26" on the page. Fine for auditing the MATCHER; a fresh
  capture is a separate ops prerequisite before this ever feeds real pricing.
- **Duplicate rows**: ~57% of listings have 2–4 rows (same `source_listing_id`,
  different `raw_input_hash`). Dedup to latest per `source_listing_id`
  (`distinct on (source_listing_id) … order by source_listing_id,
  source_captured_at desc`) so a listing isn't triple-counted in the audit.
- **`pack_count_norm` and `subcategory_norm` are NULL on ALL rows.** The market
  side can only match brand × canonical-category × (folded) size. Surface this
  as a visible limitation on pack>1 / subcategory-bearing families (e.g. a
  "pack not matchable market-side" note) — this poor matchability is itself part
  of what the operator is evaluating.
- **Distance banding available (nice-to-have context)**:
  `raw_input_jsonb->>'retailerId'` → `litalerts_retailer_locations`
  (601 rows, 563 geocoded); haversine vs `helios_store_locations` +
  `classifyPricingDistanceBand` already exist in
  `helios/src/worker/pricing/litAlertsMarket.ts`. Optional band label
  (near/mid/far/unknown) per listing; secondary to the score display.
- **Brand mapping**: `catalog_litalerts_brand_overrides` (244 catalog brands,
  223 override rows, 22 explicit-null, ~21 unmapped). Reuse the override
  expansion; render the three honest states above.
- **Perf**: lazy per-family fetch ≈ 20ms via partial index
  `fuzzy_skus_partner_brand_category_idx`. Do NOT eager-aggregate the whole
  catalog.

## Explicitly out of scope (later steps)

- The real per-family pricing view / repricing math / price+promo application
  (umbrella D).
- Improving the matcher itself beyond what's needed to display it — though this
  page exists precisely to inform that later matcher tuning.
- Multipack market matching (needs pack parsing from listingName).
- Verdict/review integration — link to the existing per-group `catalog/market-data`
  surface for the reviewed/verdict view; don't replicate it.
- Making the page permanent/polished.

## Validation (each landing commit)

- Green `cd helios && npm run check` + `npm run build`; unit tests for the brand
  nesting (T1) and for the match-surface dedup/fold/mapping-state logic (T2); no
  first-party `any`; deterministic, prod-resource-free tests.
- Recorded DB cost/plan for the new fuzzy fetch (reuse existing partial indexes;
  lazy per-family).
- Oracle design review (one already on file, see below) + diff review before
  landing + UI review of mobile layout / signal-to-noise / next-action.
- Visible on `vps-nixos-3` after `self-deploy-helios`. Agent Gate Record on each
  landing. Confirm any cross-repo trailer target with the operator first (do NOT
  prematurely close #35).

---

*A prod-verified Oracle design review informed the data facts and the
reuse-the-real-scorer approach above. The original framing over-scoped this as a
pricing view; per the operator clarification it is a matching-quality diagnostic.*

issues.body:
# Helios catalog-pricing overhaul — step 3 — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#35](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/35).
> The authoritative umbrella is
> [`docs/epics/catalog-pricing-overhaul/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo. This child epic covers **step 3** of that umbrella. Prior
> steps shipped:
> [step 1 = automation#55](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/55)
> (temporary Categorical Family Explorer + size-group normalizer + LitAlerts
> geographic-limit verification) and
> [step 2 = automation#58](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/58)
> (brand-subdivided families + a lazy per-brand-categorical-family LitAlerts
> **market-match diagnostic panel** with candidate scores, per-factor
> breakdown, and data caveats).
>
> **Do not close #35** on completion, and do not put
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#35` on any landing commit without operator
> confirmation — #35 is a long-lived, multi-step umbrella (same caution as #55
> and #58). Reference this step-3 child issue and rely on the delegation link
> back to #35.

## Step-3 operator ask (verbatim intent)

> "Providing feedback in an efficient way" *in the page itself* is the next
> step to take. Consult with Oracle on how this should be arranged to maximize
> operator efficiency on site-reviewing matches (ideas to consider include
> highlighting significant price outliers for particular review, potentially
> having the operator confirm or explain how to resolve a competitor name
> parsing / extraction issue — MOST retailers will mostly stick to a preferred
> naming convention that tends to include some aspect of unit and/or total
> sizing and/or pack qty. They tend to follow at least one convention per
> category/subcategory, if not one convention for their whole catalog. Once
> that convention is understood for that retailer, it can provide strong hints
> for subsequent listings from that retailer being examined / parsed. Consult
> with oracle on how to modify the page to best suit this purpose, especially
> when viewed in responsive / mobile. Don't waste screen space. Be efficient.
> Have oracle approve the UX design and ensure your implementation of it is
> correct.

The goal of this step is to turn the step-2 **read-only** market-match
diagnostic into a surface where the operator can **act while reviewing**: spot
the listings worth scrutinizing (price outliers), and record what a
mis-parsed competitor listing *should* have been — including the retailer's
naming convention — so subsequent listings from that retailer parse better.

## Design (Oracle-reviewed — approved with refinements)

The UX and the storage/architecture boundary below were reviewed by the
Oracle for this planning step (the operator explicitly required Oracle to
approve the UX design). The automation fleet MUST still obtain its own per-step
Oracle **design** review (before implementing) and **diff + UI** review
(before landing) — this section is the approved *shape*, not a substitute for
implementation-time review.

### The two core interactions

Both attach to the existing per-brand-categorical-family `MarketMatchPanel`
(`helios/src/client/routes/catalog/CatalogFamilyExplorerPage.tsx` +
`/api/catalog/family-explorer/market-match`). **Reuse; do not rebuild** the
panel, the shared scorer
(`helios/src/server/marketMatch/candidateScoring.ts` /
`helios/src/shared/marketMatch/confidence.ts`), or the size-group folding.

**(A) Significant price-outlier highlighting** — flag listings whose price is
a statistical outlier *within the correctly-typed, above-threshold matches for
that family* so the operator can quickly find the rows to scrutinize (a
mis-parse skewing price, or a genuinely off competitor price).

**(B) Retailer name-parsing / extraction feedback** — from a mis-parsed row,
let the operator (i) correct the extracted fields for that listing and (ii)
optionally state the retailer's naming convention, scoped by default to that
retailer × category/subcategory. Captured feedback is a durable, promotable
signal — not a hidden live parser.

### Cardinal rules (from the umbrella's core invariant + Oracle review)

- **Outlier stats are computed ONLY over above-threshold, same-hard-gated-
  family, priced candidates.** Never include below-threshold or wrong-"type-
  of-thing" candidates — doing so recreates the exact IQR-pollution failure the
  operator has repeatedly been burned by.
- **Compute outliers over the full bounded/scored set, BEFORE the display cap**
  — an outlier must never be invisible because it fell outside the top-N-by-
  score table slice.
- **The DB feedback store is NOT a second, live parser.** parsekit /
  `helios-parser-configs` remains the single authoritative *executable* parser
  after promotion. Operator feedback must not silently change production
  matching/scoring, `fuzzy_skus`, market aggregates, or IQR. Any in-page effect
  of unpromoted feedback is a clearly-labeled, opt-in **preview** only,
  excluded from aggregates.

### UX (mobile-first, no wide new table column)

Per `helios/AGENTS.md` (purpose-first, don't waste screen space) and the
"responsive/mobile, be efficient" directive:

- **Panel summary pill** — add a warning pill only when non-zero, e.g.
  `3 price review`, with a tooltip stating the IQR basis (count, median,
  fence). Show nothing when there are zero outliers (no "0 outliers" noise).
- **"Needs review" strip above the table** — when outliers exist, a compact
  section before the wide table. Desktop: one-line chips (max ~3 + "show all").
  Mobile: stacked cards, open when non-empty, each showing listing (link),
  retailer, price with a `↑$`/`↓$` direction badge, current parsed size/pack
  vs. expected family size/pack, and a **`Fix parse`** action. This is what
  lets the operator find and act on the work *without* horizontally scrolling
  the table on a phone.
- **Sticky Score cell affordances** — no new column. In the existing sticky
  score cell add a tiny `↑$`/`↓$` outlier badge and a small `Fix`/`✎` icon
  button (accessible label), plus a subtle row tint / left border and price-
  cell emphasis. These stay visible while the table is scrolled horizontally.
  A row that already has saved feedback shows a tiny `feedback`/`hint` pill.
- **Correction drawer / bottom sheet** (not inline table editing) — opened by
  `Fix parse`. Mobile: bottom sheet; desktop: side drawer. Sections:
  1. Listing context (retailer + stable id, listing link, price, distance
     band, snapshot time, score, outlier badge).
  2. Current parse vs. family expectation (two-column: current parsed
     size/pack/category/subcategory vs. the family's expected size-group /
     pack / category / subcategory).
  3. "What's wrong?" chips (`size`, `pack qty`, `category/subcategory`,
     `brand`, `name tokens/strain`, `price is genuine`,
     `not same product / no match`) that reveal only the relevant fields —
     don't front-load a giant form.
  4. Correction fields (pack count, unit size value/unit, total size
     value/unit, category/subcategory), prefilled from the current parse and
     family where possible. Keep brand correction distinct from the existing
     brand-mapping semantics unless explicitly wired into brand overrides.
  5. Convention capture (opt-in checkbox "Also propose a retailer naming
     convention"): default scope `this retailer + category/subcategory`;
     optional `retailer-wide`, `retailer + brand`, `this listing only`;
     free-text note + auto-generated examples from the corrected listing(s) +
     optional pattern chips (`brand first`, `size at end`, `pack before size`,
     `total size shown`, `unit size shown`). The operator NEVER authors
     parsekit JSON or regex.
  6. Save → persists the exact listing correction (+ convention candidate when
     selected), marks the row/card `feedback saved`, and MAY show a clearly-
     labeled preview of the corrected parse/score for that one listing.

### Storage / architecture boundary (Oracle recommendation)

Three layers, with a firm boundary between live operator input and the
authoritative parser:

1. **Helios DB — operator feedback inbox** (the live web input target). One
   normalized feedback table with a discriminated `kind` (listing correction /
   convention proposal). Store: `useCase`/`sourceKind` (`litalerts` for this
   page), `sourceListingId`, `fuzzySkuId`, **`retailerId`** (stable — display
   name is not; add it to the API contract), raw listing name + input
   hash/snapshot, family key / brand key, matched catalog product id (if any),
   corrected structured fields, issue/disposition type, convention note +
   scope + examples, actor/time, and `status` (`draft | promotion_requested |
   promoted | rejected | superseded`). This immediately improves the *operator
   workflow* (show saved feedback on rows, prefill future corrections for the
   same retailer/scope, "convention candidate exists" hints, exact-listing
   corrected-parse preview) **without** changing production scoring.
2. **No active DB parser.** Do not let DB conventions silently reparse
   subsequent listings and change the panel's real score/counts — that forks a
   second parser beside parsekit and breaks the audit page's "this is the real
   matcher" invariant. If cross-listing impact is ever wanted, it must be an
   explicit, default-off, clearly-labeled `Preview with unpromoted retailer
   hints` toggle, excluded from aggregates/IQR/pricing and never persisted into
   `fuzzy_skus` as canonical. (Out of scope for this step unless the operator
   asks — see below.)
3. **parsekit / `helios-parser-configs` — authoritative executable parser.**
   Promotion path (agent/reviewer, not the web UI): select DB feedback for a
   retailer/scope → export corrected examples as parsekit **goldens** →
   create/update `helios-parser-configs/use-cases/litalerts/parsers/<tenantId>.jsonc`
   (`litalerts` is the current source; reserve `competitor-ecom` for direct
   competitor e-commerce sources later) → run parsekit validation/goldens →
   review/push → Helios parser registry loads the new snapshot → mark the DB
   feedback `promoted` with parser/rule id + config sha. This is the concrete
   realization of the runtime-adjustable parser-config work tracked under
   [automation#19](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/19).

## Scope owned by this child epic (tasks)

### T1 — Price-outlier domain helper + market-match contract fields (must-have)

- Pure, deterministic outlier helper using **Tukey IQR fences** (`< q1 −
  1.5·IQR`, `> q3 + 1.5·IQR`) over above-threshold, same-family, finite-priced
  candidates (use `preTaxPrice`; post-tax is a constant multiplier). Guards:
  no statistical flag when basis count `< 5`; when IQR is effectively zero,
  fall back to a conservative tight-cluster rule (flag only when the value
  differs from the median by **both** an absolute and relative threshold, e.g.
  `≥ max($5, 20% of median)`). Never remove/down-rank a candidate for being an
  outlier — review signal only.
- Extend `catalogFamilyMarketMatch` contract: per-candidate
  `priceOutlier: null | { kind: 'low' | 'high'; delta; fence; median; basis }`,
  a response-level `priceOutlierSummary`, and a `reviewCandidates` array
  (full-set outliers, bounded — e.g. 25 — with an overflow warning) so
  outliers survive the display cap.
- Tests: min-sample suppression, high/low IQR flags, tight-cluster fallback,
  below-threshold excluded, missing-price excluded.

### T2 — Outlier UX in the existing panel (must-have)

- Summary `price review` pill (only when non-zero); "Needs review" strip/cards
  above the table; sticky score-cell `↑$`/`↓$` badge + `Fix` action + row
  tint. No new wide column. Mobile cards usable before the horizontal table.
  Preserve existing caveat pills and the below-threshold divider.

### T3 — Feedback persistence: schema + API + contracts (must-have)

- DB migration for the normalized feedback table (discriminated `kind`) with
  the fields listed under *Storage layer 1*. Add stable identifiers to the
  candidate contract (esp. **`retailerId`** from the raw LitAlerts data).
- Endpoints: fetch feedback for visible candidate/retailer ids; create/update
  feedback; update status. Zod contracts; no first-party `any`.
- **Record a DB cost/plan** for the new queries; reuse existing indexed reads
  where possible.

### T4 — Parse-correction drawer / mobile bottom sheet (must-have)

- Drawer/sheet per the UX above: listing context, current-vs-expected parse,
  issue chips, correction fields, opt-in convention proposal (scope + note +
  examples + pattern chips), save + `feedback saved` row badge. Optional
  clearly-labeled exact-listing corrected-parse/score preview.

### T5 — Promotion support (data shape + export, not web-side git writes) (must-have, light)

- Land the `status`/promotion metadata fields and an export/report query or
  endpoint shaped for an agent/reviewer to turn feedback into parsekit goldens
  + a `helios-parser-configs/use-cases/litalerts/parsers/<tenantId>.jsonc`
  entry. Document the promotion path. **Do not** build web UI that writes git
  configs.

### T6 — Review / polish gate (must-have)

- Deterministic, prod-resource-free tests; mobile screenshots / UI-review
  notes; Oracle design + diff + UI review before close; explicitly re-verify
  **no new unbounded LitAlerts pulls** (reuse the bounded nearest-retailer
  fan-out). Record the Agent Gate Record on each landing.

## Nice-to-haves (land only if cheap; don't block the step)

- A "price is genuine" disposition that suppresses already-reviewed outlier
  warnings. **Reconfirm with the operator** whether a saved "genuine" mark
  should permanently suppress future outlier flags for that listing/retailer.
- `Outliers only` / `Review first` filter toggle.
- Showing existing retailer convention hints on every row from that retailer.
- An export command that emits candidate parsekit golden cases directly.

## Explicitly out of scope for step 3 (later steps / other work)

- Making unpromoted DB feedback change production scoring/matching, `fuzzy_skus`,
  or any market aggregate (the default-off preview toggle is the only allowed
  cross-listing effect, and even that is out of scope unless the operator asks).
- Auto-generating or committing `helios-parser-configs` from the Helios web UI.
- The broader parsekit read-path migration owned by
  [automation#19](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/19).
- Turning the temporary page permanent/polished, the full A-subset picker,
  price/promo application, and the detailed click-through market-data page
  (umbrella D) — later steps.
- Any new/unbounded market-data collection or LitAlerts pull.

## Top risks to call out (for the implementing fleet)

1. **Second-parser risk** — active DB conventions would diverge from parsekit
   and make the audit panel stop reflecting the real matcher. Keep DB feedback
   inert w.r.t. production scoring.
2. **Outlier pollution** — stats MUST exclude below-threshold / wrong-family
   candidates, or they reproduce the IQR-pollution failure.
3. **Display-cap invisibility** — compute outliers before the display cap; keep
   `reviewCandidates` visible.
4. **Small-sample noise** — no statistical flag below the minimum basis; use the
   conservative fallback when IQR is tiny.
5. **Mobile hidden actions** — never rely on an off-screen table column; use the
   review cards + sticky score-cell action.
6. **Unstable retailer identity** — persist by retailer id / source ids / raw
   hash, not display name.
7. **Promotion target ambiguity** — the current source is LitAlerts, so promote
   into `use-cases/litalerts`; only use `competitor-ecom` for direct competitor
   e-commerce sources.

## Validation

Each landing commit MUST:

1. Land green on `automation` CI: `cd helios && npm run check` (server +
   client typecheck + `vitest run`) and `npm run build`. Add unit tests for the
   outlier helper (T1) and the feedback contracts/queries (T3). No first-party
   `any`; no bug-masking fallbacks; deterministic, prod-resource-free tests.
2. Be visible on `vps-nixos-3` after the sanctioned `self-deploy-helios`
   (never a manual `systemctl restart` of the helios units).
3. **Record a DB cost/plan** for every new feedback query (T3), reusing
   existing indexed catalog/partner reads where possible.
4. Honor canon gates: Oracle **design** review (before implementing) and
   **diff** review (before landing) for this operator-facing surface, plus
   Oracle **UI** review of the drawer + outlier affordances on mobile
   (signal-to-noise, next-action, no wasted space). Record the Agent Gate
   Record on each landing.
5. Carry the cross-repo completion trailer on the master-landing commit. **See
   the multi-step-umbrella caution above** — confirm the intended `Satisfies:`
   target with the operator on #35 before landing so a single child completion
   does not prematurely close the umbrella.

## Completion signal for the child

This child epic is done when:

- The market-match panel highlights significant price outliers (IQR-based,
  correctly-typed basis) via a compact, mobile-usable "Needs review" surface
  and sticky-cell badges, with outliers surviving the display cap (T1 + T2).
- The operator can, from a mis-parsed row, open a drawer to correct the
  extracted fields and optionally record a scoped retailer naming convention,
  persisted to the Helios feedback store with stable identifiers, and see the
  row marked as having feedback (T3 + T4).
- The promotion path into `helios-parser-configs` is documented and the data
  shape/export supports it, without any web-side git writes (T5).
- All gates green (T6), demonstrated on `vps-nixos-3`.
- An operator-facing closure/status comment is posted on
  `virusdave/top-level#35` prefixed `<!-- task-dag:status -->` (do NOT
  hand-post the `<!-- task-dag:completion -->` cross-repo signal — the peer
  repo's completion-sync workflow emits it from the `Satisfies:` trailer),
  including the live page URL, commit links, the chosen outlier method + basis
  rules, and the feedback→promotion boundary, so the operator can iterate into
  the next step.

# Agent-waste review queue — Helios child epic: second top-level read-only mirror + wire `setBacklogReader()` (re-scope of leaf `0d07aed`)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality" (Lever D).
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md)
> ("Remaining work" #3; decisions **D1/D2** RESOLVED).
> **Re-scopes** the previously operator-blocked task-dag leaf `0d07aed`
> ("Wire Helios agent-waste backlog to the real store"), whose operator gate is
> now closed ([automation#57 comment #4891081664](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/57#issuecomment-4891081664));
> that leaf is parked `--downstream` awaiting this workstream, not
> operator-blocked.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 has **several** child epics,
> the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO carry this issue's own
> `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level completion
> aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal

Make `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` (admin-only) return **real** pending-review
items instead of the 503-degrade default, by having Helios read the backlog file
that github-worker exports into `top-level` (D1/D2). This is the **re-scope** of
leaf `0d07aed`: the operator resolved the transport to be a **git-backed file in
`top-level`, read via a second read-only mirror** — superseding the earlier
same-host-NDJSON sketch in that leaf's note.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Second read-only mirror** | Add a **second** git `--mirror` of `top-level` alongside the existing `automation` mirror, using the same proven pattern as [`helios/src/server/taskDagMirror.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/taskDagMirror.ts): bare `--mirror` clone, ~60s refresh, deploy key, **loud-but-non-fatal** (a fetch failure keeps the last-good copy + reports "stale", never 500s). Reads the D2 read-only deploy key provisioned in child epic #1 (same shape as `/run/agenix/helios-github-automation-deploy-key`). |
| **Wire `setBacklogReader()`** | Implement a `BacklogReader` (the `status()` / `readBacklog()` interface already defined in [`helios/src/server/agentWasteRepo.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/agentWasteRepo.ts)) that reads the exported backlog file from the top-level mirror, and install it via `setBacklogReader()`, replacing the default `unavailableBacklogReader`. Use the hardened `parseBacklogNdjson()` / the Zod contract [`helios/src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts). |
| **Reuse the merged plumbing** | The route `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` (admin-only, 503-degrades when unwired: [`helios/src/server/routes/agentWaste.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/routes/agentWaste.ts)) already exists (issue #57 task 1). This child epic only supplies the reader + mirror. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants (carry forward)

- **Read path is loud-but-non-fatal** (taskDagMirror semantics): a `top-level`
  fetch failure shows stale/unavailable, never a 500.
- **`note` is display-only** — surface it in the admin UI, never inject it into
  any agent.
- **No prod DB dependency** — the whole point of D1 (git file) is to keep the
  producer decoupled from Helios's prod DB. Do not add a DB table for this.
- Deploy key is the **`helios` service user**'s agenix read key (D2), not the
  machine/`amp-local` credential.

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Depends on** child epic #1 (backlog file **format** + **D2 read key**) and,
  for live end-to-end data, child epic #2 (the exporter actually writing the
  file). The reader can be built against a fixture as soon as #1's format is
  fixed; live verification needs #2.
- **Closes out** the re-scoped leaf `0d07aed`.

## 5. Acceptance

- With the exporter running, `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` returns real
  pending-review items; with `top-level` unreachable it reports stale/unavailable
  and never 500s.
- Deterministic, prod-resource-free reader test (fixture backlog file, no prod
  resources), plus the live endpoint confirmed on prod **after** deploy via
  `self-deploy*` under lock. Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

Additive: a second read-only mirror + a reader install. Rollback is reverting
`setBacklogReader()` to the default (endpoint returns to 503-degrade) and
removing the mirror. Read-only credential; no writes to `top-level` from this
child epic (writes are child epic #4). Deploy follows canon (push →
`self-deploy*` under lock; never manually restart the serving Helios process).

# Agent-waste review queue — Helios child epic: promote-to-advisory admin button (server-side, admin-gated, contract-validated commit+push)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality" (Lever D).
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md)
> ("Remaining work" #4; decision **D3** and the **§Security** write-key choice
> are RESOLVED — operator adopted option **(c)** direct, admin-gated,
> server-validated push, comment [#4889206463](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/57#issuecomment-4889206463)).
> **Advisory catalog contract:**
> [`virusdave/top-level` → `docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md),
> [`docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 has **several** child epics,
> the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO carry this issue's own
> `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level completion
> aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal

Implement the operator's **promote-to-advisory admin button** (D3): a
server-side, admin-gated, contract-validated git **commit+push** that adds a new
reviewed entry to `top-level` `advisories.yaml` — the human-review gate that lets
a curated observation become an allowlisted advisory the dispatcher may inject
(~1-min latency). This **overrides** the earlier "v1 = display + link-to-promote,
no Helios button" plan; the operator explicitly asked for an in-Helios admin
action ("I do not want to modify files in git manually").

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Admin-gated route** | `POST` promote endpoint, **admin-only** (same admin gate as `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog`), with an audit log entry per promotion. |
| **applyConfig-pattern write** | Reuse the parser-config apply pattern in [`helios/src/server/parsekit/applyConfig.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/parsekit/applyConfig.ts): **validate → write → `git add` → reject no-op → commit → push → reset local commit on push failure**, with a subprocess **timeout**. Push to `top-level master` using the D3 write deploy key from child epic #1. |
| **Server-side contract validation** | Before committing, validate the resulting `advisories.yaml` against the **advisory-catalog contract** ([`ADVISORY_CATALOG.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md)): schema, **budget caps**, `id` rules. Reject invalid promotions before any write. |
| **Field mapping (audited)** | Record exactly which backlog-item fields map to an advisory entry's `id` / `text` / `severity`. **`note` is display-only and MUST NOT map to `text`** — it can never leak into the injected allowlist. |
| **Concurrency** | Promote-commits touch files adjacent to the exporter's backlog writes in the same repo. Inherit applyConfig's no-op rejection + reset-on-push-failure so a rejected push never piles up local commits; refetch/rebase and retry. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants (carry forward)

- **`note` never becomes advisory `text`.** This is the load-bearing safety
  invariant of the whole workstream — the allowlist is the boundary between
  human-reviewed text and agent-authored text.
- **Validate before commit**, server-side, against the catalog contract (schema
  + budget caps + `id` rules); reject no-op; reset-on-push-failure; subprocess
  timeout — the full applyConfig discipline.
- **Admin-gated + audited.** The human review action *is* the safety gate for a
  mutating, behaviour-changing operation (it changes what future agents may be
  injected with). Every promotion is admin-authenticated and logged.
- **§Security residual risk accepted (option (c)).** The `top-level` **write**
  deploy key is repo-wide (GitHub deploy keys are not path-scoped) and
  `top-level` has no branch protection on the current plan. The operator
  **explicitly accepted** this residual risk (comment [#4889206463](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/57#issuecomment-4889206463));
  options (a) dedicated repo and (b) PR/branch were declined. Do **not** silently
  substitute (a)/(b); the mitigation is admin-gating + server-side validation +
  audit, not key-scope reduction.

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Depends on** child epic #1 (the **D3 write deploy key** + the catalog it
  edits). Best sequenced after #3 (reader) so the admin UI can show the backlog
  item being promoted, but the write path itself only strictly needs #1.

## 5. Acceptance

- An admin can promote a reviewed backlog item to a new `advisories.yaml` entry
  via the Helios button; the change is contract-validated server-side, committed,
  and pushed to `top-level master`; invalid promotions are rejected before any
  write; every promotion is audited.
- `note` provably cannot reach advisory `text`.
- Deterministic, prod-resource-free tests of validation + the commit path
  (against a temp repo, **never** prod `top-level`), plus the live path confirmed
  on prod **after** deploy via `self-deploy*` under lock. Attach an Agent Gate
  Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

The riskiest child epic (holds a `top-level` write credential). Rollback is
disabling the route + revoking/rotating the D3 write key; a bad advisory can be
reverted in `top-level` git and the injector ships fail-safe (empty catalog =
inert). Never point tests at prod `top-level`; use an ephemeral temp repo. Deploy
follows canon (push → `self-deploy*` under lock; never manually restart Helios).
No prod DB, no schema.

## Motivation (operator directive)

The operator does **not** run `psql`/SQL against the prod DB by hand. Canon
[`rules/DB_PERFORMANCE.md` step 5](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/DB_PERFORMANCE.md)
already mandates that **a worker/agent applies an approved migration to
production** ("not an operator chore"). But the Helios surface still
contradicts that: [`pendingMigrations.ts` `makeApplyCommand`](../blob/master/helios/src/server/db/pendingMigrations.ts)
emits a copy-paste `psql -f …` line and the all-pages
[`PendingMigrationsBanner`](../blob/master/helios/src/client/components/PendingMigrationsBanner.tsx)
implies the operator runs it.

Replace that with a Helios **admin page listing every pending migration** (from
the existing `pendingMigrations.ts` sentinel registry) with an **"Apply Now"**
control per migration that triggers a **reliable, fast, worker-driven apply** —
no human psql.

## Goal

- Admin-only Helios page: one row per pending migration (id, label, apply
  status, last attempt + result, sentinel state).
- Per-row **Apply Now** that kicks off the apply and shows live progress →
  success (sentinel now reports applied) / failure (surfaced error, safe to
  retry).
- Retire the operator-facing psql copy-paste from the banner; the banner should
  instead deep-link to this admin page.

## Safety requirements (hard — prod schema mutation)

Per canon safety + `rules/DB_PERFORMANCE.md`, a web-triggered prod migration MUST:

1. Be **admin-gated** in Helios (and ideally require the migration to be marked
   **Oracle-blessed + operator-approved** before the button is enabled — the
   admin click is the operator go, but Oracle migration blessing is still a
   prerequisite; design the gating).
2. Run the **exact reviewed migration artifact** (`NNN_*.sql`, wrapped txn where
   PG allows; non-transactional statements like `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`
   handled per canon) — never ad-hoc SQL.
3. **Verify the sentinel/probe live** after apply before reporting success
   (psql exit 0 is not enough — canon step 6).
4. Be **idempotent / safe to retry** after a partial failure.
5. Record the full lifecycle (who/when, blessing ref, approval, redacted apply
   cmd, txn note, sentinel verification) — canon step 7 / Agent Gate Record.

## Mechanism options (operator: "how the button works almost doesn't matter,
reliable and fast")

- **A. Enqueue a task-dag task** that a worker claims and runs (auditable,
  matches repo flow; latency = worker pickup).
- **B. Short-lived ops `automation` epic** auto-created per apply (heavier).
- **C. Direct privileged server-side apply** via a Helios worker job invoked by
  the endpoint (fastest; must isolate creds + fail-fast + verify sentinel).

Recommend evaluating A vs C for latency/auditability; C likely fastest,
A most auditable. Decide during design.

## Scope / process

- **Needs an Oracle design review before implementation** (web-triggered prod
  DB mutation — high-risk surface), then Oracle diff review before landing.
- Reuses the existing `pendingMigrations.ts` registry + `.down.sql` convention.
- First real exercise of the flow can be applying the already-landed, currently
  pending **`097_litalerts_parse_feedback`** (automation#59 T3) once
  Oracle-blessed + operator-approved.

## Out of scope

- Auto-applying migrations on deploy/boot (still explicit, gated).
- Down/rollback execution from the web (at least in v1) — forward-apply only.
- Changing the manual/sentinel migration model itself.

issues.body:
## Summary

Two recurring, avoidable time sinks hit on nearly every helios code task in a
fresh ephemeral checkout. Both were stumbled over repeatedly while landing
#61. Filing per operator request to fix the design/implementation.

## 1. Pre-commit SPA smoke requires a pre-built `helios/dist/client`

The pre-commit hook's step `3/3 booting server + smoke-checking SPA shell`
runs `scripts/smoke-server.ts`, which hard-fails if
`helios/dist/client/index.html` is missing:

```
[smoke] FAIL: .../helios/dist/client/index.html not found. Run `npm run build:client` first.
```

A **fresh ephemeral checkout has no `dist/client`**, so committing *any*
helios change (even a one-line server/doc edit) forces a full
`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 npm run build:client` — a heavy
~23–57s / 8 GiB-heap build that must be wrapped in `large-action-lock`.
`AGENTS.md` even documents "the hook relies on an already-built dist/client",
but nothing builds it for you in a clean tree.

**Impact:** every first commit in a new worktree pays a heavy build tax that
has nothing to do with the change being committed, and serializes on the
large-action lock.

**Fix ideas (pick one):**
- Have the smoke step build `dist/client` on demand when missing (behind the
  hook, still fast on warm rebuilds), or
- Make the smoke shell-render check tolerate a missing bundle (skip with a
  loud warning) so the *typecheck* gates still run but the heavy build is not
  mandatory for unrelated commits, or
- Ship a tiny committed SPA-shell fixture the smoke can assert against without
  a full vite build.

## 2. Tracked `helios/node_modules` symlink gets materialized into a real dir

`helios/node_modules` is a **tracked symlink** to the shared tree
(`/home/amp-local/src/automation/helios/node_modules`). Any script that runs
`scripts/ensure-build-env.sh` (npm `pretest`, build, etc.) materializes it
into a real directory, which then shows up in git as:

```
 D helios/node_modules
```

and must be manually undone before every commit/push:

```
rm -rf helios/node_modules && git restore -- helios/node_modules
```

This happened several times in one task (run tests → dirty → restore → run
tests again → dirty again).

**Impact:** easy to accidentally stage a `node_modules` deletion; constant
manual restore dance; noise in `git status`.

**Fix ideas (pick one):**
- Stop tracking a symlink — `.gitignore` `helios/node_modules` and let each
  checkout populate it (via `ensure-build-env` / `npm install`), or
- Make `ensure-build-env.sh` detect the tracked symlink and rebuild it
  (rather than replacing it with a real dir) when it points at a valid,
  populated shared tree.

## Context

Found while completing #61 (agent-waste promote-to-advisory button). Both are
environment/tooling papercuts, not code bugs in the feature.
issues.creator: virusdave
issues.title: Dev-loop friction: pre-commit smoke needs pre-built dist/client, and tracked helios/node_modules symlink keeps getting materialized

# agent-pain-points migration — automation (Helios) child epic: mirror/reader/promote/client retarget

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#40](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/40)
> — "Migrate the agent-waste canonical git storage to different repo".
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`virusdave/top-level` → `docs/epics/agent-pain-points-migration/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/agent-pain-points-migration/EPIC_PLAN.md).
> **Lever-D design being amended:**
> [`docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md)
> (this migration reverses its decision **D1** storage location — it is the
> "dedicated advisories repo" option that was earlier considered and declined).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit on
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#40`, and the **final** satisfying commit MUST
> also carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer.

## 1. Goal

Re-point Helios' agent-waste review queue (backlog read) and promote button
(advisory write) from `top-level` to `virusdave/agent-pain-points`, and update
the operator-facing catalog links — preserving the admin gate, server-side
validation, audit trail, and `note`-never-becomes-`text` invariant.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Read mirror** | Add an `agent-pain-points` read-only bare mirror (model on [`helios/src/server/topLevelMirror.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/topLevelMirror.ts)). Introduce distinct, accurately-named env: `HELIOS_AGENT_PAIN_POINTS_REPO_URL`, `HELIOS_AGENT_PAIN_POINTS_MIRROR_DIR`, `HELIOS_AGENT_PAIN_POINTS_DEPLOY_KEY`, `HELIOS_AGENT_PAIN_POINTS_REFRESH_SECONDS`, `HELIOS_AGENT_PAIN_POINTS_DISABLE`. **Do not overload** `HELIOS_TOP_LEVEL_*` — the mirror dir is a *bare mirror* while promote wants a *working tree* (design §5 hazard). |
| **Backlog reader** | Re-point [`agentWasteBacklogReader.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/agentWasteBacklogReader.ts) at the new mirror; keep relative path `docs/agent-runtime/agent-waste-backlog.ndjson`; keep fail-closed (empty/unavailable → structured empty / 503). |
| **Promote** | Re-point [`agentWaste/promoteAdvisory.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/agentWaste/promoteAdvisory.ts) to commit `docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml` in `agent-pain-points` using a **separate write clone dir** (`HELIOS_AGENT_PAIN_POINTS_WRITE_DIR`) + write deploy key. Preserve validate→write→add→reject-no-op→commit→push→reset-on-failure + subprocess timeout + duplicate-id rejection + single-path staging. |
| **Client links** | Update the hard-coded `github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/{advisories.yaml,ADVISORY_CATALOG.md}` links in [`agentWasteReviewShared.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/client/routes/config/agentWasteReviewShared.ts) to `agent-pain-points`. |
| **Startup** | Update [`main.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/main.ts) to init the new mirror + reader. Keep top-level mirror only if still needed for other purposes; otherwise retire it for agent-waste. |
| **Docs** | Amend `RESOLVED_DESIGN.md` (D1 storage location now `agent-pain-points`) and any contract comments referencing `top-level`. |
| **Tests** | Update `promoteAdvisory.test.ts`, `agentWasteBacklogReader.test.ts`, `routes/agentWaste.test.ts` to the new repo/env; all against temp repos, never prod `top-level` **or** prod `agent-pain-points`. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants

- **`note` never becomes advisory `text`** — the load-bearing allowlist safety
  boundary. Unchanged.
- Promote stays **admin-gated + server-validated + audited**; the admin action
  is the safety gate for a behavior-changing mutation.
- Read mirror is read-only; only promote uses the write key/clone.
- Deploy only via `self-deploy*` under `large-action-lock`; never manually
  restart Helios.

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Depends on** the nixos-sbc child (Helios read + write deploy keys + env for
  `agent-pain-points`).
- Cutover is coordinated with the github-worker child in parent epic §6 to avoid
  the split-brain window (promotions landing where the dispatcher isn't reading).

## 5. Acceptance

- `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` reads the backlog from `agent-pain-points`;
  `POST /api/agent-waste/promote` commits `advisories.yaml` to
  `agent-pain-points`; both fail closed (structured 503) when unavailable.
- `note` provably cannot reach advisory `text`; invalid/duplicate promotions
  rejected before any write.
- Deterministic, prod-resource-free tests of validation + commit path against a
  temp repo; live path confirmed on prod **after** `self-deploy*` under lock.
- Client catalog links point at `agent-pain-points`.
- Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

Rollback = revert the retarget + redeploy; Helios fails closed (empty catalog =
inert injector, unavailable backlog = 503), never serves wrong data. A bad
advisory can be reverted in `agent-pain-points` git. Never point tests at prod.
No prod DB, no schema.

issues.body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #62 (the admin "Apply Now" pending-migrations flow). Today the
admin page [`/config/pending-migrations`](https://helios.freshlybaked.us/config/pending-migrations)
shows each pending migration's id, label, eligibility/blessing, and last
attempt — but gives the operator **no way to see the actual SQL that will be
applied**, nor a plain-English explanation of what it does, before clicking
**Apply Now**. Approving a production schema mutation without being able to read
the exact artifact (and understand it in context) is a real gap.

## Goal

Let the operator, from the pending-migrations surface, **review the exact SQL
to-be-applied and understand it in plain English** before approving — with the
detail **collapsed by default** so the page stays tight (see
[`helios/AGENTS.md`](../blob/master/helios/AGENTS.md): the table is the whole
page; at-most-once-useful content is collapsed).

## Requirements (operator directive)

1. **Collapsed-by-default expand to view the migration SQL file contents**
   (the exact artifact that `psql -f` will run, i.e. the resolved
   `NNN_*.sql` plus its `\i`/`\ir` include closure — see
   [`resolveMigrationArtifact`](../blob/master/helios/src/server/db/migrationArtifacts.ts)).
2. **If inlining the SQL on the list page makes the UI/UX cumbersome
   (especially on mobile — CONSULT ORACLE on this), then instead** provide a
   **click-to-open (new tab) per-migration "details" page**. On that details
   page:
   - a **plain-English, context-explained description** of what the migration
     does and why, **collapsible, placed ABOVE the SQL** (context first — it is
     more important to see first than raw SQL lacking context). This
     description must follow the **canon UX rules for agent→operator
     communication**, especially being effectively **self-contained** (the
     operator should not need to hunt elsewhere to understand it). See
     `top-level` `docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md` (UI/UX gate) and the
     agent-KB comms guidance.
   - the **SQL file contents**, expandable (collapsed by default), below the
     description.
3. **Operator efficiency is the north star:** whatever the operator will (or
   should) want to know or do next should be **at their fingertips** — e.g.
   from the details page, quick access back to Apply Now / the eligibility &
   blessing info / last attempt & its job / the artifact digest, etc. Oracle
   may have additional UX ideas to meet this goal — **include them if so.**

## Design questions to settle (Oracle UX review REQUIRED before build)

- Inline expandable SQL on the list row **vs.** a dedicated details page
  (`/config/pending-migrations/:id`?) — decide primarily on mobile
  ergonomics + signal-to-noise. Oracle must weigh in.
- Where does the **plain-English description** come from? Candidates: the
  migration file header comments, the sentinel `label`, the blessing `note`,
  and/or an authored/curated per-migration explanation. Decide a source of
  truth that stays correct as migrations change (don't let it drift from the
  artifact).
- Any additional operator-efficiency affordances Oracle recommends.

## Likely shape / reuse (for the implementer)

- **Server:** a new **admin-gated, read-only** endpoint returning the resolved
  artifact contents for a migration id (reuse `resolveMigrationArtifact` — it
  already allowlists the id, realpath-contains the path, and resolves the
  include closure fail-closed; just read + return the file bytes as text).
  Mirror the auth pattern in
  [`pendingMigptionsAdmin.ts`](../blob/master/helios/src/server/routes/pendingMigrationsAdmin.ts).
- **Client:** extend
  [`PendingMigrationsPage.tsx`](../blob/master/helios/src/client/routes/config/PendingMigrationsPage.tsx)
  and/or add a details route; follow `helios/AGENTS.md` (collapse secondary
  content, tight chrome, mobile-first).
- Keep everything **read-only** — this feature never runs SQL; it only
  displays the artifact + explanation.

## Scope / process

# automation child epic — eliminate hand-built JSON

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#44](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/44)
> — "Our critical tooling should NOT be constructing json by hand."
> **Parent epic plan:** [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md).
> **Governing rule:** canon `docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md` "Code
> standards" — *never hand-build / hand-parse / hand-validate JSON or YAML*.

## Scope

One offender found in the automation repo (survey 2026-07-08):

**`ads/google/scripts/run-cluster-sweep.sh`** builds `manifest.json`
structurally in shell — a sequence of `printf` lines that emit the object
braces, the `clusters` array, and the inter-element commas by hand. The
scalar *values* are already escaped via `jq -Rn`, so the escaping risk is
low, but the object/array/comma scaffolding is still hand-assembled and a
future edit (a new field, a reordered element) can easily desync a comma
and emit invalid JSON.

Convert the whole manifest to a single `jq -n` invocation that takes the
run id, timestamp, slug list, and the `strategic_context_present` boolean
as `--arg`/`--argjson` and builds the object/array natively. Re-grep the
repo before finishing to confirm nothing else was missed:

```sh
rg -n -e '\\"[a-zA-Z_]+\\":' -e "printf '\{" -e 'echo .*\{.*:.*\}' ads scripts
```

## Constraints

- The emitted `manifest.json` must be equivalent in *content* (same keys,
  same values, `schema_version: 0`, placeholder `kind`/`note`, per-slug
  `{ "slug": …, "files": ["verdict.md"] }` entries) — this is a correctness
  refactor, not a schema change. Formatting/whitespace may differ (it is
  machine-consumed); verify any downstream reader still parses it.
- Follow the repo's own `AGENTS.md` and task-dag workflow.

## Acceptance

- `run-cluster-sweep.sh` produces `manifest.json` via `jq -n` (no
  hand-assembled braces/commas); output parses under `jq -e` and matches
  the prior structure for a representative slug list.
- The **final** commit on the automation `master` that demonstrates this
  child epic's acceptance criteria are met carries
  `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#44`. Intermediate commits MUST NOT carry
  that trailer unless the child epic is already fully satisfied.

issues.title: Eliminate hand-built JSON in run-cluster-sweep.sh manifest construction

[`docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md)
"Code standards" (the `--help` rule) and

"Serving services".

Every invocable tool must accept `-h`/`--help`, print usage, and exit `0`

## Finalize

Commit with a plain imperative subject (no `feat:`/`fix:` prefix) and the
`Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47` trailer; push to this repo's default

# Helios: cluster pending agent-waste reports with an advanced Bedrock LLM

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#51](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/51)
> — "Waste review page…".
> **Delegated because:** the agent-waste review page, its API routes, the
> backlog reader, the shared contracts, and the bedrock-mantle LLM client
> all live in `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` under `helios/`. `top-level` has
> no code to change.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` for this epic MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#51`, plus
> this child epic's own `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer
> so the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* delegated
> child.

## 1. Goal

Add a **"Cluster similar reports"** action to the admin agent-waste review
page (`/config/agent-waste`). Pressing it sends the current pending backlog
to an **advanced** Bedrock model (via the existing bedrock-mantle
OpenAI-compatible gateway) which groups near-duplicate / highly-similar
observations. The page then renders the result as ranked **clusters**:

- a **primary** (representative) observation per cluster,
- a **total count** of members in that cluster,
- a **collapsed but expandable** list of the remaining members, and
- clusters **sorted by "likely aggregate agent waste"** so the operator can
  address the most common / most expensive problems first.

This lets the operator triage a noisy backlog by theme instead of scrolling
a flat, newest-first list.

## 2. Current state (all paths under `helios/`)

Read these first; the feature slots into the existing shapes.

| Concern | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Review page UI | `src/client/routes/config/AgentWasteReviewPage.tsx` | Admin-guarded page; fetches backlog, renders `ObservationCard`s, has Refresh + per-row Promote. Add the cluster button + clustered view here. |
| Client pure helpers | `src/client/routes/config/agentWasteReviewShared.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) | Fetch/parse/sort helpers are pure + unit-tested (no DOM harness). Put cluster fetch/parse/sort logic here. |
| Server routes | `src/server/routes/agentWaste.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) | `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` and `POST /api/agent-waste/promote`, both `requireSessionUser(request, reply, 'admin')`, structured 503-degrade via `handleAgentWasteError`. Add the cluster route here. |
| Backlog data layer | `src/server/agentWasteRepo.ts`, `src/server/agentWasteBacklogReader.ts` | `getBacklog()` / `getBacklogSourceStatus()`; `BacklogReader` reads the read-only agent-pain-points mirror. Reuse `getBacklog()` verbatim. |
| Shared contracts | `src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts` | `AgentWasteObservationSchema` (+ the display-only `note` rule) and the backlog/promote schemas. Add cluster request/response schemas here. |
| Bedrock env | `src/server/config/env.ts` | `bedrockMantleBaseUrl`, `bedrockMantleBearerToken`, `llmRequestTimeoutMs`. |
| Server LLM call pattern | `src/server/llm/reviewSentimentGate.ts`, `src/server/routes/configLitalertsParsing.ts` | Canonical shape: `fetch(`${baseUrl}/chat/completions`, { headers: Bearer, body: { model, messages, response_format: json_object, temperature }, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(llmRequestTimeoutMs) })`; errors returned structured, never thrown across the request boundary. |
| Model context registry | `src/shared/domain/bedrockModels.ts`, `src/server/llm/bedrockModelConfig.ts` | `BEDROCK_MODEL_CONTEXT_KEYS`, `resolveBedrockModel(db, key)`, operator overrides in `app_settings.bedrock_model_overrides`. Add an `agent_waste_clusterer` context key. |

**Backlog item identity gap (important).** `AgentWasteObservation.id` is a
*stable trigger id* (e.g. `rg-short-r-rejected`), **not** unique per event.
The client already synthesises a composite `observationKey(obs)` for local
dismiss. Clustering needs to map LLM output back to specific observations,
so **assign each observation a stable index/key server-side before sending
to the LLM** and have the model return those keys (see §4).

## 3. Design decisions (implement exactly)

1. **The server does the LLM call.** The Amp Oracle is agent-only; the live
   Helios server calls Bedrock directly through bedrock-mantle, exactly like
   `reviewSentimentGate.ts` / `configLitalertsParsing.ts`. New route:
   `POST /api/agent-waste/clusters`, `admin`-gated, reading `getBacklog()`.

2. **The LLM groups; the server ranks.** The model returns only the
   *grouping* (which observation keys belong together + a short human label /
   representative). "Likely aggregate agent waste" is computed
   **deterministically in Helios** from the members' real
   `estimated_wasted_tokens` / `estimated_wasted_seconds` — never taken from
   the model. Rationale: the ranking must be trustworthy and reproducible,
   and the numbers already exist on each observation. Define the aggregate
   explicitly (e.g. `sum(estimated_wasted_tokens over members)`, with
   `estimated_wasted_seconds` as a documented tiebreak/secondary); pick one
   and encode it in a pure, unit-tested helper. Sort clusters descending by
   that aggregate.

3. **Cluster output is display-only.** It is NOT injected into agents and
   does NOT auto-promote. Sending observation text (including `note`) to the
   *private* clustering model is read/analysis, not allowlist injection; the
   result only renders in the operator UI. The promote path and its
   `.strict()` "`note` can never be advisory text" contract are untouched.

4. **No persistence for v1.** Clusters are computed on demand when the
   operator presses the button and shown in the page; nothing is written to
   the DB or to git. (If the operator later wants shareable/persisted
   clusters, that is a follow-up; do NOT pull in the promote/applyConfig
   write-clone machinery for v1.)

5. **Advanced, operator-overridable model.** Add an `agent_waste_clusterer`
   context key so the model is configurable via the existing Bedrock
   model-override UI, and resolve it with `resolveBedrockModel(db,
   'agent_waste_clusterer')`. **Open question (§6):** the codebase has no
   confirmed-working *advanced* model id on the gateway — `google.gemma-3-27b-it`
   is the only proven model, and `anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-…` was rejected
   with "model not found". The whole point of #51 is a *more advanced* model,
   so the implementer must confirm a working advanced model id on
   bedrock-mantle (or have the operator set one via the override UI) rather
   than silently defaulting to the small model.

## 4. Contract sketch (`src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts`)

Add (names illustrative; keep zod + `.strict()` discipline):

```ts
// Request: no body needed beyond the action; server reads the live backlog.
// (An empty POST is fine, or accept an optional { } for forward-compat.)

// One clustered group, ready to render + already ranked server-side.
export const AgentWasteClusterSchema = z.object({
  label: z.string(),                       // short human theme from the model
  primary: AgentWasteObservationSchema,    // representative member
  members: z.array(AgentWasteObservationSchema), // includes primary; length = count
  count: z.number().int().nonnegative(),   // members.length
  aggregateWastedTokens: z.number().nonnegative(),
  aggregateWastedSeconds: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),
})

export const AgentWasteClustersResponseSchema = z.object({
  source: AgentWasteSourceStatusSchema,    // reuse backlog source status
  model: z.string(),                       // which model actually ran
  clusters: z.array(AgentWasteClusterSchema), // sorted desc by aggregate waste
  unclustered: z.array(AgentWasteObservationSchema).optional(), // items the model left ungrouped
})
```

- The server assigns each observation a stable key (reuse the same field set
  as the client's `observationKey`, or a simple 0-based index for the
  request round-trip) and instructs the model to return groups **by those
  keys**; the server then rehydrates full observations, drops/one-members any
  key the model hallucinated, and computes the aggregates.

## 5. Suggested leaf breakdown

Author these as the child epic's own frontier leaves (the automation
epic-root worker `task-dag breakdown`s this issue):

- **L1 — Server clustering endpoint + contract.**
  - Add cluster schemas to `contracts/api/agentWaste.ts`.
  - Add `agent_waste_clusterer` to `BEDROCK_MODEL_CONTEXT_KEYS` /
    `BEDROCK_MODEL_CONTEXTS`.
  - Add `POST /api/agent-waste/clusters` in `routes/agentWaste.ts`:
    `admin`-gated; `getBacklog()` (503-degrade via `handleAgentWasteError`);
    factor the Bedrock call into a **testable helper** (e.g.
    `src/server/agentWaste/clusterBacklog.ts`) that takes the observations +
    a model id and returns groups; compute aggregates + sort in a pure
    helper; map missing token to `503 bedrock_unconfigured` and gateway/parse
    errors to `502`, matching `configLitalertsParsing.ts`.
  - Tests: route tests via `server.inject` with mocked auth + injected
    backlog reader + stubbed `fetch` (see `agentWaste.test.ts` patterns);
    pure tests for aggregate-scoring + sort + LLM-output parsing/rehydration
    (incl. hallucinated/duplicate keys).

- **L2 — Client cluster button + clustered view.** (depends on L1)
  - Add a **"Cluster similar reports"** button near Refresh on
    `AgentWasteReviewPage.tsx`, with loading / error / unavailable states.
  - Put the fetch + response-parse + (defensive re-)sort logic in
    `agentWasteReviewShared.ts` as pure, unit-tested helpers.
  - Render clusters: a primary `ObservationCard` with a **count** pill and a
    collapsed `<details>`/`<summary>` (per `helios/AGENTS.md`) that expands to
    the member list; keep the existing flat list available (e.g. toggle
    between "flat" and "clustered" views, or show clusters above the list).
  - Pure client helper tests in `agentWasteReviewShared.test.ts`.

## 6. Open questions (resolve during implementation; not operator-blocking)

- **Which advanced model?** Confirm a working advanced model id on
  bedrock-mantle (§3.5). If none is confirmable, ship the endpoint +
  override plumbing and let the operator set the model via the existing
  Bedrock override UI, but surface (don't hide) that the default is not the
  "advanced" model the issue asked for.
- **Aggregate-waste formula.** Tokens-only vs tokens+seconds weighting, and
  how to rank clusters whose members lack `estimated_wasted_*` (treat
  missing as 0, but keep count as a secondary sort so a large all-unrated
  cluster still surfaces). Pick and document one.
- **Backlog size vs prompt budget.** The pending backlog is "tiny and rare"
  by design, so a single-shot cluster call should fit; still cap the number
  of observations / total prompt size sent and degrade clearly if exceeded.

## 7. Gates (canon `QUALITY_GATES.md`)

- `cd helios && npm run typecheck` (server) and `npm run typecheck:client`.
- Focused tests: `npm run test -- <file-or-pattern>` for the new server +
  client helper/route tests. Full `npm run check` is CI-owned.
- Client bundle build (if touched) with an enlarged heap:
  `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 npm run build:client`.
- **This adds a new LLM call on the live server request path** consuming
  agent-adjacent text (backlog notes). Even though the output is
  display-only, it is a new private-LLM surface: get an **Oracle design
  review** of the endpoint + prompt before implementing and a change review
  of the diff, and make the prompt strictly instruct the model to *only*
  cluster + return the fixed JSON shape (defend against injected instructions
  in `note`/observation text). No prompt-injection reachback exists because
  results never feed agents, but the review keeps that boundary explicit.

## 8. Out of scope for v1

- Persisting clusters (DB or git), sharing/linking to a cluster.
- Auto-promoting a cluster to an advisory (still the separate, per-row
  operator-approved promote path).
- Any change to the promote / draft-assist (L1–L3) flow or its `note`
  contract.
- Any `top-level` change beyond this delegation.

issues.title: Cluster pending agent-waste reports with an advanced Bedrock LLM

https://helios.freshlybaked.us/catalog/pending-purchases?mode=rows&packetId=65 failed with relatively straightforward hint text expanding the METRC acronyms.  This is absolutely the kind of thing that should be useful for the LLM classifier, no?

issues.body:
We've made a significant shift in how we analyze pending purchases' line-item METRC data (which might require catalog updates or mild to difficult UI matching process against the existing catalog (which sweed makes _harder_ by its choice of what to show in the match dialog - it's not a variant full product name, which can lead to horribly ambiguous match choices).  Now rather than in-sweed-UI, we use Helios.  In the far past, I used to have an amp-agent live-analyze the data returned from the purchases API and somewhat iteratively and interactively would (when needed) help guide it towards a sensible analysis outcome and proposal packet.  These were all one-off activities, although the UI/UX around the produced packet and operator examination, picture selection (or denial), price-setting, price ladder, and market pricing data comparison UI / UX and (if desired) new-tab details, evolved into an excellent, efficient, and elegant little applet.  Sadly, our current canonical implementation of this is far inferior in my opinion.  If I can track down any of those prior implementations to use as an example, i definitely will.

Then we decided to implement this within Helios proper with more "traditional" approaches to solve the pair of "what actually IS this line item", and then "what market data is a match for this", such as building a progressively more complex and unmaintainable set of regex parsing rules for the METRC data in purchase line items, various parsing (and eventual retrieval of structured data) from litalerts with various matching heuristics.  

All of this worked badly and got worse and worse over time.  "Development by ever-growing layered heuristics" breeds complexity at an alarming rate, and the declining outcome quality showed it (in addition to the MASSIVE ui/ux and operator efficiency regression caused by (poorly) reimplementing from scratch (based on rough descriptions) the evolved UI controls that had been present in the non-helios individual jobs.  At one point I thought I could improve our parsing problems dramatically by replacing regex with a parser combinator and non-turing-complete-simple-computation-or-value-modification-upon-rule-match config language.  However, at that time the *primary* problem we had that appeared to be a "parsing problem" was the litalerts SKU name data returned from some API.  Eventually, however, we learned that we could just extract the structured data from litalerts directly, map it (fuzzily) into our own preferred taxonomy, categorization, and conventions, then match based upon _those_.  This made the LitAlerts data matching issue no longer primarily one of parsing and instead one of feature extraction and fuzzy matching, so we backed out that parser approach.

Eventually, I insisted above Oracle strong objection to effectively start building a better system where the PURCHASE matching at heart would go back to being "semi interactive with SMART and CAPABLE bedrock base model", which is nondeterminstic by nature, but pure determinism on the initial parsing and proposal generation was never a strict requirement by the operator; efficiency and expedience and general correctness of approach (with the approach likely to scale and get BETTER over time, rather than the layered heuristics approach which is almost guaranteed to get worse (or at least more difficult to maintain at same quality) as the aggregate complexity skyrocks.

When designing with an Agent and discussing, the agent insisted it wouldn't be able to be invoked from within Helios.  In retrospect, I don't believe this, as we have tooling that launches agents just fine, and there's no reason we couldn't use similar approaches within helios proper, since all agentic development _already_ takes place on Helios Production server.

However, that hadn't occurred to me at that point, so I agreed to a sufficiently advanced model available on Bedrock.  Fine (although we may reassess at some point).

So:
1) Helios can live-probe sweed's current catalog entries and prior purchase history (especially those from same-distributor or eventually same vendor) and attempt to make use of vendor naming and abbreviation conventions that they tend to follow over time, or at least which don't change too rapidly or often, and thus really shouldn't be relying on stale, cached, mirrored catalog info.  It should live-refresh whatever it needs early on in the job: learn the current set of brands, categories, strains, sizes, product groups, variants, etc that can be used.
2) An advanced LLM can be provided with contextually relevant additional data, like the prior purchases from same vendor or distributor, and the eventually-sanctioned outcome for each line item.  This can help establish naming conventions for products, both spotting them from the vendor and following our own implied or explicit conventions as we make additions to existing vendor catalog subsets.
3) Initially, the "REPL" aspect of this latest model was solely limited to an operator-provided hint, which could be plain text, and which should be able to influence the LLM's reasoning.  Despite this implementation, I still had lots of trouble (hints not being "parsed" (what?), hints not parsing fast enough before the purchase job gets started (so it's missing its expected hints and fails), hint instructions being ignored entirely, hint text disappearing from the UI on job failure (boy does this ENTIRE page violate our UI/UX and agent->operator prioritization for efficiency and "what you will or should need or want next is trivially available at your fingertips" absolute UX requirements.
4) However, it now occurs to me that we don't have to stop here.  Let's make the operator interaction with the LLM somewhat turn-based (a _real_ REPL experience), and give the implementation / design for this functionality the ability to iterate potentially multiple times over a single packet, iteratively evolving the packet towards "correct".  It shouldn't take TOO many LLM turns to get to a good spot, but I really need the ability to provide immediate-term feedback and have it incorporated live, rather than having to re-trigger the entire process, from scratch, each time.  Remember, operator efficiency and utility (especially on mobile devices) is critical!
5) As an example, the existing in-helios page for purchase packets, once _completed_ and we're looking at line items (which again seems far inferior to where we landed just before "migration" (which apparently became "re-implementation of an approximation of the prior experience, from scratch, seemingly using a description rather than the former better-UX implementation itself (which the very first worker agents working on this DEFINITELY had access to, howver this predates even the migration of development onto prod machines, and certainly predates our highly constrained and controlled (in theory) development process of today, so not much of a surprise), IS TERRIBLE!  Operator interaction points are scattered all around, with unclear semantics in some cases, and outright broken implementation in others (i can't count the number of "this item already modified, reload the page" which is never good).  Things like "which category is this item", "Which brand", "what should we initially price it", "what image (if any) should we initially use"?  These all seem to be throw together as a afterthough, with operator needing multiple clicks in different, sometimes hidden page sections (and sometimes extremely convoluted effort if the packet produced isn't that great and needed lots of work), not to mention a very bizarre staging / select "visible" / apply "selected" make-live process.

None of that operator manual work in (5) of laborious and error probe UI twiddling should be necessary when we have a highly capable LLM involved in the process, and can loop / repl it with feedback until we're happy.  Rather than having to update structured data on multiple line items, one at a time, i should be able to say something like "All of those 1g prerolls are actually infused, and should be initially priced at $16.50", submit this, and a short time have a notification that the packet has been updated/regenerated.  Packets should probably track their history along with operator responses and metadata about the distributor, vendor (once this data is present), etc, and over time we should be able to build up sufficient context and prior examples (but specifically relevant!  same brand? vendor? distributor even perhaps?), potentially both of positive success LLM cases and where the operator had to redirect or guide, and the LLM should ideally be able to get quite close on most purchases on its own in the first iteration!

Work through the system design and new UI/UX experience with Oracle, and once both are approved, begin epic creation and start this project!
