# Helios signed readonly access — `automation` child epic

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#62](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/62)
> — "Need a means for local agents to access helios in trusted fashion".
> **Resolved design:** [`docs/epics/helios-agent-readonly-access/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](../../RESOLVED_DESIGN.md).
> **Delegated because:** the verifier, auth/session contracts, route gates,
> response caps, and audit logging live in `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` under
> `helios/`. Do not implement the NixOS key/config rollout or the agent-side
> browser helper in this child epic.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` for this epic MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#62`, plus
> this child epic's own `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer
> so the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to this delegated child.

## 1. Goal

Implement the **Helios-native** half of temporary, non-mutating, auditable live
verification for local agents. A local `amp-local` verifier will sign each
request with an Ed25519 private key; Helios verifies the request with configured
public keys, checks a narrow expiring allowlist, and then exposes only a
synthetic `agent_readonly` viewer principal.

This is not a general machine-to-machine API, not a write path, not a normal
operator login, and not a reason to weaken OAuth for real users.

## 2. Current state to inspect first (all paths under `helios/`)

| Concern | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Global auth gate | `src/server/auth/authGate.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) | Currently allows health/login/session/public endpoints and valid signed session cookies; all other app/API/asset paths are session-gated. Integrate signed-agent verification before the unauthenticated response, without adding broad public endpoints. |
| Session envelope + role gates | `src/server/auth/requireSession.ts` | `buildSessionEnvelope()` reads a signed cookie and DB user; `requireSessionUser()`, `requireMetricsGrant()`, `requireConfidentialMetricsGrant()`, and `requireCashierDisplayUser()` enforce downstream authorization. Add the explicit `agent_readonly` principal here, not a fake DB user or cookie. |
| Session contract | `src/shared/contracts/api/session.ts`, `src/server/routes/session.ts` | `authMode` is currently `anonymous | session`. Add `agent_readonly` and ensure `/api/session` returns a synthetic viewer envelope only for accepted signed-agent requests. |
| Permission helpers | `src/shared/domain/permissions.ts`, `src/shared/contracts/domain/auth.ts`, `src/server/auth/permissions.ts` | Reuse existing viewer permission semantics and role ordering; do not add editor/admin shortcuts for the synthetic principal. |
| Runtime config/env | `src/server/config/env.ts` | Add env/config parsing for public verifier keys, active allowlist JSON/path, timestamp skew, nonce cache sizing/TTL if needed, and default response byte cap. Keep private signing keys out of Helios config. |
| Server assembly | `src/server/app/buildServer.ts`, `src/server/main.ts` | Wire verifier/allowlist initialization through the existing app lifecycle. Signed-agent access must fail closed when config is absent or malformed. |
| Route tests/patterns | `src/server/auth/authGate.test.ts`, focused route tests under `src/server/routes/*.test.ts` | Extend existing `server.inject` patterns for accepted/denied signed requests and downstream gate denial. |
| Metrics/admin/cashier gates | `src/server/routes/metrics.ts`, `src/server/routes/catalogAnalytics.ts`, `src/server/routes/budtenderAnalytics.ts`, admin/config routes, cashier-display route using `requireCashierDisplayUser()` | Add focused coverage that `agent_readonly` can satisfy only viewer routes explicitly allowed by rule, and is denied for metrics grants, admin/config, cashier-display, and mutating routes. |

## 3. Design decisions to preserve

1. **Ed25519, not HMAC.** Helios stores public verifier keys only. A Helios
   config leak must not grant signing power.
2. **GET/HEAD only.** `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, and `OPTIONS` are denied
   before route handling, even with a valid signature and allowlist rule.
3. **No mixed credentials.** Any signed-agent request carrying `Cookie` or
   `Authorization` is rejected before route handling. Do not allow a real user
   session and an agent signature to combine.
4. **Signature covers the exact authorization decision.** The canonical payload
   covers method, host, exact path + query, timestamp, nonce, key id, and rule
   id. Reject ambiguous path/query encodings rather than silently normalizing
   them into an authorization decision.
5. **Narrow, expiring allowlist.** No `/api/*`, `/api/admin/*`, or page-rule
   implies API-rule behavior. Every rule has `not_before`, `not_after`, owner,
   reason, path entries, safe-read notes, and a response byte cap.
6. **Explicit `agent_readonly` principal.** Do not mint a cookie and do not
   create a `users` row. Viewer-only route code may see a synthetic viewer;
   editor/approver/admin, metrics grants, confidential metrics, and cashier
   display still deny.
7. **Metadata audit only.** Log accepted and denied signed requests with
   outcome/reason, key id, rule id, method, path, status, response bytes,
   remote/forwarded metadata, timestamp, and nonce. Never log private keys,
   signatures, cookies, authorization headers, or response bodies.
8. **Response caps are enforced in code.** Deny or abort oversized responses;
   do not rely on route authors or downstream clients to self-limit.

## 4. Request contract

Use a small explicit header set (names may change if implementation finds an
existing naming convention, but the semantics must stay):

| Header | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `X-Helios-Agent-Key-Id` | Selects the configured public verifier key. |
| `X-Helios-Agent-Rule-Id` | Selects the allowlist rule claimed by the request. |
| `X-Helios-Agent-Timestamp` | RFC3339 or Unix timestamp; reject outside a short 60–120s skew window. |
| `X-Helios-Agent-Nonce` | Random per request; reject replay within the skew window. |
| `X-Helios-Agent-Signature` | Base64url Ed25519 signature over the canonical payload. |

Canonical payload shape:

```text
helios-agent-readonly-v1
method:GET
host:helios.freshlybaked.us
path:/config/agent-waste?tab=pending
key_id:amp-local-vps3-2026q3
rule_id:agent-waste-review-2026-07-10
timestamp:2026-07-10T05:30:00Z
nonce:<128-bit random base64url>
```

Replay protection can be an in-memory per-process `(keyId, nonce)` cache for
v1. Document cross-process/cross-host replay within the short skew window as a
residual risk; do not add a DB/shared nonce store unless the implementation
task obtains the required review and operator approval.

## 5. Allowlist contract

Read allowlist rules from Helios runtime config provisioned by the NixOS child.
Example shape:

```json
{
  "id": "agent-waste-review-2026-07-10",
  "owner": "virusdave/top-level#62 rollout",
  "reason": "Verify the agent-waste review page after deploy and collect Oracle UI evidence.",
  "not_before": "2026-07-10T00:00:00Z",
  "not_after": "2026-07-17T00:00:00Z",
  "max_response_bytes": 1048576,
  "paths": [
    { "method": "GET", "kind": "page", "match": "exact", "path": "/config/agent-waste", "safe_read_note": "SPA route only; no write action." },
    { "method": "GET", "kind": "api", "match": "exact", "path": "/api/agent-waste/backlog", "safe_read_note": "Read-only backlog endpoint; no promote/write path." },
    { "method": "GET", "kind": "asset", "match": "prefix", "path": "/assets/", "safe_read_note": "Hashed Vite static assets only; byte-capped." },
    { "method": "GET", "kind": "session", "match": "exact", "path": "/api/session", "safe_read_note": "Returns synthetic agent_readonly envelope only." }
  ]
}
```

Implementation requirements:

- Prefer exact path matches. Prefix matches require segment-boundary checks and
  should normally be limited to hashed static assets.
- Page rules do not imply API rules; list every SPA loader/API call separately.
- API rules require route-specific safe-read notes because a `GET` handler can
  still trigger refreshes, external calls, streams, costly DB scans, cache
  writes, or large downloads.
- Deny streaming/SSE/download responses by default. Any future CSV/ZIP/report
  route needs an explicit rule and cap.
- Fail closed if allowlist JSON is absent, invalid, inactive, expired, or has an
  unknown kind/match shape.

## 6. Suggested implementation leaves

Author these as the child epic's own frontier leaves when the automation epic
root is broken down:

### H1 — Verifier + allowlist parser (no auth bypass yet)

- Add a small signed-readonly module, e.g. `src/server/auth/agentReadonly.ts`,
  that parses headers, builds the canonical payload, verifies Ed25519
  signatures using configured public keys, checks timestamp skew, rejects nonce
  replay, evaluates allowlist method/path/rule activity, and returns a typed
  accept/deny result with an audit reason.
- Add env/config parsing in `src/server/config/env.ts` for public verifier keys,
  allowlist JSON/path, skew, and default/max response cap. Helios must never
  read private signing material.
- Tests: canonical payload bytes, signature success/failure, unknown key, bad
  base64, missing headers, timestamp too old/too new, nonce replay, inactive
  rule, exact/prefix path matching, method mismatch, broad/invalid rule denial,
  and ambiguous path/query rejection.

### H2 — Auth gate integration + audit + byte caps

- Integrate the verifier into `authGate.ts` before unauthenticated redirects or
  401s. Accepted signed-agent requests should attach an `agent_readonly`
  principal to the request for downstream session code; denied signed attempts
  should return a flat 401/403-style response and should not fall through to a
  cookie path.
- Reject `Cookie` or `Authorization` on signed-agent requests before route
  handling.
- Enforce allowlist `max_response_bytes` for accepted signed-agent responses;
  abort/deny and audit `too_large` if the cap is exceeded. Ensure `HEAD` does
  not accidentally require a body to count bytes.
- Add structured log entries for accepted and denied signed-agent attempts,
  metadata only.
- Tests: `authGate.test.ts` accepted GET/HEAD, POST denied, mixed credentials
  denied, non-allowlisted page/API/asset denied, oversized response denied, and
  no signatures/secrets/cookies in logs.

### H3 — Session/principal contract

- Extend the session contract to `authMode: 'anonymous' | 'session' |
  'agent_readonly'`.
- Update `buildSessionEnvelope()` / `requireSessionUser()` so an accepted
  `agent_readonly` request returns a synthetic active viewer such as
  `agent-readonly@local.helios`, with viewer permissions and an empty
  `metricGrants` list, only where the caller asks for `viewer`.
- Ensure `requireSessionUser(..., 'editor' | 'approver' | 'admin')` denies, and
  `requireMetricsGrant()`, `requireConfidentialMetricsGrant()`, and
  `requireCashierDisplayUser()` deny because the synthetic viewer has no grants
  and is not a cashier-display allowlisted email.
- Tests: `/api/session` envelope for accepted signed-agent request;
  viewer-route success when explicitly allowlisted; editor/admin denial;
  metrics and cashier-display denial.

### H4 — Route-author docs and focused safe-read examples

- Add Helios docs for route authors describing how to decide whether a GET route
  is safe to allowlist, including hazards: writes hidden behind GET, cache or
  external refreshes, expensive scans, streaming/SSE/downloads, PII-heavy pages,
  and required byte caps.
- Include example allowlist snippets for the intended first verification page
  (`/config/agent-waste` plus its necessary loader/API/session/static asset
  routes), but keep them inactive/example-only unless the NixOS child has
  provisioned the real production config.
- Tests/docs review: verify docs explicitly say page rules do not imply API
  rules and private signing keys never belong in Helios config.

## 7. Out of scope for this child

- NixOS secrets/config rollout, nginx header stripping, optional loopback vhost,
  vps2/vps3 parity, and rollback commands live in the `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`
  child epic.
- The agent-side `fetch`/`render` helper, Playwright no-cookie context,
  per-request signing, local evidence bundle, and Oracle attachment workflow live
  in the agent-helper owner child (likely `Nicponskis/github-worker`).
- Live rollout verification is a later cross-repo leaf after Helios and NixOS
  changes are deployed through sanctioned paths. Do not fake it from unit tests.
- DB-backed audit or nonce storage is not part of v1. If implementation finds a
  DB change is necessary, stop for Oracle DB review and explicit operator go.

## 8. Gates and safety

- Follow `automation/AGENTS.md` dev-loop gates. Expected local checks for this
  Helios server/shared change:
  - `cd helios && npm run typecheck`
  - `cd helios && npm run typecheck:client` when the shared session contract or
    client-visible envelope changes
  - Focused Vitest runs for touched auth/session/route tests, e.g.
    `cd helios && npm run test -- src/server/auth/authGate.test.ts` plus any new
    verifier/require-session tests.
- No serving service restarts. Deploy, if a later implementation leaf reaches
  deployment, only via `self-deploy-helios` after push and per canon.
- No production DB writes or migrations for v1.
- Rollback is a normal revert + redeploy, and the NixOS side can separately
  expire/remove allowlist rules and public keys. With config absent or invalid,
  signed-agent access must fail closed while normal OAuth sessions keep working.

## 9. Acceptance criteria

- Helios has Ed25519 signed-agent verification with canonical payload tests.
- Signed-agent requests are accepted only for GET/HEAD, no Cookie, no
  Authorization, fresh timestamp, non-replayed nonce, valid key/signature,
  active allowlist rule, exact allowed path/query, and route-specific safe-read
  entry.
- Accepted requests expose `authMode: 'agent_readonly'` and a synthetic viewer,
  not a cookie or DB user.
- Viewer-only allowed routes can be read; mutating routes, admin/config,
  editor/approver/admin gates, metrics grants, confidential metrics, and
  cashier-display gates deny.
- Response byte caps are enforced and audited.
- Structured audit logs include metadata and deny reasons, never secrets,
  signatures, credentials, or response bodies.
- Route-author docs explain safe-read allowlisting and the page/API/asset/session
  split.

# Low-inventory review page — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Thin index over the authoritative parent plan
> [`docs/epics/low-inventory-review/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> `virusdave/top-level`. Where this and the parent disagree, the parent
> wins — fix this doc. Tracking issue:
> [virusdave/top-level#32](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/32).
> **APPROVED — parent [§6](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#6-blocking-decisions-operator)
> resolved by the operator 2026-07-06, then write model SIMPLIFIED
> 2026-07-09 (parent
> [§6.11](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#611-2026-07-09-operator-simplification-no-quantity-writes-move-to-a-configurable-not-for-sale-room)).**
> Materialises via the issue #32 decomposition (the
> `Materialise-Child-Epic: FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` trailer group under
> `Parent-Issue: #32`).
>
> **⚠️ 2026-07-09 supersede (parent §6.11).** Helios **never adjusts Sweed
> stock quantities** for this feature. Both short-count and zero-count
> perform the **same reversible action**: move the affected package(s) to a
> **UI-configurable NOT FOR SALE room** (default = per-site "Hold for Dave
> inspection"). This **retires** the set-quantity write, the METRC ceiling,
> the counted-more readback, the write-mode A/B model, and the mandatory
> two-stage `Inventory Count Verification` room. The operator's other answers
> still apply (per-package barcode/METRC-scan granularity, first-to-zero
> location verification, a universal 24h one-offs link, a barcode-scan mobile
> review queue on the roadmap). Building still proceeds phased, safest-first;
> **no write to live Sweed inventory** (now only a reversible room transfer)
> ships outside operator-approved, feature-flagged, single-site-pilot
> rollout.

## Scope (Helios only)

A new per-site Helios operator page that lists SKUs with **`1 <= combined
FOR-SALE stock <= N`** (`N` admin-configurable, default 2; combined-0
excluded), grouped by warehousing location, lets an operator enter the
**actual physical count per package** (barcode/METRC scan), and on an
operator-confirmed short/zero count reacts with a `page-dave` (short `-p 2`,
zero `-p 3`) and **moves the affected package(s) to a UI-configurable NOT FOR
SALE room** (parent §6.11; default = per-site "Hold for Dave inspection") via
the existing `move-package-to-inspection` / `stockTransferService` transfer.
**Helios does not adjust Sweed stock quantities** — short and zero count use
the same reversible transfer, differing only in page priority. Complementary
to Sweed cycle counting and to Helios' existing velocity-based reordering
analytics — do **not** duplicate them.

## First task: confirm the in-repo facts

The parent §1 cites likely files from a read-only audit; verify each before
coding (the top-level repo cannot build Helios):

- `src/server/db/schema/sweedPackageSnapshots.sql` + the
  `sweed_package_current` view — columns `available_qty`, `stock_location`,
  `internal_track_code`, `dealer_id`, `product_sku`, `inventory_item_id`.
- `src/server/metrics/_real/sweedPackageSnapshotsQueries.ts` — the shared
  `FOR SALE%` / `available_qty` low-stock query helpers to **reuse**.
- `src/server/routes/catalogMaintenance.ts` +
  `src/server/catalog/maintenance.ts` — the existing
  `move-package-to-inspection` write path (`store.inventory.item.transfer`
  into `NOT FOR SALE - Hold for Dave inspection`) to reuse for the
  zero-count action.
- `src/server/catalog/stockTransferService.ts` — the transfer primitive,
  now the **sole write path** (parent §6.11): used for both the short-count
  and the zero-count move into the configurable NOT FOR SALE room.
- **No trade-sample set-quantity spike needed (parent §6.11).** The former
  "FIND FIRST: locate & generalize the 'reduce trade sample to zero' write"
  task is **dropped** — Helios no longer adjusts Sweed quantities, so there
  is no set-quantity write, no METRC-ceiling handling, and no counted-more
  readback to build.
- `src/worker/runtime/pageDave.ts` + `src/server/routes/warehouseLocations.ts`
  — `pageDave({ priority })`; the resolved page levels are literal ntfy `-p`:
  short `-p 2`, zero `-p 3`, counted-0-but-held `-p 4` (parent §6.2/§6.8).
- `src/shared/contracts/domain/pendingPurchases.ts` — site→dealer resolution.
- `src/server/app/buildServer.ts` + `src/client/app/router.tsx` — route
  registration; mirror the Catalog Maintenance / Inventory Procurement
  pages.
- `src/client/routes/catalog/LiveBarcodeScanner.tsx` and
  `WarehouseLocationsPage.tsx` — reuse the canonical camera scanner and its
  manual/hardware-scanner fallback pattern; do not create a second scanner.
- **Confirm (parent §6.5/§6.11):** the configured NOT FOR SALE destination
  room per site — default `Hold for Dave inspection` (fuzzy name match, IDs
  differ). Wire the destination as an **admin/UI-configurable setting**
  (parent §6.11), not a hardcoded name; the operator will later create a
  dedicated NOT FOR SALE location and repoint it. No new `Inventory Count
  Verification` room is needed unless the operator opts into the optional
  second-confirm stage.
- **Confirm (parent §6.8):** `current_qty` vs `available_qty` as the
  reconciliation baseline, and the behavior of `transferReservedItems: false`
  when a counted-zero package still has `hold_qty > 0`.
- **Design (parent §6.10/§6.11):** the **24h one-offs link** on every page,
  the **first-transition-to-zero** verification (last-known location code +
  METRC-tag suffix), and — only if the operator opts in — an optional
  non-admin second-confirm stage (parent §6.11; not required for safety since
  the move is reversible). The actual representative **mobile/tablet UI and
  notification templates must be Oracle-reviewed before every
  operator-facing phase first lands, including P0.**

## Operator workflow acceptance (binding)

The page optimizes for a mobile operator walking one physical location at a
time. Keep the current item and likely next action visible; collapse
methodology/provenance; never make the operator return to a dashboard to find
the result of the action they just took.

1. **Queue:** one explicit site, grouped in practical shelf/room walking order;
   current and next unresolved package remain visible. Handle populated,
   empty, loading, error, stale, long-name, multi-location, and multi-package
   states without horizontal scrolling or explanatory clutter.
2. **Scan:** reuse `LiveBarcodeScanner` plus Warehouse Locations' camera,
   manual-entry, still-photo, and hardware-scanner patterns. Scanning never
   writes. Exactly one package becomes active; duplicate, unreadable, unknown,
   ambiguous, wrong-site, camera-denied, and camera-unavailable scans recover
   inline without losing queue position.
3. **Count:** enter/tally physical count, then show a distinct equal, short,
   zero, over, or held result. A captured discrepancy remains visibly
   unresolved as **count recorded, package still for sale, transfer pending**;
   do not suppress it or call it reconciled.
4. **Review:** inventory changes require a separate package-specific
   confirmation showing site, product, METRC suffix, Sweed and physical
   counts, source room, configured destination, and that the **whole package**
   leaves the customer menu. No bulk transfer and no fallback-all-lots
   behavior. A stale live package stops, refreshes, and requires reconfirmation.
5. **Recover and continue:** prevent double-submit; distinguish in-flight,
   conflict, timeout/unknown outcome, partial success, success, undo success,
   and undo failure. An unknown outcome is verified before retry. Success
   stays inline with destination, audit status, undo, 24h detail link, and the
   next package action.
6. **Accessibility:** no horizontal scrolling at 320/375px phone or
   768/1024px tablet widths; 44px minimum primary targets; labeled numeric
   input; keyboard/hardware-scanner completion; focus-managed dialogs,
   visible focus, `aria-live` status, and no color-only meaning.
7. **Oracle evidence before first exposure:** actual phone and tablet renders
   for every queue state in item 1; scanner idle/active/denied/unknown/
   ambiguous/matched; equal/short/zero/over/held and count-pending;
   confirmation/in-flight/conflict/unknown-outcome/success/undo; unavailable
   destination; first-to-zero verification; admin room configuration; each
   batched `page-dave` template; and active/expired 24h detail views. Oracle
   must return APPROVE for the relevant set before that surface lands.

## Phases (parent §5 — production-safety order)

- **P0 — read-only review page.** Per-site `1 <= combined FOR-SALE <= N`
  table (admin-configurable `N`, default 2; combined-0 excluded), grouped by
  warehousing location, from `sweed_package_current` (reuse the shared
  queries). No inputs/writes/pages. `viewer`/metrics-grant read. Safe to
  deploy under normal Helios deploy.
- **P1a — physical-count entry + audit record (no write, no page).**
  Per-package physical-count input (barcode/METRC scan, parent §6.3); write
  the reconciliation record (P3 table). Captured discrepancies remain pending
  and visible until resolved. `editor` grant.
- **P1b — configure and validate the NOT FOR SALE target (no inventory
  write).** Admin/UI setting per site (default = "Hold for Dave inspection").
  Resolve and display the exact site/room before transfer enablement; fail
  closed when unavailable. Optional second confirm only if the operator opts
  in.
- **P1c — short-count page + move-to-NOT-FOR-SALE (write-gated).** On
  operator-confirmed `0 < count < Sweed`: `page-dave -p 2` (parent §6.2) +
  **move the affected package(s) to the configurable NOT FOR SALE room**
  (parent §6.11, default = per-site "Hold for Dave inspection") via
  `move-package-to-inspection` / `stockTransferService`, capturing
  from-room/qty undo data in the audit row. **No Sweed quantity write** (the
  set-quantity path, METRC ceiling, write-mode A/B, and counted-more readback
  are all retired — parent §6.11). `editor` grant; write path
  operator-rollout-gated. Shares its primitive with P2.
- **P2 — zero-count action + first-to-zero verification.** On
  operator-confirmed `count == 0`: `page-dave -p 3` (§6.2) + move to the
  **same configurable NOT FOR SALE room** via `move-package-to-inspection`
  (parent §6.11, site-equivalent room, parent §6.5); the counted-0-but-held
  edge pages `-p 4` + 24h one-offs (parent §6.8); add the
  first-transition-to-zero verification (last-known location code + METRC
  suffix, parent §6.6). `editor` grant; operator-rollout-gated. Shares the
  P1c transfer primitive.
- **P3 — reconciliation audit + no-renag.** Helios table (site, SKU/package,
  Sweed-qty snapshot, operator count, action, actor, ts); suppress
  resolved lines for a configurable window; never suppress captured-but-
  unresolved discrepancies; per-SKU history. Its schema lands with P1a.
- **P4 — mobile review queue (roadmap, parent §6.10).** Non-admin
  barcode-scan re-confirmation queue on the P1a/P3 foundation.
- **Cross-cutting:** every page carries a **24h one-offs link** to an
  info-dense mobile/tablet-first operator view; that UI **must pass an Oracle
  review before first exposure, including P0** (parent §5.1/§6.10).

## Verification

- Build/lint/typecheck green.
- P0: unit test the `combined FOR-SALE <= N` query against seeded snapshot
  rows; grouping renders for both a parseable shelf code and a stock-room
  fallback.
- UI: focused interaction/accessibility tests cover the full binding workflow,
  including scan recovery, no-side-effect count capture, package-specific
  confirmation, stale and unknown-outcome handling, undo, and next-item
  continuation. Capture and Oracle-review the representative evidence set
  before first exposure.
- P1/P2: discrepancy-classification unit tests mapping short/zero count to
  the **shared move-to-NOT-FOR-SALE transfer** (parent §6.11) at the correct
  page priority; the transfer reuses the existing verify-live-item +
  restore-on-failure guarantees; the configurable destination room resolves
  per site (falls back to `Hold for Dave inspection`); `pageDave` asserted
  with the agreed priority (mocked — **never** a real page in tests, canon
  no-prod-resources-in-tests). No test performs a Sweed quantity write (that
  path is retired — parent §6.11).
- P3: audit row on every action; suppression within the window.
- Only the final rollout/stability-evidence commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#32`; intermediate phase commits must not signal delegated completion.
- P1/P2 prod rollout is operator-gated: `self-deploy-helios` under explicit
  approval, then a live probe on one known low-stock SKU per site.

## Coordination

Single repo — no cross-repo contract. The parent §6 decisions are
**resolved** (operator, 2026-07-06) and the write model was **simplified**
2026-07-09 (parent §6.11 — no quantity writes, move to a configurable NOT FOR
SALE room), so all phases are unblocked to build. The remaining gates are
operational, not decisional: (i) the mobile/tablet UI must pass an **Oracle
review** before each operator-facing surface first lands, including P0
(parent §5.1/§6.10);
(ii) every live-Sweed room-transfer phase (P1c/P2) ships only under
**operator rollout approval**, feature-flagged, single-site pilot first
(Midtown). One small confirm remains for build time: whether the operator
wants the optional non-admin second-confirm stage (parent §6.11) — it is not
required for safety.

The point of https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/68 was to allow me to not generally have to review each report from agents - rather I should be able to "batch them up" and decide per batch to leave it unreviewed, "wont-fix" it, curate and promote instructions as agent nudges to prevent similar behavior, or indicate the cluster is obsolete, or was fixed by the completion of a prior task or epic (like the large cluster of "double-invocation of large-action-lock", where rather than TELL agents not to do the thing they keep doing, we just fix the tooling that makes it so easy to make that mistake.

Currently it won't let me cluster if there are more than 200 pending, which makes clustering useless for me.  Also, when in "view clusters" mode, i sometimes might want to evict a badly-clustered report.  Fix all of these.

issues.body:
[Order Placing July first Bronx - Brands_vendors.csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30157345/Order.Placing.July.first.Bronx.-.Brands_vendors.csv)

Vendors are an important concept that for some reason Sweed completely elides.  Vendors are associated with one or more brands, usually exclusively so.  Multiple vendors will use a single distributor to ship products, and different vendors' products may end up in the same physical shipment to our stores.  However, critically, Vendors are the "atomic ordering surface" - it is THEY who we place orders with, and THEY who choose what their "case sizes" (minimum qty order granularity for a sku) are, and whether to enforce them always, not on the first order, or rarely / not at all.  Many vendors will break case sizes for initial orders to de-risk the retailers - subsequent orders will typically be subject to case sizes, however.  Usually (but not strictly ALWAYS), SKUs that are in the same brand-categorical-family (by definition from the same vendor) are similar-ish products, and usually will have the same case minimums, so we can often make reasonable educated guesses for these based on prior orders.  An example: If every purchase containing Brand X (which we now know to be Vendor Y) has 1g prerolls received in either 25, 50, 75, or 100 qty for the line item, it's a pretty reasonable inference that "1g prerolls for vendor Y come in cases of 25 units"

Somewhere in metrics (specifically `-> inventory -> Distributor baskets`), you had a clever idea, but it would (a) need to happen at the granularity of Vendor, not Distributor, and (b) would have to be realistic in the case sizing (for prerolls, cases will often be large, 25, 50, 100 are common), which we should start attempting to learn from our now extensive Purchase history across both sites over the last year.

Attached is a seed association of Brand to Vendor, occasionally with notes about case sizing or other misc info.  Use this to see our list of Vendors, and populate their associated Brands.  Given the Brands, we can then see which distributor(s) do or have carried that vendor's products historically, and go hunting for those purchases to see if we have enough data to infer useful info.

The primary goal here is to introduce the concept into the data model, update the "distributor baskets" to be "vendor baskets" with a followup ticket to dramatically improve case quantity inference, add a page in a reasonable spot in the hierarchy where I can edit this data, create new Vendors, update vendor<-->brand associations, mark a vendor as "MSO" or "Micro" or "COD only" (or no label)

All of this is new operator-facing surface, so ensure Oracle thoroughly reviews the UI/UX and makes it phenomenal and up to our high standards.
issues.creator: virusdave
issues.title: Introduce "Vendors"

issues.body:
1) Some metrics on the Budtender Performance page seem blocked.  Make an operator-blocked task for each thing you need help to unblock one or more metrics that are currently blocked (looks like you mostly need a short list of Sweed APIs that you're unfamiliar with).
2) Currently, we're smooshing all fulfillment, payment, and category/cat+subcat types together always, when that's probably not appropriate.  Instead, we probably want to compare apples-to-apples within a single (or small number of) fulfillment types, or payment types, or categories (or category+subcategory).  In particular, delivery orders tend to be 2-3 times the size of in-person orders, and since only a MUCH smaller number of employees will ever be processing those transactions (specifically, the delivery staff), they will see a disproportionately large set of competed orders compared to everyone else, which makes the comparison somewhat nonsensical.  I should be able to _easily_ restrict to "kiosk style and in-person", "express pickup / web", and "delivery COD or prepaid".  However I should be able to choose any arbitrary subset of these to restrict sales being considered.  This problem actually makes most of the "core" metrics useless, as the delivery staff then blow out the distribution pretty badly.  Further, a cashier with a tiny number of sales (<=5? <=10?) should be outright excluded.  Jackie has maybe one "sale" and it was processing a refund, i think, which further blows things out of distribution.
3) When you don't have a cashier's name, and just an opaque identified like `Cashier 22244`, that is not a sufficient state to remain in.  You should be able to retrieve the employee name with the sweed `user.compliance.list` call to access each site's employees.  Do that to refresh data liveliness when we see known-bad (especially known-stale) data; there's no reason to KEEP seeing that after several days, let alone a minute, at least when a data refresh is "cheap enough", like this should be.  Expensive DB queries should not be executed at page first-render solely in the name freshness.  Consulting a cache, however, could be.
4) Like other graphs, the tooltip is generally unusable on mobile; it seems to locate itself at the top right of the _parent container_ of the graph, which then disappears if you try to scroll the page, so most graphs' tooltips are inaccessible entirely.  If this has been canonically solved with a core "mobile-friendly tooltip positioning" implementation / fix, then try to make use of it if you can rather than duplicating an implementation.
5) Similarly, I'll want to be able to go fullscreen on both mobile and desktop on any arbitrary graph.  
6) The column headers are somewhat able to be intuited, but there's definitely some ambiguity.  They need tooltips of their own.  I'm not sure what the right way to handle "need to explain what that abbreviation actually means, but can't eat up screen space on the header to show a spinner or dropdown arrow or whatever.  It would probably have to be something like make the headers look clickable as though they were HREFs (blue or similar, underlined text inviting a click), except they wouldn't navigate, they would toggle that header's tooltip (while hiding any other visible tooltip)
7) Why do so many employees show as "DISABLED"?  that is definitely not right; Helios is misinterpreting some data somewhere
8) For the `Similar-cohort lift` column in `Dollar-Basket upsell lift`, i think we should not include "payment type" as a bucketing axis for transactions.  I'm skeptical (although willing to be convinced otherwise by compelling data) that the payment type doesn't make a whole lot of difference in customer behavior in aggregate (unless it's a payment STRONGLY correlated with a fulfillment type, such as Aeropay), whereas the fulfillment type has a HUGE correlation to different "types" of customer purchase profiles that should be able to be considered separately (or, if desired, all together; i should be able to select a subset of fulfillment types, as mentioned above; some go naturally together)
9) What is the graphic for `same lift, ±` supposed to be?  I basically can't tell what it's trying to show.  All but 1 or 2 cashiers effectively just have a tiny slice near the exact middle.  Are these supposed to be IQR or 2std dev or something like that?  If so, most cashiers' ranges are basically points, at least visually.  Mostly it's the non-cashiers who have processed like 5 transactions that have large bars in that graphic
10) Same comment on tooltips for the column headers.  There's a lot of ambiguity and i'm kind of guessing at the precise meaning of some of these.
11) For `Drawer-shift productivity`, we need to apply some sanity checking on how we produce this data.  I'm highly skeptical of it, and it seems unreliable and "off" to me in many cases.


I'm pretty sure that (4) and (5) have been brought up before, so there's likely a task-dag task for each of those, but it might have been completed.  If they exist and are open, you can make tasks for 4 & 5 that are blocked on the other ones for a canonical single implementation (be sure to note in the other tasks' thread(s) that the implementing agent should implement knowing they are creating the single core implementation, so it should be well-designed, composable, orthogonal in design, etc.

## Outcome

New generated and imported pending-purchase packets must immediately support iterative LLM refinement. Repair production packet 74 so the operator can refine it without losing any packet-row business data.

## Confirmed defect

Migration 102 backfilled refinement lineage for packets that existed at migration time, but `persistPendingPurchasePacket` still writes the legacy unrooted shape afterward. Packet 74 was generated after the prior deployment and has no packet root, revision number, or row lineage IDs, so the UI correctly but unhelpfully reports “refinement unavailable.”

## Scope

- Make packet persistence transactionally create revision-1 packet/root/row lineage metadata when migration 102 is available, while preserving the exact legacy path before that schema exists.
- Cover both generated and imported packets because both use this persistence function.
- Deploy through `self-deploy-helios`.
- In one guarded transaction after deploy, repair packet 74 only: recheck preconditions, assign its row lineage metadata, create its active root, supersede the stale packet-70 root as required, and verify packet 74 is the sole active/current root.
- Verify the refinement endpoint no longer reports packet 74 as unavailable.

## Authorization and review

The operator explicitly authorized implementation, deployment, and the production packet-74 transactional repair in the current Amp thread. Oracle previously approved the writer approach and conditioned the production write on that explicit approval, fixed-writer-first deployment, immediate precondition rechecks, an exclusive packet-table lock, and atomic rollback on any mismatch.

issues.body:
## Current state and outcome

[Vendor baskets introduced in automation issue 79](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/79) correctly leave `caseSizeUnits` unset when a mapped vendor has no structured terms. This follow-up should replace that explicit unknown with conservative, explainable case quantities learned from received Sweed purchase history.

The operator should gain a review queue for trustworthy SKU- and category-family evidence, then approved terms should make basket quantities realistic. The system must abstain when evidence is incomplete or ambiguous. It must never infer across vendors that happen to share a distributor, and it must not silently parse the seeded prose notes into policy.

**Non-goals:** changing the already-released unknown-case fallback; treating divisibility as proof of a case size; inferring terms for families with no evidence; calling Sweed from the inference path; or enabling automatic snapping before a separate operator-approved shadow rollout.

## Required behavior

### Establish typed source eligibility first

The mirror already preserves purchase/line identity, delivery date, free-text order status, quantities, distributor product identity/name, Sweed product identity/name, SKU, brand/category/subcategory/size/retail pack, costs, sample flags, package receipt data, and raw position JSON. However, it does not persist `orderStatus.id`, reversal/return semantics are not identified, and `ordered_units` currently comes from the first available value among `positionProductQty`, `orderPositionQty`, and `distributorProductQty` without recording which source won.

Before inference:

- inventory real Sweed status IDs and any return, credit, deletion, or reversal fields from representative read-only purchase responses;
- persist typed status/eligibility fields and `ordered_units_source` in the purchase mirror;
- define and test a strict received/completed status allowlist;
- fail closed on unknown status, missing delivery date, unresolved quantity semantics, unresolved vendor, samples, non-positive/fractional quantities, and any identified reversal/return/credit state.

Do not claim that returns or credits are excluded until their source signal is identified. Preserve every exclusion reason for audit.

### Form deterministic observations and scopes

Aggregate split lines into one observation per `(dealer_id, po_id, sweed_product_id)` before scoring. Sum eligible quantities only when their source semantics and family dimensions agree; otherwise mark the observation conflicting. Require `sweed_product_id` for exact-SKU scope and never merge products by name.

Support only these inferred scopes:

1. **Exact product:** canonical vendor plus `sweed_product_id`.
2. **Category family:** canonical vendor plus category, subcategory, normalized size, and retail pack count.

Extract or reuse one canonical family normalizer. Prefer stable category/subcategory IDs; normalize size with the existing catalog/pending-purchase size semantics; retain retail pack count separately. Missing or conflicting family dimensions make family inference unavailable. Do not infer vendor-wide quantities. A vendor-wide term is allowed only as an explicit manual policy.

### Select candidates conservatively

Candidate quantities are strict `Ncpk` tokens or actually observed integral order quantities, bounded to 2 through 100 units. A strict `Ncpk` token is case/order evidence, not retail `pack_count`; it must continue to leave retail `pack_count = 1`. A quantity supports candidate `q` when it is an integral multiple of `q`.

- **Exact product:** at least 3 observations from 3 distinct purchase orders over at least 30 days, including 2 observations after the possible first-order event.
- **Category family:** at least 6 observations from 4 distinct purchase orders and 2 distinct Sweed products over at least 60 days. No product may contribute more than half of supporting observations.

Select the largest candidate supported by at least 80% of observations and at least 3 purchase orders. Compare it with every other candidate; its support must lead the runner-up by at least 20 percentage points or the result is ambiguous. Quantity-only divisibility is never stronger than `medium`: for example, `[50, 100, 150]` may suggest 50 but cannot prove that the true case is not 25. `High` requires agreeing strict `Ncpk` evidence from an eligible line or operator confirmation, which becomes a manual term.

### Keep first-order breaks explicit

For each `(vendor, family, site)`, the possible first-order event is the earliest uniquely ordered purchase order, not an arbitrary earliest line. Tied or ambiguous earliest delivery timestamps cannot be excluded.

Evaluate each candidate both with all observations and with only that first purchase-order event removed. Classify the removed event as `possible_first_order_break` only when it is a non-multiple, at least 3 later observations across at least 2 later purchase orders are multiples, later support is at least 80%, and there are zero later non-multiples. Preserve its quantity, purchase order, date, and site. Any later exception prevents `high` confidence. Chronology alone never turns a possible break into ordering policy; an operator must explicitly choose `after_first_order` before it affects recommendations.

### Separate quantity, confidence, and enforcement

Persist a versioned calculation with candidate quantity, scope, deterministic band/reason codes, observation and purchase-order counts, support ratio, runner-up ratio, date range, direct `Ncpk` evidence, first-order evidence, exclusion/conflict counts, completeness/watermark, and source rows.

- `high`: scope thresholds pass; support is at least 90%; the lead is at least 20 points; direct `Ncpk` evidence agrees; there are no unexplained later exceptions; and evidence is complete/current.
- `medium`: scope thresholds and the 80% lead rules pass, but direct corroboration or the stronger support is absent.
- `unknown`: thresholds fail or evidence is stale, overflowed, conflicting, ambiguous, or from an old calculation version. Unknown yields no effective quantity.

Store enforcement independently as `always`, `after_first_order`, `rarely`, `none`, or `unknown`. The effective precedence is manual exact-product, manual family, manual vendor, high inferred exact-product, then high inferred family. A broader manual `none` or `rarely` disables narrower inference. Automatic snapping requires both an effective quantity and an explicit manual enforcement policy of `always` or `after_first_order`; inferred enforcement is review-only.

Manual changes are append-only audited with actor, time, source, reason, and prior value. Keep inferred evidence behind an override. Removing an override may reveal only the latest complete, current calculation. Migration 104's prose notes, including `25 and 50` and normal-versus-cash-on-delivery examples, are review evidence only until an operator confirms structured quantity and enforcement fields.

### Keep refresh and reads bounded

Inference must stay outside the interactive inventory-procurement request. Coalesce ingest-triggered work by vendor with a five-minute debounce. A daily repair processes only dirty/stale vendors, at most 50 vendors or 10 minutes per run. Normal single-vendor refresh uses at most 2 database round trips, a 365-day window, and 5,000 eligible lines. Avoid per-product queries and write only rows whose calculation digest changed.

Overflow remains unavailable while a consistent-watermark, keyset-chunked offline repair completes; never sample silently. Record and verify runs/day, rows scanned and written, write-ahead-log bytes, dead tuples, retained evidence/storage bytes, and cleanup behavior. At the documented caps, the implementation must also state worst-case daily scanned rows and storage.

Each database interaction must complete within 125 ms warm at p95 and one vendor refresh within 250 ms warm at p95. The procurement path adds one indexed term lookup, no per-row query, at most 25 ms incremental warm p95 latency, and at most 128 response bytes per SKU plus a bounded response-level term dictionary. Before rollout, capture isolated-fixture plans and production-read-only `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`, repeated full-fetch p95/bytes, and shadow `pg_stat_statements` evidence. Add or review a covering index if those bounds fail. No full-table background scan or Sweed remote procedure call is allowed.

## Review experience

The operator review queue must show candidate and effective quantity, exact/family scope, confidence band and reason codes, enforcement state, observation/purchase/product counts, support and runner-up ratios, date range, sites, direct `Ncpk` evidence, possible first-order breaks, conflicts/exclusions, freshness, and source purchase links.

Actions must allow approving/editing an exact or family manual quantity, setting vendor-wide manual policy, selecting enforcement, rejecting/marking no-case, and removing an override. Every action previews the effective precedence result and writes the audit trail. Conflicts, possible breaks, overflow, and stale evidence remain visible even when an override exists.

<details>
<summary>Deterministic and property-test fixtures</summary>

- `[25, 50, 75, 100]` suggests 25; it becomes `high` only with agreeing direct `25cpk` evidence.
- `[50, 100, 150]` can suggest 50 but stays non-automatic without direct corroboration.
- Chronological `[12, 25, 50, 25]` records the unique 12-unit possible first-order break; an ambiguous earliest date records none.
- Nine multiples plus one later non-multiple never becomes `high`.
- A second later exception prevents `high` rather than being relabeled as another first order.
- Split lines for one purchase/product aggregate into one observation and cannot inflate support.
- A 1g pre-roll family at 25 and a vape family at 12 never contaminate each other; missing family dimensions abstain.
- Family inference requires multiple products and enforces the per-product contribution cap; name collisions never merge products.
- Exact-product manual 20 overrides inferred family 25; manual vendor `none` disables narrower inference; removing an override reveals only current complete evidence.
- Strict `16cpk`/`12cpk`/`25cpk`/`32cpk` names contribute direct evidence while retail `pack_count` stays 1. Malformed, trailing, or conflicting tokens contribute no evidence.
- Unknown statuses, missing dates, unresolved quantity sources, samples, zero/fractional quantities, unresolved vendors, and identified cancellation/void/deletion/return/credit states fail closed.
- Conflicting migration-104 prose never becomes an automatic term.
- Overflow during concurrent ingest remains unavailable until the watermark-bounded repair finishes; stale calculation versions fail closed.

Use fixed-seed generated/property tests for divisibility, input-order invariance, split/duplicate idempotence, precedence, and this qualified monotonicity rule: once thresholds pass, adding a later contradictory observation cannot raise the candidate's band. Use isolated ephemeral PostgreSQL for query/index tests; tests never use production resources.

</details>

## Acceptance criteria

- Typed purchase eligibility and quantity-source semantics are inventoried, persisted, allowlisted, and tested before inference consumes history.
- A versioned deterministic module produces explainable exact-product and family suggestions using the thresholds above; unsupported vendor-wide inference does not exist.
- Case quantity, confidence, and enforcement are separate. Manual precedence, disable behavior, and append-only audit are implemented.
- First-order breaks are separate evidence and cannot become effective policy without operator confirmation.
- Vendor baskets read only precomputed effective terms and identify manual/inferred source, scope, confidence, and enforcement in the application programming interface, user interface, and comma-separated-value export.
- Refresh is idempotent, coalesced, bounded, off-request, and fail-closed for stale/overflow/conflicting evidence. Query plans, latency/bytes, daily load, write amplification, and storage estimates satisfy the stated budgets.
- All fixtures and qualified property tests pass, including abstention, split-line, status, first-order, override, and concurrent-overflow cases.
- Schema/backfill/rollback design receives Oracle database review before implementation. Operator review controls receive Oracle user-interface review before exposure.
- Shadow launch reviews 100% of proposed `high` terms and every break/conflict/overflow case. Automatic snapping remains disabled until separate explicit operator approval, with a tested kill switch returning immediately to manual-only/null behavior.
issues.creator: virusdave
issues.title: Infer vendor case quantities from bounded purchase history

issues.body:
## Goal

Measure the quality of Helios's capture-time nearest-transaction inference for customer reviews and design a more reliable attribution method that adds no customer steps and no checkout latency.

## Context

Issue #80 intentionally uses the nearest non-cancelled order at the same store from 30 minutes before through 4 minutes after each review. The operator accepts that this inference may be wrong because requiring a receipt, invoice ID, proof, or other customer action would reduce review volume.

## Follow-up scope

- Quantify match rate and likely false-attribution rate by site, time distance, and concurrent transaction density.
- Evaluate lower-friction signals already available to Helios or the landing page that require no customer input.
- Preserve privacy and avoid checkout-path latency.
- Propose a rollout that never retroactively rewrites historical cashier attribution without an explicit reviewed migration.
- Keep the current dashboard's dubious-quality caveat until measured evidence supports changing it.

This is a non-blocking hardening follow-up to #80.
issues.creator: virusdave
issues.title: Harden inferred customer-review cashier attribution without customer effort

issues.body:
## Outcome

Extend Helios's existing signed-agent **readonly** facility with a separate, operator-approved capability overlay for narrowly scoped mutating actions. Local workers must be able to execute an explicitly approved action sequence without receiving a general administrator session or weakening ordinary OAuth/RBAC.

Initial approved verification workflow:

1. trigger Agent Waste clustering;
2. remove one report from a displayed cluster;
3. Undo that removal.

The current Remove/Undo controls are browser-local snapshot transitions, not server mutations. Preserve that behavior unless persistence is separately approved: the initial server-side mutation grant is the exact clustering action, while browser automation exercises Remove/Undo without exposing the signing key to browser JavaScript. Any future persisted Remove/Undo endpoint requires a new approved overlay shape.

## Operator authorization and product constraints

The operator explicitly approved this capability and initial action sequence in [Amp thread T-019f7e4c-150b-77bd-b92a-d8f0c82b5d8c](https://ampcode.com/threads/T-019f7e4c-150b-77bd-b92a-d8f0c82b5d8c).

- Overlay shape is immutable once approved. Changing actions, endpoints, body/query policy, permitted keys, or extending expiry creates a new approval-bound overlay.
- Default TTL is **4 hours**; operator-selectable TTL is capped at **2 weeks**.
- Operator-assistance UX favors fast, visibly partial, useful results over brittle all-or-nothing behavior. One stochastic model/RPC failure must not erase successful work or prevent the next useful operator action.
- Do not optimize this VPN-internal operator-assistance surface around a determined attacker already inside the VPN. Preserve narrow scope, signature verification, expiry, auditability, and out-of-shape denial without making the intended workflow unusable.

## Existing systems and linked work

- Existing implementation: `helios/src/server/auth/agentReadonly.ts` and `docs/helios/signed-agent-readonly-allowlists.md`.
- Existing readonly child epic: [automation#72](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/72), from [top-level#62](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/62).
- Existing Agent Waste rollout/failures: [automation#75](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/75).
- Prior operator clustering report: [top-level#74](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/74), which specifically proposes evaluating [`clusterfck`](https://harthur.github.io/clusterfck/) or [`figue`](https://github.com/nantunes/figue) for deterministic JavaScript first-pass clustering, then optionally using the LLM to refine, improve, or critique the result.

The current facility does **not** satisfy this epic: it rejects every method except GET/HEAD, signatures do not bind a request body/action, config is process-lifetime static, nonce replay state is process-local, and `owner`/`reason` are descriptive text rather than immutable operator-approval provenance.

## Required capability-overlay contract

Design before implementation; do not mechanically add POST to `agentReadonly.ts`.

- Keep `agent_readonly` unchanged. Add a distinct signed-agent capability principal; never synthesize an admin user/cookie.
- Each immutable overlay canonically binds and digests: overlay/version ID, named action IDs, signing key IDs, HTTP method, canonical path, exact query policy, content type, request-body schema or semantic digest, body-size limit, activation, expiry, and operator-approval provenance.
- Overlay creation requires a real operator-authorized source and cannot itself be invoked through an overlay. Existing overlays are revoke-only.
- Authorization uses server time and denies before any handler side effect. Expiry during an already-admitted action does not abort its substeps.
- Default TTL 4h; hard maximum 14d. Reload/revocation semantics and their propagation bound must be explicit and must not require manually restarting Helios.
- Continue denying mixed Cookie/Authorization credentials. Keep any Origin/CSRF exception narrow to this signed capability path.
- Bind signature and authorization to action ID and body/query semantics. Add replay/idempotency appropriate for mutations and active-process topology.
- Audit overlay approval/load/revocation/expiry and every attempted action with overlay/action/key/request IDs and actual outcome, never credentials or sensitive request bodies.
- Failure to load capability overlays denies signed mutations only; ordinary sessions and existing signed readonly requests continue normally.
- Post-handler response byte caps are not rollback. Mutating routes need truthful outcome-aware response/audit semantics.
- Negative tests independently alter method, path, query, action, body, key, overlay, time, revocation, signature, and nonce; every out-of-shape request denies before mutation.

## Agent Waste clustering contract

- Evaluate `clusterfck` and `figue` on a fixed representative fixture: clustering quality, deterministic feature extraction, runtime, maintenance/license, and operational fit. Record why the selected option wins or why both are rejected.
- Provide a deterministic full-backlog baseline without model calls, with stable ordering and every observation represented exactly once in a cluster or unclustered set.
- Treat model refinement as optional and non-blocking. Failed batches remain visible as partial status; deterministic and successfully refined results remain usable.
- Response/UI expose deterministic-vs-refined provenance, failed portions, and completeness without calling partial output complete.
- Remove moves exactly one displayed occurrence, recomputes aggregates/ranking, and Undo restores the exact previous snapshot and focus.
- End-to-end verification covers signed clustering plus browser-local Remove/Undo, without putting the private signing key in page JavaScript or granting general admin navigation.

## Decomposition

1. **Capability contract and lifecycle design** — canonical shape, approval authority, storage/reload, revocation, replay/idempotency, audit, route-local guard, failure semantics, and rollback.
2. **Overlay foundation and management** — immutable approval-bound records/config, signed capability principal, operator create/revoke or canonical injection path, route helper, and full negative test matrix.
3. **Deterministic + partial clustering** — library evaluation, deterministic baseline, optional model refinement, per-batch status, and coverage invariants. This can proceed independently of leaf 2 after leaf 1 settles shared contracts.
4. **Agent Waste workflow integration** — grant only the named clustering action and reviewed read dependencies; preserve/test browser-local Remove/Undo; end-to-end tests.
5. **Rollout and stability verification** — canonical deploy; mint/inject one four-hour approved overlay; run Cluster → Remove → Undo; verify audit, revocation/expiry, partial-result behavior, and out-of-shape denial.

## Gates and closure

- Oracle reviewed this filing scope and found it ready after the criteria above were added. Re-review the concrete contract and implementation; do not substitute generic security conservatism for the explicitly documented operator-UX tradeoff.
- Any DB schema/migration or production DB write requires the normal DB review and explicit operator go. Prefer the smallest existing config/state pattern that can meet propagation/revocation requirements.
- Operator-facing UI must meet Helios's answer-first, next-action-immediate mobile and desktop bar.
- Rollback: revoke/remove the overlay, leaving existing readonly auth and ordinary OAuth unaffected; source rollback is a normal revert + canonical deploy.
- Close only after the live four-hour overlay executes the exact initial workflow and unrelated mutations remain denied.

# Agent Canon — `FreshlyBakedNYC/helios-parser-configs` child epic

> Parent epic: [virusdave/top-level#10](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/10)
>
> The implementation commit on this repo's master MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10
> ```
>
> That trailer triggers the cross-repo completion flow back to the
> parent issue.

## What this epic does

Rewrites this repo's root `AGENTS.md` to consume **canonical agent
rules** from `virusdave/top-level` instead of duplicating them
locally. The canonical rules are short, imperative, and updated in one
place — so all our repos stay in sync without manual mirroring.

## Step 0 — fetch and read canon BEFORE doing anything

The canonical agent rules live in
`virusdave/top-level : docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md` on `master`. **Read
them first** (and use the same mechanism in your final AGENTS.md
header — see Step 2):

```sh
canon_ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
              /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$canon_ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … internalize the rules — they govern this rewrite …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$canon_ws"
```

Pay particular attention to: ephemeral checkouts for your own work,
the "Canon update interrupt" in §0, the operational-reality §5, and
the §6 contract for what peer `AGENTS.md` must contain.

## Step 1 — ephemeral checkout of THIS repo

```sh
ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
        /home/amp-local/src/helios-parser-configs --label agent-canon)
cd "$ws"
```

Adjust the source path if `helios-parser-configs` lives elsewhere on
this host (`/home/amp-local/src/helios-parser-configs` is the standard).

## Step 2 — rewrite `AGENTS.md` to the pointer model

Open the existing root `AGENTS.md`, audit it for what to keep, then
replace its contents with this exact structure. Fill in the
repo-specific section from your audit.

```markdown
# Agent instructions for `FreshlyBakedNYC/helios-parser-configs`

**MANDATORY FIRST READ — agent canon.** Before doing anything in this
repo, fetch and read the latest canonical agent rules:

```sh
ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
        /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … apply the rules …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$ws"
```

That file is authoritative across **all** our repos. Re-read on every
agent session — it changes. If anything in this file conflicts with
canon, **canon wins** — fix the stale prose here.

The rest of this file lists only **helios-parser-configs-specific**
instructions.

---

## Repo purpose

<one-paragraph summary: parser configs consumed by Helios. Helios
auto-refreshes from this repo's master roughly every 60s — meaning a
push is the deploy. There is NO restart step; do not attempt to
restart Helios after editing here.>

## Editing workflow

<authoritative format of the parser config files, validation
commands (whatever lints/round-trips configs before push), and the
"how do I know it took effect" path (Helios logs / dashboard / etc.).>

## Compatibility / breaking changes

<warnings about breaking changes that would break Helios on the next
60s pull — and how to stage them safely (feature flags? new file
alongside old? coordinate with the Helios repo?).>

## Host topology / paths

<deploy targets — the Helios instances that pull from this repo and
the polling interval / endpoint.>
```

## Step 3 — what to KEEP

From the existing AGENTS.md, **keep every operational fact** an agent
needs to work here: exact deploy commands, service names, log paths,
config locations, build/test invocations, architecture diagrams,
repo-specific cross-references, contact info.

## Step 4 — what to DELETE (canon covers it)

Delete and do NOT restate any of:

- "Never SSH to self" / "SSH port" rules
- "Use ephemeral checkout" / "do not edit shared `~/src`" rules
- "Default to `master`, no feature branches" rule
- Bash vs Python / shebang style / typed-code rules
- Performance budgets (UI ≤500ms, DB ≤125ms)
- "Use Oracle / painter / Bedrock LLMs" rules
- Group-writable file rule
- Generic task-dag CLI workflow (the
  `frontier → work → complete → push` loop)
- Generic cross-repo child-epic trailer flow

If you find any of those in the current `AGENTS.md`, **delete** the
prose and rely on canon. If a rule there contradicts canon, canon
wins — flag the conflict in your commit message.

## Step 5 — target size & sanity check

The rewritten file should be **≤ 120 lines**. If it's bigger, you're
probably restating canon — re-audit and trim. If it's much shorter
than the existing file but still has all operational facts, that's
the correct outcome.

Run a final read-through asking: "could a brand-new agent who has
just read canon do real work in this repo using only what's left
here?" If yes, done.

## Step 6 — commit, link, push

```sh
git add AGENTS.md
git commit -m "agents: adopt canon pointer model (Satisfies virusdave/top-level#10)

Replace duplicated cross-repo rules with a mandatory canon-fetch
header per docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md. Repo-specific content
(deploy, paths, services) preserved.

Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10"
git push origin HEAD:<this-repo-default-branch>
```

(Use this repo's default branch — usually `master` or `main`. Do not
open a PR; push directly per the canon working-workflow rule.)

The `Satisfies:` trailer fires the cross-repo completion flow back to
top-level#10.

## Acceptance

- Root `AGENTS.md` opens with the unignorable canon-fetch header.
- Zero duplication of canon content.
- All prior repo-specific operational facts preserved.
- File length ≤ 120 lines.
- Commit includes `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10`.
- Pushed to default branch.

## If you're blocked

- **App not installed / push refused**: stop. Report the exact error
  and your proposed diff to the parent issue
  ([virusdave/top-level#10](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/10)).
- **Repo doesn't have a root `AGENTS.md`**: create one using the same
  template. The acceptance criteria still apply.
- **Existing AGENTS.md has something you don't recognize**: assume
  it's an operator customization and preserve it. When in doubt, ask.

issues.body:
## Summary

Two agents can do identical work on one GitHub issue even though the
"one claim per task" invariant holds, because an **epic root**
(`tasks/pending/<N>`) and a **leaf** it decomposes into
(`tasks/frontier/<short>`) are different SHAs for the same issue and no
mutex relates them. Root-caused from `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites#14`.

Full model + worked incident: [`docs/DISPATCH_CONCURRENCY.md`](../blob/master/docs/DISPATCH_CONCURRENCY.md) (landed).

## Root cause (mostly-static-sites #14, single host, 10 panes sharing one state file)

1. `04:53:27` issue-to-task workflow creates epic root `a5661ed` (`tasks/pending/14`).
2. `04:53:39` pane `%53` claims the undecomposed root (roots bypass the readiness gate so the first worker can break it down).
3. `04:55:35` agent `%53` runs `task-dag breakdown a5661ed`, creating leaf `aded6a5` + `tasks/frontier/aded6a5`.
4. `04:55:41` pane `%49` claims `aded6a5` — different SHA, in the ready-set, not yet claimed on origin, so neither the exact-SHA flock nor the advisory active-ref read relates it to `%53`'s root claim.
5. `05:05:31` agent `%53` ALSO implements the fix and commits to master (it both decomposed and implemented).
6. agent `%49` independently produces the byte-identical fix, then dedups.

Two contributing causes, both fixable here:
- **No per-issue (root-vs-leaf) mutex.** `issue_in_decomposed_set` suppresses a root once leaves exist, but there is no reverse guard suppressing a leaf while its issue's root worker is still active.
- **No epic-root "decompose-only" contract.** `prompts/base-worker-prompt.txt` never tells a root-dispatched agent to only decompose and exit.

## Proposed minimal fix (this repo)

1. **Carry assigned task identity into the prompt.** Thread `ref_name`/`kind` through `find_and_claim_task` -> `process_claimed_task` and append to the prompt context:
   ```
   Assigned Task SHA: <full-sha>
   Assigned Task Ref: tasks/pending/14   (or tasks/frontier/<short>)
   Assigned Task Kind: epic-root         (or frontier-leaf)
   ```
2. **Epic-root decompose-only contract** in `prompts/base-worker-prompt.txt`: if kind is epic-root, only inspect + `task-dag breakdown` (or block/page), then exit; do not implement, do not claim newly created leaves, do not complete the root as implementation.
3. **Host-local per-issue root mutex** in `lib/state.sh`: enrich `.claimed[<sha>]` records with `repo`/`issue`/`ref`/`kind` (backward-compatible) and add `issue_has_active_epic_root_claim <repo> <issue>` under the existing flock. In `find_and_claim_task`, before claiming a frontier leaf, skip if its issue has an active root claim; re-check after claim and release on race.
4. **Tests** (shell fixtures): root claimable when undecomposed; issue-14 leaf suppressed while root claim active; leaf for a different issue still dispatches; leaf becomes dispatchable after the root claim is released/completed.

## Out of scope (separate task-dag issue)
- Cross-host root protection / first-class epic-root claim state — epic roots are not protected by the cross-host `task-dag claim` CAS at all (they are `pending`, not `frontier`). Tracked in `virusdave/task-dag`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Worker prompt includes assigned task SHA/ref/kind.
- [ ] Epic-root workers are instructed to decompose-only then exit.
- [ ] Dispatcher suppresses same-issue frontier leaves while an epic-root claim is active in the host state file.
- [ ] Regression test covers root-claimed-issue leaf suppression.
- [ ] Docs (`docs/DISPATCH_CONCURRENCY.md`) updated to mark the same-host gap closed.
issues.creator: virusdave
issues.title: Prevent epic-root + leaf duplicate dispatch for the same issue (same-host)

# Amp cost reduction — `github-worker` child epic **P2**: shrink the base worker prompt + generate the runtime capsule

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality."
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> — **Lever B = §3**, phased plan = §10 (Phase 2), division of work = §10.
> **Capsule contract (already landed in top-level):**
> [`docs/agent-runtime/RUNTIME_CAPSULE.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/RUNTIME_CAPSULE.md),
> the static safety block
> [`docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md),
> and the prepared-workspace contract
> [`docs/agent-runtime/PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 now has **several**
> `github-worker` child epics, the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO
> carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so
> the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic and
> not a sibling. (github-worker's own task-dag adds those trailers when you
> `complete` a task on this issue; keep them.)

## 1. Goal (Lever B, design §3)

Every dispatched agent is fed a **~200-line static base prompt**
([`prompts/base-worker-prompt.txt`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/prompts/base-worker-prompt.txt))
that is re-billed on every turn, plus an `AGENTS.md`-driven bootstrap. Phase 1
already made the dispatcher **prepare** the whole workspace (all repos cloned,
canon on local disk, `task-dag` checked out) and emit a `manifest.json`. This
phase collapses the recurring startup surface to a small, cache-friendly,
byte-stable prefix followed by a generated **runtime capsule**, and moves deep
detail behind the already-prepared commands + on-demand deep-doc reads.

Target prompt order fed to `amp` (design §3):

```text
[stable base worker prompt — small, byte-stable]
[stable canon/runtime capsule — generated, <= budget]
--- cache boundary ---
[bounded live advisories — dynamic but tiny]   (Phase 4; leave a slot)
[per-task issue/task info — worker id, paths, SHAs, URLs]
```

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Shrink the base prompt** | Replace the ~200-line `prompts/base-worker-prompt.txt` with a **small, byte-stable** base prompt (target budget in design §8: ≤700–1,000 tokens). No dynamic content in it — it must be identical across tasks so it stays cacheable. |
| **Generate the runtime capsule** | From the prepared workspace's `manifest.json`, render the capsule per [`RUNTIME_CAPSULE.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/RUNTIME_CAPSULE.md): the "do not bootstrap" notice, work-repo path, all cloned peer-repo paths, top-level path + canon SHA, the `task-dag` script path (`<workspace>/task-dag/scripts/task-dag`), the claimed task SHA/kind/ref, the **hard safety non-negotiables** (embed [`capsule/static-block.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md) verbatim), and the scenario→deep-doc **routing table** (pointers, not the docs). Budget: ≤400–700 tokens. |
| **Order dynamic content last** | Emit worker id, paths, URLs, timestamps, per-task info, and the (future) live-advisory slot **after** the stable prefix so the prefix stays byte-stable. |
| **`agent-prompt-budget` CI check** | Add a CI check that fails if the base prompt or the rendered capsule exceeds the design §8 budgets, so the shrink can't silently regrow. (The top-level advisory-budget sibling work landed [`docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml); this check governs the github-worker-side prompt/capsule surface.) |

## 3. Constraints (do not weaken safety)

- The capsule MUST still carry the hard non-negotiables (the
  [static safety block](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md))
  and the deep-doc routing table — shrinking is a *relocation* of detail behind
  prepared commands + on-demand reads, never a removal of safety rules. See
  design §3 and the canon prepared-workspace exception.
- The static block is mirrored from canon; if you change what it mirrors, the
  canon source is authoritative — coordinate per
  [`docs/canon/UPDATING_CANON.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/UPDATING_CANON.md).
- The capsule must validate against, and stay in lockstep with, the manifest
  schema in
  [`PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md).

## 4. Acceptance (design §10 Phase 2)

- The rendered capsule is **under budget**; the `agent-prompt-budget` CI check
  is present and **enforces** both the base-prompt and capsule budgets.
- A dispatched agent receives: small byte-stable base prompt → generated
  capsule → (advisory slot) → per-task dynamic block, in that order.
- The safety non-negotiables and deep-doc routing are still present in the
  capsule (verify against `capsule/static-block.md`).
- No agent-run canon bootstrap is reintroduced (Phase 1 already removed it).
- Each implementation attaches an Agent Gate Record (canon §3), and the final
  satisfying commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34` **and** this
  issue's `Issue:`/`URL:` trailer (see the completion-signalling note above).

## 5. Production safety / rollback

- The capsule generator and the shrunk prompt are consumed only by the
  dispatcher/worker-loop when it composes the agent prompt; roll back by
  reverting the worker-loop wiring to the old base prompt. Keep the old
  `base-worker-prompt.txt` in history so revert is a one-commit operation.
- Land the CI budget check in the same change (or immediately after) so the
  shrink cannot silently regrow.
- No serving service is touched; there is no deploy step beyond landing on
  `github-worker@master` (the dispatcher reads the repo state per run).
