# Amp cost reduction — `github-worker` child epic **P4**: agent-waste store + advisory selection/injection

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality."
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> — **Lever D = §5** (and the §8 context-budget meta-problem), phased plan =
> §10 (Phase 4).
> **Reviewed advisory catalog (already landed in top-level):**
> [`docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml)
> and [`docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 now has **several**
> `github-worker` child epics, the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO
> carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so
> the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal (Lever D, design §5)

Close the ≤1-minute feedback loop the operator asked for: as agents (and the
Phase-3 guardrail wrappers) discover wasted effort, record it **structurally**,
and let the dispatcher inject a **tiny, reviewed, budgeted** set of advisories
into the next agent's capsule — *without* ever injecting free-form
agent-authored text.

> **Hard correction from Oracle (mandatory, design §5):** do **NOT** build a
> channel that injects arbitrary agent-authored "lessons learned" into future
> agents. That is simultaneously a context-bloat accumulator, a hallucination
> amplifier, a stale-junk drawer, and a prompt-injection surface. Split the
> system into **observations → reviewed advisories → guardrails**.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Observation store** | A small `agent-waste record …` CLI + the Phase-3 wrappers append **structured** events (design §5.1 schema) to a local store (SQLite WAL or flocked NDJSON under `~/.local/state/github-worker/`). Free-form notes may be stored for **human review** but are **never** injected. This must use the same store path/schema the Phase-3 `bin/rg` wrapper writes to (the P3↔P4 contract). |
| **Advisory selection** | The dispatcher reads the reviewed catalog [`advisories.yaml`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml), selects the **top-ranked** advisories whose `trigger_ids` have fired recently (design §5.3 ranking), and injects **only their allowlisted `text`**, under a hard budget (design §8: ≤300–500 tokens total, ≤3–5 advisories). |
| **Injection point** | Injected into the **dynamic** part of the prompt (after the stable prefix/capsule from Phase 2 — leave the advisory slot Phase 2 reserves), so the cacheable prefix stays byte-stable. |
| **Review backlog, not prompt text** | Unknown/free-form observations create a **review backlog** surface for the operator; they never become future prompt text. |
| **Ranking + caps** | Implement the §5.3 score (severity × recurrence × est-cost-saved × scope-match ÷ token-cost × decay(age)); TTL 7–14 days (except `permanent-safety`); an advisory still high-recurrence at TTL **must be promoted** to a guardrail/canon rule, never extended as prose forever. |

## 3. Constraints

- **Never inject agent-authored free text.** Only allowlisted `text` from the
  reviewed catalog, selected by structured event IDs, under hard caps + TTL +
  the Phase-2 `agent-prompt-budget` CI ceiling.
- Observations are structured and **never auto-injected**; the influence is
  carried by the dispatcher (re-ranking), not by agents reading each other's
  notes — no agent waits on another.
- Single prod host today makes a local store safe; mirror summaries to a git
  ref only if the fleet later goes multi-host (design §12 Q1 — confirm the
  store location with the operator).

## 4. Acceptance (design §10 Phase 4)

- An observation recorded now is reflected (re-ranked) in the **next**
  dispatched agent's capsule within ~1 min, **under budget**.
- **No free-form text is ever injected**; unknown observations land in the
  review backlog only.
- The injected advisory set respects the §8 budget (enforced by the Phase-2
  `agent-prompt-budget` check) and the §5.3 caps/TTL.
- Each implementation attaches an Agent Gate Record (canon §3), and the final
  satisfying commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34` **and** this
  issue's `Issue:`/`URL:` trailer.

## 5. Production safety / rollback

- The store + record CLI are additive and best-effort; a failed write must
  never affect an agent's run.
- Advisory injection is gated by the budget check and the allowlist; roll back
  by disabling injection (dispatcher flag) — the catalog and store are inert
  without it.
- No serving service is touched; landing on `github-worker@master` is the
  publication step (the dispatcher reads repo state per run).

# Agent-waste review queue — `github-worker` child epic: export pending-review backlog to top-level (pull-rebase-retry)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality" (Lever D).
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` → `docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md)
> ("Remaining work" #2) and
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> §5 (Lever D).
> **Producer schema (this repo):**
> [`docs/AGENT_WASTE.md`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/docs/AGENT_WASTE.md)
> (`agent-waste backlog --format json`).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 has **several** child epics,
> the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO carry this issue's own
> `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level completion
> aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal

Add a github-worker-side **exporter** that publishes the **pending-review**
agent-waste backlog (the tiny/rare unknown/free-form-`id` items needing a human
eye) to the committed backlog file in `top-level` defined by child epic #1, so
Helios can read it via its read-only mirror (D1/D2). The github-worker
dispatcher (OS user `amp-local`) already holds push creds to `top-level`, so this
reuses an existing, operator-blessed capability.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Exporter** | A step (in the dispatcher / a scheduled hook — reuse the existing worker-loop plumbing) that reads the local pending-review backlog (`agent-waste backlog --format json`, from `docs/AGENT_WASTE.md`) and writes it to the `top-level` backlog file (format from child epic #1). |
| **Raw store stays local** | Only the **pending-review** stream is exported. The chatty raw NDJSON observation store stays **local** to the dispatcher under its state dir (design §5.1); it is never pushed. Do not conflate the two streams. |
| **Pull-rebase-retry on push** | The exporter commits + pushes to `top-level master` using **pull-rebase-retry** (operator-blessed, low volume) so it never leaves piled-up local commits when Helios's promote path lands adjacent commits. Reject no-op writes (nothing changed → no commit). |
| **Idempotent + fail-safe** | Re-running with an unchanged backlog is a no-op. Push/network failure is loud-but-non-fatal (log + retry next cycle); it never blocks dispatch or a serving path. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants (carry forward)

- **Never export the raw observation store**; only the pending-review backlog.
- **`note` is display-only** and never becomes advisory `text` anywhere in the
  pipeline (the promote path in child epic #4 enforces the write side; the
  exporter must not smuggle it into `advisories.yaml`).
- **Pull-rebase-retry** on every push; **reject no-op** commits; reset local
  commit on push failure and refetch/rebase before retry — the same discipline
  the applyConfig pattern uses.
- Runtime stays **PAT-free** — use the dispatcher's existing `top-level` push
  credential (the machine credential owned by `amp-local`), not a new PAT.

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Depends on** child epic #1 (`top-level` backlog file format — the exporter's
  write target). Start after #1's format lands.
- **Feeds** child epic #3 (Helios reads the exported file).

## 5. Acceptance

- A pending-review backlog recorded locally is reflected in the `top-level`
  backlog file within one export cycle, via a pull-rebase-retry push, with no-op
  writes rejected and failures non-fatal.
- The raw observation store is verifiably **not** exported.
- Deterministic, prod-resource-free test of the exporter (fixture backlog → file
  content), no test points at prod resources. Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

Additive: a new exporter path writing one committed file in `top-level`. Rollback
is disabling the exporter (a dispatcher flag) and/or reverting the file. No
serving service is restarted; pushes go to `master` normally (no `self-deploy`
needed for a data-file push). No prod DB, no schema.

# agent-pain-points migration — github-worker child epic: dispatcher catalog/exporter retarget

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#40](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/40)
> — "Migrate the agent-waste canonical git storage to different repo".
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`virusdave/top-level` → `docs/epics/agent-pain-points-migration/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/agent-pain-points-migration/EPIC_PLAN.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit on
> [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#40`, and the **final** satisfying commit MUST
> also carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer.

## 1. Goal

Re-point the dispatcher's advisory-catalog resolution and pending-review backlog
export from `top-level` to `virusdave/agent-pain-points`, so agent-waste writes
stop bumping the `top-level` canon SHA — with a fail-safe fallback so advisory
injection never breaks during rollout.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Catalog resolution** | In [`worker-loop.sh`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/worker-loop.sh) (the `adv_catalog` block, currently resolving `manifest .canon.top_level_path/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`), resolve **first** from `manifest.repos["agent-pain-points"]/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`; fall back to the current top-level path if the new repo/catalog is absent (rollout + fail-safe). Because the exporter root is derived as `$(dirname adv_catalog)/../..`, this single change re-points **both** advisory selection and backlog export. |
| **Exporter default** | [`scripts/agent-waste-export`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/scripts/agent-waste-export): confirm the derived-root behavior writes to the `agent-pain-points` checkout; keep `AGENT_WASTE_BACKLOG_FILE` default relative path `docs/agent-runtime/agent-waste-backlog.ndjson`; ensure the push credential targets `agent-pain-points` (via the amp-local SSH alias from the nixos-sbc child). Branch stays `master`. |
| **Registry sync** | Add `agent-pain-points` to [`repos.conf`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/repos.conf) to keep it in sync with the canonical `top-level/scripts/ephemeral_checkout.d/repos.conf` (top-level leaf L2 lands the canonical copy first). |
| **CLI + docs** | Update the header/comments of [`bin/agent-waste`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/bin/agent-waste) (references to `virusdave/top-level : docs/agent-runtime/...`), the operator text in [`scripts/waste-page`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/scripts/waste-page) (tells the operator to commit to top-level + validate `advisories.yaml` — now `agent-pain-points`), and [`docs/AGENT_WASTE.md`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/docs/AGENT_WASTE.md). |
| **Tests** | Update `tests/agent-waste-export.sh`, `tests/agent-waste.sh`, `tests/prompt-capsule.sh`, `tests/waste-page.sh` to the new repo target; all against ephemeral temp repos, never prod. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants

- **Fail-safe fallback is mandatory** during rollout: if `agent-pain-points` is
  not yet in the manifest / not yet cloned, advisory injection and export must
  degrade gracefully (fall back to top-level, or skip), never crash a dispatch.
- The advisory allowlist safety invariant is unchanged: only reviewed catalog
  `text` is injected; `note` is never injected.
- The exporter stays idempotent (no-op when unchanged), pull-rebase-retry,
  best-effort + fail-safe (`|| true`).

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Depends on** the nixos-sbc child (dispatcher write deploy key for
  `agent-pain-points`) and on the repo being in the cohort (top-level leaf L2)
  so the manifest carries `.repos["agent-pain-points"]`.
- The fallback lets this land/deploy **before** the automation Helios cutover;
  final cutover is coordinated in parent epic §6 (avoid the split-brain window).

## 5. Acceptance

- On a prepared workspace with `agent-pain-points` cloned, `worker-loop.sh`
  selects the catalog from the `agent-pain-points` checkout and the exporter
  pushes the backlog to `agent-pain-points`, not `top-level`.
- With `agent-pain-points` absent, advisory injection/export still work (fallback
  path) — proven by a deterministic test.
- No `top-level` write on a normal worker completion once cut over.
- Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

Rollback = revert the resolution change (fallback returns behavior to
top-level). Best-effort export means a push failure never blocks dispatch. Tests
must target ephemeral temp repos only. No prod DB, no schema.

> Parent epic: [virusdave/top-level#47](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/47)
>
> The implementation commit on this repo's master MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47
> ```

## Step 0 — read canon first

Ephemeral checkout of top-level master, then read
[`docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md)
"Code standards" (the `--help` rule) and
[`docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md)
"Serving services".

## The requirement

Every invocable tool must accept `-h`/`--help`, print usage, and exit `0`
**before any effect** (env-var assertions, locks, network/API calls,
`git` fetch/push, file writes). Handle `--help` first, ahead of all other
option parsing and required-env checks — in particular, before any
`: "${VAR:?}"` assertions, so `--help` works without CI env vars set.

## Known violators (audit for more — this list is a starting point)

- `scripts/agent-waste-export`
- `scripts/waste-page`
- `scripts/agent-prompt-budget` (the github-worker mirror)
- Any other scripts in `scripts/` you find during the audit.

`scripts/render-capsule` already handles `-h`/`--help` — mirror its
pattern.

## Verifying

Run each tool with `--help` and confirm it prints usage and exits 0 with
no side effects (no writes, no network, no env-var requirement).

## Finalize

Commit with a plain imperative subject (no `feat:`/`fix:` prefix) and the
`Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47` trailer; push to this repo's default
branch.

# Amp cost reduction — `github-worker` child epic **P3**: `bin/rg` guardrail wrapper + hit logging

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality."
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> — **Lever C = §4**, phased plan = §10 (Phase 3).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 now has **several**
> `github-worker` child epics, the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO
> carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so
> the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal (Lever C, design §4)

Tool away the single most-recurring agent footgun: passing a value to
ripgrep's short `-r` thinking it means "recursive" (rg recurses by default;
`-r` is `--replace`), which silently rewrites output and corrupts the agent's
own next input. Replace *any prose warning about it* with a deterministic
wrapper that **rejects only the provably-footgun form**, prints the fix, and
records a structured telemetry event. The wrapper lives in the prepared
workspace's `bin/` (first on `PATH`) and logs every hit (Lever D / Phase 4).

## 2. Detection rules (the subtle part)

`-r` consumes the remainder of a bundled short cluster (or the next argv) as
its replacement value, so `-rn` means `--replace=n`, not `-r -n`. The wrapper
MUST:

- **Stop at `--`**: anything after a bare `--` is a pattern/path and MUST never
  trigger rejection (e.g. `rg -- -rfoo` is legitimate).
- **Parse short clusters left-to-right** against the set of value-taking rg
  short flags (`-A -B -C -E -M -d -e -f -g -j -m -r -t -T`): boolean shorts
  consume one char and continue; the **first value-taking short** consumes the
  rest of the cluster (or the next argv) as its value and ends parsing of that
  token.
- **Reject iff `r` is reached in *flag* position**: `-r`, `-r foo`, `-rn` (the
  canonical `--replace=n` corruption), `-nr`, `-inr`.
- **Never reject `r` in *value* position**: `-er` (pattern `r`), `-gr` (glob
  `r`), `-tr`, etc. are legitimate.
- **Pass `--replace` / `--replace=…` through untouched** — that IS the escape
  hatch; no env-var backdoor is added.
- **Fail OPEN on any parse uncertainty**: if a token doesn't match a known
  shape, `exec` the real `rg` unmodified. The guardrail fires only on the
  provably-footgun form; it must never block legitimate expert use.

## 3. Rejection behaviour

- Print a short stderr message with the fix, e.g.: *"`rg -r` rejected: ripgrep
  recurses by default; `-r` is `--replace`. Use `-n`/`-l` to search, or
  explicit `--replace` if you really mean to rewrite."*
- Exit non-zero. **Reject — never silently rewrite argv** (silent rewriting
  recreates the corrupted-output problem in reverse).

## 4. PATH blast radius (wraps `rg` for EVERY agent command)

- Resolve the **real** `rg` by removing the wrapper's own directory from `PATH`
  (or bake the absolute real-rg path in at workspace-prep time). MUST be
  recursion-proof (the wrapper must never invoke itself).
- `exec` the real binary; byte-exact stdout/stderr passthrough and **exact
  exit-code passthrough** (agents rely on rg's `exit 1` = no match, `2` =
  error).
- Pure bash, no per-arg subshells — `rg` is a hot path.
- If the real `rg` cannot be resolved, **fail loud** (do not silently swallow)
  — a missing rg is a workspace-prep bug, not a footgun.

## 5. Workspace / manifest / contract wiring

The prepared workspace currently creates **no** `bin/` dir and adds **nothing**
to `PATH`. This phase adds:

- Create `<bundle>/bin/`, install the `rg` wrapper there, and prepend
  `<bundle>/bin` to the **amp process's** `PATH` (worker-loop export).
- Record `bin_path` and the active guardrail list in `manifest.json`. **This is
  a manifest schema change** → bump `schema_version` and update
  [`PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md)
  (schema doc + validation list) **and** the workspace `--validate` **in
  lockstep**. This needs the canon §3 Oracle critical-infra diff review.
- **Green-master sequencing:** land the wrapper + tests first (or in one commit
  with tests); make worker-loop and `--validate` tolerate bundles **without**
  `bin/` so no in-flight dispatch breaks during rollout.

## 6. Hit logging → shared waste-telemetry store (Phase-4 contract)

No hard dependency on Phase 4 code. This phase **freezes** the event schema +
path as the P3↔P4 contract; P4 builds ranking on the same file.

- On each rejection, append a design-§5.1 structured NDJSON event:
  ```json
  { "time":"<iso8601>", "repo":"<work repo>", "task_sha":"<sha>",
    "kind":"tool_footgun", "id":"rg-short-r-rejected",
    "severity":"low", "estimated_wasted_tokens":0,
    "estimated_wasted_seconds":0 }
  ```
- Write via `flock -n` (non-blocking) + `O_APPEND` to the designated store
  path. **Operator open question (design §12 Q1):** proposed default
  `~/.local/state/github-worker/agent-waste.ndjson` (single prod host today);
  confirm, or choose a git-ref-mirrored location.
- Logging is **strictly best-effort**: attempt `mkdir -p`; never block on the
  lock; **any** failure is swallowed and MUST NOT alter the wrapper's
  stdout/stderr or exit code.

## 7. Promotion ladder

There is currently **no** `rg -r` advisory in the injected base worker prompt.
So the acceptance criterion is: the wrapper hit-logs, **and** no `rg -r` prose
entry is ever added to the (Phase-4) live advisory budget — the guardrail is
the permanent replacement for that prose. (Retiring any historical KB
"inject-this" flag is tracked by the Phase-3 promotion-ladder task on #34.)

## 8. Tests (deterministic, no prod resources)

- **Parser table** — reject: `-r`, `-rn`, `-nr`, `-inr`, `-r foo`; pass
  through: `--replace x`, `-er`, `-gr`, tokens after `--`, no args,
  `--version`.
- **Recursion safety** — wrapper dir first on `PATH`; wrapper must not call
  itself.
- **Exit-code passthrough** — real rg exit `0`/`1`/`2` preserved.
- **Logging-failure-is-invisible** — read-only state dir must not change the
  wrapper's output or exit code.

## 9. Acceptance

- `rg -r`/`-rn`/etc. rejected with a fix message + structured telemetry event
  logged; `--replace` and all legitimate forms pass through byte- and
  exit-code-exact; workspace/manifest/contract wiring landed with the schema
  bump; master stays green throughout rollout; canon §3 Oracle critical-infra
  diff review recorded for the PATH/manifest change.
- Each implementation attaches an Agent Gate Record (canon §3), and the final
  satisfying commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34` **and** this
  issue's `Issue:`/`URL:` trailer.

## 10. Production safety / rollback

- The wrapper is inert until the workspace installs it and worker-loop prepends
  `bin/` to `PATH`; until then nothing changes.
- Fail-open detection + best-effort logging mean the worst realistic regression
  is a legitimate `rg` invocation wrongly rejected — mitigated by rejecting
  only the provably-footgun form and keeping `--replace`.
- Rollback = stop prepending `bin/` (revert the worker-loop/manifest change);
  the wrapper script alone is harmless.
- The manifest schema bump must land with the contract + `--validate` update so
  no in-flight dispatch fails validation.
issues.creator: helios-freshly-baked[bot]
issues.title: Amp cost reduction P3: bin/rg guardrail wrapper + hit logging

# Pilot: attested surface registry + drift guard, fixing the agent-waste notification

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#57](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/57)
> — "Implement operator-comms UX enforcement". Authoritative design:
> [`docs/designs/operator-comms-ux-enforcement.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/operator-comms-ux-enforcement.md).
>
> **Delegated because:** the agent-waste notification
> ([`scripts/waste-page`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/scripts/waste-page)),
> its formatting helpers, its tests, and the new
> `.well-known/operator-surfaces/` registry all live in
> [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker).
> `top-level` has no code to change for the pilot.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` for this epic MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#57`,
> plus this child epic's own `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`)
> trailer so the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this*
> delegated child.

## 1. Goal

Deliver the design's **pilot** (design §6): the first end-to-end slice of
the surface-enforcement mechanism, proving the shape on the operator's cited
concrete defect.

1. **Establish the registry format in-repo.** Add a `.well-known/operator-surfaces/`
   directory with one JSON entry per operator-facing surface (schema in
   design §4.1: `id`, `repo`, `channel`, `reviewed_input_closure`,
   `examples_dir`, `hash` canonicalization, `oracle_review{url,
   approved_hash, approved_at}`). Author the `agent-waste-page` entry.
2. **Build `operator-surface-guard`'s drift check** (design §4.2 check 1):
   recompute the content hash of the entry's reviewed **input closure**
   (renderer + helpers + fixtures + theme, not one file) plus the
   **CI-regenerated** representative examples, and fail if it differs from
   the recorded `approved_hash`. Two layers: a **pre-landing** run in the
   sanctioned completion path (real prevention) and a **post-push** CI
   backstop (design §4.2 "honest enforcement boundary"). **Never** gate on
   any registry host being at HEAD (design §8.2).
3. **Fix the notification template + register it.** Rework
   [`scripts/waste-page`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/scripts/waste-page)
   so the ~35-40% repeated boilerplate no longer truncates the actual waste
   explanation on mobile (design §1; canon `QUALITY_GATES.md`
   "do not let boilerplate crowd out or truncate the signal"). Get an
   **Oracle UI/UX review of the template plus representative rendered
   examples** (worst-case payloads, not one hand-picked instance) before
   first operator exposure, and record it in the `agent-waste-page` entry's
   `oracle_review`.

## 2. Current state (paths in this repo)

Read these first; the pilot slots into the existing shapes.

| Concern | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Notification builder | `scripts/waste-page` | Builds `title`/`body` (~L230-294) and the `page-dave` command; also builds a one-off detail page (`build_detail_md` ~L114-169, `publish_one_off` ~L171-211). The boilerplate defect is here. |
| Advisory catalog resolver | `lib/advisory-catalog.sh` | Resolves known advisory metadata. |
| Backlog exporter | `scripts/agent-waste-export` | Publishes the backlog NDJSON to `agent-pain-points`. |
| Tests | `tests/waste-page.sh` | Existing coverage; extend for the reworked template + representative-example regeneration. |

## 3. Scope (suggested leaves — the child-epic worker breaks this down)

1. Add the `.well-known/operator-surfaces/` registry schema + a small
   validator/loader; author the `agent-waste-page` entry (closure listing
   `scripts/waste-page`, its helpers, fixtures, any theme asset).
2. Add fixture-driven **representative example regeneration** for the
   agent-waste notification (worst-case payloads) so "what Oracle saw"
   cannot silently drift from what the code renders (design §4.1).
3. Implement `operator-surface-guard`'s drift check over the input closure +
   regenerated examples; wire the **pre-landing** layer into the completion
   path and the **post-push** CI backstop (reusable workflow shape so other
   repos can adopt it later). Include the registry-integrity check that a
   hash/closure change also updates `oracle_review` (design §4.1).
4. Rework the notification template to lead with the waste explanation and
   drop repeated boilerplate; extend `tests/waste-page.sh`; get the Oracle
   UI review; record `oracle_review` in the entry.

## 4. Non-goals (kept out of the pilot)

- The **emission-time lint + new-emitter detection** at the chokepoints is
  **Phase 2** (design §4.3), not here — except that the drift guard's
  new-emitter scan may land as a reusable piece if cheap.
- The **cross-repo fleet index** is **Phase 3** (design §8.2 layer 3).
- The **canon prune** is **Phase 4** (design §4.4), in `top-level`.
- Keep the lint **warn-only** where any lint appears (operator decision 3);
  do not hard-fail emission in the pilot.

# github-worker child epic: strict dispatcher freshness and recovery

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#64`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/64)
· Binding design:
[`durable-dispatch-input-recovery.md`](../../../../designs/durable-dispatch-input-recovery.md)

## Goal

Keep dispatcher inputs observably current and recover from prolonged local
mirror or event-delivery failures without ever authorizing work from stale
state.

## Required implementation

1. **Verified mirror success evidence**
   - Fetch task refs plus default history atomically under the existing
     per-repository lock, verify `HEAD`, then atomically publish repository,
     remote fingerprint, completion time, `HEAD` SHA, and task-ref snapshot
     hash.
   - Store attempts/errors separately. Failure, malformed/future metadata, or
     remote changes do not advance success.
   - Continue roughly minute-scale polling. A failed current fetch always
     skips that repository for the cycle; the last-good mirror is never a
     dispatch authorization source.

2. **Strict prolonged-failure fallback**
   - After the configurable default 180-second success-age threshold, create
     at most one host-wide, per-repository-locked, full-history temporary bare
     clone with cooldown/backoff.
   - Strictly fetch and verify before canonical task-dag
     `frontier --no-fetch` / `roots --no-fetch`. Any uncertainty produces no
     candidate or claim.
   - Strictly refresh and recompute again before spawn.
   - Trap-own a selected fallback through claim, agent handoff,
     block/release/retirement, signals, and exit. Remove unselected fallbacks
     after scanning. Never copy fallback state to the primary mirror.

3. **Managed task-dag CLI mode fix**
   - At module source, distinguish a non-empty explicit `TASK_DAG_BIN`
     override from managed mode. A bad explicit override fails with no network
     fallback; a valid one stays pinned.
   - Managed exports never become overrides. Track attempt/success and
     backoff, build and validate a coherent checkout, then publish/export an
     exact immutable `versions/<commit>/` path.
   - Keep last-good on failure. Retain all versions initially; do not delete by
     age. Any future GC needs invocation leases and separate review.
   - Log mode, commit, success age, attempt/error, and backoff.

4. **Independent comment watchdog**
   - Under one host lease, invoke task-dag's canonical reconciler for every
     registry repo approximately every two minutes with a 15-minute overlap.
   - Run a complete audit daily and at startup when its success heartbeat is
     stale.
   - Configure per-repository `ingestion_start_at` and explicit reviewed
     historical allowlist; first full run is dry-run and bounded.
   - Monitor heartbeat independently from GitHub Actions. Bound duration,
     pagination, concurrent repos, and rate use. Never replace task-dag's
     classifier or receipt semantics in github-worker.

5. **Configuration and operations**
   - Ship fallback and watchdog disabled, with documented flags, thresholds,
     metrics, alerts, and rollback.
   - Keep existing origin claim compare-and-swap and pre-spawn verification.
   - Use the canonical task-dag checkout, never a vendored fallback.

## Required tests

- Successful atomic fetch advances success metadata; partial/failing fetch
  changes neither verified snapshot nor success time.
- A block added after last success can never spawn during later fetch failures.
- Under-threshold failure skips; over-threshold concurrent workers construct
  one fallback; fallback fetch failure produces no claim.
- Selected fallback survives pre-spawn reverify, release, retirement, signal,
  and cleanup paths. Primary recovery resumes without copying fallback state.
- Remote URL change, malformed/future timestamp, and concurrent claims fail
  safely.
- Valid explicit CLI override performs zero network; invalid override fails;
  managed first clone, pre-TTL call, successful/failed post-TTL refresh,
  backoff, candidate validation, concurrency, immutable publication, and logs
  are deterministic.
- Watchdog recent/full cadence, stale heartbeat startup, host lease, dry-run,
  bounded apply, task-dag failure, and rate-limit behavior are covered without
  production resources.
- Repository light checks and full final presubmit pass.

## Rollout and rollback

After the task-dag child is live, deploy this code disabled. Review first-audit
dry-run counts per repository, enable recent reconciliation, then bounded full
audits, and enable mirror fallback last. Roll only via github-worker's
canonical deployment path.

Production verification deliberately suppresses a test event and injects
isolated git-remote failures; it does not touch serving services or databases.
Rollback disables watchdog/fallback and selects the previous immutable CLI
version while preserving additive receipts.

This is critical infrastructure. Obtain Oracle design review before coding and
Oracle diff review after implementation; iterate to APPROVE before commit.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#64
```

issues.title: Make dispatcher inputs fresh, observable, and fail-closed

# github-worker child epic: repair reconciler and watchdog

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Provide typed, bounded host orchestration for task-dag's canonical
`repair-reconcile` command and independently detect stale or failed convergence.
github-worker must not duplicate repair classification, desired state, or
ticket semantics.

## Required implementation

1. **Typed reconciler command**
   - Read top-level's current `master` and `repos.conf` through GitHub, accept
     only equal/descendant registry generations, and enumerate only explicitly
     enrolled repositories.
   - Run five-minute jittered sweeps with a bounded pool of four. Invoke one
     coherent canonical task-dag revision and its `repair-reconcile`; never
     reproduce classifier or projection logic in github-worker.
   - Mint short-lived single-repository GitHub App installation tokens with
     only the binding design's permissions, refresh at 80 percent of lifetime,
     and keep credentials out of config, disk, logs, and command lines.
   - Fail closed with named preflight errors for installation, label,
     permission, clone, policy, or token failures.

2. **Durable status and independent watchdog**
   - Atomically replace `status.json` after each repository with registry
     commit/blob, sweep state, per-repository success/error, active-red identity,
     projection age, counters, gauges, and bounded incident keys.
   - Add a separately supervised watchdog as the sole writer of
     `watchdog.json`. It reads status every five minutes, invokes the packaged
     `page-dave`, persists attempts/results/recoveries, and implements the
     exact stale observation, pending projection, lease, duplicate, and invalid
     policy thresholds from the design.
   - Prefer at-least-once incident notification across a crash; notification
     deduplication is never repair desired-state authority.
   - Emit structured journald events without credentials, check output, issue
     bodies, or one-off contents.

3. **Configuration and lifecycle**
   - Ship orchestration, projection, and paging controls disabled. Document
     cadence, concurrency, state files, preflight, metrics, alerts, dry-run,
     enablement, restart behavior, and rollback.
   - Keep all git and API operations bounded and cancellation-safe. A stopped
     process leaves only durable task-dag state for the next pass to resume.

## Deterministic tests

Use fake registry/GitHub/task-dag boundaries and temporary state directories.
Cover registry generation rollback, malformed enrollment, bounded concurrency,
token mint/refresh/failure and redaction, partial sweeps, restart at every
handoff, atomic status replacement, stale status, every incident threshold,
page attempt crash windows, recovery, task-dag nonzero/timeout, and disabled/
dry-run/enabled controls. No test may contact production.

## Rollout and rollback

The task-dag child must land first. Deploy this code disabled through
github-worker's canonical deployment path. Run credential preflight and the
24-hour dry-run, then support observe-only and the two-repository projection
canary. The nixos-sbc child owns production unit/credential provisioning; the
top-level child owns fleet enrollment and final stability evidence.

Rollback disables the sweep/watchdog controls while preserving status evidence
and task-dag chain history. Package/version selection belongs to nixos-sbc and
must retain a new-format-compatible task-dag until the chain compatibility gate
is satisfied. Do not manually restart or stop a serving service; use only
canonical rollout paths.

This is critical fleet infrastructure. The binding architecture already has
Oracle approval, but the implementation worker must get Oracle architecture
rereview for any design change and Oracle review of the actual final diff
before commit. Iterate to APPROVE.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```

## Incident 67 rollout blocker

The activated watchdog correctly fails closed because github-worker's managed task-dag runtime cache is cloned with `--depth 1`, while canonical activation compatibility intentionally requires a full runtime history to prove the activation floor is an ancestor. `taskdag_activation_snapshot_token` therefore rejects the managed runtime before watchdog lease acquisition.

Make managed task-dag versions full, non-shallow checkouts. Validation must reject shallow published/candidate versions so stale shallow cache entries are not selected. Extend the focused runtime-manager fixture to prove a managed version is non-shallow and that shallow cached versions fail validation/rebuild. Keep the change minimal and obtain critical-architecture Oracle approval.

This blocks github-worker#14 and Incident 67 watchdog rollout. Do not weaken activation ancestry validation.

issues.body:
## Incident 67 watchdog rollout blocker

The full review-only watchdog sweep now passes pagination, but the `virusdave/top-level` complete scan needs about 172 seconds for 508 comments and 74 API requests. The launcher hard-codes `--max-seconds 120`, so it records a time-ceiling failure and cannot establish a green review sweep.

Increase the watchdog reconciler budget to 240 seconds, which remains within the existing 300-second renewable lease (`task-dag` requires at least max-seconds + 30 seconds). Direct read-only verification with 240 seconds completed successfully in 172 seconds with 508 unique comments and zero failures. Keep the change minimal; this blocks github-worker#14 / Incident 67 rollout.

issues.body:
## Incident 67 watchdog apply blocker

After task-dag convergence was repaired, top-level's canonical apply-mode recent pass correctly performed fresh delegation snapshots but exhausted the 240-second repository budget while processing issue 24. It failed closed and recorded an unsuccessful fleet result.

Raise the watchdog lease from 300 to 600 seconds and reconciler ceiling from 240 to 540 seconds; raise stale-attempt monitoring from 600 to 900 seconds so a healthy bounded repository pass is not paged as stale. The task-dag token guard requires max-seconds + 30 <= remaining lease, which remains satisfied. Keep max-apply at 100 and all other semantic ceilings unchanged.

This blocks github-worker#14 / Incident 67 rollout.
issues.creator: virusdave
issues.title: Allow apply convergence to finish within its lease

issues.body:
## Incident 67 watchdog apply blocker

Every repaired fleet recent pass now fails before reconciliation with:

```json
{"stage":"arguments","message":"invalid, stale, or insufficient watchdog lease"}
```

The 600-second lease and 540-second command ceiling are technically separated by 60 seconds, but task-dag requires `max-seconds + 30` remaining at command entry. That leaves only 30 seconds for lease renewal publication, checkout refresh, token check, and command startup; production overhead exceeds that margin.

Reduce the repository ceiling to 480 seconds. This preserves a 90-second total margin (60 seconds of pre-entry overhead in addition to task-dag's required 30-second reserve) while remaining above the observed convergence requirement (240 seconds reached issue 24 of roughly 36; expected completion around 360 seconds). Keep the 600-second lease and all semantic/apply ceilings unchanged. This blocks github-worker#14 / Incident 67.

Then refresh only through `comment-watchdog-launcher.sh --apply` and verify managed recent and complete success watermarks plus all six origin-backed checkpoint refs. issues.body:
## Goal

Add a supported launcher interface for a targeted one-off dispatcher worker. It must run one explicitly selected task through the normal guarded dispatch path, then exit after the agent returns without polling again or selecting unrelated work.

## Acceptance criteria

- Accept an exact task SHA selector, with unambiguous short-SHA support if safe.
- Require a repository selector when needed to avoid cross-repository ambiguity.
- Reuse normal repository discovery, mirror freshness, canonical task-dag readiness/claim CAS, closed-issue gate, prepared workspace, claim re-verification, agent launch, retirement, and cleanup.
- Fail closed for missing, ambiguous, blocked, claimed, not-ready, completed, or closed-issue targets. Never fall back to arbitrary frontier work.
- Launch in a unique tmux window without replacing or disrupting persistent `worker-N` windows.
- Exit after the selected agent returns, regardless of outcome; do not enter the polling loop.
- Provide innocuous `--help` behavior, deterministic shell tests, and an exact operator recipe in README.
- GitHub issue/comment URL resolution may be deferred if it materially expands this change; document that initial boundary clearly.
- Obtain Oracle design and final-change approval because this modifies fleet dispatch infrastructure.
- Validate without claiming arbitrary production work.

This issue was created directly from an operator instruction in Amp thread https://ampcode.com/threads/T-019f4991-407d-760d-b899-7facb8078905 so the implementation has a canonical task-dag claim and completion record.

issues.title: Add targeted one-off worker launches

issues.body:
Production smoke testing of the new targeted dispatcher found that a completed target can be missed when startup maintenance reaps a stale claim and invalidates the verified mirror generation before target-state classification.

Acceptance criteria:
- A targeted task proven complete terminates with a loud completed-target error even when startup maintenance changed local scheduling refs.
- It never falls through to generic no-work behavior or another task.
- Preserve the orthogonal `--no-loop` and `--repo`/`--task` design and ordinary dispatcher semantics.
- Add deterministic regression coverage and repeat the safe completed-target production smoke.
issues.creator: virusdave
issues.title: Fix completed-target detection after dispatcher maintenance

issues.body:
## Problem

`launcher.sh --no-loop --repo <repo> --task <sha>` can exit 2 before claiming a ready target. `find_and_dispatch_task` invalidates verified mirror evidence after routine task-dag maintenance and returns no dispatch so the next poll can resync. Normal workers retry, but `--no-loop` currently treats that maintenance-only scan as its one requested cycle and exits.

Observed while launching `virusdave/task-dag#23` task `9f4ab10`: two standalone windows exited 2 after maintenance although `task-dag frontier --issue=23` still reports the leaf ready.

## Required semantics

A no-loop targeted worker performs one **task loop**, not merely one repository scan. Maintenance-only generation retries must not consume it. Continue until the selected target is dispatched or reaches a loud terminal state (completed, missing/ambiguous, claim lost/held). Never claim unrelated work. Preserve independent `--no-loop` behavior without a target.

Related: https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/43
issues.creator: virusdave
issues.title: One-shot targeted dispatch must retry maintenance-only scans

issues.body:
## Production contract gap

The task-dag semantic consumer treats `refs/heads/gh/issues/*` as part of its authoritative local child/fact snapshot. github-worker refmirrors currently sync and freshness-attest `HEAD` plus `refs/heads/tasks/*`, but not `gh/issues/*`. A reused mirror can therefore retain stale issue-root refs outside the verified snapshot.

This blocks the safe repair of task-dag#75 and fleet readiness after task-dag c1a6293.

## Required outcome

Include `refs/heads/gh/issues/*` in the refmirror atomic fetch/prune and success-evidence digest/freshness validation. Add focused tests proving refresh and stale-ref deletion are attested. Do not broaden any other namespace.

issues.body:
Change standalone launcher window names to exactly `one-shot-` followed by a six-character lowercase hexadecimal suffix, for example `one-shot-f687a5`. Preserve uniqueness without embedding repository names, task SHAs, timestamps, PIDs, or long numeric strings in the visible tmux window name. Update focused launcher tests and documentation if needed.

Operator explicitly requested fast publication, no Oracle review, and no long-running pre-publish test suites.

> ```

## Scope owned by this repo

- New per-site review landing page at
  `https://reviews.freshlybaked.us/<site-slug>` (host configured by

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. M1–M4 have landing commits on `mostly-static-sites` master carrying

2. The Midtown review page renders, posts to the live Helios API, and

  pause-and-replace` against the current per-site page set.
- Per-cluster landing-page generators for the eight Batch-1 clusters
  (Strain & Brand Power, Local Discovery, Delivery — Revamped,
  Bronx / Arthur Ave, Brand Protection, General Category, Financial
  Logistics, Regulatory Legitimacy).

### B. Universal 5-component layout (Batch-2 addition)

- Shared component library under `src/lp/components/`:
  - `Hero/` — `Hero_Friction_Match`, `Hero_Traveler_Welcome`,
    `Hero_Attribute_Match`, `Hero_Utility_Clock`, plus the four
    Batch-1 hero variants. Each renders against the per-family
    image variant chosen by the route handler.
  - `Trust_Anchor_Cash_Debit/` — **frozen** universal block; cash /
    debit-on-delivery USP table copy + iconography. No per-family
    overrides; component takes only site-level palette inputs.
  - `Contextual_Utility/` — slot component that can host any of:
    `Menu_Alternative_Grid`, `ID_Utility_Check`, `Filtered_API_Menu`
    (Sweed-tag-driven), `Speed_Radius_Map`. Per-family stack picks
    which.
  - `Inventory_Carousel/` — Sweed-tag-driven menu strip used by the
    Batch-1 families and the Lab_Compliance_Block path.
  - `Friction_CTA/` — footer CTA with LLM-generated CTA text +
    standard discount tokens.

### C. Per-family component stacks (Batch-2 addition)

Implements the four Batch-2 family stacks per the parent design
§"Per-family component stacks":

| Family | Component stack |
|--------|-----------------|
| `competitor_friction` | `Hero_Friction_Match` → `Trust_Anchor_Cash_Debit` → `Menu_Alternative_Grid` → `Friction_CTA` |
| `tourist_logistics` | `Hero_Traveler_Welcome` → `ID_Utility_Check` → `Trust_Anchor_Cash_Debit` → `Travel_Bundles_Grid` |
| `dietary_specifics` | `Hero_Attribute_Match` → `Filtered_API_Menu` → `Lab_Compliance_Block` → `Trust_Anchor_Cash_Debit` |
| `workplace_late_night` | `Hero_Utility_Clock` → `Trust_Anchor_Cash_Debit` → `Speed_Radius_Map` → `Decompression_Menu` |

`Travel_Bundles_Grid`, `Lab_Compliance_Block`, and
`Decompression_Menu` are family-specific glue components landing in
the same `src/lp/components/` tree.

### D. Per-site instantiation (all sites)

Per operator decision on issue #5 Q2, the generator emits one
landing-page family per cluster per site for **every** `site_slug`
in `sites.yaml`. URLs are scoped under:

```
https://<site-slug>.freshlybaked.us/lp/<family>/<parameter-tuple>/
```

Per-site overrides for the new components live in `sites.yaml`
alongside the existing `customer-sentiment` per-site block:

```jsonc
{
    "midtown": {
        // ... existing customer-sentiment fields ...
        "lp": {
            "delivery_zone_radius_miles": 4,
            "hub_lat_lng": [40.7589, -73.9851],
            "accepted_id_kinds": ["state-issued ID 21+", "out-of-state ID 21+"],
            "tourist_neighborhoods": ["Times Square", "Hell's Kitchen", "Midtown East"]
        }
    }
}
```

### E. Asset-manifest consumer + JSON-blueprint route handler

- **Manifest format** (`assets/lp/<family>/manifest.json`) — produced
  by the `automation` asset-gen worker; lists per-asset-type variant
  pool entries with `existing > Painter` precedence and per-variant
  approval status. Manifest is the single source of truth for what
  variants the route handler may pick.
- **Route handler** at `<site>/lp/<family>/<parameter-tuple>/`:
  1. Reads UTM parameters from the request.
  2. Reads the manifest for the requested family.
  3. Selects an approved variant per slot (X₁ Hero, X₃ contextual,
     X₅ CTA) — selection is deterministic-by-UTM in v1 so the
     leaderboard can attribute conversions cleanly. A
     small-percent-traffic-random branch is supported for new
     variants entering the pool.
  4. Interpolates `<parameter-tuple>` values into the chosen
     variant's text/image at render time.
  5. Renders the 5-component stack.
- **Client-side conversion-event posting** — Add-to-Cart and
  Cart-Abandonment events POST to helios
  `/v1/conversion-events` with the variant_id + UTM payload, per
  the parent design §"Hill-climbing feedback loop". Reuses the
  existing customer-sentiment-style ~5 KB-gz client bundle conventions.

### F. `sites.yaml` schema additions

Per Section D above. The schema bump is additive — existing
fields keep working; missing `lp.*` blocks default to "use family
defaults" so smaller sites work out of the box.

## Out of scope

- Strategic-clusters config + cluster-sweep + helios page +
  asset-gen worker — owned by `automation`.
- DNS, TLS, host wiring, systemd timers — owned by `nixos-sbc`.
- Promotion of approved variants into this repo's `assets/lp/<family>/`
  tree — the `automation` asset-gen worker opens the commit; this
  repo only *consumes* what the manifest says is approved.

## Phases

- **M1.** Universal 5-component library (Hero / Trust_Anchor_Cash_Debit /
  Contextual_Utility slot / Inventory_Carousel / Friction_CTA) +
  storybook-style page for each component at fixed mock data. Behind
  a per-site `lp_v2_enabled` feature flag.
- **M2.** Asset-manifest consumer + JSON-blueprint route handler +
  per-family component stacks for the four Batch-2 families.
  Renders against a hand-crafted manifest before the asset-gen
  worker is live.
- **M3.** Landing-pages L2 cluster-mode runner + per-cluster
  generators for the eight Batch-1 families. Emits cluster-proposal
  output consumable by the helios `/ads/cluster-proposals` page.
- **M4.** Per-site instantiation across every site in `sites.yaml`
  + per-site override schema + `sites.yaml` migrations. Brings all
  Batch-2 family stacks live under
  `<site>/lp/<family>/<parameter-tuple>/` once `automation` B2/B3
  produce approved variants.
- **M5.** Client-side conversion-event posting + UTM-deterministic
  variant selection + small-percent-random new-variant exploration
  branch.

## Cross-repo dependencies

- M2 consumes the manifest format defined by `automation` B1; M2
  can render before B1 ships by using a hand-crafted manifest.
- M3 reads `strategic-clusters.jsonc` defined by `automation` P0.
- M4 needs `automation` B2/B3 to populate `asset_approvals` and the
  manifest so promoted variants render. The flag can flip per-site
  per-family independently.
- M5 needs `automation` E (the `/v1/conversion-events` ingestion
  endpoint).

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. M1–M5 have landing commits on `mostly-static-sites` master
   carrying `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#5`.
2. At least one site × family landing page per Batch-2 cluster
   renders correctly behind a UTM-gated URL under
   `https://<site>.freshlybaked.us/lp/<family>/<parameter-tuple>/`
   and posts Add-to-Cart / Cart-Abandonment events to helios.
3. The frozen `Trust_Anchor_Cash_Debit` component is present in
   every Batch-2 family stack (mechanically verifiable from the
   per-family stack manifest).
4. `sites.yaml` carries an `lp.*` block for every site whose
   `lp_v2_enabled` flag is on; smoke test confirms per-site override
   substitution works (delivery zone radius, hub coordinates,
   accepted-ID list, tourist neighborhoods).

# Agent Canon — `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites` child epic

> Parent epic: [virusdave/top-level#10](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/10)
>
> The implementation commit on this repo's master MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10
> ```
>
> That trailer triggers the cross-repo completion flow back to the
> parent issue.

## What this epic does

Rewrites this repo's root `AGENTS.md` to consume **canonical agent
rules** from `virusdave/top-level` instead of duplicating them
locally. The canonical rules are short, imperative, and updated in one
place — so all our repos stay in sync without manual mirroring.

## Step 0 — fetch and read canon BEFORE doing anything

The canonical agent rules live in
`virusdave/top-level : docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md` on `master`. **Read
them first** (and use the same mechanism in your final AGENTS.md
header — see Step 2):

```sh
canon_ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
              /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$canon_ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … internalize the rules — they govern this rewrite …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$canon_ws"
```

Pay particular attention to: ephemeral checkouts for your own work,
the "Canon update interrupt" in §0, the operational-reality §5, and
the §6 contract for what peer `AGENTS.md` must contain.

## Step 1 — ephemeral checkout of THIS repo

```sh
ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
        /home/amp-local/src/mostly-static-sites --label agent-canon)
cd "$ws"
```

Adjust the source path if `mostly-static-sites` lives elsewhere on
this host (`/home/amp-local/src/mostly-static-sites` is the standard).

## Step 2 — rewrite `AGENTS.md` to the pointer model

Open the existing root `AGENTS.md`, audit it for what to keep, then
replace its contents with this exact structure. Fill in the
repo-specific section from your audit.

```markdown
# Agent instructions for `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites`

**MANDATORY FIRST READ — agent canon.** Before doing anything in this
repo, fetch and read the latest canonical agent rules:

```sh
ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
        /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … apply the rules …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$ws"
```

That file is authoritative across **all** our repos. Re-read on every
agent session — it changes. If anything in this file conflicts with
canon, **canon wins** — fix the stale prose here.

The rest of this file lists only **mostly-static-sites-specific**
instructions.

---

## Repo purpose

<one-paragraph summary: per-site source for our mostly-static brand
sites + their nix modules. Deployed per-site via `bounce <site>` and
nix-module switch.>

## Deploy

<the canonical deploy procedure: `bounce <site>` (and the
per-site nix module deploy path). NEVER hand-restart nginx / the
serving process during a deploy — `bounce` orchestrates safely.
Preserve any nuance the old AGENTS.md had here.>

## Per-site layout

<one-line-per-site description of which directory holds which site,
and any per-site quirks (build commands, asset pipelines, special
revalidate hooks, e.g. the public-roster fetch from Helios used by
the staff strip).>

## Build / test

<per-site build commands, the canonical UI components that must NOT
be forked (cite paths so future agents reuse them).>

## Host topology / paths

<deploy targets, log paths, where built artefacts land.>
```

## Step 3 — what to KEEP

From the existing AGENTS.md, **keep every operational fact** an agent
needs to work here: exact deploy commands, service names, log paths,
config locations, build/test invocations, architecture diagrams,
repo-specific cross-references, contact info.

## Step 4 — what to DELETE (canon covers it)

Delete and do NOT restate any of:

- "Never SSH to self" / "SSH port" rules
- "Use ephemeral checkout" / "do not edit shared `~/src`" rules
- "Default to `master`, no feature branches" rule
- Bash vs Python / shebang style / typed-code rules
- Performance budgets (UI ≤500ms, DB ≤125ms)
- "Use Oracle / painter / Bedrock LLMs" rules
- Group-writable file rule
- Generic task-dag CLI workflow (the
  `frontier → work → complete → push` loop)
- Generic cross-repo child-epic trailer flow

If you find any of those in the current `AGENTS.md`, **delete** the
prose and rely on canon. If a rule there contradicts canon, canon
wins — flag the conflict in your commit message.

## Step 5 — target size & sanity check

The rewritten file should be **≤ 120 lines**. If it's bigger, you're
probably restating canon — re-audit and trim. If it's much shorter
than the existing file but still has all operational facts, that's
the correct outcome.

Run a final read-through asking: "could a brand-new agent who has
just read canon do real work in this repo using only what's left
here?" If yes, done.

## Step 6 — commit, link, push

```sh
git add AGENTS.md
git commit -m "agents: adopt canon pointer model (Satisfies virusdave/top-level#10)

Replace duplicated cross-repo rules with a mandatory canon-fetch
header per docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md. Repo-specific content
(deploy, paths, services) preserved.

Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10"
git push origin HEAD:<this-repo-default-branch>
```

(Use this repo's default branch — usually `master` or `main`. Do not
open a PR; push directly per the canon working-workflow rule.)

The `Satisfies:` trailer fires the cross-repo completion flow back to
top-level#10.

## Acceptance

- Root `AGENTS.md` opens with the unignorable canon-fetch header.
- Zero duplication of canon content.
- All prior repo-specific operational facts preserved.
- File length ≤ 120 lines.
- Commit includes `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10`.
- Pushed to default branch.

## If you're blocked

- **App not installed / push refused**: stop. Report the exact error
  and your proposed diff to the parent issue
  ([virusdave/top-level#10](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/10)).
- **Repo doesn't have a root `AGENTS.md`**: create one using the same
  template. The acceptance criteria still apply.
- **Existing AGENTS.md has something you don't recognize**: assume
  it's an operator customization and preserve it. When in doubt, ask.

# Unified landing-page engine — `mostly-static-sites` (thin runtime) child epic

> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) (rev 3). Re-read the parent
> before starting any phase — this child epic is a **thin index** over
> the parent's design, not a re-statement of it. The parent is
> authoritative; if this file ever drifts from it, the parent wins.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#13
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>`
> trailer so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post per-phase
> progress on the parent issue.

## ⚠️ Binding constraint: do NOT change the canonical URL schema

The operator rejected the manufactured `/r/<family>` and
`…/lp/<family>/<param-tuple>/b/<branch_id>` routes. **Keep the existing
canonical schema** (parent §6.1, rev-3):

```
/SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM   ·   NUM=0 = random-rotation distributor alias
```

implemented today in
[`apps/freshlybakedus-site/middleware.ts`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/apps/freshlybakedus-site/middleware.ts)
and
[`apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/purpose-families.ts`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/purpose-families.ts).
The `/0` re-roll `307`, the `utm_content=NUM:N` rewrite, and the
legacy/vacant-variant redirects already implement the URL-embedded
scatter. **No new route shapes. No Google-Ads final-URL changes.** The
one change is *who decides `NUM`*: the bundle's weights/kill-list bias
the pick instead of a uniform `Math.random()`.

## Scope owned by this repo (the thin, fast substrate)

Everything in the parent EPIC_PLAN §4 ("mss owns") and the mss slice of
the §10 phases:

- **`/cloud` bundle loader/validator/cache** — background poller reads
  the read-only `/cloud` artifact root, validates schema + `sha256` +
  signature + `min_renderer_version`, atomically swaps an in-memory
  active bundle, keeps last-known-good (N=3), **fail-closed** (never
  serve unvalidated content), exposes health
  (`loaded_bundle_id`, `validation_status`, pointer age). Off the render
  hot path; verify `/cloud` POSIX atomic-rename in P2 (parent §5, §8).
- **Sandboxed CEL evaluator wired into the EXISTING random-rotation
  middleware** — replaces the uniform `pickRandomVariant()` draw with a
  bundle-weighted (optionally gclid/gbraid/wbraid HMAC-keyed for
  per-click reproducibility) pick of `NUM`, then reuses the existing
  `utm_content=NUM:N` redirect/rewrite path unchanged. Pinned `NUM`
  (explicit `utm_content` or direct `/…/N` link) wins — no re-select
  (parent §6, §6.1). Evaluator is pure: no clock/RNG/`eval`, bounded.
- **Signed variant-kill-list enforcement at the existing variant
  route** — a dead `(site,purpose,slug,num)` redirects to the
  replacement/champion `NUM` via the existing `matchVacantVariantRedirect`
  machinery, logging `requested_num` vs `served_num` (parent §6.1).
- **X1–X5 component renderers** (data-driven from the bundle); validate
  the frozen X2 is present in every family stack (parent §7).
- **Sweed menu adapter/cache (X4)** + **delivery-zone gate** — request-
  time within the ~150 ms cap with stale/fallback; gate feeds policy
  inputs so Helios never optimizes unserviceable ZIPs (parent §7;
  decision 6: ROI control only, no OCM retention).
- **Durable local event spool + ~15-min batch flusher** → Helios
  `POST /v1/lp-events/batch`; at-least-once with per-render `event_id`
  idempotency; backpressure sheds telemetry, never blocks render
  (parent §8; decision 4). **Zero DB reads on the render path.**
- **Shadow/canary support + observability** — `LP_RUNTIME_MODE`,
  allowlists/percent, kill switch, parity + render dashboards
  (parent §10).
- Keep `MAX_VARIANT_BY_PURPOSE` / `*VariantIds` as the drift guard;
  reject any bundle referencing a `NUM` outside the active registry.

## Relationship to the gemini-clusters epic (#5)

This **supersedes the not-yet-built mss slice (M1–M5) of #5** — build
the thin runtime + bundle contract here rather than building
selection/content logic into mss and ripping it out (parent §2, §15).

## Phases

Follow parent §10 order (mss slice): P0 inventory routes/families ·
P1 (Helios-led) · P2 bundle loader (no render change) + stand up event
spool · P3 shadow-compare selection · P4 preview render (both entry
modes already exist: `/0` re-roll and direct `/…/N`) · P5 consume
bundle content · P6 canary + revenue guardrail · P7 full · P8
decommission mss-owned selection/asset ownership + cross-repo commit
consumer. See parent §10 for traffic-impact and rollback columns.

> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md). **Re-read the parent before
> starting any phase** — this child epic is a **thin index** over the
> parent's design, not a re-statement of it. The parent is authoritative;

> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>` trailer

## Role in the epic

mss is the **thin, fast, zero-DB renderer**: it polls the signed SEO
bundle from the read-only `/cloud` mount, validates it (fail-closed,
last-known-good), and renders the FAQ/blog/feed/related/head widgets
**entirely from approved bundle data** — with **zero DB reads/writes on
render and no synchronous Helios call**. The SEO brain lives in Helios
(peer child epic at `../automation/EPIC_PLAN.md`). See parent
[§2](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#2-what-moves-into-helios-answer-to-operator-question-a).

## ⚠️ Binding constraints (from the operator's decisions — parent §0)

- **Blog/widget routes slot into FB.nyc's Reserved Prefix Registry** —
  the hosted-content zone `/sites/<id>/whats-new/<slug>`. The operator
  **rejected** a flat top-level `/whats-new/<slug>`. Do **not** force
  posts onto the LP `/SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM` schema either. The exact
  registry slug is finalised in **P0** (parent §0.2, §6.3;
  rough registry design: <https://gemini.google.com/share/952a99c4b22b>).
- **No public URL changes and no Google-Ads final-URL changes** at any
  phase (parent §10).
- **Host→mode enforcement is mandatory:** FB.nyc renders **raw**, FB.us
  renders **cannabis-sanitized**; reject raw-only content on a sanitized
  host (fail-closed). Render only approved content; no arbitrary
  HTML/script from the bundle; JSON-LD must match visible content
  (parent §5, §6).
- **Fail closed.** Bad bundle → keep last-known-good; no LKG → render the
  page **without** SEO widgets and page Dave; never render
  unvalidated/generated content (parent §4).
- **Reuse #13's loader/spool**, don't fork (parent §0.6, §12).

## Subtasks (see parent §11 for the authoritative list)

- SEO bundle loader on read-only `/cloud` (sig/sha/schema/
  `min_renderer_version` validation, LKG, in-memory active bundle,
  health/metrics) — a thin specialization of #13's LP loader.
- Host→raw/sanitized mode enforcement.
- Widget-slot registry in existing templates.
- `SEOFAQFold`, `WhatsNewFeed`, `BlogPost`, `RelatedLinks`, `SEOHead`
  renderers.
- Blog index/post routes within the `/sites/<id>/…` hosted-content zone.
- `Article`/`BlogPosting`/`FAQPage`/`BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD emitters.
- Sitemap/RSS routes backed by the active bundle.
- Content-addressed asset rendering.
- SEO event instrumentation + durable local spool + ~15-min batch flush
  to `POST /v1/lp-events/batch`.
- Shadow/canary flags + contract fixtures/tests.

## Phasing

Tracks the parent's 8-phase strangler-fig (parent §10): **P0** contracts/
inventory (incl. finalising the registry slug) → **P2** bundle loader →
**P3 FAQ MVP** (smallest shippable slice — do first) → **P4** blog
index/post/feed + JSON-LD + sitemap/RSS → **P5** event attribution →
**P6** canary → **P7** cleanup. (P1 publisher dry-run is Helios-side.)
Tag commits with `Phase: P<n>`.

# FBUS FAQ — `mostly-static-sites` (thin renderer) child epic

> **MATERIALISED 2026-06-15.** The four operator decisions are resolved
> in the parent
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md` §1](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#1-operator-decisions-resolved-2026-06-15)
> and folded into the phases below.
> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md). **Re-read the parent (and the
> parent epic #15) before starting any phase** — this child epic is a
> **thin index** over the parent's design. The parent wins on any drift.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#17
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>` trailer.

## Role in the epic

`mostly-static-sites` is the **thin, zero-DB renderer**. It consumes the
signed SEO bundle Helios publishes and renders the FAQ on FBUS — on every
landing page and on a dedicated `/faq` page — selecting **sanitized**
answers for the `.us` host. It also owns the **full-HTML leak crawler**
that proves FBUS ships no `.nyc` / brand / cannabis-meta-term leak. Helios
(`automation`) is the brain (peer child epic at
`../automation/EPIC_PLAN.md`).

The `@mss/seo` package (`packages/seo/`) — `select.ts#selectFaqFolds` and
`SEOFAQFold.tsx` — and the FB-NYC wiring
(`apps/freshlybaked-site/app/seo-helios-faq-folds.tsx`) **already exist**
from epic #15 and are the pattern to mirror. This child epic **reuses**
them; FBUS currently consumes none of it.

## ⚠️ Binding constraints (parent §5–§6)

- **Zero `.nyc` / "Freshly Baked NYC" / cannabis-meta-term leak** anywhere
  in FBUS rendered output: HTML, canonical, `og:*`, `sameAs`,
  publisher/org schema, `href`, `src`, `data-*`, inline JSON-LD, **and**
  the Next RSC payload / serialized client-component props. Prefer
  internal redirect tokens over passing `.nyc` URLs to client components.
- **`.us` selects sanitized answers only.** Unknown host / invalid bundle
  → render nothing (fail closed).
- **At most one FAQ fold per route**; one visible "FAQs" header + one FAQ
  section per page; no duplicate `FAQPage` scripts.
- **SSR/ISR-visible only** — native `<details>` in server HTML; never
  client-fetched or lazy-loaded.
- **Kill-switch / mode / allowlist fail-closed**: `off`/`shadow` render no
  FAQ; `canary` requires allowlist; `SEO_KILL_SWITCH` removes it.
- **UI/UX gate (canon §3).** The LP FAQ section + `/faq` page are
  user-facing UI → Oracle UI review (mobile layout, signal-to-noise,
  next-action-at-fingertips) recorded on the peer issue before rollout.

## Subtasks (authoritative list in parent §4 / issue Phases 0, 2, 3, 4)

**P0 — audit + failing leak crawler (goes first):**
- Enumerate FBUS route families + representative sample routes
  (operator-confirmed current set: deliverance, conquest, tours, recurse,
  branding, compare — parent §1 Q1).
- **Canonical LP-family registry (operator Q1 follow-up).** Land the
  family list + route patterns as a **single source of truth in code/
  config** (e.g. a `lpFamilies`/`SEO_ROUTE_FAMILIES` registry) so future
  families have an obvious place to register, and so this crawler
  inventory, the P4 FAQ injection points, and Helios's widget
  `route_patterns` (automation P5) all read from **one** place instead of
  duplicated lists. **Define the registry schema + cross-repo handoff:**
  export a machine-readable artifact (e.g. JSON) carrying, per family,
  the **id, canonical representative route, route patterns, sample crawl
  routes, indexability policy, and source commit/provenance** so
  automation P5 can consume it (or pin its exact SHA) rather than
  re-keying the list.
- **Humor-card inventory + classification (operator Q4).** Find the LP
  filler/humor cards (the "wrong flowers" / "wrong green" joke cards),
  classify each as **pure-humor filler** (retire) vs **functional**
  (keep), and record the list on this peer issue for operator
  confirmation. The operator could not name them ("you'll have to look");
  this inventory is the deliverable that resolves the question.
- **Indexability current-state audit (operator Q2).** Record the current
  `robots` / `noindex` / canonical / sitemap state for each LP family and
  `/faq`, and confirm there is **no `gads` / policy-engine coupling** to
  `robots` (i.e. flipping indexability does not change ads behaviour).
  Feeds the P6 indexability decision; make **no** indexability change in
  P0.
- Define the forbidden token/domain list (`.nyc`, brand phrases, cannabis
  meta-terms).
- Add a CI scanner that **builds + serves FBUS, crawls sample routes, and
  scans the full HTML response (incl. inline scripts + RSC payload)**;
  fail on any forbidden string. **Expect pre-existing FBUS leaks — fix or
  explicitly scope them before adding FAQ content.**

**P2 — FBUS SEO runtime integration:**
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/seo/runtime.ts` (adapt from FB-NYC;
  distinct global symbol e.g. `mss.fbus.seo.runtime.v1`).
- Boot the SEO bundle poller in
  `apps/freshlybakedus-site/instrumentation.ts` alongside the LP runtime.
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/app/api/seo/health/route.ts`.
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/app/seo-helios-faq-folds.tsx` using
  `freshlyBakedUsSiteConfig.canonicalHost`, returning **at most one fold**.
- Add `emitJsonLd?: boolean` to `SEOFAQFold` (default `true`).

**P3 — dedicated `/faq` page:**
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/app/faq/page.tsx`, sanitized mode,
  `emitJsonLd=true`, `.us`-only metadata, `revalidate` ~300–600s. Stands
  alone if LP FAQs are disabled.

**P4 — LP FAQ insertion (replaces humor cards):**
- Inject the FAQ section above the footer (between X4 and X5) in the
  shared FBUS LP page components (deliverance/conquest/tours/recurse/
  branding/compare — the operator-confirmed set from the P0 registry),
  under a page-wide "FAQs" header; LP `emitJsonLd=false`.
- **Retire the pure-humor cards** identified in the P0 inventory (wrong
  flowers / wrong green) **only on LP families where the FAQ section is
  enabled** (operator Q4 default: per-family + reversible, **not** a
  global delete). Keep cards the P0 inventory classified as functional.
  Global retirement is a follow-up once the FAQ is broadly live.
- P4 implementation may **land behind kill-switch/canary flags** before
  P5, but **production enablement of an LP family waits until that family
  has an approved merged FAQ set from P5** — do not replace humor cards
  with generic/global boilerplate before family-specific approved content
  exists.

**Hardcoded-FAQ cleanup (mss owns this; coordinate with automation P1):**
- After Helios import is approved and bundled, remove/neutralize
  `apps/freshlybaked-site/app/sites/all/loyalty-faq/page.tsx` as a source
  of truth (render from the bundle instead; preserve/redirect any existing
  public route intentionally), and add a **CI guard** against reintroducing
  hardcoded FAQ content outside the SEO bundle. automation cannot complete
  this migration alone — the code change is here.

**P6 — ads-safe rollout mechanics:**
- Route/family allowlist canary, kill-switch verification, a production
  crawl before broad enablement, and a rollback runbook for removing FAQ
  sections / restoring prior content.
- **Indexability flip (operator Q2, operator-gated for LP families).**
  The new `/faq` ships indexable by design (P3); the **per-LP-family**
  flip waits for operator approval after the P0 audit. If approved: make
  **one canonical representative page per LP family** `index, follow` +
  self-canonical + sitemap-listed, and point per-variant / parameterised
  LPs at it via `rel=canonical` (the preferred consolidation signal),
  adding `noindex` only where a low-unique variant must stay out of the
  index (do not rely on `noindex` to consolidate ranking signals).
  Default until explicit operator approval = **no indexability change to
  existing LP families**.

## CI gates owned here (parent §7)

(4) selector tests (`.us`=sanitized, `.nyc`=raw, unknown host=[], at most
one fold/route, allowlists); (5) renderer tests (visible text == JSON-LD
when emitted; LP can suppress JSON-LD; no raw answer in HTML);
(6) metadata tests (canonical/OG always `https://freshlybaked.us…`; no
`.nyc` in structured data / `sameAs` / publisher); (7) rendered-HTML
crawler (P0); (8) kill-switch tests.

## Phasing

P0 (leak crawler) first and must pass before any FAQ content is added.
The P2 runtime can run in `shadow`; `/faq` (P3, the smallest visible
slice) should be enabled only in non-prod or canary/allowlisted mode
until the crawler, metadata, and approval gates pass. Then P4 LP
insertion lands gated. Tag commits with `Phase: P<n>`.
