> Thin index over the authoritative parent plan
> [`docs/epics/branding-opaque-slugs/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in `virusdave/top-level`. Where this and the parent disagree, the parent
> wins — fix this doc. Tracking issue:
> [virusdave/top-level#19](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/19)
> (split from #15).
> **Operator-approved (2026-06-15); parent §6 decisions are RESOLVED and
> folded in below.** This peer issue materialises under top-level **#19**
> via the `Materialise-Child-Epic:` trailer flow — the work scope here is
> final.

## Scope (FB-US thin runtime)

Make the `branding/` family's `SLUG` segment **opaque**, reusing the exact
`buildFreshlyBakedUsOpaquePublicRef` helper already powering
`compare/`/`conquest/`. The brand name must disappear from every
crawler-visible URL, with **zero 404s** for already-approved Google-Ads
`/0` final URLs.

**BINDING:** do **not** change the canonical `/SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM`
schema, the `/0` distributor, or the `utm_content=NUM:N` contract (parent
§0, [#13 §6.1](../../../unified-landing-engine/EPIC_PLAN.md)). Only the
`branding` `SLUG` representation changes.

## First task: confirm the in-repo facts

The top-level repo cannot read mss source. Begin by verifying the exact
symbols (the parent names the likely locations):

- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/purpose-families.ts` — the brand registry,
  `MAX_VARIANT_BY_PURPOSE`, and `buildFreshlyBakedUsOpaquePublicRef`
  (signature, determinism, whether it is family-scoped or global).
- the `branding/` route segment — `generateStaticParams`, page param
  parse, and the registry/NUM guard.
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/middleware.ts` — existing legacy-form `308`
  redirects (the pattern P1 extends) and the `/0` re-roll/rewrite.

## Phases (parent §5 — production-visible order)

- **P0 — dual-accept.** Route accepts **both** literal and opaque `SLUG`;
  reuse the opaque helper for `branding`; `generateStaticParams` builds
  opaque pages (+ transitional literal pages so nothing 404s yet). Page
  resolves opaque→row; the registry/NUM guard `notFound()`s unknown refs
  and out-of-range `NUM`. No emitted-surface flip yet.
- **P1 — literal back-compat live.** Middleware `308` literal→opaque
  (operator chose `308`, parent §6.1 — **not** `noindex`+canonical),
  same-origin, full query preserved (`gclid`/`gbraid`/`wbraid` + UTMs +
  ValueTrack), `/0` redirect-chain handled intentionally (parent §5.1).
- **P2 — de-emit literals.** Internal links, `<link rel=canonical>`, and
  the `branding/` sitemap entries emit **opaque only**, in the **same
  deploy** so the literal + opaque pages are never both indexable. (P1
  already protects literals.)
- **Audit (read-only, parent §6.4).** Enumerate every other LP family's
  (and FB-NYC's) URL `SLUG` source and confirm whether any literal
  brand/cannabis token can appear in a crawler-visible URL. Operator does
  not expect a leak but asked us to verify. Deliver the findings; only if
  a real leak is found does it expand into further opaque migration
  (re-scoped with the operator). Does **not** block the branding work.
- **P4 (with operator/Helios).** Operator runs the one-off Ads-Editor CSV
  final-URL **migrate** (parent §6.2) using the Helios-emitted
  literal→opaque mapping; canary one `SITE/branding` pair; monitor
  404s + Google-Ads disapprovals; deploy under operator approval. `308`
  back-compat stays in place through and after the migration.

## Verification

- Build green with opaque `generateStaticParams`.
- Redirect unit/e2e: literal→opaque preserves `gclid`/UTMs; redirect-chain
  (literal `/0` → opaque) is the intended single hop or the accepted
  two-hop `308`+`307`, correct statuses, `/0` re-roll stays `no-store`.
- **URL-emission audit test:** no literal brand name in any internal link
  / canonical / sitemap entry for `branding/`.
- **Opaque-ref stability test:** checked-in `brand-id → opaque-ref` test
  vectors (the cross-repo contract — see Coordination); ref derives from
  an immutable normalized row key; build fails on any collision.
- Each landing commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#19`.

## Coordination

The opaque scheme **must** match Helios (`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`)
output exactly. Don't rely on "same code in two repos" — publish a shared
**contract** (checked-in test vectors / generated manifest / importable
package) that both repos prove against in CI. Agree it before opaque ads
are emitted (parent P3 depends on this).

## Binding standards (from the parent, do not weaken)

- Required gates (lint, typecheck, test, build) green on `master`.
- No first-party TypeScript `any` (`as any`, `: any`, `any[]`, `<any>`).
- Tests deterministic; tests never touch prod serving resources; force
  test-only config (no `??=` fallback to ambient prod env).

  `large-action-lock`. Attach an Agent Gate Record per commit / issue
  update.

## Scope owned by this repo

### Phase A — make `pnpm check` green

1. **`pnpm check` (lint + typecheck + test + build) green on `master`.**
   Inventory the current failures first, then fix the underlying cause —
   do not weaken or skip a check to manufacture green.

### Phase B — `any` debt

2. **Remove first-party `any`** (≈15 files). Give each a real type; no
   blanket `unknown` cast-through that merely re-hides it.

### Phase C — scaffolding to stay green (do once for this repo)

   (the same `pnpm check`).

   `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: error` where ESLint exists, else
   a grep gate over first-party `src`.
5. **disabled-gate scanner** — flag `--no-verify` recipes,
   commented-out checks, `ts-ignore`, and `.skip` / `.only` in committed
   tests.
6. **test-resource scanner** — flag prod URLs / credentials and
   ambient-env `??=` fallbacks in tests.
7. **Pre-commit hooks installed and matching CI** — no carve-outs.

## Acceptance

Fresh ephemeral checkout; `pnpm check` (full gate set) run and
**recorded green** under `large-action-lock`; scanners (Phase C) added
and passing; pre-commit hooks match CI with no carve-outs; Agent Gate
Record attached. Sole exception to green is an active prod incident,
repaired to green immediately after.

GAds iteration dashboard

We have begun building (or built v1 of) a three-level GAds iteration / evolution system.  So far the results have been underwhelming, but i have confidence we'll get better.  Since last implementing any of the GAds code, we have made substantial architecture changes, the most significant and relevant to GAds is that we've moved all of the MSS landing page logic into `automation` under Helios control.  Now it (the landing page evolver) can be more tightly integrated with the GAds evolver, potentially combined, but at least operating in lock step now and without cross-repo cross-db "split brain".

What this holistic system is meant for:
- Starting with a base set of GAds and landing pages, and some input signals (GAds performance, GAds policy approvals / limits / disapprovals, asset details at all GAds levels, like campaign down through sitelink or individual keyword or ad, etc), this HOLISTIC system should be able to:
  - improve the performance of ads, 
  - revive disapproved ads after slight modification, 
  - make duplicates of known-high-performers with small exploratory budgets and modifications
  - assess the likely cause(s) of policy disapprovals or policy traffic limitations
  - hill-climb quantitatively with numbers-driven suggestions or modifications to any of the GAds entities or the landing pages themselves to improve all of click-through, interaction rate, LP CTA clicks, and eventual conversion value (NB again we are NOT trying to replace google analytics or develop our own tracking system; gads statistics will contain conversion data along with details ads performance, etc
  - use a multi-layer design, where progressively more advanced LLMs guide the configuration, prompting, and ultimately the direction and performance of the lower levels, optimizing their approaches to the holistic optimization problem


What is OUT OF SCOPE:
- This is not an accounting, auditing, or forensics system.  Do not log every possible thing, and we're not looking for absolute precision.  We're looking for "good enough", "works quite well", "works efficiently", "simple(ish) to understand", "solid architecture that can itself be evolved and iterated", etc
- An in-house replacement for google analytics, google ads results dashboards, or any google-provided analysis systems also covering GAds and user traffic.  Those vendor-provided systems are canonical in their domains and are generally quite good.  We're not trying to produce a better version of those (nor could we), we're trying to build ON TOP of those for maximum utility and operator efficiency, so he doesn't have to do all of this work manually himself.


Given this project scope, we're going to need some visibility into both the "GAds evolution system" and the "LP evolution system".
Consult with Oracle to identify what would be most useful for an operator to see / know about the system as designed and described, and start building the helios "GAds performance" page(s).   For this task and set of pages, i care far less about the *gads performance themselves* and far more about how helios has reacted.  This is meant to introspect, understand, and guide OUR optimization system for GAds, not the ads themselves, which is done via GAds web UI.

If this is unclear, ask questions in a followup ticket before starting.  Otherwise, break down into tasks and begin.

delegated_to:

    issue: 24
    note: Canonical parent for the GAds evolver introspection dashboard; all implementation delegated through its FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#51 child epic. No implementation slice in mostly-static-sites.
```

# Dev-loop optimization — `mostly-static-sites` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#26](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/26).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/dev-loop-optimization/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the
> `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites` slice** of that design.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `mostly-static-sites@master`
> that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#26
> ```
>
> **Re-read the parent `EPIC_PLAN.md` before starting** — it is the
> single source of truth; this file is a thin index over it.

## Goal

Split the monolithic `pnpm check` (lint + typecheck + test + build) so
agents iterate with **light/targeted** checks scoped to the site,
package, or module they changed, while the full `pnpm check` stays the
CI / final gate rather than something hand-run repeatedly under
`large-action-lock` before every commit.

## Binding standards (from the parent, do not weaken)

- Two-gate green tree: fast local + final presubmit. Location split, not
  a waiver — full `pnpm check` (or equivalent) stays enforced in CI.
- A check leaves pre-commit/local iteration only with equal-or-stronger
  coverage remaining in CI.
- No first-party `any`, no disabled/weakened gates, no `--no-verify`,
  tests deterministic and prod-resource-free (inherited from fleet-green
  [#20](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/20); keep green).

## Scope owned by this repo

1. **Inventory + time** the steps inside `pnpm check` (lint, typecheck,
   test, build) and any pre-commit/CI steps, from a fresh ephemeral
   checkout with a warm cache.
2. **Provide light/targeted commands** for every >~30s step:
   - lint/typecheck scoped to the changed package/site/path rather than
     the whole workspace;
   - focused test runs (changed module / pattern);
   - avoid full static site builds in the local loop — keep the full
     build in CI unless it is consistently under ~30s.
3. **Document a dev-loop table in `mostly-static-sites`' `AGENTS.md`**:
   changed site/content/module path → light local command → final
   presubmit (`pnpm check` in CI) → when an agent may hand-run the full
   build/check.
4. **Lighten pre-commit hooks** to fast/targeted checks, **after**
   confirming full `pnpm check` is a required CI status.
5. **Confirm the broken-master window is closed**: full `pnpm check`
   validates the exact commit before it publishes/`bounce`-deploys, or
   promotion waits for CI green.

## Acceptance

From a fresh ephemeral checkout:

1. `AGENTS.md` dev-loop table present; every >~30s step has a
   light/targeted command or a documented heavy-final-only exception.
2. Pre-commit hooks fast/targeted; full `pnpm check` remains a required
   CI status, recorded green for a sample commit.
3. No coverage deleted; broken-master window closed or interim exception
   documented.
4. Agent Gate Record (two-gate template) attached.

> Parent epic: [virusdave/top-level#47](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/47)
>
> The implementation commit on this repo's master MUST carry the trailer:

> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47

## Step 0 — read canon first

Ephemeral checkout of top-level master, then read
[`docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md)
"Code standards" (the `--help` rule) and
[`docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md)
"Serving services".

## The requirement

Every invocable tool must accept `-h`/`--help`, print usage, and exit `0`
**before any effect** (env-var assertions, locks, network/API calls,
`git` fetch/push, file writes). Handle `--help` first, ahead of all other
option parsing and required-env checks. This applies to bash scripts
**and** to `.ts` entry-point scripts (parse `--help` at the top of the
entrypoint, before any side-effecting work).

- Any other invocable tooling you find during the audit (including the
  `bounce` deploy helper if present — a deploy helper with `--help` must
  not deploy).

## Verifying

Run each tool with `--help` and confirm it prints usage and exits 0 with
no side effects.

## Finalize

Commit with a plain imperative subject (no `feat:`/`fix:` prefix) and the
`Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47` trailer; push to this repo's default
branch.

# mostly-static-sites child epic: durable seven-day temporary pages

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Raise the one-offs service's bounded maximum lifetime from 24 hours to seven
days, make every serving/control surface agree on manifest-derived liveness,
bound storage growth, migrate publication to daemon-owned uploads, and make the
existing private `/one-offs/` index useful and accessible on phones.

## Required implementation

1. **One liveness contract**
   - Keep the two-hour default; set the daemon and NixOS hard maximum to
     604,800 seconds. Preserve each existing manifest's immutable 24-hour
     ceiling and every shorter caller-selected lifetime.
   - Define one `liveSlots(now)` selector used by direct serving, index, list,
     get, health, extension, boot, and garbage collection. At
     `now >= expiresAtMs`, all reads are absent and extension cannot revive the
     page, regardless of disk cleanup timing.
   - Keep validated manifests as the sole source of truth; never persist or
     cache a second index.

2. **Bounded daemon-owned storage**
   - Implement the binding design's defaults for live slots, files/bytes and
     submissions per slot, 10 GiB data-directory quota, 5 GiB free-space
     reserve, reservation accounting, error codes, and one async mutation
     mutex.
   - Add the streaming upload API and update `scripts/one-offs stage` before
     retiring group-writable `incoming`. Reject symlinks/special files and
     clean abandoned reservations. Publication must fail before visibility if
     any bound would be crossed.
   - Handlers are never daemon children. A socket-activated executor accepts
     only validated slot, submission, and configured-handler IDs over the
     root-owned Unix socket, derives every path itself, selects executables only
     from the fixed Nix allowlist, and runs separately unprivileged with the
     entire one-offs data directory bind-mounted read-only.
   - Fsync atomic manifest writes. Quarantine invalid/partial/orphaned state,
     omit it from serving, garbage-collect it after 24 hours, and expose
     bounded pressure/degraded diagnostics.

3. **Canonical private index**
   - Keep the bare `/one-offs/` route, render a bounded newest-first snapshot
     of live manifests, and preserve tailnet-only serving, Unix-socket control,
     `no-store`, and `noindex, nofollow`.
   - Implement the approved information architecture, privacy language,
     exact/relative expiry, accessible uniquely named actions, collapsed
     technical details, 320-pixel card layout, optional 21+-item progressive
     search, and populated/empty/degraded/error/direct-404 states.
   - Escape all caller labels. Do not add mutation controls or imply that a
     nonce authorizes a tailnet user.

## Tests and review

Use a fake clock and temporary data directory. Cover exact expiry across every
surface, old/new ceilings, restart recovery, partial manifests, upload/create/
submission/GC/index concurrency, reservation rollback, every admission bound,
quota/free-space failures, escaping, bounded 500-item output, 21-item search
and no-script fallback, mobile markup, all states, `HEAD`, headers, and
tailnet rejection. Integration tests must prove handler IDs cannot inject paths
or executables and handlers cannot write slot data. Accessibility coverage
includes landmarks, heading order, focus, unique actions, 44-pixel targets,
light/dark contrast, reduced motion, and 320-pixel width.

Before first exposure, Oracle must review representative rendered output for
populated, empty, expiring, degraded, error, and 404 states on desktop and
mobile and return APPROVE. The approved design review alone is not the final
render review. Before implementation, any nontrivial deviation from the binding
architecture requires a fresh Oracle architecture review; the actual final
critical-infrastructure diff also requires Oracle change review.

## Rollout and rollback

Follow the four-stage client-first migration in the binding design: add the
streaming API; deploy the packaged client everywhere and update canon/runbooks
through canon's update protocol; prove seven days with zero legacy claims plus
streaming canaries; only then remove legacy upload access and enable seven-day
lifetimes. Prove the backing filesystem quota before increasing the cap.

Roll out selectors/index first under the 24-hour maximum through the canonical
mostly-static-sites deployment path. Then enable bounds and seven-day creation,
verify two-hour and seven-day canaries, delete them, and observe two GC cycles.
Rollback first restores a packaged client compatible with the running server.
Before rolling the server behind the streaming API back, restore legacy
`incoming` permissions and the prior canon/runbook in one reviewed change and
pass a short-lived canary, preserving at least one supported publication path
throughout. Then restore 24-hour creation while grandfathering already-created
longer-lived manifests; list their latest expiry rather than deleting or
shortening them.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```

# Gemini-Seeded Strategic-Cluster Campaigns — `nixos-sbc` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#5](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/5).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/gemini-clusters/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo; this child epic scope is **strictly the host /
> systemd / nix slice of that design**, covering both Batch-1 (the
> `gads-cluster-sweep.service` + timer) AND Batch-2 (the
> `asset-gen.service` + nightly timer that rebuilds manifests when
> site config or strategic-clusters config changes).
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `nixos-sbc` master and
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#5
> ```

## Scope owned by this repo

### N1. `gads-cluster-sweep.service` + timer (Batch 1)

- New systemd unit declaration under the existing Helios deployment
  on `vps-nixos-3` (whichever VM already runs the daily L2
  `gads-run-analysis.service`):
  - `gads-cluster-sweep.service` — `Type=oneshot`, invokes
    `bin/gads-cluster-sweep` from the `automation` checkout that
    Helios already deploys.
  - `gads-cluster-sweep.timer` — `OnCalendar=Mon 04:00 America/New_York`
    (weekly, per parent design §"Hybrid pipeline").
- Journal-friendly logging (stdout/stderr captured under
  `journalctl -u gads-cluster-sweep`).
- No new VM, no new port.

### N2. `asset-gen.service` + nightly timer (Batch-2 addition)

- New systemd unit on the same Helios host:
  - `asset-gen.service` — `Type=oneshot`, invokes
    `bin/asset-gen --rebuild-manifests` from the `automation`
    checkout. Reads the current `strategic-clusters.jsonc` +
    `sites.yaml` (via the helios DB / config-fetch path that
    `automation` already exposes) and rebuilds any per-family
    manifest entries whose inputs have changed since the last run.
  - `asset-gen.timer` — `OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:30 America/New_York`
    (nightly), with the existing `RandomizedDelaySec` jitter
    conventions Helios already uses.
- **Change-detection trigger** — an additional `Restart=on-failure`
  + `path-unit` watch on the on-disk copies of
  `strategic-clusters.jsonc` and `sites.yaml` so an out-of-cycle
  config change kicks an asset-gen rebuild within minutes instead of
  waiting for the nightly window.

### N3. Helios deploy considerations

- If `automation` Helios needs a new nginx route for the
  `/ads/cluster-proposals/**` endpoints or
  `/v1/conversion-events` ingestion endpoint, the declarative
  config for that lives here. Coordinate with `automation` P3 / E
  to land the unit change in lockstep.
- Public bundle exposure: the `mss-one-offs` public-URL pattern
  used by other epics is reused; no new nginx vhost is needed for
  the bundle ZIPs (they're served through helios under the existing
  authenticated route).

## Out of scope

- Helios application code, DB schema, LLM / Painter wrappers, asset
  approval flow — `automation`.
- Public landing-page rendering, sites.yaml schema, JS bundle —
  `mostly-static-sites`.
- DNS records — there are no *new* public hostnames in this epic;
  everything lives under existing per-site domains (`<site>.freshlybaked.us`)
  and the existing helios host. If that changes, file a separate
  DNS-only task.

## Phases

- **N1.** `gads-cluster-sweep.service` + `.timer` lands and runs
  end-to-end against the current `automation` checkout. Unblocks
  the production weekly sweep.
- **N2.** `asset-gen.service` + `.timer` + path-unit change watch.
  Unblocks the nightly manifest rebuild + low-latency reaction to
  config edits.
- **N3.** Any helios-side nginx / unit changes needed to serve the
  new `automation` routes (coordinated with `automation` P3 + E).
  This phase may be a no-op if the existing wildcard route covers
  the new paths.

## Cross-repo dependencies

- N1 needs `automation` P1 (CLI works) before it has anything
  meaningful to invoke.
- N2 needs `automation` B1 (asset-gen worker skeleton with
  `--rebuild-manifests` mode) before its timer is useful.
- N3 needs `automation` P3 / E (new routes defined) before the
  nginx update lands.

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. N1–N3 have landing commits on `nixos-sbc` master carrying
   `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#5`.
2. `systemctl status gads-cluster-sweep.timer` on the helios host
   shows the timer armed and the last run unit-succeeded.
3. `systemctl status asset-gen.timer` shows the same; the last
   nightly run logs `painter_calls_saved=N` for some N≥0 in its
   journal, demonstrating the existing-asset-preference path is
   reachable from production.
4. A targeted edit of `strategic-clusters.jsonc` triggers the
   path-unit watch and kicks an out-of-cycle asset-gen rebuild
   within 5 minutes (verified via journalctl timestamps).

  needing a new server block.  If a path-specific block is needed
  (e.g. to bump body-size limits for VeriScan attachments), add it
  here.
- **Body-size headroom** — VeriScan envelopes can include base64
  payloads (the `PhotoBase64` field is obsolete but still possible);
  ensure nginx `client_max_body_size` on the helios vhost is ≥ 4MB.

- Helios app code, DB migration, webhook handler, admin page,
  backfill CLI — `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`.
- VeriScan-side webhook configuration — operator.

  parent EPIC_PLAN.md §"Bearer token"; mechanical rotation is a
  follow-up if needed.

- **N1.** Add the agenix secret and wire it into helios-server's
  environment.  Restart `helios-server` once the FreshlyBakedNYC/automation A1
  release is also live so the env var is consumed by code that
  reads it.  Until then, the env var simply sits unused.
- **N2.** (Conditional) nginx body-size or path-specific tweak if
  the smoke-test in `automation` A1 reveals a default-size
  limitation.  Likely a no-op on the existing config.

## Cross-repo dependencies

- N1 has no upstream dependency.  It unblocks `automation` A1's
  prod deployment (A1 code can be developed and unit-tested
  without N1).
- N2 is reactive — only land if A1 testing surfaces a need.

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. N1 has a landing commit on `nixos-sbc` master carrying
   `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9`.
2. `systemctl show helios-server -p Environment` on `vps-nixos-3`
   (or the equivalent inspection of the rendered agenix template)
   confirms `VERISCAN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` is present.
3. `curl -i -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H
   'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{}'
   https://helios.freshlybaked.us/wh/bx/veriscan/checkin`

# Agent Canon — `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc` child epic

> Parent epic: [virusdave/top-level#10](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/10)
>
> The implementation commit on this repo's master MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10
> ```
>
> That trailer triggers the cross-repo completion flow back to the
> parent issue.

## What this epic does

Rewrites this repo's root `AGENTS.md` to consume **canonical agent
rules** from `virusdave/top-level` instead of duplicating them
locally. The canonical rules are short, imperative, and updated in one
place — so all our repos stay in sync without manual mirroring.

## Step 0 — fetch and read canon BEFORE doing anything

The canonical agent rules live in
`virusdave/top-level : docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md` on `master`. **Read
them first** (and use the same mechanism in your final AGENTS.md
header — see Step 2):

```sh
canon_ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
              /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$canon_ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … internalize the rules — they govern this rewrite …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$canon_ws"
```

Pay particular attention to: ephemeral checkouts for your own work,
the "Canon update interrupt" in §0, the operational-reality §5, and
the §6 contract for what peer `AGENTS.md` must contain.

## Step 1 — ephemeral checkout of THIS repo

```sh
ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
        /home/amp-local/src/nixos-sbc --label agent-canon)
cd "$ws"
```

Adjust the source path if `nixos-sbc` lives elsewhere on this host
(`/home/amp-local/src/nixos-sbc` is the standard).

## Step 2 — rewrite `AGENTS.md` to the pointer model

Open the existing root `AGENTS.md`, audit it for what to keep, then
replace its contents with this exact structure. Fill in the
repo-specific section from your audit.

```markdown
# Agent instructions for `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`

**MANDATORY FIRST READ — agent canon.** Before doing anything in this
repo, fetch and read the latest canonical agent rules:

```sh
ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
        /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … apply the rules …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$ws"
```

That file is authoritative across **all** our repos. Re-read on every
agent session — it changes. If anything in this file conflicts with
canon, **canon wins** — fix the stale prose here.

The rest of this file lists only **nixos-sbc-specific** instructions.

---

## Repo purpose

<one-paragraph summary: this repo holds the NixOS system closures
for our SBC fleet — vps-nixos-3 and any other managed hosts —
deployed via `self-deploy`.>

## Deploy

<the canonical deploy procedure: `self-deploy <host>` (or the
equivalent canonical wrapper). Per the operator's recurring
complaint, NEVER `nixos-rebuild switch` directly on a serving host,
NEVER restart user-facing services during the switch — the canonical
`self-deploy*` packages handle drain/mirror modes. Preserve any
nuance the old AGENTS.md had here.>

## Build / test

<repo-specific: `nix flake check`, `nix build .#<host>`, etc.>

## Host topology / paths

<exact paths agents need: which hosts this repo deploys, source
checkout location on each, where flake.nix and per-host configs
live, naming conventions for modules.>
```

## Step 3 — what to KEEP

From the existing AGENTS.md, **keep every operational fact** an agent
needs to work here: exact deploy commands, service names, log paths,
config locations, build/test invocations, architecture diagrams,
repo-specific cross-references, contact info.

## Step 4 — what to DELETE (canon covers it)

Delete and do NOT restate any of:

- "Never SSH to self" / "SSH port" rules
- "Use ephemeral checkout" / "do not edit shared `~/src`" rules
- "Default to `master`, no feature branches" rule
- Bash vs Python / shebang style / typed-code rules
- Performance budgets (UI ≤500ms, DB ≤125ms)
- "Use Oracle / painter / Bedrock LLMs" rules
- Group-writable file rule
- Generic task-dag CLI workflow (the
  `frontier → work → complete → push` loop)
- Generic cross-repo child-epic trailer flow

If you find any of those in the current `AGENTS.md`, **delete** the
prose and rely on canon. If a rule there contradicts canon, canon
wins — flag the conflict in your commit message.

## Step 5 — target size & sanity check

The rewritten file should be **≤ 120 lines**. If it's bigger, you're
probably restating canon — re-audit and trim. If it's much shorter
than the existing file but still has all operational facts, that's
the correct outcome.

Run a final read-through asking: "could a brand-new agent who has
just read canon do real work in this repo using only what's left
here?" If yes, done.

## Step 6 — commit, link, push

```sh
git add AGENTS.md
git commit -m "agents: adopt canon pointer model (Satisfies virusdave/top-level#10)

Replace duplicated cross-repo rules with a mandatory canon-fetch
header per docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md. Repo-specific content
(deploy, paths, services) preserved.

Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10"
git push origin HEAD:<this-repo-default-branch>
```

(Use this repo's default branch — usually `master` or `main`. Do not
open a PR; push directly per the canon working-workflow rule.)

The `Satisfies:` trailer fires the cross-repo completion flow back to
top-level#10.

## Acceptance

- Root `AGENTS.md` opens with the unignorable canon-fetch header.
- Zero duplication of canon content.
- All prior repo-specific operational facts preserved.
- File length ≤ 120 lines.
- Commit includes `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10`.
- Pushed to default branch.

## If you're blocked

- **App not installed / push refused**: stop. Report the exact error
  and your proposed diff to the parent issue
  ([virusdave/top-level#10](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/10)).
- **Repo doesn't have a root `AGENTS.md`**: create one using the same
  template. The acceptance criteria still apply.
- **Existing AGENTS.md has something you don't recognize**: assume
  it's an operator customization and preserve it. When in doubt, ask.
issues.creator: helios-freshly-baked[bot]
issues.title: Agent canon: rewrite nixos-sbc AGENTS.md to pointer model (Satisfies virusdave/top-level#10)

# agent-pain-points migration — nixos-sbc child epic: deploy keys + Helios service wiring (OPERATOR-GATED)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#40](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/40)
> — "Migrate the agent-waste canonical git storage to different repo".
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`virusdave/top-level` → `docs/epics/agent-pain-points-migration/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/agent-pain-points-migration/EPIC_PLAN.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit on
> [`Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc) `master`
> that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#40`, and the **final** satisfying commit MUST
> also carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer.

## 1. Goal

Provision the GitHub deploy keys, agenix secrets, SSH host aliases, and Helios
service env so that (a) the **github-worker dispatcher** (`amp-local`) can
**push** the agent-waste backlog to `virusdave/agent-pain-points`, and (b)
**Helios** can **read** it via a mirror and **write** advisory promotions to it.
This unblocks the github-worker and automation child epics.

## 2. Why this is operator-gated

Encrypting agenix secrets requires the operator's age identity; generating
write-capable GitHub deploy keys and committing encrypted private-key material
is security-sensitive. A worker may prepare the Nix code and exact steps but
**must not** self-provision the key material. Treat this child as
**`task-dag block` + `page-dave` once** until the operator supplies/approves the
key material.

## 3. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Dispatcher write key** | A write-capable GitHub deploy key for `virusdave/agent-pain-points`, wired for the `amp-local` user (agenix secret + SSH host alias `github-agent-pain-points` + gitconfig `insteadOf`/`pushInsteadOf` rewrite), so `scripts/agent-waste-export` pushes there. Model on the existing amp-local `github-top-level-deploy-key` wiring in [`hosts/per-host/vps-nixos-3.nix`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc/blob/master/hosts/per-host/vps-nixos-3.nix) + [`modules/amp-local-user.nix`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc/blob/master/modules/amp-local-user.nix). |
| **Helios read key** | A read deploy key for the mirror, exposed at a stable agenix path (e.g. `/run/agenix/helios-github-agent-pain-points-deploy-key`), owner `helios`. Add to both the primary (vps-nixos-3) and, if the backend-only mirror peer must serve the review route during self-deploy windows, vps-nixos-2. |
| **Helios write key** | A write deploy key for promote (e.g. `/run/agenix/helios-github-agent-pain-points-write-deploy-key`), owner `helios`, primary host. |
| **Helios env** | Set the new Helios env vars the automation child introduces — distinct **read mirror dir** and **write clone dir** plus repo URL + key paths (do **not** overload the `HELIOS_TOP_LEVEL_*` vars; see design §5 hazard). Wire in [`modules/helios.nix`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc/blob/master/modules/helios.nix) / the per-host service block. |
| **secrets.nix** | Register each new `.age` file with the correct `publicKeys` (operator + host) in [`secrets.nix`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc/blob/master/secrets.nix). |

## 4. Constraints / invariants

- Deploy keys are **not path-scoped** (GitHub limitation); the mitigation is
  that `agent-pain-points` is a tiny dedicated repo, so blast radius is small —
  this is precisely the "dedicated advisories repo" isolation the original
  design considered. Keep read and write keys **separate**.
- Read key must be read-only on GitHub; only the promote/export keys are
  write-enabled.
- Follow the existing helios-parser-configs / helios-github-automation deploy
  key patterns for ownership, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, and known-hosts.

## 5. Dependencies / ordering

- **Blocks** the github-worker exporter cutover (needs dispatcher write key) and
  the automation Helios cutover (needs read+write keys).
- Coordinate the actual key rotation-in with the parent epic's §6 cutover.

## 6. Acceptance

- `amp-local` on the dispatcher host can `git push` to `agent-pain-points`
  through the aliased key (verified against an ephemeral throwaway ref, then
  removed — never leave test refs).
- Helios service user can clone/fetch `agent-pain-points` read-only via its key,
  and can push a promotion via its write key (verified against a temp repo /
  ephemeral branch, cleaned up — never prod content).
- `nixos-rebuild`/eval is green; secrets decrypt on the target host.
- Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 7. Safety / rollback

Rollback = revoke/rotate the new deploy keys and revert the Nix change. Never
apply to prod outside the sanctioned deploy path. No prod DB, no schema. Do not
commit unencrypted key material. The new keys are additive; removing them makes
the dependent flows fail closed (advisory injection/review degrade to inert,
never to wrong data).
issues.creator: helios-freshly-baked[bot]
issues.title: agent-pain-points migration: deploy keys + Helios service wiring (operator-gated)

# Tooling `--help` safety — `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc` child epic (safety-critical)

> Parent epic: [virusdave/top-level#47](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/47)
>
> The implementation commit on this repo's master MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47
> ```
>
> That trailer triggers the cross-repo completion flow back to the parent
> issue.

## Why this is safety-critical

Our `self-deploy*` deploy wrappers are the single sanctioned way to roll
production services. They currently do **no flag parsing** and barge
straight into their effectful core, so an agent invoking one with
`--help` — expecting only usage text — can trigger a real production
rollout (`nixos-rebuild switch`, traffic flips, unit restarts, SSH to the
peer host). Canon now forbids this.

## Step 0 — read canon first

Read the rule before touching anything (ephemeral checkout of top-level
master):

- [`docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md) "Code standards" — the normative `--help` rule.
- [`docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md) "Serving services" — the deploy-safety face of it.

## The requirement

Every invocable tool must accept `-h` and `--help`, print usage to
stdout, and exit `0` **before any effect** — for these deploy tools,
before any `nixos-rebuild`, traffic/mirror flip, `systemctl`
restart/drain, deploy-lock acquisition, SSH to a peer, secret read, or
file write. Handle `--help` first, ahead of all other option parsing and
required-env checks.

## Known violators (audit for more — this list is a starting point)

- `self-deploy` — inline bash in `hosts/vps/amp-local.nix` (the
  whole-host `nixos-rebuild switch` package).
- `self-deploy-helios` — inline bash in `modules/helios.nix` (traffic
  flip + `helios-prep`/`helios-server` restart + `/healthzz` poll).
- `self-deploy-{site}` — generated by the `mkSelfDeployScript` factory in
  `hosts/vps/sites-mirror.nix` (per-site MSS rollout). Fix the factory
  once so every generated package inherits `--help` handling.
- `scripts/helios-deploy` — orchestrates `self-deploy-helios` across
  primary/mirror; begins Phase 1 SSH immediately.
- Any other scripts in `scripts/` and any other nix-packaged CLIs you
  find during the audit.

Note: `scripts/update-amp-local-version.sh` and
`update-amp-local-version-everywhere.sh` already handle `-h`/`--help`
correctly — mirror their pattern (a `usage()` that exits 0, parsed
first).

## Verifying without deploying

**Do not run an actual deploy to test.** For each nix-packaged tool,
`nix build` the package and run the built script with `--help`, asserting
it prints usage and exits 0 with zero side effects. Landing on
`nixos-sbc` master does not auto-deploy (deploy stays manual via
`self-deploy`), and adding an early `--help` exit ahead of all effects is
a low-risk, easily-reverted change. Keep a clean revert path.

## Finalize

Commit with a plain imperative subject (no `feat:`/`fix:` prefix) and the
`Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47` trailer; push to this repo's default
branch.

Agents repeatedly wrap self-deploy* commands in an outer large-action-lock even though those first-party deploy wrappers already lock their heavy phases internally. The nested call can wait on its own ancestor and waste operator/agent time.

Scope:

- Harden large-action-lock / deploy tooling so nested same-process-tree uses fail fast or safely re-enter instead of waiting out a TTL.
- Update runbooks so future agents do not wrap self-deploy*, especially self-deploy-helios and self-deploy.

# Trusted read-only Helios agent access — `nixos-sbc` child epic

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#62](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/62)
> — "Need a means for local agents to access helios in trusted fashion".
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`virusdave/top-level` → `docs/epics/helios-agent-readonly-access/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/helios-agent-readonly-access/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit on
> [`Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc) `master`
> that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```text
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#62
> ```
>
> The final satisfying commit should also carry this child epic's own
> `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level
> completion aggregator can attribute the peer-repo completion to the delegated
> child issue.

## 1. Goal

Provision the production host wiring that lets local `amp-local` agents make
temporary, signed, read-only Helios verification requests after sanctioned
Helios deploys. This child owns only the NixOS / nginx / secret provisioning
slice of the resolved design; the Helios verifier and the agent-side helper
land in peer repos.

The result should make the Helios application receive enough configuration to
verify Ed25519-signed agent requests on both Helios-serving hosts, while keeping
private signing material restricted to the local agent user and making every
allowlist extension reviewable through `nixos-sbc` git history.

## 2. Why this is operator-gated

This work introduces a production signing key that can unlock OAuth-gated
read-only Helios pages when combined with a live allowlist rule. Workers may
prepare the Nix code, config shape, and verification commands, but generating,
installing, or rotating the private key material is security-sensitive and must
use the fleet secrets process with operator approval.

Do **not** commit private keys, plaintext secrets, or sample secrets. If secret
material is not already supplied through agenix or a host-local root action,
block the task and page the operator with the exact key names, intended owners,
and target hosts.

## 3. Scope owned by `nixos-sbc`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **`amp-local` signing private key** | Provision an Ed25519 private key only where local agents run today: vps-nixos-3. Materialise it as a real file owned by `amp-local`, group `agents` only if needed for operator inspection, mode `0400` or stricter. Prefer a stable path such as `/home/amp-local/.secret/helios-agent-readonly/signing-key` or another path exposed to the agent-helper child. It must not be readable by `helios`, must not appear in the Nix store, and must not be passed through systemd environment variables. Private signing keys do **not** need to exist on vps-nixos-2 unless agents are intentionally run there later. |
| **Public verifier key(s)** | Provision matching public verifier key metadata for the Helios server on **both** vps-nixos-3 (primary) and vps-nixos-2 (backend-only mirror). Public keys may live in Nix config or a non-secret environment/config file, but keep key IDs explicit, stable, and documented (for example `amp-local-vps3-2026q3`). |
| **Expiring allowlist** | Provision the active agent-readonly allowlist into the Helios server config on both vps-nixos-3 and vps-nixos-2. Every rule must include `id`, `owner`, `reason`, `not_before`, `not_after`, `max_response_bytes`, and route-specific safe-read notes. Prefer exact path entries; use prefix rules only for narrow static-asset paths with segment-boundary checks handled by Helios. No broad `/api/*`, admin, metric-grant, cashier-display, or indefinite rules. |
| **Helios env/config plumbing** | Add `services.helios` options or `extraEnvironment` entries (whichever best matches the Helios child implementation) for the public verifier-key config and allowlist config. Keep primary and backend-only mirror config in parity, because public traffic may be served by either backend during `self-deploy-helios` windows. |
| **Public nginx header stripping** | Ensure the public `helios.freshlybaked.us` nginx vhost strips inbound `X-Helios-Agent-*` headers before proxying to Helios unless the Helios implementation intentionally verifies raw client headers itself. The goal is that internet clients cannot smuggle trusted agent headers through nginx. Use explicit `proxy_set_header X-Helios-Agent-… "";` lines for the final header names from the Helios child. |
| **Optional loopback-only vhost** | If the implementation chooses a loopback-only agent vhost/port as defense-in-depth, expose it only on loopback, never publicly. Only that vhost may forward the `X-Helios-Agent-*` headers to Helios. Public nginx must still strip them. The loopback vhost is not the auth model; Helios signature, freshness, no-cookie/no-authorization, and allowlist checks remain mandatory. |
| **Backend bind/firewall verification** | Verify how `helios-server` binds on vps-nixos-3 and vps-nixos-2 and whether direct backend access is reachable outside loopback. Tighten bind/firewall behavior if the existing module permits unintended direct public/LAN access, but do not rely on bind tightening as the only protection. |
| **Permissions and comments** | Keep comments near every key/allowlist entry explaining parent `virusdave/top-level#62`, expiry, owner, and how to extend or remove access. Future extension must require a normal git review and deploy. |

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- Depends on the `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` child defining the exact Helios
  config contract: public-key env/config format, allowlist env/config format,
  and final `X-Helios-Agent-*` header names.
- Blocks live verification until the agent-helper child can sign requests using
  the provisioned private key path.
- The vps-nixos-2 mirror config must land before declaring rollout complete;
  vps3-only success is incomplete because self-deploy mirror windows can serve
  requests from vps2.

## 5. Suggested implementation shape

1. Add `services.helios.agentReadonly` options in `modules/helios.nix` if the
   Helios child expects structured config, or wire the agreed env vars through
   `services.helios.extraEnvironment` in `hosts/per-host/vps-nixos-{2,3}.nix` if
   that is smaller and clearer.
2. Register any required agenix secrets in `secrets.nix`:
   - private signing key secret for vps-nixos-3 only, owned by `amp-local`,
     mode `0400`;
   - only if the Helios implementation wants verifier/allowlist as secret-ish
     files, corresponding host-specific `.age` entries for both vps-nixos-3 and
     vps-nixos-2. Prefer non-secret Nix config for public verifier keys and
     allowlist metadata unless there is a concrete reason to hide them.
3. Materialise the vps3 private key through the existing per-host secret helper
   pattern in `hosts/per-host/vps-nixos-3.nix`, not through a systemd
   environment variable.
4. Add public-nginx header stripping in the Helios nginx vhost generated by
   `modules/helios.nix`. If adding an optional loopback-only vhost, keep its
   config adjacent and document that it is defense-in-depth only.
5. Add parity comments/checks so vps-nixos-2 receives the same public verifier
   keys and active allowlist rules as vps-nixos-3.

## 6. Acceptance

- `nix flake check` or the repo's equivalent targeted Nix eval/build gate is
  green for the touched hosts/modules, or any skipped heavy gate is justified in
  the Agent Gate Record.
- The `amp-local` private signing key exists on vps-nixos-3 at the documented
  path, is owned by `amp-local`, is mode `0400` or stricter, and is not readable
  by the `helios` service user.
- Helios on both vps-nixos-3 and vps-nixos-2 receives the same public verifier
  key ID(s) and the same active expiring allowlist rules.
- Public nginx strips the final `X-Helios-Agent-*` header set before proxying
  internet-originated traffic to Helios.
- If a loopback-only vhost is added, it binds only to loopback and is the only
  nginx path that forwards agent headers.
- Backend bind/firewall behavior is explicitly verified and recorded.
- After the Helios verifier and agent helper are deployed, live verification
  from `amp-local` proves:
  - a whitelisted page route renders;
  - a whitelisted loader/API route returns;
  - a non-whitelisted route denies;
  - `POST`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` deny even with a valid signature;
  - signed requests containing `Cookie` or `Authorization` deny;
  - vps-nixos-2 has the same public key/allowlist behavior during a mirror
    window or an equivalent controlled mirror-host probe;
  - logs contain metadata only, not signatures, cookies, private keys, or
    response bodies.

## 7. Safety / rollback

Apply production changes only through the sanctioned `nixos-sbc` deploy path
(`self-deploy` / `self-deploy-helios` as appropriate for the final change). Do
not manually restart `nginx`, `helios-server`, or `helios-worker`.

Rollback is deliberately simple and does not require DB cleanup:

1. expire or remove the allowlist rule(s);
2. remove the public verifier key config from both Helios hosts;
3. remove the vps3 `amp-local` private-key secret/materialisation if access is
   being fully retired;
4. redeploy via the sanctioned wrapper;
5. verify signed requests now fail closed while normal OAuth login and Helios
   health checks still pass.

The Nix change is additive until the allowlist becomes active. Reverting the
implementation commit and redeploying removes the access path; the Helios child
must still enforce its own fail-closed behavior when config is absent.

## 8. Out of scope

- Implementing the Helios Ed25519 verifier, request principal, allowlist parser,
  response byte caps, or audit logging — owned by `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`.
- Implementing the agent fetch/render helper — likely owned by
  `Nicponskis/github-worker` unless that child chooses a different existing home.
- Granting write access, creating real Helios users/cookies, broad API access,
  metric grants, cashier-display access, or operator impersonation.
- Publishing captured HTML/CSS/screenshots to public hosts.
- Any production DB write, schema migration, or Helios data backfill.

# nixos-sbc child epic: supervise durable repair reconciliation

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Package and supervise the github-worker repair reconciler and its independent
watchdog on the production host, with encrypted least-privilege credentials,
durable state, safe rollout controls, and a reversible deployment.

## Required implementation

1. Package the reviewed github-worker reconciler/watchdog and one coherent
   canonical task-dag runtime. Do not vendor or reimplement either system.
2. Add `github-worker-repair-reconciler.service` and the separately supervised
   watchdog with the binding design's five-minute jittered cadence, pool of
   four, 30-second restart delay, five-minute start-limit window, durable state
   directories, and bounded resource/sandbox settings.
3. Provision the shared GitHub App ID/private key through age-encrypted systemd
   credentials. Tokens must remain ephemeral and must not enter the Nix store,
   environment dumps, logs, command lines, or persistent state.
4. Package `page-dave` for the watchdog and preserve the single-writer split
   between reconciler `status.json` and watchdog `watchdog.json`.
5. Expose service, dry-run, projection-rollout, and paging kill switches plus
   documented inspection, telemetry, credential-preflight, rollout, rollback,
   and failure procedures. These controls must never override repository
   enrollment: `off|observe|enforce` comes only from current top-level
   `repos.conf` authority.

## Verification

- Nix evaluation/build and unit tests prove command wiring, credentials,
  sandboxing, restart policy, state ownership, disabled defaults, and rollback
  selection without starting a production unit.
- Integration tests use fake GitHub/task-dag endpoints and disposable state;
  no test targets production resources.
- After both code-owning child epics are Oracle-approved and landed, deploy
  only through the canonical `self-deploy*` path. Never manually restart,
  stop, or kill the units.

## Rollout and rollback

Deploy disabled, verify rendered units and credentials, and support the
top-level child's preflight/dry-run and staged observe/enforce rollout. Runtime
rollback disables the new units/controls and selects the previous immutable
packages; it preserves chain refs, repair issues/tasks, and status evidence.
Retain a new-format-compatible task-dag until no active new-format chain
remains. Selecting an older incompatible package first requires the reviewed
compare-and-set migration of every active substate to legacy-safe `State=red`
and readback proving no issue/task will close. Record active red chains before
rollback. A normal git revert remains the configuration rollback path only
after that compatibility gate is satisfied.

This is production control-plane infrastructure. The binding architecture
already has Oracle approval, but the implementation worker must get Oracle
architecture rereview for any design change and Oracle review of the actual
final diff before commit and deployment. Iterate to APPROVE.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```

## Result needed

Make the Helios admin migration runner use a PostgreSQL 18 client, matching the managed production PostgreSQL 18.4 server, and deploy the corrected NixOS worker closure through the canonical whole-host rollout.

## Incident and root cause

Two audited attempts to apply `104_vendor_brand_associations` failed because `modules/helios.nix` pins `HELIOS_PSQL_BIN` and the worker path to PostgreSQL 17.10 while production is PostgreSQL 18.4. PostgreSQL 17 `psql` forwards an inline CSV `COPY` `\.` terminator; PostgreSQL 18 treats those forwarded bytes as CSV data. Both attempts therefore failed with `missing data for column "vendor_name"`, and both explicit transactions rolled back.

The migration was subsequently applied successfully through PostgreSQL 18.4 `psql`, with the exact reviewed artifact, advisory lock 620462, `COPY 240`, 84 vendors, 232 associations, `COMMIT`, and a true live schema sentinel. The durable operator direction and incident context are in [FreshlyBakedNYC/automation issue 79 comment 5014869035](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/79#issuecomment-5014869035).

## Approved design

Oracle approved this smallest repair:

1. Define one local Nix binding, `heliosMigrationPsql = pkgs.postgresql_18`.
2. Reuse that binding in both `helios-worker.path` and `HELIOS_PSQL_BIN`.
3. Correct the stale comment that says production is PostgreSQL 17.
4. Do not add a fallback, dual client, unversioned package, or tautological assertion.
5. Before deploy, evaluate the selected package version and rendered worker environment/path.
6. Deploy with canonical whole-host `self-deploy`, not `self-deploy-helios`, because this changes the NixOS unit closure.
7. Verify the worker is active, `HELIOS_PSQL_BIN` is store-absolute and reports PostgreSQL 18.x, and a read-only server query reports PostgreSQL 18.x. Do not apply another migration as a smoke test.

## Acceptance criteria

- The worker closure has one canonical PostgreSQL 18 package binding reused by path and environment.
- Focused Nix evaluation/checks pass.
- Post-implementation Oracle critical-infrastructure review approves the diff.
- The commit is pushed before canonical whole-host deployment.
- Post-deploy service, client-version, and read-only server-version probes pass.
- Rollback is git revert plus canonical `self-deploy`; no manual service restart.

issues.body:
## Outcome

Provision the production key/config boundary needed by [FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#87](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/87) so local workers can invoke only an operator-approved signed Agent Waste capability. Both Helios hot mirrors must verify the same request and attestation keys, while private keys remain narrowly scoped and public ingress cannot spoof agent headers.

This child performs and authorizes **no capability `public.app_settings` write**. Creating/revoking/emergency-disabling a grant, consuming a nonce, and executing a valid signed action remain in the separately approved automation rollout task.

## Required implementation

### Key separation and exact formats

- Generate two different Ed25519 keypairs; never reuse the existing readonly key.
- Private values are canonical unpadded base64url raw 32-byte Ed25519 seeds, not PEM/OpenSSH. Public values are canonical unpadded base64url raw 32-byte public keys.
- Stable IDs: request key `amp-local-capability-vps3-2026q3`; attestation key `helios-capability-attestation-2026q3`.
- `HELIOS_AGENT_CAPABILITY_PUBLIC_KEYS_JSON` is exactly the map form `{ "amp-local-capability-vps3-2026q3": "<public-key>" }` on both servers.
- Derive both public keys from encrypted seeds during verification; require each private/public pair to match and the two public keys to differ.

### Least-privilege secret delivery

- Add a shared `hosts/vps/helios-agent-capability.nix` imported by vps-nixos-2 and vps-nixos-3.
- Materialize the request seed only on vps-nixos-3 for `amp-local` at `~/.secret/helios-agent-capability/signing-key`: parent `0700`, resolved generation-backed agenix target `amp-local:agents 0400`. Do not use `symlink = false`; rollback must remove the plaintext target.
- Re-encrypt the same attestation environment-file plaintext separately to each host. It contains only `HELIOS_AGENT_CAPABILITY_ATTESTATION_PRIVATE_KEY=<seed>` and is generation-backed under `/run/agenix`, `root:root 0400`.
- Attach the attestation environment file **only** with `systemd.services.helios-server.serviceConfig.EnvironmentFile = lib.mkAfter [...]`. Do not use `services.helios.environmentFiles` or `extraEnvironment`, which also expose values to worker/prep/provisioner.
- Configure request public-key map, attestation ID, and attestation public key on `helios-server` only. No private value enters Nix store text, repo, browser, response, or logs. Unit scoping is not claimed as isolation from root/same-UID process inspection.

### Public ingress boundary

Extend nginx public-vhost stripping on both mirror and non-mirror branches to all eight capability headers:

- `X-Helios-Agent-Capability-Key-Id`
- `X-Helios-Agent-Capability-Grant-Id`
- `X-Helios-Agent-Capability-Action-Id`
- `X-Helios-Agent-Capability-Timestamp`
- `X-Helios-Agent-Capability-Nonce`
- `X-Helios-Agent-Capability-Idempotency-Key`
- `X-Helios-Agent-Capability-Body-Sha256`
- `X-Helios-Agent-Capability-Signature`

Signed calls originate through loopback/private backend routing, never the public vhost.

## Deployment safety prerequisite

Adding an EnvironmentFile can restart `helios-server` during generic whole-host `self-deploy`; that wrapper does not drain Helios first. Do **not** deploy until either:

1. a separately reviewed canonical whole-host rollout path protects the vps2 and vps3 Nix switches with the Helios mirror invariant; or
2. the operator explicitly approves the bounded error window after receiving its measured impact and rollback.

Do not assume `mss-bounce-vps12` solves this; its known drain-flag survival limitation must be resolved first. Any deploy-tool change is critical infrastructure and needs Oracle design review before implementation plus post-diff approval.

## Verification

- Nix-evaluate both hosts and prove identical public capability config, request secret only on vps3, attestation env `root:root 0400`, and private env absent from worker/prep/provisioner.
- Prove all eight capability headers are stripped on both public-vhost branches.
- On each local backend, send a structurally valid request using the configured key ID but an invalid signature. Require configured-path `401 invalid_signature` audit without printing secrets, reading capability state, or writing a nonce.
- Verify no production DB write occurs in this task.

## Rollback

Before config removal after activation: emergency-disable shared state, verify denial on both mirrors, revoke live grants, then remove config and deploy. If PostgreSQL is unavailable, removing config from both mirrors is acceptable fail-closed containment, but grants are recorded as dormant, not falsely claimed revoked. Verify rollback removes the decrypted request-key target and both attestation env targets; deleting encrypted `.age` files alone is insufficient.

## Gates

- Oracle reviewed this design and required server-only secret wiring, generation-backed cleanup, exact key formats, public header stripping, and the mirror-safe deploy prerequisite above.
- No DB schema/migration.
- Use canonical task-dag, agenix, and `self-deploy*`; never manual service restart or raw `nixos-rebuild`.

# Dev-loop optimization — `task-dag` child epic (broken-master auto-repair)

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#26](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/26).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/designs/ci-broken-master-auto-repair.md`](../../../../designs/ci-broken-master-auto-repair.md)
> and the parent
> [`docs/epics/dev-loop-optimization/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> (§6) in the top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the
> shared CI-driven broken-master auto-repair implementation** that lives
> in `virusdave/task-dag`.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `task-dag@master` that
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#26
> ```
>
> **Re-read the parent design doc before starting** — it is the single
> source of truth; this file is a thin index over it.

## Goal

Provide the reusable, race-safe mechanism that detects a red `master`,
files exactly **one** high-priority repair ticket per red streak ("repair
chain"), and interprets `Tree-Fix` commit trailers so a fix either
reaches green or escalates to a `continue`-mode repair task. All logic
lives once in `virusdave/task-dag` (the single home of task-dag / CI
automation); peer repos call it as a reusable workflow. top-level
coordinates only and does not host repair logic.

## Binding standards (from the parent, do not weaken)

- Two-gate green tree: this is the *final-gate* half made
  self-healing — it must never weaken the required full gate.
- No first-party `any`, no disabled/weakened gates, no `--no-verify`,
  tests deterministic and prod-resource-free (inherited from fleet-green
  [#20](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/20)).
- Trailers parsed with `git interpret-trailers`, never freeform grep.
- Idempotent + stale-run safe: never mutate chain state against a
  superseded SHA (see design §4).

## Scope owned by this repo (`virusdave/task-dag`)

1. **Reusable CI repair classifier workflow** — called after a repo's
   full required suite on `master`; implements the green/red/unknown
   classification and the chain open/update/close logic (design §2).
2. **Commit-trailer parser** for `Tree-Fix` / `Tree-Fix-Chain` /
   `Tree-Fix-Mode` via `git interpret-trailers`.
3. **Chain-state persistence** — a durable per-repo store (e.g. a
   `tasks/ci-chains/<repo>` ref or equivalent) holding the design §1
   fields (`Last-Green`, `First-Red`, `Current-Head`, `State`,
   `Repair-Mode`, `Repair-Issue`, `Repair-Attempt`).
4. **Idempotent repair ticket** creation/update — exactly one
   `ci-broken-master` + `priority:high` ticket per chain, ingested as a
   pickable task by the existing comment/issue sync.
5. **Tree-fix outcome handling** (design §3): green closes the chain +
   ticket; red-in-chain escalates to a `continue`-mode repair task; red
   with a green parent opens a fresh `initial` chain; repeated
   same-signature failures `BLOCK` + page after a small threshold.
6. **Stale-run / race handling** (design §4): per-repo/branch classifier
   concurrency (`cancel-in-progress: false`), ignore superseded SHAs,
   close green only when current.
7. **Worker verifier** helper/CLI — "is my target still the current
   first-red, unclaimed chain head?" — so workers don't hand-implement
   the §6 contract.
8. **Tests/fixtures** for the §4 race cases (out-of-order CI runs,
   continue-mode escalation, new-regression-vs-continuation, green
   closing the right chain).

## Out of scope (deferred / other repos)

- Peer repo CI wiring + branch protection (deferred peer child epics).
- Any change to top-level's pure event-wiring workflows.
- Force-push / non-FF `master` auto-repair (detect → `STALE`/`BLOCKED` +
  page instead).

## Acceptance

From a fresh ephemeral checkout, the implementation:

1. classifies green / red / unknown-parent correctly and opens **one**
   chain per red streak;
2. files exactly **one** high-priority repair ticket per chain;
3. ignores stale older CI runs (no reopen when a newer descendant is
   green);
4. on a failed tree-fix, creates a **continue**-mode repair task (not a
   new first-red task); a green tree-fix closes the chain + ticket;
5. parses `Tree-Fix*` trailers via `git interpret-trailers`, covered by
   tests/fixtures for the design §4 race cases;
6. provides the worker verifier helper used by canon
   [`WORKFLOW.md`](../../../../canon/rules/WORKFLOW.md) "CI-filed
   broken-master repair tasks";
7. Agent Gate Record (two-gate template) attached.


```yaml
{
  "delegated_to": [
    {
      "repo": "peer/repo",
      "issue": 4
    }
  ]
}
```

issues.body:
## Summary

Epic roots (`tasks/pending/<N>`) have **no cross-host claim protection**,
and `breakdown` publishes child frontier leaves without retiring the
root. Together these let the worker fleet run two agents on the same
issue's work even though the per-task-SHA claim invariant holds.
Root-caused from `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites#14`.

Lifecycle facts now documented in [`docs/REF_LIFECYCLE.md`](../blob/master/docs/REF_LIFECYCLE.md).

## The two lifecycle facts

1. **`task-dag claim` is frontier-only.** It renames `tasks/frontier/<short>` -> `tasks/active/<short>` via an atomic `--force-with-lease` CAS. A `tasks/pending/<N>` epic root is not a frontier ref, so `claim` returns `no-frontier` (exit 3). Epic roots are therefore protected **only** by each host's local worker state file, which is not shared across hosts: two different hosts can dispatch the same undecomposed root.
2. **`breakdown` keeps the root.** It publishes child frontier refs but does not delete/move/complete `tasks/pending/<N>` (the pending ref is the durable epic identity used by closure, delegation, and comment-ingest ancestry; see `.github/scripts/create-task-commit.sh`). So immediately after a breakdown the root concept and its new leaves coexist with nothing relating them under one lock.

## Incident (mostly-static-sites #14)

A worker claimed the undecomposed root, ran `breakdown` (creating a leaf), then *also implemented the fix itself*; meanwhile a second worker claimed the freshly-minted leaf and implemented the identical fix. Two distinct SHAs (root + its leaf) for one issue, each correctly single-claimed.

## Proposed design (task-dag owns this half)

Make epic-root orchestration a **first-class, cross-host-claimable** state, OR convert an undecomposed root into a single claimable frontier "decompose this issue" task, so root dispatch/decomposition is protected by the same atomic CAS as leaves. Constraints:
- Must preserve `tasks/pending/<N>` identity (or provide an equivalent) for `close-epic` / `close-completed-issues.sh`, cross-repo delegation, and comment-ingest ancestry.
- No duplicate `breakdown` across hosts.
- A root worker must not be able to keep implementing after child frontier refs exist.

This is a ref-lifecycle redesign, not an opportunistic shell edit; do not change `breakdown` to retire the root without addressing the identity/delegation/closure dependents above.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Root orchestration/decomposition is protected by a cross-host CAS (no two hosts decompose the same issue).
- [ ] No path lets a root worker implement after leaves exist.
- [ ] Pending-root identity for closure/delegation/comment ancestry preserved or explicitly replaced.
- [ ] `docs/REF_LIFECYCLE.md` updated to reflect the new model.

## Companion (host-local half)
`Nicponskis/github-worker#1` covers the same-host mitigation (decompose-only root prompt contract + leaf suppression while a root claim is active).

issues.body:
While the general mode of operation should be first-class, active use of `task-dag` by workers to keep tasks, epics, and commits all connected, at times a worker fails to achieve this or has "gone rogue" or missed instructions related to `task-dag`.  Hopefully this is few & far between nowadays, but it still happens that we discover commits that are relevant to, or should have closed, a pending task.  We should have a first-class-in-tooling way of handling this and linking the existing commit on `master` history to the task-dag task commit, as though it had been done correctly the first time.  This may require an "interstitial no-content commit" on master that is linked to or closes the task-dag task, but also directly links (in commit comments?  metadata?  where?) the historical commit that was the "real" commit in question.  

This is just a speculative approach after 10 seconds of thought; given the _actual_ design of task-dag and the git commit DAG capabilities, work with Oracle to extend the design to cover this "oops, have to link a historical commit to a task as though it were being done live right now at commit time, but without rewriting `master` history back to that commit (or even rewriting it significantly _at all_, which tends to break task-dag linkages unintentionally).

We'll for sure want to complain LOUDLY when this functionality is used that it is ONLY intended for historically missed commits, and should NOT be the way development is done moving forward; that should all be live with live uses of the `task-dag` tool as appropriate.

Finally, use `page-dave` at priority 2 to report any cases where we're using this new functionality to link historic commits.  The page should include sufficient but succinct context for a zero-context operator to understand, as well as relevant links to the github epics, issues, task-dag tasks, and commits in question.

Ask immediate followup questions in a thread comment if this is unclear, otherwise immediately implement and `page-dave` at priority 4 when this is deployed or ready for deploy, and what I'll need to do to make it available to our running workers, if anything.

issues.body:
## Design gap: no sanctioned way to close a single-repo, ops-only epic (no code commit to link)

### Summary

task-dag has **no first-class, invariant-preserving command** to close an
epic whose resolution is a real-world **operations action** — one that
produces **no implementation commit to link** and has **no cross-repo
delegated children**. Today the only way to emit the required
`Closes-Epic: #N` closure signal for such an epic is a **hand-authored
merge commit** (manual git/ref surgery), which canon's task-dag STOP
banner and `docs/INVARIANTS.md` explicitly forbid agents from doing.

This is a real, recurring pattern: **"operator-go" / ops epics** (reboot a
host, flip a manual switch, run a one-off maintenance action). The action
is performed and verified out-of-band (often read-only verification), and
then the epic simply needs to be *closed* — there is nothing to commit.

### Concrete trigger

`virusdave/top-level#37` — *"Operator go needed: reboot vps3 (prod
Helios)"*. The reboot was executed as an ops action; the reboot leaf was
`drop`ped (no commit to link); post-reboot health was verified read-only
from a vps3-local session. All that remained was to **close the epic**,
and no sanctioned tool could do it:

- `task-dag complete <root-sha>` — requires a **real implementation
  commit** distinct from (and not equal to) the task commit; it rejects
  empty/tombstone links. There is no implementation commit for an ops
  action, so `complete` cannot express this.
- `task-dag close-epic --issue 37` — fails with
  `close-epic: epic 37 has no delegated children to gate close on`. Its
  closure gating is built entirely around **cross-repo delegated
  children**; a single-repo epic with none is unsupported.
- The remaining documented path (`docs/task_dag/EPIC_CLOSURE.md` →
  "Manual fallback": hand-craft the `Closes-Epic:` merge) is exactly the
  manual commit/ref surgery agents are forbidden to perform.

Net effect: an ops-only epic-root is **un-closeable by an agent through
sanctioned tooling** and gets stuck open.

### What's needed

A sanctioned, invariant-preserving way to close a **single-repo,
ops-only / no-code epic** — either a new subcommand (e.g.
`task-dag close-ops-epic <issue>`) or an explicit mode of the existing
`close-epic` (e.g. `close-epic --issue N --no-children` / `--ops`) that:

1. Produces the **same closure signal the tooling already relies on**: a
   tree-equal merge on `master` whose non-primary parent is the epic's
   `refs/heads/tasks/pending/<N>` commit and whose message carries the
   `Closes-Epic: #<N>` trailer — constructed **by the tool**, so all
   task-dag invariants (empty-tree/known-namespace, parent shape, etc.)
   are enforced, not hand-rolled. The worker's `git push origin
   HEAD:master` then lets `close-completed-issues.yml` close the issue
   and clean up `tasks/pending/<N>` + any blocked/frontier overlay refs.
2. **Guards against premature/abusive closure** so this can't become a
   footgun equivalent to closing an in-progress epic: refuse if the epic
   has child tasks (decomposed) or any live frontier/blocked leaves;
   confirm the pending-root identity on origin (fail closed when origin
   is unreachable, mirroring `complete`'s root guard); require explicit
   confirmation for a non-TTY caller.
3. Is **idempotent** and race/stale-tip safe, consistent with the
   existing `close-epic` idempotency semantics
   (`docs/task_dag/EPIC_CLOSURE.md`).
4. Updates docs: `docs/task_dag/EPIC_CLOSURE.md` and any relevant canon
   pointers in `virusdave/top-level` (`docs/canon/rules/WORKFLOW.md`)
   describing the ops-epic closure path and when to use it vs.
   `complete` / `close-epic`.
5. Has **tests** (this repo's `tests/` + `cli-tests.yml`) covering the
   happy path and the guard rails (decomposed root refused, live-leaf
   refused, origin-unreachable fail-closed, idempotent re-run).

Note: do **not** bake an operator-paging feature into the tooling for
this — see the completion instruction below; paging here is a one-off
agent action, not a new tool capability.

### On completion — page the operator at p4

When this epic is complete (tooling landed on `master`, tests green,
docs updated), **page the operator**:

```sh
page-dave -p 4 --title "task-dag: ops-epic close support landed" \
  --click "<this issue url>" \
  "Single-repo/ops-only epic closure is now supported via sanctioned tooling. top-level#37 can now be closed with the standard command."
```

so they know they can have `virusdave/top-level#37` closed via the new
standard command (no manual surgery).

### References

- Trigger: `virusdave/top-level#37`
- `docs/task_dag/EPIC_CLOSURE.md` (closure gates + manual fallback)
- `docs/INVARIANTS.md` (why hand-rolled task/ref surgery is forbidden)
- `.github/scripts/close-completed-issues.sh` (the consumer of the
  `Closes-Epic:` + structural-parent signal)


---

### ⚠️ Required commit trailer — this epic is a blocking dependency of `virusdave/top-level#37`

`virusdave/top-level#37` (reboot vps3 — the ops epic that surfaced this
gap) has been **delegated to this issue** (`task-dag delegate --issue 37
--to virusdave/task-dag#5`). Its reboot is done and health-verified; #37
stays open *only* because no sanctioned tool can close a single-repo ops
epic — which is exactly what this issue fixes.

So the **landing commit** for this fix (the one that completes/closes
this epic on `master`) **MUST carry the trailer**:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#37
```

With that trailer, the standard cross-repo machinery
(`aggregate-cross-repo-completions` → top-level `comment-sync` →
`ingest-comment` → auto `close-epic`) will **automatically close
top-level#37** using the new sanctioned tooling — no manual git/ref
surgery, and it doubles as the end-to-end validation of the fix. Without
the trailer, #37 stays parked (downstream-blocked) forever.


```yaml
delegated_to:
  - repo: virusdave/top-level
    issue: 38
    note: top-level docs half of task-dag#5 (EPIC_CLOSURE.md + canon WORKFLOW.md); WORKFLOW.md is canon-gated
```
