# task-dag child epic: durable comment reconciliation

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#64`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/64)
· Binding design:
[`durable-dispatch-input-recovery.md`](../../../../designs/durable-dispatch-input-recovery.md)

## Goal

Make GitHub issue-comment delivery at-least-once and idempotent. The existing
event workflow remains fast, but a canonical reconciler can recover any
eligible comment still present in GitHub even when that event or workflow was
lost.

## Required implementation

1. **Receipt contract and compatibility**
   - Define well-formed human, completion, and machine-skip provenance under
     `gh/comments/<issue>/<comment-id>`.
   - New receipts identify repository, issue, comment ID, disposition,
     `created_at`, observed `updated_at`, and body SHA-256.
   - Accept existing human/completion provenance as immutable legacy shapes.
   - Update known-namespace validation, lifecycle documentation, and golden
     fixtures in the same change.

2. **Origin-authoritative atomic ingestion**
   - Check origin receipt before classifying current content; an unpushed local
     ref is never terminal.
   - Human comments atomically create receipt plus frontier with create-only
     leases. Completion comments atomically create receipt plus completion
     fact when needed. Marked comments create receipt only.
   - Install local refs only after remote success.
   - On races, validate the origin winner. Same observed body with a different
     disposition is fatal; a different observed version is superseded by the
     first valid winner.
   - A failed multi-ref transaction cannot leave half a disposition.

3. **Canonical `reconcile-comments` command**
   - Use the same classifier as event ingestion.
   - Support recent overlapping and complete-audit modes, dry-run, bounded
     apply batches, `ingestion_start_at`, and explicit historical
     `(issue, comment-id)` allowlists.
   - Enumerate with stable ascending updated order and full pagination; filter
     by `created_at`; exclude pull requests from authoritative issue metadata.
   - Fetch allowlisted historical comments directly by ID.
   - First successfully observed version wins; later edits do not remint.
   - Continue past poison comments but return nonzero and a failed heartbeat.
   - Honor rate-limit headers and never claim completeness after truncation or
     an API/classification failure.
   - Run idempotent post-scan convergence so a completion fact whose immediate
     close attempt failed still reaches the existing backstop.

4. **Coherent event runtime**
   - Replace split raw-file downloads with one checkout at one resolved
     task-dag revision. Keep the reusable workflow logic-free for callers.
   - Preserve the current App-token close semantics and least permissions.

5. **Metrics and operator contract**
   - Emit requests/pages/all returned comments, eligibility and disposition
     counts, failures, duration, rate-limit state, and recent/full success
     heartbeat data in machine-readable output.
   - A capacity ceiling fails loudly and directs sharding; it never truncates
     silently.

## Required tests

- Event versus sweep race yields one provenance and one task effect.
- Injected push failure yields neither half of a human disposition.
- Race loser ignores local-only state, validates a matching origin winner,
  rejects conflicting same-version disposition, and accepts a superseding
  different observed version.
- Marked comment creates one skip receipt and no frontier.
- Completion receipt/fact is atomic; failed derived close is later converged.
- Multi-page scans with equal timestamps and strict-`since` overlap omit
  nothing; page failure does not mark success.
- Pull-request and pre-boundary comments are excluded; explicit historical
  allowlist comments are fetched directly.
- Edits, malformed comments, legacy provenance, 403/429, dry-run, bounded
  batches, and capacity ceilings follow the binding design.
- `task-dag validate --strict` and the full task-dag presubmit pass.

## Rollout and rollback

Land receipt/atomicity support before any watchdog can emit new shapes. Verify
the event path recognizes both legacy and new receipts. Publish the reconciler
disabled until github-worker dry-runs each repository's first audit.

Rollback removes or disables the reconciler/event-runtime change without
rewriting refs. Valid additive receipts remain recognized audit evidence.

This is critical infrastructure. Obtain Oracle design review before coding and
Oracle diff review after implementation; iterate to APPROVE before commit.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#64
```
issues.creator: helios-freshly-baked[bot]
issues.title: Make GitHub comment delivery durable and idempotent

# task-dag child epic: durable broken-master convergence

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Make the existing repair-chain state machine converge from durable GitHub
evidence even when a push-triggered Actions run is missed, duplicated, or dies
between side effects. Keep task-dag's chain ref authoritative and converge to
exactly one open repair issue and one discoverable repair task for each active
policy-red streak.

## Required implementation

1. **One canonical reconciler**
   - Add `repair-reconcile <owner/repo> <branch>` as the bounded entry point
     shared by Actions hints and the host backstop.
   - Reuse and extend `classify`, `tree-fix-outcome`, `verify-target`, repair
     chains, and `repair-ticket`; do not add another classifier or state store.
   - Resolve the current top-level registry generation internally before every
     mutation. Implement strict `off|observe|enforce` semantics and fenced
     downgrade cleanup exactly as specified by the binding design.

2. **Strict evidence and policy**
   - Validate `.github/ci-repair-policy.json`, bind required checks to exact
     names and App identities, paginate check runs, and select reruns by the
     design's deterministic lifecycle tuple.
   - Persist canonical bounded evidence, first-seen grace state, policy digest,
     evidence/decision keys, aggregate, and reconciliation diagnostics in the
     existing chain history. Identical decisions are no-ops.
   - Only current-head required-check evidence may close a chain. Unknown,
     malformed policy, API failure, stale green, and identity mismatch fail
     closed.

3. **Lease, fencing, and convergence**
   - Add metadata-only reconciliation lease acquisition/renewal that preserves
     every classifier field and uses monotonically increasing fences.
   - Fence every issue, comment, task-ingestion, and scheduling-ref mutation;
     perform post-mutation readback and compensate stale accepted HTTP effects.
   - Keep the oldest matching repair issue canonical, close extras, retire all
     duplicate scheduling projections through a repair-specific validated
     operation, and retain the specified non-scheduling audit ref.
   - Make issue and continuation-comment ingestion directly replayable by
     reconciliation, with stable repair/attempt identities and existing
     `verify-target` protection for already-launched workers.
   - Preserve one blocked high-priority repair object for `blocked`,
     `policy-invalid`, and `non-fast-forward`; only authoritative green closes
     it.

4. **Contracts and telemetry**
   - Update chain parsers, namespace validation, invariant documentation,
     golden fixtures, CLI help, dry-run output, and migration compatibility for
     old `creating@…` leases.
   - Emit the bounded structured pass fields and error codes required by the
     design. Never log tokens, check output, issue bodies, or one-off content.

## Deterministic tests

Use temporary bare origins and a fake paginated GitHub API. Cover missing and
delayed runs around grace, accepted/failed checks and reruns, duplicate names,
pagination, GitHub `Date` clock-skew rejection, old-head green/red, policy edits
and malformed policy, API outage, registry rollback, and rejection of
caller-supplied generation or mode. Cover `observe→enforce` replay of an
existing decision and `enforce→observe|off` races with stale callers, late
accepted HTTP effects, and refusal to delete or retarget a registry row until
successful `off` cleanup readback. Exercise every lease-loss and interruption
boundary, expired-holder overlap, transient zero-object windows, missed
issue/comment events, duplicate issue/task convergence, blocked-chain
preservation, continuation deduplication, tree-fix outcomes, and non-fast-
forward heads. Add a property test over event order, stale holders, and crash
points proving eventual one-chain/one-open-ticket/one-discoverable-task
convergence. Run `task-dag validate --strict` and full task-dag presubmit.

## Rollout and rollback

Land inert. Complete credential preflight and a 24-hour dry-run comparison
before any projection is enabled. Then support observe-only chain writes,
followed by projection for task-dag and top-level, missed-run/crash drills, and
48 hours of stable evidence before peer expansion.

Rollback disables callers first and preserves chain refs/issues. Never run an
old `repair-ticket` against a new active substate. Any downgrade to legacy
requires the binding design's compare-and-set migration and readback; never
delete coordination refs or tickets as rollback.

This is critical fleet infrastructure. The binding architecture already has
Oracle approval, but the implementation worker must get Oracle architecture
rereview for any design change and Oracle review of the actual final diff
before commit. Iterate to APPROVE.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```

issues.title: Make broken-master repair converge durably and exactly once

issues.body:
## Problem

Task-dag agent instructions should explicitly cover an observed tooling gap: one clearly canonical thing should be created or done, especially when the operation is semantically effectful.

If an agent cannot find an appropriate task-dag command, tooling, or implementation and is about to craft the semantic operation by hand—especially with git commands, but by any means—it must **STOP** rather than improvise. It must invoke `page-dave` at **p4**.

The page must include concise details and a link to a durable, full-context record. That durable record must explain:

- the full context;
- what the expected canonical command or implementation should do;
- where the agent searched; and
- the proposed canonical implementation.

This requirement is intended to prevent semantically meaningful one-off implementations and hand-authored task-dag state.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add the requirement to the early/minimal task-dag agent instructions so agents encounter the stop-and-page rule before attempting manual semantic operations.
- Add the full procedure and durable-record requirements to the detailed canonical documentation.
- Keep the wording and behavior consistent with existing guidance that an unsupported operation is a tooling gap, not an invitation to improvise.
- Add or update tests and prompt-budget checks where applicable.
- Explicitly cover hand-crafted git operations and any other means of creating semantically meaningful one-off implementations or hand-authored task-dag state.

issues.body:
# Restore one safe task authority after Incident 67

[Top-level Incident 67](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/67) found that task completion, cross-repository child closure, and child-epic creation still have competing implementations. Those conflicts prematurely closed work, exposed dependent tasks before prerequisites were complete, and can duplicate a GitHub issue after an uncertain API response.

This issue owns the implementation and task completion in [`virusdave/task-dag`](https://github.com/virusdave/task-dag); the top-level repository remains the incident coordinator. The coordinating task is [canonical task ID `cf9c151a3059021136e664be2538aca95d52186d`, “Materialise the canonical task-dag semantic migration”](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/67). The binding design is [the `task-dag-incident-67-migration.md` design pinned to `virusdave/top-level` commit `c252e0a7fe654e09dfae85718cac31d0765df451`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/c252e0a7fe654e09dfae85718cac31d0765df451/docs/designs/task-dag-incident-67-migration.md).

The operator authorized one worker to resolve the incident prerequisites sequentially before parallel work resumes. That authorization is recorded in the [Amp incident thread](https://ampcode.com/threads/T-019f6fa9-95c4-7044-9418-c9ab5ea66b46). It permits this one bootstrap issue creation. Production activation, producer enablement, migration writes, rollout, and adoption or deduplication of ambiguous historical issues still require their separate gates.

This bootstrap is necessary because `task-dag` cannot yet create this cross-repository child through its canonical materialisation flow. Normal GitHub-issue ingestion must create the canonical task root from this issue. Do not manually construct a task reference, task-state marker, delegation, semantic commit, or task-state trailer.

The issue must have the `blocked-at-birth` label when first observed, so no implementation becomes runnable before the canonical dependency is recorded.

**Bootstrap operation ID, used only to identify this issue-create attempt:** `a591034e-6b46-4a75-bb34-77fdc280c04e`

This value must never be edited or reused. It is the sole identity for recovery after an uncertain create result:

1. Make exactly one GitHub issue-create request.
2. If GitHub returns a parseable issue URL, reread that issue and verify the repository, exact operation ID, exact title and body, and `blocked-at-birth` label.
3. If the request times out, exits unsuccessfully, or returns an unparseable result, do not retry it. Fully paginate both open and closed issues and match the exact operation ID.
   - Exactly one match: adopt that issue.
   - No matches: block and stop because the original request may still commit later.
   - Multiple matches: fail closed and require explicit deduplication and adoption review.
4. Never identify the result from title or body similarity without the exact operation ID.

After conclusive verification, wait for normal ingestion to expose this exact issue as a blocked task root. Then record the cross-repository dependency through the canonical task writer, decompose this epic into the dependent leaves below, and atomically claim the first safe child.

In the sections below, **materialisation** means converting a declared child task into canonical state and, when required, a GitHub issue. A **producer** requests that work; the **reconciler** is the sole process allowed to create the issue; a **consumer** reads task state. **Origin** is the authoritative remote Git repository. The active **migration epoch** and its fence token identify which writers are currently authorized. **Delegated-child closure** means accepting a parent as complete only after its delegated child has verified completion evidence. The **census** is the complete inventory of historical task state and every live reader and writer.

## Required invariants

- One canonical facts layer decides completion, readiness, dependency satisfaction, delegated-child closure, and epic closure.
- Reachability and ordinary implementation commits are not completion facts.
- A materialisation request has immutable payload identity. A whole batch reserves atomically before any external effect.
- Exactly one reconciler may create a GitHub issue. An uncertain issue-create result is never retried; recovery adopts exactly one proven match or fails closed.
- Origin is coordination authority. Every writer is fenced by the active migration epoch and refuses stale or uncertain authority.
- Producers remain disabled until activation, complete census, migration, consumer cutover, and an explicit producer-enable record are verified in order.
- Legacy writers are drained, then removed or replaced by effect-free rejection stubs. The retired trailer workflow must never be used as a fallback.

## Implementation sequence

Decompose this epic into dependent, reviewable leaves and atomically claim the first safe child:

1. Add an effect-free guard that rejects retired task-state metadata, controls that stop and drain legacy state writers, and a compatibility reader that can read legacy and canonical state without writing either.
2. Make one strict completion and readiness model authoritative. Accept delegated-child closure only from verified completion evidence, with property-based and adversarial tests.
3. Add immutable materialisation state plus strict whole-batch and one-child commands. Keep them default-deny and externally effect-free, with state-machine, concurrency, validator, and fixed expected-output tests.
4. Add activation records and reject writers whose migration epoch or fence token is stale.
5. Complete the historical-state inventory, migration and import, audited adoption and rearming, and dry-run evidence.
6. Switch every live task-state reader to the canonical facts and record an attestation for each reader.
7. Enable request producers only after an explicit enable record, and make the reconciler the sole issue-writing path.
8. Roll out a watchdog that detects and safely recovers missing worker comments, reject or remove legacy paths, run recovery drills, verify rollback and stability, and obtain integrated Oracle critical-infrastructure approval.

Each leaf ships its own tests and receives Oracle critical-infrastructure design and final-diff review. No production activation, producer enablement, ambiguous historical-issue adoption, migration write, or rollout occurs without its separate required gate.

## Completion criteria

- All production callers use one completion/readiness and delegated-child closure implementation.
- Canonical materialisation commands enforce immutable declarations, whole-batch reservation, fenced recovery, and a sole external issue creator.
- The historical census and migration complete without false child satisfaction or duplicate issue creation.
- Legacy decision paths are incapable of effects.
- Deterministic adversarial tests cover stale writers, crashes, races, uncertain API results, recovery, rollback, and generated interleavings.
- Production drills prove that recovery from a missing or suppressed worker comment occurs exactly once, an exclusive-work lease can be taken over safely after its previous owner fails, restart recovery is correct and bounded, rollback works, and operation remains stable.
- An [integrated Oracle critical-infrastructure review](https://ampcode.com/threads/T-019f6fa9-95c4-7044-9418-c9ab5ea66b46) approves the deployed semantics, concurrency, recovery, and idempotency evidence.

Rollback disables and drains producers, advances or disables the active epoch through the same fenced command, and retains additive receipts, intents, and verified completion evidence. It never rewrites published history or retries an uncertain external effect.

## Follow-up scope

After the incident and the planned task-dag source/test refactor, add the broader property-oriented coverage requested during Oracle review of the canonical consumer cutover (as well as create an operator-blocked followup task for better adversarial coverage and hardening)

Cover deterministic interleavings and failure injection beyond the minimum incident proof, including semantic-generation movement around graph/master/block/claim/reap publication, ambiguous accepted push readback, disabled epochs, activation disappearance, all completion variants, exact close/completion shapes, stale blocked/incomplete closure, and crash/retry convergence.

## Sequencing

This work is intentionally **operator-blocked** until the operator identifies the forthcoming testing/refactor task that it should depend on or follow. Do not implement or dispatch it before that dependency is recorded and the operator unblocks it.

## Completion criteria

- Tests assert stable semantic invariants and observable outcomes, not implementation call order.
- Property/failure-injection coverage minimizes implementation coupling.
- Full-suite wall-clock constraints and planned test-group splitting are respected.
- Oracle's non-incident-blocking enhanced test requests are traceably covered or explicitly dispositioned.


It is the operator's decision that we will migrate this critical infrastructure AWAY from massive bash scripts.  Thus, I want a project roughly sequenced as follows:
- Massively speed up all-tests (repeatedly split groups until each group is <20s wallclock; any just-before-commit-and-push runs of all-test that tattle about taking too long for the group should be noted in the commit message, referencing the specific testing group and wallclock execution time, so long as the prior three commits don't _also_ reference a nonempty set of groups.  If THAT happens, then immediately pause and possibly stash your current task and go into "test trimming" mode; splitting the offending group repeatedly until each group is under 20s wallclock time (we want a bit of room to "grow" or increase execution time naturally before hitting the 30s reporting-in-the-commit threshold for each subgroup.  If repeated splitting of the group results in a group "shard" of a single test which cannot be made to complete in 20s wallclock in isolation, the we'll live with it for the moment, but create an operator-blocked GH issue to decide what to do about the test, and page-dave with a one-offs line that gives sufficient detail to a contextless reviewer: what is the test trying to enforce, invariants-wise or assertions-wise, and how "spammy" has the test been?  Is it morally more of a "test implementation stability" test, or does it actually, usefully, with high signal-to-noise, low flakiness, and clear & details information on failure sufficient to understand the problem and point towards its cause.  If the latter, then great!  If the former, note this in the review and we'll likely drop it or replace with something else.
- This repo's test invocation process needs to be canonicalized with a single launcher (perhaps companion to the run-all script) which accepts the subset of tests to run, but like run-all, aggressively parallelizes the small sub-groups post-splitting, acually DOING group splitting and reordering as needed when repeated consecutive observations of bad test characteristics keep occurring and being documented in the prior 3-4 commits.  We should have exactly one "run these tests in parallel' implementation, which is used both for 'all tests' and 'these specific tests'.  Repo docs and manual invocations of individual test files should LOUDLY shout to stderr that these kinds of invocations are dispreferred, and instead most use cases should just use the canonical "run these" or "run all" test runners rather than trying to figure out the best way to run them themselves, this way they'll get implemented speedups, efficiency, parallelism, etc that an self-invoking agent will miss others when invoking by hand.
- Split the almost 10kloc `task-dag` script.  Identify logically bound, mutually entangled or dependent, or functionally atomic concepts and their associated implementations, and migrate those into separate files.  Compose all of the files' implementations together in the now-small `task-dag` script to produce the final canonical script implementation.
- Operator has decided that we will migrate to Rust (tooling managed via nix for development and builds) for the task-dag tool.  Learn online how a *modern*, likely flake-based development environment for rust should be created and used, and how to interact with the build tooling within the development shell.  Document this clearly.  Be careful, lots of old, legacy nix documentation and seemingly-related forum posts is terribly out of date and tends to lead one astray rather than to the modern, simple way to achieve your goal.  ensure you are following _modern_ nix-rust conventions and approach and configuration.
- I would like to start by consuming the existing tests, replacing most of them with property-based testing and invariants-for-any-possible-correct-implementation, preconditions, postconditions, semantic validity, edge cases, etc.  Use a standard Rust library (perhaps Quickcheck?) for this purpose, and this testing style should be the default in this repo (and probably in _most_ repos, but don't make this canon quite yet).  I have no idea of the maturity of rust development via nix (i *think* it's in decent shape) but we're just dealing with a single or very small number of CLI tools and various associated tests, so we should be able to make it work.  Don't mutate system state imperatively EVER to install build or language tooling, even if that's the "default, preferred" way said tooling likes to operate.  This is disallowed, and we'll follow the nix philosophy and approach instead.  Ensure that each partial step along the way of "eating the task-dag elephant" (metaphorically) still results in a valid state with fully usable and correct tooling, that won't trip up agents trying to use it, and hides the Rust<-->Bash "seam" quite well to minimize agent worker problems during transition.  Ensure each transitional step is well-documented in the GH issue so the operator can understand, and ensure each such transitional step has an associated impl or ops task, as required.  Track carefully.
- Once fully deployed and all remnants of the BASH implementation are gone, page-dave at p4 to let him know this is complete.
- Once all implementation has been consumed and replaced by Rust implementations
- Once all tests have been consumed and replaced by Rust tests, we'll next start replacing implementation pieces of BASH language with strongly typed yet simple Rust
- Once all BASH language portions of implementation are completely gone, and the only remaining canonical tooling and implementation is our Rust implementation, page me at p4 again.  Otherwise, iterate through these tasks, not stopping after each commit&push until the entire project is done.  Page me with progress at each push.  Realize that "done" includes both "implementation replaced" and "operations work to safely deploy, if any, has been performed (safely) and verified"; these are valid tasks / required steps for this (and basically all) functionality enhancement or extended iterative refactoring and replacement projects like this one.

The final Rust tool should be more or less functionally identical to the bash script being replaced, at least initially.  if we discover important or desirable enhancements while migrating to rust, the generally-preferred approach would be to file a followup ticket (post-migration, or potentially in parallel when other workers have moved to elsewhere in the repo).

However, there is some _additional_ requirements i am imposing on rust CLI tools.
1) Chose a *single* "cli tool" approach and supporting libraries, for instance for command line parsing.  All of our canonical tooling should "feel" the same, not a mismatched pile of whichever parsing utility the worker happened to reach for in the moment.  parsing isn't the only place this will apply.  We strongly prefer single, canonical, reusable/composable implementations
2) Both the base raw tool invocation (with no commands or subcommands), as when invoked with a command, or potentially even a subcommand, depending on choices for (1), every command and subcommand (as well as no-command root invocation) *MUST* support a --help flag which provides usage and invocation information, docs or design pointers, and critically MAKES NO EFFECT, even if the command or subcommand or direct invocation _normally_ would have had an observable effect or state change.  A `--help` flag, at any valid flag position, must ALWAYS make the invocation safe and side-effect-free.

## Incident blocker

The canonical apply-mode `reconcile-comments --mode recent` sweep ingests missing receipts successfully, then re-runs delegated-close convergence for every issue carrying a completion comment. It currently attempts convergence even when GitHub reports that issue as already closed and its live `tasks/pending/<N>` scheduling root has therefore been canonically retired.

Observed production evidence on 2026-07-18 EDT:

- `virusdave/task-dag`: one convergence failure after one successful receipt application.
- `virusdave/top-level`: 27 convergence failures.
- The failures correlate with closed issues whose durable `gh/issues/<N>` identity remains but whose `tasks/pending/<N>` ref is correctly absent after closure.
- Fleet result is marked failed, preventing both comment-watchdog success watermarks and Incident 67 closure.

## Required semantics

Make closed-issue reconciliation idempotent: missing comment receipts may still be classified/receipted as required, but an issue whose authoritative GitHub issue metadata says `state == closed` must not be enqueued for epic-close convergence. An already-closed issue is not a convergence failure and its retired pending ref must not be recreated.

Keep the change minimal. Add focused fixture coverage proving a completion comment on a closed issue can be receipted without attempting close convergence or requiring a live pending root. Preserve open-issue convergence behavior.

## Closure

Targeted reconciliation tests and shell checks pass; Oracle reviews the incident-critical semantic delta; publish the managed runtime; then a live apply watchdog sweep records successful recent and complete watermarks.

issues.body:
# Outcome

Make `task-dag publish` recover automatically when another task-dag writer advances the shared semantic generation while a completion is being published.

The semantic generation is the activation-authority Git ref used as a compare-and-swap (CAS) fence. It prevents a completion validated against old task state from publishing after that state changes.

Preserve the existing fail-closed guarantee: the completion and semantic generation publish atomically, or neither publishes. When recovery is unsafe or cannot be proven, stop with diagnostics that state what is known, what remains unknown, and the worker’s safe next step.

# Incident

While publishing [FreshlyBakedNYC/automation issue 79, “Build the operator vendor management page”](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/79), canonical `task-dag complete` created a local completion candidate and `task-dag publish` returned:

> canonical completion publication lost its semantic-generation fence; re-prepare and retry

Remote `master` remained unchanged. No task metadata, task refs, or issue markers were hand-crafted.

The publication was recovered by removing only the unpublished completion merge, rerunning `complete`, and publishing again. That recreation worked, but it was not required merely because the semantic generation changed: the original immutable candidate could have been safely revalidated by `task-dag publish <candidate-commit>`.

- [Full incident record and recovery evidence](https://ampcode.com/threads/T-019f7803-d9fd-7328-8bd6-338c8110bac0)
- [Recovered completion commit](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/commit/7201ec223fedd9a531faceccda3b6b7bd864956b)

# Confirmed defect

The fence behaved correctly. The defect is in liveness, outcome classification, diagnostics, and recovery.

Current implementation:

- [`cmd_publish`](https://github.com/virusdave/task-dag/blob/f6b220b7e13110faf866456ade8973ffaf888e89/scripts/task-dag#L8269-L8335) reports every nonzero fenced-push result as a lost semantic-generation fence.
- [`taskdag_activation_fenced_multi_push`](https://github.com/virusdave/task-dag/blob/f6b220b7e13110faf866456ade8973ffaf888e89/scripts/task-dag.d/activation.sh#L299-L365) uses exit code 3 for authority contention, target-lease loss, unavailable readback, malformed or unprovable authority, and other fail-closed outcomes.
- The fenced-push layer suppresses the push response and does not return the evidence needed by its caller to distinguish those outcomes.
- “Re-prepare” incorrectly suggests rerunning `complete`, although `publish <candidate-commit>` resolves a fresh snapshot and revalidates the candidate before any retry.
- Existing tests cover successful and idempotent completion publication, but not a completion publisher losing an ordinary generation race.

# Safety contract

The implementation must preserve all of these invariants:

1. Resolve one immutable completion candidate Git commit ID at invocation start. Never silently replace it during that invocation.
2. Every publication attempt must obtain a fresh coherent consumer snapshot and an activation token bound to the same authority generation.
3. Every attempt must revalidate:
   - exact canonical completion or close shape;
   - current `master` ancestry;
   - task requirements;
   - materialisation and close authority, when applicable;
   - activation compatibility.
4. Publish `master` and the semantic-generation authority in one leased atomic push.
5. Never refresh only the authority lease, skip semantic validation, or publish after unavailable, malformed, or internally inconsistent readback.
6. Keep the pre-activation legacy publication path behaviorally unchanged.
7. Preserve current behavior for every other fenced-push caller unless that caller is explicitly migrated and tested.

# Required implementation

## 1. Introduce a structured fenced-push outcome

Retain raw push status, push diagnostics, and one coherent post-push advertisement. Distinguish at least:

- `applied`: the requested target state is authoritatively proven, including an accepted push whose response was lost;
- `authority-contention`: requested targets remain at their leased values while a valid authority generation advanced;
- `target-changed`: at least one requested target changed to an incompatible value;
- `rejected-no-effect`: coherent readback proves targets and authority unchanged, but the push failed for a non-contention reason;
- `indeterminate`: coherent valid readback is unavailable, malformed, or insufficient to prove an outcome.

Do not classify outcomes solely by matching Git error text. Preserve numeric compatibility for existing callers until each caller deliberately consumes the structured contract.

For completion publication, apply domain-specific classification after fresh readback:

- if the candidate is equal to or reachable from current `master`, publication is successful;
- if `master` is unchanged and only authority advanced, retryable contention occurred;
- if `master` advanced without containing the candidate, the candidate is stale;
- if current requirements or close authority reject the candidate, stop safely;
- if the remote state cannot be proven, return an indeterminate hard failure.

## 2. Add bounded whole-publication retry

Retry only classified authority contention.

Each retry must restart from fresh consumer preparation and rerun every validation in the safety contract. It must continue using the original candidate commit.

Reuse the existing canonical CAS attempt budget and jittered backoff helpers in [`edges-write.sh`](https://github.com/virusdave/task-dag/blob/f6b220b7e13110faf866456ade8973ffaf888e89/scripts/task-dag.d/edges-write.sh#L45-L90). Extract them into a shared owner if necessary; do not create a second retry policy.

## 3. Make recovery diagnostics classification-specific

On exhaustion or failure, report:

- candidate commit ID;
- attempt count;
- classification;
- before and after `master` tips;
- before and after authority tips;
- unavailable values explicitly as unknown;
- retained push/readback diagnostic evidence.

Give the safe next step for that classification:

- contention exhaustion, confirmed no-effect failure, or indeterminate outcome: preserve the candidate and print `task-dag publish <candidate-commit>`;
- stale `master`: state that this candidate cannot publish and that the implementation must be rebased and a new completion candidate created;
- changed semantic requirements or close authority: identify the failed validation and do not imply that recreation alone will fix it;
- accepted or already-present candidate: report success.

Do not tell the worker to rerun `complete` unless fresh validation has proven the existing candidate stale or structurally unusable.

## 4. Add deterministic adversarial coverage

Use isolated bare Git remotes and deterministic hooks or shims. Tests must not depend on timing, external networks, or production resources.

Cover:

1. Generation-only contention: authority advances without moving `master`; one `publish` invocation revalidates and publishes the original candidate.
2. Contention that invalidates task requirements: retry refuses the candidate and leaves `master` unchanged.
3. Accepted push with lost response: authoritative readback reports success without a second publication.
4. Accepted push followed by an unrelated authority successor before readback: candidate reachability from `master` still reports success.
5. Unavailable or malformed readback: fail indeterminately without claiming contention.
6. Confirmed no-effect transport, authentication, or hook failure: do not classify or retry it as contention.
7. Repeated authority contention: exhaust the shared bounded retry budget with zero test backoff and report the preserved candidate.
8. Competing completion candidates from one base: one may win; the loser must never rewind or replace the winner.

Every failure fixture must assert that `master` and authority either moved together or both retained their prior state.

Add focused contract tests for every structured outcome and retain regression coverage for all existing fenced-push callers.

## 5. Update operator and worker guidance

Update:

- `task-dag publish --help`;
- completion publication and recovery documentation;
- migration or invariant documentation that describes the publication fence;
- any message that still says only “re-prepare and retry.”

Document that `task-dag publish <candidate-commit>` always performs fresh validation and is therefore safe to retry, but may correctly refuse a stale or semantically invalid candidate.

# Planned decomposition

1. **Structured outcome contract:** add the backward-compatible fenced-push result contract, evidence retention, and focused contract tests. Do not change caller behavior yet.
2. **Completion retry:** migrate `cmd_publish`, add bounded whole-publication retry, and land direct tests for successful contention recovery and semantic invalidation in the same leaf.
3. **Adversarial publication matrix:** add the remaining response-loss, successor, indeterminate, no-effect, exhaustion, competing-candidate, and atomicity fixtures. Do not change the approved contract without another critical-infrastructure design review.
4. **Guidance and release verification:** update help and documentation, run the full repository presubmit, verify existing callers and the legacy path, publish canonically, and confirm exact-commit post-push CI.

Each leaf must keep the repository green and be completed and published canonically before the next leaf begins.

# Closure criteria

- Ordinary authority-only contention completes within one `task-dag publish` invocation using the original candidate commit.
- No retry bypasses candidate, ancestry, requirements, materialisation, close-authority, or activation validation.
- Accepted-but-unacknowledged publication, including a later authority successor, converges to success.
- Stale candidates, changed semantic requirements, confirmed no-effect failures, and indeterminate outcomes remain fail-closed and receive distinct diagnostics.
- Every tested failure preserves atomicity: `master` and authority both move or neither moves.
- Existing fenced-push callers and the pre-activation legacy path retain compatible behavior.
- The old ambiguous “re-prepare and retry” guidance is removed.
- All required deterministic adversarial fixtures are green.
- No parallel retry policy or second implementation of task semantics is introduced.
- Critical-infrastructure Oracle design review and final diff review both return APPROVE.
- Full repository presubmit and exact-commit post-push CI are green for every delivered leaf.

## Incident 67 blocker

The canonical delegated-close reconciler fetches a peer's `gh/issues/<N>` and `tasks/pending/<N>` refs in one command and treats either missing ref as transport failure. That is incompatible with valid lifecycle states:

- canonical close cleanup retires `tasks/pending/<N>` while retaining `gh/issues/<N>`;
- older issue roots may have only `tasks/pending/<N>`.

Live apply watchdog evidence on 2026-07-19 EDT: top-level delegated children Automation#42, mostly-static-sites#12, and Automation#60 could not reconcile because one of the two alternative identity refs was absent. The sweep recorded three failures and did not advance its success watermark.

## Required fix

Read both optional peer identity refs authoritatively, distinguish absence from transport failure, require at least one, require equality when both exist, fetch only advertised refs, and remove any stale local mirror for an absent ref. Continue validating the peer close against that authoritative root. Add focused coverage for gh-only closed roots, pending-only legacy roots, equal dual refs, disagreement, both absent, and transport failure as appropriate to existing fixtures.

Keep the semantic delta minimal. Oracle review is required before publication.

issues.body:
## Incident 67 blocker

After task-dag #38 correctly allowed either alternative peer identity ref, the apply watchdog exposed two older valid states:

1. FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#42 is open, has no close merge, and has neither identity ref. This is simply an incomplete delegated child and must remain waiting without making reconciliation fail.
2. Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites#12 is closed and predates retained identity refs. Its authoritative master history contains one exact tree-equal, two-parent `Closes-Epic: #12` merge whose second parent is the historical epic root, but both scheduling/identity refs are gone.

## Required semantics

- Scan authoritative peer master for strict close evidence before requiring identity refs. If no valid close exists, return waiting/no-op.
- When either identity ref exists, retain #38 semantics and require the close to match that root.
- When both refs are absent but a close exists, accept only a unique strict close-root identity derived from the tree-equal two-parent close merge, with parent 2 validated as the matching historical issue epic. Reject ambiguity, malformed history, identity mismatch, and transport uncertainty.
- Add focused deterministic coverage.

This is legacy compatibility only; do not weaken modern retained-identity validation.

issues.body:
## Incident 67 blocker

The apply-mode comment watchdog repeatedly fails top-level reconciliation for historical delegated closes even after runtime `01780f5c841c2fb8936c3cd7a987d4ae537f7874`.

A mutation-fenced reproduction proved `_xrepo_peer_historical_root_matches` is nondeterministic for the same immutable root: its `git show --format=%B | awk` parsers call `exit` after the trailer section while the CLI globally enables `set -o pipefail`. If `awk` closes the pipe before `git show` finishes, git receives SIGPIPE and the command substitution fails despite emitting the unique valid `Type` or `Issue` value. The same root passed on the first resolution and failed seconds later during candidate validation.

## Required change

- Make both historical-root header parsers consume the full stream while ignoring content after the relevant header section; do not exit early.
- Preserve all existing exact-one-value, empty-tree, issue, subject, parent/tree, and historical-close semantics.
- Add a focused regression with a sufficiently large body/trailing content to make early-consumer SIGPIPE deterministic under `pipefail`, and verify valid roots remain stable while malformed roots remain rejected.
- Keep the delta minimal; no record-format or semantic change.

This blocks Incident 67 closure and green recent/complete watchdog watermarks.

issues.body:
## Problem

Distinct canonical task-dag commands currently disagree about whether the same task is pending or complete. During incident recovery for #37:

- `task-dag context 53c75507dd3893c6eed45055752f5e447cad8de1` reported `Status: pending` and showed `tasks/pending/37`;
- `task-dag claim-root 37` refused with `Epic root #37 is already canonically complete`;
- GitHub issue #37 remained open;
- the final child completion warned that child-epic materialisation intent was not durable and therefore did not auto-close.

This contradiction blocked the canonical creation of a CI-repair leaf while exact-commit master CI was red. It is therefore business-blocking, not a cosmetic display inconsistency.

## Required outcome

Make task completion a single canonical concept implementation per language and route every creator, validator, state reader, claim guard, closure decision, context/status renderer, and workflow projection through it.

Hard invariant:

`duplicate_concept_implementation_count_in_same_language == 0`

No command should independently infer completion from a different subset of refs, ancestry, receipts, projections, issue state, or legacy compatibility rules.

## Scope

1. Inventory every implementation and call site that creates or verifies task completion.
2. Define one authoritative completion-state result, including enough structured reason/evidence to distinguish complete, pending, and indeterminate.
3. Migrate `context`, `claim-root`, `claim`, `deps`, `frontier`, `complete`, epic auto-close/aggregation, and workflow projections to that implementation.
4. Fail closed as indeterminate when the coherent authoritative state cannot be established; never report contradictory booleans.
5. Add a contract fixture that presents the exact #37 state to every consumer and asserts identical classification and evidence.
6. Add a source-level reuse/ownership gate that prevents a second same-language completion-semantic implementation from being introduced.
7. Repair the currently inconsistent #37 projection/closure state canonically after the implementation lands.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every supported task-state consumer gives the same completion classification for the same coherent snapshot.
- Creation and verification share the same canonical representation and parser/validator.
- Legacy/migration behavior is centralized rather than copied into callers.
- The #37 contradictory-state fixture is deterministic and green.
- The business-blocking incident can be repaired without raw ref, commit, or issue-state manipulation.

## Problem

After `breakdown` for virusdave/top-level#83 failed during consumer preparation, canonical views disagree:

- `task-dag roots --json` says issue 83 is `decomposed`;

## Result needed

Make operations-only task closure a structural task-dag invariant rather than a prose convention, so a normal implementation completion cannot mark an operation complete before its real-world action and verification succeed.

## Incident

In [FreshlyBakedNYC/automation issue 79](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/79), task `d84929b18c7d43ca69838d8d62313ad40f9cde5c` explicitly required Oracle review, operator approval, production migration apply, live verification, and completion through `complete-ops`. It was instead completed by the non-empty migration-blessing implementation commit `568c8ac835a1d7bddef3468f327f5584e46625cd`, before any production apply. The later operation failed, leaving a durable done fact that was semantically false.

`complete-ops` already existed and correctly requires durable evidence and authorization. The gap is that task commits encode this task only as `Type: leaf`; the operations-only requirement exists solely in free-form description text, and normal `task-dag complete` has no structural fact it can reject.

The incident was recovered by a new task, a successful PostgreSQL 18 migration apply, live schema/data verification, and canonical completion. The historical done fact remains immutable evidence of the gap.

## Required design

1. Add one canonical structured operations-only leaf kind/field at task creation and decomposition boundaries.
2. Make normal `complete` and `complete-historical` fail closed for that kind.
3. Make `complete-ops` require that kind, durable HTTPS evidence, authorization, and successful real-world verification metadata.
4. Preserve explicit compatibility behavior for legacy generic leaves; do not infer task kind from natural-language descriptions.
5. Route context, frontier, validators, breakdown specs, comment ingestion, and completion renderers through the same parser/type implementation.
6. Add the exact automation task above as a regression fixture: a non-empty blessing commit must not satisfy an operations-only migration task.
7. Obtain Oracle critical-infrastructure design and post-change reviews before landing.

## Acceptance criteria

- No supported normal-completion path can complete a structurally operations-only task.
- No supported operations-only completion can occur without durable evidence and authorization.
- Legacy behavior is explicit, centralized, and tested.

issues.body:
## Objective

Migrate `task-dag` from a monolithic Bash implementation and slow, brittle Bash-heavy tests to a modular, semantics-preserving Rust CLI with property-oriented tests, while keeping every intermediate revision usable by worker agents.

No imperative system/language-tool installation is allowed. Development and builds must use modern Nix-managed tooling. Preserve semantic outcomes, next steps, reliability guarantees, rollback paths, documentation, and host-cache distribution throughout the migration.

## Planned work DAG

```text
1. Bootstrap modern Nix/Rust environment and native CLI skeleton
   ↓
2. Establish Rust test harness and aggregate-runner integration
   ↓
3a. Design acyclic Bash module DAG and migration plan; page for approval
   ↓ [operator approval recorded]
3b. Execute approved Bash modularization as independently green tasks
   ↓
4. Measure and rank Bash suites for property-test migration
   ↓
5. Migrate suites/shards to Rust property tests
   ↓
6. Audit test migration and publish final P4 results
   ↓
7. [operator-blocked] Reimplement task-dag commands/modules in Rust
   ↓
8. Post-rollout acceptance audit and final P4 report
```

Stages 3b, 5, and 7 are child epics. They must be recursively decomposed into atomic tasks from their approved inventory/manifest rather than implemented as giant leaves. Their internal plans must be partial-order DAGs: independent module antichains, disjoint suites, and independently scoped shards may proceed concurrently; shared generators, harnesses, dispatcher wiring, Cargo metadata, documentation, and cache integration require explicit prerequisite/integration tasks.

## Stage requirements

### 1. Modern Nix/Rust bootstrap

Research current authoritative Nix/Rust practice before choosing `shell.nix`, a flake development shell, or a faster/cache-friendlier canonical alternative. Avoid stale Nix guidance. Add the minimal pinned Rust toolchain and project dependencies, choose one canonical CLI parsing stack and one property-testing stack, and prove the environment can produce and run a native Hello World `task-dag` binary. Evaluate `git2` with HTTPS/SSH support for later direct repository operations, but keep dependencies minimal and justified.

### 2. Rust test foundation

Create the Rust unit/property-test harness, document one canonical “run all Rust tests” command, and make `tests/task-dag/run-all.sh` invoke it even when there are initially no substantive Rust tests. Keep one canonical parallel test-launch implementation rather than separate “all” and “selected” schedulers.

### 3a. Operator-reviewed Bash decomposition design

Inventory the approximately 10k-line Bash script’s symbols, state ownership, side effects, and dependencies. Propose small, coherent, atomic modules and an extraction order as an acyclic dependency DAG. Source/import cycles are forbidden. Environment-variable or script-variable sentinels that make out-of-order sourcing silently work are forbidden; invalid source order must fail loudly.

Publish a context-complete one-off explaining each boundary, dependency edge, partial-order parallelism opportunity, migration sequence, risks, and rollback. Page Dave for review, then operator-block this task. Record the approval URL before unblocking/completing it.

### 3b. Green Bash modularization

After approval, recursively decompose this epic according to the reviewed plan. Every extraction task must preserve behavior and pass the canonical tests. The end state is many targeted files containing canonical library functions or command wiring, with a thin `task-dag` dispatcher sourcing them in strict topological order. Parallelize only genuinely independent modules whose edits and semantic ownership do not overlap.

### 4. Ordered test-migration manifest

Measure every Bash fixture/suite and rank migration candidates primarily by wall-clock cost descending, adjusted for implementation coupling, semantic value, flakiness, and ease of replacement. Split tightly coupled suites first where that exposes useful public semantics. Identify suites that should be deferred or retained and explain why. Produce an executable partial-order migration manifest that prioritizes fast wall-clock wins and increased parallelism.

### 5. Rust property-test migration

Recursively decompose this epic into per-suite or independently scoped per-shard tasks from the manifest. Rust tests should primarily enforce semantics, invariants, preconditions, postconditions, edge cases, deterministic failure interleavings, and shrinkable manufactured cases; use unit/golden tests only where they are the clearer tool.

Invoke the `task-dag` CLI under test for tool behavior. Repository setup and Git-level verification may use Rust git bindings directly rather than repeated external `git` invocations. Remove a Bash suite only after the Rust replacement is demonstrably sufficient. Each child must record before/after timing and newly covered semantics/invariants and page Dave at P3 before completion.

### 6. Test-migration audit

Verify all migratable suites were replaced, aggregate per-suite before/after wall-clock results, summarize newly enforced invariants, and list every retained Bash suite with a concrete reason. Verify Stage 7’s durable operator block still exists before completing. Publish/page the final test-migration report at P4.

### 7. Operator-blocked Rust implementation migration

This child epic must be born-claimed during breakdown, immediately operator-blocked with durable metadata, verified blocked on origin, and only then released to a blocked frontier state. It must not be recursively decomposed or implemented until explicit operator approval is recorded and the block is removed.

After approval, derive a dependency-ordered partial DAG from the modular Bash architecture and replace core functionality incrementally with semantically equivalent Rust, preferring direct Rust git APIs where they preserve reliability. When an entire command is replaced, Bash may delegate to Rust with a loud deprecation warning. Keep documentation current and use the same host caching/distribution mechanism as the Bash tool.

Root invocation and every command/subcommand must support meaningful, side-effect-free `--help` at every valid flag position. Help must remain safe even when the corresponding operation normally mutates state.

Terminal ordering inside this epic is mandatory:

1. all commands implemented and delegating;
2. Rust binary/cache distribution, canary behavior, rollback, and production availability proven;
3. only then remove the final Bash dispatcher/implementation.

Do not fold unrelated enhancements into parity migration; file follow-ups unless an enhancement is migration-critical.

### 8. Post-rollout acceptance

Confirm no Bash implementation remains, tests/docs/cache distribution are current, rollout and rollback evidence are durable, worker-agent invocation remains reliable, and all completion criteria are met. Page Dave at P4 with the final implementation-migration result.

## Global completion criteria

- Every intermediate commit leaves canonical tooling usable and documented.
- Every implementation/refactor task has focused validation and a clean revert path.
- Bash source dependencies remain acyclic and strictly ordered throughout Stage 3.
- Rust tests replace implementation-coupled checks with stronger semantic/property coverage where practical.
- The native CLI preserves semantic meaning, next actions, and reliability guarantees.
- Root/command/subcommand `--help` is always no-op and useful.
- Host-cache distribution covers the Rust binary before Bash removal.
- Per-suite P3 and final phase P4 reports include measured wall-clock changes and coverage gains.

- **Config-driven parser engine** — JSONC ruleset loader (one
  per-competitor file under
  `config/fuzzy-sku/competitors/<slug>.jsonc`), plus the four shared
  dictionaries under `config/fuzzy-sku/_shared/*.jsonc`
  (`strain_dictionary`, `brand_dictionary`, `form_factor_rules`,
  `weight_rules`).  Rule semantics per parent design §"Per-competitor
  parser config".
- **Parser CLI + coverage report** — operator-facing tool that takes
  a competitor slug and a sample of listings, runs the parser, and
  emits a per-attribute coverage report (`coverage % by attr`,
  `unresolved_token frequency table`, `evidence-span heatmap`).
  This is the iteration loop for adding / tuning competitor configs.
- **Matcher** — 3-tier matcher per parent design §"Matcher" (exact-SKU
  / exact-family / weighted), with thresholds tunable via
  `config/fuzzy-sku/matcher-weights.jsonc`.
- **`competitor_match` DB table** + migrations.  Persists
  `MatchRecord`s only (FuzzySKUs are compute-on-demand).
- **`match-refresh` job** — runs on (a) new LitAlerts snapshot
  landing, or (b) any `config/fuzzy-sku/**` file changing on
  `automation` master.  Full table replace per refresh.
- **Repricing integration** — replaces the existing best-effort
  substring path with `MatchRecord` consumption (`tier ∈ {exact-sku,
  exact-family}`, `score ≥ repricing_min_score`, default 0.85).
- **Landingpage comp integration** — emit a tier-2 match feed that the
  landing-page templates render in the "comparable nearby" section,
  with hand-curated fallback when no tier-2 candidates exist.
- **Helios `/matches` admin page** — filter by competitor + tier +
  score, per-listing evidence inspection, operator verdict button
  ("this match is wrong" / "this should have matched").  Verdicts
  recorded but **not** auto-applied; they are inputs to the operator's
  config-tuning loop.
- **Helios `/fuzzy-skus` review page** (per
  [2026-05-19 operator follow-up](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/4#issuecomment-4489690498))
  — distinct surface from `/matches`, focused on the *parsed
  FuzzySKU* itself.  Lists FuzzySKUs filterable by competitor +
  parse-status + presence of `unresolved_tokens`; per-listing detail
  shows `raw_name` with per-attribute evidence-span highlighting,
  the attribute table with `(value, confidence, rule_id, evidence)`,
  unresolved-token affordances, and per-attribute operator flags
  (`correct` / `wrong-value` / `should-be-unknown` /
  `should-have-been-extracted`).  Flags persist in a new
  `fuzzy_sku_review_flag` table.  See parent design
  §"FuzzySKU review page + LLM-assisted config suggestions (v1)" for
  the full UI spec.
- **LLM-assisted config-suggestion endpoint** (`/api/fuzzy-sku/suggest-config`)
  — operator-triggered from the `/fuzzy-skus` page; bundles the last
  N flags + current competitor JSONC + referenced shared dictionaries
  and asks the LLM for a `{rationale, diff, affected_rule_ids}`
  payload.  Diff is rendered side-by-side in the UI; operator
  accept-path opens a PR on `automation` master (commit message
  carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#4` + the originating flag
  refs).  Prompt template versioned at
  `config/fuzzy-sku/llm/suggest_config.prompt.jsonc`.  The endpoint
  never writes config directly; LLM-offline degrades gracefully (UI
  button disabled with visible warning, review / flagging still
  works).
- **Operator runbook** — `docs/runbooks/fuzzy-sku-onboarding.md`
  walking through adding a new competitor end-to-end, **including**
  the `/fuzzy-skus` flag → LLM-suggest → review-PR loop for ongoing
  rule tuning.

## Out of scope

- ML / LLM in the **parse/match hot path** (suggestion endpoint is
  config-tooling only; matcher and parser stay deterministic).
- Auto-merge of LLM-suggested config diffs (operator always reviews
  and lands the PR manually).
- Global product graph (FuzzySKUs are ephemeral per-listing
  resolutions).
- Backfill of historical LitAlerts snapshots (parent design defers).
- Generic NER pipeline (scope is cannabis listings, attribute
  vocabulary is fixed by `variant`).

## Phases

Mirrors parent design §"Phase plan"; commits should reference these
phase tags in their messages so the coordinating progress comments
(top-level#4 leaf task 2) can group them cleanly.

- **P0.** FuzzySKU + FuzzyAttr types + JSON schema; pick the JSONC
  parser library; stub the loader so subsequent phases can register
  configs.  No parsing, no matching yet.  Land the schema doc under
  `docs/fuzzy-sku/schema.md`.
- **P1.** Config-driven parser engine + the four `_shared/*.jsonc`
  dictionaries + the first competitor config (pick the
  highest-volume LitAlerts source as the pilot — operator-confirmable
  at P1 start).  Ships the parser CLI + coverage report.
- **P2.** Matcher (3 tiers) + `competitor_match` table + migration +
  `match-refresh` job.  Wired but not yet consumed by repricing or
  landingpage.
- **P3.** Repricing integration — swap the substring path for
  `MatchRecord` consumption.  Tier-3 visible in admin UI but excluded
  from auto-repricing in v1.
- **P4.** Landingpage comp-table integration — tier-2 match feed for
  the per-product "comparable nearby" section, hand-curated fallback
  preserved.
- **P5.** Helios `/matches` admin page + operator-verdict capture.
- **P5b.** Helios `/fuzzy-skus` review page + `fuzzy_sku_review_flag`
  table + migration + `/api/fuzzy-sku/suggest-config` LLM endpoint +
  UI for diff review (accept / edit / reject) + PR-open path on
  accept.  Builds on P5's admin-shell scaffolding (auth, layout,
  table component); parser/match-refresh outputs it consumes come
  from P1/P2.
- **P6.** Wire-up + e2e + onboarding runbook (with `/fuzzy-skus`
  flagging + LLM-suggest loop included) + onboard 2 more competitors
  (total 3) to clear the parent-epic acceptance bar.

P3 / P4 / P5 are parallel after P2 lands.  P5b lands after P5.

## Acceptance criteria

Lifted from parent design §"Acceptance criteria"; this child epic is
satisfied when:

1. At least **three competitors** have working configs in
   `config/fuzzy-sku/competitors/` and the per-competitor coverage
   report shows **≥ 70 % of listings** producing a tier-1 or tier-2
   match against our catalog (measured on a manually-curated
   100-listing gold set per competitor, checked in under
   `config/fuzzy-sku/gold-sets/`).
2. Repricing's daily run consumes `MatchRecord`s and the
   per-competitor coverage on its decision log shows **≥ 2×** the
   number of matched listings vs. the previous substring path,
   measured over a 7-day window.
3. The Helios `/matches` admin page is reachable and renders the most
   recent run's matches with filtering, evidence, and the verdict
   button.
4. The Helios `/fuzzy-skus` review page is reachable, renders the
   most recent run's parsed FuzzySKUs with per-attribute evidence
   highlighting, supports the four per-attribute flag verdicts
   (`correct` / `wrong-value` / `should-be-unknown` /
   `should-have-been-extracted`), and the "Suggest config edits"
   button returns a reviewable JSONC diff that the operator can
   accept (PR-open path), edit-then-accept, or reject.  At least
   **one** LLM-suggested PR is merged end-to-end against a real
   competitor config and produces a measurable coverage uplift in
   the next `match-refresh` run.
5. The operator runbook (`docs/runbooks/fuzzy-sku-onboarding.md`)
   walks through adding a new competitor end-to-end (config →
   parser CLI → coverage report → matcher threshold check → ship)
   **and** documents the ongoing `/fuzzy-skus` flag → LLM-suggest →
   PR-review tuning loop.
6. At least one landing-page (any product page) renders a tier-2
   "comparable nearby" section drawn from `MatchRecord`s.
7. Every `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#4` commit lands on
   `automation` master (not a feature branch) per
   [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/automation/blob/master/AGENTS.md).

## Coordination back to the parent epic

- File one progress comment on `virusdave/top-level#4` per phase
  completion (P0..P6), linked to the `automation` commit(s) that
  landed it.  These comments are emitted by the top-level
  coordinating leaf task 2 of
  [`docs/epics/fuzzy-sku/task-dag-breakdown.json`](../../task-dag-breakdown.json);
  the operator does not need to hand-write them.
- Final closure: once the P6 commit lands on `automation` master with
  the `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#4` trailer, the cross-repo
  completion-sync workflow will materialise the completion ref
  (`tasks/completions/4/virusdave/automation/<peer_issue>/<sha>`),
  the top-level final-closure leaf task fires its `page-dave` with the
  Helios `/matches` URL + coverage report + 7-day comparison +
  runbook link, and `close-completed-issues.yml` closes the epic
  issue automatically.

declarations.body:
# About-Us Unification — `nixos-sbc` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#6](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/6).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/about-us-unify/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo; this child epic scope is **strictly the
> `nixos-sbc` slice of that design** — namely "stand up HTTP Basic
> auth on the two FBNYC / FBUS staging vhosts so Dave can review
> the unified about-us page before it ships to production."
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `nixos-sbc` master and
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#6
> ```

## Scope owned by this repo

### N1. HTTP Basic auth on staging vhosts

The staging hosts already exist:

- `staging.freshlybaked.nyc` — enabled by
  `services.mss.sites.freshlybaked.hosts.staging.enable = true;`
  in `hosts/vps/sites-mirror.nix` (~line 179), with ACME forced on
  (~line 185).
- `staging.freshlybaked.us` — enabled by
  `services.mss.sites.freshlybakedus.hosts.staging.enable = true;`
  with explicit `hostName = "staging.freshlybaked.us";` in the
  same file (~lines 197–198).

What's missing: neither vhost has authentication. Anyone who finds
the hostname (or who scrapes the cert transparency log) can hit
the staging site. For this epic the operator chose **HTTP Basic
auth** with credentials `letmein` / `letmein` and realm
`Freshly Baked staging`. These are intentionally weak — staging
contains no PII, no auth tokens, no payment surface; the bar is
"keep crawlers out, keep accidental visitors out, give Dave a
review URL he can paste anywhere without worry."

Concretely, add `basicAuth` (or `basicAuthFile` if the module
author prefers an out-of-band htpasswd file) on the staging
virtual-host blocks. The simplest in-tree option is:

```nix
services.nginx.virtualHosts."staging.freshlybaked.nyc" = {
  # ... existing config (enableACME, locations, etc.) ...
  basicAuth = { letmein = "letmein"; };
  basicAuthMessage = "Freshly Baked staging";
};

services.nginx.virtualHosts."staging.freshlybaked.us" = {
  # ... existing config ...
  basicAuth = { letmein = "letmein"; };
  basicAuthMessage = "Freshly Baked staging";
};
```

If the underlying nixos `services.mss.sites.<x>.hosts.staging`
module submerges the vhost config so that direct
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>` overrides cause merge issues
(it does fall back to `lib.mkForce` in at least one place — see
the `enableACME = lib.mkForce true;` precedent on line ~185),
follow the same `lib.mkForce` pattern.

If the module instead exposes a typed option for staging auth (or
the implementer prefers to add one), the option name should be
`services.mss.sites.<site>.hosts.staging.basicAuth` taking
`{ <user> = <password>; }` for in-tree credentials or
`services.mss.sites.<site>.hosts.staging.basicAuthFile` taking a
`/run/secrets/...` path for agenix-managed credentials. For this
particular epic the inline `letmein:letmein` is fine; no agenix
secret is warranted for credentials that ship in cleartext in
git history by operator request.

### Deploy

Per `nixos-sbc/AGENTS.md`: rebuild and apply the system closure
via `self-deploy` on `vps-nixos-3` (the production VPS that hosts
both staging vhosts — see the per-host module at
`hosts/per-host/vps-nixos-3.nix`).

### Smoke test

Before posting the completion `Satisfies:` trailer, verify both:

```sh
curl -I https://staging.freshlybaked.nyc/      # expect 401
curl -I -u letmein:letmein https://staging.freshlybaked.nyc/   # expect 200/302 to age gate
curl -I https://staging.freshlybaked.us/       # expect 401
curl -I -u letmein:letmein https://staging.freshlybaked.us/    # expect 200
```

## Out of scope

- DNS or ACME changes for either staging hostname — both already
  resolve and both already get certs through the existing
  `enableACME` path.
- Any change to `services.mss.sites.<x>.hosts.production.*`.
- Any change to the `mostly-static-sites` build / source — that's
  owned by the peer child epic.
- Any oauth / SSO / IP-allowlist replacement for Basic auth.
  Operator picked Basic intentionally; revisiting is a separate
  epic.

## Phases

- **N1.** Single commit landing the `basicAuth` (+ `basicAuthMessage`)
  additions on both staging vhosts, deployed via `self-deploy`,
  smoke-tested with `curl`.

## Cross-repo dependencies

- None. The mostly-static-sites peer epic's M1/M2/M3 do not gate
  N1, and N1 does not gate them. Landing N1 first is in fact
  useful because it lets Dave confirm the basic-auth challenge
  works against the *existing* staging pages before any content
  change is visible.

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. N1 commit has landed on `nixos-sbc` master carrying the
   `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#6` trailer.
2. The system closure has been applied to `vps-nixos-3` via
   `self-deploy`.
3. The two `curl` smoke tests above pass.
declarations.delegationNote: nginx basic auth letmein/letmein realm "Freshly Baked staging" on both staging vhosts so Dave can review the unified about-us before production deploy

# About-Us Unification — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#6](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/6).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/about-us-unify/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo. This child epic exists because the operator
> hoisted the "v2 staff strip" (with a 15-minute auto-refresh
> requirement) into v1 scope, and the staff-roster data lives in
> Helios.
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `automation` master and
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#6
> ```

## Scope owned by this repo (Helios)

### H1 — Public-roster export endpoint + approval workflow

1. **New GET endpoint: `/public/roster.json`** (path under the
   existing Helios HTTP surface; final route under
   `helios-server`'s decision).
   - **Auth:** none. The data emitted is the same first-names
     and approved-for-public headshots that are already destined
     to be public on the brand sites. Rate-limit to e.g.
     60 req/min per source IP via the existing reverse-proxy
     layer (or in-process if simpler).
   - **Response shape:** JSON array of rows, one per emitted
     employee:
     ```json
     [
       {
         "first_name": "Karon",
         "headshot_url": "https://helios.../public/headshots/<sha>.jpg",
         "headshot_approved_at": "2026-05-20T18:31:04Z"
       }
     ]
     ```
   - **Filter:** only rows where `headshot_approved_at IS NOT
     NULL` AND `public_excluded = false` AND `headshot_url IS
     NOT NULL`.
   - **Stability:** order alphabetically by `first_name` then by
     `headshot_approved_at` so the brand-site grid order is
     deterministic between revalidates.
   - **Caching:** server-side cache for ~60s (the brand sites
     revalidate every 15 min anyway — the 60s cache exists to
     soak up the cold-start spike when many static-site builds
     happen near the same revalidate boundary).

2. **Schema additions on the `employees` table** (or whatever
   the existing Helios employee model is named — verify in
   `helios-server`).
   - `public_excluded BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false` —
     per-employee opt-out. Admin-only writable.
   - `headshot_approved_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NULL` —
     stamped when an admin clicks "approve for public display".
     Null until then.
   - Indexed compound: `(headshot_approved_at IS NULL,
     public_excluded)` so the public-roster query filter is
     cheap.
   - Migration is additive (no backfill needed — default state
     is "not approved", which is the safe default).

3. **Admin UI: per-employee approval toggle.**
   - On the existing employee-detail view in the Helios admin
     pages (location: confirm in `helios-server`'s template /
     route inventory), add two controls beneath the headshot
     field:
     - **Toggle:** "Exclude from public roster" → writes
       `public_excluded`. Persistent across approvals.
     - **Button:** "Approve headshot for public display" →
       stamps `headshot_approved_at = NOW()`. If already
       approved, the button toggles to "Revoke public
       approval" → clears `headshot_approved_at = NULL`.
   - Both actions are admin-only (use the existing
     admin-auth middleware; no new auth model).
   - Action gets logged to the existing Helios audit log
     (operator-action style — "admin X approved employee Y's
     headshot at T").

4. **Headshot URL stability.**
   - `headshot_url` must be content-addressable so the brand
     site's ISR can rely on URL change to bust its image
     cache: serve from
     `helios.<host>/public/headshots/<sha256-of-bytes>.<ext>`.
     If today's headshots are stored at mutable URLs, add a
     thin re-publisher that copies the bytes to
     content-addressable storage on first approval (and on
     change).
   - Serve with a long `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000,
     immutable` because the URL changes when the bytes change.

## Out of scope

- Any brand-site rendering — that's M4 in the
  `mostly-static-sites` child epic.
- Any FBUS-specific image scrubbing — also lives in the
  `mostly-static-sites` child epic (on the FBUS build side).
  Helios serves the un-scrubbed headshot; FBUS scrubs locally.
- Any change to the existing employee data the parsers ingest.
  This epic only adds two columns + one read endpoint + a small
  admin UI.
- Any deploy automation — operator (Dave) handles
  `systemctl restart helios-server` per `automation`'s AGENTS.md.

## Phases (matches parent EPIC_PLAN.md)

- **H1.** Single phase. Schema migration + admin-UI controls +
  public-roster GET endpoint, all behind no feature flag (the
  endpoint returns `[]` until an admin approves the first
  headshot, so the brand-side render is a no-op until then).

## Cross-repo dependencies

- The brand-site M4 phase in `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites`
  consumes this endpoint, but it ships against a checked-in
  fixture in parallel so M4 isn't blocked on H1.
- No dependency on `helios-parser-configs` (this is a Helios
  server change, not a parser config).
- No dependency on `nixos-sbc` (Helios is already exposed
  publicly via the existing reverse-proxy chain; the new path
  rides on that).

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. H1 commits have landed on `automation` master with the
   `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#6` trailer.
2. `GET https://helios.<host>/public/roster.json` returns a
   valid JSON array on the deployed system (operator-verified
   after `systemctl restart helios-server`).
3. An admin can approve a headshot in the UI and the next
   `GET /public/roster.json` (within ≤60s server cache window)
   reflects the new row.

Consumed by mostly-static-sites M4 on a 15-minute revalidate.

Meet The Team

Meet The Founders

After working overseas in different > managerial roles, Nicolas joined Freshly Baked NYC with the > goal of helping the team grow, improving daily operations, > and creating a professional, welcoming experience for every > customer.
