declarations.body:
# Helios `/metrics` v1.3 rework — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
> for the v1.3 iteration. Authoritative design:
> [`docs/epics/business-metrics/EPIC_PLAN_v1_3_REWORK.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN_v1_3_REWORK.md)
> in the top-level repo. Oracle-approved design thread:
> [T-019e654a-8d2f-74fb-9734-3588f512d8a2](https://ampcode.com/threads/T-019e654a-8d2f-74fb-9734-3588f512d8a2).
>
> The v1 child epic is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#21`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21)
> (closed); the v1.1 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#28`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/28)
> (closed); the v1.2 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#30`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/30)
> (closed). This issue tracks the v1.3 rework only — please do
> not reopen the v1 / v1.1 / v1.2 children.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation` master that
> satisfies any part of this rework MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: V3<n>`
> trailer (e.g. `Phase: V3'3`) — distinct from v1's `P<n>`,
> v1.1's `R<n>`, and v1.2's `V2<n>` — so per-phase progress
> comments on the parent issue are visually grouped per rework
> iteration.

## Scope owned by this repo

v1.3 lands the **Budtender Performance** tab at
`/metrics/budtenders` per the parent addendum:

1. `/metrics` top-level tab strip (Dashboard | Budtenders) +
   sibling-route shell at `/metrics/budtenders` with sticky
   Core / Advanced sub-tab strip.
2. Core sub-tab panels backed by real data:
   leaderboard, daily cashier-attributed sales trend,
   customer / fulfillment / payment mix, shift productivity,
   dollar-basket upsell lift (same-customer + similar-customer).
3. Advanced sub-tab one-dot-per-cashier scatter with
   axis / color / size / opacity switchers, peer-percentile
   encoding, highlight-subset search, optional quadrant
   reference lines.
4. MISSING DATA cards for the four (five, including basket-
   quantity upsell) operator-asked-for metrics that have no
   real data path today.
5. Consolidated `/api/budtender-analytics` endpoint behind a
   single CTE-chained prepared statement; supporting indexes;
   `compareTo=peer-cohort` extension.
6. Perf measurement, runbook refresh, validation evidence,
   oracle review pass, parent closure package.

Re-read the parent addendum before starting any phase. This
child plan is intentionally a thin index over the parent.

### V3'0 — Scope freeze + route shell + canonical update

- Re-confirm the v1.3-in-scope panel set against the canonical
  v1.2 list (Budtender panels are additive — no headline-
  dashboard panel is removed).
- Extend `MetricDef` types (additive):
  - `area?: 'dashboard' | 'budtenders'` discriminator
    (defaults to `'dashboard'`).
  - `supports.peerCohort?: boolean` (Budtender metrics
    declare `true`; headline metrics unchanged).
  - `blockedBy?: { ingestIssue?: string; column?: string;
    note: string }` on MISSING DATA registry entries.
- `/metrics` top-level tab strip: add a small tab strip below
  the controls bar with "Dashboard" (default; preserves the
  v1.2 entry URL) and "Budtenders" (routes to
  `/metrics/budtenders`). Sticky across scroll like the
  controls bar.
- `/metrics/budtenders` route shell:
  - Page header band with title + coverage badge placeholder
    (wired with live data in V3'1).
  - Sticky "Core | Advanced" sub-tab strip under the global
    controls bar.
  - Empty grid containers for Core (responsive 1/2/3 cols)
    and Advanced (single full-width).
  - Sub-tab choice persists in URL
    (`?sub=core` / `?sub=advanced`).
- Backend skeleton: `GET /api/budtender-analytics` returning a
  well-typed empty payload (`cashier_rows: []`,
  `daily_trend: []`, etc.) with `meta.sources` already
  populated correctly. The CTE chain is added in V3'1 / V3'3.
- Refresh `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics-v1_2-canonical.md` to a
  `…-v1_3-canonical.md` superset that adds an "area" column
  and the `supports.peerCohort` / `blockedBy` columns; update
  the runbook anchor on the parent issue's body.

**Exit criteria**: top-level tab strip renders on `/metrics`;
`/metrics/budtenders` route loads with Core / Advanced empty
grids; the backend endpoint returns a well-typed empty payload;
canonical metric list refreshed; `MetricDef` types extended
(no behavioural change yet).

### V3'1 — Core P0: Leaderboard + Daily Cashier-Attributed Sales Trend

- Backend: first cut of `/api/budtender-analytics` CTE chain
  covering `orders`, `cashier_agg`, and a per-day rollup feeding
  `daily_trend`. Filters honour the global controls (sites,
  range, agg for the trend). Excludes `cashier_user_id IS NULL`
  from `cashier_agg`; surfaces the same count under
  `meta.coverage.unattributed_transactions`. Implemented as a
  single prepared statement to minimise round-trip overhead.
- Frontend:
  - **Budtender Leaderboard** panel: sortable, paginated table
    of cashier rows; default sort `sales desc`. Inline
    horizontal bars per numeric cell; cell colour driven by
    peer-cohort percentile within the visible window; low-n
    rows (`transactions < 20` OR `shift_coverage_minutes <
    120`) dimmed with a "low n" chip. Pagination state lives
    in the URL.
  - **Daily Cashier-Attributed Sales Trend** panel: time
    series in the v1.2 `<MetricChart/>`. Primary = daily
    sales; togglable secondary series = transactions, AOV,
    discount fraction. `cashier_user_id IS NULL` daily totals
    render as a dimmed reference-style series. Tile-level
    annotation pip + hover popover from v1.2 R'5 reused.
  - Unattributed-transactions warning chip in the Leaderboard
    panel header.
- Per-row click on the Leaderboard in v1.3 emits a "single-
  cashier detail view forthcoming" toast and pre-fills
  `highlight=<cashier_id>` for the Advanced sub-tab.

**Exit criteria**: leaderboard + daily trend render with real
production data on `/metrics/budtenders?sub=core`; peer-
percentile colour coding visible; low-n dimming visible on
known-low-volume cashiers; unattributed-transactions chip
appears when `IS NULL` rows exist in the window.

### V3'2 — Core P1: Mix + Shift Productivity

- Extend the consolidated endpoint with the `shift_agg` CTE
  (`sweed_shifts ⋈ orders` on `(dealer_id, employee_id,
  pay_time BETWEEN shift_open_at AND shift_close_at)`) and the
  three mix breakdowns under `mix.customer_segment`,
  `mix.fulfillment`, `mix.payment`.
- Frontend:
  - **Customer / Fulfillment / Payment Mix** cards: three
    stacked percentage bar charts. Per-card toggle switches
    denominator between transactions and sales. Fleet-level
    by default; re-scope to a selected cashier (URL-persisted)
    via overlay over the fleet baseline.
  - **Shift Productivity** card: scatter or ranked bar of
    `transactions / shift_hour`. If
    `shift_agg.coverage_pct < 0.4` on the visible window,
    render the panel as a MISSING DATA card with explicit
    "shift attribution coverage too low" copy + a link to
    the shifts-ingest follow-on issue (see V3'5 for the
    `blockedBy` registry shape).

**Exit criteria**: mix cards render at fleet and per-cashier
levels; overlay-on-leaderboard-select works URL-persistently;
shift productivity card either renders real data or falls
through to a MISSING DATA card with honest copy.

### V3'3 — Core P1: Dollar-Basket Upsell Lift + `compareTo=peer-cohort`

- Extend the consolidated endpoint with the `baseline_lift`
  CTE:
  - Per-order `same_customer_baseline` = leave-one-out average
    of that customer's order totals in the window (filtered to
    known, non-guest, `count >= 2`).
  - Per-order `similar_customer_baseline` = leave-one-out
    average over cohort
    `(guest_flag, first_time_flag, fulfillment_type,
    payment_method)`.
  - Per-cashier rollup is the mean of per-order
    `(order_total - baseline)` with explicit sample-size
    counts.
- Frontend:
  - **Dollar-Basket Upsell Lift** card: diverging horizontal
    bars; toggle in header switches mode between
    `same-customer` and `similar-customer`. Sample-size chip
    per cashier; low-n dimming consistent with leaderboard.
    Colour driven by `desirableDirection: 'up'`.
- `compareTo=peer-cohort` API extension:
  - The Daily Cashier-Attributed Sales Trend panel adopts
    `peer-cohort` as its default `compareTo`.
  - The reference data is the peer-cohort P25 / median / P75
    aggregated within the visible window. Renders as a faint
    band (P25..P75) with the median as a dashed line.
  - Per-panel toggle still offers `prior-period` / `year-over-
    year` / `peer-cohort` / `off`; existing headline panels
    are unchanged.
- V3'0 guardrail tightens: any metric with `area:
  'budtenders'` MUST declare `supports.peerCohort: true`.

**Exit criteria**: dollar-basket lift card renders both modes
on real data; per-cashier sample-size chips and low-n dimming
visible; peer-cohort band renders on the Daily Trend; per-
panel `compareTo` toggle works; guardrail in enforcement.

### V3'4 — Advanced sub-tab: one-dot-per-cashier scatter

- Adapt the v1.2 catalog-style scatter renderer to plot one
  dot per cashier (data source = `cashier_rows` from the
  consolidated endpoint; no extra HTTP).
- **Axis pickers** (X + Y, independent): expose 15+ fields
  per the parent addendum's enumeration, including
  peer-percentile-suffixed (`__pct`) variants computed
  client-side from `cashier_rows`.
- **Color encoding picker** with sensible per-field defaults:
  - Diverging red→gray→green for signed-lift fields.
  - Diverging blue→gray→red for `discount_pct`.
  - Sequential low→high for everything else.
  - "Match X axis" / "Match Y axis" one-click shortcuts.
- **Size encoding picker**: sqrt-scaled by `transactions`
  (default), `sales`, `unique_customers`, or
  `shift_coverage_minutes`.
- **Opacity / confidence**: auto-dim per the rules in the
  parent addendum (lift axes < 10 samples; shift-productivity
  axes < 120 min; volume axes < 20 transactions). Combination
  dimming does not stack below 0.3.
- **Highlight subset**: text input filters by cashier name /
  id / status suffix; matching dots render on top with 2 px
  stroke + label; non-matching dots fade to 0.2 opacity;
  empty input = no highlight. Pre-fills from Leaderboard
  row-click (`?highlight=<cashier_id>`).
- **Reference lines / quadrants** (optional, off by default):
  axis median + P75 lines with quadrant labels.
- **Default first paint**: `X=transactions_per_shift_hour`,
  `Y=aov`, `Color=same_customer_lift`, `Size=transactions`.
- Keyboard: axis pickers reachable via Tab; highlight input
  focusable; quadrant toggle reachable; Escape clears
  highlight.

**Exit criteria**: Advanced scatter renders one-dot-per-cashier
with default encodings on first paint; all pickers work;
highlight-subset filters; pre-fill via `?highlight=` works
from the Leaderboard row-click handoff.

### V3'5 — MISSING DATA cards + summary chip

- Wire `blockedBy` registry entries for the five known-
  missing Budtender metrics:
  1. Product Subset Comparison & Category/Subcategory
     Distribution by Cashier (blocked by line-items ingest).
  2. Returns / Refunds Distribution by Cashier (blocked by
     `sweed_returns` ingest with cashier attribution).
  3. Cashier-Attributed Customer Reviews (blocked by
     invoice → review linkage in `review_submissions`).
  4. Shift Cash +/- (Drawer Reconciliation) (blocked by
     drawer-close actuals).
  5. Basket-Quantity Upsell (blocked by line-items ingest;
     dollar lift shipped in V3'3 as the v1.3 substitute).
- For each, register a MISSING DATA registry entry with:
  - Panel header copy describing what the panel would show.
  - "What's blocked / why / next step" body section with a
    link to the tracking ingest issue on the peer repo if
    one exists, or a "file ingest issue" helper that
    prefills the title + body.
- **MISSING DATA summary chip** at the top of the Core
  sub-tab: "N panels missing data: …" — clicking expands to a
  short list of blocked panels with their ingest links. Chip
  is hidden when N = 0.
- **CI guardrail extension**: extend v1.1 R0's stub-leak
  test to assert no `dataStatus: 'pending'` card on the
  Budtender sub-route ever renders with non-empty `series` —
  catches a future regression where stub data sneaks into a
  MISSING DATA card.

**Exit criteria**: five MISSING DATA cards render in the Core
grid with honest copy + ingest links; summary chip renders
when N > 0; guardrail green.

### V3'6 — Indexes + perf + closure package

- Land four `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` indexes on
  `vps-nixos-3` production DB:
  - `sweed_orders (dealer_id, pay_time)`
  - `sweed_orders (cashier_user_id, pay_time)`
  - `sweed_orders (customer_id, pay_time)` (verify presence
    from v1.1; create only if missing).
  - `sweed_shifts (dealer_id, employee_id, shift_open_at,
    shift_close_at)`
- Perf measurement of `/api/budtender-analytics`:
  - Capture `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` for the consolidated query on
    typical windows (1d / 7d / 28d / 12wk).
  - Endpoint timing (P50 / P95 cold / P95 warm).
  - Targets: P50 < 500 ms warm, P95 < 1.2 s cold on a 4-week
    window across all sites.
- Runbook refresh: `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md` extended
  with the v1.3 surface (Budtender sub-route, sub-tab
  semantics, `compareTo=peer-cohort`, `area` discriminator,
  `blockedBy` registry, MISSING DATA summary chip).
- Validation evidence committed under the runbook:
  - Leaderboard screenshot with peer-percentile colour coding.
  - Daily Trend screenshot with peer-cohort band rendered.
  - Mix cards in fleet mode and per-cashier overlay mode.
  - Shift Productivity card (real-data mode) + the MISSING
    DATA fallback shape (separate screenshot).
  - Dollar-basket lift card in both modes.
  - Advanced scatter at default first paint.
  - Advanced scatter at a non-default
    `(X, Y, color, size, highlight)` configuration.
  - Each of the five MISSING DATA cards.
  - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` + endpoint timing table.
- Oracle review pass: re-run an oracle review on
  `/metrics/budtenders` Core + Advanced + each MISSING DATA
  card. Capture the oracle's "fit for purpose — world class for
  this operator's stated needs?" verdict. If the oracle flags
  new gaps, address them in this phase before the closure
  commit, or file an explicit follow-on epic and call it out
  in the closure package.
- Closure package: a single comment on
  [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
  containing the live URL
  (`https://helios.freshlybaked.us/metrics/budtenders`), the
  V3'0–V3'6 per-phase commit table, the AC §1–9 sign-off
  (with one-line evidence per criterion), the refreshed
  canonical Budtender metric list, the validation evidence,
  and the oracle note. The close commit MUST carry
  `Closes-Epic: #7` per #8's policy so
  `close-completed-issues.yml` closes the issue.

**Exit criteria**: parent can close based on evidence, not
trust; v1.3 AC §1–9 demonstrably hold on production; v1.1
AC §1–10 and v1.2 AC §1–8 continue to hold (no regressions);
oracle confirms `/metrics/budtenders` is fit for the
operator's stated "world-class budtender performance
dashboard" purpose.

## Cross-repo dependencies

None hard. The five MISSING DATA cards represent ingest
dependencies that are *acknowledged* as out-of-v1.3-scope.
Each card carries a `blockedBy.ingestIssue` link to a peer-
repo ingest issue (file new ones if they don't exist; e.g.
`sweed_order_line_items` ingest, `sweed_returns` ingest,
review-invoice-linkage, drawer-close-actuals ingest). v1.3 does
not block on any of these landing — the MISSING DATA cards are
the deliverable for the unblocked-data path.

When an ingest unblocks in a future iteration (v1.4+), each
MISSING DATA registry entry's panel can be promoted to a real
panel in a follow-on epic. v1.3 just leaves the slots ready
and visible.

## Acceptance criteria (delegated from parent)

The full v1.3 acceptance criteria live in the parent rework
addendum §"Refreshed acceptance criteria". Reproduced here as
a checklist for the V3'6 owner:

- [ ] (1) `/metrics/budtenders` reachable via top-level tab
      strip on `/metrics`; sub-tab + highlight selection
      persist in URL; share-link reproduces.
- [ ] (2) Core P0: Leaderboard + Daily Trend land with real
      data; peer-percentile colouring; low-n dimming;
      unattributed-transactions chip.
- [ ] (3) Core P1: Mix + Shift Productivity + Upsell Lift
      land with real data (or honest MISSING DATA fallback
      for Shift Productivity at < 40% coverage); overlay-on-
      leaderboard-select works.
- [ ] (4) Advanced sub-tab one-dot-per-cashier scatter with
      all axis / color / size / opacity / highlight pickers;
      default first paint per spec.
- [ ] (5) Five MISSING DATA cards render with "what / why /
      next step" copy + ingest links; summary chip; CI
      guardrail green.
- [ ] (6) Consolidated `/api/budtender-analytics` + four
      `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` indexes; perf targets met
      (P50 < 500 ms warm; P95 < 1.2 s cold on 4-week window).
- [ ] (7) `compareTo=peer-cohort` extension works; default on
      Budtender Daily Trend; per-panel toggle still functional;
      headline panels unchanged.
- [ ] (8) v1.1 AC §1–10 and v1.2 AC §1–8 continue to hold on
      production; no regressions.
- [ ] (9) Oracle-approved closure evidence package — live URL,
      commit table, screenshots, perf table, canonical
      Budtender metric list, oracle note; close commit
      carries `Closes-Epic: #7`.

V3'0..V3'6 phasing; oracle-approved evidence package required at V3'6 closure with Closes-Epic: #7 trailer.

issues.body:
## Problem

`close-completed-issues.sh` (and the `close-completed-issues.yml` workflow that calls it) fires on **every** merge commit on `master` that lists a `refs/heads/tasks/pending/<N>` ref as a non-primary parent. That includes commits produced by `scripts/task-dag complete`, which is the documented mechanism for *attaching* an implementation commit to an in-progress task — **not** for completing the epic.

When this fires unintentionally it:

1. Closes the epic GitHub issue with a "task epic completed in commit …" comment.
2. Deletes `refs/heads/tasks/pending/<N>` from `origin`, which removes the epic from the frontier and breaks any subsequent `scripts/task-dag delegate` or `scripts/task-dag complete` invocations against it.
3. Pages the issue author via the `@${author}` mention in the close comment.

Concrete incident: this footgun fired on issue #7 (commit `dba98c6`), which used `task-dag complete` to attach an in-progress child-epic *plan*. The epic was auto-closed and `refs/heads/tasks/pending/7` was deleted; manual recovery had to restore the pending ref from `refs/heads/gh/issues/7` and re-run `scripts/task-dag delegate` (see [#7 comment](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7#issuecomment-4539209167) for the full repro/cleanup).

## Root cause

`.github/scripts/close-completed-issues.sh` treats the merge-parent structure itself as the completion signal — there is no way for the script to distinguish "this merge attaches a sub-task" from "this merge closes the epic". `scripts/task-dag complete` uses exactly the same parent structure for both.

## Proposed fix

Require an **explicit** epic-closure signal in addition to the parent-ref structure. Either of these would work; the first is probably the least invasive:

1. **Trailer-based**: require a `Closes-Epic: #<N>` (or `Closes: #<N>`) trailer on the merge commit's message. `close-completed-issues.sh` would only act when the trailer is present and matches the task's issue number. `scripts/task-dag complete` should *not* emit this trailer by default; a new `scripts/task-dag close-epic <issue>` (or a `--close-epic` flag) would.

2. **Metadata-based**: read `Status:` (or a new `Closes-Epic:` line) from the task metadata commit body at the parent ref's tip. Only close when `Status: closed` (or `Closes-Epic: true`) is present. `scripts/task-dag close-epic` (which already exists in the CLI — see `scripts/task-dag help`) would be the supported way to flip that line.

Either way, the change is "narrow the trigger from *structural* to *explicit*."

## Acceptance criteria

- `scripts/task-dag complete <sha>` against a `tasks/pending/<N>` ref, followed by a push to `master`, does **not** close issue `<N>` and does **not** delete `refs/heads/tasks/pending/<N>`.
- A documented one-step "close the epic" path (likely `scripts/task-dag close-epic <N>` or an explicit `Closes-Epic:` trailer) **does** close the issue and delete the pending ref, with the same `@author` paging behaviour as today.
- Existing closed-as-completion behaviour is preserved for whatever the new explicit signal is, so the operator-paging design from `docs/epics/customer-sentiment/EPIC_PLAN.md` still works.
- Documented in `docs/task_dag/` so future agents don't repeat the footgun.

## Related

- Issue #7 (where this footgun fired in the wild)
- `.github/scripts/close-completed-issues.sh`
- `.github/workflows/close-completed-issues.yml`
- `scripts/task-dag` (`complete` and `close-epic` subcommands)

issues.title: close-completed-issues.sh should require an explicit close signal, not just merge-parent structure

# Customers UX — `automation` child epic

> Second child epic of
> [virusdave/top-level#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9),
> sibling to the ingestion child epic at
> [`./EPIC_PLAN.md`](./EPIC_PLAN.md).
>
> Authoritative design:
> [`docs/epics/visitor-address-ingestion/CUSTOMERS_UX_EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../CUSTOMERS_UX_EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in the top-level repo.  This file is the thin per-repo scope index;
> read the parent design before starting.
>
> Implementation commits landing on `automation` master that satisfy
> any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9
> ```
>
> and SHOULD also carry:
>
> ```
> Phase: C<n>
> ```
>
> so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post the per-phase
> progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

The Helios admin UI + helios-server API + DB compatibility views that
make `visitor_scans` operationally useful, plus the IA reorganisation
that puts CRM and Segments under a new top-level "Customers" item.

Phased as C1..C5; C6 is explicitly deferred to a separate **paused**
follow-on issue (operator's request: "Export to mp4 on demand of the
replay movie would be a plus for v2; leave an open todo and paused
github issue for this.").

### C1 — Live scans table — PAGE-BACK TRIGGER

**Operator-stated stop-the-line trigger.** Ship this first. The
operator's exact words: "Page me as soon as the 'recent / live scans'
part is complete, as i want to enable this *now*."

- Canonical route `/admin/customers/check-ins`.
- Alias `/admin/visitors/scans` (the route the ingestion epic A3
  originally planned) so it remains valid.
- Server endpoint `GET /api/admin/customers/check-ins` per parent
  design §6.6 (subset for C1: scan rows + basic filters + facets;
  purchase summary fields can return `null`/`unknown`).
- Detail endpoint `GET /api/admin/customers/check-ins/:scan_id`
  with raw payload permission gating per parent design §13.
- Canonical `checked_in_at = COALESCE(scanned_at, created_at,
  ingested_at)`; if a normalized column was added in the ingestion
  epic, use it; otherwise use the expression + matching index per
  parent design §11 "Indexes to add or verify".
- Newest-first paginated/virtualised table with the C1 columns in
  parent design §6.3.
- Basic filters (server-side SQL, NOT client-only): site,
  checked-in date range, ingest source, document type, scan status,
  authentication status, state, postal prefix.
- Row drawer with normalized fields + address/geocode panel + raw
  JSON panel (permission-gated; if Helios lacks the permission
  infrastructure, hide the raw panel rather than expose unguarded).
- Lightweight auto-refresh (every 15–30s) plus manual refresh; live
  status chip showing latest `checked_in_at` / `ingested_at`.
- No purchase joins, no map, no IA changes in C1.
- After deploy, post the C1 status comment on parent issue #9 per
  parent design §16.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C1`.

### C2 — Purchase-history facets + matching layer + CSV export

- New compatibility views over the existing CRM/orders source:
  `customer_order_facts` and `customer_order_line_facts` per parent
  design §5.3. Use the same business definitions the existing CRM
  page already uses.
- `visitor_scan_customer_matches` match layer per parent design §5.4
  with the precedence table (default purchase-history filters use
  `confidence >= 85`).
- Extend `/api/admin/customers/check-ins` to compute and return:
  `purchase.match_*`, `purchase.history_at_checkin`,
  `purchase.prior_order_count`, `purchase.last_purchase_at`,
  `purchase.converted_after_checkin`, `purchase.visit_*`,
  `purchase.lifetime_*` per parent design §6.6 sample response.
- Add purchase filters (parent §6.4.4):
  - purchase history at check-in (repeat/no-prior/unknown);
  - visit conversion (yes/no/unknown);
  - first-time purchaser conversion;
  - prior order count bands;
  - lifetime spend bands;
  - average basket bands;
  - last purchase recency bands;
  - products / product categories (via line-item facts);
  - site of prior purchases.
- Visit window (default 12h) operator-controllable per parent
  design §6.4.4.
- Add summary strip + facet counts per parent §6.5.
- Data-quality chips: unmatched scans, missing geocode,
  low-confidence matches.
- CSV export of current filter view; raw VeriScan payload
  **excluded** by default per parent §13.
- Definitions tooltip on every purchase metric.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C2`.

### C3 — Customers IA + CRM/Segments move

- New top-level Customers nav with children Check-ins, Map, CRM,
  Segments per parent §4.1.
- Move existing CRM page to `/admin/customers/crm`.
- Move existing Segments page to `/admin/customers/segments`.
- Add backwards-compatible aliases for old CRM/Segments routes per
  parent §4.2; query params must be preserved.
- No functional change to CRM or Segments behaviour; this is IA only.
- Consistent CustomersLayout / breadcrumbs across the four pages.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C3`.

### C4 — Static customer-origin map

- Route `/admin/customers/map` per parent §7.
- MapLibre GL; default NYC-focused viewport; site pins for `bx`
  and `mh` from site metadata (add if not present).
- Server endpoint `GET /api/admin/customers/map` per parent §7.4;
  reference SQL shape in parent §7.5; default `origin=id_address`,
  `agg=grid`, `grid=250m`.
- Server coarsens grid / warns when payload would exceed budget
  (parent §11 perf budgets).
- Shared filters with Check-ins (date, site, purchase history,
  conversion, document/age).
- Encoding panel (Vega-Lite-style) per parent §8.3 with channels
  `color`, `size`, `opacity`, `strokeColor`, `strokeWidth`; always-
  visible legend; colorblind-safe defaults; default preset
  "purchase-repeat-basket" per parent §8.2; encoding config
  serialised in URL state.
- Marker click → inspect drawer with aggregate metrics +
  representative scan IDs + "open matching Check-ins" deep link
  carrying the equivalent filter set.
- No exact home-address pin display by default; exact-point mode
  is gated per parent §7.3 and §13.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C4`.

### C5 — Replay playback

- New endpoint `GET /api/admin/customers/map/timeline` per parent
  §9.3; finite bucketed event series (NOT streaming) per parent
  §9.1; default bucket size per parent §9.4; server coarsens to
  meet feature-count budget (parent §11).
- Playback URL state (`bucket`, `play`, `speed`, `lifetime`,
  `fade`, `loop`, `tail`, `enc`, `viewport`) per parent §9.2;
  share URL restores the full replay configuration.
- Client lifetime/fade math per parent §9.5; default loop behaviour
  `tail=clear` per parent §9.6; small visual pause at reset.
- Controls per parent §9.7: play/pause, scrubber + current
  timestamp, speed/lifetime/fade selectors, loop toggle, reset,
  "open current frame in Check-ins" action.
- Marker rendering uses MapLibre/WebGL layers (NOT thousands of
  DOM markers) so we hit the 30–60fps target on real data
  volumes.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` → loads paused, controls remain
  available; tabular "events in current frame" fallback.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C5`.

### C6 — DEFERRED to separate paused issue

C6 (MP4 export of the replay) is **NOT** in this child epic. It is
filed as a separate paused issue in this repo titled "Customers UX
v2: export customer-origin replay to MP4". That issue is paused on
creation and only un-pauses after C5 lands and the operator
explicitly asks for it. Do not start C6 work as part of this epic.

## Out of scope

- VeriScan webhook ingestion + `visitor_scans` table + backfill CLI
  + ingestion admin page — owned by the sibling
  [`./EPIC_PLAN.md`](./EPIC_PLAN.md) child epic.
- agenix / nginx / systemd / DNS changes — `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`.
- Customer-facing UI of any kind. Helios is operator-only.
- Edit / delete of `visitor_scans`. Append-only ground truth.
- External geocoding / reverse-geocoding.
- Marketing automation, campaign sending, loyalty mutation,
  segment-membership mutation.
- Websocket / Kafka / event-bus realtime architecture.
- MP4 export (C6 — separate paused issue).

## Data-model coordination with the ingestion child epic

The Customers UX needs the following from `visitor_scans` (parent
design §14). Most are already present in the ingestion design; the
items below are coordination points to confirm with the sibling
ingestion epic before C2 lands:

1. Canonical `checked_in_at` — either a normalized column added by
   ingestion or the documented `COALESCE(scanned_at, created_at,
   ingested_at)` contract + matching index per parent §11.
2. `issuing_state` distinct from address `state` (operator
   explicitly listed this as a filter facet).
3. Raw normalized columns for `phone`, `email`, `first_name`,
   `last_name`, `birth_date` for the match layer.
4. Coordinate validity surfacing (zero/null guarded out of the map).
5. Per-row `site_slug` correctness for backfilled rows.
6. Site metadata (display name, store lat/lon, timezone, address)
   reused or added for the map's site pins and distance-from-site
   filter.

If any of these is missing when C2 / C4 start, file a focused
change request against the ingestion child epic before proceeding.

## Phase dependencies

- C1 depends on the ingestion child epic's A1 having landed (table
  + at least one row from webhook or backfill). C1 code can be
  written and unit-tested against the schema in parallel; the
  page-back trigger requires a real live row.
- C2 depends on C1 (shared endpoint + drawer) and on
  CRM/orders being readable from helios-server (already true; the
  existing CRM page reads it).
- C3 depends on C2's CRM/Segments not being broken by the
  move; can land in parallel with C2 if the routes are wired
  carefully.
- C4 depends on C2's match layer + facts views (for purchase
  encodings) and on coordinate-validity guards in `visitor_scans`.
- C5 depends on C4.
- C6 is deferred; do not start.

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. C1..C5 each have at least one commit on `automation` master
   carrying `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9` and the matching
   `Phase: C<n>` trailer.
2. The C1 page-back STATUS comment has been posted on
   [#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9) and the
   operator has confirmed live visibility.
3. At least one live VeriScan check-in is visible end-to-end:
   webhook → row → Check-ins table → matched customer →
   purchase summary → map marker → replay frame.
4. C6 has been filed as a separate paused issue in this repo and
   linked from the C5 completion comment.
declarations.delegationNote: Implement the Helios Customers top-level section consuming visitor_scans and existing CRM/orders data: C1 live Check-ins page (PAGE-BACK TRIGGER per operator — paging on real-row visibility); C2 purchase-history filters/facets with scan→customer match layer + facts views + CSV export; C3 Customers IA moving existing CRM and Segments under /admin/customers/* with old-URL aliases; C4 static MapLibre customer-origin map with Vega-Lite-style encoding picker (color/size/opacity/strokeColor/strokeWidth) + legend + drilldown; C5 finite-bucketed replay playback with operator-controlled speed/lifetime/fade and shareable URL state. C6 MP4 export is explicitly DEFERRED and already filed as paused issue FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#32.

declarations.body:
# Customer / Visitor Address Ingestion — `nixos-sbc` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/visitor-address-ingestion/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in the top-level repo; this child epic scope is **strictly the
> host / network / secret-management slice of that design**.  Every
> implementation commit landing on `nixos-sbc` master that satisfies
> any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9
> ```

## Scope owned by this repo

- **agenix secret** `secrets/veriscan-webhook-token.age` on
  `vps-nixos-3` whose plaintext is the 256-bit hex bearer token
  documented in the agent comment on
  [#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9).
- **`helios-server.service` wiring** — extend the existing systemd
  unit's `EnvironmentFile=` (or equivalent agenix-template
  generated file) to include `VERISCAN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN=<plaintext>`.
  No new unit; the existing helios-server reads it from env at
  startup.
- **Confirm nginx routing** — `helios.freshlybaked.us` already
  proxies to the helios-server backend; verify that the existing
  `location /` (or equivalent catch-all) covers `/wh/*` without
  needing a new server block.  If a path-specific block is needed
  (e.g. to bump body-size limits for VeriScan attachments), add it
  here.
- **Body-size headroom** — VeriScan envelopes can include base64
  payloads (the `PhotoBase64` field is obsolete but still possible);
  ensure nginx `client_max_body_size` on the helios vhost is ≥ 4MB.

## Out of scope

- Helios app code, DB migration, webhook handler, admin page,
  backfill CLI — `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`.
- VeriScan-side webhook configuration — operator.
- Rotation procedure for the bearer token — documented in the
  parent EPIC_PLAN.md §"Bearer token"; mechanical rotation is a
  follow-up if needed.

## Phases

- **N1.** Add the agenix secret and wire it into helios-server's
  environment.  Restart `helios-server` once the FreshlyBakedNYC/automation A1
  release is also live so the env var is consumed by code that
  reads it.  Until then, the env var simply sits unused.
- **N2.** (Conditional) nginx body-size or path-specific tweak if
  the smoke-test in `automation` A1 reveals a default-size
  limitation.  Likely a no-op on the existing config.

## Cross-repo dependencies

- N1 has no upstream dependency.  It unblocks `automation` A1's
  prod deployment (A1 code can be developed and unit-tested
  without N1).
- N2 is reactive — only land if A1 testing surfaces a need.

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. N1 has a landing commit on `nixos-sbc` master carrying
   `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9`.
2. `systemctl show helios-server -p Environment` on `vps-nixos-3`
   (or the equivalent inspection of the rendered agenix template)
   confirms `VERISCAN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` is present.
3. `curl -i -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H
   'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{}'
   https://helios.freshlybaked.us/wh/bx/veriscan/checkin`
   returns the response generated by the helios-server handler
   (post-N1 deployment of A1), not an nginx error.
declarations.delegationNote: agenix secret veriscan-webhook-token.age on vps-nixos-3, EnvironmentFile wiring into helios-server as VERISCAN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN, and verification that nginx for helios.freshlybaked.us proxies /wh/* unchanged.

declarations.body:
# Customer / Visitor Address Ingestion — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/visitor-address-ingestion/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in the top-level repo; this child epic scope is **strictly the
> `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (Helios + ingest monorepo) slice of
> that design**.  Every implementation commit landing on `automation`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: A<n>`
> trailer so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post the
> per-phase progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

Everything described in the parent EPIC_PLAN.md, broken out by phase
below.  Re-read the parent before starting — the section here is a
thin index over the parent rather than a re-statement of the design.

### A1 — DB migration + webhook handler + bearer-token auth

- Alembic / golang-migrate / whatever-helios-uses migration adding
  the `visitor_scans` table with **exactly** the columns, indices,
  and unique constraint defined in the parent design.
- Two routes, mounted on the existing helios-server HTTP router:
  - `POST /wh/bx/veriscan/checkin`
  - `POST /wh/mh/veriscan/checkin`
- Both routes share a single handler whose only per-route input is
  the literal `site_slug` (`'bx'` or `'mh'`) passed by the route
  binding.  Unknown slugs MUST be impossible by construction
  (whitelist at mount time, not at runtime).
- Bearer-token auth middleware that:
  - reads `VERISCAN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` from env at process start;
  - rejects requests with no `Authorization` header (401);
  - parses `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (case-insensitive scheme);
  - compares constant-time against the env value;
  - on mismatch: 401 with no body and a `warn`-level structured
    log including remote IP + path (no token material).
- Envelope validation per parent design (Type, EventId, WebHookId,
  Data.HashId presence).  400 on missing.
- Insert with `ON CONFLICT (provider, hash_id) DO NOTHING`.
- `info`-level structured log of every accepted body keyed by
  `hash_id` (so we have a full audit trail outside the DB).
- Smoke-test: a `curl` example committed under `docs/runbooks/`
  that POSTs a synthetic VeriScan envelope at the local helios-server
  binary and asserts a 200 + row insert.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: A1`.

### A2 — Backfill CLI

- New subcommand on the existing `helios-prep` binary:

  ```
  helios-prep visitor-scans backfill \
      --site=<bx|mh> --provider=veriscan \
      --file=<path> [--dry-run]
  ```

- Accepts JSON array, NDJSON, or CSV (sniffed from extension first,
  content second).
- For each input record, reshapes columns into the VeriScan-envelope
  `Data` schema (the operator-supplied Drive export is a flat row
  dump, not a wire envelope), synthesises an envelope with:
  - `Type='CreateCard'`,
  - `WebHookId=0` and `EventId=<stable hash of HashId>` (so re-runs
    are idempotent and not just "no-op via unique constraint" but
    also produce identical `raw_envelope` JSONB),
  - `Created`/`Sent` set to the file's mtime,
- Calls into the **exact same** insert helper used by A1.
- Reports `inserted=`, `skipped_duplicate=`, `errored=` counts at
  the end; `--dry-run` prints the would-be inserts as JSON Lines.
- Unit tests cover: round-trip with the same file twice yields
  `inserted=N` then `skipped_duplicate=N`; malformed row yields
  `errored=1` and does not abort the run.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: A2`.

### A3 — Admin page

- `/admin/visitors/scans` per parent design.  Sits behind the
  existing helios admin auth (oauth-reverse-proxy).
- Paginated table newest-first, columns + filters per parent.
- Row click → drawer with the full normalised row + a syntax-highlit
  JSON view of `raw_envelope`.
- CSV export of the current filter view (uses the same query the
  table renders, no second source of truth).

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: A3`.

## Out of scope

- DNS / TLS / nginx / agenix / systemd unit changes —
  `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`.
- VeriScan-side webhook configuration — operator.
- Downloading the Drive backfill file — operator hands the file to
  the backfill CLI via `--file=`.
- Any consumer of `visitor_scans` (marketing, segmentation,
  loyalty, geo-analyses).  Later epics will read this table.

## Phase dependencies

- A1 depends on `nixos-sbc` N1 (env var present at runtime).  A1
  code itself can be written and unit-tested without N1; only the
  deployed-to-prod step blocks.
- A2 depends on A1 landing (shared insert helper).
- A3 depends on A1 landing (table must exist).
- A2 and A3 can proceed in parallel.

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. A1, A2, A3 each have at least one commit on `automation` master
   carrying `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9` and the matching
   `Phase:` trailer.
2. The A1 smoke-test (`docs/runbooks/`) runs green against the
   deployed helios-server on `vps-nixos-3`.
3. The operator confirms (via a comment on
   [#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9)) that
   VeriScan webhook configuration on bx + mh points at the
   correct URLs with the correct bearer token, and that at least
   one live check-in has produced a row visible in
   `/admin/visitors/scans`.

issues.body:
We need a vast improvement in our documentation and organization. I find that I keep having to instruct agents the same things over and over again that I'm quite positive I'm documented before, such as to avoid self SSH, Don't try to SSH on port 22, use the `self-deploy*` packages that are installed to do updates in a canonical fashion, reuse canonical UI implementations, always consider and analyze DB performance; generally UI operations should take no more than 500ms to u update and ideally no more than 125ms per DB interaction. Anything measured in multiple seconds is unacceptable. Always use elemental checkouts, always use and update our task-dag tasks, how and when to make use of Oracle, painter, and our private bedrock based remote LLMs, how to use the task-dag commands to leave repo issue updates, etc. 

The information needs to be organized for efficient agent use, minimizing wasted context tokens, and *mandatory* use from all repos. It also *must* be kept up to date by all agents according to the efficiency scheme designed by this ticket's solution.

I'm tired of agents wandering outside of Canon and mandatory instructions and seemingly regressing repeatedly to what is common "in distribution", like trying to use Python for everything (forbidden except tiny one off commands), untyped code, use of /bin/bash rather than `/user/bin/env bash` which is canon on nixos, and especially not realizing that they are almost certainly running *on the production hosts* colocated with the running production or staging services, or at least on a neighboring machine; doing service surgery unnecessarily during deploys (directly restarting a serving service causing 5xxs rather than using the `self-deploy*` packages which will safely turn on mirror modes, etc. 

Similarly, when given instructions and told they are now canonical, agents must persist those instructions in the documentation knowledge base in a way that matches the efficiency design and ensures all agents will always follow them, including future agents started after this change but before a newly given instruction.

delegated_to:

    issue: 5

```

# Helios DB cost reduction (TigerData)

We're burning DB dollars at the current architecture's steady-state rate on the
managed TigerData (Timescale Cloud) instance that backs Helios. The aim of
this epic is to bring monthly spend down by an order of magnitude without
giving up the correctness, freshness, or low-latency properties operators
rely on.

The investigation that motivated this epic is in thread
[T-019e8ac1-0e1e-73a6-bbb7-8c83ac3731f3](https://ampcode.com/threads/T-019e8ac1-0e1e-73a6-bbb7-8c83ac3731f3).

## Cost drivers (current state)

Three reinforcing problems were identified in the
`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` codebase:

1. **A polling architecture that never sleeps.** Two worker loops
   (3 s main, 10 s fast-lane) issue a write-transaction on every
   iteration regardless of whether there is work, plus the scheduler
   runs two SELECTs against `config_worker_schedules{,_runs}` every
   3 s on the main loop.
2. **Per-row transactions inside worker hot loops.** Several worker
   jobs open one transaction per inventory item / per order / per
   variant — measured in millions of write-txns/day on the largest
   ingest path (`sweed_package_snapshots`, every 5 minutes during
   08:00–02:00 ET).
3. **Unbounded "snapshot + raw_json" tables** that we both write to
   constantly and read back with expensive JSONB-unrolling analytics
   queries (e.g. the `/metrics` catalog-analytics endpoint that does
   `cross join lateral jsonb_array_elements(so.raw_json->'items')`
   plus a per-row `sweed_package_cost_as_of_or_earliest(...)`
   correlated lookup).

A fourth, smaller contributor: several operator dashboard pages
auto-poll the server on short intervals, which in turn drives DB
reads at that cadence whenever an operator has the tab open.

## Hard constraint — DO NOT throttle live customer check-ins / scans

The
[`/visitors/scans`](https://helios.freshlybaked.us/visitors/scans)
page (and any equivalent surface for live VeriScan ingestion in the
future) MUST keep its near-real-time freshness. The current
implementation polls every 20 s; that polling cadence is not the
target of any throttling work in this epic. If the eventual
"reduce client auto-poll" work would otherwise sweep this page up,
the implementer's job is to **change the mechanism** (e.g. a
WebSocket / SSE push from the ingest webhook into the operator
UI; a Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY` fan-out; a per-scan event hook) so
that the operator continues to see scans appear within a couple
of seconds of the door, without paying the per-tab steady-state
DB-poll cost.

The same constraint applies to anything else operators rely on as
"live" feedback during a shift (jobs page during an operator-initiated
run, pricing-run detail page while a run is executing, etc.) — if the
underlying refresh cadence is operator-facing and tied to in-shift
work, change the mechanism rather than throttle it.

## Already shipped (before this epic was filed)

Commit
[`abb0b6f`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/commit/abb0b6f)
on `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation@master`, deployed to `vps-nixos-3`
via `self-deploy-helios`:

- **A.1** `sweed_package_snapshots` bulk upsert
  (`jsonb_to_recordset(...)` × DISTINCT-ON-PK SELECT in one txn per
  dealer instead of one txn per package).
- **B.1** In-process 60 s cache of `loadAllConfigSchedules()` with
  in-cache patch on every `recordConfigScheduleEnqueue`.
- **B.3** Polynomial (n^1.5, cap 15 s) empty-poll backoff in the
  worker lease loop.

This epic plans and tracks the rest.

## What's left to plan + ship

In rough priority order (also priority of $ saved per hour of work):

### A. Bulk-upsert the other per-row-txn ingest paths

A.2. `configWorkersStockRefreshJob` — per-variant
     `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` on `stock_variant_state`
     plus per-transitioning-variant `SELECT … pending_litalerts_refresh_queue`
     plus per-brand upsert on `landingpage_brand_site_presence`.
A.3. `configWorkersSweedOrdersIngestJob` — per-invoice
     `SELECT EXISTS(... sweed_orders WHERE customer_id = $1 AND pay_time < $2)`
     then per-invoice `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. The overlap-window
     poll means many of these are no-ops the DB still pays for.
A.4. `enqueueMarketRefresh` / scheduler's litalerts batch — the
     `for (const row of pendingRows) { await withTransaction(...) }`
     pattern that turns a 50-row batch into 50 transactions.
A.5. `configWorkersLitalertsRefreshJob` — ~5–7 round-trips per
     variant refresh job (queue load, catalog-group JSONB containment,
     brand expiry, prior observation lookup, observation insert,
     queue-row update, audit row). Compress to a single CTE or at
     least batch within one transaction.

### B. Calm the polling loops further

B.2. Run the expired-lease sweep in `leaseJobs` only once per
     minute (e.g. behind a lightweight per-process timestamp guard)
     instead of on every poll. The sweep currently runs every 3 s
     even when there is nothing to lease.
B.4. Add Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY` from `enqueueJob` so the worker
     wakes immediately on new work and can sleep longer between
     idle polls (i.e. raise the idle-backoff cap further without
     hurting wake-up latency). Live work paths that need this most:
     operator-initiated pricing runs, scheduling runs, ads ingest,
     anything page-dave triggers.

### C. Bound the fat tables (Timescale-native)

C.1. Convert append-only time-indexed tables to hypertables and add
     compression policies: `sweed_orders`, `sweed_package_snapshots`,
     `litalerts_competitor_observations`, `parsekit_reverse_shadow_events`,
     `audit_events`. Typical compression ratio for our row shape is
     5–15× storage reduction plus dramatically cheaper IO on aged data.
C.2. Add retention policies on diagnostic/audit data:
     `parsekit_reverse_shadow_events`, `sweed_auth_events`,
     `audit_events` (operator-tunable per table).
C.3. Stop storing `raw_json` on tables where every needed field is
     already normalised, OR move `raw_json` into a separate
     `*_raw` table with its own (shorter) retention. Re-derive
     anything we forgot from a one-time re-ingest rather than from
     a per-row stored blob.

### D. Materialise the hot dashboard queries

D.1. Build `sweed_order_line_items` (the schema TODO that's been
     written down since #24 was filed) so catalog-analytics, COGS,
     and the upcoming sell-through reports stop doing
     `cross join lateral jsonb_array_elements(...)` × correlated
     `sweed_package_cost_as_of_or_earliest(...)` per request.
     Populate it incrementally from the orders-ingest job.
D.2. Timescale continuous-aggregates for the per-day / per-dealer
     rollups on the `/metrics` page tree.

### E. Throttle / replace client auto-refresh (subject to the constraint above)

E.1. Audit every client-side `setInterval(... loadX, ...)` and either
     raise the cadence (when staleness is acceptable) or switch the
     mechanism (when it isn't — see the constraint above).
     Confirmed candidates from the investigation:
     `TasksPage` (10 s), `TaskFrontierPage` (10 s), `EpicDagPage` (30 s),
     `JobsPage`, `SweedAuthLogPage`, `PricingRunsPage`,
     `PricingRunDetailPage`, `SchedulingRunDetailPage`,
     `AdsIngestPage`, `PendingMigrationsBanner`,
     `ConfigParsingPendingPurchasesPage`,
     `CustomerReviewsDrawingPage`.
     **Excluded** (must stay live, even if mechanism must change):
     `VisitorScansPage` and any future operator-facing live-scan UI.

## Repos involved

This epic is effectively single-repo: every ingest job, query,
hypertable migration, route, and client-side refresh under audit
lives in
[`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
(the helios + ingest monorepo). Per the cross-repo task-dag driver
model we still file **one** child epic in that repo and delegate
this top-level epic to it; the parent epic exists only to give the
operator a single point of truth here and to gate closure on the
child landing `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#<this-issue>`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Steady-state TigerData write-transactions per day drop by at
   least **10×** versus the pre-A.1 baseline (commit `abb0b6f`'s
   own contribution counts; we measure on top of that).
2. TigerData storage growth per week drops by at least **5×**,
   sustained for at least one full poll-window after C.1 + C.3
   land.
3. The `/metrics` catalog-analytics endpoint p95 server-side query
   time drops to ≤ 500 ms on the current default 90-day window
   (currently multi-second).
4. The hard constraint above (live VeriScan scans page stays
   real-time) is demonstrably preserved on `vps-nixos-3` after
   every shipped phase. Operator confirms by checking the live
   page during a check-in.
5. No silent correctness regression: every ingest path has a
   before / after row-count + content spot-check posted in the
   shipping commit's body.

## Out of scope

- Switching DB providers (e.g. self-hosted Postgres, Aurora, Neon,
  CrunchyData). Even if doing so would also reduce cost, it would
  push out the engineering surface this epic intentionally keeps
  bounded.
- Architectural changes that block on multi-region. Single-region
  on TigerData is assumed throughout.
- Adding caching layers in front of the DB (Redis, etc.). The
  point of this epic is to make the DB cheap, not to dress around
  it.

## See also

- Investigation thread:
  [T-019e8ac1-0e1e-73a6-bbb7-8c83ac3731f3](https://ampcode.com/threads/T-019e8ac1-0e1e-73a6-bbb7-8c83ac3731f3).
- Already-shipped commit:
  [FreshlyBakedNYC/automation@abb0b6f](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/commit/abb0b6f).


```yaml
delegated_to:
  - repo: FreshlyBakedNYC/automation
    issue: 39
    note: Bulk-upsert the remaining per-row-txn ingest paths (A2-A5), gate the worker expired-lease sweep + add LISTEN/NOTIFY wake-up (B2/B4), convert append-only tables to Timescale hypertables with compression + retention (C1/C2) and stop storing redundant raw_json (C3), materialise sweed_order_line_items + continuous-aggregate the /metrics rollups (D1/D2), and audit/replace client-side auto-refresh cadences (E1) WITHOUT throttling the live VeriScan scans page (mechanism swap, not cadence drop).
```

The phases below are the remaining work. --- ### Phase A2 — `configWorkersStockRefreshJob` bulk upsert Files: `helios/src/worker/jobs/configWorkersStockRefreshJob.ts` (primary) plus any new query helper in `helios/src/server/db/queries/`. - Replace the per-row loop on `stock_variant_state` with a single `INSERT … SELECT FROM jsonb_to_recordset(...) … ON CONFLICT (...) DO UPDATE …` (one statement per dealer, chunked at `BULK_CHUNK_SIZE = 500` for safety — same shape as the A1 commit). - Replace the per-transitioning-variant guard SELECT against `pending_litalerts_refresh_queue` with a single `INSERT … FROM jsonb_to_recordset(...) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` that relies on the existing partial unique index. - Replace the per-brand upsert loop on `landingpage_brand_site_presence` with one bulk `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` per dealer. - All of the above inside the single existing per-dealer transaction. - Validation: - Before / after row count on `stock_snapshot_items`, `stock_variant_state`, `pending_litalerts_refresh_queue`, and `landingpage_brand_site_presence` for one full poll, posted in the commit body. - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` snippet for the new bulk statements. - Operator sign-off that the live VeriScan scans page still updates in real time post-deploy. Commits MUST carry `Phase: A2`. ### Phase A3 — `configWorkersSweedOrdersIngestJob` bulk upsert Files: `helios/src/worker/jobs/configWorkersSweedOrdersIngestJob.ts`. - Replace the per-invoice `SELECT EXISTS(...)` + `INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` loop with: - one bulk `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING … RETURNING` over the incoming batch via `jsonb_to_recordset`; - one set-based CTE that computes `first_time_for_customer` for the newly-inserted rows in a single pass against `sweed_orders` (uses the existing `sweed_orders_customer_pay_time_idx` partial index). - Highwater bump stays unchanged. - Validation: - Backfill-equivalence check: run the new path on a held-aside dealer for one full poll, diff resulting `sweed_orders` rows + `first_time_for_customer` column against the pre-deploy snapshot. - Operator sign-off as above. Commits MUST carry `Phase: A3`. ### Phase A4 — Litalerts batch + `enqueueMarketRefreshForProducts` bulk transactions Files: `helios/src/worker/runtime/configWorkersScheduler.ts` (scheduler batch path) and `helios/src/worker/litalerts/enqueueMarketRefresh.ts`. - Collapse `for (const row of pendingRows) { await withTransaction(...) }` into one transaction per batch: - one bulk insert into `job_queue` (the existing `enqueueJob` helper grows a `enqueueJobs` plural variant that takes an array and uses `INSERT … SELECT FROM jsonb_to_recordset`); - one bulk `appendAuditEvent` (likewise, a plural variant); - one `recordEnqueueAndPatchCache` call at the end of the batch. - Preserve the single-flight dedupe-key behaviour. - Validation: - Count of `job_queue` rows inserted per scheduler tick before / after. - Operator sign-off as above. Commits MUST carry `Phase: A4`. ### Phase A5 — `configWorkersLitalertsRefreshJob` round-trip compression Files: `helios/src/worker/jobs/configWorkersLitalertsRefreshJob.ts` plus index migration under `helios/src/server/db/migrations/`. - Combine the queue-row load, catalog-group containment search, brand-expiry lookup, and (when needed) prior-observation lookup into a **single CTE** that returns the assembled context in one round-trip. - Add a GIN index on `catalog_groups.live_state_json` (or a computed jsonb_path_ops index on `live_state_json -> 'products'`) so the existing `(... -> 'products') @> $1::jsonb` containment search stops doing a sequential scan. Verify via `EXPLAIN` before declaring done. - The observation insert + queue-row update + audit row stay in one transaction (already true) but use a single multi-statement pipeline rather than three sequential awaits where possible. - Validation: - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` showing the new containment index is used. - Throughput / round-trip count per job before / after. - Operator sign-off as above. Commits MUST carry `Phase: A5`. ### Phase B2 — Gate the expired-lease sweep Files: `helios/src/worker/runtime/leaseJobs.ts`. - Move the unconditional `UPDATE job_queue SET status='queued' … WHERE status='running' AND leased_until < now()` out of the per-poll path and behind a per-process timestamp guard (e.g. run at most once per minute per worker process). The guard MUST survive a process restart cleanly (i.e., default to "sweep on first tick post-startup" so we don't lose recovery semantics). - Validation: - Count of `job_queue` UPDATEs issued during a 5-minute idle window before / after. - Confirm by deliberately leaving a leased row past its deadline that the sweep still picks it up within one minute. Commits MUST carry `Phase: B2`. ### Phase B4 — `LISTEN/NOTIFY` wake-up + idle-cap raise Files: `helios/src/worker/runtime/workerLoop.ts`, `helios/src/server/jobs/enqueueJob.ts`, and any new `helios/src/server/db/notify.ts`. - `enqueueJob` (and the new `enqueueJobs` plural from A4) emits `NOTIFY helios_job_queue` after a successful commit. - The worker lease loop opens a dedicated `LISTEN` connection that races with the `delay(...)` in the idle-backoff path: whichever resolves first re-enters the lease loop. (Don't share the LISTEN connection with the lease-CTE client; a dedicated pool connection is cheap and avoids pg client-state weirdness.) - With LISTEN/NOTIFY in place, raise the empty-poll backoff cap from 15 s to 60 s. Live work paths now have sub-second wake-up latency, so the cap raise is free. - Validation: - End-to-end latency from `enqueueJob` returning to the worker actually leasing the row, before / after. Target: ≤ 200 ms in the post-B4 world. - Count of `leaseJobs` round-trips during a 5-minute idle window before / after. Commits MUST carry `Phase: B4`. ### Phase C1 — Hypertables + compression Files: new migrations under `helios/src/server/db/migrations/` (one per table), and probably a `helios/scripts/explain-coverage.ts` or equivalent EXPLAIN-diff helper to compare pre/post planner choices. Tables to convert (in order, smallest-first to validate the pattern): 1. `parsekit_reverse_shadow_events` — small, easy validator. 2. `sweed_auth_events`. 3. `audit_events`. 4. `litalerts_competitor_observations`. 5. `sweed_orders`. 6. `sweed_package_snapshots`. For each: - `create_hypertable(...)` with an appropriate `chunk_time_interval` (sized so each chunk is in the low-GB range under current write volume — start at 1 day for high-write tables, 7 days for diagnostics). - Re-create every existing index ON THE HYPERTABLE; verify via `EXPLAIN` that every production query path still uses the expected index post-conversion. - Add `add_compression_policy(..., interval ...)` with `compress_orderby` and `compress_segmentby` matching the table's access pattern (typically segment-by dealer_id and order-by the time column DESC). - Each migration MUST be reversible (drop the policy + decompress + drop the hypertable in a `down` migration) so we can back out cleanly if the planner regresses. Validation per table: post the size before/after compression, plus the EXPLAIN diff for the top 3 production queries hitting that table. Commits MUST carry `Phase: C1`. ### Phase C2 — Retention policies Files: migrations under `helios/src/server/db/migrations/`, plus a small `/config/workers` UI surface for the operator-tunable knobs. - Operator-tunable retention windows (in days, persisted in a new `db_retention_policies` table) for: - `parsekit_reverse_shadow_events` (default 30 d), - `sweed_auth_events` (default 90 d), - `audit_events` (default 365 d). - Each tunable read/write through a new `/api/config/db-retention` route + UI panel under `/config/workers` (operator can raise / lower the window per table). - The actual purge is `add_retention_policy` on the hypertable; changing the window via the UI invokes `alter_job(...) SET schedule_interval / config` on the existing retention job. - Validation: alter one window down to 1 day in staging-equivalent data and verify the next policy run removes the expected rows; raise back to default. Commits MUST carry `Phase: C2`. ### Phase C3 — Stop storing `raw_json` where it's redundant Files: schemas + ingest jobs across `helios/src/worker/jobs/` and `helios/src/server/db/schema/`. Per-table decision tree: - `sweed_package_snapshots`: every consumer reads typed columns; drop `raw_json` from the steady-state table and store it in a new `sweed_package_snapshots_raw` table with 30 d retention (so we still have a one-month rollback window for "re-derive a field we forgot"). - `sweed_orders`: catalog-analytics still unrolls `raw_json->'items'`; D1 removes that dependency. Once D1 lands, apply the same split here. - `litalerts_competitor_observations.evidence_json`: every read parses the same handful of fields. Project them into typed columns; move `evidence_json` to `_raw` with 30 d retention. - `parsekit_reverse_shadow_events`: 3 JSONB columns, all read on the diagnostics page. Project the per-page-needed fields, keep the rest in `_raw` with the C2 retention window. Validation: for each touched table, demonstrate (via the existing test suite + a one-shot sample query against staging-equivalent data) that no consumer path regresses. Commits MUST carry `Phase: C3`. ### Phase D1 — `sweed_order_line_items` Files: new migration, new query helper, modified ingest job. - New table: `sweed_order_line_items (dealer_id, invoice_id, line_seq, inventory_item_id, product_id, current_qty, subtotal_amount, wholesale_cost_dollars_as_of, …)` keyed by `(dealer_id, invoice_id, line_seq)` and indexed for the existing catalog-analytics joins. - `configWorkersSweedOrdersIngestJob` populates it incrementally alongside the `sweed_orders` insert (same transaction, same batch — bulk insert via `jsonb_to_recordset`). - One-time backfill script under `helios/scripts/backfill-sweed-order-line-items.ts` that walks `sweed_orders.raw_json -> 'items'` historically and populates the new table; idempotent via the PK so reruns are cheap. - Rewrite `helios/src/server/catalogAnalytics/catalogAnalyticsQueries.ts` to read from `sweed_order_line_items` instead of unrolling jsonb at request time. Validation: - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` before / after on the `/api/catalog-analytics` query at the default 90-day window; must hit the ≤ 500 ms p95 target. - Diff of the API response between the old and new query path on one site, demonstrating identical numbers. Commits MUST carry `Phase: D1`. ### Phase D2 — Continuous aggregates for `/metrics` Files: new migrations, route handlers under `helios/src/server/budtenderAnalytics/`, `helios/src/server/customerValueAnalytics/`, `helios/src/server/catalogAnalytics/`. - One Timescale continuous-aggregate per `(dealer_id, day, granularity)` rollup the metric pages currently compute at request time. - Route handlers read from the CAGG; "real-time" tail (the last few hours) is computed on-the-fly via the existing CTE and unioned in (Timescale's `materialized only` / real-time aggregation pattern). - Refresh policy: every 15 min during business hours, hourly overnight. Validation: - p95 server-side query time on every `/metrics` route after D2; ≤ 200 ms target. - Numeric equivalence sample on one site for the prior 7 days. Commits MUST carry `Phase: D2`. ### Phase E1 — Client auto-refresh audit + selective mechanism swap Files: `helios/src/client/routes/**/*.tsx`, plus the new push-mechanism plumbing (likely `helios/src/client/lib/realtime/visitorScans.ts` and a server-side SSE / WebSocket route). **Throttle bucket** (cadence raise, no mechanism change): - `TasksPage` (10 s → 60 s) - `TaskFrontierPage` (10 s → 60 s) - `EpicDagPage` (30 s → 300 s) - `JobsPage`, `JobDetailPage` (only between an operator-initiated state change; default cadence raise to 60 s; preserve the existing "tighter cadence while a run is pending" branch) - `SweedAuthLogPage` (raise to 60 s) - `PricingRunsPage` (raise to 60 s) - `SchedulingRunDetailPage` (raise to 30 s between runs; preserve the "tight cadence during a run" branch) - `AdsIngestPage` (raise to 60 s) - `PendingMigrationsBanner` (raise to 5 min) - `ConfigParsingPendingPurchasesPage` (raise to 60 s) - `CustomerReviewsDrawingPage` (the 5 s `setNowMs` is a display-clock tick, not a fetch — verify with grep before touching). **Mechanism-swap bucket** (must remain live, throttle forbidden): - `VisitorScansPage` — swap the 20 s `setInterval` for a server-pushed event stream: - server: `GET /api/visitors/scans/stream` SSE endpoint that emits a new event whenever the VeriScan webhook handler persists a row. Implementation: webhook handler calls `pgNotify('visitor_scans_new', JSON.stringify({ id, siteSlug, capturedAt }))` post-commit; the SSE route holds a long-lived LISTEN connection and pipes notifications back out. - client: open the SSE on mount; on each event, refetch only the head of the list (`/api/visitors/scans?since=`) and prepend the new rows. Reconnect with jittered exponential backoff on disconnect. - operator-visible behaviour: a scan at the door appears in the open browser tab in ≤ 2 s, indistinguishably from the current 20-s-poll worst case but at a fraction of the DB cost. - Add any other "during-shift live feedback" page surfaced during the audit to this bucket BEFORE applying any throttle. Validation: - For each touched page, post the before / after cadence + bucket classification in the commit body (parent epic's E1 description requires this). - Operator-visible smoke test of the live-scan SSE on `vps-nixos-3` after deploy. Commits MUST carry `Phase: E1`. --- ## Conventions - Every commit MUST carry both `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#11` and the appropriate `Phase:

` trailer. - Every commit MUST be deployable in isolation (the worker / server must boot and pass `self-deploy-helios` health checks after the commit alone). - Validation evidence (row counts, EXPLAIN diffs, operator sign-offs) goes in the commit body, not in a separate STATUS file — STATUS files in this epic's directory are reserved for "operator changed direction" events.
declarations.delegationNote: Bulk-upsert the remaining per-row-txn ingest paths (A2-A5), gate the worker expired-lease sweep + add LISTEN/NOTIFY wake-up (B2/B4), convert append-only tables to Timescale hypertables with compression + retention (C1/C2) and stop storing redundant raw_json (C3), materialise sweed_order_line_items + continuous-aggregate the /metrics rollups (D1/D2), and audit/replace client-side auto-refresh cadences (E1) WITHOUT throttling the live VeriScan scans page (mechanism swap, not cadence drop).

# Customer check-in → Sweed link, enriched admin view, cashier live view — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md). Re-read the parent
> before starting any phase — this child epic is a thin index over
> the parent's design, not a re-statement of it.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#12
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: B<n>`
> trailer so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post per-
> phase progress on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

Everything in the parent EPIC_PLAN.md §3, phases B1–B5:

- **B1.** Unblock the Sweed find-by-`documentNumber` RPC in
  `helios/src/worker/sweed/customers.ts`. Wire it into the existing
  visitor-scan link worker. Add the person-key-seen-before fast-path
  that lowers `next_probe_at` to `now()` for repeat visitors so the
  link populates sub-second. Retire the
  `NEEDS_OPERATOR_VERIFICATION` comment block.

- **B2.** Migration `041_sweed_customer_profile_snapshots.sql` per
  parent §3-B2 (table + indices). New worker job
  `refreshSweedCustomerProfileSnapshotJob` that computes #purchases
  / total / avg / favorite category / favorite product from the
  existing `sweed_orders` + `sweed_package_snapshots` tables. The
  `>= 3` repeat-count gate for favorites lives in the snapshot
  generator, not in the read path. Scheduled on (a) successful link
  in the link worker, (b) a daily cron tick for linked customers
  whose `snapshotted_at` is older than 24h.

- **B3.** Augment the existing `/admin/customers/check-ins` page
  (alias of `/admin/visitors/scans`) loader and table component
  with: `# Purchases`, `Avg $`, `Total $`, `Favorite Category`,
  `Favorite Product`. Single LEFT JOIN through `visitor_scan_links`
  → `sweed_customer_profile_snapshots`; NO N+1. Favorite columns
  blank when snapshot's repeat-count gate isn't met.

- **B4.** New cashier live view at
  `/admin/checkout-counter/check-ins` (final URL is operator's call
  — see parent §7). Components:
  - `CheckoutCounterPage.tsx` — landscape-tablet layout, reuses
    the visitor-scans table component in `privacyRedacted` mode.
  - `privacyRedacted` table mode: forces `expanded=off`, renders
    `FirstName L.` only, hides DOB / address / phone / email /
    id_num. Sweed aggregate columns (B3) stay visible (not PII).
  - New SSE route `GET /api/check-ins/stream` on the existing
    `helios-server` fastify app. In-process `EventEmitter`
    published-to by the existing webhook handler (after the link
    row is seeded) and by the link worker (after `linked` /
    `ambiguous` / `no_match` transitions). On connect: one bounded
    "last 20" query (no polling thereafter). See parent §0 — this
    is the DB-cost cap.
  - Two chime assets bundled at
    `helios/src/client/assets/audio/chime-first.ogg` and
    `chime-returning.ogg`. Click-to-enable overlay handles the
    browser autoplay policy + Notification permission in one
    gesture.
  - Browser Notification API on each event with the redacted name,
    first-vs-returning, last-visit date.

- **B5.** Auth gate on the cashier route + SSE endpoint that
  restricts to user `internal.shared_accounts@freshlybaked.nyc`.
  When that user lands on `/admin/customers/check-ins`, redirect
  to the cashier page so the un-redacted view is unreachable from
  their session. When they're on the admin check-ins page (e.g.
  via redirect race), apply the same name-redaction the cashier
  page uses — the operator was explicit about this:
  > the customer list should be like this as well on this
  > particular page, for enhanced privacy.

## Out of scope (deferred / other epics)

- Sweed CRM customer **creation** when there's no documentNumber
  match — owned by the existing customer-sentiment capture flow.
- Multi-tenant cashier RBAC beyond the one shared-account email.
- Host-level config (no `nixos-sbc` changes; nginx `proxy_buffering
  off` for the SSE location is an in-repo deploy concern, handled
  in `automation` alongside B4).

## Per-phase DB-cost statements (canon §3 — REQUIRED)

Every commit landing a phase MUST include, in the commit body:

```
DB-cost:
  per-request: <op count + index used>
  per-day:     <upper bound for steady-state>
  index:       <name(s) the path relies on>
  caching:     <TTL / pub-sub / materialisation>
```

Reviewers should reject phase commits missing this block.

## Phases — task-dag

Use the existing `scripts/task-dag` flow:

```
scripts/task-dag frontier --issue=<child-epic issue number>
# pick a leaf, do real work, then:
scripts/task-dag complete <task-sha>
git push origin HEAD:master
```

Never create empty tombstone commits for new work. Phase order is
strictly **B1 → B2 → B3 → B4 → B5**; B3 and B4 can be cut from the
same change set if both rely on B2 already being live (which they do).

## Operator pre-reqs (do not implement until done)

- Sweed session UUID pasted into the token pool at
  https://helios.freshlybaked.us/config/sweed/sessions. The new
  token supplied with the parent request is the one to paste.
  Without an active pool token, B1's Sweed RPC will return
  `Auth expired` and the worker will retire the env-fallback path.

Currently we have two mostly distinct concepts: "google ads that point to landing pages" which are ostensibly understood by and optimized by Helios in `automation`, and "landing pages being pointed to" which live (almost) entirely downstream of Helios in the `mostly-static-sites` repo.

This split doesn't really make sense.  The bare infrastructure to be able to serve these partially dynamic pages should certainly live in the mss repo, but the "brains" behind the contents of them, and the contents themselves, needs to live under Helios control so the entire system can operate as a single optimization engine at large scale holistically.

Carefully analyze the current cross-repo design and operation, and (using a consensus from Oracle and our best bedrock 1-off LLM (higher cost LLM is OK for this one-off design effort)) design what the unified system should look like as a single core set of Helios capabilities and propose a safe, zero-downtime migration plan onto that architecture.  Use `page-dave` to alert me when the proposals are ready for review.  Once approved, the entire process will be broken down using `task-dag` and implemented.

    issue: 9
    note: Thin-runtime slice. BINDING: do NOT change the canonical /SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM URL schema; wire the CEL evaluator into the existing random-rotation middleware so bundle weights/kill-list bias NUM (parent EPIC_PLAN rev 3 section 6.1).
```
