# Unified landing-page engine — `mostly-static-sites` (thin runtime) child epic

> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) (rev 3). Re-read the parent
> before starting any phase — this child epic is a **thin index** over
> the parent's design, not a re-statement of it. The parent is
> authoritative; if this file ever drifts from it, the parent wins.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#13
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>`
> trailer so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post per-phase
> progress on the parent issue.

## ⚠️ Binding constraint: do NOT change the canonical URL schema

The operator rejected the manufactured `/r/<family>` and
`…/lp/<family>/<param-tuple>/b/<branch_id>` routes. **Keep the existing
canonical schema** (parent §6.1, rev-3):

```
/SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM   ·   NUM=0 = random-rotation distributor alias
```

implemented today in
[`apps/freshlybakedus-site/middleware.ts`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/apps/freshlybakedus-site/middleware.ts)
and
[`apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/purpose-families.ts`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/purpose-families.ts).
The `/0` re-roll `307`, the `utm_content=NUM:N` rewrite, and the
legacy/vacant-variant redirects already implement the URL-embedded
scatter. **No new route shapes. No Google-Ads final-URL changes.** The
one change is *who decides `NUM`*: the bundle's weights/kill-list bias
the pick instead of a uniform `Math.random()`.

## Scope owned by this repo (the thin, fast substrate)

Everything in the parent EPIC_PLAN §4 ("mss owns") and the mss slice of
the §10 phases:

- **`/cloud` bundle loader/validator/cache** — background poller reads
  the read-only `/cloud` artifact root, validates schema + `sha256` +
  signature + `min_renderer_version`, atomically swaps an in-memory
  active bundle, keeps last-known-good (N=3), **fail-closed** (never
  serve unvalidated content), exposes health
  (`loaded_bundle_id`, `validation_status`, pointer age). Off the render
  hot path; verify `/cloud` POSIX atomic-rename in P2 (parent §5, §8).
- **Sandboxed CEL evaluator wired into the EXISTING random-rotation
  middleware** — replaces the uniform `pickRandomVariant()` draw with a
  bundle-weighted (optionally gclid/gbraid/wbraid HMAC-keyed for
  per-click reproducibility) pick of `NUM`, then reuses the existing
  `utm_content=NUM:N` redirect/rewrite path unchanged. Pinned `NUM`
  (explicit `utm_content` or direct `/…/N` link) wins — no re-select
  (parent §6, §6.1). Evaluator is pure: no clock/RNG/`eval`, bounded.
- **Signed variant-kill-list enforcement at the existing variant
  route** — a dead `(site,purpose,slug,num)` redirects to the
  replacement/champion `NUM` via the existing `matchVacantVariantRedirect`
  machinery, logging `requested_num` vs `served_num` (parent §6.1).
- **X1–X5 component renderers** (data-driven from the bundle); validate
  the frozen X2 is present in every family stack (parent §7).
- **Sweed menu adapter/cache (X4)** + **delivery-zone gate** — request-
  time within the ~150 ms cap with stale/fallback; gate feeds policy
  inputs so Helios never optimizes unserviceable ZIPs (parent §7;
  decision 6: ROI control only, no OCM retention).
- **Durable local event spool + ~15-min batch flusher** → Helios
  `POST /v1/lp-events/batch`; at-least-once with per-render `event_id`
  idempotency; backpressure sheds telemetry, never blocks render
  (parent §8; decision 4). **Zero DB reads on the render path.**
- **Shadow/canary support + observability** — `LP_RUNTIME_MODE`,
  allowlists/percent, kill switch, parity + render dashboards
  (parent §10).
- Keep `MAX_VARIANT_BY_PURPOSE` / `*VariantIds` as the drift guard;
  reject any bundle referencing a `NUM` outside the active registry.

## Relationship to the gemini-clusters epic (#5)

This **supersedes the not-yet-built mss slice (M1–M5) of #5** — build
the thin runtime + bundle contract here rather than building
selection/content logic into mss and ripping it out (parent §2, §15).

## Phases

Follow parent §10 order (mss slice): P0 inventory routes/families ·
P1 (Helios-led) · P2 bundle loader (no render change) + stand up event
spool · P3 shadow-compare selection · P4 preview render (both entry
modes already exist: `/0` re-roll and direct `/…/N`) · P5 consume
bundle content · P6 canary + revenue guardrail · P7 full · P8
decommission mss-owned selection/asset ownership + cross-repo commit
consumer. See parent §10 for traffic-impact and rollback columns.

  decision 1: CEL, never `eval`). **Critical schema constraint
  (parent §6.1, rev-3):** the policy output is a **weight per `NUM`**

  `NUM` that mss can't serve.

  overrides + approved copy/imagery + policy into one immutable,
  signed, versioned bundle; writes it to the read-only-for-mss `/cloud`
  artifact root behind an atomic `current.json` pointer with
  last-known-good (parent §5, decision 5). Signing keys live with
  Helios, **never** on the shared mount.

  `(site, purpose, slug, num)` variant tuple (`disabled_variants`, parent
  §6.1) — narrow, monotonic, auditable; not a second policy language.

  bulk insert into time + `bundle_id`/`policy_id`-partitioned tables
  (parent §8; decision 4: log ALL, cost-bounded by mss-side spool +
  ~15-min batch; no sampling). Every new query ships with an analyzed
  plan + index strategy (canon §3).

  served + counterfactual variants (parent §6, §9); surfaces deltas so
  "shut off the loser" is statistically honest. Promotion stays a
  one-click operator action.
- **Validation CLI** (`helios lp-bundle validate`) + dry-run publish.
- **Delete the cross-repo commit producer** — content flows only via
  the bundle (parent §1 defect 2, §10 P5/P8).

  change (parent decision 2, §7).

 - "page-embeddable FAQ with SEO-optimized folded text", with option to run in both raw (FB.nyc) and cannabis-sanitized (FB.us) modes.

This should include both raw and sanitized modes as well.  Content will be reviewable and editable in Helios, and rough posting schedule, topic prompts, etc will be configured there. These blog posts will also merit generated images in some cases, which may be approved or rejected independently by the reviewer

issues.body:
The Helios catalog-review page (`/catalog/review`) takes ~2 s to load and is unresponsive to input after loading — violating the canon performance budget (UI ≤500 ms, DB ≤125 ms; "multiple seconds is unacceptable").

Grounded in **direct production measurement** of `GET /api/review/family-queue`:

- Loads the **entire** pending queue every time: **3,181 line items across 443 families**, no pagination.
- Server exec ~900 ms, wall ~1.35 s, **~2.4 MB** payload, **~600 MB** executor allocation per call.
- The relational join path is **already indexed and fast (11 ms)** — indexing is *not* the problem. The ~890 ms is per-row JSON cracking (`jsonb_array_elements` ×3,181 + 4× `regexp_replace`) because the family key (`sizeName`) lives inside `live_state_json`, so grouping/paging can't happen in SQL.

**Root causes:** (1) no pagination, (2) JSON-as-query-surface, (3) client mounts all pricing ladders.

Authoritative design (measurements, Oracle review, phases A–E, acceptance criteria): `docs/epics/review-page-performance/EPIC_PLAN.md`.

Phases: **A** server family-aware keyset pagination + minimal client paging (the 9×+ win) · **B** `catalog_group_products` projection table (size/price SQL-visible) · **C** client UX parity with pending-purchases review (lazy ladders, group-level actions, group-aware pagination) · **D** resolve dead MSO filter · **E** (stretch) precomputed preview columns.

Out of scope: competitor-match correctness (0.5 g comps for a 2 g family) — tracked separately.

Implementation in Helios (`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`) via the child epic delegated below.


```yaml
delegated_to:
  - repo: FreshlyBakedNYC/automation
    issue: 45
    note: Implementation of top-level#16 in Helios. Start with Phase A (server pagination + minimal client paging) for the 9x+ win; do NOT add join-path indexes (measured fast).
```

declarations.body:
# Helios `/catalog/review` perf & UX — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#16](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/16).
> The authoritative design (measurements, root-cause analysis, phase
> rationale, Oracle review) is
> [`docs/epics/review-page-performance/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in the top-level repo. Read it first. This file is the repo-local
> implementation breakdown.
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `automation` master and
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#16
> Phase: <A|B|C|D|E>
> ```

## Where the code lives

- Slow endpoint query:
  `helios/src/server/db/queries/reviewFamilyQueueQueries.ts`
  (`listReviewFamilyQueue`).
- Route: `helios/src/server/routes/review.ts`
  (`GET /api/review/family-queue`).
- Contract: `helios/src/shared/contracts/api/review.ts`
  (`ReviewFamilyQueueQuerySchema`, `ReviewFamilyQueueResponseSchema`).
- Live-state writer (Phase B projection hook):
  `helios/src/worker/jobs/catalogGroupPersistence.ts`
  (`updateCatalogGroupLiveState`).
- Migration sentinels: `helios/src/server/db/pendingMigrations.ts`.
- Migrations: `helios/src/server/db/migrations/NNN_*.sql` (applied
  manually by an operator; idempotent `IF NOT EXISTS`).
- Client review page + the canonical pending-purchases review layout to
  reuse: `helios/src/client/routes/...` (pending-purchases review is the
  UI parity target — find and extend it, do not fork).

## Constraints (apply to every slice)

- **Typed TS only.** No untyped query/response shapes.
- **Measure before/after with a real full fetch**, not just
  `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` (canon: plans hide payload/detoast/serialization
  cost). Record server `exec_time`, wall time, payload bytes, and
  executor memory in the commit/issue.
- **Idempotent migrations** (`CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`,
  `CONCURRENTLY` where applicable) so they no-op on prod and stay
  recreate-safe. Add a matching sentinel to `pendingMigrations.ts`.
- **Do NOT add btree indexes to the join/filter path** — measured fast
  already.
- **Do not regress competitor-match correctness** (separate epic).
- **Reuse canonical UI** (pending-purchases review layout); no forked
  components.

## Slices

### R-A — Server family-aware pagination + minimal client paging *(ship together)*

Two-phase query in `listReviewFamilyQueue`:

1. Narrow family-page CTE/query over the indexed join only
   (`proposal_line_items ⋈ proposal_rows ⋈ proposal_batches ⋈
   catalog_groups`, projecting `brand/category/subcategory` columns
   only) → group → deterministic order → `LIMIT familyLimit+1`. **No**
   `jsonb_array_elements`, `regexp_replace`, `evidence_json`, or full
   `live_state_json` here.
2. Fetch full line items + reduced live state for the selected
   families' proposal rows, and observations only for that page's
   product ids.

- Add to `ReviewFamilyQueueQuerySchema`: `limit` (default 10, max 25)
  and `cursor`. Add `pageInfo { hasNextPage, endCursor }` to the
  response. Cursor encodes the sort tuple + filter state +
  `familyKeyVersion: 1`.
- Interim family key = `(brand, category, subcategory)`; multi-size
  families render `Mixed`/blank size. Keep individual actions.
- `maxItemsPerPage` safety cap; oversized family returned alone +
  logged.
- Minimal client change: request a single page; stop fetching/rendering
  the whole queue.
- **Acceptance:** payload ≪ 2.4 MB, no whole-queue
  `jsonb_array_elements`, executor memory ≪ 600 MB, DB interaction
  ≤125 ms; before/after numbers posted. Ships before R-B/R-C.

### R-B — `catalog_group_products` projection table

- Migration: `catalog_group_products(catalog_group_id, product_id,
  ordinal, name, tab, size_name, price numeric, updated_at, primary key
  (catalog_group_id, product_id))`; indexes `(product_id)`,
  `(catalog_group_id, ordinal)`. Idempotent + sentinel + idempotent
  backfill from `live_state_json`.
- Populate in `updateCatalogGroupLiveState`, write-on-change only
  (`WHERE … IS DISTINCT FROM`), inside the same transaction as the
  existing column projection.
- Size semantics: product-targeted → that product's `size_name`;
  single-size group → that size; multi-size group → `NULL`/`"Mixed"`.
- Rewrite R-A's narrow query to read `size_name` from the projection
  table (drop the lateral blob crack); upgrade the family key to
  include size; bump `familyKeyVersion → 2`.
- **Acceptance:** narrow page query has zero JSON cracking; multi-size
  groups grouped correctly; plan + timings posted.

### R-C — Client UX parity with pending-purchases review

- Lazy/virtualized mount of pricing ladders (mount on demand, not all
  at once).
- Reuse the pending-purchases review hierarchical layout: family groups
  with **group-level actions** + per-item actions.
- Group-aware pagination UI: never split a normal family across a page;
  massive family handled per R-A's guard.
- **Acceptance:** page interactive ≤500 ms after data; no all-ladders
  mount; layout matches pending-purchases review.

### R-D — Resolve dead MSO filter

- `msoOnly` is hardcoded `{ isMSOBrand: false }` → returns nothing.
  Either wire to a real brand-annotation source or remove the dead
  filter from contract + UI. Prefer removal if no source is ready.

### R-E — *(stretch)* precomputed preview columns

- Only if `regexp_replace` previews still measure material after R-A.
  Add `*_preview_text` (+ truncation flag) columns on
  `proposal_line_items`, maintained on insert/edit paths. Do not do
  pre-emptively.

declarations.title: Helios /catalog/review performance & UX overhaul

issues.title: Helios /catalog/review page performance & UX overhaul

issues.body:
## Summary

Add an **FBUS-safe, auto-LLM-sanitized, cached, periodically-synced FAQ** to
`freshlybakedus-site` (FBUS, `freshlybaked.us`):

1. **Embedded on every landing page**, just above the footer, under a
   page-wide **"FAQs"** header.
2. **A dedicated `/faq` page** on FBUS.

It should **replace the repeated generic humor/cartoon cards** (the
"wrong flowers" / "wrong green" style joke cards) currently used as
filler on landing pages.

**Why:** lift the organic SEO / domain authority of `freshlybaked.us` and
improve the **quality (and therefore performance + Quality Score)** of our
paid-ad landing pages, so ads convert better and cost less. Useful,
intent-matched FAQ content on each LP family is the lever; the humor cards
add no SEO value and dilute the page.

This is the **FBUS counterpart** to the already-shipped FB-NYC SEO FAQ
work under epic #15 ("FB.nyc MSS needs helios-driven components"). It is
mostly an **extension/integration of existing, mature infrastructure**,
not a new build.

> Designed with input from the Oracle (architecture review) and our private
> Bedrock LLM (`openai.gpt-oss-120b`). Where they disagreed (FAQ JSON-LD on
> mass LPs), this issue follows the conservative, current-best-practice
> stance — see "Key design decisions" §3.

---

## What already exists (REUSE — do not rebuild)

The `nyc-seo-widgets` pipeline (epic #15) already provides:

- **Helios FAQ control plane** (`automation` repo,
  `helios/src/server/seo/`): `faqGenerate.ts` produces **raw + sanitized**
  FAQ drafts via the private Bedrock-mantle LLM; `faqContent.ts` does
  content fingerprinting (`content_sha256`), id minting, and the
  raw-only-leak denylist (`findRawOnlyLeaks` / `RAW_ONLY_TERMS`). Drafts
  are `source='generated', approval_id=null` and **never publish without a
  human IRONCLAD review/approve gate**.
- **Signed SEO bundle** published by Helios and polled into memory by the
  site runtime (ed25519-verified, schema-validated, fail-closed).
- **`@mss/seo` package** (`packages/seo/`): `select.ts#selectFaqFolds`
  resolves host -> mode (`freshlybaked.nyc`=raw, `freshlybaked.us`=
  sanitized), enforces allowlists/kill-switch, and picks the
  mode-correct answer per item; `SEOFAQFold.tsx` is the server widget that
  renders SSR-visible `<details>`/`<summary>` accordion markup + a
  `FAQPage` JSON-LD block built from the SAME visible items.
- **Already wired into FB-NYC**:
  `apps/freshlybaked-site/app/seo-helios-faq-folds.tsx`.

## What's missing (the work)

- **FBUS consumes none of it.** No `apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/seo/`, no
  bundle poller boot in its `instrumentation.ts`, no fold rendering.
- **The seed FAQ content is hardcoded, not in the bundle.** The FB-NYC
  loyalty + general FAQ currently lives as a hand-maintained page at
  `apps/freshlybaked-site/app/sites/all/loyalty-faq/page.tsx`. It must
  become Helios-owned so both sites render from the bundle and changes
  flow through review.
- **No family-contextual FAQs** for the LP families.
- **No upstream change-detection / sync -> review -> page-dave loop.**
- **No FBUS leak/ads-safety CI gates.**

---

## Target architecture

```diagram
                          ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                          │ Helios (brain, `automation` repo)    │
                          │  • FAQ drafts via private Bedrock LLM │
                          │  • raw + sanitized variants          │
                          │  • content_sha256 fingerprint        │
                          │  • HUMAN IRONCLAD review/approve gate │ ◀── operator review page
                          │  • signed SEO bundle publisher       │      (+ page-dave on new draft)
                          └───────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                                          │ signed bundle (ed25519)
                            ┌─────────────┴──────────────┐
                            ▼                             ▼
                 ┌────────────────────┐        ┌────────────────────┐
                 │ FB-NYC (raw)       │        │ FBUS (sanitized)    │
                 │ renders raw answers│        │ NEW: lib/seo runtime│
                 │ (already wired)    │        │  + selectFaqFolds   │
                 └────────────────────┘        │  + SEOFAQFold       │
                                               │   - every LP (X4↔X5)│
                                               │   - dedicated /faq  │
                                               └────────────────────┘
```

FBUS landing pages use the unified X1–X5 component stack
(`unified-landing-engine` epic): X5 = `Friction_CTA` footer. **Inject the
FAQ section between X4 (menu) and X5 (footer)**, under a page-wide "FAQs"
header. The FAQ section **replaces the generic humor cards** wherever it is
enabled.

---

## Key design decisions

1. **Helios is the single source of truth for FAQ content.** One-time
   bootstrap import of the current hardcoded FB-NYC FAQ into Helios, then
   **delete/neutralize the hardcoded page** (add a CI guard so nobody
   reintroduces a hardcoded FAQ array). Both sites render from the bundle.
   Rejected alternative: keep the TSX page canonical with a watcher that
   parses it — brittle and creates an approval bypass.

2. **One merged, human-approved FAQ set per route family**, not "global
   widget + family widget stacked at render time" (which risks duplicate
   headers / multiple `FAQPage` scripts). Each family set =
   ~2–3 shared/global items + ~3–4 family-specific items. **Caps:** LPs
   5–7 items; dedicated `/faq` 10–16. Selector tests must assert **at most
   one fold per route**.

3. **JSON-LD policy (resolves the Oracle/LLM disagreement):** Google
   restricted `FAQPage` rich results to authoritative health/gov sites in
   2023, so emitting it across thousands of LP variants gives little
   upside and looks like scaled boilerplate. Therefore: add an
   `emitJsonLd?: boolean` prop to `SEOFAQFold` (default `true` for
   backward-compat). **LPs: `emitJsonLd=false` initially. Dedicated
   `/faq`: `emitJsonLd=true`.** Revisit per-LP JSON-LD only if canary data
   later justifies it. (The private LLM argued for JSON-LD everywhere; we
   are intentionally not doing that.)

4. **Content uniqueness beats schema spam.** The SEO win comes from
   genuinely useful, intent-matched, per-family-unique content — not
   identical boilerplate. Enforce uniqueness checks (duplicate question +
   near-duplicate answer) in the review pipeline.

5. **SSR/ISR-visible only.** The FAQ must be in the server-rendered HTML
   (native `<details>`), never client-fetched or lazy-loaded (contra one
   LLM suggestion) — both for crawlability and to avoid cloaking.

6. **Fail-closed everywhere**, reusing the existing kill-switch / mode /
   allowlist env flags (`SEO_WIDGETS_MODE`, `SEO_ROUTE_ALLOWLIST`,
   `SEO_SITE_ALLOWLIST`, `SEO_KILL_SWITCH`).

---

## Hard constraints (non-negotiable)

- **Zero leak of `freshlybaked.nyc`** (or any `.nyc` URL / "Freshly Baked
  NYC" brand phrase) in FBUS HTML **or** metadata — canonical, `og:*`,
  `sameAs`, publisher/org schema, `href`, `src`, `data-*`, inline JSON-LD,
  and the Next RSC payload / serialized client-component props.
- **Zero cannabis meta-terms** on `.us`. The sanitized-host denylist
  should be **stricter than the current `RAW_ONLY_TERMS`** for FBUS
  (include currently-"ambiguous" terms like `flower(s)`, `strain(s)` if the
  rule is truly zero meta-terms).
- **No increase in Google Ads disapproval rate** attributable to the added
  content. Canary + monitoring + kill switch are mandatory before any
  broad LP rollout.
- **No medical/legal claims, no competitor disparagement, no
  price/availability promises** unless sourced and approved.
- **No invented facts.** (We have repeatedly caught the LLM inventing
  claims this cycle — e.g. "all five boroughs", a nonexistent app, a
  price-match guarantee. Every generated answer is a draft to be
  fact-checked + human-approved.)

---

## Phased work breakdown (farmable to workers)

### Phase 0 — Audit, route inventory, leak policy + failing CI scanner
- Enumerate FBUS route families and representative sample routes.
- Define the forbidden token/domain list (`.nyc`, brand phrases, cannabis
  meta-terms).
- Add a CI scanner that **builds + serves FBUS, crawls sample routes, and
  scans the full HTML response (incl. inline scripts + RSC payload)**;
  fail on any forbidden string. **Expect it to find pre-existing FBUS leaks
  — fix those or scope them explicitly before adding FAQ content.**
- Accept: scanner runs in CI, fails on `.nyc`/meta-terms, documents
  existing leaks.

### Phase 1 — Helios FAQ source migration + sync loop
- One-time import the hardcoded FB-NYC FAQ into Helios; generate sanitized
  variants; human review/approve; publish bundle with FAQ sets + widgets.
- Add a **source-key** model (e.g. `fbus-global-faq`,
  `fbus-deliverance-faq`, … `fbus-dedicated-faq`).
- Add a **sync/change-detection job**: on upstream/source change, recompute
  `content_sha256`, create/update a Helios **draft**, fire **`page-dave`**,
  and **never auto-publish**.
- Remove/neutralize the hardcoded FB-NYC FAQ page (+ CI guard against
  reintroduction). FB-NYC now renders raw from the bundle.
- Accept: nothing publishes without approval-ledger match; sanitized
  content cannot contain `.nyc` or forbidden terms; page-dave fires on
  detected change.

### Phase 2 — FBUS SEO runtime integration
- Add `apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/seo/runtime.ts` (adapt from FB-NYC;
  distinct global symbol e.g. `mss.fbus.seo.runtime.v1`).
- Boot the SEO bundle poller in `apps/freshlybakedus-site/instrumentation.ts`
  alongside the existing LP runtime.
- Add `apps/freshlybakedus-site/app/api/seo/health/route.ts`.
- Add `apps/freshlybakedus-site/app/seo-helios-faq-folds.tsx` using
  `freshlyBakedUsSiteConfig.canonicalHost`, returning **at most one fold**.
- Add `emitJsonLd?: boolean` to `SEOFAQFold` (default `true`).
- Accept: `off`/`shadow` render no FAQ; `canary` requires allowlist;
  unknown host / invalid bundle render nothing; `.us` selects sanitized
  answers only.

### Phase 3 — Dedicated FBUS `/faq` page
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/app/faq/page.tsx`, sanitized mode,
  `emitJsonLd=true`, `.us`-only metadata, `revalidate` ~300–600s.
- Accept: `.us` canonical + OG; no `.nyc` anywhere; JSON-LD exactly matches
  visible text; page stands alone if LP FAQs are disabled.

### Phase 4 — LP FAQ insertion (replaces humor cards)
- Inject the FAQ section above the footer (between X4 and X5) in the shared
  FBUS LP page components (delivery/conquest/brand/tours/recurse/compare),
  under a page-wide "FAQs" header; LP `emitJsonLd=false`.
- **Remove the generic humor cards** (wrong flowers / wrong green) where
  the FAQ is enabled.
- Accept: one visible "FAQs" header + one FAQ section per page; no
  duplicate `FAQPage` scripts; canary controls work; humor cards gone on
  FAQ-enabled pages.

### Phase 5 — Family-contextual FAQ generation + governance
- Generate per-family drafts (deliverance, conquest, tours, recurse,
  branding, compare) via the private LLM, scoped via widget
  `route_patterns`.
- Governance checks before review: item-count cap, answer-length cap,
  forbidden-term scan, duplicate-question check, near-duplicate-answer
  check (token/Jaccard/shingle overlap is fine to start).
- Review page shows: raw + sanitized + rendered FBUS preview + route
  patterns + approx impacted route count + diff vs previous + leak/dup
  warnings.
- Accept: each family FAQ is distinct + useful; caps enforced; sample
  routes resolve to the expected set.

### Phase 6 — Ads-safe rollout
- Rollout doc + canary allowlists + kill-switch procedure + **Ads
  disapproval-rate monitoring (per route/family, 7- and 14-day delta)**.
- Stages: CI-only -> production `shadow` -> `/faq` canary -> one low-risk
  LP family canary -> family-by-family -> full. Keep LP JSON-LD off
  throughout initial rollout.
- Accept: shadow healthy; `/faq` canary clean; first LP canary shows no
  disapproval-rate increase over the agreed window; rollback tested.

---

## Family FAQ seeds (ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY — fact-check + human-approve each)

Questions only; sanitized; no cannabis/medical/legal/disparagement. These
are **starting prompts for the LLM**, not approved copy. Answers must be
verified against real store data (hours, areas, payment, policies) before
approval — do not ship invented specifics.

- **Deliverance (delivery):** "What are today's delivery windows?" ·
  "Can I track my order?" · "Which areas do you deliver to?"
- **Conquest (comparison):** "How does your pricing work?" · "What loyalty
  benefits do you offer?" · "What makes your service different?"
- **Tours (store/neighborhood):** "Where are your store locations?" ·
  "What should I bring for an in-store visit?" · "What are your store
  hours?"
- **Recurse (SEO mesh / coverage):** "Do you serve my neighborhood?" ·
  "How do I place an order online?" · "What payment methods do you accept?"
- **Branding (brand pages):** "How long has Freshly Baked operated in New
  York?" · "What does your loyalty program offer?" · "How do I contact
  your team?"
- **Compare (feature comparison):** "What's the difference between your
  product lines?" · "Which items are eligible for delivery?" · "How does
  the rewards program work across products?"

---

## Required CI / test gates (before any production LP rollout)

1. **Sanitized-content unit tests** — leak scanner catches `.nyc` domains,
   source URLs, cannabis/meta-terms, brand phrases.
2. **Helios approval tests** — approval rejects any leaked sanitized
   answer/shared question / `.nyc` URL.
3. **Bundle validation tests** — sanitized-site content + rendered widget
   `data-*` ids scanned pre-publish; `content_sha256` must match approval.
4. **Selector tests** — `.us`=sanitized, `.nyc`=raw, unknown host=[]; each
   sample FBUS route resolves to **at most one** fold; allowlists work.
5. **Renderer tests** — visible text == JSON-LD when emitted; LP can
   suppress JSON-LD; rendered HTML contains no raw answer.
6. **Metadata tests** — canonical/OG always `https://freshlybaked.us…`; no
   `.nyc` in any structured data / `sameAs` / publisher.
7. **Rendered-HTML crawler** — build + serve FBUS, crawl canary routes,
   scan full response incl. inline scripts + RSC payload.
8. **Kill-switch tests** — `SEO_KILL_SWITCH`, `mode=off/shadow`, empty
   canary allowlist all remove the FAQ.
9. **Ads-policy lint** — reject medical/legal/effect claims, competitor
   disparagement, unsourced price/availability promises.

---

## Top risks and guardrails

| Risk | Guardrail |
|------|-----------|
| Scaled/duplicate boilerplate FAQ across thousands of LPs hurts DA | Per-family unique merged sets; hard item caps; dup/near-dup checks; JSON-LD off on LPs |
| `.nyc` domain / brand / meta-term leak in HTML, metadata, or RSC payload | Full-HTML crawler gate (not just FAQ props); stricter FBUS denylist; approval + bundle gates; prefer internal redirect tokens over passing `.nyc` URLs to client components |
| Google Ads disapproval spike from added content | Shadow -> `/faq` -> single LP family canary; per-family disapproval-delta monitoring; kill switch + disabled_content rollback |
| Pre-existing FBUS leaks surface (already-serialized `.nyc`) | Phase 0 scanner first; fix before adding FAQ; do not claim safe until full page is clean |
| LLM invents facts (hours/areas/app/price-match) | Generated answers are drafts only; deterministic scanners + mandatory human approval; verify against store data |
| Noindex LP families get no organic benefit | Indexability is a separate, gated decision; LP FAQ still aids Quality Score/conversion even on noindex pages |
| ISR means approved updates aren't instant | Acceptable for FAQ; documented rollback via kill switch + targeted revalidation; `/faq` shorter `revalidate` |

---

## Open questions for the operator

1. Confirm the canonical **list of FBUS LP families + their route
   patterns** (deliverance, conquest, tours, recurse, branding, compare —
   any others?).
2. Should any LP families be flipped **indexable** as part of this, or is
   indexability strictly out of scope here?
3. Confirm the **sync cadence** for upstream change detection (event-driven
   on FB-NYC FAQ approval vs. nightly/weekly poll).
4. Confirm which **humor card components** to retire and whether to remove
   them globally or only where the FAQ is enabled.

---

## References

- Parent epic: #15 (FB.nyc MSS needs helios-driven components)
- `nyc-seo-widgets` epic plan: `docs/epics/nyc-seo-widgets/EPIC_PLAN.md`
- `unified-landing-engine` epic plan (X1–X5 stack):
  `docs/epics/unified-landing-engine/EPIC_PLAN.md`
- Widget: `packages/seo/src/widgets/SEOFAQFold.tsx`
- Selector: `packages/seo/src/select.ts`
- FB-NYC wiring (pattern to mirror):
  `apps/freshlybaked-site/app/seo-helios-faq-folds.tsx`
- Seed content (to migrate into Helios):
  `apps/freshlybaked-site/app/sites/all/loyalty-faq/page.tsx`
- Helios generation + sanitization:
  `automation: helios/src/server/seo/faqGenerate.ts`,
  `helios/src/server/seo/faqContent.ts`


```yaml
delegated_to:
  - repo: FreshlyBakedNYC/automation
    issue: 46
    note: Helios FAQ brain. BINDING: IRONCLAD human-approval gate (canon section 1) - nothing auto-publishes; FBUS sanitized denylist stricter than RAW_ONLY_TERMS; hybrid sync (approval->publish, change/new-content->draft+page-dave); approval publishes only the approved content_sha256; consume mss P0 LP-family registry artifact. Phases P1, P5.
  - repo: Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites
    issue: 11
    note: Thin zero-DB renderer. P0 first (failing full-HTML leak crawler + canonical LP-family registry + humor-card inventory + indexability/robots audit). BINDING: zero .nyc/brand/cannabis-meta leak in HTML+metadata+RSC payload; .us=sanitized fail-closed; at most one fold/route; JSON-LD off on LPs, on for /faq; humor-card retirement only where FAQ enabled; per-family indexability flip operator-gated. Phases P0, P2, P3, P4.
```

declarations.body:
# FBUS FAQ — `mostly-static-sites` (thin renderer) child epic

> **MATERIALISED 2026-06-15.** The four operator decisions are resolved
> in the parent
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md` §1](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#1-operator-decisions-resolved-2026-06-15)
> and folded into the phases below.
> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md). **Re-read the parent (and the
> parent epic #15) before starting any phase** — this child epic is a
> **thin index** over the parent's design. The parent wins on any drift.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#17
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>` trailer.

## Role in the epic

`mostly-static-sites` is the **thin, zero-DB renderer**. It consumes the
signed SEO bundle Helios publishes and renders the FAQ on FBUS — on every
landing page and on a dedicated `/faq` page — selecting **sanitized**
answers for the `.us` host. It also owns the **full-HTML leak crawler**
that proves FBUS ships no `.nyc` / brand / cannabis-meta-term leak. Helios
(`automation`) is the brain (peer child epic at
`../automation/EPIC_PLAN.md`).

The `@mss/seo` package (`packages/seo/`) — `select.ts#selectFaqFolds` and
`SEOFAQFold.tsx` — and the FB-NYC wiring
(`apps/freshlybaked-site/app/seo-helios-faq-folds.tsx`) **already exist**
from epic #15 and are the pattern to mirror. This child epic **reuses**
them; FBUS currently consumes none of it.

## ⚠️ Binding constraints (parent §5–§6)

- **Zero `.nyc` / "Freshly Baked NYC" / cannabis-meta-term leak** anywhere
  in FBUS rendered output: HTML, canonical, `og:*`, `sameAs`,
  publisher/org schema, `href`, `src`, `data-*`, inline JSON-LD, **and**
  the Next RSC payload / serialized client-component props. Prefer
  internal redirect tokens over passing `.nyc` URLs to client components.
- **`.us` selects sanitized answers only.** Unknown host / invalid bundle
  → render nothing (fail closed).
- **At most one FAQ fold per route**; one visible "FAQs" header + one FAQ
  section per page; no duplicate `FAQPage` scripts.
- **SSR/ISR-visible only** — native `<details>` in server HTML; never
  client-fetched or lazy-loaded.
- **Kill-switch / mode / allowlist fail-closed**: `off`/`shadow` render no
  FAQ; `canary` requires allowlist; `SEO_KILL_SWITCH` removes it.
- **UI/UX gate (canon §3).** The LP FAQ section + `/faq` page are
  user-facing UI → Oracle UI review (mobile layout, signal-to-noise,
  next-action-at-fingertips) recorded on the peer issue before rollout.

## Subtasks (authoritative list in parent §4 / issue Phases 0, 2, 3, 4)

**P0 — audit + failing leak crawler (goes first):**
- Enumerate FBUS route families + representative sample routes
  (operator-confirmed current set: deliverance, conquest, tours, recurse,
  branding, compare — parent §1 Q1).
- **Canonical LP-family registry (operator Q1 follow-up).** Land the
  family list + route patterns as a **single source of truth in code/
  config** (e.g. a `lpFamilies`/`SEO_ROUTE_FAMILIES` registry) so future
  families have an obvious place to register, and so this crawler
  inventory, the P4 FAQ injection points, and Helios's widget
  `route_patterns` (automation P5) all read from **one** place instead of
  duplicated lists. **Define the registry schema + cross-repo handoff:**
  export a machine-readable artifact (e.g. JSON) carrying, per family,
  the **id, canonical representative route, route patterns, sample crawl
  routes, indexability policy, and source commit/provenance** so
  automation P5 can consume it (or pin its exact SHA) rather than
  re-keying the list.
- **Humor-card inventory + classification (operator Q4).** Find the LP
  filler/humor cards (the "wrong flowers" / "wrong green" joke cards),
  classify each as **pure-humor filler** (retire) vs **functional**
  (keep), and record the list on this peer issue for operator
  confirmation. The operator could not name them ("you'll have to look");
  this inventory is the deliverable that resolves the question.
- **Indexability current-state audit (operator Q2).** Record the current
  `robots` / `noindex` / canonical / sitemap state for each LP family and
  `/faq`, and confirm there is **no `gads` / policy-engine coupling** to
  `robots` (i.e. flipping indexability does not change ads behaviour).
  Feeds the P6 indexability decision; make **no** indexability change in
  P0.
- Define the forbidden token/domain list (`.nyc`, brand phrases, cannabis
  meta-terms).
- Add a CI scanner that **builds + serves FBUS, crawls sample routes, and
  scans the full HTML response (incl. inline scripts + RSC payload)**;
  fail on any forbidden string. **Expect pre-existing FBUS leaks — fix or
  explicitly scope them before adding FAQ content.**

**P2 — FBUS SEO runtime integration:**
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/seo/runtime.ts` (adapt from FB-NYC;
  distinct global symbol e.g. `mss.fbus.seo.runtime.v1`).
- Boot the SEO bundle poller in
  `apps/freshlybakedus-site/instrumentation.ts` alongside the LP runtime.
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/app/api/seo/health/route.ts`.
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/app/seo-helios-faq-folds.tsx` using
  `freshlyBakedUsSiteConfig.canonicalHost`, returning **at most one fold**.
- Add `emitJsonLd?: boolean` to `SEOFAQFold` (default `true`).

**P3 — dedicated `/faq` page:**
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/app/faq/page.tsx`, sanitized mode,
  `emitJsonLd=true`, `.us`-only metadata, `revalidate` ~300–600s. Stands
  alone if LP FAQs are disabled.

**P4 — LP FAQ insertion (replaces humor cards):**
- Inject the FAQ section above the footer (between X4 and X5) in the
  shared FBUS LP page components (deliverance/conquest/tours/recurse/
  branding/compare — the operator-confirmed set from the P0 registry),
  under a page-wide "FAQs" header; LP `emitJsonLd=false`.
- **Retire the pure-humor cards** identified in the P0 inventory (wrong
  flowers / wrong green) **only on LP families where the FAQ section is
  enabled** (operator Q4 default: per-family + reversible, **not** a
  global delete). Keep cards the P0 inventory classified as functional.
  Global retirement is a follow-up once the FAQ is broadly live.
- P4 implementation may **land behind kill-switch/canary flags** before
  P5, but **production enablement of an LP family waits until that family
  has an approved merged FAQ set from P5** — do not replace humor cards
  with generic/global boilerplate before family-specific approved content
  exists.

**Hardcoded-FAQ cleanup (mss owns this; coordinate with automation P1):**
- After Helios import is approved and bundled, remove/neutralize
  `apps/freshlybaked-site/app/sites/all/loyalty-faq/page.tsx` as a source
  of truth (render from the bundle instead; preserve/redirect any existing
  public route intentionally), and add a **CI guard** against reintroducing
  hardcoded FAQ content outside the SEO bundle. automation cannot complete
  this migration alone — the code change is here.

**P6 — ads-safe rollout mechanics:**
- Route/family allowlist canary, kill-switch verification, a production
  crawl before broad enablement, and a rollback runbook for removing FAQ
  sections / restoring prior content.
- **Indexability flip (operator Q2, operator-gated for LP families).**
  The new `/faq` ships indexable by design (P3); the **per-LP-family**
  flip waits for operator approval after the P0 audit. If approved: make
  **one canonical representative page per LP family** `index, follow` +
  self-canonical + sitemap-listed, and point per-variant / parameterised
  LPs at it via `rel=canonical` (the preferred consolidation signal),
  adding `noindex` only where a low-unique variant must stay out of the
  index (do not rely on `noindex` to consolidate ranking signals).
  Default until explicit operator approval = **no indexability change to
  existing LP families**.

## CI gates owned here (parent §7)

(4) selector tests (`.us`=sanitized, `.nyc`=raw, unknown host=[], at most
one fold/route, allowlists); (5) renderer tests (visible text == JSON-LD
when emitted; LP can suppress JSON-LD; no raw answer in HTML);
(6) metadata tests (canonical/OG always `https://freshlybaked.us…`; no
`.nyc` in structured data / `sameAs` / publisher); (7) rendered-HTML
crawler (P0); (8) kill-switch tests.

## Phasing

P0 (leak crawler) first and must pass before any FAQ content is added.
The P2 runtime can run in `shadow`; `/faq` (P3, the smallest visible
slice) should be enabled only in non-prod or canary/allowlisted mode
until the crawler, metadata, and approval gates pass. Then P4 LP
insertion lands gated. Tag commits with `Phase: P<n>`.

Phases P0, P2, P3, P4.

# FBUS FAQ — `automation` (Helios control plane) child epic

> **MATERIALISED 2026-06-15.** The four operator decisions are resolved
> in the parent
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md` §1](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#1-operator-decisions-resolved-2026-06-15)
> and folded into the phases below.
> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md). **Re-read the parent (and the
> parent epic #15) before starting any phase** — this child epic is a
> **thin index** over the parent's design, not a re-statement of it. The
> parent wins on any drift.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#17
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>` trailer
> so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post per-phase progress
> on the parent issue.

## Role in the epic

Helios (`automation`) is the **FAQ brain**: it owns the FAQ content
source-of-truth, generation + the editorial review/approve workflow, the
sanitized-host denylist, the change-detection/sync loop, governance
checks, and the signed SEO-bundle publisher. mss stays a thin, zero-DB
renderer (peer child epic at `../mostly-static-sites/EPIC_PLAN.md`).

This builds **directly on the FB-NYC SEO FAQ control plane already
shipped under epic #15** (`helios/src/server/seo/faqGenerate.ts`,
`faqContent.ts`, signed bundle publisher). This child epic **extends**,
it does not rebuild.

## ⚠️ Binding constraints (parent §5–§6, canon §1)

- **IRONCLAD human-approval gate (canon §1).** No FAQ draft, sanitized
  variant, family content, or sync-detected change becomes publicly
  visible without a human approving that **specific** content first.
  Generation and the sync loop only ever produce **drafts**
  (`source='generated', approval_id=null`) + fire `page-dave`; they
  **never auto-publish**.
- **Zero `.nyc` / brand / cannabis-meta-term leak in sanitized content.**
  The FBUS sanitized-host denylist must be **stricter than the current
  `RAW_ONLY_TERMS`** (include `flower(s)`, `strain(s)`, etc. if the rule
  is truly zero meta-terms). Approval and bundle publish must both fail
  closed on any leak.
- **`content_sha256` must match the approval ledger** before publish.
- **No invented facts.** Generated answers are drafts; verify against real
  store data (hours, areas, payment, policies) before approval.
- **DB-cost discipline (canon §3).** The sync/change-detection job is a
  recurring background DB workload → written cost budget + Oracle
  DB-efficiency review recorded on the peer issue **before deploy**.

## Subtasks (authoritative list in parent §4 / issue Phases 1 & 5)

**P1 — FAQ source migration + sync loop:**
- One-time import the hardcoded FB-NYC FAQ
  (`mostly-static-sites: apps/freshlybaked-site/app/sites/all/loyalty-faq/page.tsx`)
  into Helios; generate sanitized variants; human review/approve; publish
  the bundle with FAQ sets + widgets.
- Add a **source-key** model (`fbus-global-faq`, `fbus-deliverance-faq`,
  … `fbus-dedicated-faq`).
- Add a **sync/change-detection job** with the **hybrid cadence the
  operator chose** (parent §1 Q3): **(a)** an *approval* of FAQ content
  (FB-NYC / Helios) **drives the bundle push** (event-driven publish of
  already-approved content); **(b)** an *observed* upstream/source change
  — or **creation/modification of content** such as a newly added or
  modified LP family — recomputes `content_sha256`, creates/updates a
  Helios **draft**, and fires **`page-dave`** for review. Path (b)
  **never auto-publishes**; only path (a)'s human approval does. **Guard:**
  path (a) may publish **only** the exact `content_sha256` / sanitized
  content that was approved — a raw/upstream approval that would change the
  FBUS *sanitized* output routes through path (b) (new draft + page), never
  an implicit sanitized publish.
- Coordinate with mss to remove/neutralize the hardcoded FB-NYC FAQ page
  (+ CI guard against reintroduction). FB-NYC then renders raw from the
  bundle.

**P5 — family-contextual generation + governance:**
- Generate per-family drafts (deliverance, conquest, tours, recurse,
  branding, compare — the operator-confirmed current set, parent §1 Q1)
  via the private Bedrock LLM, scoped via widget `route_patterns` that
  **consume the machine-readable LP-family registry artifact** mss P0
  exports (family id, canonical representative route, route patterns,
  sample routes, indexability policy, source SHA) — or, if a generated
  copy is unavoidable, record the exact mss source SHA for provenance.
  Do **not** maintain a second hand-edited family list here.
- Governance before review: item-count cap, answer-length cap,
  forbidden-term scan, duplicate-question check, near-duplicate-answer
  check (token/Jaccard/shingle overlap is fine to start).
- Review page shows: raw + sanitized + rendered FBUS preview + route
  patterns + approx impacted route count + diff vs previous + leak/dup
  warnings.

**P6 — rollout support / monitoring:**
- Provide approved-content status, disabled-content rollback, `page-dave`
  alerts, and any ads-policy lint / reporting needed for rollout
  decisions.
- Coordinate with the operator on the ads-disapproval baseline + window.

## CI gates owned here (parent §7)

(1) sanitized-content leak unit tests; (2) approval rejects any leaked
sanitized answer / shared question / `.nyc` URL; (3) bundle-validation
tests (`content_sha256` must match approval); (9) ads-policy lint.

## Phasing

P1 (source migration + sync) is the unblocking control-plane slice and
goes first; P5 (family content + governance) follows once mss can render.
Tag commits with `Phase: P<n>`.
declarations.delegationNote: Helios FAQ brain. BINDING: IRONCLAD human-approval gate (canon section 1) - nothing auto-publishes; FBUS sanitized denylist stricter than RAW_ONLY_TERMS; hybrid sync (approval->publish, change/new-content->draft+page-dave); approval publishes only the approved content_sha256; consume mss P0 LP-family registry artifact. Phases P1, P5.

issues.body:
## Summary

Now that Helios is the control plane for landing pages (parent epic #13 / `automation#42`, the unified landing engine), we should turn the conversion-feedback data it already collects into an operator-facing analytics surface. This issue proposes a **new `GAds` (Google Ads) metrics page** in Helios, built as a tab in the existing `/metrics` dashboard, with **sub-pages**. The **first sub-page is "Landing pages."** It is explicitly the first slice of a larger, holistic paid-acquisition and lead-gen measurement system (Campaigns, Creative, Keywords, Policy health, Experiments to follow).

This design was produced from a consensus of our best available private Bedrock LLM (GLM-5; GPT-5.x is gated on our account) for the expert SEO/analytics metric inventory, plus an Oracle architecture, DB, and UI review. Open questions for you are collected at the bottom.

## What we already have to build on

The unified landing engine already ships an append-only event log into Helios:

- **Table `lp_events`** (migration `070_lp_events.sql`), written by the `mostly-static-sites` runtime's durable spool via `POST /v1/lp-events/batch`.
- **Funnel event types:** `lp_assignment` -> `lp_impression` -> `lp_redirect` (visitor clicks the CTA and is sent to the Sweed online-ordering menu) -> `lp_conversion`.
- **Rich selection provenance per event:** `assignment_id`, `bundle_id`, `policy_id`, `policy_rule_id`, `experiment_id`, `branch_id`, `selected_variants`, `counterfactual_variants`, `candidate_weights`, `served_probability_bps` (the bandit propensity), `bucket_bps`.
- **Attribution keys:** `gclid_hash` (hashed Google click id) and `assignment_key_type` (`gclid` / `gbraid` / `wbraid` / `cookie` / `session` / `default`).
- **Placement:** `site`, `family` (page purpose), `cluster_slug`, `traffic_flags`.

We also have Google Ads cost/click/keyword data (the `ads-snapshot-live.jsonl` snapshot, see note in Open Questions about granularity) and Sweed order/revenue data.

This is a contextual-bandit / experiment engine: Helios selects per-slot variants and records the propensity it served them at. That makes proper bandit-aware (off-policy) analysis possible later, but it also means naive A/B math is wrong here (see V2 notes).

## 1. Information architecture: reuse, do not fork

**Recommendation: add `GAds` as a new top-level tab in the existing metrics dashboard**, not a new sibling route family. The dashboard is already a URL-addressable tab system in `helios/src/client/routes/metrics/MetricsLayoutPage.tsx` (`METRICS_TABS`, `MetricsTabId`, `METRICS_TAB_ALIASES`, per-tab grant gating via `MetricGrantKey`). Several tabs already own their full internal UI (e.g. `CatalogAnalyticsTab`, `BudtenderPerformanceTab`), which is exactly the pattern a multi-sub-page `GAds` tab needs.

Plan:

- Add `'gads'` to `MetricsTabId` and a `METRICS_TABS` entry (`include: () => false`, owns its own UI), short-circuit-rendered to a new `GAdsTab` like the catalog/budtender tabs.
- `GAdsTab` owns a small internal sub-page nav. V1 sub-page: **Landing pages** (`GAdsLandingPagesTab`). Reserve later sub-pages: Campaigns, Creative, Keywords, Policy health, Experiments.
- Preferred URLs: `/metrics/gads/landing-pages`, with `/metrics/gads` defaulting to it (or `?sub=` if nested routing is too invasive for V1).
- **Reuse, do not re-invent** (canon reuse-before-build gate): the tab strip + `MetricsAccessGate`, `MetricGrantKey` gating, `defaultSiteSelection` / `toggleSiteSelection`, `RangeNudgeRow` and range presets, `TimeAxisProvider` / `useTimeAxis`, `MetricChart` (for the optional trend card only), `ControlsSection`, and existing metrics card/table/chip CSS. Extract a small shared `MetricSiteRangeControls` from `MetricsLayoutPage` rather than copy-pasting its controls.
- **One consolidated endpoint for first paint:** `GET /api/gads/landing-pages` (contract `shared/contracts/api/gadsLandingPages.ts`, query module `server/db/queries/gadsLandingPagesQueries.ts`) returning hero + funnel + table in one payload. Do NOT fan out 6-10 independent `MetricChart` requests on load (breaks the 500ms page budget).
- **Access:** add a new `MetricGrantKey` value `'gads'` (the enum in `shared/contracts/domain/auth.ts` is explicitly designed to be extended; gate the endpoint with the metrics grant check). Ad spend / ROAS / acquisition data is sensitive enough to warrant its own grant rather than reusing `explore`. (Confirm in Open Questions.)

## 2. Metrics: V1 must-have vs V2-later

### V1 KPI strip (6, each with a data-quality badge when cost/revenue attribution is incomplete)

1. **Ad spend** = sum(attributed/allocated cost)
2. **Attributed revenue** = sum(attributed revenue)
3. **ROAS** = attributed revenue / ad spend (badge if cost is allocated, not click-exact)
4. **CPA** = ad spend / unique attributed conversions
5. **Landing-page conversion rate** = unique converted assignments / unique assignments
6. **Redirect rate** = unique redirected assignments / unique impressed assignments (the metric the landing page most directly controls)

All counts are **assignment-level uniques**, never raw event counts.

### V1 funnel (one view)

A single horizontal **waterfall**: `Assigned -> Impressed -> Redirected -> Converted`, each assignment counted once per stage, with drop-off percentages and a small warning when unattributed events exist (e.g. events without `assignment_id`). No Sankey in V1 (worse on mobile, slower, no clearer).

### V1 variant view (one table)

Table grouped by `site, family, experiment_id, policy_rule_id, branch_id`. Columns: variant/branch, assignments, traffic share, impression rate, redirect rate, conversion rate, revenue per assignment, ROAS and CPA (when cost/revenue available), avg served probability (diagnostic only), data-quality/sample badge, and an action link (open landing page / inspect policy / open Sweed menu).

Rules: label it **observed performance, not causal lift**; hide low-sample rows by default (e.g. < 25 assignments) behind a toggle; sort by action priority (high spend + low ROAS, then high traffic + low redirect rate, then high traffic + low conversion rate).

### V2 (deliberately deferred)

Bandit-aware off-policy estimates (IPS / doubly-robust), win probability, credible intervals, regret; anomaly detection and guardrail surfacing; hour-by-day heatmap; cost-vs-revenue scatter; dwell-time histogram; scroll depth, viewport-active time, Core Web Vitals; device class; campaign/keyword/match-type segmentation; cross-device `gbraid`/`wbraid` attribution; counterfactual-variant analysis.

### Corrections applied to the raw LLM inventory (so we do not bake in errors)

- `served_probability_bps` is **basis points**: probability = bps / 10000; IPS weight = 1 / p (guard against p approaching 0; cap weights). Compute IPS on **one assignment-level fact per assignment**, never over raw event rows.
- Beta-binomial posteriors with fractional IPS weights are not a safe default; use weighted bootstrap / robust or doubly-robust variance in V2 after a stats review. "Non-overlapping intervals = winner" is too simplistic; compare the distribution of the difference. **Regret is not observable** from served rewards alone (needs a counterfactual reward model).
- `candidate_weights` is not the realized traffic split; use `served_probability_bps` for realized propensity. `branch_id` needs a definition (whole-page variant vs one slot) before per-slot analysis.
- "Rapid bounce = redirect under 2s" can be a **fast, good** CTA click, not a bounce. Dwell time from `last_event_ts - first_impression_ts` is unreliable without visibility/heartbeat events. Both deferred until we have the right signals.

## 3. Database and performance design (TigerData / TimescaleDB on Postgres)

Hard budget: interactive DB reads <= 125ms, page <= 500ms. **Dashboard reads must not touch raw `lp_events`, must not do live `COUNT(DISTINCT assignment_id)`, and must not join Google Ads cost or Sweed revenue at request time.**

Proposed serving model:

1. **`lp_events`** stays the append-only source of truth (current migration 070 is good). Add minimal indexes only as needed: `(assignment_id, event_ts) where assignment_id is not null`; `(gclid_hash) where gclid_hash is not null` only once a cost-attribution table exists.
2. **`lp_assignment_facts`** (derived, one row per `assignment_id`): denormalized placement + provenance, plus `first_impression_ts` / `first_redirect_ts` / `first_conversion_ts` / `last_event_ts`, `impression_count` / `redirect_count`, `converted`, `attributed_revenue_cents`, `attributed_cost_micros`, and `cost_attribution_status` / `revenue_attribution_status`. **This is the key perf fix:** it turns distinct-session counting into cheap exact counts and is where cost/revenue are joined once, offline.
3. **Rollup tables `lp_metrics_hourly` / `lp_metrics_daily`**, grouped by bucket + site + family + experiment_id + policy_rule_id + branch_id + assignment_key_type, summing assignments / impressions / redirects / conversions / revenue / cost / served_probability. V1 keeps campaign / keyword / cluster / device OUT of the default rollup (cardinality blowup). Add IPS-term columns (`sum_inv_p`, `sum_inv_p_converted`, `sum_inv_p_revenue`, `sum_inv_p_squared`) only in V2.
4. **Async derivation, not work inside ingest:** the batch route stays fast (insert + return); a background worker tracks a high-water mark over `lp_events`, rebuilds touched assignment facts (write-on-change only, `IS DISTINCT FROM` guards), joins current cost/revenue attribution, then invalidates and rebuilds the affected hourly/daily buckets. Late Sweed revenue / Google Ads cost backfills enqueue the affected buckets explicitly.
5. **Serving endpoint** reads only rollups + small dimension tables, bounds the variant table to top N (e.g. 25-50), and returns one compact payload. Every query ships with an `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` plan and a full-fetch byte-size measurement per canon DB gate.

Where it will actually hurt: distinct-session counting (fixed by assignment facts), the gclid -> Google Ads cost join (our snapshot looks campaign/ad-group aggregate, NOT gclid-level, so cost is **allocated**, not click-exact, and must be labelled as such), and revenue attribution (the `lp_conversion` event currently carries no order id / revenue, and time-window joins to Sweed are fuzzy and arrive late).

**High-risk DB changes that will each need a dedicated Oracle DB review before they land:** converting `lp_events` to a hypertable + compression; continuous aggregates over mutable assignment facts (and hierarchical daily-over-hourly); HLL / Timescale Toolkit availability on TigerData; the gclid-level cost attribution source; the Sweed revenue attribution model and late-arrival windows; cardinality of campaign/keyword/cluster/device/per-slot dimensions; historical backfill; refresh locking and write amplification under event volume.

## 4. UI/UX (canon hard gates: mobile-excellent, high signal-to-noise, next action at fingertips, no em-dashes)

Landing-pages sub-page, first screen in order:

1. **Freshness + attribution status** strip (e.g. "Updated 4 min ago", "Cost allocated", "Revenue attribution incomplete"), compact but visible.
2. **Profitability KPI strip** (the 6 above).
3. **Next-action card**: top 3 issues only, each with a direct action ("Review variant", "Open landing page", "Inspect policy", "Open Sweed menu") so the operator never hunts for the result of what they just saw.
4. **Funnel waterfall** with the biggest drop-off called out inline.
5. **Variant table**: dense on desktop, mobile-first column + action column with horizontal scroll.

Hidden by default (advanced / V2): IPS estimates, win probability, credible intervals, regret, raw events / JSON, candidate weights, counterfactuals, scroll depth, viewport time, web vitals, device breakdown, keyword/match-type filters, cluster drilldowns, low-sample variants. Short badge copy ("Cost allocated", "Low sample", "Attribution gap", "Needs review"); collapsed filters (site / range / family / experiment, rest behind "more"); one-column mobile cards with sticky compact filter row. No em-dashes anywhere in copy. **The actual UI will go through the canon Oracle UI review before it ships.**

## 5. Open questions (need your call before / during implementation)

**IA and access**
1. Own `gads` metric grant, or visible to existing `explore` users?
2. Confirm URL shape `/metrics/gads/landing-pages` (with `/metrics/gads` defaulting to it)?
3. Which future GAds sub-page names should the IA reserve (Campaigns, Creative, Keywords, Policy health, Experiments)?

**V1 scope**
4. Can V1 launch with funnel + variant **observed performance** even if cost/revenue attribution is not fully wired?
5. Is ROAS mandatory for V1, or shown as "pending" until attribution is reliable?
6. Default date range for paid-acquisition decisions: 7d, 30d, or 90d?

**Conversion definition**
7. What counts as a conversion: redirect to Sweed, checkout start, submitted order, paid Sweed invoice, or lead capture?
8. Attribute to assignment time or conversion time? What attribution window (same day / 7d / 30d)?
9. How to treat cancellations, refunds, failed payments, test orders, and guest orders that cannot be linked back to an assignment?

**Revenue definition**
10. ROAS revenue basis: gross receipts incl. tax, net sales excl. tax, subtotal before discounts, or margin dollars? Include delivery fees / discounts / tips? First attributed order only, or all orders in the window?

**Google Ads cost**
11. Do we have (or plan to get) **gclid-level** click cost from the Google Ads API? Our current snapshot looks campaign/ad-group aggregate. If aggregate-only, are you OK with **allocated** cost (clearly labelled in the UI)?
12. Which Google Ads dimensions are reliably available today (campaign, ad group, ad, keyword, match type, campaign type)?

**Event-schema gaps (each blocks specific metrics)**
13. Will `lp_conversion` carry order id / invoice id / revenue so we can attribute money without fuzzy Sweed time-joins?
14. Is `assignment_id` guaranteed on every event stage? Is `branch_id` the whole-page variant or a single slot? Is `served_probability_bps` the served branch's full probability or per-slot?
15. Should we persist user agent / derived device class? Are scroll depth, viewport-active time, and Core Web Vitals in scope for V2? Can the runtime emit a page-load-failure event for assignments that never impress?

**Bandit / experiment semantics**
16. Should V1 make any causal claims, or strictly say "observed performance"? What sample threshold hides/badges a variant row? Should the page only surface review candidates, or also suggest disabling variants, and who may act on that?

**Ops / data**
17. What historical backfill exists for `lp_events`, Google Ads cost, and Sweed revenue? Expected event volume over the next 90 days? Is Timescale Toolkit (HLL) available on TigerData? Freshness SLA that matters (1 / 5 / 15 min / hourly)? Should we ship manual rollup tables first and review CAGGs separately?

---

### Agent Gate Record

- **Canon refresh:** read fresh from `top-level@b849e0e` (Core + rules/QUALITY_GATES, DB_PERFORMANCE, WORKFLOW, TOOL_ROUTING). Re-read before this final response.
- **Tool-first:** ephemeral checkouts used for `top-level` and `automation` (`5b5e65f`); no edits in shared `~/src`. Bedrock consulted via the sanctioned private `bedrock-mantle` gateway (no public LLM). No deploy / SSH / heavy build in this design task.
- **Reuse-search-before-build:** searched `helios/src/client/routes/metrics/*` and the metrics tab/grant machinery; design reuses the existing tab system, `MetricsAccessGate`, `MetricGrantKey`, `RangeNudgeRow`, `MetricChart`, site-selection, and metrics CSS rather than forking. No code shipped in this issue.
- **Oracle UI review:** architecture + UI/UX + DB design reviewed by Oracle for this proposal; the actual UI implementation will get the mandatory canon Oracle UI review before it ships (recorded then).
- **DB efficiency:** cost-aware serving model specified (assignment facts + rollups, no raw-`lp_events` reads, no live distinct/joins on the hot path); high-risk DB changes enumerated for dedicated Oracle DB reviews before they land. No DB change shipped here.
- **Write-back:** no new canonical rule from this task. Candidate KB entry: catalog the metrics tab system as the canonical "add a new analytics surface" pattern under `docs/agent-kb/catalog/shared-ui.md` once the GAds tab lands (not yet, since nothing shipped).


```yaml
delegated_to:
  - repo: FreshlyBakedNYC/automation
    issue: 47
    note: Helios GAds landing-pages analytics V1. BINDING: three per-site confidential grants gads-bronx/gads-midtown/gads-all (gads-all is its own grant, never synthesised; server derives site scope from the grant, never from a client param); cheapest DB (one small periodically-refreshed gads_lp_rollup, no fact table/hourly+daily/derivation worker/CAGGs/hypertable/HLL - do not fight epic #11); serving never reads raw lp_events; observed performance not accounting (revenue/ROAS Unavailable, cost allocated+badged, hide rows <25 assignments, no causal claims, no auto-disable). P0 first: define+test the GAds traffic predicate, pick reporting timezone, lock formulas. Phases P0-P5.
```

declarations.body:
# GAds → Landing-pages analytics (V1) — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#18](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/18).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/gads-landing-analytics/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in the top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the
> `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (Helios) slice of that design**, which in
> V1 is the whole thing — no other peer repo is on the critical path.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation@master` that
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#18
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>` trailer
> (`P0`..`P5`) so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post the
> per-phase progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

Everything in the parent `EPIC_PLAN.md`, broken out by phase below.
**Re-read the parent before starting** — the parent is the single source
of truth; this file is a thin phase index over it.

## Binding constraints (from the parent, do not weaken)

- **Confidential, per-site access.** Three grants `gads-bronx`,
  `gads-midtown`, `gads-all`. `gads-all` is its own grant, never
  synthesised from the per-site grants. The server derives the site
  predicate from the authenticated route/grant and MUST NOT accept a
  client `site`/`sites` param that widens scope.
- **Cheap DB, by operator decree.** One small rollup table refreshed
  out-of-band; **no** per-assignment fact table, **no** hourly+daily
  rollup pair, **no** always-on derivation worker, **no** CAGGs /
  hypertable conversion / compression / HLL in V1. Each of those, if
  ever proposed, needs its own Oracle DB review. Do not fight epic #11.
- **Serving never touches raw `lp_events`.** Dashboard reads hit only
  `gads_lp_rollup` (+ the refresh-state row). A test asserts this.
- **Observed performance, not accounting.** No causal claims. Revenue
  and ROAS render "Unavailable" (no fake numbers). Cost is allocated and
  badged. Hide variant rows < 25 assignments behind a toggle.
- **Canon gates at implementation time:** the DB migration + refresh
  query ship with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` plans and a payload
  byte-size measurement (canon DB gate); the UI gets the mandatory
  Oracle UI review before it ships; record the Agent Gate Record on each
  commit / issue update.

---

### P0 — Audit + lock semantics (do this first)

No schema change yet; produce a short design note (committed or linked).

- Verify the live `lp_events` columns + existing indexes match the
  parent's assumptions (`assignment_id`, event types, `site`, `family`,
  `cluster_slug`, `experiment_id`, `policy_id`, `policy_rule_id`,
  `branch_id`, `served_probability_bps`, `assignment_key_type`,
  `gclid_hash`, `traffic_flags`, `event_ts`). Confirm `assignment_id`
  presence per stage and whether `branch_id` is whole-page vs per-slot.
- **Define + test the GAds traffic predicate** (biggest correctness
  risk): which `assignment_key_type` / `traffic_flags` count as paid.
  Decide handling of `cookie`/`session`/`default` (default: exclude
  from cost/CPA, badge "GAds-detected traffic only").
- Pick the **reporting timezone** (America/New_York / Ads business
  zone) for `assignment_day`; document it.
- Lock the exact metric formulas: assignment-level-unique funnel counts;
  `conversions_7d/30d/90d` semantics; right-censoring of immature
  cohorts; sample threshold (25); allocated-cost basis (must sum back to
  the aggregate snapshot total per day/site/campaign bucket).
- `EXPLAIN` the candidate refresh query over a realistic date range on
  current data volume; decide whether the one partial `lp_events` index
  is needed.
- Pick the initial refresh cadence (30-60 min; default to the slower
  end).

Deliverable: design note + the confirmed predicate/timezone/formulas.

### P1 — Grants, routes, access enforcement

Files: `shared/contracts/domain/auth.ts` (grant enum),
`helios/src/client/routes/metrics/MetricsLayoutPage.tsx`
(`MetricsTabId`, `METRICS_TABS`, `METRICS_TAB_ALIASES`), server auth
middleware/route guard.

- Add `MetricGrantKey` values `gads-bronx`, `gads-midtown`, `gads-all`.
- Add the three tab ids + aliases so
  `/metrics/gads-<site>` -> `/metrics/gads-<site>/landing-pages`.
- Add the typed `GADS_METRIC_SCOPES` registry (grant -> site scope).
- Server-side grant + scope enforcement; `gads-all` requires its own
  grant explicitly.
- Regression tests: Bronx user cannot read Midtown or all; Midtown
  cannot read Bronx or all; holding both site grants does **not** grant
  all; unauthorized responses leak no site list / no cross-site data.

### P2 — Rollup storage + refresh job

Files: new migration under `helios/...migrations`, new worker job under
`helios/src/worker/jobs/`, query helper under
`helios/src/server/db/queries/`.

- Migration: `gads_lp_rollup` (grain + measures per parent §3),
  `gads_lp_rollup_refresh_state`, and (only if P0 proved it needed) the
  one partial `lp_events` index.
- Idempotent refresh job on the P0 cadence: recompute a **bounded 90-day
  assignment-day horizon** (so late `lp_conversion`s update the correct
  older bucket), dedupe duplicate event posts, apply the GAds traffic
  predicate, compute counts in the reporting timezone, join allocated
  GAds cost conservatively, write the refresh-state row.
- Ship `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` for the refresh query in the commit
  body.
- Tests/fixtures: duplicate events deduped; late conversion updates the
  right assignment-day bucket; 7/30/90d counts correct; allocated cost
  sums back to the snapshot total.

### P3 — Serving endpoint

Files: `shared/contracts/api/gadsLandingPages.ts`,
`server/db/queries/gadsLandingPagesQueries.ts`, the route handler.

- `GET /api/gads/<site-scope>/landing-pages` returns hero KPIs + funnel
  + variant table (top N, 25-50) + per-site breakdown (for `gads-all`) +
  freshness/badging metadata, in **one** compact payload.
- Site predicate derived from the grant, never widened by client input.
- Reads **only** `gads_lp_rollup` + the refresh-state row; a test
  asserts no raw `lp_events` query on the serving path.
- Ship the full-fetch payload byte-size measurement (canon DB gate).

### P4 — UI (Landing pages sub-page)

Files: `helios/src/client/routes/metrics/gads/` (new `GAdsTab`,
`GAdsLandingPagesTab`), reuse `MetricsAccessGate`, range presets +
`RangeNudgeRow`, `ControlsSection`, metrics CSS; extract shared
`MetricRangeControls`.

- Sub-page nav: Landing pages active; Campaigns / Creative / Keywords /
  Policy health / Experiments / Evolution / Iteration as disabled
  "Coming soon" stubs.
- First screen order per parent §5: freshness+attribution strip -> KPI
  strip -> next-action card (top 3 review candidates, each with a direct
  action) -> funnel waterfall (biggest drop-off inline) -> variant table
  (mobile-first, sticky action column, low-sample toggle).
- Revenue/ROAS rendered "Unavailable" with explanatory copy; cost
  badged "allocated"; right-censored cohorts badged. No em-dashes.
- **Mandatory canon Oracle UI review before it ships** (record the link
  on the peer issue).

### P5 — Docs, observability, rollout

- Runbook notes: refresh cadence, how to inspect the last refresh, how
  to manually rebuild the rollup.
- Lightweight job logging/metrics for the refresh.
- Document the deferred V2 items (mss enrichment, revenue/ROAS, Timescale
  features, future sub-pages).
- Deploy via the canonical `self-deploy-helios` path (no manual service
  surgery).

---

## Out of scope (V2 / later epics)

mss event-schema enrichment (order id / revenue / device class /
page-load-failure event on `lp_conversion`); exact Sweed revenue
attribution + ROAS/CPA + cancellation/refund handling; gclid-level cost;
bandit-aware off-policy stats; the reserved sub-pages; Timescale
CAGGs/hypertable/HLL. Each gets its own design + Oracle review when it
lands.

P0 first: define+test the GAds traffic predicate, pick reporting timezone, lock formulas. Phases P0-P5.

Opaque slugs for the FB-US `branding/` landing-page family. **Split out of [#15](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/15) per operator decision (2026-06-15)** so this epic has its own tracking issue (one epic = one top-level issue, like #13/#16/#17/#18). #15 had already delegated both peers for the separate `nyc-seo-widgets` sub-epic, so the `materialise-child-epic` idempotency marker `(issue, peer)` would no-op under #15 — hence this dedicated issue.

## Goal

Make the FB-US `branding/` family's per-row `SLUG` segment **opaque** (reusing the existing `buildFreshlyBakedUsOpaquePublicRef` already used by `compare/`/`conquest/`) so cannabis brand names stop appearing in URL path segments and scoring against ad-policy / SEO classifiers. The canonical `/SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM` schema, the `/0` distributor, and the `utm_content=NUM:N` contract are unchanged — only the `branding` `SLUG` representation changes (literal → opaque).

The hard part: the `branding/` `/0` aliases are **live, already-approved Google-Ads final URLs**, so the cutover must not 404 any approved ad.

## Authoritative plan (already in-repo, operator-approved & Oracle-reviewed)

- Parent plan: [`docs/epics/branding-opaque-slugs/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/branding-opaque-slugs/EPIC_PLAN.md)
- Decisions resolved: [`docs/epics/branding-opaque-slugs/STATUS_2026-06-15_decisions-resolved.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/branding-opaque-slugs/STATUS_2026-06-15_decisions-resolved.md)
- Child plans: [`child-epics/mostly-static-sites/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/branding-opaque-slugs/child-epics/mostly-static-sites/EPIC_PLAN.md), [`child-epics/automation/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/branding-opaque-slugs/child-epics/automation/EPIC_PLAN.md)

## Operator decisions (RESOLVED — EPIC_PLAN §6)

1. **308** literal→opaque (not `noindex`+canonical).
2. **Migrate** the approved ads' final URLs to opaque, via an **operator-run** Google Ads Editor CSV round-trip; agents emit the literal→opaque mapping (Helios P3) but never touch the Ads account; P1 `308` back-compat stays through the re-review window.
3. Branding migration proceeds + a **read-only brand-name-leakage audit** of the other families & FB-NYC slugs (expands only if a real leak is found).

## Next action for the worker that picks this up

Materialise the two peer child epics via the `Materialise-Child-Epic:` trailer flow with **`Parent-Issue: #<THIS ISSUE>`** (body files are already committed in the tree). Single trailer block, e.g.:

Materialise-Child-Epic: FreshlyBakedNYC/automation
Child-Epic-Title: Opaque branding/ slugs - Helios control plane (top-level#<THIS>)
Child-Epic-Body-File: docs/epics/branding-opaque-slugs/child-epics/automation/EPIC_PLAN.md

# Opaque `branding/` slugs — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Thin index over the authoritative parent plan
> [`docs/epics/branding-opaque-slugs/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in `virusdave/top-level`. Where this and the parent disagree, the parent
> wins — fix this doc. Tracking issue:
> [virusdave/top-level#19](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/19)
> (split from #15).
> **Operator-approved (2026-06-15); parent §6 decisions are RESOLVED and
> folded in below.** This peer issue materialises under top-level **#19**
> via the `Materialise-Child-Epic:` trailer flow — the work scope here is
> final.

## Scope (Helios control plane)

Make Helios speak the **same opaque `branding` ref** that
`mostly-static-sites` consumes, so the bandit/`NUM` emission, the signed
bundle, and any ad-URL producer reference branding rows **without the
literal brand name**.

**BINDING:** Helios still only decides **`NUM`** (the variant) and
publishes weights/kill-lists evaluated locally by the existing mss
middleware (parent §0, [#13 §6](../../../unified-landing-engine/EPIC_PLAN.md)).
This epic changes only the **`SLUG` representation** Helios emits for
`branding` — literal → opaque. No new route shapes, no schema change.

## First task: confirm the in-repo facts

The top-level repo cannot read automation source. Locate (parent names the
likely area, `helios/src/server/ads/…`):

- where the bandit / `NUM` emission and the signed bundle reference a
  branding row's `SLUG` (currently the literal brand id);
- any ad-final-URL / ValueTrack producer that builds `branding/` `/0`
  URLs;
- how `compare/`/`conquest/` already emit their opaque refs (reuse that
  exact path/helper-equivalent for parity with mss).

## Phase (parent §5)

- **P3 — emit the opaque branding ref.** Only after mss prod serves opaque
  and protects literal URLs (parent P0–P2). The bandit/`NUM` emission, the
  bundle, and any new-ad-URL producer reference branding rows by the
  **same** opaque ref mss uses. Add a **bundle-compile parity check**:
  every emitted branding ref must resolve in the mss registry (same spirit
  as the existing `MAX_VARIANT_BY_PURPOSE` / variant-id drift guard) so
  Helios can never publish an opaque ref mss cannot decode. The operator
  chose **migrate** (parent §6.2), so Helios additionally emits the
  **literal→opaque mapping** for every affected `branding/` `/0` final URL
  — the input the operator's one-off Ads-Editor CSV migration consumes.
  Agents do **not** touch the Ads account.
- **P4 (with operator/mss).** Staged rollout + deploy via
  `self-deploy-helios` under operator approval. The operator runs the
  one-off Ads-Editor CSV final-URL **migrate** (parent §6.2 — export →
  rewrite literal finals to opaque → re-import) using the mapping above
  for the already-approved ad final URLs; absorb the Google re-review on
  migrated ads. mss P1 `308` back-compat stays in place throughout.

## Verification

- Bundle-compile parity test: every emitted branding ref resolves in the
  mss registry; build/test green.
- Prove identical `brand-id → opaque-ref` output against the **shared
  contract** mss publishes (checked-in test vectors / generated manifest /
  importable package — parent §7), in CI.
- Each landing commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#19`.

## Coordination

P3 depends on the mss opaque scheme (parent P0–P2) landing first — agree
the shared output **contract** (not just "same code") before Helios emits
opaque branding refs.

# Opaque `branding/` slugs — `mostly-static-sites` child epic

> Thin index over the authoritative parent plan
