> folded in below.** This peer issue materialises under top-level **#19**
> via the `Materialise-Child-Epic:` trailer flow — the work scope here is
> final.

## Scope (FB-US thin runtime)

Make the `branding/` family's `SLUG` segment **opaque**, reusing the exact
`buildFreshlyBakedUsOpaquePublicRef` helper already powering
`compare/`/`conquest/`. The brand name must disappear from every
crawler-visible URL, with **zero 404s** for already-approved Google-Ads
`/0` final URLs.

**BINDING:** do **not** change the canonical `/SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM`
schema, the `/0` distributor, or the `utm_content=NUM:N` contract (parent
§0, [#13 §6.1](../../../unified-landing-engine/EPIC_PLAN.md)). Only the
`branding` `SLUG` representation changes.

## First task: confirm the in-repo facts

The top-level repo cannot read mss source. Begin by verifying the exact
symbols (the parent names the likely locations):

- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/purpose-families.ts` — the brand registry,
  `MAX_VARIANT_BY_PURPOSE`, and `buildFreshlyBakedUsOpaquePublicRef`
  (signature, determinism, whether it is family-scoped or global).
- the `branding/` route segment — `generateStaticParams`, page param
  parse, and the registry/NUM guard.
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/middleware.ts` — existing legacy-form `308`
  redirects (the pattern P1 extends) and the `/0` re-roll/rewrite.

## Phases (parent §5 — production-visible order)

- **P0 — dual-accept.** Route accepts **both** literal and opaque `SLUG`;
  reuse the opaque helper for `branding`; `generateStaticParams` builds
  opaque pages (+ transitional literal pages so nothing 404s yet). Page
  resolves opaque→row; the registry/NUM guard `notFound()`s unknown refs
  and out-of-range `NUM`. No emitted-surface flip yet.
- **P1 — literal back-compat live.** Middleware `308` literal→opaque
  (operator chose `308`, parent §6.1 — **not** `noindex`+canonical),
  same-origin, full query preserved (`gclid`/`gbraid`/`wbraid` + UTMs +
  ValueTrack), `/0` redirect-chain handled intentionally (parent §5.1).
- **P2 — de-emit literals.** Internal links, `<link rel=canonical>`, and
  the `branding/` sitemap entries emit **opaque only**, in the **same
  deploy** so the literal + opaque pages are never both indexable. (P1
  already protects literals.)
- **Audit (read-only, parent §6.4).** Enumerate every other LP family's
  (and FB-NYC's) URL `SLUG` source and confirm whether any literal
  brand/cannabis token can appear in a crawler-visible URL. Operator does
  not expect a leak but asked us to verify. Deliver the findings; only if
  a real leak is found does it expand into further opaque migration
  (re-scoped with the operator). Does **not** block the branding work.
- **P4 (with operator/Helios).** Operator runs the one-off Ads-Editor CSV
  final-URL **migrate** (parent §6.2) using the Helios-emitted
  literal→opaque mapping; canary one `SITE/branding` pair; monitor
  404s + Google-Ads disapprovals; deploy under operator approval. `308`
  back-compat stays in place through and after the migration.

## Verification

- Build green with opaque `generateStaticParams`.
- Redirect unit/e2e: literal→opaque preserves `gclid`/UTMs; redirect-chain
  (literal `/0` → opaque) is the intended single hop or the accepted
  two-hop `308`+`307`, correct statuses, `/0` re-roll stays `no-store`.
- **URL-emission audit test:** no literal brand name in any internal link
  / canonical / sitemap entry for `branding/`.
- **Opaque-ref stability test:** checked-in `brand-id → opaque-ref` test
  vectors (the cross-repo contract — see Coordination); ref derives from
  an immutable normalized row key; build fails on any collision.
- Each landing commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#19`.

## Coordination

The opaque scheme **must** match Helios (`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`)
output exactly. Don't rely on "same code in two repos" — publish a shared
**contract** (checked-in test vectors / generated manifest / importable
package) that both repos prove against in CI. Agree it before opaque ads
are emitted (parent P3 depends on this).

Reuse buildFreshlyBakedUsOpaquePublicRef; zero 404 for approved /0 ad URLs; read-only leakage audit of other families + FB-NYC. Operator chose 308 + migrate (parent EPIC_PLAN §6).

> top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the
> `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (Helios monorepo) slice** of that design,
> covering both the `helios/` and `ads/` packages.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation@master` that
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#20
> ```

> **Re-read the parent `EPIC_PLAN.md` before starting** — it is the
> single source of truth; this file is a thin index over it.

## Binding standards (from the parent, do not weaken)

- Required gates (lint, typecheck, test, build) green on `master`.
- No first-party TypeScript `any` (`as any`, `: any`, `any[]`, `<any>`).
- Tests deterministic; tests never touch prod serving resources; force
  test-only config (no `??=` fallback to ambient prod env).
- No disabled/weakened gates (`--no-verify`, `ts-ignore`, `.skip` /
  `.only`, commented-out checks) without an equal-or-stronger replacement.
- Verify in a fresh ephemeral checkout; heavy commands under
  `large-action-lock`. Attach an Agent Gate Record per commit / issue
  update.

## Scope owned by this repo

### Phase A — `helios/` client typecheck debt

1. **Fix the ~13 real client type errors** so
   `tsc -p tsconfig.client.json --noEmit` passes:
   - `Pill` `children` typed `string` but passed `string[]`;
   - `number` → `string` prop mismatches;
   - maplibre `Geometry` / `LngLatLike` casts.
2. **`tsconfig.client.json` hygiene** — stop pulling `*.test.ts` and
   node-using `shared/` modules into the *client* typecheck; they belong
   to the server/node typecheck, not the browser bundle. (Doing this
   first may shrink the error list in step 1.)
3. **Re-enable the client typecheck** in `.githooks/pre-commit`
   (`tsc -p tsconfig.client.json --noEmit`) and remove the
   "disabled, ~9 errors" note. The re-enabled hook must match CI.

### Phase B — `helios/` `any` + test-config debt

4. **Remove the ~31 first-party `any`** in `helios/src` (give each a
   real type; no blanket `unknown` cast-through that re-hides it).
5. **Force test-only config** in smoke/tests — replace
   `DATABASE_URL ??= ...` and any sibling ambient-prod fallbacks with an
   explicit ephemeral test resource, GC'd on every exit path. No test
   may reach a prod DB / live server / prod credential.

### Phase C — `ads/`

6. **Remove first-party `any`** (≈14 files).
7. **Ensure a typecheck/test gate exists for `ads/`** and is green
   (if `ads/` has no gate wired today, add one).

### Phase D — scaffolding to stay green (do once for this repo)

8. **Required-status CI** on `master` / PRs running the full gate set
   (lint, typecheck — server *and* client, test, build).
9. **no-explicit-`any` scanner** — ESLint
   `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: error` where ESLint exists, else
   a grep gate over first-party `src`.
10. **disabled-gate scanner** — flag `--no-verify` recipes,
    commented-out checks, `ts-ignore`, and `.skip` / `.only` in
    committed tests.
11. **test-resource scanner** — flag prod URLs / credentials and
    ambient-env `??=` fallbacks in tests.
12. **Pre-commit hooks installed and matching CI** — no client-typecheck
    carve-out.

## Acceptance

Fresh ephemeral checkout; full gate set (server + client typecheck,
lint, test, build) run and **recorded green** under `large-action-lock`;
scanners (Phase D) added and passing; pre-commit hooks match CI with no
carve-outs; Agent Gate Record attached. Sole exception to green is an
active prod incident, repaired to green immediately after.

# task-dag: one canonical RUNTIME (B1) — retire per-repo vendored copies

## Decision

task-dag must be a **true single-canonical runtime** living **only** in
`virusdave/top-level` (`scripts/task-dag` + `scripts/task-dag.d/`), invoked
from there by every consumer. Retire the current "single source +
byte-identical **vendored copies**" model (peer copies + the
`task-dag-drift-guard.yml` CI), which the operator does not want as the
steady state.

Rationale recorded in `docs/task_dag/CLI_DISTRIBUTION.md`. The old
vendoring justification ("Actions runners can't reach top-level") is
obsolete: the fleet has a GitHub App with cross-org auth (used by
`cross-repo-completion-sync.yml` / `materialise-child-epic.yml`), and
agents already make an ephemeral top-level checkout for canon.

**Verified keystone:** `task-dag.d/` is sourced relative to `BASH_SOURCE[0]`
while all git ops run against the **cwd** (no `-C`, no startup `cd`), so the
canonical script invoked by absolute path from a peer repo's cwd operates on
that peer repo using canonical helpers. Proven against `automation`.

## Phase A — DONE (top-level `0f88976`)

Agent-facing, doc-only, reversible:
- `docs/canon/rules/WORKFLOW.md`: agents run `"$cw/scripts/task-dag"` from
  their ephemeral top-level checkout against the peer cwd; keep/recreate the
  checkout for the session.
- `docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md`: stop removing the canon-read checkout
  immediately (it is the task-dag runtime).
- `scripts/task-dag` header + `docs/task_dag/CLI_DISTRIBUTION.md`: record B1
  + phased plan.

## Phase B — peer CI runtime fetch (must land before C)

For each peer that runs task-dag in CI (`automation`, `mostly-static-sites`,
`nixos-sbc`, `helios-parser-configs`, `shared-workflows`):
- Add a centralised setup in `Nicponskis/shared-workflows`: mint a GitHub
  App token with `contents:read` on top-level, fetch the canonical CLI to
  `$RUNNER_TEMP` at a **pinned top-level SHA**, expose
  `TASK_DAG="$RUNNER_TEMP/.../scripts/task-dag"`.
- Convert peer workflows/scripts (e.g. automation
  `.github/scripts/create-task-commit.sh`) to call `"$TASK_DAG"` (with a
  transitional `: "${TASK_DAG:=scripts/task-dag}"` fallback). Always invoke
  from the peer repo cwd (`$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`), fetch top-level into
  `$RUNNER_TEMP` so it never dirties the peer worktree.
- **Canary `automation` first** (it exercises `delegate` + claim flows);
  require one green full run before touching other peers.
- Keep vendored copies + drift-guard as rollback during all of Phase B.
- Verify token scope across the three credential surfaces: top-level fetch,
  peer task-ref push, and `gh` issue ops for `delegate`/completion-sync.

## Phase C — remove vendored copies + retire drift-guard (last)

Per peer, only after that peer's Phase B is green:
- Delete `scripts/task-dag` + `scripts/task-dag.d/`.
- Remove the `task-dag-drift-guard.yml` invocation.
- Clean stale `scripts/task-dag` references in peer `AGENTS.md`.
- Replace drift-guard protection with **central top-level quality gates**:
  `bash -n`, shellcheck, and fixture-repo smoke tests of
  `frontier`/`claim`/`complete`/`breakdown`/`block`/`unblock`/`drop` + a
  cross-repo dry path.

## Optional follow-up — `github-worker/bin/task-dag` shim

Durable convenience so agents/CI never depend on a hand-managed `$cw`. Must
**exec the real canonical script by absolute path** (NOT a symlink — symlink
breaks `BASH_SOURCE[0]` helper resolution), resolving via
`$TASK_DAG_TOP_LEVEL` or a short-lived ephemeral top-level checkout. Treat
as a small follow-up, not a blocker.

## Cross-cutting guardrails

- Maintain task-ref/metadata backward compatibility; bump `task-dag
  --version` when protocol changes; don't use new commands in a peer CI
  until that peer's pin is bumped.
- A→B→C ordering is mandatory: never remove a vendored copy before that
  repo's CI proves it can fetch+run the canonical runtime.

Oracle-reviewed (plan, ordering, safety). See top-level
`docs/task_dag/CLI_DISTRIBUTION.md`.

issues.body:
We seem to have a couple of recurring issues that add massive development time, cost, and waste.

1) The build process appears to be quite sensitive, sometimes requiring particular folders, outputs, node_modules, etc, and other times or modes (test?) failing if it does see those things?  Am I getting this right?  This needs to be redesigned so that a build and a test run will always succeed on master.  If the build has prerequisites, the build script should effect those or ensure they exist before wasting lots of time.

2) The build process appears to be EXTREMELY heavyweight.  I don't know where the time and resources are being spent; i suspect it is in a heavy core build process plus overweight testing, but you can figure this out.  Fundamentally we keep getting development serialized by all workers wanting to run MASSIVE build jobs, sometimes more than one job in sequence each, and they each have to take a large-task-lock to move forward.  Very bad; if we can get the benefits of automated checking (typechecking, property testing, etc) and pare WAY down the resources and time needed to complete a build, and to ensure that a build, once started over valid code, will succeed and not get derailed by various ancillary concerns like whether it should setup its dependencies or assume they've already been set up.

3) Any tool using "git reset --hard" is asking for trouble.  That is one of the few TRULY destructive git commands, and it generally doesn't require confirmation and is probably acting on the CWD's closest parent git repo.  Highly dangerous.  Let's not wait for that to bite us; fix it.

4) Are we sure that we've solved the "workers claiming available task-dag tasks have lengthy race windows where multiple workers can and do grab the same task"?  Or has that been finally solved in general?

5) Is there any way to make use of build artifact caching?  There's not a whole lot of first person code, all things considered, and I wouldn't be surprised if much of our build work is spent typechecking and building 3rdparty code or libraries.

Generally, builds and commits take WAY too long, are not super reliable, consume VAST resources, and need to be made sane.

Work with Oracle to design a better system and document the design here for operator approval, using `page-dave` when it's ready.

# Helios build hygiene — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#22](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/22)
> ("codebase cleanup & hygiene"). The authoritative design is
> [`docs/designs/codebase-cleanup-and-hygiene.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/codebase-cleanup-and-hygiene.md)
> in the top-level repo (§1 verified findings, §3.2 build design, §4
> Phase 3, §6 resolved decisions 4 & 5).
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`
> `master` and satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#22
> ```
>
> This is **Phase 3** only: small, low-risk build-setup changes that help
> even on the current shared production build box and need no off-prod
> infrastructure. The heavier "move build off prod / off-prod CI"
> work is **Phase 4**, tracked separately and parked in
> [virusdave/top-level#23](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/23).

## Verified starting state (read directly from `automation`)

- Helios build = plain `tsc` + `vite` over npm (`helios/package.json`):
  `build` = `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` (+ asset copy) then `vite
  build`. No turbo/nx, no build cache, no build/test CI.
- `helios/package.json` has **no** `typecheck` / `test` / `lint` scripts
  (so "build & test always pass on master" is currently unenforceable).
  `vitest` is a dependency but unscripted.
- `tsconfig.server.json` names a `tsBuildInfoFile` but does **not** set
  `incremental` / `composite`, so the file is inert and every server
  build re-typechecks from scratch. `skipLibCheck: true` is already set.
- No `flake.nix` / devShell — toolchain (node/tsc/vite) is whatever the
  host provides.

> Re-verify all of the above in a **fresh ephemeral checkout** before
> editing; do not trust this snapshot blindly. Run any heavy command
> (`npm ci`, `tsc`, `vite build`, `vitest`) under `large-action-lock` —
> the build host is the 2 vCPU / ~2 GiB production box.

## Scope owned by this repo (Helios) — Phase 3

### H1 — Turn on incremental TypeScript (near-zero risk, behavior-preserving)
- Set `"incremental": true` in `tsconfig.server.json` so the existing
  `tsBuildInfoFile` actually caches and warm `build:server` stops
  re-typechecking from scratch. Consider `composite` + project
  references for the client/server split if it's a clean win; don't
  force it.
- Persist the `.tsbuildinfo` between runs (on-box now; graduates to
  `actions/*` cache when an off-prod builder exists — that's Phase 4 / #23).
- Ensure `tsc` `include` does **not** pick up `dist`/build outputs as
  source (`exclude` them) so outputs are never re-consumed as input.

### H2 — Add the missing check scripts + make `check` the required pre-push gate
- Add to `helios/package.json`:
  - `typecheck` → `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit` (and the client
    tsconfig if applicable),
  - `test` → `vitest run`,
  - `check` → runs `typecheck` + `test` (+ a fast build sanity if cheap).
- Wire `check` as the **required pre-push gate** each agent runs before
  `git push` (the decided "master always green" mechanism for now;
  design decision 5). A GitHub-hosted/self-hosted CI backstop +
  branch-protection is Phase 4 (#23), not this epic.

### H3 — Idempotent, self-prerequisite build env (#22 problem 1)
- Add an `ensure-build-env` step the build owns and that is safe cold or
  warm:
  - `npm ci` (lockfile-pinned) when `node_modules` is absent/stale,
    using the on-box `~/.npm` cache;
  - `mkdir -p` every output dir the scripts assume (generalise the
    existing `mkdir -p dist/server/...` so no step fails on a
    missing-or-already-present dir);
  - never assume — and never fail merely because — `node_modules`/`dist`
    already exist.
- Wire `build` / `test` / `check` to call `ensure-build-env` first.
- Add an **idempotence matrix** test (cold checkout; warm `node_modules`;
  stale `dist`; post `git clean -xfd`; run `check` twice) so artifact
  flakiness can't regress.

### H4 — Reproducible toolchain via Nix devShell (operator suggestion D)
- Add a `flake.nix` (or `shell.nix`) devShell pinning node + npm (+ any
  system libs) so `nix develop` / `nix-shell` gives an identical,
  declarative build environment locally and on the box. Additive; pairs
  with `ensure-build-env` (devShell = toolchain, script = project
  prereqs).

## Out of scope (Phase 4 — see #23)
- Moving heavy build/test off the production box onto a builder host.
- Off-prod build/test CI + `actions/*` caches + branch-protection
  required checks.
- Nix **binary cache** / Nix-closure deploy.

## Acceptance
- `helios` has working `typecheck` / `test` / `check` scripts; `check`
  is green on `master` and is the documented required pre-push gate.
- Server build is incremental (warm builds measurably faster) and never
  consumes build outputs as source.
- A cold checkout and a warm checkout both `check` successfully (the
  idempotence matrix passes); the build sets up its own prerequisites.
- A `flake.nix` devShell pins the toolchain.
- Every satisfying commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#22`.

Re-verify state in a fresh ephemeral checkout; run any heavy cmd (npm ci/tsc/vite/vitest) under large-action-lock since the build host is the 2vCPU/2GiB prod box. Out of scope (Phase 4, see top-level#23): moving build off-prod, off-prod CI/caches, branch protection, Nix binary cache. Every satisfying commit carries Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#22.

> **Parked epic — immediately blocked pending operator approval to pick it back up.**
> Migrated out of [#22](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/22) ("codebase cleanup & hygiene") per operator instruction so #22 can close on its in-scope work (task-dag safety + Helios build hygiene). Do **not** start this work until the operator unblocks it.

# Future improvements to building

This epic captures the **heavier, infrastructure-dependent** build improvements that were "Phase 4" in the codebase-cleanup design ([`docs/designs/codebase-cleanup-and-hygiene.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/codebase-cleanup-and-hygiene.md), §3.2 / §4 / §6). They are deliberately deferred: each needs an operator decision and/or new infrastructure, so this epic stays **blocked** until the operator says to resume.

## Scope (deferred work)

1. **Move heavy build off the production box.** Today all heavyweight `tsc` + `vitest` + `vite build` runs on `vps-nixos-3` (production Helios: 2 vCPU / ~2 GiB), funnelled through one host-wide `large-action-lock`. This is the root cause of build serialization (#22 problem 2). The fix is to run heavy CI on a dedicated builder host so the prod box only does lightweight deploy/smoke.
   - **Gated on:** the operator provisioning/upgrading a builder host (design §A — operator indicated one is coming).

2. **Add off-prod build/test CI** with `actions/*` npm + tsc `.tsbuildinfo` caches, as a backstop to the per-push `check` gate that Helios build hygiene (#22) introduces.
   - **Open decision:** CI home + credentials — GitHub-hosted runners (metered, both repos are private) vs. a self-hosted runner on the builder host.

3. **Branch-protection required checks** on `master` (the durable "master always green" backstop), layered on top of the required pre-push `check`.

4. **Nix-closure deploy (longer term):** build the Helios derivation off-prod, push to a binary cache, and have `self-deploy-helios` realize it, so production never compiles third-party code and the global `large-action-lock` serialization disappears.
   - **Deferred sub-decision:** Nix **binary cache** itself was deferred at #22's current scale (design decision 4); revisit when it earns its keep (a spare S3 bucket + closure-signing key).

## Why blocked

Every item above needs either new infrastructure (a builder host) or an operator decision (CI home/credentials, binary-cache investment) that the operator chose to defer on cost grounds. Parking it as its own blocked epic keeps it tracked without re-dispatching workers onto it.

## To resume

Operator unblocks the epic (or replies here) once a builder host exists and the CI-topology/credentials questions are decided.

## GAds evolver introspection dashboard (Evolution + Iteration sub-pages)

Canonical top-level epic promoting the approved design from
[`Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites#15`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/issues/15)
("GAds iteration dashboard"). The operator approved the design proposal
on that issue ("Approved proceed"); this epic carries it forward.

**Origin & approval:** [mostly-static-sites#15](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/issues/15)
(design proposal `docs/epics/gads-evolver-introspection/PROPOSAL.md`, Oracle-reviewed).
**IA lineage:** [virusdave/top-level#18](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/18)
(`gads-landing-analytics`) — this epic builds out the **`Evolution`** and
**`Iteration`** sub-pages that #18 reserved as "Coming soon" stubs under
`/metrics/gads-<site>/`.
**Design philosophy:** decision
[`0003-joint-gads-lp-optimization-not-audit-grade`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-kb/decisions/0003-joint-gads-lp-optimization-not-audit-grade.md)
— a rapid hill-climbing introspection surface, **not** an audit-grade system.

### What this is
An observability surface for **how Helios reacted** — the GAds + landing-page
evolver's own decisions, actions, and outcomes (L1/L2/L3 loop). Every screen
answers: **"Is Helios learning from its own GAds decisions, or repeating
waste?"** It is **not** a re-implementation of Google's ad-performance
dashboards (those stay canonical in the GAds web UI).

### Where the implementation lives
**Entirely in [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)**
(the Helios monorepo — the GAds + LP evolvers are under Helios now). This
top-level issue is the canonical parent; a single automation child epic
(materialised via the standard `Materialise-Child-Epic:` flow) holds all
implementation. `mostly-static-sites#15` has **no implementation slice** and
is delegated here.

issues.body:
This ticket is the landing-page-system equivalent of https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/24 for GAds.

Consult with Oracle to design the page, its UI/UX, its contents, etc.  Ensure it is mobile-friendly and helpful for a non-context operator.  Page must be responsive, efficient, organized into subpages if appropriate for the contents & length, etc.

I want to know how the GAds hill-climbing system is, well, hill-climbing, how it made the decisions it did, why those are good, why rejected ideas aren't, etc.  I especially want to see that it's not reverting to generic "slop" as an easy way to hit the "policy approval" goal.  It's easy to get text that will pass policy in isolation, and it's easy to post text people will click on in isolation, but the goal isn't JUST policy passing and clicks, it's holistic in nature:  We want the RIGHT impressions, that lead to the RIGHT clicks, leading to the RIGHT interactions that yield eventual conversions.  To date, I have been generally concerned that the suggested replacements or modifications on the GAds side have been all "generic slop" oriented, geared towards passing policy checks, but without anything compelling that I, as a person skimming the google results page, would want to click on.  They generally wouldn't be relevant _at all_ to my search, so i would just scroll past them quickly.  The stuff being replaced, for better or worse, tended to be contextually relevant (for competitors, a play on their name or slogan.  For brands, a play on the branding or name) intended to actually catch people's attention.  

To date, these have actually worked reasonably well, *when they pass policy* well enough to get impressions.  Far better than the generic ads i started with (which were very much like the LLM suggestions that concern me).  The problem is keeping them approved, and my *suspicion* is that the disapprovals were *mostly* LP-related rather than ad-related.  I could be wrong, however.  But either way, this set of dashboards and pages should help me understand this sytem in detail, and conclusively answer the questions mentioned.

Ask questions here before implementing if the intent and desire here is unclear, otherwise begin breaking this down into tasks.

```yaml
delegated_to:
  - repo: FreshlyBakedNYC/automation
    issue: 53
    note: Build the LP-system companion to the GAds evolver introspection dashboard: inferred disapproval attribution (LP vs ad, with hill-climbable/versioned criteria), slop/signal copy-quality inspection, and LP iteration run drilldowns under the existing grant-gated GAds metrics IA.
```

# Helios LP evolution inspection pages — automation child epic

> **Child epic of** [`virusdave/top-level#25`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/25)
> (`lp-evolution-inspection`). The **parent epic plan is authoritative**
> for design, philosophy, IA, data sources, page content, and the
> boundary vs #24:
> [`virusdave/top-level:docs/epics/lp-evolution-inspection/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/lp-evolution-inspection/EPIC_PLAN.md).
> This child holds the Helios (`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`) implementation
> scope only.
>
> **Every implementation commit** that satisfies any part of this epic MUST
> carry the trailer `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#25`, and SHOULD also
> carry `Phase: P<n>` (`P1`..`P7`) so the cross-repo-completion-sync
> workflow posts a per-phase progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope (one-line)

Implement the **LP-system companion** to the GAds evolver introspection
dashboard ([#24](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/24)) under
the existing per-site, grant-gated `/metrics/gads-<site>/` GAds tab system
(IA + grants from [#18](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/18)):
an **LP Evolution** overview with **inferred disapproval attribution**
(LP-related vs ad-related — Google gives only a coarse signal, so this is a
**cross-entity LP/family correlation** engine, not a field lookup),
**suspect-LP / suspect-family** steering, and a **slop-vs-signal**
copy-quality lens, plus an **LP Iteration** per-run / per-candidate
drilldown. It reads the evolver's own
LP decision/outcome data already in the Helios DB / filesystem. An
**introspection surface for how Helios reacted on landing pages and joint
ad/LP decisions**, not a re-implementation of Google's ad dashboards.
Rapid hill-climb, **not** audit-grade (decision
[0003](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-kb/decisions/0003-joint-gads-lp-optimization-not-audit-grade.md)).

## Binding constraints

- **Reuse #18's IA, grants (`gads-bronx` / `gads-midtown` / `gads-all`),
  scope registry, and serving model verbatim.** No new route shapes, no
  forked access model. `gads-all` is its own grant, never synthesised.
- **Coordinate with #24 — do not duplicate its ad-evolver pages.** Keep
  #24's `/evolution` + `/iteration` for ad-evolver loop health; #25 owns
  LP + joint-decision inspection. Cross-link both ways (parent plan §3);
  do not move #24's LP-reaction panel.
- **Server-derived site predicate.** Never trust a client-supplied
  site-widening param. Per-site pages must not leak cross-site rows.
- **Cheapest defensible DB use.** Bounded aggregate queries over the
  existing small tables (`landingpage_ad_outcomes`, `gads_ad_attempts`,
  `gads_lp_rollup`) + bounded reads of recent L2/L3/morning-bundle
  artifacts. **No** per-event fact table, no always-on derivation worker,
  no rollup/hypertable/CAGG/HLL in V1.
- **Honest approximations + first-class `unknown`.** Every estimate badged;
  never a fabricated precise-looking number; **never force an
  attribution** — `unknown` is a real answer. Honest empty states where a
  write path / data field is not yet confirmed.
- **Migrations do not auto-apply on deploy.** Any schema change is applied
  on prod by the agent only after Oracle DB review **and** explicit
  operator approval, then verified live (canon §3).

## Attribution is inference, not a lookup (binding — parent §0.1)

Google **deliberately withholds** the precise reason for a policy limit /
disapproval. The only signal it gives is **which hierarchy level**
(campaign / asset group / ad group / asset / ad) was limited and **which
policy topic** fired. There is **no ad-text-vs-LP source field** to read.
So the LP-vs-ad verdict is **inferred** by **correlating per-entity policy
state over the shared-final-URL/LP and page-family dimensions** (e.g. all
ad groups on a given LP limited while same-family siblings on other LPs
stay clean → that LP is suspect; the pattern may span a whole family). The
fix for a suspect LP must repair the *right* page — **never** flatten the
ad copy **or** the landing page into generic slop.

## Attribution criteria are hill-climbable, not constant (binding — parent §0.2)

The operator approved on the explicit condition that **the attribution
criteria themselves must be hill-climbable** — a simple fixed heuristic
(e.g. "95% of ads pointing at the LP are rejected") will be too crude once
the low-hanging fruit is gone. Binding on the Helios implementation:

- **No magic numbers in code.** Every verdict-deciding threshold, weight,
  and minimum (contrast minimums, suspicion-score weighting, topic→lever
  priors, confidence cutoffs) lives in **one named, versioned criteria
  set**, not scattered literals. V1 may be a deliberately simple ruleset,
  but it must be swappable without rewriting the engine.
- **Versioned + traceable verdicts.** Each attribution result records the
  **criteria version** that produced it plus the raw inputs it saw
  (implicated/clean contrast counts, topics, hierarchy level, outcome
  sequence). Responses carry the active criteria version; the UI badges it
  on every verdict/suspect row and exposes a "how this verdict was decided"
  trace so the operator can tune the *criteria*, not just read output.
- **V1 = explicit substrate for tuning, not a learned model.** An
  automated/learned attribution model is out of scope for V1; making the
  criteria explicit, parameterised, versioned, and auditable is in scope.
  See parent §0.2 / §7.2.2.

## Data + capability gates (P1 must resolve before the engine claims a verdict)

- Confirm prod population/scoping of `landingpage_ad_outcomes`,
  `gads_ad_attempts`, `gads_lp_rollup`, L2/morning-bundle artifacts, L3
  outputs.
- **Confirm whether candidate copy + rejected candidates are recorded** in
  artifacts (the slop-vs-signal "why rejected" view depends on it).
- **Confirm the inference substrate** (the centerpiece depends on it, not
  on a Google source field — there isn't one): (a) we capture **per-entity
  policy state over time + hierarchy level + policy topic**; (b) we can
  **join each entity to its final-URL/LP and to its page family** (likely
  via `landingpage_ad_outcomes` / `gads_lp_rollup` / the cluster registry).
  Without the LP/family join the correlation engine cannot run.
- Confirm whether any cheap LP text snapshot exists (LP-promise match); do
  **not** crawl live pages in V1.
- Emit a **capability matrix** mapping every parent-plan panel (§7–§8) to
  `wired` / `partially wired` / `not wired yet`; missing fields become UI
  badges, not guessed data.

## Phases (detail in the parent plan §6–§8)

| Phase | Deliverable | Closure criteria |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Data audit + capability matrix | Confirm prod population/scoping of the tables/artifacts above; confirm candidate/rejected-candidate presence; **confirm the inference substrate** — per-entity policy state + hierarchy level + policy topic, **and** the entity→final-URL/LP and entity→family join the correlation engine needs (no Google ad-vs-LP source field exists); produce the panel→capability matrix. No per-site page ships until site scoping is safe; the engine must have the LP/family join before claiming a suspect. |
| **P2** | Minimal schema/index support | Reuse #24's `site` fix for `gads_ad_attempts` if landed; else add `site text null` + best-effort backfill; hide unknown-scope per-site, show under `gads-all` badged. Optional tiny artifact/run-index table **only if** P1 proves scans are expensive (no large JSON/prompts in DB). Cheap indexes only if justified by plans. No rollup/hypertable/CAGG/HLL. Migration gated on Oracle DB review + operator approval. |
| **P3** | Backend contracts + **correlation/inference engine** | Typed `GadsLpEvolutionResponse` / `GadsLpIterationRunsResponse` / `GadsLpIterationRunDetailResponse` (capability flags in every response); grant-gated `GET /api/gads/lp-evolution`, `/api/gads/lp-iterations`, `/api/gads/lp-iterations/:runId`; server-derived site predicate; bounded ranges. **Cross-entity correlation engine (parent §7.2):** group per-entity policy state by shared final-URL/LP and family; emit `lp_related`/`ad_related`/`mixed`/`undetermined` with evidence grade, confidence bucket, and implicated-vs-clean contrast counts (anti-coincidence guard); never force a verdict. **Criteria are a single named, versioned set (parent §0.2): no magic numbers in code; each verdict records its criteria version + raw inputs; the response carries the active criteria version.** Tests cover correlation logic (suspect LP when siblings clean; no false suspect on thin contrast) + access (Bronx cannot read Midtown/all; `gads-all` explicit; unknown-scope hidden per-site; payload bounded). |
| **P4** | LP Evolution UI (overview + attribution + suspect LP/family) | `/metrics/gads-<site>/lp-evolution` (parent §7): scope/freshness/capability strip, LP heartbeat, attribution snapshot + `?panel=attribution` detail, **suspect-LP / suspect-family ranked list (parent §7.2.1)**, planned-action×outcome matrix, hotspots, funnel guardrail, recent decision log. Honest empty/low-confidence states + contrast counts; no fake attribution. **Mandatory Oracle UI review before ship.** |
| **P5** | Slop-vs-signal lens | Quality triage on overview + `?panel=slop-signal` (parent §7.3): deterministic context-token preservation, generic-phrase + reuse detector, intent specificity, hook preservation, optional LP-promise match (badged if unwired), chosen-vs-rejected comparison, context-loss watchlist, **positive-examples table**. Deterministic/explainable V1 lens; candidate/rejected absence handled honestly; no opaque LLM score required. |
| **P6** | LP Iteration browser | `/metrics/gads-<site>/lp-iteration` (parent §8): bounded run timeline + run detail (decision flow + attempt/candidate table), candidate detail drawer, bounded artifact links, DB-only fallback + badge when L2 JSON missing. No unbounded historical-file loads. Run-detail links from #24 can target this page. |
| **P7** | Docs, tests, rollout readiness | Operator runbook (read attribution + evidence grades; interpret slop risk; interpret `unknown`; debug missing site scope; #24 vs #25); access + classifier tests; query-cost notes; UI reviewed; epics updated; ready for **gated `self-deploy-helios`** (no deploy from the planning worker). |

## Backend contract sketch (P3)

```ts
GadsLpEvolutionResponse          // overview + attribution + slop/signal summaries + capability flags
GadsLpIterationRunsResponse      // bounded run timeline
GadsLpIterationRunDetailResponse // single run: decision flow + attempt/candidate rows + artifact links
```

Each response carries `capabilities` flags (`siteScopedAttempts`,
`entityPolicyState`, `policyTopics`, `entityLpJoin`, `familyMapping`,
`candidateText`, `rejectedCandidates`, `lpTextSnapshot`, `lpRollup`) so the
UI badges exactly what is / isn't wired. (Note: there is **no**
`explicitPolicySource` flag — Google does not expose an ad-vs-LP cause;
the verdict comes from the correlation engine, gated on `entityLpJoin` /
`familyMapping`.) Site scope is derived server-side from the
authenticated GAds metrics tab context, never from a widening query param;
follow Helios's existing route/site-encoding convention (the binding rule
is the access model, not the literal endpoint strings).

The attribution payload also carries the **active criteria version** (e.g.
`attributionCriteriaVersion`) and, per verdict/suspect row, the criteria
version + raw inputs that produced it (parent §0.2 / §7.2.2), so the UI can
badge which ruleset decided each call and the operator can hill-climb the
criteria rather than just read their current output.

## Out of scope (V1)

Causal lift / off-policy estimates, win probability, credible intervals,
regret; prompt/rule approval workflow + prompt-diff persistence; opaque LLM
copy-quality score; live LP crawling for promise-match; per-click cost /
revenue / ROAS; anomaly detection; heatmaps; any Timescale
CAGG/hypertable/HLL.

issues.body:
Worker dev loop needs optimization

I'm all for safe development, but my observations show agents are manually running full tests and large operations WAY too often, and those get serialized.  It's not at all uncommon for a single agent to self-serialize (via large task lock) two or three times PRIOR to committing a change, which then goes and runs all of those same tests and checks again!  The end result is that even trivial changes are taking agents 10-20 minutes to achieve, which is obscene.  We need to modify the default development process to streamline towards efficient development, where safety is (to extent possible) mechanically enforced via types, checks, etc, but where only FINAL gates are responsible for heavy checks, smoke tests, etc, which should basically never be run by agents directly.  Any check which takes more than ~30 seconds to run from a new ephemeral checkout on an existing worker with a normally-populated cache should be a candidate for splitting into two: the full "presubmit" version, and a "light, targeted" version that an agent can run and point to JUST the area that needs checking / testing / whatever.  When this ISN'T possible, and the check/test/whatever MUST be heavy, then agents must be warned that they shouldn't generally be invoking these by hand as part of the "normal" dev cycle unless there's an overriding, highly compelling reason to do so.

Most generally, the "dev cycle time" has roughly been increasing linearly with development progress, and that's highly concerning on its own, but when we consider that we still see many bugs DESPITE paying these development tax, it's not at all clear we're getting net benefit.  Optimize this, with oracle's help!

```yaml
delegated_to:
  - repo: FreshlyBakedNYC/automation
    issue: 52
    note: Split >30s helios/ + ads/ checks into a full CI presubmit plus light/targeted local commands; document a dev-loop table in AGENTS.md; lighten pre-commit hooks to fast/targeted (keep full gate as required CI). See parent docs/epics/dev-loop-optimization/EPIC_PLAN.md.
  - repo: Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites
    issue: 16
    note: Split the monolithic pnpm check into a full CI presubmit plus site/path-targeted local commands; document a dev-loop table in AGENTS.md; lighten pre-commit hooks to fast/targeted (keep full pnpm check as required CI). See parent docs/epics/dev-loop-optimization/EPIC_PLAN.md.
  - repo: virusdave/task-dag
    issue: 1
    note: Implement the reusable broken-master repair classifier + Tree-Fix trailer interpretation + chain-state + worker verifier per docs/designs/ci-broken-master-auto-repair.md. Carry Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#26 on implementation commits.
```

# Dev-loop optimization — `task-dag` child epic (broken-master auto-repair)

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#26](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/26).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/designs/ci-broken-master-auto-repair.md`](../../../../designs/ci-broken-master-auto-repair.md)
> and the parent
> [`docs/epics/dev-loop-optimization/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> (§6) in the top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the
> shared CI-driven broken-master auto-repair implementation** that lives
> in `virusdave/task-dag`.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `task-dag@master` that
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#26
> ```
>
> **Re-read the parent design doc before starting** — it is the single
> source of truth; this file is a thin index over it.

## Goal

Provide the reusable, race-safe mechanism that detects a red `master`,
files exactly **one** high-priority repair ticket per red streak ("repair
chain"), and interprets `Tree-Fix` commit trailers so a fix either
reaches green or escalates to a `continue`-mode repair task. All logic
lives once in `virusdave/task-dag` (the single home of task-dag / CI
automation); peer repos call it as a reusable workflow. top-level
coordinates only and does not host repair logic.

## Binding standards (from the parent, do not weaken)

- Two-gate green tree: this is the *final-gate* half made
  self-healing — it must never weaken the required full gate.
- No first-party `any`, no disabled/weakened gates, no `--no-verify`,
  tests deterministic and prod-resource-free (inherited from fleet-green
  [#20](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/20)).
- Trailers parsed with `git interpret-trailers`, never freeform grep.
- Idempotent + stale-run safe: never mutate chain state against a
  superseded SHA (see design §4).

## Scope owned by this repo (`virusdave/task-dag`)

1. **Reusable CI repair classifier workflow** — called after a repo's
   full required suite on `master`; implements the green/red/unknown
   classification and the chain open/update/close logic (design §2).
2. **Commit-trailer parser** for `Tree-Fix` / `Tree-Fix-Chain` /
   `Tree-Fix-Mode` via `git interpret-trailers`.
3. **Chain-state persistence** — a durable per-repo store (e.g. a
   `tasks/ci-chains/<repo>` ref or equivalent) holding the design §1
   fields (`Last-Green`, `First-Red`, `Current-Head`, `State`,
   `Repair-Mode`, `Repair-Issue`, `Repair-Attempt`).
4. **Idempotent repair ticket** creation/update — exactly one
   `ci-broken-master` + `priority:high` ticket per chain, ingested as a
   pickable task by the existing comment/issue sync.
5. **Tree-fix outcome handling** (design §3): green closes the chain +
   ticket; red-in-chain escalates to a `continue`-mode repair task; red
   with a green parent opens a fresh `initial` chain; repeated
   same-signature failures `BLOCK` + page after a small threshold.
6. **Stale-run / race handling** (design §4): per-repo/branch classifier
   concurrency (`cancel-in-progress: false`), ignore superseded SHAs,
   close green only when current.
7. **Worker verifier** helper/CLI — "is my target still the current
   first-red, unclaimed chain head?" — so workers don't hand-implement
   the §6 contract.
8. **Tests/fixtures** for the §4 race cases (out-of-order CI runs,
   continue-mode escalation, new-regression-vs-continuation, green
   closing the right chain).

## Out of scope (deferred / other repos)

- Peer repo CI wiring + branch protection (deferred peer child epics).
- Any change to top-level's pure event-wiring workflows.
- Force-push / non-FF `master` auto-repair (detect → `STALE`/`BLOCKED` +
  page instead).

## Acceptance

From a fresh ephemeral checkout, the implementation:

1. classifies green / red / unknown-parent correctly and opens **one**
   chain per red streak;
2. files exactly **one** high-priority repair ticket per chain;
3. ignores stale older CI runs (no reopen when a newer descendant is
   green);
4. on a failed tree-fix, creates a **continue**-mode repair task (not a
   new first-red task); a green tree-fix closes the chain + ticket;
5. parses `Tree-Fix*` trailers via `git interpret-trailers`, covered by
   tests/fixtures for the design §4 race cases;
6. provides the worker verifier helper used by canon
   [`WORKFLOW.md`](../../../../canon/rules/WORKFLOW.md) "CI-filed
   broken-master repair tasks";
7. Agent Gate Record (two-gate template) attached.
declarations.delegationNote: Implement the reusable broken-master repair classifier + Tree-Fix trailer interpretation + chain-state + worker verifier per docs/designs/ci-broken-master-auto-repair.md. Carry Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#26 on implementation commits.

Split the monolithic `pnpm check` (lint + typecheck + test + build) so

2. Pre-commit hooks fast/targeted; full `pnpm check` remains a required

## Summary

Add a **loud deprecation notice** to the `local` codepath of
[`scripts/ephemeral_checkout`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/scripts/ephemeral_checkout)
as **phase 1, before removing it**. The intended purpose of
`ephemeral_checkout` is *"a lightweight way to get a bespoke, owned clone
of a small remote repository in a self-cleaning location."* The `local`
mode (`git worktree add` / `git clone --local --shared` against an
on-disk repo) predates that intent, can lead agents astray (shared object
store, "attractive nuisance" local checkouts), and is slated for removal —
the remote/registry path will become the **only** path.

This task does **not** remove anything yet. It makes any agent/workflow
still relying on `local` mode *fail loudly* so we can find and migrate
them safely before removal.

## Background — where `local` mode lives

`scripts/ephemeral_checkout` resolves a `source_kind`. `source_kind="local"`
is reached two ways:

1. Explicit `--from-local` flag — parsed at
   [`scripts/ephemeral_checkout` ~L182](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/scripts/ephemeral_checkout#L182).
2. **Implicit fallback**: a positional `<repo-path>` that has no `origin`
   remote falls back to local —
   [~L252-L253](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/scripts/ephemeral_checkout#L252-L253).

The actual local clone/worktree work is the `local)` case at
[~L327-L349](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/scripts/ephemeral_checkout#L327-L349).

## Scope (this task)

In the `local` codepath, emit a prominent **deprecation notice to BOTH
stdout and stderr** on every invocation that resolves to `source_kind="local"`
(cover **both** entry points above — explicit `--from-local` and the
no-`origin` fallback).

The notice must clearly say:

- The `local`/`--from-local` mode is **deprecated and will be removed**;
  the remote/registry path is becoming the **only** supported path.
- Any agent or workflow that sees this and **cannot trivially adapt** to
  the remote path must:
  1. **shout loudly** (do not silently proceed),
  2. **`page-dave -p 4`** with details (what invoked `ephemeral_checkout`,
     which repo/path, and why it can't use the remote path), and
  3. **update the relevant GitHub issue** for the about-to-break
     process/workflow (or file one if none exists).

## Critical implementation constraint

`ephemeral_checkout`'s **stdout last line is the workspace path** — it is
script-consumed (`ws=$(ephemeral_checkout ... | tail -1)`; see
[~L355-L356](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/scripts/ephemeral_checkout#L355-L356))
and `--print-only` prints just the path. The stdout notice MUST be emitted
**before** the workspace path so the path remains the final stdout line and
`tail -1` consumers keep working. Do **not** alter `--print-only` output.
(Callers that capture *all* of stdout rather than `tail -1` will now also
see the notice — that is intentional per the operator request: such callers
*should* break loudly.)

Keep existing remote/registry behavior **unchanged** (no notice there).

## Out of scope (explicit follow-up, NOT this task)

- Actually **removing** `--from-local` / the `local)` case / the no-`origin`
  fallback and the related usage docs. File/track that as a follow-up once
  consumers have migrated.
- Known consumer to evaluate at removal time: `github-worker` passes a
  filesystem path as the checkout arg for transitional "local" repos under
  `REPO_SCAN_ROOT` — confirm it no longer depends on local mode before
  removal.

## Closure criteria

- Both `--from-local` and the no-`origin` fallback emit the notice on
  **stdout AND stderr**.
- Remote/registry path behavior unchanged (no notice).
- Machine contract preserved: `ephemeral_checkout <name> | tail -1` still
  yields the workspace path; `--print-only` output unchanged.
- `bash -n` + `shellcheck` clean; a smoke test confirms the notice on both
  streams and that the returned path is still usable.
- Decision/notes recorded (and a follow-up for removal noted).

## One-line summary

Some automated workers ("agents") still hand the operator terse, unexpanded,
un-hyperlinked text on operator-facing channels, **even after** we tightened
the rule that requires the opposite. This ticket is to investigate *why it
still happens* and add whatever enforcement is needed so it stops. It is
deliberately **parked (blocked)** until the operator confirms a fresh
recurrence — see "Why this is pre-blocked" below.

## Plain-language background (no prior context assumed)

- **What an "agent" is here:** an automated coding worker (an AI process)
  that picks up a task, does the work, and reports back to the operator
  (you) through some channel — a chat reply, a GitHub issue comment, a
  paged alert, or a published document.
- **What "operator-facing UX" means:** any text or document an agent puts in
  front of the operator is treated as user-interface / user-experience — it
  must be readable by someone with *zero* context. Concretely, every
  shorthand reference (a task, a plan, an "epic" = a self-contained
  sub-project, a numbered design-document section like "§2", a GitHub issue
  number like "#1", a repository name, a commit hash, an acronym) must be
  **spelled out in plain English the first time it appears** and
  **hyperlinked to its exact source**.

## What triggered this ticket

While finishing the broken-main auto-repair work tracked in
[`virusdave/task-dag` issue #1, "CI-driven broken-master auto-repair"](https://github.com/virusdave/task-dag/issues/1)
(the project that builds automation to detect and fix a broken shared code
branch), an agent **published an operator-facing design document** that was
full of unexpanded shorthand: bare section references like "§2"/"§4" (meaning
numbered sections of a design file) and bare issue numbers, with no inline
explanation and no hyperlinks. It was unusable by a no-context reader.

Two fixes were already made in response, both in the
[`virusdave/top-level`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level) repository
(the "canon" repository that holds the fleet-wide rules all agents must
follow):

1. **The published document was rewritten** to be fully self-contained and
   hyperlinked, re-reviewed by our automated reviewer ("Oracle"), and
   re-published.
2. **The rule itself was generalized** in commit
   [`9234d78` — "Update canon: operator-facing UX bar applies to every channel and published artifact"](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/commit/9234d78cb4bfa786b65aa9bfa5d0cb7eac2dada6).
   The previous rule was written per-channel (it named chat replies,
   decision requests, and issue comments individually), so a **published
   document/one-off page** — a fourth surface none of those three named —
   slipped through. The new wording makes the rule channel-agnostic: *every*
   agent→operator surface, in any format including published artifacts, must
   meet the zero-context, expanded-reference, hyperlinked bar. The edited
   files were [`docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md)
   and [`docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md).

## Why a *separate* follow-up is still needed

Commit `9234d78` closes the specific gap (published artifacts weren't named
as a channel). But the operator has separately observed that **even for the
channels canon already named explicitly** (chat replies, issue comments),
agents *still occasionally* emit overly terse, unexpanded, un-hyperlinked
output. In other words, the problem is not only "a channel was missing from
the list" — it is also that the existing, already-mandated rule is
**sometimes ignored in practice**. Generalizing the rule does not, by
itself, prove the recurrence is fixed.

This ticket is to:

1. **Investigate** why agents still under-expand/under-link on operator-
   facing channels despite the canon mandate (e.g. the rule is buried, not
   enforced by any automated gate, easy to rationalize away under length
   pressure, or not surfaced at the moment of writing).
2. **Tighten** the canon wording and/or add **enforcement** so compliance is
   not optional — for example an automated pre-publish/pre-comment check that
   flags bare "§N", bare "#N", or bare short commit hashes that are not
   hyperlinked and expanded, or an explicit self-review checklist gate before
   any operator-facing artifact is sent.

## Acceptance criteria

- A short written root-cause analysis of *why* the recurrence persists
  despite canon.
- A concrete canon and/or tooling change that measurably reduces it (ideally
  an automated check, not just more prose), with the change linked here.
- Confirmation (with at least one before/after example) that the previously
  observed failure mode no longer passes review.

## Why this is pre-blocked (parked, not abandoned)

The operator asked for this to be created as a **pre-blocked follow-up**: it
should **not** be auto-dispatched to a worker yet. It is parked in the
task-tracking system (its task is marked *blocked*, so no worker will pick it
up) until the operator confirms the problem is still occurring **after**
commit `9234d78`. The operator has said they will **post a comment on this
issue** noting a fresh recurrence (ideally with a link to the offending
output) if they observe one. That comment is the signal to un-block and work
this ticket. Until then it intentionally sits idle so it neither disappears
nor consumes a worker.

---
<!-- Created as a pre-blocked follow-up per operator request on virusdave/task-dag#1. -->

# Low-inventory review page — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Thin index over the authoritative parent plan
> [`docs/epics/low-inventory-review/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> `virusdave/top-level`. Where this and the parent disagree, the parent
> wins — fix this doc. Tracking issue:
> [virusdave/top-level#32](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/32).
> **APPROVED — parent [§6](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#6-blocking-decisions-operator)
> resolved by the operator 2026-07-06, then write model SIMPLIFIED
> 2026-07-09 (parent
> [§6.11](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#611-2026-07-09-operator-simplification-no-quantity-writes-move-to-a-configurable-not-for-sale-room)).**
> Materialises via the issue #32 decomposition (the
> `Materialise-Child-Epic: FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` trailer group under
> `Parent-Issue: #32`).
>
> **⚠️ 2026-07-09 supersede (parent §6.11).** Helios **never adjusts Sweed
> stock quantities** for this feature. Both short-count and zero-count
> perform the **same reversible action**: move the affected package(s) to a
> **UI-configurable NOT FOR SALE room** (default = per-site "Hold for Dave
> inspection"). This **retires** the set-quantity write, the METRC ceiling,
> the counted-more readback, the write-mode A/B model, and the mandatory
> two-stage `Inventory Count Verification` room. The operator's other answers
> still apply (per-package barcode/METRC-scan granularity, first-to-zero
> location verification, a universal 24h one-offs link, a barcode-scan mobile
> review queue on the roadmap). Building still proceeds phased, safest-first;
> **no write to live Sweed inventory** (now only a reversible room transfer)
> ships outside operator-approved, feature-flagged, single-site-pilot
> rollout.

## Scope (Helios only)

A new per-site Helios operator page that lists SKUs with **`1 <= combined
FOR-SALE stock <= N`** (`N` admin-configurable, default 2; combined-0
excluded), grouped by warehousing location, lets an operator enter the
**actual physical count per package** (barcode/METRC scan), and on an
operator-confirmed short/zero count reacts with a `page-dave` (short `-p 2`,
zero `-p 3`) and **moves the affected package(s) to a UI-configurable NOT FOR
SALE room** (parent §6.11; default = per-site "Hold for Dave inspection") via
the existing `move-package-to-inspection` / `stockTransferService` transfer.
**Helios does not adjust Sweed stock quantities** — short and zero count use
the same reversible transfer, differing only in page priority. Complementary
to Sweed cycle counting and to Helios' existing velocity-based reordering
analytics — do **not** duplicate them.

## First task: confirm the in-repo facts

The parent §1 cites likely files from a read-only audit; verify each before
coding (the top-level repo cannot build Helios):

- `src/server/db/schema/sweedPackageSnapshots.sql` + the
  `sweed_package_current` view — columns `available_qty`, `stock_location`,
  `internal_track_code`, `dealer_id`, `product_sku`, `inventory_item_id`.
- `src/server/metrics/_real/sweedPackageSnapshotsQueries.ts` — the shared
  `FOR SALE%` / `available_qty` low-stock query helpers to **reuse**.
- `src/server/routes/catalogMaintenance.ts` +
  `src/server/catalog/maintenance.ts` — the existing
  `move-package-to-inspection` write path (`store.inventory.item.transfer`
  into `NOT FOR SALE - Hold for Dave inspection`) to reuse for the
  zero-count action.
- `src/server/catalog/stockTransferService.ts` — the transfer primitive,
  now the **sole write path** (parent §6.11): used for both the short-count
  and the zero-count move into the configurable NOT FOR SALE room.
- **No trade-sample set-quantity spike needed (parent §6.11).** The former
  "FIND FIRST: locate & generalize the 'reduce trade sample to zero' write"
  task is **dropped** — Helios no longer adjusts Sweed quantities, so there
  is no set-quantity write, no METRC-ceiling handling, and no counted-more
  readback to build.
- `src/worker/runtime/pageDave.ts` + `src/server/routes/warehouseLocations.ts`
  — `pageDave({ priority })`; the resolved page levels are literal ntfy `-p`:
  short `-p 2`, zero `-p 3`, counted-0-but-held `-p 4` (parent §6.2/§6.8).
- `src/shared/contracts/domain/pendingPurchases.ts` — site→dealer resolution.
- `src/server/app/buildServer.ts` + `src/client/app/router.tsx` — route
  registration; mirror the Catalog Maintenance / Inventory Procurement
  pages.
- `src/client/routes/catalog/LiveBarcodeScanner.tsx` and
  `WarehouseLocationsPage.tsx` — reuse the canonical camera scanner and its
  manual/hardware-scanner fallback pattern; do not create a second scanner.
- **Confirm (parent §6.5/§6.11):** the configured NOT FOR SALE destination
  room per site — default `Hold for Dave inspection` (fuzzy name match, IDs
  differ). Wire the destination as an **admin/UI-configurable setting**
  (parent §6.11), not a hardcoded name; the operator will later create a
  dedicated NOT FOR SALE location and repoint it. No new `Inventory Count
  Verification` room is needed unless the operator opts into the optional
  second-confirm stage.
- **Confirm (parent §6.8):** `current_qty` vs `available_qty` as the
  reconciliation baseline, and the behavior of `transferReservedItems: false`
  when a counted-zero package still has `hold_qty > 0`.
- **Design (parent §6.10/§6.11):** the **24h one-offs link** on every page,
  the **first-transition-to-zero** verification (last-known location code +
  METRC-tag suffix), and — only if the operator opts in — an optional
  non-admin second-confirm stage (parent §6.11; not required for safety since
  the move is reversible). The actual representative **mobile/tablet UI and
  notification templates must be Oracle-reviewed before every
  operator-facing phase first lands, including P0.**

## Operator workflow acceptance (binding)

The page optimizes for a mobile operator walking one physical location at a
time. Keep the current item and likely next action visible; collapse
methodology/provenance; never make the operator return to a dashboard to find
the result of the action they just took.

1. **Queue:** one explicit site, grouped in practical shelf/room walking order;
   current and next unresolved package remain visible. Handle populated,
   empty, loading, error, stale, long-name, multi-location, and multi-package
   states without horizontal scrolling or explanatory clutter.
2. **Scan:** reuse `LiveBarcodeScanner` plus Warehouse Locations' camera,
   manual-entry, still-photo, and hardware-scanner patterns. Scanning never
   writes. Exactly one package becomes active; duplicate, unreadable, unknown,
   ambiguous, wrong-site, camera-denied, and camera-unavailable scans recover
   inline without losing queue position.
3. **Count:** enter/tally physical count, then show a distinct equal, short,
   zero, over, or held result. A captured discrepancy remains visibly
   unresolved as **count recorded, package still for sale, transfer pending**;
   do not suppress it or call it reconciled.
4. **Review:** inventory changes require a separate package-specific
   confirmation showing site, product, METRC suffix, Sweed and physical
   counts, source room, configured destination, and that the **whole package**
   leaves the customer menu. No bulk transfer and no fallback-all-lots
   behavior. A stale live package stops, refreshes, and requires reconfirmation.
5. **Recover and continue:** prevent double-submit; distinguish in-flight,
   conflict, timeout/unknown outcome, partial success, success, undo success,
   and undo failure. An unknown outcome is verified before retry. Success
   stays inline with destination, audit status, undo, 24h detail link, and the
   next package action.
6. **Accessibility:** no horizontal scrolling at 320/375px phone or
   768/1024px tablet widths; 44px minimum primary targets; labeled numeric
   input; keyboard/hardware-scanner completion; focus-managed dialogs,
   visible focus, `aria-live` status, and no color-only meaning.
7. **Oracle evidence before first exposure:** actual phone and tablet renders
   for every queue state in item 1; scanner idle/active/denied/unknown/
   ambiguous/matched; equal/short/zero/over/held and count-pending;
   confirmation/in-flight/conflict/unknown-outcome/success/undo; unavailable
   destination; first-to-zero verification; admin room configuration; each
   batched `page-dave` template; and active/expired 24h detail views. Oracle
   must return APPROVE for the relevant set before that surface lands.

## Phases (parent §5 — production-safety order)

- **P0 — read-only review page.** Per-site `1 <= combined FOR-SALE <= N`
  table (admin-configurable `N`, default 2; combined-0 excluded), grouped by
  warehousing location, from `sweed_package_current` (reuse the shared
  queries). No inputs/writes/pages. `viewer`/metrics-grant read. Safe to
  deploy under normal Helios deploy.
- **P1a — physical-count entry + audit record (no write, no page).**
  Per-package physical-count input (barcode/METRC scan, parent §6.3); write
  the reconciliation record (P3 table). Captured discrepancies remain pending
  and visible until resolved. `editor` grant.
- **P1b — configure and validate the NOT FOR SALE target (no inventory
  write).** Admin/UI setting per site (default = "Hold for Dave inspection").
  Resolve and display the exact site/room before transfer enablement; fail
  closed when unavailable. Optional second confirm only if the operator opts
  in.
- **P1c — short-count page + move-to-NOT-FOR-SALE (write-gated).** On
  operator-confirmed `0 < count < Sweed`: `page-dave -p 2` (parent §6.2) +
  **move the affected package(s) to the configurable NOT FOR SALE room**
  (parent §6.11, default = per-site "Hold for Dave inspection") via
  `move-package-to-inspection` / `stockTransferService`, capturing
  from-room/qty undo data in the audit row. **No Sweed quantity write** (the
  set-quantity path, METRC ceiling, write-mode A/B, and counted-more readback
  are all retired — parent §6.11). `editor` grant; write path
  operator-rollout-gated. Shares its primitive with P2.
- **P2 — zero-count action + first-to-zero verification.** On
  operator-confirmed `count == 0`: `page-dave -p 3` (§6.2) + move to the
  **same configurable NOT FOR SALE room** via `move-package-to-inspection`
  (parent §6.11, site-equivalent room, parent §6.5); the counted-0-but-held
  edge pages `-p 4` + 24h one-offs (parent §6.8); add the
  first-transition-to-zero verification (last-known location code + METRC
  suffix, parent §6.6). `editor` grant; operator-rollout-gated. Shares the
  P1c transfer primitive.
- **P3 — reconciliation audit + no-renag.** Helios table (site, SKU/package,
  Sweed-qty snapshot, operator count, action, actor, ts); suppress
  resolved lines for a configurable window; never suppress captured-but-
  unresolved discrepancies; per-SKU history. Its schema lands with P1a.
- **P4 — mobile review queue (roadmap, parent §6.10).** Non-admin
  barcode-scan re-confirmation queue on the P1a/P3 foundation.
- **Cross-cutting:** every page carries a **24h one-offs link** to an
  info-dense mobile/tablet-first operator view; that UI **must pass an Oracle
  review before first exposure, including P0** (parent §5.1/§6.10).

## Verification

- Build/lint/typecheck green.
- P0: unit test the `combined FOR-SALE <= N` query against seeded snapshot
  rows; grouping renders for both a parseable shelf code and a stock-room
  fallback.
- UI: focused interaction/accessibility tests cover the full binding workflow,
  including scan recovery, no-side-effect count capture, package-specific
  confirmation, stale and unknown-outcome handling, undo, and next-item
  continuation. Capture and Oracle-review the representative evidence set
  before first exposure.
- P1/P2: discrepancy-classification unit tests mapping short/zero count to
  the **shared move-to-NOT-FOR-SALE transfer** (parent §6.11) at the correct
  page priority; the transfer reuses the existing verify-live-item +
  restore-on-failure guarantees; the configurable destination room resolves
  per site (falls back to `Hold for Dave inspection`); `pageDave` asserted
  with the agreed priority (mocked — **never** a real page in tests, canon
  no-prod-resources-in-tests). No test performs a Sweed quantity write (that
  path is retired — parent §6.11).
- P3: audit row on every action; suppression within the window.
- Each landing commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#32`.
- P1/P2 prod rollout is operator-gated: `self-deploy-helios` under explicit
  approval, then a live probe on one known low-stock SKU per site.

## Coordination

Single repo — no cross-repo contract. The parent §6 decisions are
**resolved** (operator, 2026-07-06) and the write model was **simplified**
2026-07-09 (parent §6.11 — no quantity writes, move to a configurable NOT FOR
SALE room), so all phases are unblocked to build. The remaining gates are
operational, not decisional: (i) the mobile/tablet UI must pass an **Oracle
review** before each operator-facing surface first lands, including P0
(parent §5.1/§6.10);
(ii) every live-Sweed room-transfer phase (P1c/P2) ships only under
**operator rollout approval**, feature-flagged, single-site pilot first
(Midtown). One small confirm remains for build time: whether the operator
wants the optional non-admin second-confirm stage (parent §6.11) — it is not
required for safety.

issues.body:
## Prospective LLM-driven pending-purchase classifier + pricing-safety lifecycle

Replace Helios's **reactive** pending-purchase classifier (rule parser + row-local LLM fallback that breaks on every new distributor/SKU and sometimes maps confidently wrong) with a **prospective**, event-level classifier: Helios calls our private Bedrock gateway directly with the full order + live catalog + optional hint documents (wholesale menus, sibling POs), behind a **deterministic validator** that decides whether any model mapping is safe. The human review + apply gate stays; Amp stays as a human-triggered import/escalation path, not an autonomous per-event runtime. Separately, a **quarantine → reprice → release lifecycle** closes the first-sale mispricing race for brand-new SKUs.

Origin: the Stop 31 LLC / Bronx Sweed purchase 151113 incident, where the reactive worker packet (#52) was unusable and an Amp agent hand-built the corrected packet (#53). That manual path is Stage 0 of this epic (already operational).

### Authoritative docs (in `virusdave/top-level`)
- Design: [`docs/designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md)
- Epic plan (stages + the 8 operator decisions + FT-1..FT-4 follow-ups): [`docs/epics/prospective-pending-purchase/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/prospective-pending-purchase/EPIC_PLAN.md)

### Operator decisions captured (2026-06-20)
1. **Model** — config-driven default = current "standard, most capable general reasoning model," chosen dynamically; below-the-fold Bedrock config page for rare overrides.
2. **Hints** — v1 pasted text, LLM-parsed for *how* it helps; file uploads = follow-up FT-1.
3. **Auto-trigger** — v1 manual; auto = FT-2, gated on the LitAlerts redesign (FT-3).
4. **Rollout** — go direct: delete the legacy classifier; no dual-mode / fallback.
5. **Quarantine** — optional, not enforced; after receive, offer bulk move-to-quarantine + full lifecycle, or reprice-in-place.
6. **Release target** — dropdown, default "FOR SALE - Sales Floor".
7. **Freshness** — weekly cadence; LitAlerts data >2 weeks excluded from calcs/display but never blocking (its own future epic, FT-3 — out of scope here).
8. **Pricing** — SKU-level repricing; badge when a reprice affects already-on-floor stock (broader pricing redesign = FT-4).

### Delegation
All implementation lands in **`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`** (the Helios app). This top-level issue is the coordinating epic; a child epic is materialised in `automation` and carries the staged work (classifier Stages 0–8 + pricing-safety lifecycle L1–L3). Implementation commits there must carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#<this>`.

### Out of scope
- FT-3 (LitAlerts competitor-data redesign) — its own future top-level epic.
- FT-4 (broader pricing process redesign) — its own future epic.

### Gates
Each implementation stage honors the canon gates recorded in the epic plan: Oracle critical-infra/DB review + explicit operator approval before any prod DB migration or live-inventory write; green tree; Oracle UI review for operator-facing surfaces.


```yaml
delegated_to:
  - repo: FreshlyBakedNYC/automation
    issue: 54
    note: Implement classifier stages C0-C8 and lifecycle stages L1-L3 per docs/designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md. Each stage honors its canon Oracle critical-infra/DB + UI reviews and explicit operator approval before any prod DB migration or live-inventory write. Carry Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#33 on implementation commits.
```
