declarations.body:
# Prospective Pending-Purchase Classifier — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#33](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/33).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md`](../../../../designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md)
> and the staged plan + the 8 operator decisions live in
> [`docs/epics/prospective-pending-purchase/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md),
> both in the top-level repo. This child epic exists because **all
> implementation lands in `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (the Helios app
> under `helios/`)**: the worker classifier, server routes, DB schema,
> review UI, and the inventory lifecycle are all Helios surfaces.
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `automation` master and
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#33
> ```

## Scope owned by this repo (Helios)

Two parallel tracks. The **classifier track** replaces the reactive
pending-purchase generator with a prospective Bedrock-driven one behind a
deterministic validator. The **pricing-safety lifecycle track** closes the
first-sale mispricing race for brand-new SKUs. They are independent and
meet only where catalog-apply creates the live product the lifecycle then
prices.

### Classifier track

- **C0 — Amp → `import_json` bridge runbook** (already operational; no
  code). Purchase 151113 packet #53 was built this way. Documents the
  manual escalation path that stays as the human-triggered escape hatch.
- **C1 — Refactor the generator into seams.** Carve
  `collectPendingPurchaseContext`, `buildPendingPurchasePacket`,
  `persistGeneratedPendingPurchasePacket` out of
  `worker/jobs/generatePendingPurchasePacketJob.ts`; no behavior change
  yet. Isolate the legacy rule-based row-builder behind ONE seam **so it
  can be deleted at cutover (C8)** — it is not a preserved path
  (decision 4: go direct).
- **C2 — Hint bundle storage + admin API.** New
  `pending_purchase_hint_bundles` / `pending_purchase_hint_documents`
  tables; admin endpoints; `hintBundleId` on the generate job + route.
  v1 = pasted arbitrary hint text only (decision 2).
- **C3 — Hint fact extraction + intent classification.**
  `extractPendingPurchaseHintFacts` (Bedrock JSON for menus; deterministic
  for Sweed PO JSON). First LLM-classify the hint for *how* it helps
  (canonical SKU list / ordered-items expectation / free-text description /
  line-item list — decision 2), then extract inert cited facts.
- **C4 — Prospective LLM classifier.**
  `classifyPendingPurchasePacketWithLlm`; event-level prompt over the full
  order + live catalog + hint facts; `PendingPurchaseLlmDraftRow` output
  contract (model proposes a reuse link, never authorizes it). Default
  model = the current "standard, most capable general reasoning model,"
  chosen dynamically + a below-the-fold Bedrock config page for rare
  per-context overrides (decision 1).
- **C5 — Deterministic validator / reconciler (the safety layer).**
  Validate every reuse candidate vs the live product; taxonomy/size/pack/
  house-brand guards; duplicate detection; Helios (not the model) computes
  deterministic fields + price + inline market evidence.
- **C6 — Review-UI surfacing.** Show confidence, rationale, hint
  citations, reuse candidates, and new-brand/new-group/no-comps warnings
  (all from the passthrough `raw_row_json`).
- **C7 — Apply-time drift guard + optional post-apply refresh.**
  Generated-reuse drift guard in the apply job; optional enqueue of created
  product ids after apply.
- **C8 — Direct cutover + legacy deletion.** Switch
  `catalog.pending_purchases.generate` to the LLM-prospective path and
  **delete the legacy rule-based classifier** (decision 4). A short
  dev-only shadow comparison during validation is fine, but it ships as the
  single path — no permanent `generationMode` toggle, no legacy fallback.

### Pricing-safety lifecycle track (independent; can ship first)

- **L1 — Lifecycle record + gates (no reverse move).**
  `purchase_inventory_lifecycle_runs` / `_items` tables keyed by
  `(dealer_id, po_id)`; start / verify-quarantine / purchase-market-refresh
  / purchase-reprice routes; market-completion (timestamp-based) +
  price-applied (live-price-equality) verifiers; reuse the existing pricing
  review UI. No release route yet.
- **L2 — Bulk quarantine repair + gated release.** Extract a shared
  stock-transfer service from the one-way move-to-inspection; purchase-
  scoped bulk move-to-inspection (repair); reverse + bulk **release** to a
  chosen FOR SALE room (dropdown, default "FOR SALE - Sales Floor" —
  decision 6) with immediate-before-transfer preflight (live price + live
  quarantine re-verify), post-transfer verification, and partial-failure
  recovery. Quarantine is **optional, not enforced** (decision 5): the UI
  offers bulk move-to-quarantine + full lifecycle OR reprice-in-place
  skipping the release/move-back. Repricing is SKU-level with a small badge
  when a SKU already has on-floor stock (decision 8).
- **L3 — Automation + monitoring.** `inventory.lifecycle.advance` job to
  poll/advance async gates; quarantine-breach monitor; alerts (lot in FOR
  SALE before priced, market timeout, price-apply failure, release partial
  failure).

## Dependency order (for task breakdown)

```
C0 (done) ─▶ C1 ─▶ C4 ─▶ C5 ─▶ (C6, C7) ─▶ C8
              C2 ─▶ C3 ─────────▲
L1 ─▶ L2 ─▶ L3        (lifecycle track, parallel to the classifier track)
```

- C1 unblocks C4; C2 unblocks C3; C3 feeds C4; C5 depends on C4; C6 & C7
  depend on C5; C8 depends on C5+C6+C7.
- L-track is fully parallel and independent of the classifier track.

## Out of scope (explicit)

- **FT-1** hint file uploads (CSV/PDF/manifests/POs/catalogs/scrapings) —
  near-term follow-up, separate task.
- **FT-2** auto-generated proposal packets — gated on FT-3.
- **FT-3** LitAlerts competitor-data redesign — its own future top-level
  epic (decision 7); not created here.
- **FT-4** broader pricing process/engine redesign — its own future epic.
- Any change to the human review + apply approval gate (kept as-is).

## Required gates (per canon)

- **Oracle critical-infra / DB review** for the validator (C5), the apply
  drift guard (C7), the hint tables + generate-job changes (C2), and the
  lifecycle tables + release safety (L1/L2). DB migrations apply on prod
  only after Oracle blessing **and** explicit operator approval, then
  live-sentinel verification.
- **Green tree** — repo-documented light/targeted lint/typecheck/test for
  touched Helios areas in the dev loop; full presubmit before merge. No
  first-party `any`; no bug-masking fallbacks.
- **Oracle UI review** for C6 review-UI changes, the L1 lifecycle panel,
  and any operator-facing copy.

## Completion signal

This child epic is complete when both tracks have landed on `automation`
master with `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#33` trailers: the legacy
classifier is deleted and `catalog.pending_purchases.generate` runs the
validated prospective path (C8), and the quarantine→reprice→release
lifecycle is operator-usable end-to-end with its hard release gates (L3).
declarations.delegationNote: Implement classifier stages C0-C8 (prospective Bedrock classifier behind a deterministic validator; delete the legacy reactive path) and lifecycle stages L1-L3 (quarantine→reprice→release with hard release gates) per docs/designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md. Each stage honors its canon Oracle critical-infra/DB + UI reviews and explicit operator approval before any prod DB migration or live-inventory write. Carry Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#33 on implementation commits.

# Amp cost reduction — `github-worker` child epic **P4**: agent-waste store + advisory selection/injection

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality."
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> — **Lever D = §5** (and the §8 context-budget meta-problem), phased plan =
> §10 (Phase 4).
> **Reviewed advisory catalog (already landed in top-level):**
> [`docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml)
> and [`docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 now has **several**
> `github-worker` child epics, the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO
> carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so
> the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal (Lever D, design §5)

Close the ≤1-minute feedback loop the operator asked for: as agents (and the
Phase-3 guardrail wrappers) discover wasted effort, record it **structurally**,
and let the dispatcher inject a **tiny, reviewed, budgeted** set of advisories
into the next agent's capsule — *without* ever injecting free-form
agent-authored text.

> **Hard correction from Oracle (mandatory, design §5):** do **NOT** build a
> channel that injects arbitrary agent-authored "lessons learned" into future
> agents. That is simultaneously a context-bloat accumulator, a hallucination
> amplifier, a stale-junk drawer, and a prompt-injection surface. Split the
> system into **observations → reviewed advisories → guardrails**.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Observation store** | A small `agent-waste record …` CLI + the Phase-3 wrappers append **structured** events (design §5.1 schema) to a local store (SQLite WAL or flocked NDJSON under `~/.local/state/github-worker/`). Free-form notes may be stored for **human review** but are **never** injected. This must use the same store path/schema the Phase-3 `bin/rg` wrapper writes to (the P3↔P4 contract). |
| **Advisory selection** | The dispatcher reads the reviewed catalog [`advisories.yaml`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml), selects the **top-ranked** advisories whose `trigger_ids` have fired recently (design §5.3 ranking), and injects **only their allowlisted `text`**, under a hard budget (design §8: ≤300–500 tokens total, ≤3–5 advisories). |
| **Injection point** | Injected into the **dynamic** part of the prompt (after the stable prefix/capsule from Phase 2 — leave the advisory slot Phase 2 reserves), so the cacheable prefix stays byte-stable. |
| **Review backlog, not prompt text** | Unknown/free-form observations create a **review backlog** surface for the operator; they never become future prompt text. |
| **Ranking + caps** | Implement the §5.3 score (severity × recurrence × est-cost-saved × scope-match ÷ token-cost × decay(age)); TTL 7–14 days (except `permanent-safety`); an advisory still high-recurrence at TTL **must be promoted** to a guardrail/canon rule, never extended as prose forever. |

## 3. Constraints

- **Never inject agent-authored free text.** Only allowlisted `text` from the
  reviewed catalog, selected by structured event IDs, under hard caps + TTL +
  the Phase-2 `agent-prompt-budget` CI ceiling.
- Observations are structured and **never auto-injected**; the influence is
  carried by the dispatcher (re-ranking), not by agents reading each other's
  notes — no agent waits on another.
- Single prod host today makes a local store safe; mirror summaries to a git
  ref only if the fleet later goes multi-host (design §12 Q1 — confirm the
  store location with the operator).

## 4. Acceptance (design §10 Phase 4)

- An observation recorded now is reflected (re-ranked) in the **next**
  dispatched agent's capsule within ~1 min, **under budget**.
- **No free-form text is ever injected**; unknown observations land in the
  review backlog only.
- The injected advisory set respects the §8 budget (enforced by the Phase-2
  `agent-prompt-budget` check) and the §5.3 caps/TTL.
- Each implementation attaches an Agent Gate Record (canon §3), and the final
  satisfying commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34` **and** this
  issue's `Issue:`/`URL:` trailer.

## 5. Production safety / rollback

- The store + record CLI are additive and best-effort; a failed write must
  never affect an agent's run.
- Advisory injection is gated by the budget check and the allowlist; roll back
  by disabling injection (dispatcher flag) — the catalog and store are inert
  without it.
- No serving service is touched; landing on `github-worker@master` is the
  publication step (the dispatcher reads repo state per run).
declarations.delegationNote: Lever D / design §5 + §10 Phase 4; consumes the advisories.yaml catalog + agent-prompt-budget CI already landed in top-level.
declarations.title: Amp cost reduction P4: agent-waste store + advisory selection/injection

# Agent-waste review queue — `top-level` child epic: backlog file format + agenix read/write deploy keys (D2/D3)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality" (Lever D,
> the structured agent-waste → reviewed-advisory loop).
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` → `docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md)
> ("Remaining work" #1; decisions **D1/D2/D3** and the **§Security** write-key
> choice are all RESOLVED by the operator) and
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](../../../../designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> §5 (Lever D) / §5.1 (raw-observation store, stays local — **not** this file).
> **Advisory catalog contract (already landed in top-level):**
> [`docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`](../../../../agent-runtime/advisories.yaml),
> [`docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md`](../../../../agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`virusdave/top-level`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level) `master` that
> satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`.
> Because #34 has **several** child epics, the **final** satisfying commit MUST
> ALSO carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer
> so the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal

Establish, in `virusdave/top-level`, the two load-bearing pieces the rest of the
agent-waste review queue depends on:

1. A committed **`agent-waste-backlog` file format**, co-located with
   [`docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`](../../../../agent-runtime/advisories.yaml),
   that github-worker's exporter writes and Helios reads.
2. The **agenix deploy keys** the `helios` service user needs: a **read-only**
   key for the D2 mirror and a scoped **write** key for the D3 promote path.

This is per operator decision **D1** (storage is a git file in `top-level`,
because "workers will already have that checked out in their
ephemeral-workspace"), **D2** (Helios reads it read-only via a git mirror), and
**D3** (promote is an in-Helios admin button that pushes to `top-level`). All of
these are **closed operator decisions** — this child epic is routine
implementation + agenix provisioning, no further operator input required.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Backlog file format** | Define + commit the on-disk format for the **pending-review** backlog (the tiny/rare unknown/free-form-`id` items a human must triage — **not** the chatty raw NDJSON observation store, which stays local to the dispatcher per design §5.1). Co-locate with `advisories.yaml` under `docs/agent-runtime/` (e.g. `docs/agent-runtime/agent-waste-backlog.ndjson` or `.yaml`). Ship it **empty and fail-safe**, exactly like `advisories.yaml` shipped empty. |
| **Contract alignment** | The format MUST round-trip through the already-merged Helios contract: [`helios/src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts) (Zod) and the producer's [`Nicponskis/github-worker` → `docs/AGENT_WASTE.md`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/docs/AGENT_WASTE.md) (`agent-waste backlog --format json`). The **`note` field is display-only and MUST NEVER be injected into agents** — carry that invariant into the schema doc. |
| **Read-only deploy key (D2)** | Provision a **new read-only agenix deploy key** for the `helios` user to mirror `top-level` (Helios today only mirrors `automation`). Same shape as the existing automation read key that [`helios/src/server/taskDagMirror.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/taskDagMirror.ts) reads from `/run/agenix/helios-github-automation-deploy-key`. |
| **Write deploy key (D3)** | Provision a scoped **write** agenix deploy key for the `helios` user for the promote path (option **(c)** direct, admin-gated, server-validated push to `top-level master`). Same shape as the existing `helios-parser-configs` write key. The residual repo-wide-deploy-key risk is **explicitly accepted** by the operator (RESOLVED_DESIGN §Security, comment [#4889206463](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/57#issuecomment-4889206463)) — do not re-litigate; do not silently substitute option (a)/(b). |
| **Docs** | A short `docs/agent-runtime/AGENT_WASTE_BACKLOG.md` describing the file format, the producer/consumer contract, and the two keys' purpose/scope, cross-linking `RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants (carry forward)

- **`note` never becomes advisory `text`.** The backlog file is display + human
  triage only; nothing in it is ever auto-injected into an agent. Only reviewed
  `advisories.yaml` entries are injectable (that is the allowlist invariant).
- **Two distinct streams — do not conflate.** The raw observation store is a
  local flocked NDJSON under the dispatcher's state dir and **Helios never reads
  it** (design §5.1). This file is only the small pending-review backlog.
- **Fail-safe empty default**, like `advisories.yaml`: an empty/missing backlog
  must degrade gracefully on both the producer and consumer sides.
- **Keys are for the `helios` service user**, provisioned via agenix, mirroring
  the existing automation read key and `helios-parser-configs` write key. This
  is routine infra, **not** the machine/`amp-local` credentials.

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Blocks** child epics #2 (github-worker exporter — needs the file format),
  #3 (Helios reader — needs the format + D2 read key), and #4 (Helios promote —
  needs the D3 write key). This is the root of the workstream; land it first.

## 5. Acceptance

- The pending-review backlog file format exists in `top-level` (empty,
  fail-safe), documented, and validates against the Helios Zod contract and the
  github-worker producer output.
- A read-only agenix deploy key for `helios` to mirror `top-level` is
  provisioned; a scoped write key for the promote path is provisioned; both are
  documented with their scope and the accepted residual risk.
- No serving service is touched by this child epic beyond agenix secret material
  (rollout of consumers is #2/#3/#4). Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

Additive: a new (empty) committed file + two new agenix secrets. Rollback is
removing the file and revoking/rotating the keys. No prod DB, no schema, no
serving-process change. Any nixos-sbc/host permission or tmpfiles change that
provisioning implies follows canon (push → `self-deploy*` under lock).
declarations.delegationNote: RESOLVED_DESIGN Remaining-work #1; root of the workstream — backlog file format + D2 read / D3 write agenix keys. Blocks the other three.
declarations.title: Agent-waste review queue — top-level: backlog file format + agenix read/write deploy keys (D2/D3)

# Agent-waste review queue — Helios child epic: promote-to-advisory admin button (server-side, admin-gated, contract-validated commit+push)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality" (Lever D).
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md)
> ("Remaining work" #4; decision **D3** and the **§Security** write-key choice
> are RESOLVED — operator adopted option **(c)** direct, admin-gated,
> server-validated push, comment [#4889206463](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/57#issuecomment-4889206463)).
> **Advisory catalog contract:**
> [`virusdave/top-level` → `docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md),
> [`docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 has **several** child epics,
> the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO carry this issue's own
> `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level completion
> aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal

Implement the operator's **promote-to-advisory admin button** (D3): a
server-side, admin-gated, contract-validated git **commit+push** that adds a new
reviewed entry to `top-level` `advisories.yaml` — the human-review gate that lets
a curated observation become an allowlisted advisory the dispatcher may inject
(~1-min latency). This **overrides** the earlier "v1 = display + link-to-promote,
no Helios button" plan; the operator explicitly asked for an in-Helios admin
action ("I do not want to modify files in git manually").

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Admin-gated route** | `POST` promote endpoint, **admin-only** (same admin gate as `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog`), with an audit log entry per promotion. |
| **applyConfig-pattern write** | Reuse the parser-config apply pattern in [`helios/src/server/parsekit/applyConfig.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/parsekit/applyConfig.ts): **validate → write → `git add` → reject no-op → commit → push → reset local commit on push failure**, with a subprocess **timeout**. Push to `top-level master` using the D3 write deploy key from child epic #1. |
| **Server-side contract validation** | Before committing, validate the resulting `advisories.yaml` against the **advisory-catalog contract** ([`ADVISORY_CATALOG.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md)): schema, **budget caps**, `id` rules. Reject invalid promotions before any write. |
| **Field mapping (audited)** | Record exactly which backlog-item fields map to an advisory entry's `id` / `text` / `severity`. **`note` is display-only and MUST NOT map to `text`** — it can never leak into the injected allowlist. |
| **Concurrency** | Promote-commits touch files adjacent to the exporter's backlog writes in the same repo. Inherit applyConfig's no-op rejection + reset-on-push-failure so a rejected push never piles up local commits; refetch/rebase and retry. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants (carry forward)

- **`note` never becomes advisory `text`.** This is the load-bearing safety
  invariant of the whole workstream — the allowlist is the boundary between
  human-reviewed text and agent-authored text.
- **Validate before commit**, server-side, against the catalog contract (schema
  + budget caps + `id` rules); reject no-op; reset-on-push-failure; subprocess
  timeout — the full applyConfig discipline.
- **Admin-gated + audited.** The human review action *is* the safety gate for a
  mutating, behaviour-changing operation (it changes what future agents may be
  injected with). Every promotion is admin-authenticated and logged.
- **§Security residual risk accepted (option (c)).** The `top-level` **write**
  deploy key is repo-wide (GitHub deploy keys are not path-scoped) and
  `top-level` has no branch protection on the current plan. The operator
  **explicitly accepted** this residual risk (comment [#4889206463](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/57#issuecomment-4889206463));
  options (a) dedicated repo and (b) PR/branch were declined. Do **not** silently
  substitute (a)/(b); the mitigation is admin-gating + server-side validation +
  audit, not key-scope reduction.

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Depends on** child epic #1 (the **D3 write deploy key** + the catalog it
  edits). Best sequenced after #3 (reader) so the admin UI can show the backlog
  item being promoted, but the write path itself only strictly needs #1.

## 5. Acceptance

- An admin can promote a reviewed backlog item to a new `advisories.yaml` entry
  via the Helios button; the change is contract-validated server-side, committed,
  and pushed to `top-level master`; invalid promotions are rejected before any
  write; every promotion is audited.
- `note` provably cannot reach advisory `text`.
- Deterministic, prod-resource-free tests of validation + the commit path
  (against a temp repo, **never** prod `top-level`), plus the live path confirmed
  on prod **after** deploy via `self-deploy*` under lock. Attach an Agent Gate
  Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

The riskiest child epic (holds a `top-level` write credential). Rollback is
disabling the route + revoking/rotating the D3 write key; a bad advisory can be
reverted in `top-level` git and the injector ships fail-safe (empty catalog =
inert). Never point tests at prod `top-level`; use an ephemeral temp repo. Deploy
follows canon (push → `self-deploy*` under lock; never manually restart Helios).
No prod DB, no schema.
declarations.delegationNote: RESOLVED_DESIGN Remaining-work #4; depends on child epic 1 (D3 write key + catalog). Operator adopted Security option (c).
declarations.title: Agent-waste review queue — Helios: promote-to-advisory admin button (server-side, admin-gated, contract-validated commit+push)

# Amp cost reduction — `github-worker` child epic **P2**: shrink the base worker prompt + generate the runtime capsule

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality."
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> — **Lever B = §3**, phased plan = §10 (Phase 2), division of work = §10.
> **Capsule contract (already landed in top-level):**
> [`docs/agent-runtime/RUNTIME_CAPSULE.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/RUNTIME_CAPSULE.md),
> the static safety block
> [`docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md),
> and the prepared-workspace contract
> [`docs/agent-runtime/PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 now has **several**
> `github-worker` child epics, the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO
> carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so
> the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic and
> not a sibling. (github-worker's own task-dag adds those trailers when you
> `complete` a task on this issue; keep them.)

## 1. Goal (Lever B, design §3)

Every dispatched agent is fed a **~200-line static base prompt**
([`prompts/base-worker-prompt.txt`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/prompts/base-worker-prompt.txt))
that is re-billed on every turn, plus an `AGENTS.md`-driven bootstrap. Phase 1
already made the dispatcher **prepare** the whole workspace (all repos cloned,
canon on local disk, `task-dag` checked out) and emit a `manifest.json`. This
phase collapses the recurring startup surface to a small, cache-friendly,
byte-stable prefix followed by a generated **runtime capsule**, and moves deep
detail behind the already-prepared commands + on-demand deep-doc reads.

Target prompt order fed to `amp` (design §3):

```text
[stable base worker prompt — small, byte-stable]
[stable canon/runtime capsule — generated, <= budget]
--- cache boundary ---
[bounded live advisories — dynamic but tiny]   (Phase 4; leave a slot)
[per-task issue/task info — worker id, paths, SHAs, URLs]
```

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Shrink the base prompt** | Replace the ~200-line `prompts/base-worker-prompt.txt` with a **small, byte-stable** base prompt (target budget in design §8: ≤700–1,000 tokens). No dynamic content in it — it must be identical across tasks so it stays cacheable. |
| **Generate the runtime capsule** | From the prepared workspace's `manifest.json`, render the capsule per [`RUNTIME_CAPSULE.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/RUNTIME_CAPSULE.md): the "do not bootstrap" notice, work-repo path, all cloned peer-repo paths, top-level path + canon SHA, the `task-dag` script path (`<workspace>/task-dag/scripts/task-dag`), the claimed task SHA/kind/ref, the **hard safety non-negotiables** (embed [`capsule/static-block.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md) verbatim), and the scenario→deep-doc **routing table** (pointers, not the docs). Budget: ≤400–700 tokens. |
| **Order dynamic content last** | Emit worker id, paths, URLs, timestamps, per-task info, and the (future) live-advisory slot **after** the stable prefix so the prefix stays byte-stable. |
| **`agent-prompt-budget` CI check** | Add a CI check that fails if the base prompt or the rendered capsule exceeds the design §8 budgets, so the shrink can't silently regrow. (The top-level advisory-budget sibling work landed [`docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml); this check governs the github-worker-side prompt/capsule surface.) |

## 3. Constraints (do not weaken safety)

- The capsule MUST still carry the hard non-negotiables (the
  [static safety block](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md))
  and the deep-doc routing table — shrinking is a *relocation* of detail behind
  prepared commands + on-demand reads, never a removal of safety rules. See
  design §3 and the canon prepared-workspace exception.
- The static block is mirrored from canon; if you change what it mirrors, the
  canon source is authoritative — coordinate per
  [`docs/canon/UPDATING_CANON.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/UPDATING_CANON.md).
- The capsule must validate against, and stay in lockstep with, the manifest
  schema in
  [`PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md).

## 4. Acceptance (design §10 Phase 2)

- The rendered capsule is **under budget**; the `agent-prompt-budget` CI check
  is present and **enforces** both the base-prompt and capsule budgets.
- A dispatched agent receives: small byte-stable base prompt → generated
  capsule → (advisory slot) → per-task dynamic block, in that order.
- The safety non-negotiables and deep-doc routing are still present in the
  capsule (verify against `capsule/static-block.md`).
- No agent-run canon bootstrap is reintroduced (Phase 1 already removed it).
- Each implementation attaches an Agent Gate Record (canon §3), and the final
  satisfying commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34` **and** this
  issue's `Issue:`/`URL:` trailer (see the completion-signalling note above).

## 5. Production safety / rollback

- The capsule generator and the shrunk prompt are consumed only by the
  dispatcher/worker-loop when it composes the agent prompt; roll back by
  reverting the worker-loop wiring to the old base prompt. Keep the old
  `base-worker-prompt.txt` in history so revert is a one-commit operation.
- Land the CI budget check in the same change (or immediately after) so the
  shrink cannot silently regrow.
- No serving service is touched; there is no deploy step beyond landing on
  `github-worker@master` (the dispatcher reads the repo state per run).
declarations.delegationNote: Lever B / design §3 + §10; consumes the runtime-capsule contract already landed in top-level.
declarations.title: Amp cost reduction P2: shrink base worker prompt + generate runtime capsule

# Amp cost reduction — `github-worker` child epic **P3**: `bin/rg` guardrail wrapper + hit logging

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality."
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> — **Lever C = §4**, phased plan = §10 (Phase 3).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 now has **several**
> `github-worker` child epics, the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO
> carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so
> the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal (Lever C, design §4)

Tool away the single most-recurring agent footgun: passing a value to
ripgrep's short `-r` thinking it means "recursive" (rg recurses by default;
`-r` is `--replace`), which silently rewrites output and corrupts the agent's
own next input. Replace *any prose warning about it* with a deterministic
wrapper that **rejects only the provably-footgun form**, prints the fix, and
records a structured telemetry event. The wrapper lives in the prepared
workspace's `bin/` (first on `PATH`) and logs every hit (Lever D / Phase 4).

## 2. Detection rules (the subtle part)

`-r` consumes the remainder of a bundled short cluster (or the next argv) as
its replacement value, so `-rn` means `--replace=n`, not `-r -n`. The wrapper
MUST:

- **Stop at `--`**: anything after a bare `--` is a pattern/path and MUST never
  trigger rejection (e.g. `rg -- -rfoo` is legitimate).
- **Parse short clusters left-to-right** against the set of value-taking rg
  short flags (`-A -B -C -E -M -d -e -f -g -j -m -r -t -T`): boolean shorts
  consume one char and continue; the **first value-taking short** consumes the
  rest of the cluster (or the next argv) as its value and ends parsing of that
  token.
- **Reject iff `r` is reached in *flag* position**: `-r`, `-r foo`, `-rn` (the
  canonical `--replace=n` corruption), `-nr`, `-inr`.
- **Never reject `r` in *value* position**: `-er` (pattern `r`), `-gr` (glob
  `r`), `-tr`, etc. are legitimate.
- **Pass `--replace` / `--replace=…` through untouched** — that IS the escape
  hatch; no env-var backdoor is added.
- **Fail OPEN on any parse uncertainty**: if a token doesn't match a known
  shape, `exec` the real `rg` unmodified. The guardrail fires only on the
  provably-footgun form; it must never block legitimate expert use.

## 3. Rejection behaviour

- Print a short stderr message with the fix, e.g.: *"`rg -r` rejected: ripgrep
  recurses by default; `-r` is `--replace`. Use `-n`/`-l` to search, or
  explicit `--replace` if you really mean to rewrite."*
- Exit non-zero. **Reject — never silently rewrite argv** (silent rewriting
  recreates the corrupted-output problem in reverse).

## 4. PATH blast radius (wraps `rg` for EVERY agent command)

- Resolve the **real** `rg` by removing the wrapper's own directory from `PATH`
  (or bake the absolute real-rg path in at workspace-prep time). MUST be
  recursion-proof (the wrapper must never invoke itself).
- `exec` the real binary; byte-exact stdout/stderr passthrough and **exact
  exit-code passthrough** (agents rely on rg's `exit 1` = no match, `2` =
  error).
- Pure bash, no per-arg subshells — `rg` is a hot path.
- If the real `rg` cannot be resolved, **fail loud** (do not silently swallow)
  — a missing rg is a workspace-prep bug, not a footgun.

## 5. Workspace / manifest / contract wiring

The prepared workspace currently creates **no** `bin/` dir and adds **nothing**
to `PATH`. This phase adds:

- Create `<bundle>/bin/`, install the `rg` wrapper there, and prepend
  `<bundle>/bin` to the **amp process's** `PATH` (worker-loop export).
- Record `bin_path` and the active guardrail list in `manifest.json`. **This is
  a manifest schema change** → bump `schema_version` and update
  [`PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md)
  (schema doc + validation list) **and** the workspace `--validate` **in
  lockstep**. This needs the canon §3 Oracle critical-infra diff review.
- **Green-master sequencing:** land the wrapper + tests first (or in one commit
  with tests); make worker-loop and `--validate` tolerate bundles **without**
  `bin/` so no in-flight dispatch breaks during rollout.

## 6. Hit logging → shared waste-telemetry store (Phase-4 contract)

No hard dependency on Phase 4 code. This phase **freezes** the event schema +
path as the P3↔P4 contract; P4 builds ranking on the same file.

- On each rejection, append a design-§5.1 structured NDJSON event:
  ```json
  { "time":"<iso8601>", "repo":"<work repo>", "task_sha":"<sha>",
    "kind":"tool_footgun", "id":"rg-short-r-rejected",
    "severity":"low", "estimated_wasted_tokens":0,
    "estimated_wasted_seconds":0 }
  ```
- Write via `flock -n` (non-blocking) + `O_APPEND` to the designated store
  path. **Operator open question (design §12 Q1):** proposed default
  `~/.local/state/github-worker/agent-waste.ndjson` (single prod host today);
  confirm, or choose a git-ref-mirrored location.
- Logging is **strictly best-effort**: attempt `mkdir -p`; never block on the
  lock; **any** failure is swallowed and MUST NOT alter the wrapper's
  stdout/stderr or exit code.

## 7. Promotion ladder

There is currently **no** `rg -r` advisory in the injected base worker prompt.
So the acceptance criterion is: the wrapper hit-logs, **and** no `rg -r` prose
entry is ever added to the (Phase-4) live advisory budget — the guardrail is
the permanent replacement for that prose. (Retiring any historical KB
"inject-this" flag is tracked by the Phase-3 promotion-ladder task on #34.)

## 8. Tests (deterministic, no prod resources)

- **Parser table** — reject: `-r`, `-rn`, `-nr`, `-inr`, `-r foo`; pass
  through: `--replace x`, `-er`, `-gr`, tokens after `--`, no args,
  `--version`.
- **Recursion safety** — wrapper dir first on `PATH`; wrapper must not call
  itself.
- **Exit-code passthrough** — real rg exit `0`/`1`/`2` preserved.
- **Logging-failure-is-invisible** — read-only state dir must not change the
  wrapper's output or exit code.

## 9. Acceptance

- `rg -r`/`-rn`/etc. rejected with a fix message + structured telemetry event
  logged; `--replace` and all legitimate forms pass through byte- and
  exit-code-exact; workspace/manifest/contract wiring landed with the schema
  bump; master stays green throughout rollout; canon §3 Oracle critical-infra
  diff review recorded for the PATH/manifest change.
- Each implementation attaches an Agent Gate Record (canon §3), and the final
  satisfying commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34` **and** this
  issue's `Issue:`/`URL:` trailer.

## 10. Production safety / rollback

- The wrapper is inert until the workspace installs it and worker-loop prepends
  `bin/` to `PATH`; until then nothing changes.
- Fail-open detection + best-effort logging mean the worst realistic regression
  is a legitimate `rg` invocation wrongly rejected — mitigated by rejecting
  only the provably-footgun form and keeping `--replace`.
- Rollback = stop prepending `bin/` (revert the worker-loop/manifest change);
  the wrapper script alone is harmless.
- The manifest schema bump must land with the contract + `--validate` update so
  no in-flight dispatch fails validation.
declarations.delegationNote: Lever C / design §4 + §5.1 hit-logging + §10 Phase 3; installs into the Phase-1 prepared workspace, logs to the Phase-4 waste store.
declarations.title: Amp cost reduction P3: bin/rg guardrail wrapper + hit logging

# Agent-waste review queue — Helios child epic: second top-level read-only mirror + wire `setBacklogReader()` (re-scope of leaf `0d07aed`)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality" (Lever D).
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md)
> ("Remaining work" #3; decisions **D1/D2** RESOLVED).
> **Re-scopes** the previously operator-blocked task-dag leaf `0d07aed`
> ("Wire Helios agent-waste backlog to the real store"), whose operator gate is
> now closed ([automation#57 comment #4891081664](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/57#issuecomment-4891081664));
> that leaf is parked `--downstream` awaiting this workstream, not
> operator-blocked.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 has **several** child epics,
> the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO carry this issue's own
> `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level completion
> aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal

Make `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` (admin-only) return **real** pending-review
items instead of the 503-degrade default, by having Helios read the backlog file
that github-worker exports into `top-level` (D1/D2). This is the **re-scope** of
leaf `0d07aed`: the operator resolved the transport to be a **git-backed file in
`top-level`, read via a second read-only mirror** — superseding the earlier
same-host-NDJSON sketch in that leaf's note.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Second read-only mirror** | Add a **second** git `--mirror` of `top-level` alongside the existing `automation` mirror, using the same proven pattern as [`helios/src/server/taskDagMirror.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/taskDagMirror.ts): bare `--mirror` clone, ~60s refresh, deploy key, **loud-but-non-fatal** (a fetch failure keeps the last-good copy + reports "stale", never 500s). Reads the D2 read-only deploy key provisioned in child epic #1 (same shape as `/run/agenix/helios-github-automation-deploy-key`). |
| **Wire `setBacklogReader()`** | Implement a `BacklogReader` (the `status()` / `readBacklog()` interface already defined in [`helios/src/server/agentWasteRepo.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/agentWasteRepo.ts)) that reads the exported backlog file from the top-level mirror, and install it via `setBacklogReader()`, replacing the default `unavailableBacklogReader`. Use the hardened `parseBacklogNdjson()` / the Zod contract [`helios/src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts). |
| **Reuse the merged plumbing** | The route `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` (admin-only, 503-degrades when unwired: [`helios/src/server/routes/agentWaste.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/routes/agentWaste.ts)) already exists (issue #57 task 1). This child epic only supplies the reader + mirror. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants (carry forward)

- **Read path is loud-but-non-fatal** (taskDagMirror semantics): a `top-level`
  fetch failure shows stale/unavailable, never a 500.
- **`note` is display-only** — surface it in the admin UI, never inject it into
  any agent.
- **No prod DB dependency** — the whole point of D1 (git file) is to keep the
  producer decoupled from Helios's prod DB. Do not add a DB table for this.
- Deploy key is the **`helios` service user**'s agenix read key (D2), not the
  machine/`amp-local` credential.

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Depends on** child epic #1 (backlog file **format** + **D2 read key**) and,
  for live end-to-end data, child epic #2 (the exporter actually writing the
  file). The reader can be built against a fixture as soon as #1's format is
  fixed; live verification needs #2.
- **Closes out** the re-scoped leaf `0d07aed`.

## 5. Acceptance

- With the exporter running, `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` returns real
  pending-review items; with `top-level` unreachable it reports stale/unavailable
  and never 500s.
- Deterministic, prod-resource-free reader test (fixture backlog file, no prod
  resources), plus the live endpoint confirmed on prod **after** deploy via
  `self-deploy*` under lock. Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

Additive: a second read-only mirror + a reader install. Rollback is reverting
`setBacklogReader()` to the default (endpoint returns to 503-degrade) and
removing the mirror. Read-only credential; no writes to `top-level` from this
child epic (writes are child epic #4). Deploy follows canon (push →
`self-deploy*` under lock; never manually restart the serving Helios process).
declarations.delegationNote: RESOLVED_DESIGN Remaining-work #3; depends on child epic 1 (format + read key) and 2 (live data). Re-scopes/closes blocked leaf 0d07aed.
declarations.title: Agent-waste review queue — Helios: second top-level read-only mirror + wire setBacklogReader() (re-scope of 0d07aed)

# Agent-waste review queue — `github-worker` child epic: export pending-review backlog to top-level (pull-rebase-retry)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality" (Lever D).
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` → `docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md)
> ("Remaining work" #2) and
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> §5 (Lever D).
> **Producer schema (this repo):**
> [`docs/AGENT_WASTE.md`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/docs/AGENT_WASTE.md)
> (`agent-waste backlog --format json`).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 has **several** child epics,
> the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO carry this issue's own
> `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level completion
> aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal

Add a github-worker-side **exporter** that publishes the **pending-review**
agent-waste backlog (the tiny/rare unknown/free-form-`id` items needing a human
eye) to the committed backlog file in `top-level` defined by child epic #1, so
Helios can read it via its read-only mirror (D1/D2). The github-worker
dispatcher (OS user `amp-local`) already holds push creds to `top-level`, so this
reuses an existing, operator-blessed capability.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Exporter** | A step (in the dispatcher / a scheduled hook — reuse the existing worker-loop plumbing) that reads the local pending-review backlog (`agent-waste backlog --format json`, from `docs/AGENT_WASTE.md`) and writes it to the `top-level` backlog file (format from child epic #1). |
| **Raw store stays local** | Only the **pending-review** stream is exported. The chatty raw NDJSON observation store stays **local** to the dispatcher under its state dir (design §5.1); it is never pushed. Do not conflate the two streams. |
| **Pull-rebase-retry on push** | The exporter commits + pushes to `top-level master` using **pull-rebase-retry** (operator-blessed, low volume) so it never leaves piled-up local commits when Helios's promote path lands adjacent commits. Reject no-op writes (nothing changed → no commit). |
| **Idempotent + fail-safe** | Re-running with an unchanged backlog is a no-op. Push/network failure is loud-but-non-fatal (log + retry next cycle); it never blocks dispatch or a serving path. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants (carry forward)

- **Never export the raw observation store**; only the pending-review backlog.
- **`note` is display-only** and never becomes advisory `text` anywhere in the
  pipeline (the promote path in child epic #4 enforces the write side; the
  exporter must not smuggle it into `advisories.yaml`).
- **Pull-rebase-retry** on every push; **reject no-op** commits; reset local
  commit on push failure and refetch/rebase before retry — the same discipline
  the applyConfig pattern uses.
- Runtime stays **PAT-free** — use the dispatcher's existing `top-level` push
  credential (the machine credential owned by `amp-local`), not a new PAT.

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Depends on** child epic #1 (`top-level` backlog file format — the exporter's
  write target). Start after #1's format lands.
- **Feeds** child epic #3 (Helios reads the exported file).

## 5. Acceptance

- A pending-review backlog recorded locally is reflected in the `top-level`
  backlog file within one export cycle, via a pull-rebase-retry push, with no-op
  writes rejected and failures non-fatal.
- The raw observation store is verifiably **not** exported.
- Deterministic, prod-resource-free test of the exporter (fixture backlog → file
  content), no test points at prod resources. Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

Additive: a new exporter path writing one committed file in `top-level`. Rollback
is disabling the exporter (a dispatcher flag) and/or reverting the file. No
serving service is restarted; pushes go to `master` normally (no `self-deploy`
needed for a data-file push). No prod DB, no schema.
declarations.delegationNote: RESOLVED_DESIGN Remaining-work #2; depends on child epic 1 (backlog file format).
declarations.title: Agent-waste review queue — github-worker: export pending-review backlog to top-level (pull-rebase-retry)

issues.body:
We are going to overhaul the operator experience for catalog pricing maintanance and competitor / market data comparison.  We're going to do this in multiple steps, each of which will likely be mostly or entirely contained to the `automation` repo's helios codebase.  Turn this issue into a top-level epic to which we'll link a sequence of child epics that you'll create, one per operator top-level (non-response) comment to this issue, as he guides you through the desired implementation path.

The final goal will be to have an operator be able to view subsets of SKUs/variants by various useful criteria (A), potentially grouped into "equivalency groups" by additional criteria (B), which may or may not be in stock at either site at the time, and be able to see and do each of (D)

A) The expected subsets to review would include but not be limited to (and not in likelihood order):
i) The entire variant catalog
ii) The subset of the variant catalog that is currently in stock at a given site
iii) The subset of the variant catalog that has ever been in stock at a given site (or ever present over a particular time period)
iv) The subset of the variant catalog that was present in one or more recent purchases / inventory receives
v) The superset of (ii) through (iv) that would include the remaining categorical-family, brand-categorical-family, or vendor-categorical-family present in the catalog but that otherwise wouldn't be included, being not in stock (or never in stock) at that site, as such concepts are defined below
My initial expectation is that the most _common_ uses will be a (v) augmented version of (iii) done periodically, perhaps weekly, and (iv) done often, immediately after each inventory receive is completed, but before the newly arriving stock has been made available for sale.

B) Most common for an operator would be to either be examining a single product/SKU by itself at a time, or wanting to look at "[nonbrand] categorical families" (ie, all products of the same {category} X {subcategory} X {pack qty} X {unit size "group", where most distinct sizes are separate "groups", except that the operator may eventually designate certain unit sizes as being "morally equivalent", for instance the 0.5g unit size preroll compared to the 0.6g semi-novelty size preroll; those will be grouped}), or looking at "brand categorical families" (as above but from the same brand) or in the future "vendor categorical families" (once that mapping from vendor to sets of brands has been finally added).  The idea for looking at the families as that will _often_ (but not always) want to "price" (E) that family the same way or the same amount for brand price consistency.

C)

D) Operator will ultimately want to:
i) View (live-pulled from Litalerts if needed due to cached data staleness or missing) Near-distance-Competitor and near-to-mid-distance broader market pricing data, at operator's choice either (a) limited to each individual sku/variant, (b) aggregating the pricing data along a "___ categorical family" grouping.  In the former case, all litalerts pricing data MUST be a categorical family match, meaning it MUST be the same "type of thing" (category, ideally subcategory if we could tell), "qty of thing" (mostly for edibles and preroll multipacks - a 10pack and a 5pack are very different classes of product), and "size of thing" (unit size in general; usually 10mg for edibles, 3.5g, 7g, 14g, 28g for flower, the vape size for vapes pods and cartridges along with the "all in one / disposable" attribute or lack thereof, or a small group of equivalency classes for preroll sizes (roughly: 0.35, 0.5g, 1.0g, 1.5g, 2.0g [can't remember if we have any >1.5g blunts, but if so those are standard sizes].  In particular, "novelty / marketing" preroll unit sizes like 0.6g should be rolled together with the 0.5s, and 1.1g should be rolled into the 1.0s.  Often in prior pricing pages, i see the wrong "kind of thing" being included in the market pricing data, which really messes up analysis of a "market price" and our pricing strategies.  This usually occurs when one of the structured data is either misparsed, misunderstood, or ignored (for instance, when i'm looking at a 1.0g Fernway disposable vape, and helios includes litalerts pricing for a same (or different) strain but at 0.3g size, which would be MUCH cheaper, messing up IQR and price proposals etc.  Definitely post followup questions if oracle can't understand what i mean after seeing a representative sampling of the catalog's structured data for prerolls.

ii) Click-to-new-tab to see a full, detailed market data page, which includes not only the pricing ladder (much expanded on this page), but also analysis summary, recommendation engine summary, insights if any from our prior X time that we may have stocked and sold these items,, whether they sold well or not, at what effective price, etc.  Operator might also like to do all the things we've already built the pricing pages to do: examine proposed price, its effect on GM%, see recent cost(s), etc

iii) Be able to manually tag a litalerts pricing listings in bulk as being "mismatched" to the family, and being able to rerun analysis on that product or family afterwards, excluding the incorrect listing(s).  "Mismatched" listings should be retained and ultimately analyzed to fix whatever caused the mismatch.

iv) Select a new Global or site-Local price to be applied to each member of the family, or if preferred to set them individually on each SKU.  This should use the evolved pricing ladder control we've implemented.

v) Select a new Promo price to be applied to a then-to-be-created Promo (at a site level) for all items in the same-priced categorical family


This is where we are going.  However, the steps we'll take will each be Oracle reviewed, and done as child epics created for each issue comment below.

```yaml
{
  "delegated_to": [
    {
      "repo": "FreshlyBakedNYC/automation",
      "issue": 55,
      "note": "Implement step 1 (T1 temporary family-explorer page, T2 category-aware size-group equivalency normalizer wired only into the explorer, T3 verify/enforce geographic-limited LitAlerts pulls) per docs/epics/catalog-pricing-overhaul/child-epics/automation/EPIC_PLAN.md. Honor per-step Oracle design/diff/UI reviews and confirm the size buckets and the Satisfies trailer target with the operator on #35 before landing. #35 is a long-lived multi-step umbrella - do not let a single child completion prematurely close it."
    },
    {
      "repo": "FreshlyBakedNYC/automation",
      "issue": 59,
      "note": "Implement step 3 (T1 price-outlier IQR helper + market-match contract fields, T2 outlier UX in the existing panel, T3 feedback persistence schema/API + stable retailerId, T4 parse-correction drawer/bottom sheet with scoped convention capture, T5 promotion support into helios-parser-configs use-cases/litalerts, T6 review/polish gate) per docs/epics/catalog-pricing-overhaul/child-epics/automation/step-3-in-page-feedback/EPIC_PLAN.md. Keep DB feedback inert w.r.t. production scoring (no second parser); outlier stats over above-threshold same-family priced candidates only, computed before the display cap; mobile-first, no wide new column. Honor per-step Oracle design/diff/UI reviews and confirm the Satisfies trailer target with the operator on #35 before landing - #35 is a long-lived multi-step umbrella, do not let a single child completion prematurely close it."
    }
  ]
}
```

# Helios catalog-pricing overhaul — step 3 — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#35](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/35).
> The authoritative umbrella is
> [`docs/epics/catalog-pricing-overhaul/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo. This child epic covers **step 3** of that umbrella. Prior
> steps shipped:
> [step 1 = automation#55](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/55)
> (temporary Categorical Family Explorer + size-group normalizer + LitAlerts
> geographic-limit verification) and
> [step 2 = automation#58](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/58)
> (brand-subdivided families + a lazy per-brand-categorical-family LitAlerts
> **market-match diagnostic panel** with candidate scores, per-factor
> breakdown, and data caveats).
>
> **Do not close #35** on completion, and do not put
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#35` on any landing commit without operator
> confirmation — #35 is a long-lived, multi-step umbrella (same caution as #55
> and #58). Reference this step-3 child issue and rely on the delegation link
> back to #35.

## Step-3 operator ask (verbatim intent)

> "Providing feedback in an efficient way" *in the page itself* is the next
> step to take. Consult with Oracle on how this should be arranged to maximize
> operator efficiency on site-reviewing matches (ideas to consider include
> highlighting significant price outliers for particular review, potentially
> having the operator confirm or explain how to resolve a competitor name
> parsing / extraction issue — MOST retailers will mostly stick to a preferred
> naming convention that tends to include some aspect of unit and/or total
> sizing and/or pack qty. They tend to follow at least one convention per
> category/subcategory, if not one convention for their whole catalog. Once
> that convention is understood for that retailer, it can provide strong hints
> for subsequent listings from that retailer being examined / parsed. Consult
> with oracle on how to modify the page to best suit this purpose, especially
> when viewed in responsive / mobile. Don't waste screen space. Be efficient.
> Have oracle approve the UX design and ensure your implementation of it is
> correct.

The goal of this step is to turn the step-2 **read-only** market-match
diagnostic into a surface where the operator can **act while reviewing**: spot
the listings worth scrutinizing (price outliers), and record what a
mis-parsed competitor listing *should* have been — including the retailer's
naming convention — so subsequent listings from that retailer parse better.

## Design (Oracle-reviewed — approved with refinements)

The UX and the storage/architecture boundary below were reviewed by the
Oracle for this planning step (the operator explicitly required Oracle to
approve the UX design). The automation fleet MUST still obtain its own per-step
Oracle **design** review (before implementing) and **diff + UI** review
(before landing) — this section is the approved *shape*, not a substitute for
implementation-time review.

### The two core interactions

Both attach to the existing per-brand-categorical-family `MarketMatchPanel`
(`helios/src/client/routes/catalog/CatalogFamilyExplorerPage.tsx` +
`/api/catalog/family-explorer/market-match`). **Reuse; do not rebuild** the
panel, the shared scorer
(`helios/src/server/marketMatch/candidateScoring.ts` /
`helios/src/shared/marketMatch/confidence.ts`), or the size-group folding.

**(A) Significant price-outlier highlighting** — flag listings whose price is
a statistical outlier *within the correctly-typed, above-threshold matches for
that family* so the operator can quickly find the rows to scrutinize (a
mis-parse skewing price, or a genuinely off competitor price).

**(B) Retailer name-parsing / extraction feedback** — from a mis-parsed row,
let the operator (i) correct the extracted fields for that listing and (ii)
optionally state the retailer's naming convention, scoped by default to that
retailer × category/subcategory. Captured feedback is a durable, promotable
signal — not a hidden live parser.

### Cardinal rules (from the umbrella's core invariant + Oracle review)

- **Outlier stats are computed ONLY over above-threshold, same-hard-gated-
  family, priced candidates.** Never include below-threshold or wrong-"type-
  of-thing" candidates — doing so recreates the exact IQR-pollution failure the
  operator has repeatedly been burned by.
- **Compute outliers over the full bounded/scored set, BEFORE the display cap**
  — an outlier must never be invisible because it fell outside the top-N-by-
  score table slice.
- **The DB feedback store is NOT a second, live parser.** parsekit /
  `helios-parser-configs` remains the single authoritative *executable* parser
  after promotion. Operator feedback must not silently change production
  matching/scoring, `fuzzy_skus`, market aggregates, or IQR. Any in-page effect
  of unpromoted feedback is a clearly-labeled, opt-in **preview** only,
  excluded from aggregates.

### UX (mobile-first, no wide new table column)

Per `helios/AGENTS.md` (purpose-first, don't waste screen space) and the
"responsive/mobile, be efficient" directive:

- **Panel summary pill** — add a warning pill only when non-zero, e.g.
  `3 price review`, with a tooltip stating the IQR basis (count, median,
  fence). Show nothing when there are zero outliers (no "0 outliers" noise).
- **"Needs review" strip above the table** — when outliers exist, a compact
  section before the wide table. Desktop: one-line chips (max ~3 + "show all").
  Mobile: stacked cards, open when non-empty, each showing listing (link),
  retailer, price with a `↑$`/`↓$` direction badge, current parsed size/pack
  vs. expected family size/pack, and a **`Fix parse`** action. This is what
  lets the operator find and act on the work *without* horizontally scrolling
  the table on a phone.
- **Sticky Score cell affordances** — no new column. In the existing sticky
  score cell add a tiny `↑$`/`↓$` outlier badge and a small `Fix`/`✎` icon
  button (accessible label), plus a subtle row tint / left border and price-
  cell emphasis. These stay visible while the table is scrolled horizontally.
  A row that already has saved feedback shows a tiny `feedback`/`hint` pill.
- **Correction drawer / bottom sheet** (not inline table editing) — opened by
  `Fix parse`. Mobile: bottom sheet; desktop: side drawer. Sections:
  1. Listing context (retailer + stable id, listing link, price, distance
     band, snapshot time, score, outlier badge).
  2. Current parse vs. family expectation (two-column: current parsed
     size/pack/category/subcategory vs. the family's expected size-group /
     pack / category / subcategory).
  3. "What's wrong?" chips (`size`, `pack qty`, `category/subcategory`,
     `brand`, `name tokens/strain`, `price is genuine`,
     `not same product / no match`) that reveal only the relevant fields —
     don't front-load a giant form.
  4. Correction fields (pack count, unit size value/unit, total size
     value/unit, category/subcategory), prefilled from the current parse and
     family where possible. Keep brand correction distinct from the existing
     brand-mapping semantics unless explicitly wired into brand overrides.
  5. Convention capture (opt-in checkbox "Also propose a retailer naming
     convention"): default scope `this retailer + category/subcategory`;
     optional `retailer-wide`, `retailer + brand`, `this listing only`;
     free-text note + auto-generated examples from the corrected listing(s) +
     optional pattern chips (`brand first`, `size at end`, `pack before size`,
     `total size shown`, `unit size shown`). The operator NEVER authors
     parsekit JSON or regex.
  6. Save → persists the exact listing correction (+ convention candidate when
     selected), marks the row/card `feedback saved`, and MAY show a clearly-
     labeled preview of the corrected parse/score for that one listing.

### Storage / architecture boundary (Oracle recommendation)

Three layers, with a firm boundary between live operator input and the
authoritative parser:

1. **Helios DB — operator feedback inbox** (the live web input target). One
   normalized feedback table with a discriminated `kind` (listing correction /
   convention proposal). Store: `useCase`/`sourceKind` (`litalerts` for this
   page), `sourceListingId`, `fuzzySkuId`, **`retailerId`** (stable — display
   name is not; add it to the API contract), raw listing name + input
   hash/snapshot, family key / brand key, matched catalog product id (if any),
   corrected structured fields, issue/disposition type, convention note +
   scope + examples, actor/time, and `status` (`draft | promotion_requested |
   promoted | rejected | superseded`). This immediately improves the *operator
   workflow* (show saved feedback on rows, prefill future corrections for the
   same retailer/scope, "convention candidate exists" hints, exact-listing
   corrected-parse preview) **without** changing production scoring.
2. **No active DB parser.** Do not let DB conventions silently reparse
   subsequent listings and change the panel's real score/counts — that forks a
   second parser beside parsekit and breaks the audit page's "this is the real
   matcher" invariant. If cross-listing impact is ever wanted, it must be an
   explicit, default-off, clearly-labeled `Preview with unpromoted retailer
   hints` toggle, excluded from aggregates/IQR/pricing and never persisted into
   `fuzzy_skus` as canonical. (Out of scope for this step unless the operator
   asks — see below.)
3. **parsekit / `helios-parser-configs` — authoritative executable parser.**
   Promotion path (agent/reviewer, not the web UI): select DB feedback for a
   retailer/scope → export corrected examples as parsekit **goldens** →
   create/update `helios-parser-configs/use-cases/litalerts/parsers/<tenantId>.jsonc`
   (`litalerts` is the current source; reserve `competitor-ecom` for direct
   competitor e-commerce sources later) → run parsekit validation/goldens →
   review/push → Helios parser registry loads the new snapshot → mark the DB
   feedback `promoted` with parser/rule id + config sha. This is the concrete
   realization of the runtime-adjustable parser-config work tracked under
   [automation#19](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/19).

## Scope owned by this child epic (tasks)

### T1 — Price-outlier domain helper + market-match contract fields (must-have)

- Pure, deterministic outlier helper using **Tukey IQR fences** (`< q1 −
  1.5·IQR`, `> q3 + 1.5·IQR`) over above-threshold, same-family, finite-priced
  candidates (use `preTaxPrice`; post-tax is a constant multiplier). Guards:
  no statistical flag when basis count `< 5`; when IQR is effectively zero,
  fall back to a conservative tight-cluster rule (flag only when the value
  differs from the median by **both** an absolute and relative threshold, e.g.
  `≥ max($5, 20% of median)`). Never remove/down-rank a candidate for being an
  outlier — review signal only.
- Extend `catalogFamilyMarketMatch` contract: per-candidate
  `priceOutlier: null | { kind: 'low' | 'high'; delta; fence; median; basis }`,
  a response-level `priceOutlierSummary`, and a `reviewCandidates` array
  (full-set outliers, bounded — e.g. 25 — with an overflow warning) so
  outliers survive the display cap.
- Tests: min-sample suppression, high/low IQR flags, tight-cluster fallback,
  below-threshold excluded, missing-price excluded.

### T2 — Outlier UX in the existing panel (must-have)

- Summary `price review` pill (only when non-zero); "Needs review" strip/cards
  above the table; sticky score-cell `↑$`/`↓$` badge + `Fix` action + row
  tint. No new wide column. Mobile cards usable before the horizontal table.
  Preserve existing caveat pills and the below-threshold divider.

### T3 — Feedback persistence: schema + API + contracts (must-have)

- DB migration for the normalized feedback table (discriminated `kind`) with
  the fields listed under *Storage layer 1*. Add stable identifiers to the
  candidate contract (esp. **`retailerId`** from the raw LitAlerts data).
- Endpoints: fetch feedback for visible candidate/retailer ids; create/update
  feedback; update status. Zod contracts; no first-party `any`.
- **Record a DB cost/plan** for the new queries; reuse existing indexed reads
  where possible.

### T4 — Parse-correction drawer / mobile bottom sheet (must-have)

- Drawer/sheet per the UX above: listing context, current-vs-expected parse,
  issue chips, correction fields, opt-in convention proposal (scope + note +
  examples + pattern chips), save + `feedback saved` row badge. Optional
  clearly-labeled exact-listing corrected-parse/score preview.

### T5 — Promotion support (data shape + export, not web-side git writes) (must-have, light)

- Land the `status`/promotion metadata fields and an export/report query or
  endpoint shaped for an agent/reviewer to turn feedback into parsekit goldens
  + a `helios-parser-configs/use-cases/litalerts/parsers/<tenantId>.jsonc`
  entry. Document the promotion path. **Do not** build web UI that writes git
  configs.

### T6 — Review / polish gate (must-have)

- Deterministic, prod-resource-free tests; mobile screenshots / UI-review
  notes; Oracle design + diff + UI review before close; explicitly re-verify
  **no new unbounded LitAlerts pulls** (reuse the bounded nearest-retailer
  fan-out). Record the Agent Gate Record on each landing.

## Nice-to-haves (land only if cheap; don't block the step)

- A "price is genuine" disposition that suppresses already-reviewed outlier
  warnings. **Reconfirm with the operator** whether a saved "genuine" mark
  should permanently suppress future outlier flags for that listing/retailer.
- `Outliers only` / `Review first` filter toggle.
- Showing existing retailer convention hints on every row from that retailer.
- An export command that emits candidate parsekit golden cases directly.

## Explicitly out of scope for step 3 (later steps / other work)

- Making unpromoted DB feedback change production scoring/matching, `fuzzy_skus`,
  or any market aggregate (the default-off preview toggle is the only allowed
  cross-listing effect, and even that is out of scope unless the operator asks).
- Auto-generating or committing `helios-parser-configs` from the Helios web UI.
- The broader parsekit read-path migration owned by
  [automation#19](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/19).
- Turning the temporary page permanent/polished, the full A-subset picker,
  price/promo application, and the detailed click-through market-data page
  (umbrella D) — later steps.
- Any new/unbounded market-data collection or LitAlerts pull.

## Top risks to call out (for the implementing fleet)

1. **Second-parser risk** — active DB conventions would diverge from parsekit
   and make the audit panel stop reflecting the real matcher. Keep DB feedback
   inert w.r.t. production scoring.
2. **Outlier pollution** — stats MUST exclude below-threshold / wrong-family
   candidates, or they reproduce the IQR-pollution failure.
3. **Display-cap invisibility** — compute outliers before the display cap; keep
   `reviewCandidates` visible.
4. **Small-sample noise** — no statistical flag below the minimum basis; use the
   conservative fallback when IQR is tiny.
5. **Mobile hidden actions** — never rely on an off-screen table column; use the
   review cards + sticky score-cell action.
6. **Unstable retailer identity** — persist by retailer id / source ids / raw
   hash, not display name.
7. **Promotion target ambiguity** — the current source is LitAlerts, so promote
   into `use-cases/litalerts`; only use `competitor-ecom` for direct competitor
   e-commerce sources.

## Validation

Each landing commit MUST:

1. Land green on `automation` CI: `cd helios && npm run check` (server +
   client typecheck + `vitest run`) and `npm run build`. Add unit tests for the
   outlier helper (T1) and the feedback contracts/queries (T3). No first-party
   `any`; no bug-masking fallbacks; deterministic, prod-resource-free tests.
2. Be visible on `vps-nixos-3` after the sanctioned `self-deploy-helios`
   (never a manual `systemctl restart` of the helios units).
3. **Record a DB cost/plan** for every new feedback query (T3), reusing
   existing indexed catalog/partner reads where possible.
4. Honor canon gates: Oracle **design** review (before implementing) and
   **diff** review (before landing) for this operator-facing surface, plus
   Oracle **UI** review of the drawer + outlier affordances on mobile
   (signal-to-noise, next-action, no wasted space). Record the Agent Gate
   Record on each landing.
5. Carry the cross-repo completion trailer on the master-landing commit. **See
   the multi-step-umbrella caution above** — confirm the intended `Satisfies:`
   target with the operator on #35 before landing so a single child completion
   does not prematurely close the umbrella.

## Completion signal for the child

This child epic is done when:

- The market-match panel highlights significant price outliers (IQR-based,
  correctly-typed basis) via a compact, mobile-usable "Needs review" surface
  and sticky-cell badges, with outliers surviving the display cap (T1 + T2).
- The operator can, from a mis-parsed row, open a drawer to correct the
  extracted fields and optionally record a scoped retailer naming convention,
  persisted to the Helios feedback store with stable identifiers, and see the
  row marked as having feedback (T3 + T4).
- The promotion path into `helios-parser-configs` is documented and the data
  shape/export supports it, without any web-side git writes (T5).
- All gates green (T6), demonstrated on `vps-nixos-3`.
- An operator-facing closure/status comment is posted on
  `virusdave/top-level#35` prefixed `<!-- task-dag:status -->` (do NOT
  hand-post the `<!-- task-dag:completion -->` cross-repo signal — the peer
  repo's completion-sync workflow emits it from the `Satisfies:` trailer),
  including the live page URL, commit links, the chosen outlier method + basis
  rules, and the feedback→promotion boundary, so the operator can iterate into
  the next step.
declarations.delegationNote: Implement step 3 (T1 price-outlier IQR helper + market-match contract fields, T2 outlier UX in the existing panel, T3 feedback persistence schema/API + stable retailerId, T4 parse-correction drawer/bottom sheet with scoped convention capture, T5 promotion support into helios-parser-configs use-cases/litalerts, T6 review/polish gate) per docs/epics/catalog-pricing-overhaul/child-epics/automation/step-3-in-page-feedback/EPIC_PLAN.md. Keep DB feedback inert w.r.t. production scoring (no second parser); outlier stats over above-threshold same-family priced candidates only, computed before the display cap; mobile-first, no wide new column. Honor per-step Oracle design/diff/UI reviews and confirm the Satisfies trailer target with the operator on #35 before landing - #35 is a long-lived multi-step umbrella, do not let a single child completion prematurely close it.
