issues.body:
**Follow-up to the Amp cost-reduction epic [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)** (which introduced the prepared-workspace *runtime capsule* — the small dispatcher-injected block that replaces reading full canon on every task).

## Problem (systemic, observed across many worker agents)

Two **fleet-wide, every-task** conventions are being violated by nearly every worker agent:

1. **Commit subjects use Conventional-Commits prefixes** (`feat(helios):`, `fix(mss):`, `chore:`) instead of the mandated plain, capitalized, imperative English sentence. Canon rule: [`docs/canon/rules/WORKFLOW.md` → "Commit messages"](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/WORKFLOW.md).
2. **Agents push the implementation commit to `master` *before* running `task-dag complete` locally.** The canonical order is commit → `git fetch` → `git rebase origin/master` → `task-dag complete` (which builds the completion **merge** locally) → push implementation+completion together. Pushing first creates a race: if another commit lands, recovery must use `task-dag complete-historical`, which encodes the task↔commit link only in a commit-message trailer instead of in git **parentage**, losing the normal, queryable linkage.

## Root cause (confirmed with Oracle)

This is a **delivery-path** failure, not a missing-doc failure. Both rules already exist in canon `WORKFLOW.md`. But the dominant execution mode is the **prepared workspace**, where the agent reads only two always-injected surfaces — the github-worker **base worker prompt** (`prompts/base-worker-prompt.txt`) and the **runtime capsule** (single-sourced from top-level `docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md`) — and deliberately does **not** read full canon (that is the whole cost saving).

- The capsule is a **router**: it carries safety bans + the Agent Gate Record, then a "Scenario → deep doc" table, and ends with *"the routine frontier→work→complete→push loop needs no Core re-read."* The row that points to `WORKFLOW.md` is labeled *"non-routine task-dag … commit/issue conventions."*
- The two violated rules apply to **100% of tasks**, yet they live **only** in the deep doc the routine path is told to skip. An agent making an ordinary commit does not self-identify as "non-routine" or "changing conventions," so it never follows the pointer.
- **Commit-message style is absent from both always-injected surfaces**, colliding with the base model's strong Conventional-Commits prior → near-guaranteed miss.
- The **finalize order** *is* in the base prompt, but terse and without the *why* (the `complete-historical` / lost-parentage hazard), so it is underweighted.
- The tooling does not catch it either: `task-dag guard-commit-message` today only rejects task-dag control-plane markers; its tests explicitly *allow* `fix(scope):`-style subjects.

Because prompt text alone has already failed, the fix combines **point-of-action prompt text** with **mechanical enforcement**.

## Design (Oracle-reviewed)

**Layer 1 — inline the universal rules in the always-injected surfaces:**
- **Capsule static block** (`top-level:docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md`): add a compact "Universal workflow invariants" section (commit-style ban + finalize order + the *why*) after the Delivery gate. ~50 words; fits the 500-word budget (currently 434).
- **Base worker prompt** (`github-worker:prompts/base-worker-prompt.txt`): fold the same into the "Finalize" section at the point of push, with a small compensating cut to stay under budget.
- **`WORKFLOW.md`** stays authoritative; add the explicit finalize order + race rationale if not already spelled out. **No** third copy in canon Core.
- **Budget/drift guards** (`top-level:scripts/agent-prompt-budget` + `github-worker` mirror): add required-text anchors so these load-bearing lines cannot be silently shrunk away, and a mirror check that the commit/finalize tokens appear in both the capsule and `WORKFLOW.md`.

**Layer 2 — mechanical enforcement (the part that makes it stick):**
- **`task-dag` guards** (`virusdave/task-dag:scripts/task-dag`): extend `guard-commit-message` to reject Conventional-Commits subjects (`^lowercase-type(scope)?!?:`); run the same subject check inside `task-dag complete` (block live work, warn-only for `complete-historical`); add a `guard-pre-push` that refuses pushing an implementation commit ahead of `origin/master` unless HEAD is a completion/close-merge shape. With tests.
- **Chained hooks in prepared workspaces** (`github-worker`): install session-local `commit-msg` + `pre-push` hooks that **chain** (never replace) existing repo hooks and call the canonical task-dag CLI.

Ranked: prompt-only = medium lift (relies on the already-failed mechanism); **prompt + task-dag guards + chained hooks = recommended** (near-total for non-malicious workers). Rejected: forcing routine workers to read full canon (defeats the capsule's cost purpose).

**Do-not-do:** no full `WORKFLOW.md` prose in the capsule/Core; no third unsynchronized canon copy; do not overwrite repo hooks (chain them); keep `complete-historical` loud/exceptional; do not broaden the subject regex into a grammar checker (mechanically reject only the high-signal `lowercase-type(scope):` pattern; leave "imperative/capitalized" to prompt/canon).

## Ownership / execution

Per operator instruction, a **single owner** implements all pieces **sequentially** in one session (no cross-repo `Materialise-Child-Epic:` delegation to other workers). task-dag has no single-DAG cross-repo epic primitive, so: this epic + its born-claimed children live in `top-level` for the top-level work; the `github-worker` and `task-dag` changes land as commits linked back via canonical `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#<this-issue>` trailers. Both critical-infra diffs (task-dag guards, github-worker hook installation) get an Oracle change-review before push.

issues.title: Enforce canonical commit-message style and complete-before-push across the agent fleet

issues.body:
## Context

`scripts/ephemeral_checkout` had a legacy "clone strictly from a local
repo" code path (shared-object-store / `git clone --local --shared` /
`--from-local`) that was **removed in Issue #27**. Standard development
always does an ephemeral checkout **from `origin` (or another remote)**,
never from a local repo's object store.

**Scope guard:** this is *not* about the still-supported path where you
pass a local checkout path and we clone *its `origin` URL* — that path
is fine and stays. This epic is specifically about the *removed*
clone-strictly-from-the-local-repo behavior.

## What we want

If anything attempts to use the now-removed clone-strictly-from-local
code path, `ephemeral_checkout` should emit a **LOUD stderr** message and
**stop**, rather than silently doing something else or falling back.

The tooling **cannot know** the reason for its atypical invocation, so it
must not attempt to create any page or page the operator itself. Instead,
the stderr message **instructs the (now-paused) agent** to:

1. Recognize it is **likely straying from the intended development
   process**, and **pause work**.
2. Consult the **full canon + repo docs** (not just the initial
   conservative subset) to confirm it truly needs this.
3. If it still believes local-cloning is correct:
   - **author a self-contained one-offs page** (no other operator
     context needed) that clearly explains:
     - why the worker is attempting this non-standard local-clone thing,
     - why the normal "ephemeral checkout from `origin` or another
       remote" is insufficient for the goal, and
     - why the attempted local-clone is the correct approach that our
       tooling should support;
   - then **`page-dave`** (per canon paging) with a **24h one-offs link**
     to that page.

## Rationale / accepted risk

This path realistically only triggers if **all remotes are
simultaneously unavailable** (origin + every mirror). The operator
**accepts that as a worker-pool-development-blocking risk** — we would
rather hard-stop-and-page than silently fall back to a divergent local
clone.

## Status

**Operator-blocked.** The operator will unblock this when ready to
implement.

Relevant file: `scripts/ephemeral_checkout` (see the Issue #27 removal
notes near the top of the file).

All of our tools, whether living as bash scripts in a repo, or built as nix packages and installed on a system, should have an *innocuous* operation mode where it accepts a `--help` flag.  In particular, some or all of our `self-deploy*` nix-config-defined packages do not have this, and will just barge ahead with the normal potentially effectful core functionality, when the agent invoking with `--help` likely did not intend any effects other than an expected help text to be displayed.

This is a _very_ reasonable expectation, so lets audit all of our tooling to ensure we follow that standard, and ensure this new requirement is documented unambiguously in a way that agents who work on existing tooling or create new tooling won't ignore or overlook

# Tooling `--help` safety — `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc` child epic (safety-critical)

> Parent epic: [virusdave/top-level#47](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/47)
>
> The implementation commit on this repo's master MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47
> ```
>
> That trailer triggers the cross-repo completion flow back to the parent
> issue.

## Why this is safety-critical

Our `self-deploy*` deploy wrappers are the single sanctioned way to roll
production services. They currently do **no flag parsing** and barge
straight into their effectful core, so an agent invoking one with
`--help` — expecting only usage text — can trigger a real production
rollout (`nixos-rebuild switch`, traffic flips, unit restarts, SSH to the
peer host). Canon now forbids this.

## Step 0 — read canon first

Read the rule before touching anything (ephemeral checkout of top-level
master):

- [`docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md) "Code standards" — the normative `--help` rule.
- [`docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md) "Serving services" — the deploy-safety face of it.

## The requirement

Every invocable tool must accept `-h` and `--help`, print usage to
stdout, and exit `0` **before any effect** — for these deploy tools,
before any `nixos-rebuild`, traffic/mirror flip, `systemctl`
restart/drain, deploy-lock acquisition, SSH to a peer, secret read, or
file write. Handle `--help` first, ahead of all other option parsing and
required-env checks.

## Known violators (audit for more — this list is a starting point)

- `self-deploy` — inline bash in `hosts/vps/amp-local.nix` (the
  whole-host `nixos-rebuild switch` package).
- `self-deploy-helios` — inline bash in `modules/helios.nix` (traffic
  flip + `helios-prep`/`helios-server` restart + `/healthzz` poll).
- `self-deploy-{site}` — generated by the `mkSelfDeployScript` factory in
  `hosts/vps/sites-mirror.nix` (per-site MSS rollout). Fix the factory
  once so every generated package inherits `--help` handling.
- `scripts/helios-deploy` — orchestrates `self-deploy-helios` across
  primary/mirror; begins Phase 1 SSH immediately.
- Any other scripts in `scripts/` and any other nix-packaged CLIs you
  find during the audit.

Note: `scripts/update-amp-local-version.sh` and
`update-amp-local-version-everywhere.sh` already handle `-h`/`--help`
correctly — mirror their pattern (a `usage()` that exits 0, parsed
first).

## Verifying without deploying

**Do not run an actual deploy to test.** For each nix-packaged tool,
`nix build` the package and run the built script with `--help`, asserting
it prints usage and exits 0 with zero side effects. Landing on
`nixos-sbc` master does not auto-deploy (deploy stays manual via
`self-deploy`), and adding an early `--help` exit ahead of all effects is
a low-risk, easily-reverted change. Keep a clean revert path.

## Finalize

Commit with a plain imperative subject (no `feat:`/`fix:` prefix) and the
`Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47` trailer; push to this repo's default
branch.

# task-dag child epic — `reconcile-closed-issue` command

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#48](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/48)
> — "There are a large number of incorrectly still open tasks".
> **Gating design (signed off):**
> [`docs/designs/closed-issue-task-reconciliation.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/closed-issue-task-reconciliation.md)
> in `virusdave/top-level` — read §2 (disposition policy), §3 (CLI
> contract), §6 (rollback). The operator signed off the §2 policy on #48.
> **Governing rule:** canon `docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md`
> "Critical-infrastructure changes" (task-dag is the dispatch/claim core)
> and "never hand-roll ref surgery — reusable, tested logic belongs in the
> CLI".

## Why this lives in task-dag

The task-dag CLI now has a single canonical home in `virusdave/task-dag`.
Closed-issue reconciliation is reusable, tested issue→task discovery plus
ref deletion — exactly the kind of logic canon forbids hand-rolling as
one-off workflow bash. It must be a first-class CLI subcommand so both the
automation (parent epic child 3) and the one-time backfill (child 4) call
one implementation, not two.

## Problem recap

The github-worker dispatcher gates every candidate task on **live** GitHub
issue state: when a task's issue is observed `CLOSED` it skips the task and
prunes only the **local** `refs/heads/tasks/*` ref. The authoritative
`tasks/frontier/<short>`, `tasks/active/<short>`,
`tasks/blocked/<full-sha>` (+ `tasks/blocked-meta/<full-sha>`) refs on
**origin** survive and re-materialise on every `git fetch`. Such a task is
never worked and never cleaned — it clutters the frontier and dashboards
forever. Issue #48 is the accumulated backlog of exactly these tasks.

The existing sweep
(`.github/scripts/cleanup-closed-issue-task-refs.sh`) only runs on the
sanctioned bot `Closes-Epic:` push path; manual/out-of-band closes (the
common case behind #48) only fire a pager and never reconcile the refs.

## Scope — implement `task-dag reconcile-closed-issue`

Add one subcommand (policy-named, not mechanism-named):

```
task-dag reconcile-closed-issue <issue> [--dry-run] [--json] [--yes]
```

### Behaviour (per design §3)

1. **Confirm the issue is CLOSED first.** Resolve the issue's live state
   via the same authority as the dispatcher (`gh issue view … --json
   state`). Undetermined or not-`CLOSED` ⇒ **no mutation**; report and
   exit `0` on a clean not-closed no-op, non-zero only on a genuine error.
2. **Enumerate** the non-completed, open task refs that resolve to this
   `(repo, issue)`: `tasks/frontier/<short>`, `tasks/blocked/<full-sha>`
   (+ `tasks/blocked-meta/<full-sha>`). Reuse the canonical resolution
   (the same `blocked --json` meta-overridden-issue + derived-repo
   semantics); a cross-repo `Repo:` block that is not *this* repo is **not**
   a match. Never re-parse commit bodies ad hoc.
3. **Delete only** refs that point at the expected task SHA, honouring the
   **frontier-first** invariant (delete `frontier` before `blocked` under a
   `--force-with-lease` on the observed SHA, so a concurrent breakdown that
   re-pointed a short-sha ref is never clobbered and no pickable window
   opens) — the exact discipline already proven in
   `cleanup-closed-issue-task-refs.sh`. **Absorb / share that logic so
   there is one implementation, not two** (ideally refactor
   `cleanup-closed-issue-task-refs.sh` to call the new subcommand).
4. **Never delete** `tasks/pending/<N>` (epic identity) or
   `gh/comments/<N>/<id>` (comment provenance). Leave `tasks/active/*`
   alone — a live claim's worker CAS-cleans it on `complete`; deleting it
   only makes that worker fail loud, and a stale active ref for a closed
   issue is harmless debris.
5. **`--dry-run`** reports exactly what *would* be removed and mutates
   nothing. Non-dry runs require `--yes` when stdin is not a TTY (matching
   `drop`'s guard).
6. **Output** is both human-readable and machine-readable (`--json`): the
   removed task SHAs and ref names, the skipped/undetermined items with
   reasons, and a summary count. **Idempotent**: a second run over an
   already-clean issue is a successful no-op. **Race-safe**: origin
   readback + `--force-with-lease`-style deletes.

### Fail-safe (per design §2.1)

No mutation unless the issue is **CONFIRMED CLOSED**. Any of the following
⇒ **no-op + report for manual review** (never assume closed):

- `gh` missing / unauthenticated for the repo, or any GitHub API failure
  (mirror `is_issue_closed`'s "undetermined ⇒ don't act", conservative
  direction = *don't delete*);
- ambiguous or unresolved task→issue association (e.g. a cross-repo
  `Repo:`/`Issue:` block not resolving to *this* repo + issue);
- issue state anything other than `CLOSED`.

## Constraints (critical infra)

- **No change to task commit/ref FORMAT and no new ref namespace.** This is
  a reconciliation command built on existing `drop`/ref-helper semantics.
  If implementation ends up needing a format change or a new archival
  namespace, that is critical-infra: **stop, get operator approval + an
  Oracle design review** before proceeding (the design does not anticipate
  this; child must re-check at implementation time).
- **Oracle change review** applies per canon "Critical-infrastructure
  changes" — task-dag is the dispatch/claim core.
- Reuse existing primitives (`drop`, ref helpers, `blocked --json`
  resolution, `is_issue_closed`); do not fork a parallel implementation.

## Tests + docs

- Unit/integration tests for: confirmed-closed happy path (frontier +
  blocked + blocked-meta dropped, pending + provenance kept, active left);
  not-closed ⇒ no-op; `gh` missing/unauth ⇒ no-op + report; ambiguous
  cross-repo association ⇒ skip + report; `--dry-run` mutates nothing;
  idempotent second run; `--json` shape parses under `jq -e`; frontier-first
  race safety (`--force-with-lease` refuses a re-pointed short-sha ref).
- An optional audit/report mode for `validate` that surfaces closed-issue
  lingering refs **WITHOUT** making normal offline `validate` depend on the
  live GitHub API (offline `validate` must stay offline).
- Update the task-dag CLI docs/help for the new subcommand.
- Keep `validate --strict` green; run `tests/task-dag/run-all.sh` as the
  final gate.

## Acceptance

- `task-dag reconcile-closed-issue <issue>` exists and behaves per the
  contract above, with `--dry-run`/`--json`/`--yes`.
- Fail-safe verified: no mutation on any uncertainty; only refs at the
  expected SHA deleted; `pending`/provenance refs preserved.
- `cleanup-closed-issue-task-refs.sh` shares the CLI's logic (single code
  path) or a follow-up to do so is filed.
- Tests (existing + new adversarial/fail-safe cases) and docs land.
- The **final** commit on `virusdave/task-dag` `master` demonstrating this
  child epic's acceptance carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#48`.
  Intermediate commits MUST NOT carry that trailer unless the child epic is
  already fully satisfied. (task-dag's own `complete` adds the peer
  `Issue:`/`URL:` attribution trailer.)
declarations.delegationNote: Implement `reconcile-closed-issue <issue>` per top-level docs/designs/closed-issue-task-reconciliation.md §3 (operator-signed-off policy §2). Default drop-with-audit; --dry-run/--json/--yes; fail-safe (no mutation unless issue CONFIRMED CLOSED); frontier-first --force-with-lease deletes of only refs at the expected SHA; never delete tasks/pending/<N> or gh/comments provenance; leave tasks/active/* alone. Reuse drop/ref-helper/blocked --json resolution and share logic with cleanup-closed-issue-task-refs.sh. Critical infra: Oracle change review; NO ref/commit FORMAT change or new namespace (stop + get operator+Oracle approval if one becomes necessary). Tests + docs; keep offline validate offline.
declarations.title: Implement task-dag reconcile-closed-issue command for closed-issue task cleanup

issues.body:
## Problem

The `Materialise-Child-Epic:` cross-repo flow reads commit trailers with
`git interpret-trailers --parse`
([`materialise-child-epics.sh`](https://github.com/virusdave/task-dag/blob/master/.github/scripts/materialise-child-epics.sh)),
which only recognises the **last contiguous trailer paragraph** of the
commit message. If an author puts *any* trailer after the
`Materialise-Child-Epic:` group separated by a blank line — most naturally
a `Related: <issue-url>` line — that later line becomes the "trailer
block" and the whole `Materialise-Child-Epic:` group is treated as body
text and silently ignored.

Symptom: the Task-DAG `materialise` job goes **green** and logs
`No Materialise-Child-Epic trailers acted upon`, but no peer issue,
marker ref, or delegation is created. The failure is invisible unless you
read the job log and notice nothing happened.

This just bit the [#44](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/44)
decomposition (two materialise commits no-op'd; a corrective commit with a
single contiguous trailer block fixed it). It is an easy, repeatable
mistake — "add a blank line, add a `Related:`/note trailer" is a natural
edit — and the same last-block-only semantics apply anywhere we parse
trailers this way.

## Why it matters

- **Silent no-op on critical infra.** Cross-repo delegation just doesn't
  happen; the parent epic looks decomposed but the peer work is never
  filed. Canon forbids silent bug-masking — this should fail loud.
- Semantically significant blank lines are exactly the whitespace footgun
  canon warns about, but here it is in commit-message trailer parsing, not
  a file format, so no existing gate catches it.

## Requested fix (pick one or combine; needs Oracle design review — critical infra)

1. **Fail loud in the materialise workflow.** When a commit body *contains*
   the literal `Materialise-Child-Epic:` but `interpret-trailers --parse`
   exposes zero such groups, emit `::error::` and `page-dave` instead of
   the benign "No trailers acted upon" line. Cheapest, highest-signal.
2. **Parse the whole body, not just the last block.** Scan the full commit
   message for the `Materialise-Child-Epic:` group(s) (as the loop already
   does per-line) rather than pre-filtering through `interpret-trailers`,
   so extra blank lines / trailing trailers don't hide them.
3. **Pre-commit / pre-push gate** (top-level and/or the task-dag hooks):
   reject a commit whose message has a `Materialise-Child-Epic:` line that
   is not part of the final contiguous trailer block, with a message
   telling the author to collapse the blank line.

Option 1 is the minimal safety net; option 2 removes the footgun entirely;
option 3 catches it before it ever reaches CI. Combining 1+2 (or 1+3) is
ideal.

## Notes

- Recorded as agent-waste (`tool-footgun` / `materialise-trailer-related-block`).
- Related design: [`docs/designs/cross-repo-task-dag-driver.md`](docs/designs/cross-repo-task-dag-driver.md).
- The trailer-scanning logic lives in the task-dag repo, so implementation
  will likely delegate a child epic there; the pre-commit-gate option may
  live in top-level. Decompose accordingly.


```yaml
delegated_to:
  - repo: virusdave/task-dag
    issue: 11
    note: Replace interpret-trailers --parse with a whole-message scanner (opt 2) plus fail-loud accounting (opt 1); drop the pre-commit-hook option; keep the marker/delegate flow unchanged. Critical infra: Oracle design+change review and the script bash -n/shellcheck/materialise tests apply.
```

declarations.body:
# task-dag: parse Materialise-Child-Epic groups from the whole commit message, and fail loud

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#49](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/49)
> — "Materialise-Child-Epic trailers silently ignored when not in the
> final trailer block."
> **Delegated because:** the materialise trailer-scanning logic lives
> entirely in `virusdave/task-dag`
> ([`.github/scripts/materialise-child-epics.sh`](https://github.com/virusdave/task-dag/blob/master/.github/scripts/materialise-child-epics.sh)),
> and the reusable `materialise-child-epic.yml` workflow it drives is what
> every wired peer repo calls — so the fix is repo-local to task-dag and
> automatically protects all callers.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** the implementation commit landing
> on [`virusdave/task-dag`](https://github.com/virusdave/task-dag) `master`
> MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#49`, plus this child epic's own
> `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level
> completion aggregator attributes it to *this* delegated child.

## 1. Goal

`git interpret-trailers --parse` only recognises the **last contiguous
trailer paragraph** of a commit message. The materialise scanner pre-filters
each commit message through it:

```sh
trailers="$(printf '%s\n' "$msg" | git interpret-trailers --parse)"
[ -z "$trailers" ] && continue
```

so a `Materialise-Child-Epic:` group followed (after a blank line) by any
other trailer paragraph — `Related:`, or a task-dag
`Task-Commit:/Issue:/URL:/Status:` block — is dropped, and the job goes
green logging `No Materialise-Child-Epic trailers acted upon`. Silent no-op
on critical cross-repo delegation. Fix it two ways:

1. **Parse the whole body** (option 2): recognise `Materialise-Child-Epic:`
   groups anywhere in the message, delimited only by the next
   `Materialise-Child-Epic:` opener or EOF.
2. **Fail loud** (option 1): a commit that carries an explicit materialise
   directive but produces zero successful materialisations must exit
   non-zero with an `::error::` (and page where a parent issue is known),
   never a benign green summary.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Replace the pre-filter** | Remove the `git interpret-trailers --parse` pre-filter in the main scan of `materialise-child-epics.sh`. Add a purpose-built raw scanner (extracted into a helper so it is unit-testable under `MATERIALISE_LIB_ONLY=1` with no network/GitHub side effects). |
| **Parser contract** | See §3 — a group opens **only** on a column-1, case-insensitive `Materialise-Child-Epic:` / `Materialize-Child-Epic:` key line, and stays open until the next opener or EOF. Blank lines, prose, and unrelated trailer-like lines (`Related:`, `Task-Commit:`, `Issue:`, `URL:`, `Status:`, unknown keys) are **ignored, never group terminators**. |
| **Fail-loud accounting** | Track groups seen / created / already-materialised / failed and a `had_error` flag. Parser/validation failures in `flush_group` (bad peer, missing required keys, bad parent, bad slug, missing body file) set `had_error=1`. At end: benign no-op message **only** when no materialise opener-like line was seen; if an opener was seen but no group parsed, `::error::` + page; if `had_error`, exit non-zero. `::error::` annotations alone do **not** fail a step — an explicit non-zero exit is required. |
| **Tests** | Extend the `MATERIALISE_LIB_ONLY=1` unit tests: (a) group followed by blank line + `Related:` (the #44 regression); (b) group followed by an interleaved task-dag `Status:` block; (c) multiple groups separated by blank lines / unrelated trailers; (d) the plain contiguous-block case (regression); (e) blank line *inside* a group is accepted; (f) indented `Word: value` example lines do not open a group; (g) value containing a colon (`RFC: parser fix`) survives; (h) a malformed explicit group (missing required keys) reports failure, not benign no-op. |
| **Docs** | Remove the header-comment warning that all groups must live in a single final contiguous trailer block; document the new contract (parsed from the full message, delimited only by the next opener or EOF). Update `top-level` `AGENTS.md` / cross-repo-driver design doc references only if they restate the old rule (best-effort, may be a follow-up). |
| **Gates** | `bash -n`, `shellcheck -S error` (as task-dag already runs it), and the materialise unit-test script all green. Critical-infra Oracle design review **before** implementing and change review of the diff **after** (canon `QUALITY_GATES.md`). |

## 3. Parser contract (implement exactly)

1. A group starts **only** on a column-1, exact trailer-key line:
   `Materialise-Child-Epic: <owner/repo>` or `Materialize-Child-Epic:
   <owner/repo>` (key match case-insensitive).
2. Once opened, the group stays active until the next materialise opener or
   EOF.
3. Blank lines, prose, `Related:`, `Task-Commit:`, `Issue:`, `URL:`,
   `Status:`, and unknown trailer-like lines are ignored — **not** group
   terminators. (Closing a group on a blank line or prose would reintroduce
   the whitespace footgun.)
4. Only recognised child-epic keys at column 1 are collected into the open
   group: `Child-Epic-Title`, `Child-Epic-Body-File`, `Parent-Issue`,
   `Child-Epic-Slug`, `Delegation-Note`.
5. Keys before the first opener are ignored.
6. Values preserve existing behaviour: split on the **first** `:`, trim
   leading whitespace after it, preserve later colons in the value.
7. Require column-1 keys (`^[A-Za-z0-9-]+:` with no leading whitespace) so
   indented examples / code blocks in commit messages cannot trigger a
   group. Strip a trailing `\r` and handle a final line with no trailing
   newline (`while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]`).
8. Duplicate recognised keys: preserve existing last-wins behaviour (do not
   silently change semantics as part of this fix).

Suggested shape: an `extract_materialise_trailers_from_message` helper that
emits a normalised synthetic trailer stream, which the existing
`while read line; case "$key_lc"` group-flush loop then consumes with
minimal change. Keep marker-ref identity, ordering, and the
check→create-issue→push-marker→`delegate` sequence **unchanged** — this is a
parser fix only.

## 4. Non-goals

- No change to the `Materialise-Child-Epic:` trailer **format** or the set
  of recognised keys (this is a parser fix, not a format change — but note
  it still touches critical-infra behaviour, so the Oracle review and the
  script's own gates apply).
- No change to marker-ref namespaces, idempotency, App-token minting, or the
  `task-dag delegate` step.
- No pre-commit/pre-push hook (option 3), and no folded/multi-line trailer
  support.
- No change to the pre-existing marker-check → issue-create race (out of
  scope; the parser fix does not worsen it).

## 5. Completion

A single task-dag implementation commit on `master` carrying
`Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#49` and this child epic's `Issue:`/`URL:`
trailer satisfies this child epic; the top-level aggregator then records the
delegated-child completion against #49.
declarations.delegationNote: Replace interpret-trailers --parse with a whole-message scanner (opt 2) plus fail-loud accounting (opt 1); drop the pre-commit-hook option; keep the marker/delegate flow unchanged. Critical infra: Oracle design+change review and the script bash -n/shellcheck/materialise tests apply.

issues.body:
## Summary

While completing the guard leaf of #44 ("Confirm both peer child epics
delegated and keep #44 open for cross-repo closure"), #44 was **auto-closed
as COMPLETED within ~5 seconds of the leaf completing**, even though both
its delegated peer child epics are still OPEN and unsatisfied
([FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#66](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/66),
[virusdave/task-dag#10](https://github.com/virusdave/task-dag/issues/10)),
and **no `Closes-Epic:` merge exists** on `master`.

This is exactly the failure the guard leaf and the delegated-children close
gate were designed to prevent. #44 has been manually **reopened**; this
issue tracks debugging + fixing the tooling/design gap(s) that allowed it.

## Evidence / timeline (2026-07-08)

- `16:08:55–57` — worker ran `task-dag complete 28d3b68`; posted the
  completion status comment (triggered the `issue_comment` Task-DAG run,
  which correctly **skipped** the marked comment and did nothing).
- `16:09:02` — **#44 closed**, `state_reason = COMPLETED`,
  `actor = virusdave` (**type `User`**, i.e. a Personal Access Token — not
  `github-actions[bot]` and not the task-dag App bot).
- `16:09:03–04` — worker `git push` landed; the push-triggered
  `close-completed` job ran **afterwards** (`16:09:07`), scanned
  `691f5af..5f2db47`, found **no `Closes-Epic:` trailer**, and closed
  nothing.

## What was ruled out (root-cause investigation)

The close is **not** attributable to any inspectable, version-controlled
machinery:

- **`task-dag complete`** — does not close the GitHub issue; for an epic
  with delegated children `maybe_emit_local_epic_close` short-circuits via
  `epic_has_delegated_children` (verified in `virusdave/task-dag`
  `scripts/task-dag`). No direct REST close remains.
- **`close-completed-issues.yml`** — closed nothing (no `Closes-Epic:`
  trailer in the pushed range) and ran *after* the close timestamp.
- **`comment-sync` / `sync-comment-to-task`** — ingest-comment skipped the
  marked status comment; no close.
- **github-worker dispatcher/worker** — only *reads* issue state
  (`is_issue_closed` → `gh issue view --json state`); it never mutates
  issue state. No `gh issue close` / state PATCH anywhere in the repo.
- **GitHub native commit-keyword auto-close** — none of the pushed commit
  messages (`f08aed8`, `5f2db47`) contain a `close/fixes/resolves #44`
  keyword (`Closes-Epic:` is hyphenated and not a GitHub keyword).

Conclusion: an **out-of-band process using the operator's PAT** closed #44
(marked COMPLETED) right as the issue's local task-dag frontier emptied,
**bypassing the delegated-children close gate**. The closer is not in any
repo I can inspect and needs to be identified (operator-side cron / sync /
dashboard, or another automation holding the `virusdave` PAT).

## Bugs / gaps to debug and fix

### 1. Root cause — an unknown closer bypasses the delegated-children gate
Something closes an epic issue as COMPLETED when its **local** frontier is
exhausted, without honoring unsatisfied `tasks/delegated/<N>/*` refs. This
is the exact gate `task-dag complete` / `close-epic` implement, so whatever
closed #44 is circumventing it. **Action:** find the closer (audit
processes/crons running under the `virusdave` PAT) and make it defer to the
same delegated-children gate (or drive closure only through the
`Closes-Epic:` merge path).

### 2. Concrete, provable bug — the "manual/unexpected close" pager is broken
`.github/workflows/page-on-manual-issue-close.yml` runs
`bash .github/scripts/page-on-manual-issue-close.sh` **with no
`actions/checkout` step**, so the runner has no repo checkout and the job
fails with `bash: .github/scripts/page-on-manual-issue-close.sh: No such
file or directory` (see the failed run on the #44 close). The sibling
`post-issue-comment.yml` correctly checks out first (`actions/checkout@v4`
before its `bash .github/scripts/...`). **Result:** the operator-alert
safety net for exactly this scenario (a non-bot / unexpected close) never
runs — which is why the anomaly went unnoticed until a worker caught it.
**Action:** add `actions/checkout@v4` to the `page-author` job.

### 3. Design gap — a "keep-pending guard leaf" cannot hold an epic open
The #44 epic plan relied on leaving the guard leaf **pending on purpose**
to keep the delegated epic open
(`docs/epics/no-hand-built-json/EPIC_PLAN.md`, decomposition item 4). That
is not enforceable: dispatchers pick *every* pickable frontier leaf, so the
guard is always completed, and epic-open-ness must instead be guaranteed
solely by the delegated-children close gate. The "leave it pending"
pattern should be removed from the playbook (documented as a footgun in the
epic STATUS doc + `agent-waste`). **Action:** decide the canonical way to
hold a delegated epic open and update the cross-repo driver docs / canon
accordingly.

## Impact

Self-healing at *final* cross-repo completion (the delegated/completion
refs are intact, and `close-epic` will still emit the real `Closes-Epic:`
merge once both peers satisfy), but in the interim a delegated epic shows
**closed while its actual implementation work is unstarted in the peer
repos** — misleading, and (bug #2) the safety net that should have flagged
it is dead.

## Repro for bug #2

Close any issue in this repo as a non-`github-actions[bot]` actor → the
`Page Issue Author On Manual Close` workflow run fails at the `bash
.github/scripts/page-on-manual-issue-close.sh` step with "No such file or
directory" (missing checkout).

declarations.body:
# Helios: cluster pending agent-waste reports with an advanced Bedrock LLM

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#51](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/51)
> — "Waste review page…".
> **Delegated because:** the agent-waste review page, its API routes, the
> backlog reader, the shared contracts, and the bedrock-mantle LLM client
> all live in `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` under `helios/`. `top-level` has
> no code to change.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` for this epic MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#51`, plus
> this child epic's own `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer
> so the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* delegated
> child.

## 1. Goal

Add a **"Cluster similar reports"** action to the admin agent-waste review
page (`/config/agent-waste`). Pressing it sends the current pending backlog
to an **advanced** Bedrock model (via the existing bedrock-mantle
OpenAI-compatible gateway) which groups near-duplicate / highly-similar
observations. The page then renders the result as ranked **clusters**:

- a **primary** (representative) observation per cluster,
- a **total count** of members in that cluster,
- a **collapsed but expandable** list of the remaining members, and
- clusters **sorted by "likely aggregate agent waste"** so the operator can
  address the most common / most expensive problems first.

This lets the operator triage a noisy backlog by theme instead of scrolling
a flat, newest-first list.

## 2. Current state (all paths under `helios/`)

Read these first; the feature slots into the existing shapes.

| Concern | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Review page UI | `src/client/routes/config/AgentWasteReviewPage.tsx` | Admin-guarded page; fetches backlog, renders `ObservationCard`s, has Refresh + per-row Promote. Add the cluster button + clustered view here. |
| Client pure helpers | `src/client/routes/config/agentWasteReviewShared.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) | Fetch/parse/sort helpers are pure + unit-tested (no DOM harness). Put cluster fetch/parse/sort logic here. |
| Server routes | `src/server/routes/agentWaste.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) | `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` and `POST /api/agent-waste/promote`, both `requireSessionUser(request, reply, 'admin')`, structured 503-degrade via `handleAgentWasteError`. Add the cluster route here. |
| Backlog data layer | `src/server/agentWasteRepo.ts`, `src/server/agentWasteBacklogReader.ts` | `getBacklog()` / `getBacklogSourceStatus()`; `BacklogReader` reads the read-only agent-pain-points mirror. Reuse `getBacklog()` verbatim. |
| Shared contracts | `src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts` | `AgentWasteObservationSchema` (+ the display-only `note` rule) and the backlog/promote schemas. Add cluster request/response schemas here. |
| Bedrock env | `src/server/config/env.ts` | `bedrockMantleBaseUrl`, `bedrockMantleBearerToken`, `llmRequestTimeoutMs`. |
| Server LLM call pattern | `src/server/llm/reviewSentimentGate.ts`, `src/server/routes/configLitalertsParsing.ts` | Canonical shape: `fetch(`${baseUrl}/chat/completions`, { headers: Bearer, body: { model, messages, response_format: json_object, temperature }, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(llmRequestTimeoutMs) })`; errors returned structured, never thrown across the request boundary. |
| Model context registry | `src/shared/domain/bedrockModels.ts`, `src/server/llm/bedrockModelConfig.ts` | `BEDROCK_MODEL_CONTEXT_KEYS`, `resolveBedrockModel(db, key)`, operator overrides in `app_settings.bedrock_model_overrides`. Add an `agent_waste_clusterer` context key. |

**Backlog item identity gap (important).** `AgentWasteObservation.id` is a
*stable trigger id* (e.g. `rg-short-r-rejected`), **not** unique per event.
The client already synthesises a composite `observationKey(obs)` for local
dismiss. Clustering needs to map LLM output back to specific observations,
so **assign each observation a stable index/key server-side before sending
to the LLM** and have the model return those keys (see §4).

## 3. Design decisions (implement exactly)

1. **The server does the LLM call.** The Amp Oracle is agent-only; the live
   Helios server calls Bedrock directly through bedrock-mantle, exactly like
   `reviewSentimentGate.ts` / `configLitalertsParsing.ts`. New route:
   `POST /api/agent-waste/clusters`, `admin`-gated, reading `getBacklog()`.

2. **The LLM groups; the server ranks.** The model returns only the
   *grouping* (which observation keys belong together + a short human label /
   representative). "Likely aggregate agent waste" is computed
   **deterministically in Helios** from the members' real
   `estimated_wasted_tokens` / `estimated_wasted_seconds` — never taken from
   the model. Rationale: the ranking must be trustworthy and reproducible,
   and the numbers already exist on each observation. Define the aggregate
   explicitly (e.g. `sum(estimated_wasted_tokens over members)`, with
   `estimated_wasted_seconds` as a documented tiebreak/secondary); pick one
   and encode it in a pure, unit-tested helper. Sort clusters descending by
   that aggregate.

3. **Cluster output is display-only.** It is NOT injected into agents and
   does NOT auto-promote. Sending observation text (including `note`) to the
   *private* clustering model is read/analysis, not allowlist injection; the
   result only renders in the operator UI. The promote path and its
   `.strict()` "`note` can never be advisory text" contract are untouched.

4. **No persistence for v1.** Clusters are computed on demand when the
   operator presses the button and shown in the page; nothing is written to
   the DB or to git. (If the operator later wants shareable/persisted
   clusters, that is a follow-up; do NOT pull in the promote/applyConfig
   write-clone machinery for v1.)

5. **Advanced, operator-overridable model.** Add an `agent_waste_clusterer`
   context key so the model is configurable via the existing Bedrock
   model-override UI, and resolve it with `resolveBedrockModel(db,
   'agent_waste_clusterer')`. **Open question (§6):** the codebase has no
   confirmed-working *advanced* model id on the gateway — `google.gemma-3-27b-it`
   is the only proven model, and `anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-…` was rejected
   with "model not found". The whole point of #51 is a *more advanced* model,
   so the implementer must confirm a working advanced model id on
   bedrock-mantle (or have the operator set one via the override UI) rather
   than silently defaulting to the small model.

## 4. Contract sketch (`src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts`)

Add (names illustrative; keep zod + `.strict()` discipline):

```ts
// Request: no body needed beyond the action; server reads the live backlog.
// (An empty POST is fine, or accept an optional { } for forward-compat.)

// One clustered group, ready to render + already ranked server-side.
export const AgentWasteClusterSchema = z.object({
  label: z.string(),                       // short human theme from the model
  primary: AgentWasteObservationSchema,    // representative member
  members: z.array(AgentWasteObservationSchema), // includes primary; length = count
  count: z.number().int().nonnegative(),   // members.length
  aggregateWastedTokens: z.number().nonnegative(),
  aggregateWastedSeconds: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),
})

export const AgentWasteClustersResponseSchema = z.object({
  source: AgentWasteSourceStatusSchema,    // reuse backlog source status
  model: z.string(),                       // which model actually ran
  clusters: z.array(AgentWasteClusterSchema), // sorted desc by aggregate waste
  unclustered: z.array(AgentWasteObservationSchema).optional(), // items the model left ungrouped
})
```

- The server assigns each observation a stable key (reuse the same field set
  as the client's `observationKey`, or a simple 0-based index for the
  request round-trip) and instructs the model to return groups **by those
  keys**; the server then rehydrates full observations, drops/one-members any
  key the model hallucinated, and computes the aggregates.

## 5. Suggested leaf breakdown

Author these as the child epic's own frontier leaves (the automation
epic-root worker `task-dag breakdown`s this issue):

- **L1 — Server clustering endpoint + contract.**
  - Add cluster schemas to `contracts/api/agentWaste.ts`.
  - Add `agent_waste_clusterer` to `BEDROCK_MODEL_CONTEXT_KEYS` /
    `BEDROCK_MODEL_CONTEXTS`.
  - Add `POST /api/agent-waste/clusters` in `routes/agentWaste.ts`:
    `admin`-gated; `getBacklog()` (503-degrade via `handleAgentWasteError`);
    factor the Bedrock call into a **testable helper** (e.g.
    `src/server/agentWaste/clusterBacklog.ts`) that takes the observations +
    a model id and returns groups; compute aggregates + sort in a pure
    helper; map missing token to `503 bedrock_unconfigured` and gateway/parse
    errors to `502`, matching `configLitalertsParsing.ts`.
  - Tests: route tests via `server.inject` with mocked auth + injected
    backlog reader + stubbed `fetch` (see `agentWaste.test.ts` patterns);
    pure tests for aggregate-scoring + sort + LLM-output parsing/rehydration
    (incl. hallucinated/duplicate keys).

- **L2 — Client cluster button + clustered view.** (depends on L1)
  - Add a **"Cluster similar reports"** button near Refresh on
    `AgentWasteReviewPage.tsx`, with loading / error / unavailable states.
  - Put the fetch + response-parse + (defensive re-)sort logic in
    `agentWasteReviewShared.ts` as pure, unit-tested helpers.
  - Render clusters: a primary `ObservationCard` with a **count** pill and a
    collapsed `<details>`/`<summary>` (per `helios/AGENTS.md`) that expands to
    the member list; keep the existing flat list available (e.g. toggle
    between "flat" and "clustered" views, or show clusters above the list).
  - Pure client helper tests in `agentWasteReviewShared.test.ts`.

## 6. Open questions (resolve during implementation; not operator-blocking)

- **Which advanced model?** Confirm a working advanced model id on
  bedrock-mantle (§3.5). If none is confirmable, ship the endpoint +
  override plumbing and let the operator set the model via the existing
  Bedrock override UI, but surface (don't hide) that the default is not the
  "advanced" model the issue asked for.
- **Aggregate-waste formula.** Tokens-only vs tokens+seconds weighting, and
  how to rank clusters whose members lack `estimated_wasted_*` (treat
  missing as 0, but keep count as a secondary sort so a large all-unrated
  cluster still surfaces). Pick and document one.
- **Backlog size vs prompt budget.** The pending backlog is "tiny and rare"
  by design, so a single-shot cluster call should fit; still cap the number
  of observations / total prompt size sent and degrade clearly if exceeded.

## 7. Gates (canon `QUALITY_GATES.md`)

- `cd helios && npm run typecheck` (server) and `npm run typecheck:client`.
- Focused tests: `npm run test -- <file-or-pattern>` for the new server +
  client helper/route tests. Full `npm run check` is CI-owned.
- Client bundle build (if touched) with an enlarged heap:
  `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 npm run build:client`.
- **This adds a new LLM call on the live server request path** consuming
  agent-adjacent text (backlog notes). Even though the output is
  display-only, it is a new private-LLM surface: get an **Oracle design
  review** of the endpoint + prompt before implementing and a change review
  of the diff, and make the prompt strictly instruct the model to *only*
  cluster + return the fixed JSON shape (defend against injected instructions
  in `note`/observation text). No prompt-injection reachback exists because
  results never feed agents, but the review keeps that boundary explicit.

## 8. Out of scope for v1

- Persisting clusters (DB or git), sharing/linking to a cluster.
- Auto-promoting a cluster to an advisory (still the separate, per-row
  operator-approved promote path).
- Any change to the promote / draft-assist (L1–L3) flow or its `note`
  contract.
- Any `top-level` change beyond this delegation.
declarations.delegationNote: Add an admin-gated POST /api/agent-waste/clusters that reads getBacklog() and calls an advanced bedrock-mantle model (LLM groups only; server computes+sorts aggregate waste), plus the client cluster button + collapsed/expandable clustered view. Display-only output; no persistence; no promote/advisory changes. New LLM-on-request-path surface: Oracle design+change review applies.

issues.body:
Currently, an epic seems to get decomposed into smaller tasks and a task DAG by the initially assigned worker.  Often the worker will decompose the epic into multiple tasks or cross-repo epics that will then need to be decomposed, etc.

The operator considers "decomposed an epic into smaller tasks" to be a minor-ish step for an agent, and not something that should occupy a "operator-blocking worker cycle" (since every time an agent finishes working, it stops and waits for the operator to prompt it more or ctrl-c to exit it).  So in particular, an agent will often read an epic, spend time and effort building context, break the effort down into tasks, and then just... stop working, waiting for other, context-less agents to pick up ALL the tasks or break down child epics, etc.  That seems INCREDIBLY wasteful both in terms of time (the new subtasks take time to be picked often) and resources (new agents will have to establish context again from their launch pointers and assigned task.

Instead, any agent that executes a "breakdown" or comparable process (replacing one HIGH-LEVEL task-dag task with multiple others, including ones that themselves might need to be broken down recursively) should be able to page-dave at p3 the task gate summary it normally blocks on after the breakdown/similar, and instead self-assign-at-birth the first task that has no blocked dependencies.  If this is another breakdown in a different repo, so be it; recurse and break THAT down.  If it's an implementation or ops task, ESPECIALLY if there are other tasks dependent / blocked on it, just create it immediately assigned to that creating agent somehow and proceed to implement.  The agent SHOULD STOP after an actual implementation commit and task closure, just not after breakdowns.

Ensure there are no race conditions and that the broken-down tasks can indeed have the topologically first task assigned at birth so the agent can move right into it, carrying its existing context into the implementation task.  This is true EVEN IF it's in a different repo.

Notes to avoid additional waste: The newly-created task(s) stuff might need to be retrieved from origin; only the original dispatcher-assigned task will have been initially fetched.  On the other hand, the worker, using our tooling to create new tasks, might naturally have them locally already (but we need to ensure that the task it moves on to is DEFINITELY present locally and not-shallow before the worker switches to that task.

Review the design changes and proposed implementation with Oracle, and once approved, page-dave at p4 with a one-offs link giving me the proposal (in an agent->operator comms&UX canon compliant fashion

issues.body:
Agents should prefer canonical 1stparty tooling rather than bespoke crafted 3rdparty CLI commands that replicate implimentations where possible

The title says it all.  I often see workers attempting to use `git` commands to view tasks, and manually parse semantics from the `git` command results.  This is backwards, and can only lead to trouble.  We don't want N different stochastic "implementations" of our semantics/conventions/requirements/etc (where N is number of worker invocations, because the workers just (attempt to) recreate the sufficient structure or semantics in their manual interactions/requests/invocations of 3rdparty "base" tooling.

For all things `task-dag` related (viewing, interacting with, considering dependency relationships between, considering parentage and ancestory, whatever), agents should be first choosing to use our canonical tools, which should have SINGLE, standard, generally tested implementations and semantics.  ONE implementation, reused.  As number of parallel "implementations" of a thing grows, the likelihood that one of them gets things wrong in a very bad, destructive fashion increases dramatically.

As a development philosophy: Encode truth, semantics, constraints, invariants, requirements, etc into a SINGLE, REUSABLE/SHARED implementation via a canonical implementation (tool, code library, canonical shared widget implementation [esp for UI], etc) and reuse it as needed.  Agents should generally ALWAYS prefer an available 1stparty tool, as it implies the above!  Even when a 3rdparty tool can access similar or overlapping data, the 1stparty tooling should be first choice if possible due to the above benefits.

As a design principle, as semantics, constraints, invariants, requirements, etc become clear, we should encode our canonical choices into a single implementation that can be reused as needed, and found easily by agents for such use or reuse.  They shouldn't have to guess or stumble upon this principle or how to enact it.  This likely requires keeping structured, primarily-agent-useful docs or indexes that are mandatory to keep up-to-date, or some other such highly efficient approach to ensure "agents needing a canonical implementation of a thing can find it easily" and "agents needing canonical tooling can find it easily and trivially make use of it to achieve their goals.
issues.creator: virusdave
issues.title: Agents should prefer canonical 1stparty tooling rather than bespoke crafted 3rdparty CLI commands that replicate implimentations where possible

issues.body:
**One-line ask:** investigate (do not build yet) whether we can mechanically
verify an agent's "Oracle reviewed this" claim by pulling the agent's Amp
thread from `ampcode.com` via the thread ID that is usually embedded in the
commit message, and confirming an Oracle-approval of the reviewed surface
actually exists in that thread.

This ticket is **born blocked on the operator** on purpose (label
`blocked-at-birth`): it is a research/scoping item you asked to *file*, not
to action now. Nothing runs it until you `unblock` it. It surfaces on the
[operator-blocked dashboard (#29)](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/29).

## Why this exists (context for a zero-context reader)

The approved design
[`docs/designs/operator-comms-ux-enforcement.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/operator-comms-ux-enforcement.md)
("mechanically enforce the operator-comms UX bar") argues, in its root-cause
section, that **"Oracle approved this" is an unverifiable claim in a gate
record, not a checkable fact** — so the design leans on a content-hash
registry instead of trusting the claim. ("Oracle" = our automated GPT-5
reviewer; a "gate record" is the Agent Gate Record every worker writes
citing what it reviewed; "canon" = the fleet-wide agent rulebook in
[`virusdave/top-level`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level).)

In [issue #30, comment 4922852664](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/30#issuecomment-4922852664)
you pushed back: the claim is **not strictly unverifiable**. The agent's Amp
thread ID is usually present in the commit message, and we could in principle
fetch that thread from `ampcode.com` and confirm an Oracle approval of the
surface exists in it. You noted two honest limits:

1. Confirming the surface **wasn't changed significantly afterwards** (or
   changed in a way that obsoleted the review) is probably not feasible.
2. This may not be worth the effort **until we actually see agents
   misreporting Oracle reviews** — which you have not yet observed (you read
   many).

So this is filed as a **deferred investigation**, not committed work.

## What a worker should do when unblocked

1. Confirm the mechanics: is a usable Amp thread ID reliably present in
   commit messages / gate records today? How stable is that convention?
2. Determine whether `ampcode.com` thread contents are fetchable by the
   fleet (auth, rate limits, API vs scrape) for a given thread ID.
3. Assess feasibility + cost of a check that: (a) extracts the thread ID,
   (b) fetches the thread, (c) confirms an Oracle-approval of the *specific*
   reviewed surface is present — and honestly documents the "was it changed
   after review?" gap you flagged.
4. Recommend go / no-go. If go, size it against the design's existing
   content-hash registry (does this *replace*, *complement*, or *not earn
   its keep* next to the hash-drift check?).

## Explicit non-goals / guardrails

- **Do not build the verifier off this ticket** without a fresh operator go;
  this is scoping only.
- Respect the operator's stated bar: **skip it unless there is evidence of
  agents misreporting Oracle reviews**, or a clear cheap win emerges.
- Read-only investigation; no production services, no prod data.

Related: [operator-comms UX enforcement, issue #30](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/30)

# Pilot: attested surface registry + drift guard, fixing the agent-waste notification

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#57](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/57)
> — "Implement operator-comms UX enforcement". Authoritative design:
> [`docs/designs/operator-comms-ux-enforcement.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/operator-comms-ux-enforcement.md).
>
> **Delegated because:** the agent-waste notification
> ([`scripts/waste-page`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/scripts/waste-page)),
> its formatting helpers, its tests, and the new
> `.well-known/operator-surfaces/` registry all live in
> [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker).
> `top-level` has no code to change for the pilot.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` for this epic MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#57`,
> plus this child epic's own `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`)
> trailer so the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this*
> delegated child.

## 1. Goal

Deliver the design's **pilot** (design §6): the first end-to-end slice of
the surface-enforcement mechanism, proving the shape on the operator's cited
concrete defect.

1. **Establish the registry format in-repo.** Add a `.well-known/operator-surfaces/`
   directory with one JSON entry per operator-facing surface (schema in
   design §4.1: `id`, `repo`, `channel`, `reviewed_input_closure`,
   `examples_dir`, `hash` canonicalization, `oracle_review{url,
   approved_hash, approved_at}`). Author the `agent-waste-page` entry.
2. **Build `operator-surface-guard`'s drift check** (design §4.2 check 1):
   recompute the content hash of the entry's reviewed **input closure**
   (renderer + helpers + fixtures + theme, not one file) plus the
   **CI-regenerated** representative examples, and fail if it differs from
   the recorded `approved_hash`. Two layers: a **pre-landing** run in the
   sanctioned completion path (real prevention) and a **post-push** CI
   backstop (design §4.2 "honest enforcement boundary"). **Never** gate on
   any registry host being at HEAD (design §8.2).
3. **Fix the notification template + register it.** Rework
   [`scripts/waste-page`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/scripts/waste-page)
   so the ~35-40% repeated boilerplate no longer truncates the actual waste
   explanation on mobile (design §1; canon `QUALITY_GATES.md`
   "do not let boilerplate crowd out or truncate the signal"). Get an
   **Oracle UI/UX review of the template plus representative rendered
   examples** (worst-case payloads, not one hand-picked instance) before
   first operator exposure, and record it in the `agent-waste-page` entry's
   `oracle_review`.

## 2. Current state (paths in this repo)

Read these first; the pilot slots into the existing shapes.

| Concern | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Notification builder | `scripts/waste-page` | Builds `title`/`body` (~L230-294) and the `page-dave` command; also builds a one-off detail page (`build_detail_md` ~L114-169, `publish_one_off` ~L171-211). The boilerplate defect is here. |
| Advisory catalog resolver | `lib/advisory-catalog.sh` | Resolves known advisory metadata. |
| Backlog exporter | `scripts/agent-waste-export` | Publishes the backlog NDJSON to `agent-pain-points`. |
| Tests | `tests/waste-page.sh` | Existing coverage; extend for the reworked template + representative-example regeneration. |

## 3. Scope (suggested leaves — the child-epic worker breaks this down)

1. Add the `.well-known/operator-surfaces/` registry schema + a small
   validator/loader; author the `agent-waste-page` entry (closure listing
   `scripts/waste-page`, its helpers, fixtures, any theme asset).
2. Add fixture-driven **representative example regeneration** for the
   agent-waste notification (worst-case payloads) so "what Oracle saw"
   cannot silently drift from what the code renders (design §4.1).
3. Implement `operator-surface-guard`'s drift check over the input closure +
   regenerated examples; wire the **pre-landing** layer into the completion
   path and the **post-push** CI backstop (reusable workflow shape so other
   repos can adopt it later). Include the registry-integrity check that a
   hash/closure change also updates `oracle_review` (design §4.1).
4. Rework the notification template to lead with the waste explanation and
   drop repeated boilerplate; extend `tests/waste-page.sh`; get the Oracle
   UI review; record `oracle_review` in the entry.

## 4. Non-goals (kept out of the pilot)

- The **emission-time lint + new-emitter detection** at the chokepoints is
  **Phase 2** (design §4.3), not here — except that the drift guard's
  new-emitter scan may land as a reusable piece if cheap.
- The **cross-repo fleet index** is **Phase 3** (design §8.2 layer 3).
- The **canon prune** is **Phase 4** (design §4.4), in `top-level`.
- Keep the lint **warn-only** where any lint appears (operator decision 3);
  do not hard-fail emission in the pilot.

## 5. Acceptance

- `.well-known/operator-surfaces/agent-waste-page.json` exists with a real
  `reviewed_input_closure`, CI-regenerated `examples_dir`, and a recorded
  `oracle_review` (URL + `approved_hash` + date).
- `operator-surface-guard` drift check runs **pre-landing and in CI**; a
  deliberate edit to any input-closure file fails it until the entry's
  review + hash are refreshed. No check requires any registry host at HEAD.
- The agent-waste notification leads with the waste explanation and fits the
  mobile-visible space without truncating it; `tests/waste-page.sh` covers
  the reworked template and passes; `master` stays green.
- An Agent Gate Record is attached, and every commit carries
  `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#57` + this child epic's `Issue:` trailer.

https://github.com/virusdave/task-dag/issues/13 was implemented as a meaningful rearchitecture of some core critical infrastructure.  Apparently though, it was only implemented and never actually applied and rolled out.

That's a crazy miss. Let's fix that now for every repo.  Have an epic task for the rollout that will be broken down per-repo, but prior to breakdown we should actually do a super-comprehensive multi-LLM review of the design, architecture, and implementation of the new system, looking for design flaws, invalid assumptions (any 3rdparty action that is assumed to always work under some specific condition), implementation errors, logical or natural gaps in tooling or functionality (ie, something a partially or mostly uninformed agent would perhaps assume exists and might reach for without actually checking, then have to thrash as it figures out what went wrong).  Anything that prevents this from being a comprehensive yet simple, principled, orthogonal, safe (in the sense of the canonical tooling enforces The Right Thing™ always and ideally makes it easy to do the typical next thing right without the invoking agent having to go hunt that next step down.

Use both Oracle and one of our more coding-enabled, highly advanced Bedrock-accessible models as well for this one-off holistic, potentially multi-pass review, and see if they are generally in agreement.  `page-dave` with a summary page the click-to-new-tabs to more details where useful.  This page should show me the meaningful ways in which they concur on the design or implementation, and where especially where they disagree  (if one of them is not CLEARLY wrong, perhaps because it doesn't know something that is ultimately contextually important) so the operator can assess and decide.  It is critical that all operator-facing surfaces satisfy our aggressively high canonical UX & Agent->Operator comms standards.  If you introduce a new operator-facing surface, even if it is temporary or throwaway, it must be optimized per canon and reviewed for fitness for standards by Oracle.

issues.body:
We seem to now have a pattern where a THING is requested, perhaps in a top level issue, and it's minted into an epic task, then broken down into a mini DAG and progressively implemented, completing tasks recursively back through the DAG until eventually the root epic task is satisfied and closed along with the GitHub issue the started it. 

One major problem: often just writing code to implement a thing in no way guarantees it'll be rolled out in a timely and safe fashion, if ever! 

Operator is ops of last resort and generally does not issue commands directly to the system.  Leaving some instructions within the repo, which the operator rarely if ever looks into, is for all practical purposes abandoning the responsibility to deploy the thing in a safe and time with fashion, which should generally be an implicit corollary through the initial development of a thing when I ask for a thing.

I would have thought that would be obvious but at this point it's recurring enough to clearly it's not. 

So now there are two tasks for you to do: create an GitHub issue to investigate, debug, and prevent this pattern. A small mandate that usually functionality request epics alignment be closed until the functionality is live and stable safely in production, thus usable, unless there's a strongly compelling, documented and approved reason why this can't happen.  Possibly one final leaf in the epic would be the deploy task, which could be blocked initially on many things, other tasks, operator approval, or nothing. Completing this task might be a non commit ops completion, not that's fine. The deployment must happen by default, and the request for thing isn't satisfied fully until it both exists and is usefully available in production as intended for its use.  Someone else should break that down and proceed.

Next you should create a claimed at birth epic for the skipped deploy half of the job, then break that down into one or more steps as needed, using the auto claim flag to claim the first unblocked new child, then proceed to handle the task appropriately

issues.body:
## Problem

Functionality request epics can currently appear "done" when code or docs have landed, even though the requested thing is not safely live, stable, and usable in production. That leaves deployment/rollout as implicit follow-up work, which agents can miss or abandon.

This repeats the failure mode called out in virusdave/top-level#60: the operator asked for a thing, agents implemented part of it, but the deploy/rollout half was not guaranteed by the task shape.

## Desired invariant

For ordinary functionality request epics, completion should mean the functionality exists **and** is usefully available in the intended production environment, with stability verified, unless there is a strongly compelling, documented, and operator-approved reason to stop before rollout.

A common task shape should make the final rollout/deploy/verification step explicit by default. It may be blocked initially on implementation, tests, downstream tasks, or operator approval, but it should not be omitted.

## Investigation scope

- Identify where the current task-dag / worker prompt / canon workflow permits an epic to close after code-only implementation.
- Decide whether the prevention belongs in canon, task-dag tooling, dispatcher prompts, issue templates, or all of them.
- Make the default decomposition for functionality epics include a live/stable rollout verification leaf when production availability is part of the request.
- Ensure an ops-only completion is expressible when the rollout action produces no implementation commit.
- Preserve legitimate exceptions: docs-only tasks, investigation-only tasks, explicitly non-deployable work, or cases with documented operator approval to stop before production rollout.

## Done criteria

- Future agents see a clear rule before closing functionality request epics.
- The task shape/tooling makes the deploy/rollout verification step hard to skip.
- Exceptions require a documented reason and, where appropriate, operator approval.
- A regression test or workflow check covers at least one epic that must not close before its rollout/verification leaf is complete.

Related: virusdave/top-level#59, virusdave/top-level#60.

issues.title: Prevent functionality epics from closing before rollout
