declarations.body:
# Helios signed readonly access — `automation` child epic

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#62](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/62)
> — "Need a means for local agents to access helios in trusted fashion".
> **Resolved design:** [`docs/epics/helios-agent-readonly-access/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](../../RESOLVED_DESIGN.md).
> **Delegated because:** the verifier, auth/session contracts, route gates,
> response caps, and audit logging live in `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` under
> `helios/`. Do not implement the NixOS key/config rollout or the agent-side
> browser helper in this child epic.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` for this epic MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#62`, plus
> this child epic's own `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer
> so the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to this delegated child.

## 1. Goal

Implement the **Helios-native** half of temporary, non-mutating, auditable live
verification for local agents. A local `amp-local` verifier will sign each
request with an Ed25519 private key; Helios verifies the request with configured
public keys, checks a narrow expiring allowlist, and then exposes only a
synthetic `agent_readonly` viewer principal.

This is not a general machine-to-machine API, not a write path, not a normal
operator login, and not a reason to weaken OAuth for real users.

## 2. Current state to inspect first (all paths under `helios/`)

| Concern | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Global auth gate | `src/server/auth/authGate.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) | Currently allows health/login/session/public endpoints and valid signed session cookies; all other app/API/asset paths are session-gated. Integrate signed-agent verification before the unauthenticated response, without adding broad public endpoints. |
| Session envelope + role gates | `src/server/auth/requireSession.ts` | `buildSessionEnvelope()` reads a signed cookie and DB user; `requireSessionUser()`, `requireMetricsGrant()`, `requireConfidentialMetricsGrant()`, and `requireCashierDisplayUser()` enforce downstream authorization. Add the explicit `agent_readonly` principal here, not a fake DB user or cookie. |
| Session contract | `src/shared/contracts/api/session.ts`, `src/server/routes/session.ts` | `authMode` is currently `anonymous | session`. Add `agent_readonly` and ensure `/api/session` returns a synthetic viewer envelope only for accepted signed-agent requests. |
| Permission helpers | `src/shared/domain/permissions.ts`, `src/shared/contracts/domain/auth.ts`, `src/server/auth/permissions.ts` | Reuse existing viewer permission semantics and role ordering; do not add editor/admin shortcuts for the synthetic principal. |
| Runtime config/env | `src/server/config/env.ts` | Add env/config parsing for public verifier keys, active allowlist JSON/path, timestamp skew, nonce cache sizing/TTL if needed, and default response byte cap. Keep private signing keys out of Helios config. |
| Server assembly | `src/server/app/buildServer.ts`, `src/server/main.ts` | Wire verifier/allowlist initialization through the existing app lifecycle. Signed-agent access must fail closed when config is absent or malformed. |
| Route tests/patterns | `src/server/auth/authGate.test.ts`, focused route tests under `src/server/routes/*.test.ts` | Extend existing `server.inject` patterns for accepted/denied signed requests and downstream gate denial. |
| Metrics/admin/cashier gates | `src/server/routes/metrics.ts`, `src/server/routes/catalogAnalytics.ts`, `src/server/routes/budtenderAnalytics.ts`, admin/config routes, cashier-display route using `requireCashierDisplayUser()` | Add focused coverage that `agent_readonly` can satisfy only viewer routes explicitly allowed by rule, and is denied for metrics grants, admin/config, cashier-display, and mutating routes. |

## 3. Design decisions to preserve

1. **Ed25519, not HMAC.** Helios stores public verifier keys only. A Helios
   config leak must not grant signing power.
2. **GET/HEAD only.** `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, and `OPTIONS` are denied
   before route handling, even with a valid signature and allowlist rule.
3. **No mixed credentials.** Any signed-agent request carrying `Cookie` or
   `Authorization` is rejected before route handling. Do not allow a real user
   session and an agent signature to combine.
4. **Signature covers the exact authorization decision.** The canonical payload
   covers method, host, exact path + query, timestamp, nonce, key id, and rule
   id. Reject ambiguous path/query encodings rather than silently normalizing
   them into an authorization decision.
5. **Narrow, expiring allowlist.** No `/api/*`, `/api/admin/*`, or page-rule
   implies API-rule behavior. Every rule has `not_before`, `not_after`, owner,
   reason, path entries, safe-read notes, and a response byte cap.
6. **Explicit `agent_readonly` principal.** Do not mint a cookie and do not
   create a `users` row. Viewer-only route code may see a synthetic viewer;
   editor/approver/admin, metrics grants, confidential metrics, and cashier
   display still deny.
7. **Metadata audit only.** Log accepted and denied signed requests with
   outcome/reason, key id, rule id, method, path, status, response bytes,
   remote/forwarded metadata, timestamp, and nonce. Never log private keys,
   signatures, cookies, authorization headers, or response bodies.
8. **Response caps are enforced in code.** Deny or abort oversized responses;
   do not rely on route authors or downstream clients to self-limit.

## 4. Request contract

Use a small explicit header set (names may change if implementation finds an
existing naming convention, but the semantics must stay):

| Header | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `X-Helios-Agent-Key-Id` | Selects the configured public verifier key. |
| `X-Helios-Agent-Rule-Id` | Selects the allowlist rule claimed by the request. |
| `X-Helios-Agent-Timestamp` | RFC3339 or Unix timestamp; reject outside a short 60–120s skew window. |
| `X-Helios-Agent-Nonce` | Random per request; reject replay within the skew window. |
| `X-Helios-Agent-Signature` | Base64url Ed25519 signature over the canonical payload. |

Canonical payload shape:

```text
helios-agent-readonly-v1
method:GET
host:helios.freshlybaked.us
path:/config/agent-waste?tab=pending
key_id:amp-local-vps3-2026q3
rule_id:agent-waste-review-2026-07-10
timestamp:2026-07-10T05:30:00Z
nonce:<128-bit random base64url>
```

Replay protection can be an in-memory per-process `(keyId, nonce)` cache for
v1. Document cross-process/cross-host replay within the short skew window as a
residual risk; do not add a DB/shared nonce store unless the implementation
task obtains the required review and operator approval.

## 5. Allowlist contract

Read allowlist rules from Helios runtime config provisioned by the NixOS child.
Example shape:

```json
{
  "id": "agent-waste-review-2026-07-10",
  "owner": "virusdave/top-level#62 rollout",
  "reason": "Verify the agent-waste review page after deploy and collect Oracle UI evidence.",
  "not_before": "2026-07-10T00:00:00Z",
  "not_after": "2026-07-17T00:00:00Z",
  "max_response_bytes": 1048576,
  "paths": [
    { "method": "GET", "kind": "page", "match": "exact", "path": "/config/agent-waste", "safe_read_note": "SPA route only; no write action." },
    { "method": "GET", "kind": "api", "match": "exact", "path": "/api/agent-waste/backlog", "safe_read_note": "Read-only backlog endpoint; no promote/write path." },
    { "method": "GET", "kind": "asset", "match": "prefix", "path": "/assets/", "safe_read_note": "Hashed Vite static assets only; byte-capped." },
    { "method": "GET", "kind": "session", "match": "exact", "path": "/api/session", "safe_read_note": "Returns synthetic agent_readonly envelope only." }
  ]
}
```

Implementation requirements:

- Prefer exact path matches. Prefix matches require segment-boundary checks and
  should normally be limited to hashed static assets.
- Page rules do not imply API rules; list every SPA loader/API call separately.
- API rules require route-specific safe-read notes because a `GET` handler can
  still trigger refreshes, external calls, streams, costly DB scans, cache
  writes, or large downloads.
- Deny streaming/SSE/download responses by default. Any future CSV/ZIP/report
  route needs an explicit rule and cap.
- Fail closed if allowlist JSON is absent, invalid, inactive, expired, or has an
  unknown kind/match shape.

## 6. Suggested implementation leaves

Author these as the child epic's own frontier leaves when the automation epic
root is broken down:

### H1 — Verifier + allowlist parser (no auth bypass yet)

- Add a small signed-readonly module, e.g. `src/server/auth/agentReadonly.ts`,
  that parses headers, builds the canonical payload, verifies Ed25519
  signatures using configured public keys, checks timestamp skew, rejects nonce
  replay, evaluates allowlist method/path/rule activity, and returns a typed
  accept/deny result with an audit reason.
- Add env/config parsing in `src/server/config/env.ts` for public verifier keys,
  allowlist JSON/path, skew, and default/max response cap. Helios must never
  read private signing material.
- Tests: canonical payload bytes, signature success/failure, unknown key, bad
  base64, missing headers, timestamp too old/too new, nonce replay, inactive
  rule, exact/prefix path matching, method mismatch, broad/invalid rule denial,
  and ambiguous path/query rejection.

### H2 — Auth gate integration + audit + byte caps

- Integrate the verifier into `authGate.ts` before unauthenticated redirects or
  401s. Accepted signed-agent requests should attach an `agent_readonly`
  principal to the request for downstream session code; denied signed attempts
  should return a flat 401/403-style response and should not fall through to a
  cookie path.
- Reject `Cookie` or `Authorization` on signed-agent requests before route
  handling.
- Enforce allowlist `max_response_bytes` for accepted signed-agent responses;
  abort/deny and audit `too_large` if the cap is exceeded. Ensure `HEAD` does
  not accidentally require a body to count bytes.
- Add structured log entries for accepted and denied signed-agent attempts,
  metadata only.
- Tests: `authGate.test.ts` accepted GET/HEAD, POST denied, mixed credentials
  denied, non-allowlisted page/API/asset denied, oversized response denied, and
  no signatures/secrets/cookies in logs.

### H3 — Session/principal contract

- Extend the session contract to `authMode: 'anonymous' | 'session' |
  'agent_readonly'`.
- Update `buildSessionEnvelope()` / `requireSessionUser()` so an accepted
  `agent_readonly` request returns a synthetic active viewer such as
  `agent-readonly@local.helios`, with viewer permissions and an empty
  `metricGrants` list, only where the caller asks for `viewer`.
- Ensure `requireSessionUser(..., 'editor' | 'approver' | 'admin')` denies, and
  `requireMetricsGrant()`, `requireConfidentialMetricsGrant()`, and
  `requireCashierDisplayUser()` deny because the synthetic viewer has no grants
  and is not a cashier-display allowlisted email.
- Tests: `/api/session` envelope for accepted signed-agent request;
  viewer-route success when explicitly allowlisted; editor/admin denial;
  metrics and cashier-display denial.

### H4 — Route-author docs and focused safe-read examples

- Add Helios docs for route authors describing how to decide whether a GET route
  is safe to allowlist, including hazards: writes hidden behind GET, cache or
  external refreshes, expensive scans, streaming/SSE/downloads, PII-heavy pages,
  and required byte caps.
- Include example allowlist snippets for the intended first verification page
  (`/config/agent-waste` plus its necessary loader/API/session/static asset
  routes), but keep them inactive/example-only unless the NixOS child has
  provisioned the real production config.
- Tests/docs review: verify docs explicitly say page rules do not imply API
  rules and private signing keys never belong in Helios config.

## 7. Out of scope for this child

- NixOS secrets/config rollout, nginx header stripping, optional loopback vhost,
  vps2/vps3 parity, and rollback commands live in the `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`
  child epic.
- The agent-side `fetch`/`render` helper, Playwright no-cookie context,
  per-request signing, local evidence bundle, and Oracle attachment workflow live
  in the agent-helper owner child (likely `Nicponskis/github-worker`).
- Live rollout verification is a later cross-repo leaf after Helios and NixOS
  changes are deployed through sanctioned paths. Do not fake it from unit tests.
- DB-backed audit or nonce storage is not part of v1. If implementation finds a
  DB change is necessary, stop for Oracle DB review and explicit operator go.

## 8. Gates and safety

- Follow `automation/AGENTS.md` dev-loop gates. Expected local checks for this
  Helios server/shared change:
  - `cd helios && npm run typecheck`
  - `cd helios && npm run typecheck:client` when the shared session contract or
    client-visible envelope changes
  - Focused Vitest runs for touched auth/session/route tests, e.g.
    `cd helios && npm run test -- src/server/auth/authGate.test.ts` plus any new
    verifier/require-session tests.
- No serving service restarts. Deploy, if a later implementation leaf reaches
  deployment, only via `self-deploy-helios` after push and per canon.
- No production DB writes or migrations for v1.
- Rollback is a normal revert + redeploy, and the NixOS side can separately
  expire/remove allowlist rules and public keys. With config absent or invalid,
  signed-agent access must fail closed while normal OAuth sessions keep working.

## 9. Acceptance criteria

- Helios has Ed25519 signed-agent verification with canonical payload tests.
- Signed-agent requests are accepted only for GET/HEAD, no Cookie, no
  Authorization, fresh timestamp, non-replayed nonce, valid key/signature,
  active allowlist rule, exact allowed path/query, and route-specific safe-read
  entry.
- Accepted requests expose `authMode: 'agent_readonly'` and a synthetic viewer,
  not a cookie or DB user.
- Viewer-only allowed routes can be read; mutating routes, admin/config,
  editor/approver/admin gates, metrics grants, confidential metrics, and
  cashier-display gates deny.
- Response byte caps are enforced and audited.
- Structured audit logs include metadata and deny reasons, never secrets,
  signatures, credentials, or response bodies.
- Route-author docs explain safe-read allowlisting and the page/API/asset/session
  split.
declarations.delegationNote: Implement the Helios-native signed readonly primitive from the resolved design: Ed25519 verifier, expiring narrow allowlist, explicit agent_readonly viewer principal/session envelope, GET/HEAD-only + no Cookie/Authorization, byte caps, metadata audit logs, route-author docs, and focused auth/session/metrics/admin/cashier denial tests. NixOS provisioning and agent helper are separate children.

declarations.body:
# Trusted read-only Helios agent access — `nixos-sbc` child epic

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#62](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/62)
> — "Need a means for local agents to access helios in trusted fashion".
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`virusdave/top-level` → `docs/epics/helios-agent-readonly-access/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/helios-agent-readonly-access/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit on
> [`Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc) `master`
> that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```text
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#62
> ```
>
> The final satisfying commit should also carry this child epic's own
> `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level
> completion aggregator can attribute the peer-repo completion to the delegated
> child issue.

## 1. Goal

Provision the production host wiring that lets local `amp-local` agents make
temporary, signed, read-only Helios verification requests after sanctioned
Helios deploys. This child owns only the NixOS / nginx / secret provisioning
slice of the resolved design; the Helios verifier and the agent-side helper
land in peer repos.

The result should make the Helios application receive enough configuration to
verify Ed25519-signed agent requests on both Helios-serving hosts, while keeping
private signing material restricted to the local agent user and making every
allowlist extension reviewable through `nixos-sbc` git history.

## 2. Why this is operator-gated

This work introduces a production signing key that can unlock OAuth-gated
read-only Helios pages when combined with a live allowlist rule. Workers may
prepare the Nix code, config shape, and verification commands, but generating,
installing, or rotating the private key material is security-sensitive and must
use the fleet secrets process with operator approval.

Do **not** commit private keys, plaintext secrets, or sample secrets. If secret
material is not already supplied through agenix or a host-local root action,
block the task and page the operator with the exact key names, intended owners,
and target hosts.

## 3. Scope owned by `nixos-sbc`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **`amp-local` signing private key** | Provision an Ed25519 private key only where local agents run today: vps-nixos-3. Materialise it as a real file owned by `amp-local`, group `agents` only if needed for operator inspection, mode `0400` or stricter. Prefer a stable path such as `/home/amp-local/.secret/helios-agent-readonly/signing-key` or another path exposed to the agent-helper child. It must not be readable by `helios`, must not appear in the Nix store, and must not be passed through systemd environment variables. Private signing keys do **not** need to exist on vps-nixos-2 unless agents are intentionally run there later. |
| **Public verifier key(s)** | Provision matching public verifier key metadata for the Helios server on **both** vps-nixos-3 (primary) and vps-nixos-2 (backend-only mirror). Public keys may live in Nix config or a non-secret environment/config file, but keep key IDs explicit, stable, and documented (for example `amp-local-vps3-2026q3`). |
| **Expiring allowlist** | Provision the active agent-readonly allowlist into the Helios server config on both vps-nixos-3 and vps-nixos-2. Every rule must include `id`, `owner`, `reason`, `not_before`, `not_after`, `max_response_bytes`, and route-specific safe-read notes. Prefer exact path entries; use prefix rules only for narrow static-asset paths with segment-boundary checks handled by Helios. No broad `/api/*`, admin, metric-grant, cashier-display, or indefinite rules. |
| **Helios env/config plumbing** | Add `services.helios` options or `extraEnvironment` entries (whichever best matches the Helios child implementation) for the public verifier-key config and allowlist config. Keep primary and backend-only mirror config in parity, because public traffic may be served by either backend during `self-deploy-helios` windows. |
| **Public nginx header stripping** | Ensure the public `helios.freshlybaked.us` nginx vhost strips inbound `X-Helios-Agent-*` headers before proxying to Helios unless the Helios implementation intentionally verifies raw client headers itself. The goal is that internet clients cannot smuggle trusted agent headers through nginx. Use explicit `proxy_set_header X-Helios-Agent-… "";` lines for the final header names from the Helios child. |
| **Optional loopback-only vhost** | If the implementation chooses a loopback-only agent vhost/port as defense-in-depth, expose it only on loopback, never publicly. Only that vhost may forward the `X-Helios-Agent-*` headers to Helios. Public nginx must still strip them. The loopback vhost is not the auth model; Helios signature, freshness, no-cookie/no-authorization, and allowlist checks remain mandatory. |
| **Backend bind/firewall verification** | Verify how `helios-server` binds on vps-nixos-3 and vps-nixos-2 and whether direct backend access is reachable outside loopback. Tighten bind/firewall behavior if the existing module permits unintended direct public/LAN access, but do not rely on bind tightening as the only protection. |
| **Permissions and comments** | Keep comments near every key/allowlist entry explaining parent `virusdave/top-level#62`, expiry, owner, and how to extend or remove access. Future extension must require a normal git review and deploy. |

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- Depends on the `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` child defining the exact Helios
  config contract: public-key env/config format, allowlist env/config format,
  and final `X-Helios-Agent-*` header names.
- Blocks live verification until the agent-helper child can sign requests using
  the provisioned private key path.
- The vps-nixos-2 mirror config must land before declaring rollout complete;
  vps3-only success is incomplete because self-deploy mirror windows can serve
  requests from vps2.

## 5. Suggested implementation shape

1. Add `services.helios.agentReadonly` options in `modules/helios.nix` if the
   Helios child expects structured config, or wire the agreed env vars through
   `services.helios.extraEnvironment` in `hosts/per-host/vps-nixos-{2,3}.nix` if
   that is smaller and clearer.
2. Register any required agenix secrets in `secrets.nix`:
   - private signing key secret for vps-nixos-3 only, owned by `amp-local`,
     mode `0400`;
   - only if the Helios implementation wants verifier/allowlist as secret-ish
     files, corresponding host-specific `.age` entries for both vps-nixos-3 and
     vps-nixos-2. Prefer non-secret Nix config for public verifier keys and
     allowlist metadata unless there is a concrete reason to hide them.
3. Materialise the vps3 private key through the existing per-host secret helper
   pattern in `hosts/per-host/vps-nixos-3.nix`, not through a systemd
   environment variable.
4. Add public-nginx header stripping in the Helios nginx vhost generated by
   `modules/helios.nix`. If adding an optional loopback-only vhost, keep its
   config adjacent and document that it is defense-in-depth only.
5. Add parity comments/checks so vps-nixos-2 receives the same public verifier
   keys and active allowlist rules as vps-nixos-3.

## 6. Acceptance

- `nix flake check` or the repo's equivalent targeted Nix eval/build gate is
  green for the touched hosts/modules, or any skipped heavy gate is justified in
  the Agent Gate Record.
- The `amp-local` private signing key exists on vps-nixos-3 at the documented
  path, is owned by `amp-local`, is mode `0400` or stricter, and is not readable
  by the `helios` service user.
- Helios on both vps-nixos-3 and vps-nixos-2 receives the same public verifier
  key ID(s) and the same active expiring allowlist rules.
- Public nginx strips the final `X-Helios-Agent-*` header set before proxying
  internet-originated traffic to Helios.
- If a loopback-only vhost is added, it binds only to loopback and is the only
  nginx path that forwards agent headers.
- Backend bind/firewall behavior is explicitly verified and recorded.
- After the Helios verifier and agent helper are deployed, live verification
  from `amp-local` proves:
  - a whitelisted page route renders;
  - a whitelisted loader/API route returns;
  - a non-whitelisted route denies;
  - `POST`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` deny even with a valid signature;
  - signed requests containing `Cookie` or `Authorization` deny;
  - vps-nixos-2 has the same public key/allowlist behavior during a mirror
    window or an equivalent controlled mirror-host probe;
  - logs contain metadata only, not signatures, cookies, private keys, or
    response bodies.

## 7. Safety / rollback

Apply production changes only through the sanctioned `nixos-sbc` deploy path
(`self-deploy` / `self-deploy-helios` as appropriate for the final change). Do
not manually restart `nginx`, `helios-server`, or `helios-worker`.

Rollback is deliberately simple and does not require DB cleanup:

1. expire or remove the allowlist rule(s);
2. remove the public verifier key config from both Helios hosts;
3. remove the vps3 `amp-local` private-key secret/materialisation if access is
   being fully retired;
4. redeploy via the sanctioned wrapper;
5. verify signed requests now fail closed while normal OAuth login and Helios
   health checks still pass.

The Nix change is additive until the allowlist becomes active. Reverting the
implementation commit and redeploying removes the access path; the Helios child
must still enforce its own fail-closed behavior when config is absent.

## 8. Out of scope

- Implementing the Helios Ed25519 verifier, request principal, allowlist parser,
  response byte caps, or audit logging — owned by `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`.
- Implementing the agent fetch/render helper — likely owned by
  `Nicponskis/github-worker` unless that child chooses a different existing home.
- Granting write access, creating real Helios users/cookies, broad API access,
  metric grants, cashier-display access, or operator impersonation.
- Publishing captured HTML/CSS/screenshots to public hosts.
- Any production DB write, schema migration, or Helios data backfill.
declarations.delegationNote: Provision amp-local Ed25519 signing key, Helios public verifier keys and expiring allowlist on vps-nixos-3/vps-nixos-2, nginx agent-header handling, mirror parity, deployment verification, and rollback for trusted read-only Helios agent access.

issues.body:
## Problem

Issue #59 reached a legitimate completed state, but none of the sanctioned task-dag epic closers could express it.

Observed state:

- The rollout was made useful and safely available for the participating repos.
- All live rollout leaves were completed, or explicitly deferred/dropped as non-participating optional repos.
- The final no-code confirmation leaf was completed with `task-dag complete-ops` at `4c66968`.
- `task-dag validate --strict` passed with 0 warnings.

But closure tooling failed closed:

- `task-dag close-epic --issue 59` refused because the epic had no delegated children to gate on.
- `task-dag close-ops-epic --issue 59 --yes ...` refused because the epic was decomposed and had DAG child tasks.
- `task-dag graph-converge` over the final ops completion emitted no close fact.

The operator approved a one-off `gh issue close 59 --reason completed` because the issue should be closed by rights. That manual close should remain exceptional; this issue tracks adding a sanctioned task-dag path for the same state.

## Desired support

Add a sanctioned task-dag closer for a decomposed epic whose DAG children are all satisfied/completed/superseded/dropped as no-longer-participating, with no remaining frontier/active/blocked work, and whose rollout/done criteria have been explicitly recorded.

Possible shape:

- `task-dag close-completed-epic --issue N --yes --reason "..."`, or
- teach `task-dag complete-ops` / final-child completion / graph convergence to emit the existing `Closes-Epic: #N` merge when the reconciler proves the decomposed epic is complete.

## Guard rails

The command should fail closed unless it can prove:

1. `tasks/pending/<N>` exists on origin and matches the epic root.
2. The epic is decomposed, but has no remaining pickable, active, blocked, or unresolved child work.
3. Every DAG child is completed/satisfied/superseded, or was explicitly dropped/deferred as non-participating with durable issue trail evidence.
4. For functionality epics, rollout/useful-availability evidence is present or an operator-approved exception is cited.
5. The close action emits the normal tool-built tree-equal merge with `Closes-Epic: #N`, not a hand-authored merge or raw ref edit.
6. The operation is idempotent and race-safe like `close-epic` / `close-ops-epic`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add tests/fixtures covering the #59-like state: decomposed epic, all children done/deferred, no delegated children, no live work, issue still open.
- The sanctioned command closes that state by producing the standard `Closes-Epic: #N` merge.
- Existing guards still reject incomplete decomposed epics, blocked leaves, active claims, and unresolved delegated children.
- Update `docs/task_dag/EPIC_CLOSURE.md` and the relevant task-dag docs to describe when to use the new path.

We definitely need to fix the design.

```
Separate latent bug: dispatcher CLI refresh is broken                                                                                                                               █
                                                                                                                                                                                     █
 The workers started with task-dag commit ba74d75; current task-dag is 50f37ba.                                                                                                      █
                                                                                                                                                                                     █
 ensure_taskdag_cli intends to refresh hourly, but startup exports the managed path as TASK_DAG_BIN. Every later call sees TASK_DAG_BIN set and mistakes it for an explicit          █
 operator override, returning before its TTL refresh logic. Thus workers remain on their startup CLI indefinitely.                                                                   █
                                                                                                                                                                                     █
 This did not cause today’s zero-work result—the current CLI produces the same result against the authoritative mirrors—but it is a genuine semantic split-brain risk. The code      █
 needs to remember whether an override was supplied before initialization, rather than inferring that from its own exported variable.                                                █
                                                                                                                                                                                     █
 Bottom line                                                                                                                                                                         █
                                                                                                                                                                                     █
 Your concern is correct:                                                                                                                                                            █
                                                                                                                                                                                     █
 - The visible closed-task loop is mostly stale-ref noise.                                                                                                                           █
 - The apparently idle fleet genuinely has no visible claimable work.                                                                                                                █
 - It should have had work from your recent comments.                                                                                                                                █
 - Those comments were dropped by failed one-shot GitHub Actions runs.                                                                                                               █
 - There is no durable comment replay/reconciliation mechanism.                                                                                                                      █
 - That is an unsafe assumption and should be fixed as a delivery-guarantee problem, not with more ad hoc retries.                                                                   
 - ```

1) If we have a local repo mirror for refs, it needs to update maybe once per minute or two, not hourly.
2) Alongside the mirror, we should probably track the time of latest successful fetch attempt (even if it was a no-op), so workers can detect a long-stuck mirror and just use their own ephemeral copy of the repo(s), using canonical task-dag tooling inside of those repos to pull the various required objects and refs.
3) The holistic design appears to rely in some cases on a thirdparty tool always successfully working, which is a guaranteed-false assumption.  In particular, it seems as though at least some issue operator comments can become permanently stranded when the repo's worker / action fails to complete successfully for any reason.  This is a quite significant design flaw if there's not a relatively rapid backup process that could detect this and fix it.

      "issue": 18,
      "note": "Implement origin-atomic comment receipts and effects, reusable reconciliation, coherent event tooling, deterministic race and recovery tests, and strict validation/documentation."

}
```

declarations.body:
# task-dag child epic: durable comment reconciliation

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#64`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/64)
· Binding design:
[`durable-dispatch-input-recovery.md`](../../../../designs/durable-dispatch-input-recovery.md)

## Goal

Make GitHub issue-comment delivery at-least-once and idempotent. The existing
event workflow remains fast, but a canonical reconciler can recover any
eligible comment still present in GitHub even when that event or workflow was
lost.

## Required implementation

1. **Receipt contract and compatibility**
   - Define well-formed human, completion, and machine-skip provenance under
     `gh/comments/<issue>/<comment-id>`.
   - New receipts identify repository, issue, comment ID, disposition,
     `created_at`, observed `updated_at`, and body SHA-256.
   - Accept existing human/completion provenance as immutable legacy shapes.
   - Update known-namespace validation, lifecycle documentation, and golden
     fixtures in the same change.

2. **Origin-authoritative atomic ingestion**
   - Check origin receipt before classifying current content; an unpushed local
     ref is never terminal.
   - Human comments atomically create receipt plus frontier with create-only
     leases. Completion comments atomically create receipt plus completion
     fact when needed. Marked comments create receipt only.
   - Install local refs only after remote success.
   - On races, validate the origin winner. Same observed body with a different
     disposition is fatal; a different observed version is superseded by the
     first valid winner.
   - A failed multi-ref transaction cannot leave half a disposition.

3. **Canonical `reconcile-comments` command**
   - Use the same classifier as event ingestion.
   - Support recent overlapping and complete-audit modes, dry-run, bounded
     apply batches, `ingestion_start_at`, and explicit historical
     `(issue, comment-id)` allowlists.
   - Enumerate with stable ascending updated order and full pagination; filter
     by `created_at`; exclude pull requests from authoritative issue metadata.
   - Fetch allowlisted historical comments directly by ID.
   - First successfully observed version wins; later edits do not remint.
   - Continue past poison comments but return nonzero and a failed heartbeat.
   - Honor rate-limit headers and never claim completeness after truncation or
     an API/classification failure.
   - Run idempotent post-scan convergence so a completion fact whose immediate
     close attempt failed still reaches the existing backstop.

4. **Coherent event runtime**
   - Replace split raw-file downloads with one checkout at one resolved
     task-dag revision. Keep the reusable workflow logic-free for callers.
   - Preserve the current App-token close semantics and least permissions.

5. **Metrics and operator contract**
   - Emit requests/pages/all returned comments, eligibility and disposition
     counts, failures, duration, rate-limit state, and recent/full success
     heartbeat data in machine-readable output.
   - A capacity ceiling fails loudly and directs sharding; it never truncates
     silently.

## Required tests

- Event versus sweep race yields one provenance and one task effect.
- Injected push failure yields neither half of a human disposition.
- Race loser ignores local-only state, validates a matching origin winner,
  rejects conflicting same-version disposition, and accepts a superseding
  different observed version.
- Marked comment creates one skip receipt and no frontier.
- Completion receipt/fact is atomic; failed derived close is later converged.
- Multi-page scans with equal timestamps and strict-`since` overlap omit
  nothing; page failure does not mark success.
- Pull-request and pre-boundary comments are excluded; explicit historical
  allowlist comments are fetched directly.
- Edits, malformed comments, legacy provenance, 403/429, dry-run, bounded
  batches, and capacity ceilings follow the binding design.
- `task-dag validate --strict` and the full task-dag presubmit pass.

## Rollout and rollback

Land receipt/atomicity support before any watchdog can emit new shapes. Verify
the event path recognizes both legacy and new receipts. Publish the reconciler
disabled until github-worker dry-runs each repository's first audit.

Rollback removes or disables the reconciler/event-runtime change without
rewriting refs. Valid additive receipts remain recognized audit evidence.

This is critical infrastructure. Obtain Oracle design review before coding and
Oracle diff review after implementation; iterate to APPROVE before commit.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#64
```
declarations.delegationNote: Implement origin-atomic comment receipts and effects, reusable reconciliation, coherent event tooling, deterministic race and recovery tests, and strict validation/documentation.
declarations.title: Make GitHub comment delivery durable and idempotent

declarations.body:
# github-worker child epic: strict dispatcher freshness and recovery

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#64`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/64)
· Binding design:
[`durable-dispatch-input-recovery.md`](../../../../designs/durable-dispatch-input-recovery.md)

## Goal

Keep dispatcher inputs observably current and recover from prolonged local
mirror or event-delivery failures without ever authorizing work from stale
state.

## Required implementation

1. **Verified mirror success evidence**
   - Fetch task refs plus default history atomically under the existing
     per-repository lock, verify `HEAD`, then atomically publish repository,
     remote fingerprint, completion time, `HEAD` SHA, and task-ref snapshot
     hash.
   - Store attempts/errors separately. Failure, malformed/future metadata, or
     remote changes do not advance success.
   - Continue roughly minute-scale polling. A failed current fetch always
     skips that repository for the cycle; the last-good mirror is never a
     dispatch authorization source.

2. **Strict prolonged-failure fallback**
   - After the configurable default 180-second success-age threshold, create
     at most one host-wide, per-repository-locked, full-history temporary bare
     clone with cooldown/backoff.
   - Strictly fetch and verify before canonical task-dag
     `frontier --no-fetch` / `roots --no-fetch`. Any uncertainty produces no
     candidate or claim.
   - Strictly refresh and recompute again before spawn.
   - Trap-own a selected fallback through claim, agent handoff,
     block/release/retirement, signals, and exit. Remove unselected fallbacks
     after scanning. Never copy fallback state to the primary mirror.

3. **Managed task-dag CLI mode fix**
   - At module source, distinguish a non-empty explicit `TASK_DAG_BIN`
     override from managed mode. A bad explicit override fails with no network
     fallback; a valid one stays pinned.
   - Managed exports never become overrides. Track attempt/success and
     backoff, build and validate a coherent checkout, then publish/export an
     exact immutable `versions/<commit>/` path.
   - Keep last-good on failure. Retain all versions initially; do not delete by
     age. Any future GC needs invocation leases and separate review.
   - Log mode, commit, success age, attempt/error, and backoff.

4. **Independent comment watchdog**
   - Under one host lease, invoke task-dag's canonical reconciler for every
     registry repo approximately every two minutes with a 15-minute overlap.
   - Run a complete audit daily and at startup when its success heartbeat is
     stale.
   - Configure per-repository `ingestion_start_at` and explicit reviewed
     historical allowlist; first full run is dry-run and bounded.
   - Monitor heartbeat independently from GitHub Actions. Bound duration,
     pagination, concurrent repos, and rate use. Never replace task-dag's
     classifier or receipt semantics in github-worker.

5. **Configuration and operations**
   - Ship fallback and watchdog disabled, with documented flags, thresholds,
     metrics, alerts, and rollback.
   - Keep existing origin claim compare-and-swap and pre-spawn verification.
   - Use the canonical task-dag checkout, never a vendored fallback.

## Required tests

- Successful atomic fetch advances success metadata; partial/failing fetch
  changes neither verified snapshot nor success time.
- A block added after last success can never spawn during later fetch failures.
- Under-threshold failure skips; over-threshold concurrent workers construct
  one fallback; fallback fetch failure produces no claim.
- Selected fallback survives pre-spawn reverify, release, retirement, signal,
  and cleanup paths. Primary recovery resumes without copying fallback state.
- Remote URL change, malformed/future timestamp, and concurrent claims fail
  safely.
- Valid explicit CLI override performs zero network; invalid override fails;
  managed first clone, pre-TTL call, successful/failed post-TTL refresh,
  backoff, candidate validation, concurrency, immutable publication, and logs
  are deterministic.
- Watchdog recent/full cadence, stale heartbeat startup, host lease, dry-run,
  bounded apply, task-dag failure, and rate-limit behavior are covered without
  production resources.
- Repository light checks and full final presubmit pass.

## Rollout and rollback

After the task-dag child is live, deploy this code disabled. Review first-audit
dry-run counts per repository, enable recent reconciliation, then bounded full
audits, and enable mirror fallback last. Roll only via github-worker's
canonical deployment path.

Production verification deliberately suppresses a test event and injects
isolated git-remote failures; it does not touch serving services or databases.
Rollback disables watchdog/fallback and selects the previous immutable CLI
version while preserving additive receipts.

This is critical infrastructure. Obtain Oracle design review before coding and
Oracle diff review after implementation; iterate to APPROVE before commit.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#64
```

## Immediate outcome

Repair the currently red `virusdave/top-level` master branch first. The Agent Prompt Budget gate is enforcing obsolete guidance: task-dag now provides the sanctioned `complete-ops` command for evidence-backed, operations-only leaf completion, but top-level's worker guidance and issue-interaction model still say that no no-code child-completion path exists.

The repair must remove the stale prompt-budget assertions, prune the superseded guidance, and replace it with concise direction to use `complete-ops`, while preserving the valid requirement that functionality epics include rollout/stability verification and never use fake or tombstone commits. Add regression coverage for the current contract rather than weakening the rollout guard.

Failing run: https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/actions/runs/29109741477

When this epic is decomposed, this repair leaf must be the first dependency-ready child and must be born self-claimed by the decomposing worker.

## Durable broken-master response

Design and implement a robust response whenever an authoritative branch is broken or policy considers it broken. Existing task-dag `classify`, repair-chain, and `repair-ticket` machinery must be investigated and reused rather than duplicated.

A GitHub Actions run is an at-most-once hint for a particular commit, not a delivery guarantee: it may fail, be cancelled, never start, or lose a downstream API write. The design must keep durable source evidence, use idempotent reconciliation/backstop processing independent of the one-shot event, and reliably converge to exactly one open high-priority repair epic/task per active red streak. It must recover after interruption at every boundary, avoid duplicate tasks under concurrency, close only on authoritative green evidence, expose stale/failed reconciliation telemetry, and document rollout and rollback.

This is critical fleet coordination infrastructure. Oracle must approve the architecture before implementation and the final diff afterward. Publish the approved design as a self-contained, styled one-off and page the operator with that page before implementation proceeds.

## One-offs service durability and discovery

Audit the canonical one-offs service implementation and ownership. If its maximum page lifetime is 24 hours, raise the supported upper limit to seven days. Preserve shorter caller-selected lifetimes and enforce a bounded maximum.

Provide a canonical index URL for currently live one-offs if one does not already exist. Define authoritative live/expired semantics, safe concurrent publication and expiry cleanup, privacy/access behavior, bounded index cost, and rollback. The index must not resurrect expired pages or become a second mutable source of truth.

The index is an operator-facing product surface. Oracle must approve its information architecture, mobile usability, signal-to-noise, zero-context labels, direct next actions, empty/error/expired states, and representative rendered output before first exposure. Include this design in the same self-contained one-off report and operator page described above.

## Completion criteria

- Top-level master is green, with stale gate assertions removed rather than obsolete prose restored or the valid rollout guard weakened.
- Broken-master detection and repair-ticket creation recover from missed, failed, duplicated, and interrupted Actions runs without relying on an event being delivered exactly once.
- Exactly one repair epic/task remains discoverable for each active red streak until authoritative green evidence closes it.
- One-offs support a seven-day upper lifetime and have one canonical, Oracle-approved live index.
- Targeted deterministic tests, full final gates, production rollout through canonical paths, stability evidence, telemetry, and rollback verification are complete.
- This functionality epic remains open until the durable repair flow and one-offs changes are live and verified.

# task-dag child epic: durable broken-master convergence

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Make the existing repair-chain state machine converge from durable GitHub
evidence even when a push-triggered Actions run is missed, duplicated, or dies
between side effects. Keep task-dag's chain ref authoritative and converge to
exactly one open repair issue and one discoverable repair task for each active
policy-red streak.

## Required implementation

1. **One canonical reconciler**
   - Add `repair-reconcile <owner/repo> <branch>` as the bounded entry point
     shared by Actions hints and the host backstop.
   - Reuse and extend `classify`, `tree-fix-outcome`, `verify-target`, repair
     chains, and `repair-ticket`; do not add another classifier or state store.
   - Resolve the current top-level registry generation internally before every
     mutation. Implement strict `off|observe|enforce` semantics and fenced
     downgrade cleanup exactly as specified by the binding design.

2. **Strict evidence and policy**
   - Validate `.github/ci-repair-policy.json`, bind required checks to exact
     names and App identities, paginate check runs, and select reruns by the
     design's deterministic lifecycle tuple.
   - Persist canonical bounded evidence, first-seen grace state, policy digest,
     evidence/decision keys, aggregate, and reconciliation diagnostics in the
     existing chain history. Identical decisions are no-ops.
   - Only current-head required-check evidence may close a chain. Unknown,
     malformed policy, API failure, stale green, and identity mismatch fail
     closed.

3. **Lease, fencing, and convergence**
   - Add metadata-only reconciliation lease acquisition/renewal that preserves
     every classifier field and uses monotonically increasing fences.
   - Fence every issue, comment, task-ingestion, and scheduling-ref mutation;
     perform post-mutation readback and compensate stale accepted HTTP effects.
   - Keep the oldest matching repair issue canonical, close extras, retire all
     duplicate scheduling projections through a repair-specific validated
     operation, and retain the specified non-scheduling audit ref.
   - Make issue and continuation-comment ingestion directly replayable by
     reconciliation, with stable repair/attempt identities and existing
     `verify-target` protection for already-launched workers.
   - Preserve one blocked high-priority repair object for `blocked`,
     `policy-invalid`, and `non-fast-forward`; only authoritative green closes
     it.

4. **Contracts and telemetry**
   - Update chain parsers, namespace validation, invariant documentation,
     golden fixtures, CLI help, dry-run output, and migration compatibility for
     old `creating@…` leases.
   - Emit the bounded structured pass fields and error codes required by the
     design. Never log tokens, check output, issue bodies, or one-off content.

## Deterministic tests

Use temporary bare origins and a fake paginated GitHub API. Cover missing and
delayed runs around grace, accepted/failed checks and reruns, duplicate names,
pagination, GitHub `Date` clock-skew rejection, old-head green/red, policy edits
and malformed policy, API outage, registry rollback, and rejection of
caller-supplied generation or mode. Cover `observe→enforce` replay of an
existing decision and `enforce→observe|off` races with stale callers, late
accepted HTTP effects, and refusal to delete or retarget a registry row until
successful `off` cleanup readback. Exercise every lease-loss and interruption
boundary, expired-holder overlap, transient zero-object windows, missed
issue/comment events, duplicate issue/task convergence, blocked-chain
preservation, continuation deduplication, tree-fix outcomes, and non-fast-
forward heads. Add a property test over event order, stale holders, and crash
points proving eventual one-chain/one-open-ticket/one-discoverable-task
convergence. Run `task-dag validate --strict` and full task-dag presubmit.

## Rollout and rollback

Land inert. Complete credential preflight and a 24-hour dry-run comparison
before any projection is enabled. Then support observe-only chain writes,
followed by projection for task-dag and top-level, missed-run/crash drills, and
48 hours of stable evidence before peer expansion.

Rollback disables callers first and preserves chain refs/issues. Never run an
old `repair-ticket` against a new active substate. Any downgrade to legacy
requires the binding design's compare-and-set migration and readback; never
delete coordination refs or tickets as rollback.

This is critical fleet infrastructure. The binding architecture already has
Oracle approval, but the implementation worker must get Oracle architecture
rereview for any design change and Oracle review of the actual final diff
before commit. Iterate to APPROVE.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```

# nixos-sbc child epic: supervise durable repair reconciliation

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Package and supervise the github-worker repair reconciler and its independent
watchdog on the production host, with encrypted least-privilege credentials,
durable state, safe rollout controls, and a reversible deployment.

## Required implementation

1. Package the reviewed github-worker reconciler/watchdog and one coherent
   canonical task-dag runtime. Do not vendor or reimplement either system.
2. Add `github-worker-repair-reconciler.service` and the separately supervised
   watchdog with the binding design's five-minute jittered cadence, pool of
   four, 30-second restart delay, five-minute start-limit window, durable state
   directories, and bounded resource/sandbox settings.
3. Provision the shared GitHub App ID/private key through age-encrypted systemd
   credentials. Tokens must remain ephemeral and must not enter the Nix store,
   environment dumps, logs, command lines, or persistent state.
4. Package `page-dave` for the watchdog and preserve the single-writer split
   between reconciler `status.json` and watchdog `watchdog.json`.
5. Expose service, dry-run, projection-rollout, and paging kill switches plus
   documented inspection, telemetry, credential-preflight, rollout, rollback,
   and failure procedures. These controls must never override repository
   enrollment: `off|observe|enforce` comes only from current top-level
   `repos.conf` authority.

## Verification

- Nix evaluation/build and unit tests prove command wiring, credentials,
  sandboxing, restart policy, state ownership, disabled defaults, and rollback
  selection without starting a production unit.
- Integration tests use fake GitHub/task-dag endpoints and disposable state;
  no test targets production resources.
- After both code-owning child epics are Oracle-approved and landed, deploy
  only through the canonical `self-deploy*` path. Never manually restart,
  stop, or kill the units.

## Rollout and rollback

Deploy disabled, verify rendered units and credentials, and support the
top-level child's preflight/dry-run and staged observe/enforce rollout. Runtime
rollback disables the new units/controls and selects the previous immutable
packages; it preserves chain refs, repair issues/tasks, and status evidence.
Retain a new-format-compatible task-dag until no active new-format chain
remains. Selecting an older incompatible package first requires the reviewed
compare-and-set migration of every active substate to legacy-safe `State=red`
and readback proving no issue/task will close. Record active red chains before
rollback. A normal git revert remains the configuration rollback path only
after that compatibility gate is satisfied.

This is production control-plane infrastructure. The binding architecture
already has Oracle approval, but the implementation worker must get Oracle
architecture rereview for any design change and Oracle review of the actual
final diff before commit and deployment. Iterate to APPROVE.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```

# github-worker child epic: repair reconciler and watchdog

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Provide typed, bounded host orchestration for task-dag's canonical
`repair-reconcile` command and independently detect stale or failed convergence.
github-worker must not duplicate repair classification, desired state, or
ticket semantics.

## Required implementation

1. **Typed reconciler command**
   - Read top-level's current `master` and `repos.conf` through GitHub, accept
     only equal/descendant registry generations, and enumerate only explicitly
     enrolled repositories.
   - Run five-minute jittered sweeps with a bounded pool of four. Invoke one
     coherent canonical task-dag revision and its `repair-reconcile`; never
     reproduce classifier or projection logic in github-worker.
   - Mint short-lived single-repository GitHub App installation tokens with
     only the binding design's permissions, refresh at 80 percent of lifetime,
     and keep credentials out of config, disk, logs, and command lines.
   - Fail closed with named preflight errors for installation, label,
     permission, clone, policy, or token failures.

2. **Durable status and independent watchdog**
   - Atomically replace `status.json` after each repository with registry
     commit/blob, sweep state, per-repository success/error, active-red identity,
     projection age, counters, gauges, and bounded incident keys.
   - Add a separately supervised watchdog as the sole writer of
     `watchdog.json`. It reads status every five minutes, invokes the packaged
     `page-dave`, persists attempts/results/recoveries, and implements the
     exact stale observation, pending projection, lease, duplicate, and invalid
     policy thresholds from the design.
   - Prefer at-least-once incident notification across a crash; notification
     deduplication is never repair desired-state authority.
   - Emit structured journald events without credentials, check output, issue
     bodies, or one-off contents.

3. **Configuration and lifecycle**
   - Ship orchestration, projection, and paging controls disabled. Document
     cadence, concurrency, state files, preflight, metrics, alerts, dry-run,
     enablement, restart behavior, and rollback.
   - Keep all git and API operations bounded and cancellation-safe. A stopped
     process leaves only durable task-dag state for the next pass to resume.

## Deterministic tests

Use fake registry/GitHub/task-dag boundaries and temporary state directories.
Cover registry generation rollback, malformed enrollment, bounded concurrency,
token mint/refresh/failure and redaction, partial sweeps, restart at every
handoff, atomic status replacement, stale status, every incident threshold,
page attempt crash windows, recovery, task-dag nonzero/timeout, and disabled/
dry-run/enabled controls. No test may contact production.

## Rollout and rollback

The task-dag child must land first. Deploy this code disabled through
github-worker's canonical deployment path. Run credential preflight and the
24-hour dry-run, then support observe-only and the two-repository projection
canary. The nixos-sbc child owns production unit/credential provisioning; the
top-level child owns fleet enrollment and final stability evidence.

Rollback disables the sweep/watchdog controls while preserving status evidence
and task-dag chain history. Package/version selection belongs to nixos-sbc and
must retain a new-format-compatible task-dag until the chain compatibility gate
is satisfied. Do not manually restart or stop a serving service; use only
canonical rollout paths.

This is critical fleet infrastructure. The binding architecture already has
Oracle approval, but the implementation worker must get Oracle architecture
rereview for any design change and Oracle review of the actual final diff
before commit. Iterate to APPROVE.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Own the authoritative fleet enrollment, per-repository policy rollout, staged
production enablement, stability evidence, and final closure decision after the
task-dag, github-worker, nixos-sbc, and mostly-static-sites implementations are
reviewed and available.

## Required implementation

1. Extend `scripts/ephemeral_checkout.d/repos.conf` to accept exactly two or
   four fields and document `<mode> <branch>` without breaking existing
   two-field consumers. Two fields mean `off`; reject three/trailing fields.
2. Add strict version-1 `.github/ci-repair-policy.json` files to each enrolled
   repository in its owning repo. Bind every required check to its exact name,
   GitHub App identity, accepted terminal conclusions, and explicit grace.
   Missing, empty, malformed, unsupported, or identity-mismatched policy is
   never green.
3. Update final-gate callers to invoke the canonical `repair-reconcile` only as
   a low-latency hint without weakening, replacing, or making correctness
   depend on the final gate. Coordinate peer-owned policy/caller edits through
   their own repository task trails and `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65`.
4. Keep all rows `off` until the three repair-infrastructure child epics have
   Oracle-approved diffs, landed code, disabled deployment, and successful
   credential preflight. Then execute the binding design's dry-run, observe,
   projection-canary, crash-drill, peer-by-peer, and fleetwide sequence.
5. Record durable evidence for aggregate parity, missed-run recovery, restart
   at every interruption boundary, exactly-one issue/task convergence under
   duplicate creators, authoritative-green closure, stale/failure telemetry,
   watchdog paging/recovery, cost bounds, and rollback readback.

## Required gates

- Every nontrivial critical-infrastructure diff gets Oracle architecture review
  before implementation and Oracle review of the actual diff before commit.
- Changes to canon or any `AGENTS.md` follow the canonical update protocol.
- Tests use fake APIs and temporary git origins; drills use isolated test
  evidence and never point tests at production resources.
- Deploy only through canonical paths. Never manually restart, stop, or kill a
  serving service. No database work is in scope.

## Rollout and rollback

Run credential preflight, then 24 hours of dry-run parity. Enroll task-dag and
top-level in observe mode, enable chain writes without projection, then enable
projection and inject missed-run/post-create-crash drills. Require 48 stable
hours before adding one peer at a time and enabling the fleet sweep. Keep
missing/invalid-policy paging disabled until that stability evidence is
complete; enabling it is the final rollout stage.

Rollback disables the host sweep and peer hints first. It then changes registry
modes to `off` through fenced cleanup and verifies projection readback.
Preserve all chain refs and issue/task audit history. If old task-dag code
cannot read an active new substate, use only the reviewed compare-and-set legacy
migration from the binding design; never delete refs or repair tickets. List
active red chains in the rollback record.

Issue #65 remains open until both systems are live and stable: durable repair
convergence is proven fleetwide, and mostly-static-sites has completed its
seven-day one-offs/index rollout, rendered-output Oracle approval, canaries,
two GC cycles, telemetry, and rollback verification.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```

# mostly-static-sites child epic: durable seven-day temporary pages

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Raise the one-offs service's bounded maximum lifetime from 24 hours to seven
days, make every serving/control surface agree on manifest-derived liveness,
bound storage growth, migrate publication to daemon-owned uploads, and make the
existing private `/one-offs/` index useful and accessible on phones.

## Required implementation

1. **One liveness contract**
   - Keep the two-hour default; set the daemon and NixOS hard maximum to
     604,800 seconds. Preserve each existing manifest's immutable 24-hour
     ceiling and every shorter caller-selected lifetime.
   - Define one `liveSlots(now)` selector used by direct serving, index, list,
     get, health, extension, boot, and garbage collection. At
     `now >= expiresAtMs`, all reads are absent and extension cannot revive the
     page, regardless of disk cleanup timing.
   - Keep validated manifests as the sole source of truth; never persist or
     cache a second index.

2. **Bounded daemon-owned storage**
   - Implement the binding design's defaults for live slots, files/bytes and
     submissions per slot, 10 GiB data-directory quota, 5 GiB free-space
     reserve, reservation accounting, error codes, and one async mutation
     mutex.
   - Add the streaming upload API and update `scripts/one-offs stage` before
     retiring group-writable `incoming`. Reject symlinks/special files and
     clean abandoned reservations. Publication must fail before visibility if
     any bound would be crossed.
   - Handlers are never daemon children. A socket-activated executor accepts
     only validated slot, submission, and configured-handler IDs over the
     root-owned Unix socket, derives every path itself, selects executables only
     from the fixed Nix allowlist, and runs separately unprivileged with the
     entire one-offs data directory bind-mounted read-only.
   - Fsync atomic manifest writes. Quarantine invalid/partial/orphaned state,
     omit it from serving, garbage-collect it after 24 hours, and expose
     bounded pressure/degraded diagnostics.

3. **Canonical private index**
   - Keep the bare `/one-offs/` route, render a bounded newest-first snapshot
     of live manifests, and preserve tailnet-only serving, Unix-socket control,
     `no-store`, and `noindex, nofollow`.
   - Implement the approved information architecture, privacy language,
     exact/relative expiry, accessible uniquely named actions, collapsed
     technical details, 320-pixel card layout, optional 21+-item progressive
     search, and populated/empty/degraded/error/direct-404 states.
   - Escape all caller labels. Do not add mutation controls or imply that a
     nonce authorizes a tailnet user.

## Tests and review

Use a fake clock and temporary data directory. Cover exact expiry across every
surface, old/new ceilings, restart recovery, partial manifests, upload/create/
submission/GC/index concurrency, reservation rollback, every admission bound,
quota/free-space failures, escaping, bounded 500-item output, 21-item search
and no-script fallback, mobile markup, all states, `HEAD`, headers, and
tailnet rejection. Integration tests must prove handler IDs cannot inject paths
or executables and handlers cannot write slot data. Accessibility coverage
includes landmarks, heading order, focus, unique actions, 44-pixel targets,
light/dark contrast, reduced motion, and 320-pixel width.

Before first exposure, Oracle must review representative rendered output for
populated, empty, expiring, degraded, error, and 404 states on desktop and
mobile and return APPROVE. The approved design review alone is not the final
render review. Before implementation, any nontrivial deviation from the binding
architecture requires a fresh Oracle architecture review; the actual final
critical-infrastructure diff also requires Oracle change review.

## Rollout and rollback

Follow the four-stage client-first migration in the binding design: add the
streaming API; deploy the packaged client everywhere and update canon/runbooks
through canon's update protocol; prove seven days with zero legacy claims plus
streaming canaries; only then remove legacy upload access and enable seven-day
lifetimes. Prove the backing filesystem quota before increasing the cap.

Roll out selectors/index first under the 24-hour maximum through the canonical
mostly-static-sites deployment path. Then enable bounds and seven-day creation,
verify two-hour and seven-day canaries, delete them, and observe two GC cycles.
Rollback first restores a packaged client compatible with the running server.
Before rolling the server behind the streaming API back, restore legacy
`incoming` permissions and the prior canon/runbook in one reviewed change and
pass a short-lived canary, preserving at least one supported publication path
throughout. Then restore 24-hour creation while grandfathering already-created
longer-lived manifests; list their latest expiry rather than deleting or
shortening them.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```
