declarations.body:
# Seven-day temporary pages and canonical live index

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`, System 2](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md#system-2-seven-day-one-offs-and-one-canonical-live-index)

## Goal

Extend the existing `mss-one-offs` service without creating another source of
truth. New temporary pages may last up to seven days, callers may still choose
any shorter lifetime, and the existing bare `/one-offs/` route becomes a
mobile-friendly view of every page that is live according to its manifest.

The binding design has Oracle architecture and template approval. Follow it
exactly. Any nontrivial design change needs fresh architecture review before
implementation. The actual rendered index and recovery states need Oracle UI
review before first operator exposure.

The durable top-level coordination point is the pending
[`Roll out and verify repair convergence and one-offs operations` leaf](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/commit/ba3ddc914238987ae3bfaebe4d259e30ffba0348).
It depends on this materialisation task, remains open across both peer
checkpoints, and owns caller migration plus production deployment, canaries,
cleanup-cycle observation, telemetry, stability, and rollback evidence.

## Existing implementation to extend

Keep ownership in the existing implementation:

- [`tools/one-offs-server/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/tools/one-offs-server/src/index.ts)
  owns manifests, the in-memory registry, request serving, expiry, garbage
  collection, control endpoints, submissions, and the current bare index;
- [`nix/modules/mss-one-offs.nix`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/nix/modules/mss-one-offs.nix)
  owns service configuration, users, storage, filesystem isolation,
  environment, and the tailnet-only listener;
- [`scripts/one-offs`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/scripts/one-offs)
  is the supported publishing client; and
- [`docs/HOW_ONE_OFFS_WORKS.md`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/docs/HOW_ONE_OFFS_WORKS.md)
  is the repository-local operational contract.

Do not persist an index, add a second registry, or place index-only
authentication in front of direct page URLs. A strictly validated manifest is
the sole authority.

## Implementation sequence

### 1. One live selector and reviewed index, with the 24-hour cap retained

- Introduce one `liveSlots(now)` selector used by direct serving, the HTML
  index, `GET /v1/slots`, `GET /v1/slots/<nonce>`, health counts, extension,
  startup, and garbage collection. A page is absent at `now >= expiresAtMs`;
  garbage collection only reclaims disk and can never define liveness.
- Snapshot live manifests under the mutation mutex using one captured clock
  value, then render outside the lock. Keep newest-first order and bounded
  O(live slots) rendering.
- Keep the bare `/one-offs/` route as the only index and render it directly
  from that snapshot. Preserve `Cache-Control: no-store`; add
  `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`.
- Implement the binding mobile and desktop information architecture: linked
  human note with an untitled fallback, prominent relative and exact UTC
  expiry, secondary creator metadata, a uniquely named direct action, and the
  short nonce only in collapsed technical details. Use one `<main>`, one H1,
  H2 item titles, 44-pixel targets, high-contrast focus rings, WCAG AA light
  and dark colors, and no horizontal scrolling at 320 pixels.
- Preserve the complete privacy boundary: serve only through `tailscale0` with
  daemon CIDR enforcement as defense in depth; keep the Unix control socket
  restricted to the `mss-one-offs` group; and expose nothing publicly. State
  that every live nonce is discoverable to any tailnet node that can reach the
  service and that a nonce is not authorization inside the tailnet. Require
  operator-safe `note` and `requestedBy` labels and content-free logs. Never
  expose delete or extend controls on the read-only TCP listener.
- At more than 20 live pages, add progressively enhanced search with the exact
  labels and announced result count from the design. Every page remains visible
  and usable without JavaScript.
- Implement the populated, empty, concurrent-expiry, degraded-load, plain 503,
  and indistinguishable direct-page 404 states from the binding design.
- Render representative populated, 21-item search, empty, degraded, 503, 404,
  concurrent-expiry, mobile, and dark-mode fixtures. Obtain Oracle UI approval
  of the actual output before any of it is exposed to the operator.

### 2. Bounded mutation, storage, and handler isolation

- Add one daemon-owned asynchronous mutation mutex covering capacity pruning,
  reservations, activation, extension, deletion, garbage-collection registry
  changes, and submission accounting.
- Enforce the binding configurable defaults: 500 live slots, 5,000 persisted
  files and 100 MiB per slot, 1,000 submissions per slot, a 10 GiB whole-data
  project quota, and a 5 GiB post-admission host free-space reserve.
- Count files and bytes during the existing tree-validation traversal, not in a
  second pass. Reserve capacity before mutation and release or reduce every
  reservation on every success, rejection, disconnect, timeout, and crash
  recovery path. Fail publication before a partial slot can become visible.
- Fsync atomic manifest writes and their parent directory. At startup,
  quarantine invalid, mismatched, manifest-less, and orphan temporary slot
  directories outside the serving registry; expire quarantine after 24 hours
  with bounded diagnostics. Never resurrect an expired manifest.
- Replace daemon-child submission handlers with the binding socket-activated,
  separately unprivileged `mss-one-offs-handler`. Accept only validated slot,
  submission, and configured-handler identifiers; derive paths in the executor;
  use a fixed Nix allowlist; and bind-mount the whole one-offs data directory
  read-only for the handler.
- Expose bounded disk-usage, rejected-publication, quarantine, degraded-load,
  and reservation metrics without logging page content.

### 3. Migrate publication to daemon-owned streaming uploads

Follow the client-first migration order. Do not combine or reorder these gates.

1. Add the daemon-owned streaming upload API from the binding design while
   preserving legacy `incoming/`. Update `scripts/one-offs stage` to walk the
   source, declare counts and bytes, stream only validated regular files, abort
   cleanly, and activate only a complete upload.
2. Package that exact client in every one-offs host's NixOS system path. Prove
   old and new publishing paths work before any caller migration.
3. Stop before retiring legacy `incoming/`. Post durable checkpoint evidence on
   [parent issue #65](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65), but do
   not use a `Satisfies:` trailer yet. The
   [durable parent rollout leaf](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/commit/ba3ddc914238987ae3bfaebe4d259e30ffba0348)
   deploys this 24-hour-cap checkpoint and owns the dependent top-level canon,
   shared runbook, and known-caller migration to the packaged `stage` command.
4. After that migration lands, the parent rollout observes legacy claims for
   seven days. Continue only after the count is zero and streaming
   create/delete/rollback canaries pass.
5. Make upload storage daemon-only mode 0750, remove the legacy API and path,
   and land the seven-day maximum. Do not use a `Satisfies:` trailer yet; the
   parent must still deploy and verify this final runtime candidate.

The streaming API reserves declared capacity under the mutex, rejects
symlinks and special files, refuses count or byte overruns, expires abandoned
uploads, and leaves no group-writable path that can bypass admission or consume
cleanup headroom.

### 4. Raise the maximum only after capacity and migration gates pass

- Change the daemon fallback and NixOS `maxTtlSeconds` default from 86,400 to
  604,800 seconds. Keep `defaultTtlSeconds` at 7,200 seconds.
- Preserve each manifest's immutable `maxExpiresAtMs`. Existing 24-hour pages
  cannot be extended beyond their original ceiling. New pages can request any
  positive shorter lifetime, clamped only at seven days.
- Before enabling the longer cap, prove the backing filesystem enforces the
  10 GiB systemd state-directory project quota and admission preserves the
  5 GiB cleanup reserve. A missing proof blocks enablement.

## Required deterministic coverage

Use a fake clock and isolated temporary directories. Cover:

- seven-day clamping, shorter lifetimes, immutable extension ceilings, old
  24-hour manifests, and `now == expiresAtMs` across every route and API;
- restart with expired, invalid, partial, mismatched, and orphan state;
- create, extension, deletion, garbage collection, submissions, reservations,
  streaming uploads, and index snapshots under concurrency and injected
  interruption;
- rollback of every reservation and partial upload, all per-slot and global
  bounds, project-quota and free-space failures, and single-pass accounting;
- escaped labels, bounded 500-item rendering, 21-item search and no-script
  fallback, `HEAD`, no-store, noindex, and tailnet rejection;
- populated, empty, degraded, 503, indistinguishable 404, concurrent-expiry,
  light, dark, and 320-pixel output; and
- landmarks, heading order, visible exact times, unique action names, focus,
  44-pixel targets, contrast, and reduced-motion behavior.

Add a focused test path for the one-offs daemon if the package still lacks one,
then run the repository's documented targeted checks. CI owns the full
retrospective `pnpm check` gate.

## Rollout, rollback, and completion

Land code inertly and preserve the 24-hour cap until the parent rollout leaf.
The parent uses the normal `mostly-static-sites` deployment path, first exposes
the selector and Oracle-approved index, then performs the client migration and
capacity rollout, and only then enables seven-day lifetimes. It verifies one
two-hour and one seven-day canary, deletes both, and observes two garbage-
collection cycles.

Rollback restores a packaged client compatible with the running server before
rolling server behavior back. Restore legacy `incoming/`, canon, and runbook
together before reverting the streaming API. Reverting the configured cap to
86,400 seconds does not shorten or delete pages created under the seven-day
version; report those grandfathered pages and let their recorded manifests
expire normally.

Use this completion handshake so delegated completion cannot close the parent
functionality epic before rollout:

1. Land the inert 24-hour selector, reviewed UI, bounds, upload API, packaged
   client, tests, and documentation without a `Satisfies:` trailer.
2. Hand the checkpoint to the
   [durable parent rollout leaf](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/commit/ba3ddc914238987ae3bfaebe4d259e30ffba0348),
   which deploys it, migrates top-level canon/runbook/callers, and records seven
   days with zero legacy claims.
3. Land legacy-path removal and the seven-day maximum without a `Satisfies:`
   trailer.
4. Hand the final candidate back to that rollout leaf. It deploys through the
   canonical path, proves quota enforcement, verifies two-hour and seven-day
   canaries, observes cleanup, exercises rollback, records stability, and
   durably completes that rollout task.
5. Only then land one real peer evidence/operational-documentation commit with
   the completion trailer below. Intermediate commits must not carry it.

The child is complete only after deterministic tests and final gates pass,
Oracle approves the actual rendered output and any nontrivial
critical-infrastructure diff, every migration gate is met, and the parent has
durable rollout and stability evidence. The final peer commit must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```
declarations.delegationNote: Preserve manifests and the bare index as sole authority; coordinate both peer checkpoints with rollout task ba3ddc914238987ae3bfaebe4d259e30ffba0348.

# top-level child epic: enroll and verify durable repair convergence

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Own the authoritative fleet enrollment, per-repository policy rollout, staged
production enablement, stability evidence, and final closure decision after the
task-dag, github-worker, nixos-sbc, and mostly-static-sites implementations are
reviewed and available.

## Required implementation

1. Extend `scripts/ephemeral_checkout.d/repos.conf` to accept exactly two or
   four fields and document `<mode> <branch>` without breaking existing
   two-field consumers. Two fields mean `off`; reject three/trailing fields.
2. Add strict version-1 `.github/ci-repair-policy.json` files to each enrolled
   repository in its owning repo. Bind every required check to its exact name,
   GitHub App identity, accepted terminal conclusions, and explicit grace.
   Missing, empty, malformed, unsupported, or identity-mismatched policy is
   never green.
3. Update final-gate callers to invoke the canonical `repair-reconcile` only as
   a low-latency hint without weakening, replacing, or making correctness
   depend on the final gate. Coordinate peer-owned policy/caller edits through
   their own repository task trails and `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65`.
4. Keep all rows `off` until the three repair-infrastructure child epics have
   Oracle-approved diffs, landed code, disabled deployment, and successful
   credential preflight. Then execute the binding design's dry-run, observe,
   projection-canary, crash-drill, peer-by-peer, and fleetwide sequence.
5. Record durable evidence for aggregate parity, missed-run recovery, restart
   at every interruption boundary, exactly-one issue/task convergence under
   duplicate creators, authoritative-green closure, stale/failure telemetry,
   watchdog paging/recovery, cost bounds, and rollback readback.

## Required gates

- Every nontrivial critical-infrastructure diff gets Oracle architecture review
  before implementation and Oracle review of the actual diff before commit.
- Changes to canon or any `AGENTS.md` follow the canonical update protocol.
- Tests use fake APIs and temporary git origins; drills use isolated test
  evidence and never point tests at production resources.
- Deploy only through canonical paths. Never manually restart, stop, or kill a
  serving service. No database work is in scope.

## Rollout and rollback

Run credential preflight, then 24 hours of dry-run parity. Enroll task-dag and
top-level in observe mode, enable chain writes without projection, then enable
projection and inject missed-run/post-create-crash drills. Require 48 stable
hours before adding one peer at a time and enabling the fleet sweep. Keep
missing/invalid-policy paging disabled until that stability evidence is
complete; enabling it is the final rollout stage.

Rollback disables the host sweep and peer hints first. It then changes registry
modes to `off` through fenced cleanup and verifies projection readback.
Preserve all chain refs and issue/task audit history. If old task-dag code
cannot read an active new substate, use only the reviewed compare-and-set legacy
migration from the binding design; never delete refs or repair tickets. List
active red chains in the rollback record.

Issue #65 remains open until both systems are live and stable: durable repair
convergence is proven fleetwide, and mostly-static-sites has completed its
seven-day one-offs/index rollout, rendered-output Oracle approval, canaries,
two GC cycles, telemetry, and rollback verification.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```

issues.body:
## Outcome

Review the Freshly Baked US landing-event delivery and deployment process for simple, maintainable failure handling after production ingestion is proven. Preserve the current design goal: page serving must never depend on analytics availability.

A landing event is an impression, assignment, redirect, or conversion record generated by `freshlybaked.us`. Each site replica writes events to its own local file spool, periodically sends a batch to the Helios analytics service, and Helios bulk-inserts the batch into its `lp_events` database table. Current implementation references: [sender failure handling](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/commit/3cdc88af3a0071ceee185b49aa5910c1606a581b), [production credential and endpoint wiring](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc/commit/0da0bc2e889e354912abce7fc6bc1f46d02b367e), and [Helios ingestion design and implementation record](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/4ff27f32a82d24b34019bffdc1b7f399b135ba0e/docs/epics/unified-landing-engine/STATUS_2026-06-11_implementation-progress.md#L40-L53).

**Follow-up only:** this issue starts after the approved initial rollout. It must not delay, reopen, or become a new acceptance gate for that rollout.

## Questions to resolve

### 1. Queue progress and data retention

- The sender currently retains the entire first-in-first-out batch after any non-success response. Define a response and recovery contract that distinguishes retryable system failures from permanently rejected individual events, preserves good events and diagnostic evidence, bounds quarantine retention, and lets later events continue.
- Move pending events out of `/tmp`, define the acceptable durability boundary, and decide whether writes need temporary-file-plus-rename, startup drain, and graceful shutdown drain.
- Make quarantined, corrupt, capacity-shed, and stale pending events observable without putting telemetry on the page-serving critical path.

### 2. Retry behavior and efficiency

- Add bounded exponential backoff and jitter so an unavailable sink does not produce synchronized retries across replicas.
- Replace repeated whole-batch serialization and per-enqueue directory scans with simple incremental accounting if measured traffic makes the current linear work material.
- Confirm drain capacity, storage growth, write-ahead-log volume, index amplification, and whether duplicating every event into `raw_event` remains worth its database cost.

### 3. Credential and rollout consistency

- Narrow the Helios ingest token to the server process instead of every process that inherits the shared Helios environment bundle.
- Design token rotation with an overlap window or versioned credentials so Agenix materialization and process reload cannot create a split-brain authentication interval.
- Map the owner, acquisition order, timeout, and crash cleanup for every deployment lock and mirror flag. Prove concurrent Helios and site deployments either serialize or fail before changing state, and cannot create proxy loops, deadlock or livelock, strand mirror flags, or leave peers on mismatched credentials. Add fleet-wide coordination only if the existing invariants are insufficient.

### 4. Recovery from partial work

- Specify what happens when a host, deployment wrapper, network link, or database response fails after a database commit but before acknowledgement.
- Verify replay remains idempotent, pending work cannot silently disappear or repeat analytically, and operators can distinguish healthy emptiness from a stuck sender.
- Do not assume notifications, webhooks, or monitoring deliveries are complete; periodic state reconciliation must be enough to rediscover missed failures.

### 5. Privacy and unreliable diagnostics

- Inventory which token and event fields can reach health responses, logs, pages, GitHub comments, and agent tooling. Keep complete payloads restricted to authoritative storage; expose only redacted metadata and aggregate counts to diagnostics or agent model context.
- Treat deployment output, pages, notifications, GitHub Actions, and webhooks as advisory rather than authoritative. Periodic reconciliation from durable state must detect missed or contradictory signals.

## Design bar

Prefer the smallest model that is understandable from first principles. It should have one authoritative owner and state per event, explicit state transitions, bounded cost, safe retry/recovery, no secret or event payload leakage to agent model context, and no reliance on complete webhooks or best-effort notifications.

Before implementation, get Oracle architecture review. Database work also requires database cost review; deployment or coordination changes require post-implementation Oracle review of the actual diff. Validate failure, replay, quarantine, restart, rotation, and concurrent-deploy scenarios with deterministic tests or an isolated harness, never production resources.

## Completion evidence

- A reviewed design records invariants, state transitions, ownership, recovery behavior, cost bounds, and rollback.
- Every question is resolved as an accepted boundary, a measured no-change decision, an implemented change, or a linked scoped follow-up with an owner and evidence. This issue stays open until each chosen change is verified or explicitly delegated; it does not turn every possible hardening item into one rollout gate.
- Production rollout, if any, uses canonical health-checked wrappers and verifies queue progress plus indexed event IDs; code landing alone is not completion.

issues.body:
After observing amp worker agents, when left mostly unsupervised beyond canonical instructions and a task, would make some truly bizarre decisions, often ignoring the system design, standard patterns, canonical instructions, etc, or would create UI surfaces that were incredibly poorly designed for the intended use (operator-efficient digestion of unfamiliar context and rapid decision making / response handling, etc).  Progressively, we started requiring reviews (generally Oracle reviews) when agents do certain things, like:
* Change canon (IMPORTANT!)
* Change critical infrastructure design/architecture
* Create novel operator-facing UI- or comms-surfaces
* DB efficiency and sanity
* Various other cases?

However, the end result is that a single task implementation end-to-end often has between 4 and 20 large, expensive, "thread-serializing" (meaning i cannot inject new instructions or updates while Oracle is in control), interactions.  These cost a lot (comparatively), take a long time (wall clock), and while they are undoubtedly improving the result quality in many cases, they have increased costs and development time unreasonably.  In some cases, I think this is due to HOW agents are using Oracle for review ([A] get a review, [B] review comes back with blockers, [C] changes made [D] Oracle re-consulted to determine if blockers are fixed, [E] Oracle needs context, requests prior review details, [F] Prior review context gathered by agent (or possibly not, or poorly, if thread compaction has occurred!!)  [G] Oracle invoked _again_ (or responded to) with additional details, proceed to assess - all of E and beyond should be skippable if we just planned ahead at [A], to durably capture both the question and response locally, and at [C] where in parallel to the captured review we record the Blocker being fixed and the pointer to or summary of the change addressing it, and providing this up front to oracle during re-review, so it doesn't have to learn by hand each time that it lacks sufficient context to re-review.  

Overall, the proliferation of Oracle reviews is now problematic.  Propose a systemic change or process update to reduce the cost & impact, or number of (without seriously degrading quality) Oracle reviews in a typical task cycle.  Post the proposal(s) here for operator review and page-dave.

issues.body:
Right now our Helios UI is organized in a frankly horrific way.  The nav bar _typically_ grants access to most functionality, if you know where to look.

I'd like our Navbar to be reorganized by likely operator utility and frequency of use, but ALSO i would like the nav menu to appear slightly differently to different "user archetypes", which can initially be inferred from the maximal permissions grant, but which ultimately should be a single selection from (initially; eventually might be a union of) an enum of archetypes.

The first archetype to implement will be "packer", a generally-untrusted (but somehow has minimal helios access) user account that will will give EXTREMELY limited page access to, and thus the nav menu should both reflect the reduced access, and be optimized in terms of contents and layout to maximize the efficiency of this archetype.

For the moment, the most common operation for this archetype will be the "low-inventory audit page", where we send an inventory packer around to check the status of "seemingly-almost-out-of-stock items" to ensure we have physically what we THINK we have in our pos inventory, and if not to make the inventory transfer needed to avoid selling non-existent or cannot-be-found inventory to customers, which is a terrible experience for those customers.  I expect we'd have one staff do this audit once per day, likely in the AM, although possibly once more in the PM as well.  Initially, results should be paged (p2) to dave for audit, with a link to a one-off page usefully containing the results of the audit done, who did it, what was discovered, what was moved and needs to potentially be removed from inventory, etc.  I'll change this pretty quickly to stop paging once i'm comfortable that it's all working.

The archetype-facing pages should NOT include notice banners like "DB is behind" or "agent waste queue is full", those are irrelevant to these users.

issues.body:
Starting with https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7 we created some very helpful metrics pages and displays.  These even work _reasonably_ well on mobile (although i'd LOVE to be able to full-screen-and-back individual graph/chart/metric-displays; add a task for that for all chart types).

However, not all is great; several of the charts present on this page (https://helios.freshlybaked.us/metrics/sales) and perhaps others do not show ANY title, and i have to guess or infer the meaning from the data.  Confounding this issue, (at least on mobile) pressing the `!` icon to generate a tooltip usually creates the tooltip way too far away!  Originally it was covering the data being displayed, which wasn't good, but the next change seems to have moved it to the top area of the containing parent control (or similar), which is usually off screen!  Thus many metrics charts are simply dark magic data with no explanation available on mobile.  

Improve these; one suggestion would be to position the tooltip just above the chart area and title area, extending upwards from there to contain as much of the tooltip text as will fit on a single screen.  Don't let it be positioned farther away from the display.

For pages with a "focus" chart at the top, pressing the `!` on a non-focused chart should *NOT* focus it (and let's be liberal in our determination of "user pressed for tooltip; unintentionally scrolling the entire screen to the top can be VERY disruptive.  Speaking of, if there IS a focus chart currently, there should be an adjacent "jump to source" or "jump back" action available that will position the screen back at the original position of the chart, scrolling until it's centered on the display.

For operator efficiency, oftentimes line charts and box charts (and their variants) are insufficiently natural to express the data conveniently; or at least a "point-in-time snapshot".  When clicking the chart to pop into focus mode, WHILE in focus mode, clicking a particular x-axis position or data point should, where helpful, pop down (immediately below the focus chart) additional helpful displays, contexts, or essential info & actions.  An example would be:  It's really hard to interpret the "by-category distribution of margin dollars from sales".  Even a stacked chart has a lot of noise in it.  Selecting a particular x-axis point/bucket might be well-served by popping up a pie chart for that datapoint, showing the relative SIZES of the components?  In some other cases, you're already choosing a better default visualization scheme (the cohort drop-off 2d colored chart comes to mind).  Have Oracle help you assess each batch of charts and see if (a) the chart is "stable" enough in meaning to be able to provide useful additional data (ie, the cohort analysis scatter plots _possibly_ won't be helped here, unless oracle is more clever than I am about useful visualizations or subsequent questions or actions), and if so (b) design an "automatic augmenter for focus charts" to turbocharge the operator's efficiency.

issues.body:
The metrics page here: https://helios.freshlybaked.us/metrics/inventory#view=mix&sites=midtown&window=28  could use some improvements.  I was reading the methodology on the page, and i can see some very clear tweaks to make to get this page MUCH more useful.  Here are some concepts / concerns that procurement process needs to consider when placing orders:
- A vendor will have a certain minimum lead time to delivery, which could be 1 day to 1+ weeks, depending on the distributor
- A vendor will _often_ but not always have generally-applicable minimums: minimum order (cost) total, minimum case sizing for each SKU (where `5` is NOT a great approximation; we should probably find the smallest non-sample order quantity for the categorical cohort/family SKUs *from that vendor*, and approximate the minimum order qty for the current SKU (being present in that categorical cohort / family where we grabbed the smallest non-sample order qty in any purchase over the prior 3 months) by this found minimum. I *think* this will end up being MUCH more accurate of an initial approximation.  The line items also need a way to easily fix the case sizing for that line item / sku
- On the very first order from a vendor, often they will disregard case minimum order sizes, to let us purchase smaller quantities of an unknown vendor and minimize our risk.  Beyond that, they generally will apply, however.
- Minimum order value is generally considered by *vendor* not by distributor, so we will need this as a first class Helios concept very soon.  It'll be quite hard to infer what the order minimum value is per vendor, but one operator will be able to feed you some initial data eventually, and we'll require a good way to update this within helios as the details slowly change over time.  For data modelling, a vendor provides an atomic inventory ordering surface.  They typically "own" one or more brands, which will be semi-permanently associated with that vendor from then on.  Once the full set of brands per vendor is known, along with vendor order minimums, then (much!) better order suggestions should be possible.  Currently the suggestions aren't realistic because some categories assume unrealistically low case sizes (prerolls _usually_ don't come in case size 5, its often 20, 25, 50, or 100 even).
- The details of minimum quantities and values do change over time potentially for a given vendor.  Observing a change of this type at some moment shouldn't immediately retroactively apply to other observations or data points for that vendor's order requirements (for whatever that might mean).  It just is forward-looking until itself superseded.
- While the contents of subpages (reorder queue, distributor baskets (useless currently, sadly, we'd need 'vendor baskets' for this type of page to be useful, as that's the atomic unit of ordering), exit/liquidate, mix drift) do provide some useful information, it's still somewhat limited (although the line item expansion-to-details-on-click on the reorder and liquidate pages is quite nice; we'll want to augment that details "sleeve" with market pricing data soon).  Consult with Oracle about what other visualizations or operator efficiency improvements could be made to make these even more streamlined for the operator and efficient.  Mix Drift page, for instance, is pretty static, doesn't really explain itself or the data being presented, presents VERY limited data, and overall doesn't clearly answer an operator question efficiently, or draw them naturally to the next logical question or action to take.  It's just kind of a novelty "blah" page, perhaps a little better.  Unlike the nice click-for-details on the other pages, THIS page's category line items do no such useful thing, sadly.  Also, selecting a grain of "subcategory" should be INCLUSIVE of the category, not ignore it!  Most items have a category with no subcategory.  But the categories are DEFINITELY different, so the products are wildly different.  Grain "subcategory" just lumps them all into a "no subcategory" bucket.  Lame
- Why would Beverages go into "Other"?  Is this due to our seemingly shitty and ill-designed and seemingly always out of date inventory and catalog mirror?  I added that top-level category probably two months ago.  Why hasn't this been updated within helios to actually reflect the change rather than lumping into "other"?
- In case it IS related to staleness and mirroring, I'm in favor of just generally beating directly on live production Sweed's backends via direct RPCs with leased session to retrieve live data anytime a mirror / cache / db group's age/latency/time-since-fresh exceeds an hour, roughly, as WELL as on first page render (user will almost certainly want real, fresh data when viewing a new operator page, such as the warehousing location assignment page, or the 'submit product pictures and barcodes" page, etc.  (not ACTUALLY beating on their servers, we'll want a *SUB*exponential backoff for server errors, roughly quadratically increasing until bounded at max retry delay of roughly 10 seconds (always jitterred slightly, of course).  Our current mirror approach has brought me nothing by sadness and pain and the confusion of other, less technical staff.

Update canonical database standards to treat schemaless or wide known-schema JSON/JSONB storage as a temporary early-development escape hatch, not a durable default.

slots.body:
# Helios `/metrics` v1.2 rework — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
> for the v1.2 iteration. Authoritative design:
> [`docs/epics/business-metrics/EPIC_PLAN_v1_2_REWORK.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN_v1_2_REWORK.md)
> in the top-level repo.
>
> The v1 child epic is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#21`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21)
> (closed); the v1.1 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#28`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/28)
> (closed at the R6 closure commit). This issue tracks the v1.2
> rework only — please do not reopen the v1 or v1.1 children.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation` master that
> satisfies any part of this rework MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: V2<n>`
> trailer (e.g. `Phase: V2'3`) — distinct from v1's `P<n>` and
> v1.1's `R<n>` — so per-phase progress comments on the parent
> issue are visually grouped per rework iteration.

## Scope owned by this repo

v1.2 closes the six oracle-flagged gaps captured in the parent
addendum:

1. Prior-period comparison & variance as the default render of
   every time-series panel.
2. Tabular drilldown renderer (per-SKU / per-(category,
   subcategory) tables behind slow-mover, low-stock, inventory
   misalignment).
3. CSV / PNG / SVG export from every panel.
4. Aggregation parity — `dow` / `dom` / `dofortnight` either work
   end-to-end or are removed from the global control set.
5. On-tile annotation drill (annotation popover available without
   first expanding the panel).
6. `inventory.cost_distribution` perf refactor (single all-snapshots
   fetch + JS as-of fold).

Re-read the parent addendum before starting any phase. This child
plan is intentionally a thin index over the parent.

### R'0 — Scope freeze + agg-parity decision + canonical update

- Re-confirm the v1.2-in-scope panel set against the canonical
  v1.1 panel list landed in R6 of the v1.1 rework. Any panel
  added or removed from the registry since v1.1 closure is
  reconciled here.
- Pick `dow` / `dom` / `dofortnight`'s fate:
  - default position is "implement them generically across every
    time-series metric via a client-side reduce over already-fetched
    bucketed data";
  - fall-back position is "remove them from the global agg
    dropdown until per-metric opt-in lands" — fall back **only**
    with explicit operator sign-off on the parent issue.
- Extend `MetricDef` types:
  - `supports?: { priorPeriod?: boolean; yearOverYear?: boolean; ... }`
  - `desirableDirection?: 'up' | 'down' | 'neutral'`
    (drives variance-readout colour; default `'up'`).
  - `drilldowns[].tableMode?: TableModeDef` (see parent §"Tabular
    drilldown contract").
- Add a CI guardrail that fails the build if any visible
  time-series metric is missing `supports.priorPeriod: true` after
  R'1 lands.
- Refresh `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics-v1_1-canonical.md` to a
  `…-v1_2-canonical.md` superset that adds `supports.priorPeriod`
  / `desirableDirection` / `tableMode` columns, and update the
  runbook anchor on the parent issue's body.

**Exit criteria**: single authoritative v1.2 panel list,
aggregation-parity decision recorded, `MetricDef` types
extended (no behavioural change yet — types are additive),
guardrail wired (currently passing because nothing declares
`supports.priorPeriod` yet — flips to enforcement in R'1).

### R'1 — `compareTo` API + reference series rendering

- Server side:
  - Every time-series metric's `GET /api/metrics/<id>` accepts a
    new optional `compareTo` query param:
    `prior-period` (default), `year-over-year`, `none`.
  - When `compareTo !== 'none'` the response includes a parallel
    `series` entry with `kind: 'reference'`, `baselineRange:
    { from, to }`, sampled at the **same** bucket boundaries as
    the primary series (zero-fill explicit; missing data
    explicit, not silently zero).
  - Variance readout for the latest visible bucket (and totals
    across the visible window) computed server-side:
    `meta.variance: { absolute, fraction, baselineRange }`
    per primary series.
  - All work done in the same SQL pass where possible; if a
    second SQL is required, batched in the same handler so each
    request is one round-trip from the client's perspective.
- Client side:
  - `<MetricChart/>` renders `kind: 'reference'` series as a
    dimmed (e.g. 38% opacity) version of the primary's stroke
    colour, behind the primary, with no `×` markers; keeps
    primary stroke + markers identical to v1.1.
  - Hover-readout tooltip shows current bucket value, reference
    value, and variance per series; the synchronized crosshair
    from v1.1 R2 includes reference values in its readout.
  - Per-panel `compareTo` toggle in the panel header (chevron menu:
    `Prior period` / `Year over year` / `Off`). Per-page default
    is `prior-period`; per-panel choice persists in the URL via
    `compareTo[<metricId>]=…` so share-links reproduce.

**Exit criteria**: every visible time-series panel renders a
prior-period reference series by default; toggling per-panel
between prior-period / YoY / off works and persists in the URL;
the R'0 guardrail is in enforcement.

### R'2 — Variance readouts + optional shading

- Panel header readout: small chip rendering
  `Δ <sign> <abs> (<pct>)` for the visible-window totals, with
  colour driven by `MetricDef.desirableDirection` (up = green-on-pos,
  down = green-on-neg, neutral = no colour). On hover/focus, expand
  to a small popover with `current = X`, `reference (prior period)
  = Y`, `Δ = X−Y`, `Δ% = (X−Y)/Y`.
- Hover-readout tooltip (the crosshair tooltip from v1.1 R2) gains
  a per-series variance row (`Δ = X−Y (Δ%)`) under each existing
  value row.
- Variance shading: optional faint shaded band between primary
  and reference, gated by a page-level toggle (off by default for
  dashboard density; on by default in detail / expanded mode).
- Verify the panel header readout doesn't cause layout shift when
  the value loads (reserve space with a skeleton placeholder).

**Exit criteria**: variance is readable at a glance from the
dashboard without clicking; colour direction respects
`desirableDirection`; expanded mode shows the shaded band.

### R'3 — `TableModeDef` + per-metric `/rows` endpoint + table tab

- Server side:
  - New endpoint family `GET /api/metrics/<id>/rows?<global filters>
    & sort=<col>:<dir> & page=<n> & pageSize=<m>`. Implemented per
    metric; default `pageSize` from `TableModeDef.pageSize ?? 50`,
    server-clamps `pageSize ≤ 200`.
  - Response shape:
    ```ts
    {
      columns: TableColumnDef[];           // mirror of MetricDef
      rows: Record<string, unknown>[];     // server-formatted values for export honesty
      totalRows: number;
      page: number;
      pageSize: number;
      sort: { column: string; direction: 'asc' | 'desc' };
      meta: { sources, lastUpdatedAt, coverageFrom, coverageTo, warnings };
    }
    ```
  - Sort + page implemented in SQL (no JS-side reshuffle on
    pagination — pagination is the whole point).
- Client side:
  - `MetricDef.drilldowns[].tableMode` declared → detail route
    (`/metrics/<metricId>`) shows a tab strip `Chart | Table`.
    Default tab when arrived via row-click drill is `Table`; via
    a regular expand affordance, `Chart`.
  - `<MetricTable/>` component: column headers click to sort
    (multi-cycle: asc → desc → off), page controls at the
    bottom, per-row action button when
    `tableMode.rowAction` is declared.
- Land the three required tables:
  - `slowmovers.cost_at_risk` rows: `{ sku, name, on_hand_cost,
    retail_value, last_sold_date, days_since_sold }`.
  - `lowstock.upcoming_outs` rows: `{ sku, name, days_of_cover,
    expected_margin_loss, daily_margin_run_rate, next_reorder_date }`.
  - `inventory.misalignment` rows: `{ category, subcategory,
    on_hand_cost, cogs_30d, observed_ratio, target_ratio,
    divergence }`.
- The R'4 CSV export builds on the same `/rows` endpoint with a
  capped unpaginated mode (see R'4); land that hook in this phase
  even if the export menu wiring happens in R'4.

**Exit criteria**: three required tables render with server-side
sort + pagination on the detail route; row-click drills (where
declared) link out; CI smoke confirms each declared
`tableMode.endpoint` returns 200 on a representative window.

### R'4 — Export (CSV / PNG / SVG)

- Server side:
  - `GET /api/metrics/<id>/export?fmt=csv` — long-form CSV. In
    chart mode: `metric_id,series_id,bucket_start,value,kind`
    (`kind` is `'primary'` or `'reference'`). In table mode:
    columns mirror `TableColumnDef.key` order; rows are
    unpaginated, server-clamped at `max=10000`. Response carries
    `X-Export-Clipped: true` + a leading `# clipped at 10000
    rows` comment line when clamp hits.
  - `GET /api/metrics/<id>/export?fmt=png` and `fmt=svg` —
    server-side render of the panel SVG via a headless render of
    `<MetricChart/>` (use `satori` or the existing SSR path if
    one is wired; otherwise `node-canvas` over a hand-built SVG
    string is acceptable). Width / height / DPR fixed
    (`w=1200,h=600,dpr=2` default; overridable via query).
    Output preserves current global state from the request query
    (site / range / agg / compareTo / drill).
- Client side:
  - Panel header (dashboard tile + detail view) exposes an export
    chevron menu with `CSV` / `PNG` / `SVG` actions. Selecting an
    action issues a normal download via a hidden `<a download>`
    so the browser handles it natively.
  - In table mode, the same export menu emits a rows-based CSV
    (the server endpoint switches mode automatically based on
    the `mode=table` flag the client adds).
- Smoke tests:
  - CSV round-trip: render a panel, export, re-parse, assert
    bucket count + first/last bucket match the rendered chart.
  - PNG smoke: response is `image/png`, byte length > 1KB, magic
    bytes `\x89PNG`.
  - SVG smoke: response is `image/svg+xml`, contains the metric
    id in a `data-metric` attribute on the root `<svg>`.

**Exit criteria**: every panel exports cleanly to all three
formats from both dashboard tile and detail view; exports honour
current global state; clip notices appear when row cap is hit.

### R'5 — Aggregation parity + on-tile annotation drill

- Aggregation parity (per R'0 decision):
  - Path (1) **implement**: add a generic client-side reducer
    that takes the bucketed `series` response and folds it to
    `dow` (Mon..Sun, ISO weekday), `dom` (1..31), and
    `dofortnight` (1..14, anchored on a configurable epoch).
    Stacked / percent / area chart types share the reducer.
    Scatter / map / table panels declare
    `supportsAggregations: ['total','month','week','date','hour']`
    only and the global agg dropdown disables non-supported
    options when only such panels are visible (rare).
  - Path (2) **remove**: drop `dow` / `dom` / `dofortnight` from
    the global agg dropdown; document in the runbook how a
    metric opts in per-metric (would be a v1.3+ thing).
- On-tile annotation drill:
  - Reuse the expanded-mode annotation popover component for
    on-tile pip hover/focus/tap; pip hit area is the rendered
    indicator + a small invisible padding (8px) for touch.
  - Popover shows: annotation title, author, ISO timestamp, an
    excerpt of the comment body, and a `Open panel detail`
    button that routes to the owning panel's detail view scrolled
    to the annotated `t`.
  - Crosshair (from v1.1 R2) does not fire while the annotation
    popover is open over the pip — popover takes precedence.
  - Keyboard: annotation pips are reachable via Tab, popover
    opens on Enter / Space, closes on Escape, never traps focus.

**Exit criteria**: agg dropdown advertises only options that all
visible time-series metrics support (or implements them
generically); on-tile annotations are inspectable without first
expanding the panel; touch / keyboard parity verified.

### R'6 — `inventory.cost_distribution` perf + closure package

- Perf refactor:
  - Replace the per-bucket DISTINCT-ON snapshot scan with a
    single window-scoped pull: `SELECT … FROM inventory_snapshots
    WHERE snapshot_ts BETWEEN window_start - max_lookback AND
    window_end` (and any filter that already narrows the read).
  - JS-side as-of fold: for each requested bucket boundary
    (already produced by `walkBuckets`), pick the most recent
    snapshot row per (sku, location) with `snapshot_ts ≤ boundary`.
    Reduce to per-(category[, subcategory]) cost totals.
  - Server-side cache: snapshot stream is roughly append-only,
    so cache the window pull with a 60s TTL keyed on
    `(start, end, max_lookback)`. Cache layer is the existing
    in-process LRU; no Redis required.
  - Measurement: produce a `before` / `after` timing table for
    P50 / P95 cold / P95 warm on the live `vps-nixos-3` against
    typical dashboard windows (1d / 7d / 28d / 12wk). Target:
    P50 < 250 ms warm, P95 < 600 ms cold.
- Runbook refresh: `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md` extended
  with the v1.2 surface (compareTo, table mode, export, agg
  parity, annotation tile drill, snapshot-fold).
- Validation evidence committed under the runbook:
  - prior-period overlay screenshot (default render);
  - variance readout in header + tooltip screenshots;
  - table-mode tab screenshot on a real slow-mover row;
  - CSV / PNG / SVG export sample (CSV first 20 lines; PNG
    thumbnail; SVG embed-able snippet);
  - annotation popover on a dashboard tile screenshot;
  - `inventory.cost_distribution` before/after timing table.
- Oracle review pass: re-run an oracle review on the live
  `/metrics` page + the new v1.2 surfaces + the canonical metric
  list. Capture the oracle's "fit for purpose — world class for
  this operator's stated needs?" verdict. If the oracle flags new
  gaps, address them in this phase before the closure commit, or
  file an explicit follow-on epic and call it out in the closure
  package.
- Closure package: a single comment on
  [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
  containing the live URL, the R'0–R'6 per-phase commit table,
  the AC §1–8 sign-off (with one-line evidence per criterion),
  the refreshed canonical metric list, the validation evidence,
  and the oracle note. The close commit MUST carry
  `Closes-Epic: #7` per #8's policy so
  `close-completed-issues.yml` closes the issue.

**Exit criteria**: parent can close based on evidence, not trust;
all v1.2 AC §1–8 demonstrably hold on production; v1.1 AC §1–10
continue to hold (no regressions); the oracle confirms the
dashboard is fit for the operator's stated "world-class business
performance metrics dashboard" purpose.

## Cross-repo dependencies

None hard. v1.2's data needs are entirely covered by the ingest
streams already wired in v1.1 (orders / cost / inventory snapshots
/ delivery / weather / shifts). If a v1.2 phase discovers a
missing column or a stream-shape problem, file an additional child
epic against the appropriate peer per the
[cross-repo task-dag driver](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/cross-repo-task-dag-driver.md)
model and link it from the parent issue.

## Acceptance criteria (delegated from parent)

The full v1.2 acceptance criteria live in the parent rework
addendum §"Refreshed acceptance criteria". Reproduced here as a
checklist for the R'6 owner:

- [ ] (1) Prior-period comparable by default; per-panel
      compareTo toggle (prior-period / YoY / off); variance in
      header + hover; reference fetched in same round-trip.
- [ ] (2) Table tab on detail route for slow-movers,
      low-stock, inventory-misalignment; server-side sort +
      paging; CSV export of unpaginated rows with clip notice.
- [ ] (3) CSV / PNG / SVG export from every panel (tile +
      detail); preserves global state; CSV is canonical machine
      format.
- [ ] (4) Aggregation parity — `dow` / `dom` / `dofortnight`
      either work on every visible time-series metric or are
      removed from the global control set.
- [ ] (5) On-tile annotation drill — popover on pip hover /
      focus / tap with title / author / timestamp / excerpt;
      `Open panel detail` button routes correctly.
- [ ] (6) `inventory.cost_distribution` P50 < 250 ms warm,
      P95 < 600 ms cold on `vps-nixos-3` 12-week window;
      timing note in R'6 commit.
- [ ] (7) v1.1 AC §1–10 continue to hold on production; no
      regressions in the dashboard / crosshair / expand+drill /
      stub-leak guardrail.
- [ ] (8) Oracle-approved closure evidence package — live URL,
      commit table, screenshots, canonical metric list, oracle
      note; close commit carries `Closes-Epic: #7`.
slots.delegationNote: Helios /metrics v1.2 rework — close the six oracle-flagged gaps after v1.1 (prior-period reference + variance as default render; tabular drilldown tab on detail route for slow-movers / low-stock / inventory-misalignment; CSV/PNG/SVG export from every panel; aggregation parity for dow/dom/dofortnight; on-tile annotation drill; inventory.cost_distribution snapshot-fold perf refactor). V2'0..V2'6 phasing; oracle-approved evidence package required at V2'6 closure with Closes-Epic: #7 trailer.

# Unified landing-page engine — `mostly-static-sites` (thin runtime) child epic

> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) (rev 3). Re-read the parent
> before starting any phase — this child epic is a **thin index** over
> the parent's design, not a re-statement of it. The parent is
> authoritative; if this file ever drifts from it, the parent wins.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#13
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>`
> trailer so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post per-phase
> progress on the parent issue.

## ⚠️ Binding constraint: do NOT change the canonical URL schema

The operator rejected the manufactured `/r/<family>` and
`…/lp/<family>/<param-tuple>/b/<branch_id>` routes. **Keep the existing
canonical schema** (parent §6.1, rev-3):

```
/SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM   ·   NUM=0 = random-rotation distributor alias
```

implemented today in
[`apps/freshlybakedus-site/middleware.ts`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/apps/freshlybakedus-site/middleware.ts)
and
[`apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/purpose-families.ts`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/purpose-families.ts).
The `/0` re-roll `307`, the `utm_content=NUM:N` rewrite, and the
legacy/vacant-variant redirects already implement the URL-embedded
scatter. **No new route shapes. No Google-Ads final-URL changes.** The
one change is *who decides `NUM`*: the bundle's weights/kill-list bias
the pick instead of a uniform `Math.random()`.

## Scope owned by this repo (the thin, fast substrate)

Everything in the parent EPIC_PLAN §4 ("mss owns") and the mss slice of
the §10 phases:

- **`/cloud` bundle loader/validator/cache** — background poller reads
  the read-only `/cloud` artifact root, validates schema + `sha256` +
  signature + `min_renderer_version`, atomically swaps an in-memory
  active bundle, keeps last-known-good (N=3), **fail-closed** (never
  serve unvalidated content), exposes health
  (`loaded_bundle_id`, `validation_status`, pointer age). Off the render
  hot path; verify `/cloud` POSIX atomic-rename in P2 (parent §5, §8).
- **Sandboxed CEL evaluator wired into the EXISTING random-rotation
  middleware** — replaces the uniform `pickRandomVariant()` draw with a
  bundle-weighted (optionally gclid/gbraid/wbraid HMAC-keyed for
  per-click reproducibility) pick of `NUM`, then reuses the existing
  `utm_content=NUM:N` redirect/rewrite path unchanged. Pinned `NUM`
  (explicit `utm_content` or direct `/…/N` link) wins — no re-select
  (parent §6, §6.1). Evaluator is pure: no clock/RNG/`eval`, bounded.
- **Signed variant-kill-list enforcement at the existing variant
  route** — a dead `(site,purpose,slug,num)` redirects to the
  replacement/champion `NUM` via the existing `matchVacantVariantRedirect`
  machinery, logging `requested_num` vs `served_num` (parent §6.1).
- **X1–X5 component renderers** (data-driven from the bundle); validate
  the frozen X2 is present in every family stack (parent §7).
- **Sweed menu adapter/cache (X4)** + **delivery-zone gate** — request-
  time within the ~150 ms cap with stale/fallback; gate feeds policy
  inputs so Helios never optimizes unserviceable ZIPs (parent §7;
  decision 6: ROI control only, no OCM retention).
- **Durable local event spool + ~15-min batch flusher** → Helios
  `POST /v1/lp-events/batch`; at-least-once with per-render `event_id`
  idempotency; backpressure sheds telemetry, never blocks render
  (parent §8; decision 4). **Zero DB reads on the render path.**
- **Shadow/canary support + observability** — `LP_RUNTIME_MODE`,
  allowlists/percent, kill switch, parity + render dashboards
  (parent §10).
- Keep `MAX_VARIANT_BY_PURPOSE` / `*VariantIds` as the drift guard;
  reject any bundle referencing a `NUM` outside the active registry.

## Relationship to the gemini-clusters epic (#5)

This **supersedes the not-yet-built mss slice (M1–M5) of #5** — build
the thin runtime + bundle contract here rather than building
selection/content logic into mss and ripping it out (parent §2, §15).

## Phases

Follow parent §10 order (mss slice): P0 inventory routes/families ·
P1 (Helios-led) · P2 bundle loader (no render change) + stand up event
spool · P3 shadow-compare selection · P4 preview render (both entry
modes already exist: `/0` re-roll and direct `/…/N`) · P5 consume
bundle content · P6 canary + revenue guardrail · P7 full · P8
decommission mss-owned selection/asset ownership + cross-repo commit
consumer. See parent §10 for traffic-impact and rollback columns.
slots.delegationNote: Thin-runtime slice. BINDING: do NOT change the canonical /SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM URL schema; wire the CEL evaluator into the existing random-rotation middleware so bundle weights/kill-list bias NUM (parent EPIC_PLAN rev 3 section 6.1).

# Amp cost reduction — `github-worker` child epic **P4**: agent-waste store + advisory selection/injection

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality."
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> — **Lever D = §5** (and the §8 context-budget meta-problem), phased plan =
> §10 (Phase 4).
> **Reviewed advisory catalog (already landed in top-level):**
> [`docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml)
> and [`docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 now has **several**
> `github-worker` child epics, the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO
> carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so
> the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal (Lever D, design §5)

Close the ≤1-minute feedback loop the operator asked for: as agents (and the
Phase-3 guardrail wrappers) discover wasted effort, record it **structurally**,
and let the dispatcher inject a **tiny, reviewed, budgeted** set of advisories
into the next agent's capsule — *without* ever injecting free-form
agent-authored text.

> **Hard correction from Oracle (mandatory, design §5):** do **NOT** build a
> channel that injects arbitrary agent-authored "lessons learned" into future
> agents. That is simultaneously a context-bloat accumulator, a hallucination
> amplifier, a stale-junk drawer, and a prompt-injection surface. Split the
> system into **observations → reviewed advisories → guardrails**.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Observation store** | A small `agent-waste record …` CLI + the Phase-3 wrappers append **structured** events (design §5.1 schema) to a local store (SQLite WAL or flocked NDJSON under `~/.local/state/github-worker/`). Free-form notes may be stored for **human review** but are **never** injected. This must use the same store path/schema the Phase-3 `bin/rg` wrapper writes to (the P3↔P4 contract). |
| **Advisory selection** | The dispatcher reads the reviewed catalog [`advisories.yaml`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml), selects the **top-ranked** advisories whose `trigger_ids` have fired recently (design §5.3 ranking), and injects **only their allowlisted `text`**, under a hard budget (design §8: ≤300–500 tokens total, ≤3–5 advisories). |
| **Injection point** | Injected into the **dynamic** part of the prompt (after the stable prefix/capsule from Phase 2 — leave the advisory slot Phase 2 reserves), so the cacheable prefix stays byte-stable. |
| **Review backlog, not prompt text** | Unknown/free-form observations create a **review backlog** surface for the operator; they never become future prompt text. |
| **Ranking + caps** | Implement the §5.3 score (severity × recurrence × est-cost-saved × scope-match ÷ token-cost × decay(age)); TTL 7–14 days (except `permanent-safety`); an advisory still high-recurrence at TTL **must be promoted** to a guardrail/canon rule, never extended as prose forever. |

## 3. Constraints

- **Never inject agent-authored free text.** Only allowlisted `text` from the
  reviewed catalog, selected by structured event IDs, under hard caps + TTL +
  the Phase-2 `agent-prompt-budget` CI ceiling.
- Observations are structured and **never auto-injected**; the influence is
  carried by the dispatcher (re-ranking), not by agents reading each other's
  notes — no agent waits on another.
- Single prod host today makes a local store safe; mirror summaries to a git
  ref only if the fleet later goes multi-host (design §12 Q1 — confirm the
  store location with the operator).

## 4. Acceptance (design §10 Phase 4)

- An observation recorded now is reflected (re-ranked) in the **next**
  dispatched agent's capsule within ~1 min, **under budget**.
- **No free-form text is ever injected**; unknown observations land in the
  review backlog only.
- The injected advisory set respects the §8 budget (enforced by the Phase-2
  `agent-prompt-budget` check) and the §5.3 caps/TTL.
- Each implementation attaches an Agent Gate Record (canon §3), and the final
  satisfying commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34` **and** this
  issue's `Issue:`/`URL:` trailer.

## 5. Production safety / rollback

- The store + record CLI are additive and best-effort; a failed write must
  never affect an agent's run.
- Advisory injection is gated by the budget check and the allowlist; roll back
  by disabling injection (dispatcher flag) — the catalog and store are inert
  without it.
- No serving service is touched; landing on `github-worker@master` is the
  publication step (the dispatcher reads repo state per run).
slots.delegationNote: Lever D / design §5 + §10 Phase 4; consumes the advisories.yaml catalog + agent-prompt-budget CI already landed in top-level.

# Dev-loop optimization — `task-dag` child epic (broken-master auto-repair)

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#26](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/26).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/designs/ci-broken-master-auto-repair.md`](../../../../designs/ci-broken-master-auto-repair.md)
> and the parent
> [`docs/epics/dev-loop-optimization/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> (§6) in the top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the
> shared CI-driven broken-master auto-repair implementation** that lives
> in `virusdave/task-dag`.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `task-dag@master` that
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#26
> ```
>
> **Re-read the parent design doc before starting** — it is the single
> source of truth; this file is a thin index over it.

## Goal

Provide the reusable, race-safe mechanism that detects a red `master`,
files exactly **one** high-priority repair ticket per red streak ("repair
chain"), and interprets `Tree-Fix` commit trailers so a fix either
reaches green or escalates to a `continue`-mode repair task. All logic
lives once in `virusdave/task-dag` (the single home of task-dag / CI
automation); peer repos call it as a reusable workflow. top-level
coordinates only and does not host repair logic.

## Binding standards (from the parent, do not weaken)

- Two-gate green tree: this is the *final-gate* half made
  self-healing — it must never weaken the required full gate.
- No first-party `any`, no disabled/weakened gates, no `--no-verify`,
  tests deterministic and prod-resource-free (inherited from fleet-green
  [#20](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/20)).
- Trailers parsed with `git interpret-trailers`, never freeform grep.
- Idempotent + stale-run safe: never mutate chain state against a
  superseded SHA (see design §4).

## Scope owned by this repo (`virusdave/task-dag`)

1. **Reusable CI repair classifier workflow** — called after a repo's
   full required suite on `master`; implements the green/red/unknown
   classification and the chain open/update/close logic (design §2).
2. **Commit-trailer parser** for `Tree-Fix` / `Tree-Fix-Chain` /
   `Tree-Fix-Mode` via `git interpret-trailers`.
3. **Chain-state persistence** — a durable per-repo store (e.g. a
   `tasks/ci-chains/<repo>` ref or equivalent) holding the design §1
   fields (`Last-Green`, `First-Red`, `Current-Head`, `State`,
   `Repair-Mode`, `Repair-Issue`, `Repair-Attempt`).
4. **Idempotent repair ticket** creation/update — exactly one
   `ci-broken-master` + `priority:high` ticket per chain, ingested as a
   pickable task by the existing comment/issue sync.
5. **Tree-fix outcome handling** (design §3): green closes the chain +
   ticket; red-in-chain escalates to a `continue`-mode repair task; red
   with a green parent opens a fresh `initial` chain; repeated
   same-signature failures `BLOCK` + page after a small threshold.
6. **Stale-run / race handling** (design §4): per-repo/branch classifier
   concurrency (`cancel-in-progress: false`), ignore superseded SHAs,
   close green only when current.
7. **Worker verifier** helper/CLI — "is my target still the current
   first-red, unclaimed chain head?" — so workers don't hand-implement
   the §6 contract.
8. **Tests/fixtures** for the §4 race cases (out-of-order CI runs,
   continue-mode escalation, new-regression-vs-continuation, green
   closing the right chain).

## Out of scope (deferred / other repos)

- Peer repo CI wiring + branch protection (deferred peer child epics).
- Any change to top-level's pure event-wiring workflows.
- Force-push / non-FF `master` auto-repair (detect → `STALE`/`BLOCKED` +
  page instead).

## Acceptance

From a fresh ephemeral checkout, the implementation:

1. classifies green / red / unknown-parent correctly and opens **one**
   chain per red streak;
2. files exactly **one** high-priority repair ticket per chain;
3. ignores stale older CI runs (no reopen when a newer descendant is
   green);
4. on a failed tree-fix, creates a **continue**-mode repair task (not a
   new first-red task); a green tree-fix closes the chain + ticket;
5. parses `Tree-Fix*` trailers via `git interpret-trailers`, covered by
   tests/fixtures for the design §4 race cases;
6. provides the worker verifier helper used by canon
   [`WORKFLOW.md`](../../../../canon/rules/WORKFLOW.md) "CI-filed
   broken-master repair tasks";
7. Agent Gate Record (two-gate template) attached.
slots.delegationNote: Implement the reusable broken-master repair classifier + Tree-Fix trailer interpretation + chain-state + worker verifier per docs/designs/ci-broken-master-auto-repair.md. Carry Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#26 on implementation commits.
slots.title: CI-driven broken-master auto-repair (dev-loop epic #26 phase 2)

# Agent-waste review queue — `top-level` child epic: backlog file format + agenix read/write deploy keys (D2/D3)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality" (Lever D,
> the structured agent-waste → reviewed-advisory loop).
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` → `docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md)
> ("Remaining work" #1; decisions **D1/D2/D3** and the **§Security** write-key
> choice are all RESOLVED by the operator) and
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](../../../../designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> §5 (Lever D) / §5.1 (raw-observation store, stays local — **not** this file).
> **Advisory catalog contract (already landed in top-level):**
> [`docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`](../../../../agent-runtime/advisories.yaml),
> [`docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md`](../../../../agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`virusdave/top-level`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level) `master` that
> satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`.
> Because #34 has **several** child epics, the **final** satisfying commit MUST
> ALSO carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer
> so the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal

Establish, in `virusdave/top-level`, the two load-bearing pieces the rest of the
agent-waste review queue depends on:

1. A committed **`agent-waste-backlog` file format**, co-located with
   [`docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`](../../../../agent-runtime/advisories.yaml),
   that github-worker's exporter writes and Helios reads.
2. The **agenix deploy keys** the `helios` service user needs: a **read-only**
   key for the D2 mirror and a scoped **write** key for the D3 promote path.

This is per operator decision **D1** (storage is a git file in `top-level`,
because "workers will already have that checked out in their
ephemeral-workspace"), **D2** (Helios reads it read-only via a git mirror), and
**D3** (promote is an in-Helios admin button that pushes to `top-level`). All of
these are **closed operator decisions** — this child epic is routine
implementation + agenix provisioning, no further operator input required.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Backlog file format** | Define + commit the on-disk format for the **pending-review** backlog (the tiny/rare unknown/free-form-`id` items a human must triage — **not** the chatty raw NDJSON observation store, which stays local to the dispatcher per design §5.1). Co-locate with `advisories.yaml` under `docs/agent-runtime/` (e.g. `docs/agent-runtime/agent-waste-backlog.ndjson` or `.yaml`). Ship it **empty and fail-safe**, exactly like `advisories.yaml` shipped empty. |
| **Contract alignment** | The format MUST round-trip through the already-merged Helios contract: [`helios/src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts) (Zod) and the producer's [`Nicponskis/github-worker` → `docs/AGENT_WASTE.md`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/docs/AGENT_WASTE.md) (`agent-waste backlog --format json`). The **`note` field is display-only and MUST NEVER be injected into agents** — carry that invariant into the schema doc. |
| **Read-only deploy key (D2)** | Provision a **new read-only agenix deploy key** for the `helios` user to mirror `top-level` (Helios today only mirrors `automation`). Same shape as the existing automation read key that [`helios/src/server/taskDagMirror.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/taskDagMirror.ts) reads from `/run/agenix/helios-github-automation-deploy-key`. |
| **Write deploy key (D3)** | Provision a scoped **write** agenix deploy key for the `helios` user for the promote path (option **(c)** direct, admin-gated, server-validated push to `top-level master`). Same shape as the existing `helios-parser-configs` write key. The residual repo-wide-deploy-key risk is **explicitly accepted** by the operator (RESOLVED_DESIGN §Security, comment [#4889206463](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/57#issuecomment-4889206463)) — do not re-litigate; do not silently substitute option (a)/(b). |
| **Docs** | A short `docs/agent-runtime/AGENT_WASTE_BACKLOG.md` describing the file format, the producer/consumer contract, and the two keys' purpose/scope, cross-linking `RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants (carry forward)

- **`note` never becomes advisory `text`.** The backlog file is display + human
  triage only; nothing in it is ever auto-injected into an agent. Only reviewed
  `advisories.yaml` entries are injectable (that is the allowlist invariant).
- **Two distinct streams — do not conflate.** The raw observation store is a
  local flocked NDJSON under the dispatcher's state dir and **Helios never reads
  it** (design §5.1). This file is only the small pending-review backlog.
- **Fail-safe empty default**, like `advisories.yaml`: an empty/missing backlog
  must degrade gracefully on both the producer and consumer sides.
- **Keys are for the `helios` service user**, provisioned via agenix, mirroring
  the existing automation read key and `helios-parser-configs` write key. This
  is routine infra, **not** the machine/`amp-local` credentials.

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Blocks** child epics #2 (github-worker exporter — needs the file format),
  #3 (Helios reader — needs the format + D2 read key), and #4 (Helios promote —
  needs the D3 write key). This is the root of the workstream; land it first.

## 5. Acceptance

- The pending-review backlog file format exists in `top-level` (empty,
  fail-safe), documented, and validates against the Helios Zod contract and the
  github-worker producer output.
- A read-only agenix deploy key for `helios` to mirror `top-level` is
  provisioned; a scoped write key for the promote path is provisioned; both are
  documented with their scope and the accepted residual risk.
- No serving service is touched by this child epic beyond agenix secret material
  (rollout of consumers is #2/#3/#4). Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

Additive: a new (empty) committed file + two new agenix secrets. Rollback is
removing the file and revoking/rotating the keys. No prod DB, no schema, no
serving-process change. Any nixos-sbc/host permission or tmpfiles change that
provisioning implies follows canon (push → `self-deploy*` under lock).
slots.delegationNote: RESOLVED_DESIGN Remaining-work #1; root of the workstream — backlog file format + D2 read / D3 write agenix keys. Blocks the other three.

# Helios-driven SEO widgets — `mostly-static-sites` (thin runtime) child epic

> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md). **Re-read the parent before
> starting any phase** — this child epic is a **thin index** over the
> parent's design, not a re-statement of it. The parent is authoritative;
> if this file ever drifts from it, the parent wins.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#15
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>` trailer
> so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post per-phase progress
> on the parent issue.

## Role in the epic

mss is the **thin, fast, zero-DB renderer**: it polls the signed SEO
bundle from the read-only `/cloud` mount, validates it (fail-closed,
last-known-good), and renders the FAQ/blog/feed/related/head widgets
**entirely from approved bundle data** — with **zero DB reads/writes on
render and no synchronous Helios call**. The SEO brain lives in Helios
(peer child epic at `../automation/EPIC_PLAN.md`). See parent
[§2](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#2-what-moves-into-helios-answer-to-operator-question-a).

## ⚠️ Binding constraints (from the operator's decisions — parent §0)

- **Blog/widget routes slot into FB.nyc's Reserved Prefix Registry** —
  the hosted-content zone `/sites/<id>/whats-new/<slug>`. The operator
  **rejected** a flat top-level `/whats-new/<slug>`. Do **not** force
  posts onto the LP `/SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM` schema either. The exact
  registry slug is finalised in **P0** (parent §0.2, §6.3;
  rough registry design: <https://gemini.google.com/share/952a99c4b22b>).
- **No public URL changes and no Google-Ads final-URL changes** at any
  phase (parent §10).
- **Host→mode enforcement is mandatory:** FB.nyc renders **raw**, FB.us
  renders **cannabis-sanitized**; reject raw-only content on a sanitized
  host (fail-closed). Render only approved content; no arbitrary
  HTML/script from the bundle; JSON-LD must match visible content
  (parent §5, §6).
- **Fail closed.** Bad bundle → keep last-known-good; no LKG → render the
  page **without** SEO widgets and page Dave; never render
  unvalidated/generated content (parent §4).
- **Reuse #13's loader/spool**, don't fork (parent §0.6, §12).

## Subtasks (see parent §11 for the authoritative list)

- SEO bundle loader on read-only `/cloud` (sig/sha/schema/
  `min_renderer_version` validation, LKG, in-memory active bundle,
  health/metrics) — a thin specialization of #13's LP loader.
- Host→raw/sanitized mode enforcement.
- Widget-slot registry in existing templates.
- `SEOFAQFold`, `WhatsNewFeed`, `BlogPost`, `RelatedLinks`, `SEOHead`
  renderers.
- Blog index/post routes within the `/sites/<id>/…` hosted-content zone.
- `Article`/`BlogPosting`/`FAQPage`/`BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD emitters.
- Sitemap/RSS routes backed by the active bundle.
- Content-addressed asset rendering.
- SEO event instrumentation + durable local spool + ~15-min batch flush
  to `POST /v1/lp-events/batch`.
- Shadow/canary flags + contract fixtures/tests.

## Phasing

Tracks the parent's 8-phase strangler-fig (parent §10): **P0** contracts/
inventory (incl. finalising the registry slug) → **P2** bundle loader →
**P3 FAQ MVP** (smallest shippable slice — do first) → **P4** blog
index/post/feed + JSON-LD + sitemap/RSS → **P5** event attribution →
**P6** canary → **P7** cleanup. (P1 publisher dry-run is Helios-side.)
Tag commits with `Phase: P<n>`.
slots.delegationNote: Thin-runtime slice. BINDING: blog/widget routes slot into FB.nyc Reserved Prefix Registry /sites/<id>/whats-new/<slug> (NOT flat /whats-new); zero-DB render; host raw-vs-sanitized; fail-closed; reuse #13 loader (parent section 0).
