# Dev-loop optimization — `mostly-static-sites` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#26](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/26).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/dev-loop-optimization/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the
> `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites` slice** of that design.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `mostly-static-sites@master`
> that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#26
> ```
>
> **Re-read the parent `EPIC_PLAN.md` before starting** — it is the
> single source of truth; this file is a thin index over it.

## Goal

Split the monolithic `pnpm check` (lint + typecheck + test + build) so
agents iterate with **light/targeted** checks scoped to the site,
package, or module they changed, while the full `pnpm check` stays the
CI / final gate rather than something hand-run repeatedly under
`large-action-lock` before every commit.

## Binding standards (from the parent, do not weaken)

- Two-gate green tree: fast local + final presubmit. Location split, not
  a waiver — full `pnpm check` (or equivalent) stays enforced in CI.
- A check leaves pre-commit/local iteration only with equal-or-stronger
  coverage remaining in CI.
- No first-party `any`, no disabled/weakened gates, no `--no-verify`,
  tests deterministic and prod-resource-free (inherited from fleet-green
  [#20](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/20); keep green).

## Scope owned by this repo

1. **Inventory + time** the steps inside `pnpm check` (lint, typecheck,
   test, build) and any pre-commit/CI steps, from a fresh ephemeral
   checkout with a warm cache.
2. **Provide light/targeted commands** for every >~30s step:
   - lint/typecheck scoped to the changed package/site/path rather than
     the whole workspace;
   - focused test runs (changed module / pattern);
   - avoid full static site builds in the local loop — keep the full
     build in CI unless it is consistently under ~30s.
3. **Document a dev-loop table in `mostly-static-sites`' `AGENTS.md`**:
   changed site/content/module path → light local command → final
   presubmit (`pnpm check` in CI) → when an agent may hand-run the full
   build/check.
4. **Lighten pre-commit hooks** to fast/targeted checks, **after**
   confirming full `pnpm check` is a required CI status.
5. **Confirm the broken-master window is closed**: full `pnpm check`
   validates the exact commit before it publishes/`bounce`-deploys, or
   promotion waits for CI green.

## Acceptance

From a fresh ephemeral checkout:

1. `AGENTS.md` dev-loop table present; every >~30s step has a
   light/targeted command or a documented heavy-final-only exception.
2. Pre-commit hooks fast/targeted; full `pnpm check` remains a required
   CI status, recorded green for a sample commit.
3. No coverage deleted; broken-master window closed or interim exception
   documented.
4. Agent Gate Record (two-gate template) attached.
slots.delegationNote: Split the monolithic pnpm check into a full CI presubmit plus site/path-targeted local commands; document a dev-loop table in AGENTS.md; lighten pre-commit hooks to fast/targeted (keep full pnpm check as required CI). See parent docs/epics/dev-loop-optimization/EPIC_PLAN.md.
slots.title: Dev-loop optimization: mostly-static-sites targeted checks, CI owns pnpm check

# Customers UX — `automation` child epic

> Second child epic of
> [virusdave/top-level#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9),
> sibling to the ingestion child epic at
> [`./EPIC_PLAN.md`](./EPIC_PLAN.md).
>
> Authoritative design:
> [`docs/epics/visitor-address-ingestion/CUSTOMERS_UX_EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../CUSTOMERS_UX_EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in the top-level repo.  This file is the thin per-repo scope index;
> read the parent design before starting.
>
> Implementation commits landing on `automation` master that satisfy
> any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9
> ```
>
> and SHOULD also carry:
>
> ```
> Phase: C<n>
> ```
>
> so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post the per-phase
> progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

The Helios admin UI + helios-server API + DB compatibility views that
make `visitor_scans` operationally useful, plus the IA reorganisation
that puts CRM and Segments under a new top-level "Customers" item.

Phased as C1..C5; C6 is explicitly deferred to a separate **paused**
follow-on issue (operator's request: "Export to mp4 on demand of the
replay movie would be a plus for v2; leave an open todo and paused
github issue for this.").

### C1 — Live scans table — PAGE-BACK TRIGGER

**Operator-stated stop-the-line trigger.** Ship this first. The
operator's exact words: "Page me as soon as the 'recent / live scans'
part is complete, as i want to enable this *now*."

- Canonical route `/admin/customers/check-ins`.
- Alias `/admin/visitors/scans` (the route the ingestion epic A3
  originally planned) so it remains valid.
- Server endpoint `GET /api/admin/customers/check-ins` per parent
  design §6.6 (subset for C1: scan rows + basic filters + facets;
  purchase summary fields can return `null`/`unknown`).
- Detail endpoint `GET /api/admin/customers/check-ins/:scan_id`
  with raw payload permission gating per parent design §13.
- Canonical `checked_in_at = COALESCE(scanned_at, created_at,
  ingested_at)`; if a normalized column was added in the ingestion
  epic, use it; otherwise use the expression + matching index per
  parent design §11 "Indexes to add or verify".
- Newest-first paginated/virtualised table with the C1 columns in
  parent design §6.3.
- Basic filters (server-side SQL, NOT client-only): site,
  checked-in date range, ingest source, document type, scan status,
  authentication status, state, postal prefix.
- Row drawer with normalized fields + address/geocode panel + raw
  JSON panel (permission-gated; if Helios lacks the permission
  infrastructure, hide the raw panel rather than expose unguarded).
- Lightweight auto-refresh (every 15–30s) plus manual refresh; live
  status chip showing latest `checked_in_at` / `ingested_at`.
- No purchase joins, no map, no IA changes in C1.
- After deploy, post the C1 status comment on parent issue #9 per
  parent design §16.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C1`.

### C2 — Purchase-history facets + matching layer + CSV export

- New compatibility views over the existing CRM/orders source:
  `customer_order_facts` and `customer_order_line_facts` per parent
  design §5.3. Use the same business definitions the existing CRM
  page already uses.
- `visitor_scan_customer_matches` match layer per parent design §5.4
  with the precedence table (default purchase-history filters use
  `confidence >= 85`).
- Extend `/api/admin/customers/check-ins` to compute and return:
  `purchase.match_*`, `purchase.history_at_checkin`,
  `purchase.prior_order_count`, `purchase.last_purchase_at`,
  `purchase.converted_after_checkin`, `purchase.visit_*`,
  `purchase.lifetime_*` per parent design §6.6 sample response.
- Add purchase filters (parent §6.4.4):
  - purchase history at check-in (repeat/no-prior/unknown);
  - visit conversion (yes/no/unknown);
  - first-time purchaser conversion;
  - prior order count bands;
  - lifetime spend bands;
  - average basket bands;
  - last purchase recency bands;
  - products / product categories (via line-item facts);
  - site of prior purchases.
- Visit window (default 12h) operator-controllable per parent
  design §6.4.4.
- Add summary strip + facet counts per parent §6.5.
- Data-quality chips: unmatched scans, missing geocode,
  low-confidence matches.
- CSV export of current filter view; raw VeriScan payload
  **excluded** by default per parent §13.
- Definitions tooltip on every purchase metric.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C2`.

### C3 — Customers IA + CRM/Segments move

- New top-level Customers nav with children Check-ins, Map, CRM,
  Segments per parent §4.1.
- Move existing CRM page to `/admin/customers/crm`.
- Move existing Segments page to `/admin/customers/segments`.
- Add backwards-compatible aliases for old CRM/Segments routes per
  parent §4.2; query params must be preserved.
- No functional change to CRM or Segments behaviour; this is IA only.
- Consistent CustomersLayout / breadcrumbs across the four pages.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C3`.

### C4 — Static customer-origin map

- Route `/admin/customers/map` per parent §7.
- MapLibre GL; default NYC-focused viewport; site pins for `bx`
  and `mh` from site metadata (add if not present).
- Server endpoint `GET /api/admin/customers/map` per parent §7.4;
  reference SQL shape in parent §7.5; default `origin=id_address`,
  `agg=grid`, `grid=250m`.
- Server coarsens grid / warns when payload would exceed budget
  (parent §11 perf budgets).
- Shared filters with Check-ins (date, site, purchase history,
  conversion, document/age).
- Encoding panel (Vega-Lite-style) per parent §8.3 with channels
  `color`, `size`, `opacity`, `strokeColor`, `strokeWidth`; always-
  visible legend; colorblind-safe defaults; default preset
  "purchase-repeat-basket" per parent §8.2; encoding config
  serialised in URL state.
- Marker click → inspect drawer with aggregate metrics +
  representative scan IDs + "open matching Check-ins" deep link
  carrying the equivalent filter set.
- No exact home-address pin display by default; exact-point mode
  is gated per parent §7.3 and §13.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C4`.

### C5 — Replay playback

- New endpoint `GET /api/admin/customers/map/timeline` per parent
  §9.3; finite bucketed event series (NOT streaming) per parent
  §9.1; default bucket size per parent §9.4; server coarsens to
  meet feature-count budget (parent §11).
- Playback URL state (`bucket`, `play`, `speed`, `lifetime`,
  `fade`, `loop`, `tail`, `enc`, `viewport`) per parent §9.2;
  share URL restores the full replay configuration.
- Client lifetime/fade math per parent §9.5; default loop behaviour
  `tail=clear` per parent §9.6; small visual pause at reset.
- Controls per parent §9.7: play/pause, scrubber + current
  timestamp, speed/lifetime/fade selectors, loop toggle, reset,
  "open current frame in Check-ins" action.
- Marker rendering uses MapLibre/WebGL layers (NOT thousands of
  DOM markers) so we hit the 30–60fps target on real data
  volumes.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` → loads paused, controls remain
  available; tabular "events in current frame" fallback.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: C5`.

### C6 — DEFERRED to separate paused issue

C6 (MP4 export of the replay) is **NOT** in this child epic. It is
filed as a separate paused issue in this repo titled "Customers UX
v2: export customer-origin replay to MP4". That issue is paused on
creation and only un-pauses after C5 lands and the operator
explicitly asks for it. Do not start C6 work as part of this epic.

## Out of scope

- VeriScan webhook ingestion + `visitor_scans` table + backfill CLI
  + ingestion admin page — owned by the sibling
  [`./EPIC_PLAN.md`](./EPIC_PLAN.md) child epic.
- agenix / nginx / systemd / DNS changes — `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`.
- Customer-facing UI of any kind. Helios is operator-only.
- Edit / delete of `visitor_scans`. Append-only ground truth.
- External geocoding / reverse-geocoding.
- Marketing automation, campaign sending, loyalty mutation,
  segment-membership mutation.
- Websocket / Kafka / event-bus realtime architecture.
- MP4 export (C6 — separate paused issue).

## Data-model coordination with the ingestion child epic

The Customers UX needs the following from `visitor_scans` (parent
design §14). Most are already present in the ingestion design; the
items below are coordination points to confirm with the sibling
ingestion epic before C2 lands:

1. Canonical `checked_in_at` — either a normalized column added by
   ingestion or the documented `COALESCE(scanned_at, created_at,
   ingested_at)` contract + matching index per parent §11.
2. `issuing_state` distinct from address `state` (operator
   explicitly listed this as a filter facet).
3. Raw normalized columns for `phone`, `email`, `first_name`,
   `last_name`, `birth_date` for the match layer.
4. Coordinate validity surfacing (zero/null guarded out of the map).
5. Per-row `site_slug` correctness for backfilled rows.
6. Site metadata (display name, store lat/lon, timezone, address)
   reused or added for the map's site pins and distance-from-site
   filter.

If any of these is missing when C2 / C4 start, file a focused
change request against the ingestion child epic before proceeding.

## Phase dependencies

- C1 depends on the ingestion child epic's A1 having landed (table
  + at least one row from webhook or backfill). C1 code can be
  written and unit-tested against the schema in parallel; the
  page-back trigger requires a real live row.
- C2 depends on C1 (shared endpoint + drawer) and on
  CRM/orders being readable from helios-server (already true; the
  existing CRM page reads it).
- C3 depends on C2's CRM/Segments not being broken by the
  move; can land in parallel with C2 if the routes are wired
  carefully.
- C4 depends on C2's match layer + facts views (for purchase
  encodings) and on coordinate-validity guards in `visitor_scans`.
- C5 depends on C4.
- C6 is deferred; do not start.

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. C1..C5 each have at least one commit on `automation` master
   carrying `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9` and the matching
   `Phase: C<n>` trailer.
2. The C1 page-back STATUS comment has been posted on
   [#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9) and the
   operator has confirmed live visibility.
3. At least one live VeriScan check-in is visible end-to-end:
   webhook → row → Check-ins table → matched customer →
   purchase summary → map marker → replay frame.
4. C6 has been filed as a separate paused issue in this repo and
   linked from the C5 completion comment.
slots.delegationNote: Implement the Helios Customers top-level section consuming visitor_scans and existing CRM/orders data: C1 live Check-ins page (PAGE-BACK TRIGGER per operator — paging on real-row visibility); C2 purchase-history filters/facets with scan→customer match layer + facts views + CSV export; C3 Customers IA moving existing CRM and Segments under /admin/customers/* with old-URL aliases; C4 static MapLibre customer-origin map with Vega-Lite-style encoding picker (color/size/opacity/strokeColor/strokeWidth) + legend + drilldown; C5 finite-bucketed replay playback with operator-controlled speed/lifetime/fade and shareable URL state. C6 MP4 export is explicitly DEFERRED and already filed as paused issue FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#32.
slots.title: Customers UX: Check-ins, purchase-history filters, origin map, and replay playback

# Helios catalog-pricing overhaul — step 3 — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#35](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/35).
> The authoritative umbrella is
> [`docs/epics/catalog-pricing-overhaul/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo. This child epic covers **step 3** of that umbrella. Prior
> steps shipped:
> [step 1 = automation#55](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/55)
> (temporary Categorical Family Explorer + size-group normalizer + LitAlerts
> geographic-limit verification) and
> [step 2 = automation#58](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/58)
> (brand-subdivided families + a lazy per-brand-categorical-family LitAlerts
> **market-match diagnostic panel** with candidate scores, per-factor
> breakdown, and data caveats).
>
> **Do not close #35** on completion, and do not put
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#35` on any landing commit without operator
> confirmation — #35 is a long-lived, multi-step umbrella (same caution as #55
> and #58). Reference this step-3 child issue and rely on the delegation link
> back to #35.

## Step-3 operator ask (verbatim intent)

> "Providing feedback in an efficient way" *in the page itself* is the next
> step to take. Consult with Oracle on how this should be arranged to maximize
> operator efficiency on site-reviewing matches (ideas to consider include
> highlighting significant price outliers for particular review, potentially
> having the operator confirm or explain how to resolve a competitor name
> parsing / extraction issue — MOST retailers will mostly stick to a preferred
> naming convention that tends to include some aspect of unit and/or total
> sizing and/or pack qty. They tend to follow at least one convention per
> category/subcategory, if not one convention for their whole catalog. Once
> that convention is understood for that retailer, it can provide strong hints
> for subsequent listings from that retailer being examined / parsed. Consult
> with oracle on how to modify the page to best suit this purpose, especially
> when viewed in responsive / mobile. Don't waste screen space. Be efficient.
> Have oracle approve the UX design and ensure your implementation of it is
> correct.

The goal of this step is to turn the step-2 **read-only** market-match
diagnostic into a surface where the operator can **act while reviewing**: spot
the listings worth scrutinizing (price outliers), and record what a
mis-parsed competitor listing *should* have been — including the retailer's
naming convention — so subsequent listings from that retailer parse better.

## Design (Oracle-reviewed — approved with refinements)

The UX and the storage/architecture boundary below were reviewed by the
Oracle for this planning step (the operator explicitly required Oracle to
approve the UX design). The automation fleet MUST still obtain its own per-step
Oracle **design** review (before implementing) and **diff + UI** review
(before landing) — this section is the approved *shape*, not a substitute for
implementation-time review.

### The two core interactions

Both attach to the existing per-brand-categorical-family `MarketMatchPanel`
(`helios/src/client/routes/catalog/CatalogFamilyExplorerPage.tsx` +
`/api/catalog/family-explorer/market-match`). **Reuse; do not rebuild** the
panel, the shared scorer
(`helios/src/server/marketMatch/candidateScoring.ts` /
`helios/src/shared/marketMatch/confidence.ts`), or the size-group folding.

**(A) Significant price-outlier highlighting** — flag listings whose price is
a statistical outlier *within the correctly-typed, above-threshold matches for
that family* so the operator can quickly find the rows to scrutinize (a
mis-parse skewing price, or a genuinely off competitor price).

**(B) Retailer name-parsing / extraction feedback** — from a mis-parsed row,
let the operator (i) correct the extracted fields for that listing and (ii)
optionally state the retailer's naming convention, scoped by default to that
retailer × category/subcategory. Captured feedback is a durable, promotable
signal — not a hidden live parser.

### Cardinal rules (from the umbrella's core invariant + Oracle review)

- **Outlier stats are computed ONLY over above-threshold, same-hard-gated-
  family, priced candidates.** Never include below-threshold or wrong-"type-
  of-thing" candidates — doing so recreates the exact IQR-pollution failure the
  operator has repeatedly been burned by.
- **Compute outliers over the full bounded/scored set, BEFORE the display cap**
  — an outlier must never be invisible because it fell outside the top-N-by-
  score table slice.
- **The DB feedback store is NOT a second, live parser.** parsekit /
  `helios-parser-configs` remains the single authoritative *executable* parser
  after promotion. Operator feedback must not silently change production
  matching/scoring, `fuzzy_skus`, market aggregates, or IQR. Any in-page effect
  of unpromoted feedback is a clearly-labeled, opt-in **preview** only,
  excluded from aggregates.

### UX (mobile-first, no wide new table column)

Per `helios/AGENTS.md` (purpose-first, don't waste screen space) and the
"responsive/mobile, be efficient" directive:

- **Panel summary pill** — add a warning pill only when non-zero, e.g.
  `3 price review`, with a tooltip stating the IQR basis (count, median,
  fence). Show nothing when there are zero outliers (no "0 outliers" noise).
- **"Needs review" strip above the table** — when outliers exist, a compact
  section before the wide table. Desktop: one-line chips (max ~3 + "show all").
  Mobile: stacked cards, open when non-empty, each showing listing (link),
  retailer, price with a `↑$`/`↓$` direction badge, current parsed size/pack
  vs. expected family size/pack, and a **`Fix parse`** action. This is what
  lets the operator find and act on the work *without* horizontally scrolling
  the table on a phone.
- **Sticky Score cell affordances** — no new column. In the existing sticky
  score cell add a tiny `↑$`/`↓$` outlier badge and a small `Fix`/`✎` icon
  button (accessible label), plus a subtle row tint / left border and price-
  cell emphasis. These stay visible while the table is scrolled horizontally.
  A row that already has saved feedback shows a tiny `feedback`/`hint` pill.
- **Correction drawer / bottom sheet** (not inline table editing) — opened by
  `Fix parse`. Mobile: bottom sheet; desktop: side drawer. Sections:
  1. Listing context (retailer + stable id, listing link, price, distance
     band, snapshot time, score, outlier badge).
  2. Current parse vs. family expectation (two-column: current parsed
     size/pack/category/subcategory vs. the family's expected size-group /
     pack / category / subcategory).
  3. "What's wrong?" chips (`size`, `pack qty`, `category/subcategory`,
     `brand`, `name tokens/strain`, `price is genuine`,
     `not same product / no match`) that reveal only the relevant fields —
     don't front-load a giant form.
  4. Correction fields (pack count, unit size value/unit, total size
     value/unit, category/subcategory), prefilled from the current parse and
     family where possible. Keep brand correction distinct from the existing
     brand-mapping semantics unless explicitly wired into brand overrides.
  5. Convention capture (opt-in checkbox "Also propose a retailer naming
     convention"): default scope `this retailer + category/subcategory`;
     optional `retailer-wide`, `retailer + brand`, `this listing only`;
     free-text note + auto-generated examples from the corrected listing(s) +
     optional pattern chips (`brand first`, `size at end`, `pack before size`,
     `total size shown`, `unit size shown`). The operator NEVER authors
     parsekit JSON or regex.
  6. Save → persists the exact listing correction (+ convention candidate when
     selected), marks the row/card `feedback saved`, and MAY show a clearly-
     labeled preview of the corrected parse/score for that one listing.

### Storage / architecture boundary (Oracle recommendation)

Three layers, with a firm boundary between live operator input and the
authoritative parser:

1. **Helios DB — operator feedback inbox** (the live web input target). One
   normalized feedback table with a discriminated `kind` (listing correction /
   convention proposal). Store: `useCase`/`sourceKind` (`litalerts` for this
   page), `sourceListingId`, `fuzzySkuId`, **`retailerId`** (stable — display
   name is not; add it to the API contract), raw listing name + input
   hash/snapshot, family key / brand key, matched catalog product id (if any),
   corrected structured fields, issue/disposition type, convention note +
   scope + examples, actor/time, and `status` (`draft | promotion_requested |
   promoted | rejected | superseded`). This immediately improves the *operator
   workflow* (show saved feedback on rows, prefill future corrections for the
   same retailer/scope, "convention candidate exists" hints, exact-listing
   corrected-parse preview) **without** changing production scoring.
2. **No active DB parser.** Do not let DB conventions silently reparse
   subsequent listings and change the panel's real score/counts — that forks a
   second parser beside parsekit and breaks the audit page's "this is the real
   matcher" invariant. If cross-listing impact is ever wanted, it must be an
   explicit, default-off, clearly-labeled `Preview with unpromoted retailer
   hints` toggle, excluded from aggregates/IQR/pricing and never persisted into
   `fuzzy_skus` as canonical. (Out of scope for this step unless the operator
   asks — see below.)
3. **parsekit / `helios-parser-configs` — authoritative executable parser.**
   Promotion path (agent/reviewer, not the web UI): select DB feedback for a
   retailer/scope → export corrected examples as parsekit **goldens** →
   create/update `helios-parser-configs/use-cases/litalerts/parsers/<tenantId>.jsonc`
   (`litalerts` is the current source; reserve `competitor-ecom` for direct
   competitor e-commerce sources later) → run parsekit validation/goldens →
   review/push → Helios parser registry loads the new snapshot → mark the DB
   feedback `promoted` with parser/rule id + config sha. This is the concrete
   realization of the runtime-adjustable parser-config work tracked under
   [automation#19](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/19).

## Scope owned by this child epic (tasks)

### T1 — Price-outlier domain helper + market-match contract fields (must-have)

- Pure, deterministic outlier helper using **Tukey IQR fences** (`< q1 −
  1.5·IQR`, `> q3 + 1.5·IQR`) over above-threshold, same-family, finite-priced
  candidates (use `preTaxPrice`; post-tax is a constant multiplier). Guards:
  no statistical flag when basis count `< 5`; when IQR is effectively zero,
  fall back to a conservative tight-cluster rule (flag only when the value
  differs from the median by **both** an absolute and relative threshold, e.g.
  `≥ max($5, 20% of median)`). Never remove/down-rank a candidate for being an
  outlier — review signal only.
- Extend `catalogFamilyMarketMatch` contract: per-candidate
  `priceOutlier: null | { kind: 'low' | 'high'; delta; fence; median; basis }`,
  a response-level `priceOutlierSummary`, and a `reviewCandidates` array
  (full-set outliers, bounded — e.g. 25 — with an overflow warning) so
  outliers survive the display cap.
- Tests: min-sample suppression, high/low IQR flags, tight-cluster fallback,
  below-threshold excluded, missing-price excluded.

### T2 — Outlier UX in the existing panel (must-have)

- Summary `price review` pill (only when non-zero); "Needs review" strip/cards
  above the table; sticky score-cell `↑$`/`↓$` badge + `Fix` action + row
  tint. No new wide column. Mobile cards usable before the horizontal table.
  Preserve existing caveat pills and the below-threshold divider.

### T3 — Feedback persistence: schema + API + contracts (must-have)

- DB migration for the normalized feedback table (discriminated `kind`) with
  the fields listed under *Storage layer 1*. Add stable identifiers to the
  candidate contract (esp. **`retailerId`** from the raw LitAlerts data).
- Endpoints: fetch feedback for visible candidate/retailer ids; create/update
  feedback; update status. Zod contracts; no first-party `any`.
- **Record a DB cost/plan** for the new queries; reuse existing indexed reads
  where possible.

### T4 — Parse-correction drawer / mobile bottom sheet (must-have)

- Drawer/sheet per the UX above: listing context, current-vs-expected parse,
  issue chips, correction fields, opt-in convention proposal (scope + note +
  examples + pattern chips), save + `feedback saved` row badge. Optional
  clearly-labeled exact-listing corrected-parse/score preview.

### T5 — Promotion support (data shape + export, not web-side git writes) (must-have, light)

- Land the `status`/promotion metadata fields and an export/report query or
  endpoint shaped for an agent/reviewer to turn feedback into parsekit goldens
  + a `helios-parser-configs/use-cases/litalerts/parsers/<tenantId>.jsonc`
  entry. Document the promotion path. **Do not** build web UI that writes git
  configs.

### T6 — Review / polish gate (must-have)

- Deterministic, prod-resource-free tests; mobile screenshots / UI-review
  notes; Oracle design + diff + UI review before close; explicitly re-verify
  **no new unbounded LitAlerts pulls** (reuse the bounded nearest-retailer
  fan-out). Record the Agent Gate Record on each landing.

## Nice-to-haves (land only if cheap; don't block the step)

- A "price is genuine" disposition that suppresses already-reviewed outlier
  warnings. **Reconfirm with the operator** whether a saved "genuine" mark
  should permanently suppress future outlier flags for that listing/retailer.
- `Outliers only` / `Review first` filter toggle.
- Showing existing retailer convention hints on every row from that retailer.
- An export command that emits candidate parsekit golden cases directly.

## Explicitly out of scope for step 3 (later steps / other work)

- Making unpromoted DB feedback change production scoring/matching, `fuzzy_skus`,
  or any market aggregate (the default-off preview toggle is the only allowed
  cross-listing effect, and even that is out of scope unless the operator asks).
- Auto-generating or committing `helios-parser-configs` from the Helios web UI.
- The broader parsekit read-path migration owned by
  [automation#19](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/19).
- Turning the temporary page permanent/polished, the full A-subset picker,
  price/promo application, and the detailed click-through market-data page
  (umbrella D) — later steps.
- Any new/unbounded market-data collection or LitAlerts pull.

## Top risks to call out (for the implementing fleet)

1. **Second-parser risk** — active DB conventions would diverge from parsekit
   and make the audit panel stop reflecting the real matcher. Keep DB feedback
   inert w.r.t. production scoring.
2. **Outlier pollution** — stats MUST exclude below-threshold / wrong-family
   candidates, or they reproduce the IQR-pollution failure.
3. **Display-cap invisibility** — compute outliers before the display cap; keep
   `reviewCandidates` visible.
4. **Small-sample noise** — no statistical flag below the minimum basis; use the
   conservative fallback when IQR is tiny.
5. **Mobile hidden actions** — never rely on an off-screen table column; use the
   review cards + sticky score-cell action.
6. **Unstable retailer identity** — persist by retailer id / source ids / raw
   hash, not display name.
7. **Promotion target ambiguity** — the current source is LitAlerts, so promote
   into `use-cases/litalerts`; only use `competitor-ecom` for direct competitor
   e-commerce sources.

## Validation

Each landing commit MUST:

1. Land green on `automation` CI: `cd helios && npm run check` (server +
   client typecheck + `vitest run`) and `npm run build`. Add unit tests for the
   outlier helper (T1) and the feedback contracts/queries (T3). No first-party
   `any`; no bug-masking fallbacks; deterministic, prod-resource-free tests.
2. Be visible on `vps-nixos-3` after the sanctioned `self-deploy-helios`
   (never a manual `systemctl restart` of the helios units).
3. **Record a DB cost/plan** for every new feedback query (T3), reusing
   existing indexed catalog/partner reads where possible.
4. Honor canon gates: Oracle **design** review (before implementing) and
   **diff** review (before landing) for this operator-facing surface, plus
   Oracle **UI** review of the drawer + outlier affordances on mobile
   (signal-to-noise, next-action, no wasted space). Record the Agent Gate
   Record on each landing.
5. Carry the cross-repo completion trailer on the master-landing commit. **See
   the multi-step-umbrella caution above** — confirm the intended `Satisfies:`
   target with the operator on #35 before landing so a single child completion
   does not prematurely close the umbrella.

## Completion signal for the child

This child epic is done when:

- The market-match panel highlights significant price outliers (IQR-based,
  correctly-typed basis) via a compact, mobile-usable "Needs review" surface
  and sticky-cell badges, with outliers surviving the display cap (T1 + T2).
- The operator can, from a mis-parsed row, open a drawer to correct the
  extracted fields and optionally record a scoped retailer naming convention,
  persisted to the Helios feedback store with stable identifiers, and see the
  row marked as having feedback (T3 + T4).
- The promotion path into `helios-parser-configs` is documented and the data
  shape/export supports it, without any web-side git writes (T5).
- All gates green (T6), demonstrated on `vps-nixos-3`.
- An operator-facing closure/status comment is posted on
  `virusdave/top-level#35` prefixed `<!-- task-dag:status -->` (do NOT
  hand-post the `<!-- task-dag:completion -->` cross-repo signal — the peer
  repo's completion-sync workflow emits it from the `Satisfies:` trailer),
  including the live page URL, commit links, the chosen outlier method + basis
  rules, and the feedback→promotion boundary, so the operator can iterate into
  the next step.
slots.delegationNote: Implement step 3 (T1 price-outlier IQR helper + market-match contract fields, T2 outlier UX in the existing panel, T3 feedback persistence schema/API + stable retailerId, T4 parse-correction drawer/bottom sheet with scoped convention capture, T5 promotion support into helios-parser-configs use-cases/litalerts, T6 review/polish gate) per docs/epics/catalog-pricing-overhaul/child-epics/automation/step-3-in-page-feedback/EPIC_PLAN.md. Keep DB feedback inert w.r.t. production scoring (no second parser); outlier stats over above-threshold same-family priced candidates only, computed before the display cap; mobile-first, no wide new column. Honor per-step Oracle design/diff/UI reviews and confirm the Satisfies trailer target with the operator on #35 before landing - #35 is a long-lived multi-step umbrella, do not let a single child completion prematurely close it.
slots.title: Helios catalog-pricing overhaul - step 3: in-page operator feedback (price-outlier review + retailer name-parse convention capture) (top-level #35)

# Tooling `--help` safety — `Nicponskis/github-worker` child epic

> Parent epic: [virusdave/top-level#47](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/47)
>
> The implementation commit on this repo's master MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47
> ```

## Step 0 — read canon first

Ephemeral checkout of top-level master, then read
[`docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md)
"Code standards" (the `--help` rule) and
[`docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md)
"Serving services".

## The requirement

Every invocable tool must accept `-h`/`--help`, print usage, and exit `0`
**before any effect** (env-var assertions, locks, network/API calls,
`git` fetch/push, file writes). Handle `--help` first, ahead of all other
option parsing and required-env checks — in particular, before any
`: "${VAR:?}"` assertions, so `--help` works without CI env vars set.

## Known violators (audit for more — this list is a starting point)

- `scripts/agent-waste-export`
- `scripts/waste-page`
- `scripts/agent-prompt-budget` (the github-worker mirror)
- Any other scripts in `scripts/` you find during the audit.

`scripts/render-capsule` already handles `-h`/`--help` — mirror its
pattern.

## Verifying

Run each tool with `--help` and confirm it prints usage and exits 0 with
no side effects (no writes, no network, no env-var requirement).

## Finalize

Commit with a plain imperative subject (no `feat:`/`fix:` prefix) and the
`Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47` trailer; push to this repo's default
branch.
slots.delegationNote: Handle -h/--help before any env assertions or effects (agent-waste-export, waste-page, agent-prompt-budget, etc.).
slots.title: Add innocuous --help to github-worker helper scripts

# automation child epic — eliminate hand-built JSON

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#44](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/44)
> — "Our critical tooling should NOT be constructing json by hand."
> **Parent epic plan:** [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md).
> **Governing rule:** canon `docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md` "Code
> standards" — *never hand-build / hand-parse / hand-validate JSON or YAML*.

## Scope

One offender found in the automation repo (survey 2026-07-08):

**`ads/google/scripts/run-cluster-sweep.sh`** builds `manifest.json`
structurally in shell — a sequence of `printf` lines that emit the object
braces, the `clusters` array, and the inter-element commas by hand. The
scalar *values* are already escaped via `jq -Rn`, so the escaping risk is
low, but the object/array/comma scaffolding is still hand-assembled and a
future edit (a new field, a reordered element) can easily desync a comma
and emit invalid JSON.

Convert the whole manifest to a single `jq -n` invocation that takes the
run id, timestamp, slug list, and the `strategic_context_present` boolean
as `--arg`/`--argjson` and builds the object/array natively. Re-grep the
repo before finishing to confirm nothing else was missed:

```sh
rg -n -e '\\"[a-zA-Z_]+\\":' -e "printf '\{" -e 'echo .*\{.*:.*\}' ads scripts
```

## Constraints

- The emitted `manifest.json` must be equivalent in *content* (same keys,
  same values, `schema_version: 0`, placeholder `kind`/`note`, per-slug
  `{ "slug": …, "files": ["verdict.md"] }` entries) — this is a correctness
  refactor, not a schema change. Formatting/whitespace may differ (it is
  machine-consumed); verify any downstream reader still parses it.
- Follow the repo's own `AGENTS.md` and task-dag workflow.

## Acceptance

- `run-cluster-sweep.sh` produces `manifest.json` via `jq -n` (no
  hand-assembled braces/commas); output parses under `jq -e` and matches
  the prior structure for a representative slug list.
- The **final** commit on the automation `master` that demonstrates this
  child epic's acceptance criteria are met carries
  `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#44`. Intermediate commits MUST NOT carry
  that trailer unless the child epic is already fully satisfied.
slots.delegationNote: Build manifest.json with a single jq -n (--arg/--argjson); keep the content/schema identical.

# Unified landing-page engine — `automation` (Helios control plane) child epic

> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) (rev 3). Re-read the parent
> before starting any phase — this child epic is a **thin index** over
> the parent's design, not a re-statement of it. The parent is
> authoritative; if this file ever drifts from it, the parent wins.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#13
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>`
> trailer so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post per-phase
> progress on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo (the brain)

Helios becomes the single optimization engine. This repo owns
everything in the parent EPIC_PLAN §4 ("Helios owns") and the Helios
slice of the §10 migration phases:

- **Unified config source of truth** (`config/landing-pages/`):
  `families/<family>.blueprint.jsonc` (the X1–X5 stack + slot
  requirements), `sites.jsonc` (migrated from mss `sites.yaml` — parent
  decision 3), the frozen X2 `trust-anchor-cash-debit.jsonc` contract,
  and `policies/` selection-policy templates.
- **CEL policy compiler** — compiles the selection policy into the
  sandboxed, locally-evaluable form mss consumes (parent §6; locked
  decision 1: CEL, never `eval`). **Critical schema constraint
  (parent §6.1, rev-3):** the policy output is a **weight per `NUM`**
  on the existing canonical `/SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM` schema. The
  compiler MUST validate that every variant id it references exists in
  the active mss per-purpose `*VariantIds` registry / respects
  `MAX_VARIANT_BY_PURPOSE` — it must **never** emit a new URL shape or a
  `NUM` that mss can't serve.
- **Bundle publisher** — compiles clusters + blueprints + site
  overrides + approved copy/imagery + policy into one immutable,
  signed, versioned bundle; writes it to the read-only-for-mss `/cloud`
  artifact root behind an atomic `current.json` pointer with
  last-known-good (parent §5, decision 5). Signing keys live with
  Helios, **never** on the shared mount.
- **Signed kill-list** in `current.json` keyed on the canonical
  `(site, purpose, slug, num)` variant tuple (`disabled_variants`, parent
  §6.1) — narrow, monotonic, auditable; not a second policy language.
- **`lp_events` ingestion** — `POST /v1/lp-events/batch` append-only
  bulk insert into time + `bundle_id`/`policy_id`-partitioned tables
  (parent §8; decision 4: log ALL, cost-bounded by mss-side spool +
  ~15-min batch; no sampling). Every new query ships with an analyzed
  plan + index strategy (canon §3).
- **Leaderboard with propensity-corrected (unbiased) lift** over
  served + counterfactual variants (parent §6, §9); surfaces deltas so
  "shut off the loser" is statistically honest. Promotion stays a
  one-click operator action.
- **Validation CLI** (`helios lp-bundle validate`) + dry-run publish.
- **Delete the cross-repo commit producer** — content flows only via
  the bundle (parent §1 defect 2, §10 P5/P8).
- **`page-dave -p 4`** on fail-closed bundle validation and on any X2
  change (parent decision 2, §7).

## Phases (follow parent §10 order; Helios slice)

P0 contracts/flags · P1 publisher dry-run · P2 (mss-led; provide bundle)
· P3 shadow-compare feed · P4 preview bundle · P5 dual-publish + stop
cross-repo writes · P6 canary (publish + revenue-guardrail auto-revert)
· P7 full · P8 decommission. See parent §10 for the per-phase
traffic-impact and rollback columns.

## Out of scope (owned elsewhere)

The mss thin runtime (bundle loader, CEL evaluator wiring into the
existing random-rotation middleware, renderer, Sweed adapter,
delivery-zone gate, event spool/flusher) is the
`Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites` child epic. **No URL-schema changes in
either repo** (parent §6.1, rev-3). Lane B auto-API ad mutation, sub-
bundle-cadence bandits, and new-site stand-up remain out of scope
(parent §15).
slots.delegationNote: Control-plane slice. BINDING: keep the canonical /SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM URL schema; the policy compiler emits weights per existing NUM, never new routes (parent EPIC_PLAN rev 3 section 6.1).

# Helios catalog-pricing overhaul — step 4 — purchase-family review

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#35](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/35).
> The authoritative umbrella is
> [`docs/epics/catalog-pricing-overhaul/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../../EPIC_PLAN.md).
> This child follows the deployed pending-purchase refinement loop from
> [FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#74](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/74)
> and the existing purchase-inventory pricing lifecycle.
>
> **Do not close #35** on completion and do not put
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#35` on a landing commit. This step delivers
> one missing subset/review path; #35 remains a long-lived umbrella with price
> application, promos, detailed market pages, and other subsets still open.

## Why this is the next step

The operator reported that automation#74 was intended to unlock #35, but its
closing agent did not follow the soft cross-issue linkage. Automation#74 made
the pending-purchase refinement loop available in production. Separately, the
existing purchase-inventory lifecycle can refresh and reprice the exact
product ids in one received purchase and deep-link to the generic pricing-run
review.

What remains missing from #35 is the operator's common post-receive review
shape: start from the products in a recent purchase (**A-iv**), then include
the remaining members of their categorical families (**the A-v
augmentation**) so the operator can assess consistent family pricing. This
child adds that read-only bridge to the existing Family Explorer. It does not
replace the exact-product pricing lifecycle or imply that the whole umbrella
is complete.

## Oracle-reviewed design

Oracle approved this shape with the following refinements:

- Key the scope by the canonical purchase identity **`(dealerId, poId)`**,
  not a pending-purchase packet id. Packets are revisioned proposal artifacts;
  the received purchase and its pricing lifecycle already share the stable
  purchase tuple.
- Enter from the Catalog purchase detail / pricing-lifecycle surface. A
  pre-receive packet link is out of scope until a typed, authoritative
  packet-to-purchase identity bridge exists; never infer one from titles or
  untyped JSON.
- Reuse the lifecycle's definition of purchase products: distinct mapped
  `sweed_product_id` values from positive-quantity purchase lines. Reuse or
  extract that resolver rather than implementing a second definition.
- Reuse the shared Family Explorer grouping and size-equivalency normalizer.
  Expand valid seeds to the union of their **nonbrand categorical families**;
  brand mode subdivides the same returned membership rather than changing the
  scope.
- Keep the current lifecycle actions — market refresh, exact-product reprice,
  pricing review, approval, price verification, and release — unchanged.
  This child is a secondary read-only review action.

## Operator experience

From a purchase detail, **Review purchase families** opens the Family Explorer
scoped to that purchase. The first screenful must answer:

1. Which purchase is being reviewed, and how to return to it?
2. How many mapped positive-quantity products seed the review?
3. Which displayed products are **In this purchase** versus **Family peer**?
4. Which purchase lines/products could not be expanded safely, and why?

Purchase seeds sort before peers. Out-of-stock catalog peers remain included:
stock is not a family-membership criterion. Existing lazy market-match,
outlier, and parse-feedback interactions remain available for valid brand
subfamilies. Whole-catalog `/catalog/family-explorer` behavior remains
unchanged when no purchase scope is supplied.

Mobile must not make the operator traverse the existing wide variant table to
learn the essential facts. Purchase context, return action, seed/peer status,
name, brand, size, unresolved warnings, and grouping controls must be readable
without horizontal scrolling.

## Integrity and boundedness

Fail closed rather than manufacturing or silently widening a family:

- A positive-quantity line with no product mapping contributes to a visible
  unmapped-line count but cannot seed a family.
- A mapped product absent from the current catalog snapshot is reported by id
  as unresolved; it is never silently omitted.
- A seed missing category, subcategory, pack count, or a parseable numeric
  size appears under **Unable to expand safely** with the exact reason. It
  adds no peers and exposes no family market aggregate.
- A null brand may participate in a valid nonbrand family. Its existing
  no-brand market-match behavior remains honest and unchanged.
- Seed and member caps are explicit and tested. An over-limit request fails
  wholly with counts; it never returns a misleading truncated family.
- The return link is constructed from the validated purchase identity. Do not
  accept an arbitrary `returnTo` URL.

The implementation must reuse or extract the existing short-TTL catalog
family snapshot instead of creating an independently computed family model.
Measure and record `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`, endpoint latency, source row
count, response row count, and response bytes. Prefer the existing ~3,500-row
catalog projection; add schema/index work only if measurements justify it.

## Tasks and dependencies

### T1 — Canonical purchase-product scope

- Reuse or extract the positive-quantity mapped-product resolver used by the
  purchase lifecycle.
- Distinguish purchase-not-found, zero positive-quantity lines, unmapped
  lines, mapped product ids, and mapped ids absent from the catalog snapshot.
- Add deterministic, production-resource-free tests.

### T2 — Bounded purchase-scoped family API (depends on T1)

- Add a strict viewer-gated endpoint keyed by `(dealerId, poId)`.
- Reuse the canonical shared grouping and catalog snapshot; return valid
  family members with seed/peer provenance plus unresolved metadata.
- Enforce explicit seed/member caps and fail closed on overflow.
- Record the DB plan, latency, row counts, and response bytes.

### T3 — Purchase-scoped Family Explorer UX (depends on T2)

- Add URL-aware loading while preserving whole-catalog mode.
- Render purchase identity, one-action return, seed/peer totals and badges,
  seed-first ordering, and the **Unable to expand safely** section.
- Preserve existing valid-family market-match/outlier/parse-feedback tools.
- Add desktop and narrow-mobile tests/screenshots, including mapped,
  partially unmapped, unresolved-family, empty, and over-limit scopes.

### T4 — Purchase-lifecycle entry point and review gates (depends on T3)

- Add **Review purchase families** as a secondary action on the purchase
  pricing-lifecycle surface without changing lifecycle state or pricing
  actions.
- Obtain Oracle implementation diff, DB-efficiency, and responsive UI review;
  address all blocking findings.
- Verify that the new action cannot enqueue a refresh, create a pricing batch,
  write prices/promos, release inventory, or mutate lifecycle state.

### T5 — Deploy and stability verification (depends on T4)

- Land with green exact-commit automation CI and the required focused tests.
- Deploy only through the sanctioned `self-deploy-helios` wrapper.
- Verify the authenticated production surface with real **read-only** mapped,
  partially unmapped, and empty purchase scopes; do not create test purchases,
  pricing runs, or other production data.
- Record durable rollout evidence and a status update on top-level#35 that
  explicitly says the umbrella remains open.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A purchase-detail operator can open the scoped explorer and return in one
   action each, preserving `(dealerId, poId)`.
2. Seeds exactly equal distinct mapped product ids from positive-quantity
   purchase lines; zero-quantity and unmapped lines never seed a family.
3. Every valid seed is visibly marked, and every peer has the same canonical
   nonbrand family key as at least one seed. Brand mode only subdivides that
   membership.
4. Out-of-stock peers remain included.
5. Unmapped lines, catalog-missing products, and incomplete/unparseable seeds
   are visible and never widen a family or market aggregate.
6. Existing lazy market-match, outlier, and parse-feedback behavior remains
   available and bounded for valid brand subfamilies.
7. Whole-catalog Family Explorer behavior is unchanged without purchase scope.
8. The new path is read-only and leaves exact-product lifecycle repricing
   unchanged.
9. Caps and over-limit behavior are explicit, deterministic, and tested.
10. Mobile exposes context, return action, seed/peer distinction, unresolved
    warnings, and grouping controls without requiring horizontal scrolling.
11. The exact delivered commit is deployed and stable, while #35 remains open.

## Explicit non-goals

- Replacing or family-expanding the lifecycle's exact-product refresh,
  pricing batch, approval, live-price verification, or release gates.
- Price writes, promo creation, Sweed changes, or lifecycle state mutation.
- Pending-purchase packet-id scoping or fuzzy packet-to-PO linkage.
- Multi-purchase selection, site-stock/time-window subsets, vendor families,
  or claiming all of A-v.
- Fixing incomplete taxonomy/size data in this child; surface it safely for
  later correction.
- The detailed market-data page and pricing/promo actions in D(ii), D(iv), and
  D(v), or closure of the umbrella.

## Required delivery gates

- Oracle design review is recorded above; implementation still requires
  Oracle diff, DB-efficiency, and mobile UI review before landing.
- Run focused deterministic tests, `cd helios && npm run check`, and
  `npm run build`; do not use production serving resources as test fixtures.
- No migration is expected. Any discovered need for schema or production DB
  mutation requires a fresh Oracle DB review and explicit operator approval
  before apply.
- Every landing records an Agent Gate Record. The final leaf includes
  sanctioned deploy and stability evidence.
- Child completion references its own automation issue/delegation. It must not
  emit `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#35` or otherwise close #35.
slots.delegationNote: Implement step 4 only. Keep the existing exact-product purchase lifecycle unchanged; use dealerId plus poId, reuse canonical family grouping, preserve whole-catalog mode, require Oracle diff/DB/mobile reviews and a deploy/stability leaf, and do not emit Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#35.

# Fuzzy SKU Modelling — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#4](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/4).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/fuzzy-sku/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in the
> top-level repo; this child epic scope is **the entirety of the
> `automation` slice** of that design (fuzzy-SKU is single-repo, with
> the parent epic existing only as the operator's coordinating
> umbrella).  Every implementation commit that lands on `automation`
> master and satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#4
> ```
>
> so the top-level coordinator's
> `cross-repo-completion-sync.yml` ingests it as a completion ref.

## Configuration format policy (settled)

**All configuration in this epic is [JSONC](https://github.com/microsoft/node-jsonc-parser)**
(strict-JSON value payload with `//` and `/* */` comments, trailing
commas allowed).  **No YAML / TOML / significant-whitespace formats**
anywhere we get to choose; this is the operator-mandated house style
and applies to every config file landed under this epic.  Reuse the
JSONC loader pattern already in flight in
[`helios-parser-configs`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/helios-parser-configs)
(the pending-purchases parser configs Helios already loads at
runtime).

The one carved-out exception is GitHub Actions workflow files
(`.github/workflows/*.yml`), which GitHub Actions mandates be YAML.

## Scope owned by this repo

- **FuzzySKU data model** — Python (or whatever the implementing
  service uses; pick once at P0) types + JSON schema for sparse
  `(value, confidence, rule_id, evidence_span)` per-attribute tuples,
  mirroring the attribute set of our `variant` model.
- **Config-driven parser engine** — JSONC ruleset loader (one
  per-competitor file under
  `config/fuzzy-sku/competitors/<slug>.jsonc`), plus the four shared
  dictionaries under `config/fuzzy-sku/_shared/*.jsonc`
  (`strain_dictionary`, `brand_dictionary`, `form_factor_rules`,
  `weight_rules`).  Rule semantics per parent design §"Per-competitor
  parser config".
- **Parser CLI + coverage report** — operator-facing tool that takes
  a competitor slug and a sample of listings, runs the parser, and
  emits a per-attribute coverage report (`coverage % by attr`,
  `unresolved_token frequency table`, `evidence-span heatmap`).
  This is the iteration loop for adding / tuning competitor configs.
- **Matcher** — 3-tier matcher per parent design §"Matcher" (exact-SKU
  / exact-family / weighted), with thresholds tunable via
  `config/fuzzy-sku/matcher-weights.jsonc`.
- **`competitor_match` DB table** + migrations.  Persists
  `MatchRecord`s only (FuzzySKUs are compute-on-demand).
- **`match-refresh` job** — runs on (a) new LitAlerts snapshot
  landing, or (b) any `config/fuzzy-sku/**` file changing on
  `automation` master.  Full table replace per refresh.
- **Repricing integration** — replaces the existing best-effort
  substring path with `MatchRecord` consumption (`tier ∈ {exact-sku,
  exact-family}`, `score ≥ repricing_min_score`, default 0.85).
- **Landingpage comp integration** — emit a tier-2 match feed that the
  landing-page templates render in the "comparable nearby" section,
  with hand-curated fallback when no tier-2 candidates exist.
- **Helios `/matches` admin page** — filter by competitor + tier +
  score, per-listing evidence inspection, operator verdict button
  ("this match is wrong" / "this should have matched").  Verdicts
  recorded but **not** auto-applied; they are inputs to the operator's
  config-tuning loop.
- **Helios `/fuzzy-skus` review page** (per
  [2026-05-19 operator follow-up](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/4#issuecomment-4489690498))
  — distinct surface from `/matches`, focused on the *parsed
  FuzzySKU* itself.  Lists FuzzySKUs filterable by competitor +
  parse-status + presence of `unresolved_tokens`; per-listing detail
  shows `raw_name` with per-attribute evidence-span highlighting,
  the attribute table with `(value, confidence, rule_id, evidence)`,
  unresolved-token affordances, and per-attribute operator flags
  (`correct` / `wrong-value` / `should-be-unknown` /
  `should-have-been-extracted`).  Flags persist in a new
  `fuzzy_sku_review_flag` table.  See parent design
  §"FuzzySKU review page + LLM-assisted config suggestions (v1)" for
  the full UI spec.
- **LLM-assisted config-suggestion endpoint** (`/api/fuzzy-sku/suggest-config`)
  — operator-triggered from the `/fuzzy-skus` page; bundles the last
  N flags + current competitor JSONC + referenced shared dictionaries
  and asks the LLM for a `{rationale, diff, affected_rule_ids}`
  payload.  Diff is rendered side-by-side in the UI; operator
  accept-path opens a PR on `automation` master (commit message
  carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#4` + the originating flag
  refs).  Prompt template versioned at
  `config/fuzzy-sku/llm/suggest_config.prompt.jsonc`.  The endpoint
  never writes config directly; LLM-offline degrades gracefully (UI
  button disabled with visible warning, review / flagging still
  works).
- **Operator runbook** — `docs/runbooks/fuzzy-sku-onboarding.md`
  walking through adding a new competitor end-to-end, **including**
  the `/fuzzy-skus` flag → LLM-suggest → review-PR loop for ongoing
  rule tuning.

## Out of scope

- ML / LLM in the **parse/match hot path** (suggestion endpoint is
  config-tooling only; matcher and parser stay deterministic).
- Auto-merge of LLM-suggested config diffs (operator always reviews
  and lands the PR manually).
- Global product graph (FuzzySKUs are ephemeral per-listing
  resolutions).
- Backfill of historical LitAlerts snapshots (parent design defers).
- Generic NER pipeline (scope is cannabis listings, attribute
  vocabulary is fixed by `variant`).

## Phases

Mirrors parent design §"Phase plan"; commits should reference these
phase tags in their messages so the coordinating progress comments
(top-level#4 leaf task 2) can group them cleanly.

- **P0.** FuzzySKU + FuzzyAttr types + JSON schema; pick the JSONC
  parser library; stub the loader so subsequent phases can register
  configs.  No parsing, no matching yet.  Land the schema doc under
  `docs/fuzzy-sku/schema.md`.
- **P1.** Config-driven parser engine + the four `_shared/*.jsonc`
  dictionaries + the first competitor config (pick the
  highest-volume LitAlerts source as the pilot — operator-confirmable
  at P1 start).  Ships the parser CLI + coverage report.
- **P2.** Matcher (3 tiers) + `competitor_match` table + migration +
  `match-refresh` job.  Wired but not yet consumed by repricing or
  landingpage.
- **P3.** Repricing integration — swap the substring path for
  `MatchRecord` consumption.  Tier-3 visible in admin UI but excluded
  from auto-repricing in v1.
- **P4.** Landingpage comp-table integration — tier-2 match feed for
  the per-product "comparable nearby" section, hand-curated fallback
  preserved.
- **P5.** Helios `/matches` admin page + operator-verdict capture.
- **P5b.** Helios `/fuzzy-skus` review page + `fuzzy_sku_review_flag`
  table + migration + `/api/fuzzy-sku/suggest-config` LLM endpoint +
  UI for diff review (accept / edit / reject) + PR-open path on
  accept.  Builds on P5's admin-shell scaffolding (auth, layout,
  table component); parser/match-refresh outputs it consumes come
  from P1/P2.
- **P6.** Wire-up + e2e + onboarding runbook (with `/fuzzy-skus`
  flagging + LLM-suggest loop included) + onboard 2 more competitors
  (total 3) to clear the parent-epic acceptance bar.

P3 / P4 / P5 are parallel after P2 lands.  P5b lands after P5.

## Acceptance criteria

Lifted from parent design §"Acceptance criteria"; this child epic is
satisfied when:

1. At least **three competitors** have working configs in
   `config/fuzzy-sku/competitors/` and the per-competitor coverage
   report shows **≥ 70 % of listings** producing a tier-1 or tier-2
   match against our catalog (measured on a manually-curated
   100-listing gold set per competitor, checked in under
   `config/fuzzy-sku/gold-sets/`).
2. Repricing's daily run consumes `MatchRecord`s and the
   per-competitor coverage on its decision log shows **≥ 2×** the
   number of matched listings vs. the previous substring path,
   measured over a 7-day window.
3. The Helios `/matches` admin page is reachable and renders the most
   recent run's matches with filtering, evidence, and the verdict
   button.
4. The Helios `/fuzzy-skus` review page is reachable, renders the
   most recent run's parsed FuzzySKUs with per-attribute evidence
   highlighting, supports the four per-attribute flag verdicts
   (`correct` / `wrong-value` / `should-be-unknown` /
   `should-have-been-extracted`), and the "Suggest config edits"
   button returns a reviewable JSONC diff that the operator can
   accept (PR-open path), edit-then-accept, or reject.  At least
   **one** LLM-suggested PR is merged end-to-end against a real
   competitor config and produces a measurable coverage uplift in
   the next `match-refresh` run.
5. The operator runbook (`docs/runbooks/fuzzy-sku-onboarding.md`)
   walks through adding a new competitor end-to-end (config →
   parser CLI → coverage report → matcher threshold check → ship)
   **and** documents the ongoing `/fuzzy-skus` flag → LLM-suggest →
   PR-review tuning loop.
6. At least one landing-page (any product page) renders a tier-2
   "comparable nearby" section drawn from `MatchRecord`s.
7. Every `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#4` commit lands on
   `automation` master (not a feature branch) per
   [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/automation/blob/master/AGENTS.md).

## Coordination back to the parent epic

- File one progress comment on `virusdave/top-level#4` per phase
  completion (P0..P6), linked to the `automation` commit(s) that
  landed it.  These comments are emitted by the top-level
  coordinating leaf task 2 of
  [`docs/epics/fuzzy-sku/task-dag-breakdown.json`](../../task-dag-breakdown.json);
  the operator does not need to hand-write them.
- Final closure: once the P6 commit lands on `automation` master with
  the `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#4` trailer, the cross-repo
  completion-sync workflow will materialise the completion ref
  (`tasks/completions/4/virusdave/automation/<peer_issue>/<sha>`),
  the top-level final-closure leaf task fires its `page-dave` with the
  Helios `/matches` URL + coverage report + 7-day comparison +
  runbook link, and `close-completed-issues.yml` closes the epic
  issue automatically.
slots.delegationNote: FuzzySKU data model + per-competitor JSONC parser + matcher + repricing/landingpage-comp integration + Helios /matches + /fuzzy-skus review page + LLM-suggest-config loop
slots.title: Fuzzy SKU modelling — data model + parser + matcher + integrations

# task-dag child epic: durable broken-master convergence

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Make the existing repair-chain state machine converge from durable GitHub
evidence even when a push-triggered Actions run is missed, duplicated, or dies
between side effects. Keep task-dag's chain ref authoritative and converge to
exactly one open repair issue and one discoverable repair task for each active
policy-red streak.

## Required implementation

1. **One canonical reconciler**
   - Add `repair-reconcile <owner/repo> <branch>` as the bounded entry point
     shared by Actions hints and the host backstop.
   - Reuse and extend `classify`, `tree-fix-outcome`, `verify-target`, repair
     chains, and `repair-ticket`; do not add another classifier or state store.
   - Resolve the current top-level registry generation internally before every
     mutation. Implement strict `off|observe|enforce` semantics and fenced
     downgrade cleanup exactly as specified by the binding design.

2. **Strict evidence and policy**
   - Validate `.github/ci-repair-policy.json`, bind required checks to exact
     names and App identities, paginate check runs, and select reruns by the
     design's deterministic lifecycle tuple.
   - Persist canonical bounded evidence, first-seen grace state, policy digest,
     evidence/decision keys, aggregate, and reconciliation diagnostics in the
     existing chain history. Identical decisions are no-ops.
   - Only current-head required-check evidence may close a chain. Unknown,
     malformed policy, API failure, stale green, and identity mismatch fail
     closed.

3. **Lease, fencing, and convergence**
   - Add metadata-only reconciliation lease acquisition/renewal that preserves
     every classifier field and uses monotonically increasing fences.
   - Fence every issue, comment, task-ingestion, and scheduling-ref mutation;
     perform post-mutation readback and compensate stale accepted HTTP effects.
   - Keep the oldest matching repair issue canonical, close extras, retire all
     duplicate scheduling projections through a repair-specific validated
     operation, and retain the specified non-scheduling audit ref.
   - Make issue and continuation-comment ingestion directly replayable by
     reconciliation, with stable repair/attempt identities and existing
     `verify-target` protection for already-launched workers.
   - Preserve one blocked high-priority repair object for `blocked`,
     `policy-invalid`, and `non-fast-forward`; only authoritative green closes
     it.

4. **Contracts and telemetry**
   - Update chain parsers, namespace validation, invariant documentation,
     golden fixtures, CLI help, dry-run output, and migration compatibility for
     old `creating@…` leases.
   - Emit the bounded structured pass fields and error codes required by the
     design. Never log tokens, check output, issue bodies, or one-off content.

## Deterministic tests

Use temporary bare origins and a fake paginated GitHub API. Cover missing and
delayed runs around grace, accepted/failed checks and reruns, duplicate names,
pagination, GitHub `Date` clock-skew rejection, old-head green/red, policy edits
and malformed policy, API outage, registry rollback, and rejection of
caller-supplied generation or mode. Cover `observe→enforce` replay of an
existing decision and `enforce→observe|off` races with stale callers, late
accepted HTTP effects, and refusal to delete or retarget a registry row until
successful `off` cleanup readback. Exercise every lease-loss and interruption
boundary, expired-holder overlap, transient zero-object windows, missed
issue/comment events, duplicate issue/task convergence, blocked-chain
preservation, continuation deduplication, tree-fix outcomes, and non-fast-
forward heads. Add a property test over event order, stale holders, and crash
points proving eventual one-chain/one-open-ticket/one-discoverable-task
convergence. Run `task-dag validate --strict` and full task-dag presubmit.

## Rollout and rollback

Land inert. Complete credential preflight and a 24-hour dry-run comparison
before any projection is enabled. Then support observe-only chain writes,
followed by projection for task-dag and top-level, missed-run/crash drills, and
48 hours of stable evidence before peer expansion.

Rollback disables callers first and preserves chain refs/issues. Never run an
old `repair-ticket` against a new active substate. Any downgrade to legacy
requires the binding design's compare-and-set migration and readback; never
delete coordination refs or tickets as rollback.

This is critical fleet infrastructure. The binding architecture already has
Oracle approval, but the implementation worker must get Oracle architecture
rereview for any design change and Oracle review of the actual final diff
before commit. Iterate to APPROVE.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```
slots.delegationNote: Extend the canonical repair-chain state machine with strict evidence, fenced idempotent reconciliation, exactly-one issue/task convergence, deterministic crash/concurrency tests, and inert staged rollout.
slots.title: Make broken-master repair converge durably and exactly once

# task-dag child epic: durable comment reconciliation

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#64`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/64)
· Binding design:
[`durable-dispatch-input-recovery.md`](../../../../designs/durable-dispatch-input-recovery.md)

## Goal

Make GitHub issue-comment delivery at-least-once and idempotent. The existing
event workflow remains fast, but a canonical reconciler can recover any
eligible comment still present in GitHub even when that event or workflow was
lost.

## Required implementation

1. **Receipt contract and compatibility**
   - Define well-formed human, completion, and machine-skip provenance under
     `gh/comments/<issue>/<comment-id>`.
   - New receipts identify repository, issue, comment ID, disposition,
     `created_at`, observed `updated_at`, and body SHA-256.
   - Accept existing human/completion provenance as immutable legacy shapes.
   - Update known-namespace validation, lifecycle documentation, and golden
     fixtures in the same change.

2. **Origin-authoritative atomic ingestion**
   - Check origin receipt before classifying current content; an unpushed local
     ref is never terminal.
   - Human comments atomically create receipt plus frontier with create-only
     leases. Completion comments atomically create receipt plus completion
     fact when needed. Marked comments create receipt only.
   - Install local refs only after remote success.
   - On races, validate the origin winner. Same observed body with a different
     disposition is fatal; a different observed version is superseded by the
     first valid winner.
   - A failed multi-ref transaction cannot leave half a disposition.

3. **Canonical `reconcile-comments` command**
   - Use the same classifier as event ingestion.
   - Support recent overlapping and complete-audit modes, dry-run, bounded
     apply batches, `ingestion_start_at`, and explicit historical
     `(issue, comment-id)` allowlists.
   - Enumerate with stable ascending updated order and full pagination; filter
     by `created_at`; exclude pull requests from authoritative issue metadata.
   - Fetch allowlisted historical comments directly by ID.
   - First successfully observed version wins; later edits do not remint.
   - Continue past poison comments but return nonzero and a failed heartbeat.
   - Honor rate-limit headers and never claim completeness after truncation or
     an API/classification failure.
   - Run idempotent post-scan convergence so a completion fact whose immediate
     close attempt failed still reaches the existing backstop.

4. **Coherent event runtime**
   - Replace split raw-file downloads with one checkout at one resolved
     task-dag revision. Keep the reusable workflow logic-free for callers.
   - Preserve the current App-token close semantics and least permissions.

5. **Metrics and operator contract**
   - Emit requests/pages/all returned comments, eligibility and disposition
     counts, failures, duration, rate-limit state, and recent/full success
     heartbeat data in machine-readable output.
   - A capacity ceiling fails loudly and directs sharding; it never truncates
     silently.

## Required tests

- Event versus sweep race yields one provenance and one task effect.
- Injected push failure yields neither half of a human disposition.
- Race loser ignores local-only state, validates a matching origin winner,
  rejects conflicting same-version disposition, and accepts a superseding
  different observed version.
- Marked comment creates one skip receipt and no frontier.
- Completion receipt/fact is atomic; failed derived close is later converged.
- Multi-page scans with equal timestamps and strict-`since` overlap omit
  nothing; page failure does not mark success.
- Pull-request and pre-boundary comments are excluded; explicit historical
  allowlist comments are fetched directly.
- Edits, malformed comments, legacy provenance, 403/429, dry-run, bounded
  batches, and capacity ceilings follow the binding design.
- `task-dag validate --strict` and the full task-dag presubmit pass.

## Rollout and rollback

Land receipt/atomicity support before any watchdog can emit new shapes. Verify
the event path recognizes both legacy and new receipts. Publish the reconciler
disabled until github-worker dry-runs each repository's first audit.

Rollback removes or disables the reconciler/event-runtime change without
rewriting refs. Valid additive receipts remain recognized audit evidence.

This is critical infrastructure. Obtain Oracle design review before coding and
Oracle diff review after implementation; iterate to APPROVE before commit.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#64
```
slots.delegationNote: Implement origin-atomic comment receipts and effects, reusable reconciliation, coherent event tooling, deterministic race and recovery tests, and strict validation/documentation.
slots.title: Make GitHub comment delivery durable and idempotent

# About-Us Unification — `nixos-sbc` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#6](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/6).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/about-us-unify/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo; this child epic scope is **strictly the
> `nixos-sbc` slice of that design** — namely "stand up HTTP Basic
> auth on the two FBNYC / FBUS staging vhosts so Dave can review
> the unified about-us page before it ships to production."
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `nixos-sbc` master and
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#6
> ```

## Scope owned by this repo

### N1. HTTP Basic auth on staging vhosts

The staging hosts already exist:

- `staging.freshlybaked.nyc` — enabled by
  `services.mss.sites.freshlybaked.hosts.staging.enable = true;`
  in `hosts/vps/sites-mirror.nix` (~line 179), with ACME forced on
  (~line 185).
- `staging.freshlybaked.us` — enabled by
  `services.mss.sites.freshlybakedus.hosts.staging.enable = true;`
  with explicit `hostName = "staging.freshlybaked.us";` in the
  same file (~lines 197–198).

What's missing: neither vhost has authentication. Anyone who finds
the hostname (or who scrapes the cert transparency log) can hit
the staging site. For this epic the operator chose **HTTP Basic
auth** with credentials `letmein` / `letmein` and realm
`Freshly Baked staging`. These are intentionally weak — staging
contains no PII, no auth tokens, no payment surface; the bar is
"keep crawlers out, keep accidental visitors out, give Dave a
review URL he can paste anywhere without worry."

Concretely, add `basicAuth` (or `basicAuthFile` if the module
author prefers an out-of-band htpasswd file) on the staging
virtual-host blocks. The simplest in-tree option is:

```nix
services.nginx.virtualHosts."staging.freshlybaked.nyc" = {
  # ... existing config (enableACME, locations, etc.) ...
  basicAuth = { letmein = "letmein"; };
  basicAuthMessage = "Freshly Baked staging";
};

services.nginx.virtualHosts."staging.freshlybaked.us" = {
  # ... existing config ...
  basicAuth = { letmein = "letmein"; };
  basicAuthMessage = "Freshly Baked staging";
};
```

If the underlying nixos `services.mss.sites.<x>.hosts.staging`
module submerges the vhost config so that direct
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>` overrides cause merge issues
(it does fall back to `lib.mkForce` in at least one place — see
the `enableACME = lib.mkForce true;` precedent on line ~185),
follow the same `lib.mkForce` pattern.

If the module instead exposes a typed option for staging auth (or
the implementer prefers to add one), the option name should be
`services.mss.sites.<site>.hosts.staging.basicAuth` taking
`{ <user> = <password>; }` for in-tree credentials or
`services.mss.sites.<site>.hosts.staging.basicAuthFile` taking a
`/run/secrets/...` path for agenix-managed credentials. For this
particular epic the inline `letmein:letmein` is fine; no agenix
secret is warranted for credentials that ship in cleartext in
git history by operator request.

### Deploy

Per `nixos-sbc/AGENTS.md`: rebuild and apply the system closure
via `self-deploy` on `vps-nixos-3` (the production VPS that hosts
both staging vhosts — see the per-host module at
`hosts/per-host/vps-nixos-3.nix`).

### Smoke test

Before posting the completion `Satisfies:` trailer, verify both:

```sh
curl -I https://staging.freshlybaked.nyc/      # expect 401
curl -I -u letmein:letmein https://staging.freshlybaked.nyc/   # expect 200/302 to age gate
curl -I https://staging.freshlybaked.us/       # expect 401
curl -I -u letmein:letmein https://staging.freshlybaked.us/    # expect 200
```

## Out of scope

- DNS or ACME changes for either staging hostname — both already
  resolve and both already get certs through the existing
  `enableACME` path.
- Any change to `services.mss.sites.<x>.hosts.production.*`.
- Any change to the `mostly-static-sites` build / source — that's
  owned by the peer child epic.
- Any oauth / SSO / IP-allowlist replacement for Basic auth.
  Operator picked Basic intentionally; revisiting is a separate
  epic.

## Phases

- **N1.** Single commit landing the `basicAuth` (+ `basicAuthMessage`)
  additions on both staging vhosts, deployed via `self-deploy`,
  smoke-tested with `curl`.

## Cross-repo dependencies

- None. The mostly-static-sites peer epic's M1/M2/M3 do not gate
  N1, and N1 does not gate them. Landing N1 first is in fact
  useful because it lets Dave confirm the basic-auth challenge
  works against the *existing* staging pages before any content
  change is visible.

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. N1 commit has landed on `nixos-sbc` master carrying the
   `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#6` trailer.
2. The system closure has been applied to `vps-nixos-3` via
   `self-deploy`.
3. The two `curl` smoke tests above pass.
slots.delegationNote: nginx basic auth letmein/letmein realm "Freshly Baked staging" on both staging vhosts so Dave can review the unified about-us before production deploy
slots.title: About-Us unification — HTTP Basic auth on staging.freshlybaked.nyc + staging.freshlybaked.us vhosts
