# Helios LP evolution inspection pages — automation child epic

> **Child epic of** [`virusdave/top-level#25`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/25)
> (`lp-evolution-inspection`). The **parent epic plan is authoritative**
> for design, philosophy, IA, data sources, page content, and the
> boundary vs #24:
> [`virusdave/top-level:docs/epics/lp-evolution-inspection/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/lp-evolution-inspection/EPIC_PLAN.md).
> This child holds the Helios (`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`) implementation
> scope only.
>
> **Every implementation commit** that satisfies any part of this epic MUST
> carry the trailer `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#25`, and SHOULD also
> carry `Phase: P<n>` (`P1`..`P7`) so the cross-repo-completion-sync
> workflow posts a per-phase progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope (one-line)

Implement the **LP-system companion** to the GAds evolver introspection
dashboard ([#24](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/24)) under
the existing per-site, grant-gated `/metrics/gads-<site>/` GAds tab system
(IA + grants from [#18](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/18)):
an **LP Evolution** overview with **inferred disapproval attribution**
(LP-related vs ad-related — Google gives only a coarse signal, so this is a
**cross-entity LP/family correlation** engine, not a field lookup),
**suspect-LP / suspect-family** steering, and a **slop-vs-signal**
copy-quality lens, plus an **LP Iteration** per-run / per-candidate
drilldown. It reads the evolver's own
LP decision/outcome data already in the Helios DB / filesystem. An
**introspection surface for how Helios reacted on landing pages and joint
ad/LP decisions**, not a re-implementation of Google's ad dashboards.
Rapid hill-climb, **not** audit-grade (decision
[0003](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-kb/decisions/0003-joint-gads-lp-optimization-not-audit-grade.md)).

## Binding constraints

- **Reuse #18's IA, grants (`gads-bronx` / `gads-midtown` / `gads-all`),
  scope registry, and serving model verbatim.** No new route shapes, no
  forked access model. `gads-all` is its own grant, never synthesised.
- **Coordinate with #24 — do not duplicate its ad-evolver pages.** Keep
  #24's `/evolution` + `/iteration` for ad-evolver loop health; #25 owns
  LP + joint-decision inspection. Cross-link both ways (parent plan §3);
  do not move #24's LP-reaction panel.
- **Server-derived site predicate.** Never trust a client-supplied
  site-widening param. Per-site pages must not leak cross-site rows.
- **Cheapest defensible DB use.** Bounded aggregate queries over the
  existing small tables (`landingpage_ad_outcomes`, `gads_ad_attempts`,
  `gads_lp_rollup`) + bounded reads of recent L2/L3/morning-bundle
  artifacts. **No** per-event fact table, no always-on derivation worker,
  no rollup/hypertable/CAGG/HLL in V1.
- **Honest approximations + first-class `unknown`.** Every estimate badged;
  never a fabricated precise-looking number; **never force an
  attribution** — `unknown` is a real answer. Honest empty states where a
  write path / data field is not yet confirmed.
- **Migrations do not auto-apply on deploy.** Any schema change is applied
  on prod by the agent only after Oracle DB review **and** explicit
  operator approval, then verified live (canon §3).

## Attribution is inference, not a lookup (binding — parent §0.1)

Google **deliberately withholds** the precise reason for a policy limit /
disapproval. The only signal it gives is **which hierarchy level**
(campaign / asset group / ad group / asset / ad) was limited and **which
policy topic** fired. There is **no ad-text-vs-LP source field** to read.
So the LP-vs-ad verdict is **inferred** by **correlating per-entity policy
state over the shared-final-URL/LP and page-family dimensions** (e.g. all
ad groups on a given LP limited while same-family siblings on other LPs
stay clean → that LP is suspect; the pattern may span a whole family). The
fix for a suspect LP must repair the *right* page — **never** flatten the
ad copy **or** the landing page into generic slop.

## Attribution criteria are hill-climbable, not constant (binding — parent §0.2)

The operator approved on the explicit condition that **the attribution
criteria themselves must be hill-climbable** — a simple fixed heuristic
(e.g. "95% of ads pointing at the LP are rejected") will be too crude once
the low-hanging fruit is gone. Binding on the Helios implementation:

- **No magic numbers in code.** Every verdict-deciding threshold, weight,
  and minimum (contrast minimums, suspicion-score weighting, topic→lever
  priors, confidence cutoffs) lives in **one named, versioned criteria
  set**, not scattered literals. V1 may be a deliberately simple ruleset,
  but it must be swappable without rewriting the engine.
- **Versioned + traceable verdicts.** Each attribution result records the
  **criteria version** that produced it plus the raw inputs it saw
  (implicated/clean contrast counts, topics, hierarchy level, outcome
  sequence). Responses carry the active criteria version; the UI badges it
  on every verdict/suspect row and exposes a "how this verdict was decided"
  trace so the operator can tune the *criteria*, not just read output.
- **V1 = explicit substrate for tuning, not a learned model.** An
  automated/learned attribution model is out of scope for V1; making the
  criteria explicit, parameterised, versioned, and auditable is in scope.
  See parent §0.2 / §7.2.2.

## Data + capability gates (P1 must resolve before the engine claims a verdict)

- Confirm prod population/scoping of `landingpage_ad_outcomes`,
  `gads_ad_attempts`, `gads_lp_rollup`, L2/morning-bundle artifacts, L3
  outputs.
- **Confirm whether candidate copy + rejected candidates are recorded** in
  artifacts (the slop-vs-signal "why rejected" view depends on it).
- **Confirm the inference substrate** (the centerpiece depends on it, not
  on a Google source field — there isn't one): (a) we capture **per-entity
  policy state over time + hierarchy level + policy topic**; (b) we can
  **join each entity to its final-URL/LP and to its page family** (likely
  via `landingpage_ad_outcomes` / `gads_lp_rollup` / the cluster registry).
  Without the LP/family join the correlation engine cannot run.
- Confirm whether any cheap LP text snapshot exists (LP-promise match); do
  **not** crawl live pages in V1.
- Emit a **capability matrix** mapping every parent-plan panel (§7–§8) to
  `wired` / `partially wired` / `not wired yet`; missing fields become UI
  badges, not guessed data.

## Phases (detail in the parent plan §6–§8)

| Phase | Deliverable | Closure criteria |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Data audit + capability matrix | Confirm prod population/scoping of the tables/artifacts above; confirm candidate/rejected-candidate presence; **confirm the inference substrate** — per-entity policy state + hierarchy level + policy topic, **and** the entity→final-URL/LP and entity→family join the correlation engine needs (no Google ad-vs-LP source field exists); produce the panel→capability matrix. No per-site page ships until site scoping is safe; the engine must have the LP/family join before claiming a suspect. |
| **P2** | Minimal schema/index support | Reuse #24's `site` fix for `gads_ad_attempts` if landed; else add `site text null` + best-effort backfill; hide unknown-scope per-site, show under `gads-all` badged. Optional tiny artifact/run-index table **only if** P1 proves scans are expensive (no large JSON/prompts in DB). Cheap indexes only if justified by plans. No rollup/hypertable/CAGG/HLL. Migration gated on Oracle DB review + operator approval. |
| **P3** | Backend contracts + **correlation/inference engine** | Typed `GadsLpEvolutionResponse` / `GadsLpIterationRunsResponse` / `GadsLpIterationRunDetailResponse` (capability flags in every response); grant-gated `GET /api/gads/lp-evolution`, `/api/gads/lp-iterations`, `/api/gads/lp-iterations/:runId`; server-derived site predicate; bounded ranges. **Cross-entity correlation engine (parent §7.2):** group per-entity policy state by shared final-URL/LP and family; emit `lp_related`/`ad_related`/`mixed`/`undetermined` with evidence grade, confidence bucket, and implicated-vs-clean contrast counts (anti-coincidence guard); never force a verdict. **Criteria are a single named, versioned set (parent §0.2): no magic numbers in code; each verdict records its criteria version + raw inputs; the response carries the active criteria version.** Tests cover correlation logic (suspect LP when siblings clean; no false suspect on thin contrast) + access (Bronx cannot read Midtown/all; `gads-all` explicit; unknown-scope hidden per-site; payload bounded). |
| **P4** | LP Evolution UI (overview + attribution + suspect LP/family) | `/metrics/gads-<site>/lp-evolution` (parent §7): scope/freshness/capability strip, LP heartbeat, attribution snapshot + `?panel=attribution` detail, **suspect-LP / suspect-family ranked list (parent §7.2.1)**, planned-action×outcome matrix, hotspots, funnel guardrail, recent decision log. Honest empty/low-confidence states + contrast counts; no fake attribution. **Mandatory Oracle UI review before ship.** |
| **P5** | Slop-vs-signal lens | Quality triage on overview + `?panel=slop-signal` (parent §7.3): deterministic context-token preservation, generic-phrase + reuse detector, intent specificity, hook preservation, optional LP-promise match (badged if unwired), chosen-vs-rejected comparison, context-loss watchlist, **positive-examples table**. Deterministic/explainable V1 lens; candidate/rejected absence handled honestly; no opaque LLM score required. |
| **P6** | LP Iteration browser | `/metrics/gads-<site>/lp-iteration` (parent §8): bounded run timeline + run detail (decision flow + attempt/candidate table), candidate detail drawer, bounded artifact links, DB-only fallback + badge when L2 JSON missing. No unbounded historical-file loads. Run-detail links from #24 can target this page. |
| **P7** | Docs, tests, rollout readiness | Operator runbook (read attribution + evidence grades; interpret slop risk; interpret `unknown`; debug missing site scope; #24 vs #25); access + classifier tests; query-cost notes; UI reviewed; epics updated; ready for **gated `self-deploy-helios`** (no deploy from the planning worker). |

## Backend contract sketch (P3)

```ts
GadsLpEvolutionResponse          // overview + attribution + slop/signal summaries + capability flags
GadsLpIterationRunsResponse      // bounded run timeline
GadsLpIterationRunDetailResponse // single run: decision flow + attempt/candidate rows + artifact links
```

Each response carries `capabilities` flags (`siteScopedAttempts`,
`entityPolicyState`, `policyTopics`, `entityLpJoin`, `familyMapping`,
`candidateText`, `rejectedCandidates`, `lpTextSnapshot`, `lpRollup`) so the
UI badges exactly what is / isn't wired. (Note: there is **no**
`explicitPolicySource` flag — Google does not expose an ad-vs-LP cause;
the verdict comes from the correlation engine, gated on `entityLpJoin` /
`familyMapping`.) Site scope is derived server-side from the
authenticated GAds metrics tab context, never from a widening query param;
follow Helios's existing route/site-encoding convention (the binding rule
is the access model, not the literal endpoint strings).

The attribution payload also carries the **active criteria version** (e.g.
`attributionCriteriaVersion`) and, per verdict/suspect row, the criteria
version + raw inputs that produced it (parent §0.2 / §7.2.2), so the UI can
badge which ruleset decided each call and the operator can hill-climb the
criteria rather than just read their current output.

## Out of scope (V1)

Causal lift / off-policy estimates, win probability, credible intervals,
regret; prompt/rule approval workflow + prompt-diff persistence; opaque LLM
copy-quality score; live LP crawling for promise-match; per-click cost /
revenue / ROAS; anomaly detection; heatmaps; any Timescale
CAGG/hypertable/HLL.
slots.delegationNote: Build the LP-system companion to the GAds evolver introspection dashboard: inferred disapproval attribution (LP vs ad, with hill-climbable/versioned criteria), slop/signal copy-quality inspection, and LP iteration run drilldowns under the existing grant-gated GAds metrics IA.
slots.title: Helios LP evolution inspection pages

# Helios `/metrics` v1.1 rework — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
> (reopened after v1 shipped as a single-chart picker with stubbed
> data). The authoritative design for this rework is
> [`docs/epics/business-metrics/EPIC_PLAN_v1_1_REWORK.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN_v1_1_REWORK.md)
> in the top-level repo; the original v1 design at
> [`docs/epics/business-metrics/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> remains authoritative for the bits v1.1 does **not** rework
> (schema, API contract, `MetricDef` shape, v2 deferrals).
>
> The corresponding v1 child epic is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#21`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21);
> this issue tracks the v1.1 rework only — please do not reopen the
> v1 child.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation` master that
> satisfies any part of this rework MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: R<n>`
> trailer (note `R`, not `P`, to distinguish from v1 phases) so the
> cross-repo-completion-sync workflow posts a per-phase progress
> comment on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

Everything described in the parent rework addendum, broken out by
phase below. **Re-read the parent rework addendum before starting
any phase** — this child plan is deliberately a thin index over
the parent, not a re-statement of the design. The parent is the
single source of truth for both UX and data-contract decisions.

The original v1 codebase under `server/src/metrics/**`,
`server/src/api/metrics.ts`, `server/src/api/metric-annotations.ts`,
and the `MetricChart` / `/metrics` React tree is the **starting
point**, not the throw-away — v1.1 is a re-shaping, not a rewrite.

### R0 — Reality audit + v1.1 scope freeze

- Inventory every `MetricDef` currently registered under
  `server/src/metrics/**`. For each entry record:
  - whether it is real-data backed or backed by a synthetic stub
    today (this is already partly visible from the existing
    `STUB:` description prefix; the audit should be authoritative
    and machine-readable, not based on the description string);
  - which `sweed_orders` / `sweed_*` / external table(s) it reads;
  - what would be required to flip it to real data (which ingest
    follow-on it depends on; how big the SQL is).
- Reconcile this list against the v1 metric enumeration in
  [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) §"v1 metric panels".
  Resolve any orphans (registered but not in spec) and any holes
  (in spec but never registered).
- Produce the **canonical v1.1 panel list** as a checked-in
  artefact: `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics-v1_1-canonical.md` (or
  equivalent location consistent with the existing runbook). Each
  row: metric id, dashboard section, chart type, current data
  status, required source, planned R4 tranche, "in v1.1"
  yes/no/deferred.
- For any panel proposed to be **deferred from v1.1**, post a
  comment on [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
  listing the proposed deferrals + rationale and wait for explicit
  operator sign-off **before** removing them from the registry.
- Extend the `MetricDef` type with the `dataQuality` block from
  the parent rework addendum (`status: 'real' | 'experimental'`,
  `sources: string[]`, optional `freshnessSla`). Add a
  pre-deploy / CI check that rejects a build where any
  production-visible `MetricDef` is missing `dataQuality` or has
  `dataQuality.status !== 'real'`. (Permit `'experimental'` only
  for entries explicitly marked `dashboard.defaultVisible: false`.)
- Hide / remove demo metrics (`_demo.flat_line`,
  `_demo.random_walk` — and any other v1-era placeholders) from
  the production registry.

**Exit criteria**: a single authoritative list answers "what
ships in v1.1", every entry has a status + source-table mapping,
the build refuses to ship a stub-as-real, demo metrics are gone
from production.

### R1 — Dashboard shell rework

- Replace the existing single-chart picker layout at `/metrics`
  with a **sectioned multi-panel grid**. Sections per the parent
  addendum suggestion (Executive health / Revenue mix / Inventory
  risk / Operations / Context) — the precise grouping is owned by
  this phase and may be retuned, but the result must be a
  dashboard, not a picker.
- Extend `MetricDef` with a `dashboard: { section, order, size,
  defaultVisible }` block. R0's canonical list drives where each
  metric lands in the grid.
- Refactor the existing left-nav into a **table-of-contents**:
  sticky, jumps to dashboard sections / metrics, shows a status
  dot (real / fresh / stale / error) per metric. Clicking a TOC
  entry **scrolls to** the dashboard panel; it must not replace
  the dashboard with a single chart.
- Preserve all v1 global controls (site filter, time range,
  aggregation, axis lock state) at the top of the dashboard, and
  ensure global state is encoded in URL query params so the page
  is shareable / reload-safe.
- All existing real-data panels render as dashboard tiles using
  the existing `<MetricChart/>` component, scaled down to tile
  density.

**Exit criteria**: `/metrics` on a desktop browser shows multiple
charts simultaneously without the operator interacting with the
nav; the left-nav no longer hides every chart except one;
URL-encoded global state is restored on reload.

### R2 — Synchronized crosshair / hover-readout

- Extend `TimeAxisContext` (or add a sibling `TimeHoverContext` —
  implementer's choice; the existing context wiring may make a
  sibling cleaner) with the `TimeHoverBus` contract from the
  parent rework addendum:

  ```ts
  type TimeHoverEvent = {
    t: string;
    sourcePanelId: string;
    bucket?: string;
  };

  type TimeHoverBus = {
    publish(event: TimeHoverEvent): void;
    clear(sourcePanelId: string): void;
    subscribe(listener: (event: TimeHoverEvent | null) => void): () => void;
  };
  ```

- Implement the publish path inside `<MetricChart/>` mousemove,
  `requestAnimationFrame`-throttled. No React state updates on
  every pixel.
- Implement the subscribe path: on subscription update, render a
  vertical crosshair at the nearest bucket boundary + a per-series
  readout pane (panel-local, no shared layout shift).
- Only locked, time-compatible panels (line / area / stacked-area
  / bar) participate in cross-panel hover. Scatter / map / table
  panels are free to ignore the bus or publish their own
  underlying timestamp on hover-over-element if useful (weather
  scatter dot → publish that day so other panels can show the
  corresponding day's values).
- Explicit "no data at hovered `t`" rendering — do not silently
  show the last available value, that misleads the operator.
- Verify zero network traffic on hover (devtools network tab
  empty while mousing across the dashboard).

**Exit criteria**: hovering one locked time-series panel updates
every other compatible locked panel; readouts are accurate at the
hovered bucket; performance is smooth (no visible jank on a
~10-panel dashboard); detail route inherits the same behaviour.

### R3 — Routable expansion + drill-down UX

- Add a `/metrics/<metricId>` detail route. Use the same React
  shell + `TimeAxisContext` as the dashboard so global state
  persists when expanding / collapsing.
- Add an expand affordance to every dashboard tile (title-bar
  icon at minimum; whole-tile click on the chart title is also
  acceptable). Clicking routes to the detail view, carrying the
  current global state in the URL.
- Detail view renders the same `<MetricChart/>` larger, with a
  richer legend / readout pane and annotation controls. The
  detail view's "back to dashboard" preserves dashboard scroll
  position.
- Extend `MetricDef` with a `drilldowns?: DrillDef[]` array:

  ```ts
  type DrillDef = {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    appliesTo: 'series' | 'category' | 'point' | 'row';
    queryParam: string;
  };
  ```

- Implement, at minimum, these v1.1-required drilldowns:
  - **`category.*`** stacks: click a category band → reload the
    panel split by that category's subcategories.
  - **`fulfillment.*`** panels: click a fulfillment-type band /
    legend entry → detail view filtered to that fulfillment.
  - **`delivery.*`** panels: click a zone band → detail view
    filtered to that delivery zone.
  - **`slowmovers.cost_at_risk`** and **`lowstock.upcoming_outs`**
    table rows: row click → SKU-focused detail (filter /
    highlight is acceptable if a per-SKU detail route is out of
    v1.1 scope).
- Encode drill state in the URL (`?drill=<drillId>&value=<...>`)
  so detail views are shareable / reload-safe.

**Exit criteria**: every dashboard panel can be expanded into a
real route; the four required drilldowns above are implemented
and reload-safe; share-link of an expanded panel reproduces the
exact view (site filter + range + agg + drill).

### R4 — Real-data wiring, by source tranche

The dominant work of the rework. Broken into source-grouped
sub-phases so each tranche is independently shippable and
reviewable. Each sub-phase commit carries `Phase: R4a` / `R4b` /
etc. so the parent issue gets fine-grained progress updates.

#### R4a — orders / cost / margin-backed metrics

Depends on the existing `sweed_orders` ingest + closed
[#23](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/23)
wholesale-cost cache. Wires real data for:

- `acquisition.first_vs_returning` (verify the v1 "first-time"
  definition pin: `customer_id` with no prior completed order in
  our system — document in the runbook if Sweed identity is
  unstable in the chosen window);
- `margins.effective_gm_pct`, `margins.gross_margin_dollars`,
  `margins.stack_new_vs_returning`;
- `basket.size_by_fulfillment`, `basket.size_by_customer_type`;
- `category.sales_stack_dollars`, `category.sales_stack_fraction`,
  `category.margin_dollars_stack` (and the
  category → subcategory drill from R3);
- `fulfillment.order_count`, `fulfillment.sales_dollars`,
  `fulfillment.margin_dollars`, `fulfillment.effective_gm_pct`;
- `payment.order_count`, `payment.sales_dollars`.

Each metric's response includes the `meta` block from the parent
rework addendum (sources, lastUpdatedAt, coverage). Sanity-check
total sales $ and total margin $ against the existing Helios
operational reports where one exists; note any discrepancy in the
phase's commit message + parent-issue comment.

#### R4b — inventory / SKU-risk metrics

Depends on
[#24](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/24)
Sweed per-package snapshot ingest. Wires:

- `inventory.cost_distribution` (with category → subcategory
  drill);
- `inventory.misalignment` (diverging bar at latest `t` ranked by
  `(on_hand_cost / 30d_cogs_run_rate) - target_ratio`);
- `slowmovers.cost_at_risk` (table-as-chart with the columns from
  v1 spec, plus the row-click → SKU drill from R3);
- `lowstock.upcoming_outs` (table-as-chart including the
  "expected margin loss $" column = `days_out × daily_margin_run_rate`).

R4b lands the ingest work in
[#24](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/24) as
its first commit if not already complete, then the SQL on top.

#### R4c — delivery / customer-geography metrics

Depends on
[#25](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/25)
Sweed per-invoice detail fetch. Wires:

- `delivery.order_count_by_zone` (with zone drill from R3);
- `delivery.margin_pct`;
- `customers.origin_map` (OSM-tile choropleth + heatmap; static
  date-range selector + diff-vs-prior overlay; playback remains
  v2 per the v1 plan).

#### R4d — external / operational context

Depends on
[#26](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/26)
daily-weather ingest and
[#27](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/27)
Sweed Shifts ingest. Wires:

- `weather.scatter_margin_vs_high_temp`,
  `weather.scatter_margin_vs_low_temp`,
  `weather.scatter_margin_vs_precip`;
- `cashier.transactions_per_hour`.

**Exit criteria for each R4 sub-phase**: every metric in the
sub-phase reports `dataQuality.status = 'real'` and renders real
production values on the live `/metrics` page; the CI guardrail
passes; the sanity-check note (where one applies) is committed
into the phase's commit message; no synthetic fallback remains in
production.

**Net exit criterion for R4**: zero production-visible panels are
backed by stubs.

### R5 — Data-quality hardening + dashboard usefulness pass

- Loading / empty / stale / error states for every panel (no
  silent blank tiles, no infinite spinners on a single source
  outage).
- Source / freshness badges in panel headers (small badge that
  reads e.g. `sweed_orders · 14 min ago`; hover for full
  source-list tooltip).
- Performance review: measure dashboard cold-load on
  `vps-nixos-3`; first useful panel within ~3 s, full settle
  within ~8–10 s absent source outages. Add server-side caching /
  concurrency limits where a single panel's query dominates.
- Stub-leak guardrail: a CI / pre-deploy test that walks the
  production registry and fails the build if any visible metric
  has `dataQuality.status !== 'real'` (matches R0's contract;
  this phase tightens it to a hard gate).
- Visual polish: tile density, readable typography, sensible
  default chart sizes. Not a redesign — just enough that the
  dashboard is comfortable to leave open on an operator screen.
- Verify global controls (site filter, aggregation, range) apply
  cleanly to every locked panel within one round-trip; verify
  per-panel lock / unlock interacts correctly with global
  changes.

**Exit criteria**: the operator can tell at a glance whether
every panel is fresh and trustworthy; cold-load meets the latency
budget; the build refuses to ship a stub.

### R6 — Runbook, validation evidence, closure package

- Refresh `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md` for the v1.1 reality:
  - dashboard model (sections, panel placement, drill contract,
    hover bus);
  - how to add a new metric (now includes `dashboard`,
    `dataQuality`, optional `drilldowns` blocks);
  - how the stub-leak guardrail works and how to disable a
    metric temporarily;
  - how to verify the synchronized crosshair after a change;
  - how to bring up `/metrics` locally and confirm real-data
    metadata.
- Validation evidence (committed under the runbook):
  - dashboard-overview screenshot;
  - synchronized-hover screenshot (or short GIF) showing two
    panels' crosshairs synced;
  - expand / detail route screenshot showing URL + drill state;
  - real-data badges screenshot (source + freshness visible);
  - one representative drill screenshot (e.g. category →
    subcategory).
- Parent closure package: a single comment on
  [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
  containing the live URL, the R0–R6 per-phase commit table, the
  canonical metric list with per-panel data-source mapping, the
  validation-evidence screenshots, and the oracle review note
  (see below).
- **Oracle review**: before R6 closure, the rework owner runs an
  oracle review pass against the live `/metrics` page and the
  canonical metric list, captures the oracle's "fit for purpose"
  assessment, addresses any blocking feedback, and includes the
  final oracle note in the closure package. This is the operator's
  stated bar; do not skip it.

**Exit criteria**: parent can close based on evidence, not trust.

## Cross-repo dependencies

Same as v1 — none hard. The ingest follow-ons
([#22](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/22),
[#24](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/24),
[#25](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/25),
[#26](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/26),
[#27](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/27))
all live in this repo and are picked up by the R4 sub-phases.

If during R4 a new external ingest stream is discovered to be
needed (e.g. a different NOAA station list owned by
`helios-parser-configs`), file an additional child epic against
the appropriate peer per the
[cross-repo task-dag driver](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/cross-repo-task-dag-driver.md)
model and link it from the parent issue.

## Acceptance criteria (delegated from parent)

The full v1.1 acceptance criteria live in the parent rework
addendum §"Refreshed acceptance criteria". Reproduced here as a
checklist for the R6 owner:

- [ ] (1) Dashboard, not picker — `/metrics` shows multiple charts
      at once by default; left-nav is TOC only.
- [ ] (2) Routable expansion — `/metrics/<metricId>` route exists,
      preserves global state in URL, supports browser back.
- [ ] (3) Useful drilldowns — minimum four implemented (category,
      fulfillment, delivery zone, SKU); drill state in URL.
- [ ] (4) Synchronized crosshair + readouts — hover on one locked
      panel drives all compatible locked panels; no network
      traffic on hover; explicit no-data state.
- [ ] (5) Real data only — zero stub / synthetic / demo metrics
      visible on production `/metrics`; all deferrals removed
      from registry with operator sign-off on #7.
- [ ] (6) Data transparency — source / freshness badges on every
      panel; stale / error / empty states explicit; key totals
      sanity-checked against Helios reports.
- [ ] (7) Global controls coherent — site / aggregation / range
      apply across locked panels within one round-trip.
- [ ] (8) Annotations integrated — CRUD works in tile + detail
      modes; annotations cross-render on other panels covering
      the annotated `t`.
- [ ] (9) Performance — first paint ~3 s, full settle ~8–10 s on
      `vps-nixos-3`; skeleton states for slow panels.
- [ ] (10) Oracle-approved evidence package — live URL, commit
      table, screenshots, canonical metric list, oracle note.
slots.delegationNote: Helios /metrics v1.1 rework — replace the single-chart picker with a sectioned multi-panel dashboard, demote left-nav to a TOC, add routable /metrics/<metricId> expansion + per-metric drilldowns, add synchronized crosshair / hover-readout via a TimeAxisContext hover bus, and wire every v1.1 production-visible panel to real data (no stubs). R0..R6 phasing; oracle-approved evidence package required at R6 closure.

# FBUS FAQ — `mostly-static-sites` (thin renderer) child epic

> **MATERIALISED 2026-06-15.** The four operator decisions are resolved
> in the parent
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md` §1](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#1-operator-decisions-resolved-2026-06-15)
> and folded into the phases below.
> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md). **Re-read the parent (and the
> parent epic #15) before starting any phase** — this child epic is a
> **thin index** over the parent's design. The parent wins on any drift.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#17
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>` trailer.

## Role in the epic

`mostly-static-sites` is the **thin, zero-DB renderer**. It consumes the
signed SEO bundle Helios publishes and renders the FAQ on FBUS — on every
landing page and on a dedicated `/faq` page — selecting **sanitized**
answers for the `.us` host. It also owns the **full-HTML leak crawler**
that proves FBUS ships no `.nyc` / brand / cannabis-meta-term leak. Helios
(`automation`) is the brain (peer child epic at
`../automation/EPIC_PLAN.md`).

The `@mss/seo` package (`packages/seo/`) — `select.ts#selectFaqFolds` and
`SEOFAQFold.tsx` — and the FB-NYC wiring
(`apps/freshlybaked-site/app/seo-helios-faq-folds.tsx`) **already exist**
from epic #15 and are the pattern to mirror. This child epic **reuses**
them; FBUS currently consumes none of it.

## ⚠️ Binding constraints (parent §5–§6)

- **Zero `.nyc` / "Freshly Baked NYC" / cannabis-meta-term leak** anywhere
  in FBUS rendered output: HTML, canonical, `og:*`, `sameAs`,
  publisher/org schema, `href`, `src`, `data-*`, inline JSON-LD, **and**
  the Next RSC payload / serialized client-component props. Prefer
  internal redirect tokens over passing `.nyc` URLs to client components.
- **`.us` selects sanitized answers only.** Unknown host / invalid bundle
  → render nothing (fail closed).
- **At most one FAQ fold per route**; one visible "FAQs" header + one FAQ
  section per page; no duplicate `FAQPage` scripts.
- **SSR/ISR-visible only** — native `<details>` in server HTML; never
  client-fetched or lazy-loaded.
- **Kill-switch / mode / allowlist fail-closed**: `off`/`shadow` render no
  FAQ; `canary` requires allowlist; `SEO_KILL_SWITCH` removes it.
- **UI/UX gate (canon §3).** The LP FAQ section + `/faq` page are
  user-facing UI → Oracle UI review (mobile layout, signal-to-noise,
  next-action-at-fingertips) recorded on the peer issue before rollout.

## Subtasks (authoritative list in parent §4 / issue Phases 0, 2, 3, 4)

**P0 — audit + failing leak crawler (goes first):**
- Enumerate FBUS route families + representative sample routes
  (operator-confirmed current set: deliverance, conquest, tours, recurse,
  branding, compare — parent §1 Q1).
- **Canonical LP-family registry (operator Q1 follow-up).** Land the
  family list + route patterns as a **single source of truth in code/
  config** (e.g. a `lpFamilies`/`SEO_ROUTE_FAMILIES` registry) so future
  families have an obvious place to register, and so this crawler
  inventory, the P4 FAQ injection points, and Helios's widget
  `route_patterns` (automation P5) all read from **one** place instead of
  duplicated lists. **Define the registry schema + cross-repo handoff:**
  export a machine-readable artifact (e.g. JSON) carrying, per family,
  the **id, canonical representative route, route patterns, sample crawl
  routes, indexability policy, and source commit/provenance** so
  automation P5 can consume it (or pin its exact SHA) rather than
  re-keying the list.
- **Humor-card inventory + classification (operator Q4).** Find the LP
  filler/humor cards (the "wrong flowers" / "wrong green" joke cards),
  classify each as **pure-humor filler** (retire) vs **functional**
  (keep), and record the list on this peer issue for operator
  confirmation. The operator could not name them ("you'll have to look");
  this inventory is the deliverable that resolves the question.
- **Indexability current-state audit (operator Q2).** Record the current
  `robots` / `noindex` / canonical / sitemap state for each LP family and
  `/faq`, and confirm there is **no `gads` / policy-engine coupling** to
  `robots` (i.e. flipping indexability does not change ads behaviour).
  Feeds the P6 indexability decision; make **no** indexability change in
  P0.
- Define the forbidden token/domain list (`.nyc`, brand phrases, cannabis
  meta-terms).
- Add a CI scanner that **builds + serves FBUS, crawls sample routes, and
  scans the full HTML response (incl. inline scripts + RSC payload)**;
  fail on any forbidden string. **Expect pre-existing FBUS leaks — fix or
  explicitly scope them before adding FAQ content.**

**P2 — FBUS SEO runtime integration:**
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/seo/runtime.ts` (adapt from FB-NYC;
  distinct global symbol e.g. `mss.fbus.seo.runtime.v1`).
- Boot the SEO bundle poller in
  `apps/freshlybakedus-site/instrumentation.ts` alongside the LP runtime.
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/app/api/seo/health/route.ts`.
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/app/seo-helios-faq-folds.tsx` using
  `freshlyBakedUsSiteConfig.canonicalHost`, returning **at most one fold**.
- Add `emitJsonLd?: boolean` to `SEOFAQFold` (default `true`).

**P3 — dedicated `/faq` page:**
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/app/faq/page.tsx`, sanitized mode,
  `emitJsonLd=true`, `.us`-only metadata, `revalidate` ~300–600s. Stands
  alone if LP FAQs are disabled.

**P4 — LP FAQ insertion (replaces humor cards):**
- Inject the FAQ section above the footer (between X4 and X5) in the
  shared FBUS LP page components (deliverance/conquest/tours/recurse/
  branding/compare — the operator-confirmed set from the P0 registry),
  under a page-wide "FAQs" header; LP `emitJsonLd=false`.
- **Retire the pure-humor cards** identified in the P0 inventory (wrong
  flowers / wrong green) **only on LP families where the FAQ section is
  enabled** (operator Q4 default: per-family + reversible, **not** a
  global delete). Keep cards the P0 inventory classified as functional.
  Global retirement is a follow-up once the FAQ is broadly live.
- P4 implementation may **land behind kill-switch/canary flags** before
  P5, but **production enablement of an LP family waits until that family
  has an approved merged FAQ set from P5** — do not replace humor cards
  with generic/global boilerplate before family-specific approved content
  exists.

**Hardcoded-FAQ cleanup (mss owns this; coordinate with automation P1):**
- After Helios import is approved and bundled, remove/neutralize
  `apps/freshlybaked-site/app/sites/all/loyalty-faq/page.tsx` as a source
  of truth (render from the bundle instead; preserve/redirect any existing
  public route intentionally), and add a **CI guard** against reintroducing
  hardcoded FAQ content outside the SEO bundle. automation cannot complete
  this migration alone — the code change is here.

**P6 — ads-safe rollout mechanics:**
- Route/family allowlist canary, kill-switch verification, a production
  crawl before broad enablement, and a rollback runbook for removing FAQ
  sections / restoring prior content.
- **Indexability flip (operator Q2, operator-gated for LP families).**
  The new `/faq` ships indexable by design (P3); the **per-LP-family**
  flip waits for operator approval after the P0 audit. If approved: make
  **one canonical representative page per LP family** `index, follow` +
  self-canonical + sitemap-listed, and point per-variant / parameterised
  LPs at it via `rel=canonical` (the preferred consolidation signal),
  adding `noindex` only where a low-unique variant must stay out of the
  index (do not rely on `noindex` to consolidate ranking signals).
  Default until explicit operator approval = **no indexability change to
  existing LP families**.

## CI gates owned here (parent §7)

(4) selector tests (`.us`=sanitized, `.nyc`=raw, unknown host=[], at most
one fold/route, allowlists); (5) renderer tests (visible text == JSON-LD
when emitted; LP can suppress JSON-LD; no raw answer in HTML);
(6) metadata tests (canonical/OG always `https://freshlybaked.us…`; no
`.nyc` in structured data / `sameAs` / publisher); (7) rendered-HTML
crawler (P0); (8) kill-switch tests.

## Phasing

P0 (leak crawler) first and must pass before any FAQ content is added.
The P2 runtime can run in `shadow`; `/faq` (P3, the smallest visible
slice) should be enabled only in non-prod or canary/allowlisted mode
until the crawler, metadata, and approval gates pass. Then P4 LP
insertion lands gated. Tag commits with `Phase: P<n>`.
slots.delegationNote: Thin zero-DB renderer. P0 first (failing full-HTML leak crawler + canonical LP-family registry + humor-card inventory + indexability/robots audit). BINDING: zero .nyc/brand/cannabis-meta leak in HTML+metadata+RSC payload; .us=sanitized fail-closed; at most one fold/route; JSON-LD off on LPs, on for /faq; humor-card retirement only where FAQ enabled; per-family indexability flip operator-gated. Phases P0, P2, P3, P4.
slots.title: FBUS SEO FAQ - thin mss runtime (top-level#17)

# Dev-loop optimization — `automation` child epic (helios + ads)

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#26](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/26).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/dev-loop-optimization/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the
> `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (Helios monorepo) slice** of that design,
> covering both the `helios/` and `ads/` packages.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation@master` that
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#26
> ```
>
> **Re-read the parent `EPIC_PLAN.md` before starting** — it is the
> single source of truth; this file is a thin index over it.

## Goal

Make the everyday Helios dev loop fast: agents iterate with
**light/targeted** checks scoped to the package/service/files they
touched, while the **full** lint/typecheck/test/build/smoke suite is
owned by CI / the final gate and is no longer hand-run repeatedly under
`large-action-lock` before every commit.

## Binding standards (from the parent, do not weaken)

- Two-gate green tree: fast local + final presubmit. Location split, not
  a waiver — full required CI coverage stays enforced.
- A check leaves pre-commit/local iteration only with equal-or-stronger
  coverage remaining in CI.
- No first-party `any`, no disabled/weakened gates, no `--no-verify`,
  tests deterministic and prod-resource-free (inherited from fleet-green
  [#20](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/20); keep green).

## Scope owned by this repo

1. **Inventory + time** every check in `helios/` and `ads/`: lint,
   server typecheck, client typecheck, unit tests, build, smoke, and the
   fleet-green scanners (no-any, disabled-gate, test-resource). Record
   each command's wall-clock from a fresh ephemeral checkout with a warm
   cache.
2. **Provide light/targeted commands** for every >~30s check. Likely
   splits:
   - per-package lint (`helios/` vs `ads/`) and changed-file lint;
   - server-vs-client typecheck run independently, scoped to the package
     touched, instead of the whole monorepo;
   - focused test runs (single file / pattern / changed behavior) rather
     than the full suite;
   - keep the full `next build` / full test suite / smoke as CI-only.
3. **Document a dev-loop table in `automation`'s `AGENTS.md`**: touched
   area (`helios/` server, `helios/` client, `ads/`) → light local
   command → final presubmit CI status → when an agent may hand-run a
   heavy command (debug a CI failure, harness change, operator ask).
4. **Lighten `.githooks/pre-commit`** from the full-CI mirror to
   fast/targeted checks (changed-file lint + scoped typecheck of the
   touched package), **after** confirming the full gate is a required CI
   status. Do not reintroduce the client-typecheck carve-out fleet-green
   removed — keep it enforced in CI; just don't run the *whole* monorepo
   typecheck in the hook.
5. **Confirm the broken-master window is closed**: the full gate must
   validate the exact commit before it publishes/deploys (required PR
   check / branch protection), or deploy promotion waits for CI green.

## Acceptance

From a fresh ephemeral checkout:

1. `AGENTS.md` dev-loop table present; every >~30s `helios/`/`ads/` check
   has a light/targeted command or a documented heavy-final-only
   exception.
2. Pre-commit hook is fast/targeted; full lint/typecheck (server +
   client)/test/build remains a required CI status, recorded green for a
   sample commit.
3. No coverage deleted; broken-master window closed or interim exception
   documented.
4. Agent Gate Record (two-gate template) attached.
slots.delegationNote: Split >30s helios/ + ads/ checks into a full CI presubmit plus light/targeted local commands; document a dev-loop table in AGENTS.md; lighten pre-commit hooks to fast/targeted (keep full gate as required CI). See parent docs/epics/dev-loop-optimization/EPIC_PLAN.md.
slots.title: Dev-loop optimization: Helios fast local checks, CI owns the heavy gate

slots.body:
# Helios `/metrics` v1.4 rework — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
> for the v1.4 iteration. Authoritative design:
> [`docs/epics/business-metrics/EPIC_PLAN_v1_4_REWORK.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN_v1_4_REWORK.md)
> in the top-level repo.
>
> The v1 child epic is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#21`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21)
> (closed); the v1.1 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#28`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/28)
> (closed); the v1.2 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#30`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/30)
> (closed); the v1.3 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#34`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/34)
> (closed). This issue tracks the v1.4 rework only — please do
> not reopen the v1 / v1.1 / v1.2 / v1.3 children.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation` master that
> satisfies any part of this rework MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: V4<n>`
> trailer (e.g. `Phase: V4'3`) — distinct from v1's `P<n>`,
> v1.1's `R<n>`, v1.2's `V2<n>`, and v1.3's `V3<n>` — so per-
> phase progress comments on the parent issue are visually
> grouped per rework iteration.

## Scope owned by this repo

v1.4 picks up the five-item operator wishlist from the
[v1.3-slice status comment on top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7#issuecomment-4570305082):

1. Scatter chart light-grey dashed gridlines (parity with
   `MetricChart`).
2. Margin-$ basis on the four mandatory LTV histograms (on
   `/metrics/customer-value`) backed by a new per-invoice
   `sweed_order_margin_mv` materialized view.
3. Cohort retention curve panel + first-to-second conversion
   rate sparkline on `/metrics/customer-value`.
4. Click-to-drill on every histogram bucket and every scatter
   dot (Budtender Advanced + catalog analytics + Customer
   Value histograms).
5. VeriScan link coverage badge + disabled "Show only
   VeriScan-linked customers" toggle on the Customer Value
   tab header (full functionality gated on coverage threshold
   — v1.4.1).

All five are refinements of already-shipped tabs / panels.
v1.4 introduces **no new top-level tabs**, **no new
sub-routes**, and **one new materialized view**
(`sweed_order_margin_mv`).

Re-read the parent addendum before starting any phase. This
child plan is intentionally a thin index over the parent.

### V4'0 — Scope freeze + helper extraction + endpoint decisions

- Re-confirm the v1.4-in-scope panel set against the
  v1.3-slice canonical list (no Budtender or headline-grid
  panel is removed; the only registry change is the planned
  removal of two MISSING DATA cards on Customer Value when
  V4'2 / V4'3 promote their content).
- Extract a `niceXTicks(min, max, opts)` helper alongside the
  existing `niceYTicks` in
  `helios/src/client/routes/metrics/gridlines.ts`. Same
  `{1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10} × 10^k` ladder; same
  `stepFractionDigits` discipline (regression-guarded for the
  `2.5` / `0.25` / `0.025` cases per v1.2 R5 oracle review).
  No visual behaviour change in V4'0 — this is just the helper.
- Extend `MetricDef` types (additive):
  - `supports.drillSelection?: ('histogramBucket' |
    'scatterDot')[]`.
- Decision: retention payload placement.
  - Default: extend the existing consolidated
    `/api/customer-value-analytics` endpoint with an
    `?include=retention` query-param toggle that adds
    `cohort_retention[]` and `first_second_conversion[]` to
    the payload. Existing callers don't pay the cost.
  - Alternative (only if measurement shows > 1.5 s P95 cold
    with `?include=retention`): a sibling
    `/api/customer-retention` endpoint, separately cached.
  - Decision recorded in the V4'0 commit message and in
    `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md`.
- Decision: `sweed_order_margin_mv` refresh cadence.
  - Default: incremental refresh by the existing helios
    refresh job on the same cadence as other materialized
    views.
  - Alternative: per-trigger on `sweed_orders` insert (only
    if measurement shows the helios refresh job's cadence
    introduces > 1h staleness on the margin-$ histograms).
  - Decision recorded in the V4'0 commit message and in
    `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md`.

**Exit criteria**: `niceXTicks` extracted and unit-tested
(with the 2.5 / 0.25 / 0.025 regression cases);
`MetricDef.supports.drillSelection` typed in shared types;
retention-payload-placement and MV-refresh-cadence decisions
recorded; canonical metric list refreshed (notes the planned
v1.4 changes — actual registry edits land in V4'2 / V4'3).

### V4'1 — Scatter chart gridlines

- Wire `niceXTicks` + `niceYTicks` into the scatter renderer
  used on:
  - `/metrics/budtenders?sub=advanced` (the one-dot-per-
    cashier scatter from v1.3 V3'4).
  - Any catalog-analytics-style scatter on the v1.2-shipped
    catalog analytics tab.
- Visual treatment: 1px dashed light-grey (`stroke="currentColor"
  opacity="0.12" stroke-dasharray="4 4"`) lines at each nice
  tick, drawn **under** the dot cloud and **under** any
  reference / quadrant lines.
- Axis label formatting honours the axis's declared kind. New
  helper: `formatAxisValue(value, kind)` in `gridlines.ts`,
  covering `$ / int / pct / ratio / minutes`. Each kind has a
  unit test asserting the expected formatting.
- CI guardrail: extend the v1.2 R5 `niceYTicks` test that
  asserts "least-significant digit in {0, 2, 5}" for the 2.5 /
  0.25 / 0.025 cases to also assert it for `niceXTicks`.
- Verify on phone (operator wishlist note) — the V4'1
  validation evidence captures a screenshot from a 412px-
  wide mobile viewport showing the scatter with gridlines
  rendered correctly (no label collision; gridline density
  scales down).

**Exit criteria**: both scatter renderers show gridlines
matching the time-series chart visual treatment on desktop
**and** mobile; reference / quadrant lines remain on top of
gridlines; CI guardrail green; mobile screenshot in the V4'1
PR.

### V4'2 — `sweed_order_margin_mv` + Margin-$ basis on LTV histograms

- Add `sweed_order_margin_mv` materialized view to the helios
  warehouse:
  - PK `(dealer_id, invoice_id)`.
  - Columns `(customer_id, pay_time, gross_margin)`.
  - Source:
    `sweed_orders so
       JOIN sweed_order_line_items oli USING (dealer_id, invoice_id)
       JOIN product_cost_history pch ON (pch.dealer_id, pch.product_id, pch.effective_at_or_before(oli.created_at))`.
  - Gross margin = `oli.line_revenue - oli.line_quantity *
    pch.unit_cost`, summed per invoice.
  - `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` is acceptable
    (PK is unique). Refreshed by the existing helios refresh
    job.
- Acknowledged dependency: line-items ingest must be live
  on production (v1.3-slice `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#22`
  or its successor). If line-items ingest is **not** live at
  V4'2 start, **do not stub margins** — flip V4'2 into a
  blocked-on-ingest state, file the unblock issue, and skip
  to V4'3 / V4'4 / V4'5 / V4'6 (V4'2 then ships as a separate
  follow-on commit once ingest lands).
- Extend `/api/customer-value-analytics`:
  - Each per-purchase-ordinal row gains `margin: number |
    null`.
  - The basis selector accepts `gross_margin` as a fourth
    option (`gross_sales`, `net_sales`, `gross_receipts`,
    `gross_margin`).
- Frontend:
  - The basis selector dropdown on `/metrics/customer-value`
    gains the "Gross Margin" option.
  - All four mandatory histograms re-render under the new
    basis with no re-fetch (selection toggles a client-side
    field projection over the already-loaded rows).
  - The MISSING DATA card "Lifetime margin $ histograms" is
    removed from the registry; the registry test from v1.1 R0
    is updated to reflect the new MISSING DATA card count.
- Runbook: document `sweed_order_margin_mv` schema, refresh
  cadence, and the line-items-ingest dependency. Note the
  rollback procedure (drop the MV; revert the basis selector
  to three options; restore the MISSING DATA card).

**Exit criteria**: `sweed_order_margin_mv` lives in production;
margin-$ basis is selectable on every LTV histogram; the
"Lifetime margin $ histograms" MISSING DATA card is gone;
runbook updated; rollback procedure documented.

### V4'3 — Cohort retention + first-to-second conversion

- Extend the consolidated endpoint with the `cohort_retention`
  and `first_second_conversion` CTEs:
  - Cohort = `date_trunc('week', first_purchase_at)` (default)
    or `date_trunc('month', first_purchase_at)` (selector).
  - Retention row per `(cohort_key, weeks_since_acquisition)`
    or `(cohort_key, months_since_acquisition)`:
    `retained_count / cohort_size`.
  - First-to-second-conversion row per `cohort_key`:
    `customers_with_second_purchase_ever / cohort_size`, with
    parallel `_within_30d`, `_within_60d`, `_within_90d`
    fields.
  - Query honours the v1.3-slice cohort scope control (all-
    known / active-in-range / acquired-in-range).
- Gated behind the `?include=retention` query-param toggle
  decided in V4'0.
- Frontend:
  - **Cohort retention curve** panel: time-series-like chart
    with cohort lines. Most recent cohort = most opaque; older
    cohorts fade. Max 12 cohorts visible by default; "show
    all" toggle in the panel header. Hover-readout shows
    cohort + weeks-since-acquisition + retention %.
  - **First-to-second conversion sparkline** panel: small
    inline bar chart, one bar per cohort. Hover shows the
    cohort plus all four conversion fields (`ever`, `30d`,
    `60d`, `90d`).
- The MISSING DATA card "Cohort retention curves" is removed
  from the registry; registry test updated.

**Exit criteria**: retention curve + conversion sparkline
render real data on `/metrics/customer-value`; cohort-scope
control honoured; max-12 default + "show all" works; the
"Cohort retention curves" MISSING DATA card is gone.

### V4'4 — Histogram / scatter drill-clicks

- Extend the v1.2 `/rows` endpoint to accept an optional
  `selection` query param (JSON-encoded `{ kind, …meta }`):
  - `{ kind: 'histogramBucket', metricId, bucketKey }`:
    rows-WHERE-clause restricts to rows in that bucket.
  - `{ kind: 'scatterDot', cashierId }`: rows-WHERE-clause
    restricts to that cashier's per-day rows.
  - Per-metric implementation in the existing `tableModeFor
    (metric)` switch — additive, not a refactor.
- Frontend:
  - Every histogram bucket on `/metrics/customer-value` and
    every scatter dot on `/metrics/budtenders?sub=advanced`
    (and on the catalog analytics scatter) becomes click-
    handled. Click navigates to the routable detail route
    with `?selection=…` set in the URL.
  - Detail route's Table tab reads the `selection` from the
    URL and passes it to `/rows`; renders the filtered rows.
  - Chart tab on the detail route highlights the selected
    bucket / dot with a 2px stroke + label.
  - Keyboard: every bucket / dot is reachable via Tab (with
    `tabindex="0"`); Enter activates the click; Escape returns
    to the parent tab (focus restored to the original
    clickable).
  - Share-link parity: copy-link from the drilled-down state
    reproduces the selection.
- `MetricDef.supports.drillSelection` declared on every metric
  in scope; metrics without `drillSelection` continue to
  render non-interactive buckets / dots.
- Smoke test: a single Playwright (or equivalent) test that
  drives one click-to-drill flow end-to-end per metric kind
  (one histogram, one scatter).

**Exit criteria**: click-to-drill works on every histogram +
every scatter in scope; URL share-link reproduces; keyboard
parity holds; smoke test green; `supports.drillSelection`
declared on every in-scope metric.

### V4'5 — VeriScan link coverage badge

- Extend `/api/customer-value-analytics` to compute
  `meta.veriscanCoverage: { linked: number, total: number,
  pct: number }` over the visible window, sourced from
  `visitor_scan_links ⋈ sweed_orders` (left-join on
  `customer_id`).
- Frontend:
  - Customer Value tab header renders the badge `N% linked`
    next to the existing coverage / freshness badges.
  - Tooltip text (operator-approved before deploy):
    "X of Y purchases in this window are attributed to a
    VeriScan-known identity. Cohort retention, basket size at
    purchase N, and lifetime $ histograms key off
    `customer_id` from `sweed_orders` and are unaffected.
    VeriScan-keyed views are MISSING DATA until coverage
    crosses the operator-set threshold (today: 25%)."
  - A disabled toggle reads: "Show only VeriScan-linked
    customers (gated on ≥ 25% coverage)". When coverage
    `pct >= 25`, the toggle is enabled but is a no-op in v1.4
    (with an inline note linking to the v1.4.1 follow-on
    issue). The intent is to put the affordance in place
    today.

**Exit criteria**: badge + disabled toggle render on
`/metrics/customer-value` with real data; operator has signed
off on the tooltip text (capture the sign-off in the V4'5 PR);
`meta.veriscanCoverage` is on the consolidated payload.

### V4'6 — Perf + runbook + closure

- Perf measurement:
  - `/api/customer-value-analytics?include=retention` — P50 /
    P95 cold / P95 warm on typical windows (4w / 12w / all-
    time); target P50 < 700 ms warm, P95 < 1.5 s cold.
  - `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY
    sweed_order_margin_mv` — measured wall-clock against
    production; documented in the runbook.
  - `/api/metrics/<id>/rows?selection=…` — sanity-check that
    the new `selection` param doesn't degrade the existing
    `/rows` P50 / P95.
- Runbook refresh: `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md` extended
  with v1.4 surface (scatter gridlines, margin-$ basis,
  cohort retention, first-to-second conversion, drill-click
  selection contract, VeriScan coverage badge,
  `sweed_order_margin_mv` schema + refresh + rollback).
- Validation evidence committed under the runbook:
  - Scatter with gridlines on both Budtender Advanced and the
    catalog analytics scatter (desktop + 412px mobile).
  - Each of the four LTV histograms with `gross_margin`
    basis selected.
  - Cohort retention curve in default (max-12) and "show all"
    modes.
  - First-to-second conversion sparkline with hover open
    showing the 30d / 60d / 90d readouts.
  - Histogram bucket drill landed in the detail Table tab
    (with URL bar visible to evidence share-link parity).
  - Scatter dot drill landed in the cashier-detail Table tab
    (with URL bar visible).
  - VeriScan coverage badge + the disabled toggle.
  - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` + endpoint timing table for the new
    endpoints / params.
- Oracle review pass: re-run an oracle review on the v1.4
  surface (scatter gridlines; margin-$ histograms; retention
  curves; drill-clicks; VeriScan coverage). Capture the
  oracle's "fit for purpose — world-class for this operator's
  stated needs?" verdict. If the oracle flags new gaps,
  address them in this phase before the closure commit, or
  file an explicit follow-on epic and call it out in the
  closure package.
- Closure package: a single comment on
  [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
  containing the live URLs (`https://helios.freshlybaked.us/metrics`,
  `/essentials`, `/customer-value`, `/budtenders`), the
  V4'0–V4'6 per-phase commit table, the AC §1–7 sign-off
  (with one-line evidence per criterion), the refreshed
  canonical metric list (Customer Value tab gains cohort
  retention + first-to-second-conversion entries; four LTV
  histograms gain `bases: [gross_sales, net_sales,
  gross_receipts, gross_margin]`), the validation evidence,
  and the oracle note. The close commit MUST carry
  `Closes-Epic: #7` per #8's policy so
  `close-completed-issues.yml` closes the issue.

**Exit criteria**: parent can close based on evidence, not
trust; v1.4 AC §1–7 demonstrably hold on production; v1.1
AC §1–10, v1.2 AC §1–8, and v1.3 AC §1–9 continue to hold
(no regressions); oracle confirms the v1.4 surface is fit
for the operator's stated "world-class business performance
metrics dashboard" purpose.

## Cross-repo dependencies

- **Line-items ingest** (v1.3-slice issue
  [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#22`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/22)
  or successor) is a hard prerequisite for V4'2
  (`sweed_order_margin_mv` is computed from
  `sweed_order_line_items`). If line-items ingest is not live
  at V4'2 start, V4'2 ships separately once ingest lands;
  V4'3 / V4'4 / V4'5 / V4'6 proceed on the rest of the scope.
- **VeriScan link coverage** is not a hard prerequisite — v1.4
  just surfaces the current coverage. v1.4.1 wires the toggle
  to actually filter the histograms; that work is explicitly
  out of v1.4 scope.

## Acceptance criteria (delegated from parent)

The full v1.4 acceptance criteria live in the parent rework
addendum §"Refreshed acceptance criteria". Reproduced here as
a checklist for the V4'6 owner:

- [ ] (1) Scatter charts on Budtender Advanced + catalog
      analytics render light-grey 1px dashed gridlines at
      nice X and Y ticks (desktop + mobile); reference /
      quadrant lines render on top of gridlines; CI guardrail
      on tick "least-significant digit in {0, 2, 5}" passes
      on the X-axis ladder.
- [ ] (2) Margin-$ basis is live on every LTV histogram on
      `/metrics/customer-value`, sourced from
      `sweed_order_margin_mv`; "Lifetime margin $ histograms"
      MISSING DATA card removed.
- [ ] (3) Cohort retention curve + first-to-second conversion
      sparkline are live on `/metrics/customer-value` with
      real data; max-12 default + "show all" toggle; cohort-
      scope control honoured; "Cohort retention curves"
      MISSING DATA card removed.
- [ ] (4) Click-to-drill works on every histogram bucket +
      every scatter dot in scope; URL share-link reproduces;
      Tab / Enter / Escape keyboard parity holds; chart
      highlights the selected element with a 2px stroke.
- [ ] (5) VeriScan link coverage badge renders on
      `/metrics/customer-value` header with operator-approved
      tooltip; disabled toggle present;
      `meta.veriscanCoverage` on the consolidated endpoint
      payload.
- [ ] (6) v1.1 AC §1–10, v1.2 AC §1–8, and v1.3 AC §1–9
      continue to hold on production; no regressions.
- [ ] (7) Oracle-approved closure evidence package — live
      URLs, commit table, screenshots, perf table, canonical
      metric list, oracle note; close commit carries
      `Closes-Epic: #7`.
slots.delegationNote: Helios /metrics v1.4 follow-on — five-item operator wishlist from issue#7#issuecomment-4570305082: (1) scatter chart light-grey dashed gridlines via shared niceXTicks helper (parity with MetricChart); (2) margin-$ basis on the four mandatory LTV histograms backed by a new sweed_order_margin_mv per-invoice materialized view; (3) cohort retention curve + first-to-second conversion sparkline panels on /metrics/customer-value; (4) click-to-drill on every histogram bucket + every scatter dot via an additive `selection` query-param on the v1.2 /rows endpoint with URL share-link parity; (5) VeriScan link-coverage badge + disabled "Show only VeriScan-linked customers" toggle on the Customer Value header (functional in v1.4.1). V4'0..V4'6 phasing; oracle-approved evidence package required at V4'6 closure with Closes-Epic: #7 trailer.

# Prospective Pending-Purchase Classifier — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#33](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/33).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md`](../../../../designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md)
> and the staged plan + the 8 operator decisions live in
> [`docs/epics/prospective-pending-purchase/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md),
> both in the top-level repo. This child epic exists because **all
> implementation lands in `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (the Helios app
> under `helios/`)**: the worker classifier, server routes, DB schema,
> review UI, and the inventory lifecycle are all Helios surfaces.
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `automation` master and
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#33
> ```

## Scope owned by this repo (Helios)

Two parallel tracks. The **classifier track** replaces the reactive
pending-purchase generator with a prospective Bedrock-driven one behind a
deterministic validator. The **pricing-safety lifecycle track** closes the
first-sale mispricing race for brand-new SKUs. They are independent and
meet only where catalog-apply creates the live product the lifecycle then
prices.

### Classifier track

- **C0 — Amp → `import_json` bridge runbook** (already operational; no
  code). Purchase 151113 packet #53 was built this way. Documents the
  manual escalation path that stays as the human-triggered escape hatch.
- **C1 — Refactor the generator into seams.** Carve
  `collectPendingPurchaseContext`, `buildPendingPurchasePacket`,
  `persistGeneratedPendingPurchasePacket` out of
  `worker/jobs/generatePendingPurchasePacketJob.ts`; no behavior change
  yet. Isolate the legacy rule-based row-builder behind ONE seam **so it
  can be deleted at cutover (C8)** — it is not a preserved path
  (decision 4: go direct).
- **C2 — Hint bundle storage + admin API.** New
  `pending_purchase_hint_bundles` / `pending_purchase_hint_documents`
  tables; admin endpoints; `hintBundleId` on the generate job + route.
  v1 = pasted arbitrary hint text only (decision 2).
- **C3 — Hint fact extraction + intent classification.**
  `extractPendingPurchaseHintFacts` (Bedrock JSON for menus; deterministic
  for Sweed PO JSON). First LLM-classify the hint for *how* it helps
  (canonical SKU list / ordered-items expectation / free-text description /
  line-item list — decision 2), then extract inert cited facts.
- **C4 — Prospective LLM classifier.**
  `classifyPendingPurchasePacketWithLlm`; event-level prompt over the full
  order + live catalog + hint facts; `PendingPurchaseLlmDraftRow` output
  contract (model proposes a reuse link, never authorizes it). Default
  model = the current "standard, most capable general reasoning model,"
  chosen dynamically + a below-the-fold Bedrock config page for rare
  per-context overrides (decision 1).
- **C5 — Deterministic validator / reconciler (the safety layer).**
  Validate every reuse candidate vs the live product; taxonomy/size/pack/
  house-brand guards; duplicate detection; Helios (not the model) computes
  deterministic fields + price + inline market evidence.
- **C6 — Review-UI surfacing.** Show confidence, rationale, hint
  citations, reuse candidates, and new-brand/new-group/no-comps warnings
  (all from the passthrough `raw_row_json`).
- **C7 — Apply-time drift guard + optional post-apply refresh.**
  Generated-reuse drift guard in the apply job; optional enqueue of created
  product ids after apply.
- **C8 — Direct cutover + legacy deletion.** Switch
  `catalog.pending_purchases.generate` to the LLM-prospective path and
  **delete the legacy rule-based classifier** (decision 4). A short
  dev-only shadow comparison during validation is fine, but it ships as the
  single path — no permanent `generationMode` toggle, no legacy fallback.

### Pricing-safety lifecycle track (independent; can ship first)

- **L1 — Lifecycle record + gates (no reverse move).**
  `purchase_inventory_lifecycle_runs` / `_items` tables keyed by
  `(dealer_id, po_id)`; start / verify-quarantine / purchase-market-refresh
  / purchase-reprice routes; market-completion (timestamp-based) +
  price-applied (live-price-equality) verifiers; reuse the existing pricing
  review UI. No release route yet.
- **L2 — Bulk quarantine repair + gated release.** Extract a shared
  stock-transfer service from the one-way move-to-inspection; purchase-
  scoped bulk move-to-inspection (repair); reverse + bulk **release** to a
  chosen FOR SALE room (dropdown, default "FOR SALE - Sales Floor" —
  decision 6) with immediate-before-transfer preflight (live price + live
  quarantine re-verify), post-transfer verification, and partial-failure
  recovery. Quarantine is **optional, not enforced** (decision 5): the UI
  offers bulk move-to-quarantine + full lifecycle OR reprice-in-place
  skipping the release/move-back. Repricing is SKU-level with a small badge
  when a SKU already has on-floor stock (decision 8).
- **L3 — Automation + monitoring.** `inventory.lifecycle.advance` job to
  poll/advance async gates; quarantine-breach monitor; alerts (lot in FOR
  SALE before priced, market timeout, price-apply failure, release partial
  failure).

## Dependency order (for task breakdown)

```
C0 (done) ─▶ C1 ─▶ C4 ─▶ C5 ─▶ (C6, C7) ─▶ C8
              C2 ─▶ C3 ─────────▲
L1 ─▶ L2 ─▶ L3        (lifecycle track, parallel to the classifier track)
```

- C1 unblocks C4; C2 unblocks C3; C3 feeds C4; C5 depends on C4; C6 & C7
  depend on C5; C8 depends on C5+C6+C7.
- L-track is fully parallel and independent of the classifier track.

## Out of scope (explicit)

- **FT-1** hint file uploads (CSV/PDF/manifests/POs/catalogs/scrapings) —
  near-term follow-up, separate task.
- **FT-2** auto-generated proposal packets — gated on FT-3.
- **FT-3** LitAlerts competitor-data redesign — its own future top-level
  epic (decision 7); not created here.
- **FT-4** broader pricing process/engine redesign — its own future epic.
- Any change to the human review + apply approval gate (kept as-is).

## Required gates (per canon)

- **Oracle critical-infra / DB review** for the validator (C5), the apply
  drift guard (C7), the hint tables + generate-job changes (C2), and the
  lifecycle tables + release safety (L1/L2). DB migrations apply on prod
  only after Oracle blessing **and** explicit operator approval, then
  live-sentinel verification.
- **Green tree** — repo-documented light/targeted lint/typecheck/test for
  touched Helios areas in the dev loop; full presubmit before merge. No
  first-party `any`; no bug-masking fallbacks.
- **Oracle UI review** for C6 review-UI changes, the L1 lifecycle panel,
  and any operator-facing copy.

## Completion signal

This child epic is complete when both tracks have landed on `automation`
master with `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#33` trailers: the legacy
classifier is deleted and `catalog.pending_purchases.generate` runs the
validated prospective path (C8), and the quarantine→reprice→release
lifecycle is operator-usable end-to-end with its hard release gates (L3).
slots.delegationNote: Implement classifier stages C0-C8 (prospective Bedrock classifier behind a deterministic validator; delete the legacy reactive path) and lifecycle stages L1-L3 (quarantine→reprice→release with hard release gates) per docs/designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md. Each stage honors its canon Oracle critical-infra/DB + UI reviews and explicit operator approval before any prod DB migration or live-inventory write. Carry Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#33 on implementation commits.
slots.title: Prospective LLM pending-purchase classifier + pricing-safety lifecycle (top-level #33)

# Agent-waste review queue — Helios child epic: promote-to-advisory admin button (server-side, admin-gated, contract-validated commit+push)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality" (Lever D).
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md)
> ("Remaining work" #4; decision **D3** and the **§Security** write-key choice
> are RESOLVED — operator adopted option **(c)** direct, admin-gated,
> server-validated push, comment [#4889206463](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/57#issuecomment-4889206463)).
> **Advisory catalog contract:**
> [`virusdave/top-level` → `docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md),
> [`docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 has **several** child epics,
> the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO carry this issue's own
> `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level completion
> aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal

Implement the operator's **promote-to-advisory admin button** (D3): a
server-side, admin-gated, contract-validated git **commit+push** that adds a new
reviewed entry to `top-level` `advisories.yaml` — the human-review gate that lets
a curated observation become an allowlisted advisory the dispatcher may inject
(~1-min latency). This **overrides** the earlier "v1 = display + link-to-promote,
no Helios button" plan; the operator explicitly asked for an in-Helios admin
action ("I do not want to modify files in git manually").

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Admin-gated route** | `POST` promote endpoint, **admin-only** (same admin gate as `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog`), with an audit log entry per promotion. |
| **applyConfig-pattern write** | Reuse the parser-config apply pattern in [`helios/src/server/parsekit/applyConfig.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/parsekit/applyConfig.ts): **validate → write → `git add` → reject no-op → commit → push → reset local commit on push failure**, with a subprocess **timeout**. Push to `top-level master` using the D3 write deploy key from child epic #1. |
| **Server-side contract validation** | Before committing, validate the resulting `advisories.yaml` against the **advisory-catalog contract** ([`ADVISORY_CATALOG.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/ADVISORY_CATALOG.md)): schema, **budget caps**, `id` rules. Reject invalid promotions before any write. |
| **Field mapping (audited)** | Record exactly which backlog-item fields map to an advisory entry's `id` / `text` / `severity`. **`note` is display-only and MUST NOT map to `text`** — it can never leak into the injected allowlist. |
| **Concurrency** | Promote-commits touch files adjacent to the exporter's backlog writes in the same repo. Inherit applyConfig's no-op rejection + reset-on-push-failure so a rejected push never piles up local commits; refetch/rebase and retry. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants (carry forward)

- **`note` never becomes advisory `text`.** This is the load-bearing safety
  invariant of the whole workstream — the allowlist is the boundary between
  human-reviewed text and agent-authored text.
- **Validate before commit**, server-side, against the catalog contract (schema
  + budget caps + `id` rules); reject no-op; reset-on-push-failure; subprocess
  timeout — the full applyConfig discipline.
- **Admin-gated + audited.** The human review action *is* the safety gate for a
  mutating, behaviour-changing operation (it changes what future agents may be
  injected with). Every promotion is admin-authenticated and logged.
- **§Security residual risk accepted (option (c)).** The `top-level` **write**
  deploy key is repo-wide (GitHub deploy keys are not path-scoped) and
  `top-level` has no branch protection on the current plan. The operator
  **explicitly accepted** this residual risk (comment [#4889206463](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/57#issuecomment-4889206463));
  options (a) dedicated repo and (b) PR/branch were declined. Do **not** silently
  substitute (a)/(b); the mitigation is admin-gating + server-side validation +
  audit, not key-scope reduction.

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Depends on** child epic #1 (the **D3 write deploy key** + the catalog it
  edits). Best sequenced after #3 (reader) so the admin UI can show the backlog
  item being promoted, but the write path itself only strictly needs #1.

## 5. Acceptance

- An admin can promote a reviewed backlog item to a new `advisories.yaml` entry
  via the Helios button; the change is contract-validated server-side, committed,
  and pushed to `top-level master`; invalid promotions are rejected before any
  write; every promotion is audited.
- `note` provably cannot reach advisory `text`.
- Deterministic, prod-resource-free tests of validation + the commit path
  (against a temp repo, **never** prod `top-level`), plus the live path confirmed
  on prod **after** deploy via `self-deploy*` under lock. Attach an Agent Gate
  Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

The riskiest child epic (holds a `top-level` write credential). Rollback is
disabling the route + revoking/rotating the D3 write key; a bad advisory can be
reverted in `top-level` git and the injector ships fail-safe (empty catalog =
inert). Never point tests at prod `top-level`; use an ephemeral temp repo. Deploy
follows canon (push → `self-deploy*` under lock; never manually restart Helios).
No prod DB, no schema.
slots.delegationNote: RESOLVED_DESIGN Remaining-work #4; depends on child epic 1 (D3 write key + catalog). Operator adopted Security option (c).
slots.title: Agent-waste review queue — Helios: promote-to-advisory admin button (server-side, admin-gated, contract-validated commit+push)
