# Amp cost reduction — `github-worker` child epic **P2**: shrink the base worker prompt + generate the runtime capsule

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality."
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> — **Lever B = §3**, phased plan = §10 (Phase 2), division of work = §10.
> **Capsule contract (already landed in top-level):**
> [`docs/agent-runtime/RUNTIME_CAPSULE.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/RUNTIME_CAPSULE.md),
> the static safety block
> [`docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md),
> and the prepared-workspace contract
> [`docs/agent-runtime/PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 now has **several**
> `github-worker` child epics, the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO
> carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so
> the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic and
> not a sibling. (github-worker's own task-dag adds those trailers when you
> `complete` a task on this issue; keep them.)

## 1. Goal (Lever B, design §3)

Every dispatched agent is fed a **~200-line static base prompt**
([`prompts/base-worker-prompt.txt`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/prompts/base-worker-prompt.txt))
that is re-billed on every turn, plus an `AGENTS.md`-driven bootstrap. Phase 1
already made the dispatcher **prepare** the whole workspace (all repos cloned,
canon on local disk, `task-dag` checked out) and emit a `manifest.json`. This
phase collapses the recurring startup surface to a small, cache-friendly,
byte-stable prefix followed by a generated **runtime capsule**, and moves deep
detail behind the already-prepared commands + on-demand deep-doc reads.

Target prompt order fed to `amp` (design §3):

```text
[stable base worker prompt — small, byte-stable]
[stable canon/runtime capsule — generated, <= budget]
--- cache boundary ---
[bounded live advisories — dynamic but tiny]   (Phase 4; leave a slot)
[per-task issue/task info — worker id, paths, SHAs, URLs]
```

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Shrink the base prompt** | Replace the ~200-line `prompts/base-worker-prompt.txt` with a **small, byte-stable** base prompt (target budget in design §8: ≤700–1,000 tokens). No dynamic content in it — it must be identical across tasks so it stays cacheable. |
| **Generate the runtime capsule** | From the prepared workspace's `manifest.json`, render the capsule per [`RUNTIME_CAPSULE.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/RUNTIME_CAPSULE.md): the "do not bootstrap" notice, work-repo path, all cloned peer-repo paths, top-level path + canon SHA, the `task-dag` script path (`<workspace>/task-dag/scripts/task-dag`), the claimed task SHA/kind/ref, the **hard safety non-negotiables** (embed [`capsule/static-block.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md) verbatim), and the scenario→deep-doc **routing table** (pointers, not the docs). Budget: ≤400–700 tokens. |
| **Order dynamic content last** | Emit worker id, paths, URLs, timestamps, per-task info, and the (future) live-advisory slot **after** the stable prefix so the prefix stays byte-stable. |
| **`agent-prompt-budget` CI check** | Add a CI check that fails if the base prompt or the rendered capsule exceeds the design §8 budgets, so the shrink can't silently regrow. (The top-level advisory-budget sibling work landed [`docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml); this check governs the github-worker-side prompt/capsule surface.) |

## 3. Constraints (do not weaken safety)

- The capsule MUST still carry the hard non-negotiables (the
  [static safety block](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/capsule/static-block.md))
  and the deep-doc routing table — shrinking is a *relocation* of detail behind
  prepared commands + on-demand reads, never a removal of safety rules. See
  design §3 and the canon prepared-workspace exception.
- The static block is mirrored from canon; if you change what it mirrors, the
  canon source is authoritative — coordinate per
  [`docs/canon/UPDATING_CANON.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/UPDATING_CANON.md).
- The capsule must validate against, and stay in lockstep with, the manifest
  schema in
  [`PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md).

## 4. Acceptance (design §10 Phase 2)

- The rendered capsule is **under budget**; the `agent-prompt-budget` CI check
  is present and **enforces** both the base-prompt and capsule budgets.
- A dispatched agent receives: small byte-stable base prompt → generated
  capsule → (advisory slot) → per-task dynamic block, in that order.
- The safety non-negotiables and deep-doc routing are still present in the
  capsule (verify against `capsule/static-block.md`).
- No agent-run canon bootstrap is reintroduced (Phase 1 already removed it).
- Each implementation attaches an Agent Gate Record (canon §3), and the final
  satisfying commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34` **and** this
  issue's `Issue:`/`URL:` trailer (see the completion-signalling note above).

## 5. Production safety / rollback

- The capsule generator and the shrunk prompt are consumed only by the
  dispatcher/worker-loop when it composes the agent prompt; roll back by
  reverting the worker-loop wiring to the old base prompt. Keep the old
  `base-worker-prompt.txt` in history so revert is a one-commit operation.
- Land the CI budget check in the same change (or immediately after) so the
  shrink cannot silently regrow.
- No serving service is touched; there is no deploy step beyond landing on
  `github-worker@master` (the dispatcher reads the repo state per run).
slots.delegationNote: Lever B / design §3 + §10; consumes the runtime-capsule contract already landed in top-level.
slots.title: Amp cost reduction P2: shrink base worker prompt + generate runtime capsule

# nixos-sbc child epic: supervise durable repair reconciliation

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Package and supervise the github-worker repair reconciler and its independent
watchdog on the production host, with encrypted least-privilege credentials,
durable state, safe rollout controls, and a reversible deployment.

## Required implementation

1. Package the reviewed github-worker reconciler/watchdog and one coherent
   canonical task-dag runtime. Do not vendor or reimplement either system.
2. Add `github-worker-repair-reconciler.service` and the separately supervised
   watchdog with the binding design's five-minute jittered cadence, pool of
   four, 30-second restart delay, five-minute start-limit window, durable state
   directories, and bounded resource/sandbox settings.
3. Provision the shared GitHub App ID/private key through age-encrypted systemd
   credentials. Tokens must remain ephemeral and must not enter the Nix store,
   environment dumps, logs, command lines, or persistent state.
4. Package `page-dave` for the watchdog and preserve the single-writer split
   between reconciler `status.json` and watchdog `watchdog.json`.
5. Expose service, dry-run, projection-rollout, and paging kill switches plus
   documented inspection, telemetry, credential-preflight, rollout, rollback,
   and failure procedures. These controls must never override repository
   enrollment: `off|observe|enforce` comes only from current top-level
   `repos.conf` authority.

## Verification

- Nix evaluation/build and unit tests prove command wiring, credentials,
  sandboxing, restart policy, state ownership, disabled defaults, and rollback
  selection without starting a production unit.
- Integration tests use fake GitHub/task-dag endpoints and disposable state;
  no test targets production resources.
- After both code-owning child epics are Oracle-approved and landed, deploy
  only through the canonical `self-deploy*` path. Never manually restart,
  stop, or kill the units.

## Rollout and rollback

Deploy disabled, verify rendered units and credentials, and support the
top-level child's preflight/dry-run and staged observe/enforce rollout. Runtime
rollback disables the new units/controls and selects the previous immutable
packages; it preserves chain refs, repair issues/tasks, and status evidence.
Retain a new-format-compatible task-dag until no active new-format chain
remains. Selecting an older incompatible package first requires the reviewed
compare-and-set migration of every active substate to legacy-safe `State=red`
and readback proving no issue/task will close. Record active red chains before
rollback. A normal git revert remains the configuration rollback path only
after that compatibility gate is satisfied.

This is production control-plane infrastructure. The binding architecture
already has Oracle approval, but the implementation worker must get Oracle
architecture rereview for any design change and Oracle review of the actual
final diff before commit and deployment. Iterate to APPROVE.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```
slots.delegationNote: Package and supervise the reviewed reconciler/watchdog with encrypted credentials, durable state, kill switches, canonical deployment, compatibility-gated rollback, and production verification.
slots.title: Supervise durable broken-master reconciliation safely

# Helios catalog-pricing overhaul — step 1 — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#35](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/35).
> The authoritative umbrella is
> [`docs/epics/catalog-pricing-overhaul/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo. This child epic covers **only step 1** of that umbrella
> (the operator's first #35 comment); later steps are separate child epics.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation` master that satisfies
> any part of this child epic MUST carry a cross-repo completion trailer
> linking back to the parent epic — but see the **Caution** in *Validation*
> below: because #35 is a long-lived multi-step umbrella, confirm the exact
> `Satisfies:` target with the operator before landing so a single completed
> child does not prematurely close #35.

## Step-1 operator ask (verbatim intent)

> Our first step will be a temporary page to let the operator request to see
> the categorical family groups described, and see which product variants
> would be included. We'll use this temporary page to iterate until this part
> works correctly.
>
> Also, verify that our use of LitAlerts now includes geographic limits in the
> request, so we can limit to (a) close competitors and (b) near-mid market
> data without timing out the server requests constantly.

This step is deliberately a **scaffold for iteration**: get family grouping
provably correct and confirm market pulls are geographically bounded, before
building the richer per-family pricing/market UX in later steps.

## Scope owned by this child epic

### T1 — Temporary "Categorical Family Explorer" page

An operator-only, clearly-temporary Helios page (e.g. route
`catalog/family-explorer`, labelled TEMPORARY in-page) that lets the operator:

- Pick the grouping mode: **[nonbrand] categorical family** or **brand
  categorical family** (vendor family is out of scope until the vendor→brand
  mapping exists — say so in the UI).
- Choose the source subset to group over. The operator's step-1 comment does
  not ask for subsets, so the **minimal** deliverable is the whole variant
  catalog (umbrella A-i). "Currently in stock at site" (A-ii) is an optional
  stretch for this step; the richer A-iii/iv/v subsets are later steps. Ship
  the whole-catalog case first; do not block step 1 on any subset.
- See, for the chosen mode/subset, the **resolved family groups** and, for
  each group, **exactly which variants/SKUs are included** (name, SKU,
  brand, category, subcategory, pack qty, unit size, and the size "group" it
  resolved to). The point is auditable membership so the operator can confirm
  the grouping is right.

Reuse, do not rebuild:
- `helios/src/shared/domain/catalogCohort.ts`
  (`buildCatalogCohortKey`, `parseUnitSize`, `CatalogCohortInput`) for the
  non-brand key; extend the key with `brandNorm` for brand families.
- Catalog variant data from `catalog_groups` / catalog snapshots as used by
  `helios/src/server/db/queries/catalogMarketMatchQueries.ts` (`CatalogVariant`).
- Standard page/route wiring: component+loader under
  `helios/src/client/routes/`, registered in
  `helios/src/client/app/router.tsx`; a `registerXRoutes` server module
  registered in `helios/src/server/app/buildServer.ts`; `loadJson` client
  helper; `requireSessionUser(...,'viewer')` on read endpoints.

### T2 — Unit-size "group" equivalency (the operator's core correctness bar)

The family grouping MUST expose a **unit-size group** that implements the
operator's "morally equivalent" size buckets, because plain numeric size is
not what he means:

- Prerolls: roll novelty/marketing sizes into standard ones — 0.6 g → 0.5 g,
  1.1 g → 1.0 g — with **candidate** standard buckets around 0.35, 0.5, 1.0,
  1.5, 2.0 g (boundaries to be confirmed with the operator, see below).
- Other categories keep their natural sizes (edibles ~10 mg; flower 3.5/7/14/28
  g; vapes by size + all-in-one/disposable attribute).

Investigation found this is **not** currently implemented: `catalogCohort.ts`
keys on exact parsed size and `marketMatch/listingParse.ts`'s `sameSizeFamily`
uses numeric tolerance (`max(0.05, size*0.08)`) that does **not** group
0.5/0.6 or 1.0/1.1. Implement a small, well-tested, category-aware size-group
normalizer as a **single-source shared module** (unit-tested with the
operator's examples), and in step 1 wire it **only into the explorer
grouping** so the operator can validate it in isolation. Do **not** rewire
`catalogCohort.ts`'s cohort keys or `sameSizeFamily`'s market matching in this
step — changing those alters the semantics of existing pricing runs and
belongs to the later step that actually touches the pricing/market path. The
bucket table must be easy to review and adjust as the operator iterates.
**Post a representative sample of the prerolls' structured data on #35 and
confirm the bucket boundaries with the operator before hard-coding them** (the
operator explicitly invited follow-up questions here).

### T3 — Verify (and, if needed, enforce) geographic limiting of LitAlerts pulls

This task is **independent of the T1 explorer page**, which pulls no market
data (per-family market pricing is out of scope for step 1). It verifies the
operator's actual ask — that *our use of LitAlerts* in the shared
pricing/market-evidence code is geographically bounded and does not fall back
to unbounded statewide pulls that time out.

Wording reconciliation (must be stated in the closure comment): the operator
says "geographic limits **in the request**", but the LitAlerts partner client
(`helios/src/worker/litalerts/partnerClient.ts`) exposes **no** lat/lng/radius
request parameter — its params are `state`, `includeOOS`, `categoryFilter`,
`subcategoryFilter`, `brandIds`. Helios instead implements the geographic
limit **client-side by retailer selection**: it picks the nearest retailers
(from geocoded `litalerts_retailer_locations`) and issues per-retailer pulls.
The child epic's job is to confirm this selection actually achieves the
intent (bounded, non-timing-out pulls limited to close + near-mid retailers)
and to surface, in the closure comment, that the limit is done by retailer
selection rather than a request param — asking the operator to confirm that
satisfies him, or to say if he specifically wants a request-level radius
(in which case checking whether the LitAlerts API even offers one becomes a
follow-up, not step-1 work).

- The live-evidence path in `helios/src/worker/pricing/litAlertsMarket.ts`
  already fans out over the ~50 nearest retailers
  (`PRICING_NEARBY_RETAILER_FETCH_LIMIT`) via
  `/v1/retailers/:id/products?brandIds=` rather than the statewide
  `/v1/brands/:id/products` "that routinely times out". Distance banding
  (near/mid/far) is in `helios/src/shared/domain/pricingGeneration.ts`.
- **Fan-out count is not the same as a band limit.** The ~50-nearest cap
  bounds request *volume*; it does not by itself guarantee those retailers
  fall within the operator's "(a) close competitors" (near band) or "(b)
  near-mid market" (near + mid bands). The verification MUST establish where
  (if anywhere) evidence is actually filtered to near / near+mid before
  aggregation, and whether the fan-out can currently include far-band
  retailers. Map the operator's (a)/(b) explicitly onto the near / near+mid
  bands and confirm that mapping is enforced, not just assumed.
- Deliverable: a focused test/assertion over the shared market-evidence code
  that any live LitAlerts pull is geographically bounded (nearest-retailer
  fan-out with the near/near+mid band limit applied) and **never** issues the
  unbounded statewide brand call. If any relied-upon path can still issue an
  unbounded statewide pull, or can pull far-band retailers into the "market"
  aggregate, fix it.
- Also confirm the partner client's timeout/retry behavior
  (`helios/src/worker/litalerts/partnerClient.ts`) is unchanged and adequate;
  the fix is bounding request scope, not lengthening timeouts.

This step verifies existing behavior and closes any gap; it is explicitly
**not** a rewrite of the LitAlerts subsystem.

## Explicitly out of scope for step 1 (later child epics)

- The full A subset picker (ever-in-stock / recent-receive / family-superset).
- Per-family market pricing view, mismatch bulk-tagging + re-run, price/promo
  application, and the detailed click-through market-data page (umbrella D).
- Vendor categorical families.
- Making the temporary page permanent/polished — it is a throwaway iteration
  surface; the durable UX comes in later steps.

## Validation

Each landing commit MUST:

1. Land green on `automation` CI: `cd helios && npm run check` (server + client
   typecheck + `vitest run`) and `npm run build`. Add unit tests for the
   size-group normalizer (T2) covering the operator's preroll examples and for
   the geographic-bounding assertion (T3). No first-party `any`; no
   bug-masking fallbacks; deterministic, prod-resource-free tests.
2. Be visible on `vps-nixos-3` after the sanctioned `self-deploy-helios`
   (never manual `systemctl restart` of the helios units).
3. Carry the cross-repo completion trailer on the master-landing commit (or
   the final commit of a multi-commit change). **Caution — #35 is a
   long-lived, multi-step umbrella.** A `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#35`
   trailer feeds `cross-repo-completion-sync` / `close-completed-issues`,
   which close the top-level epic once *every delegated child* has a
   completion. If this step-1 child is the only delegated child when it
   completes, that trailer could **prematurely close #35** before later steps
   are materialised. Before landing, the automation fleet MUST confirm the
   intended trailer target with the operator on #35 — reference the
   materialised step-1 child issue (and rely on the delegation link back to
   #35) rather than blindly closing #35 — so the umbrella stays open across
   steps. Do not assume `Satisfies: #35` is correct here without that check.
4. Honor canon gates: Oracle design review (before implementing) and diff
   review (before landing) for this operator-facing surface; Oracle UI review
   of the page's mobile layout / signal-to-noise / next-action; a recorded
   DB cost/plan for any new catalog query (reuse existing indexed catalog
   reads where possible). Record the Agent Gate Record on each landing.

## Completion signal for the child

This child epic is done when:

- The temporary Categorical Family Explorer renders correct non-brand and
  brand family groups with auditable per-group variant membership, using the
  reviewed size-group equivalency (T1 + T2), demonstrated on `vps-nixos-3`.
- The geographic-limiting verification (T3) is landed with a passing
  assertion/test and a short written confirmation.
- An operator-facing closure/status comment is posted on
  `virusdave/top-level#35` prefixed `<!-- task-dag:status -->` (the automated
  `<!-- task-dag:completion -->` cross-repo signal is emitted by the peer
  repo's completion-sync workflow from the `Satisfies:` trailer — do not
  hand-post it), including the live page URL on `vps-nixos-3`, the commit
  links, the confirmed size-bucket table, and the geographic-band mapping
  with the request-param-vs-retailer-selection reconciliation from T3, so the
  operator can iterate from a concrete baseline into step 2.
slots.delegationNote: Implement step 1 (T1 temporary family-explorer page, T2 category-aware size-group equivalency normalizer wired only into the explorer, T3 verify/enforce geographic-limited LitAlerts pulls) per docs/epics/catalog-pricing-overhaul/child-epics/automation/EPIC_PLAN.md. Honor per-step Oracle design/diff/UI reviews and confirm the size buckets and the Satisfies trailer target with the operator on #35 before landing. #35 is a long-lived multi-step umbrella - do not let a single child completion prematurely close it.

# agent-pain-points migration — nixos-sbc child epic: deploy keys + Helios service wiring (OPERATOR-GATED)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#40](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/40)
> — "Migrate the agent-waste canonical git storage to different repo".
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`virusdave/top-level` → `docs/epics/agent-pain-points-migration/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/agent-pain-points-migration/EPIC_PLAN.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit on
> [`Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc) `master`
> that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#40`, and the **final** satisfying commit MUST
> also carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer.

## 1. Goal

Provision the GitHub deploy keys, agenix secrets, SSH host aliases, and Helios
service env so that (a) the **github-worker dispatcher** (`amp-local`) can
**push** the agent-waste backlog to `virusdave/agent-pain-points`, and (b)
**Helios** can **read** it via a mirror and **write** advisory promotions to it.
This unblocks the github-worker and automation child epics.

## 2. Why this is operator-gated

Encrypting agenix secrets requires the operator's age identity; generating
write-capable GitHub deploy keys and committing encrypted private-key material
is security-sensitive. A worker may prepare the Nix code and exact steps but
**must not** self-provision the key material. Treat this child as
**`task-dag block` + `page-dave` once** until the operator supplies/approves the
key material.

## 3. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Dispatcher write key** | A write-capable GitHub deploy key for `virusdave/agent-pain-points`, wired for the `amp-local` user (agenix secret + SSH host alias `github-agent-pain-points` + gitconfig `insteadOf`/`pushInsteadOf` rewrite), so `scripts/agent-waste-export` pushes there. Model on the existing amp-local `github-top-level-deploy-key` wiring in [`hosts/per-host/vps-nixos-3.nix`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc/blob/master/hosts/per-host/vps-nixos-3.nix) + [`modules/amp-local-user.nix`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc/blob/master/modules/amp-local-user.nix). |
| **Helios read key** | A read deploy key for the mirror, exposed at a stable agenix path (e.g. `/run/agenix/helios-github-agent-pain-points-deploy-key`), owner `helios`. Add to both the primary (vps-nixos-3) and, if the backend-only mirror peer must serve the review route during self-deploy windows, vps-nixos-2. |
| **Helios write key** | A write deploy key for promote (e.g. `/run/agenix/helios-github-agent-pain-points-write-deploy-key`), owner `helios`, primary host. |
| **Helios env** | Set the new Helios env vars the automation child introduces — distinct **read mirror dir** and **write clone dir** plus repo URL + key paths (do **not** overload the `HELIOS_TOP_LEVEL_*` vars; see design §5 hazard). Wire in [`modules/helios.nix`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc/blob/master/modules/helios.nix) / the per-host service block. |
| **secrets.nix** | Register each new `.age` file with the correct `publicKeys` (operator + host) in [`secrets.nix`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc/blob/master/secrets.nix). |

## 4. Constraints / invariants

- Deploy keys are **not path-scoped** (GitHub limitation); the mitigation is
  that `agent-pain-points` is a tiny dedicated repo, so blast radius is small —
  this is precisely the "dedicated advisories repo" isolation the original
  design considered. Keep read and write keys **separate**.
- Read key must be read-only on GitHub; only the promote/export keys are
  write-enabled.
- Follow the existing helios-parser-configs / helios-github-automation deploy
  key patterns for ownership, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, and known-hosts.

## 5. Dependencies / ordering

- **Blocks** the github-worker exporter cutover (needs dispatcher write key) and
  the automation Helios cutover (needs read+write keys).
- Coordinate the actual key rotation-in with the parent epic's §6 cutover.

## 6. Acceptance

- `amp-local` on the dispatcher host can `git push` to `agent-pain-points`
  through the aliased key (verified against an ephemeral throwaway ref, then
  removed — never leave test refs).
- Helios service user can clone/fetch `agent-pain-points` read-only via its key,
  and can push a promotion via its write key (verified against a temp repo /
  ephemeral branch, cleaned up — never prod content).
- `nixos-rebuild`/eval is green; secrets decrypt on the target host.
- Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 7. Safety / rollback

Rollback = revoke/rotate the new deploy keys and revert the Nix change. Never
apply to prod outside the sanctioned deploy path. No prod DB, no schema. Do not
commit unencrypted key material. The new keys are additive; removing them makes
the dependent flows fail closed (advisory injection/review degrade to inert,
never to wrong data).
slots.delegationNote: Operator-gated (agenix/deploy-key provisioning); unblocks the github-worker + automation cutovers.
slots.title: agent-pain-points migration: deploy keys + Helios service wiring (operator-gated)

# Eliminate broken-codebase debt — `automation` child epic (helios + ads)

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#20](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/20).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/fleet-green/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in the
> top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the
> `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (Helios monorepo) slice** of that design,
> covering both the `helios/` and `ads/` packages.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation@master` that
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#20
> ```
>
> **Re-read the parent `EPIC_PLAN.md` before starting** — it is the
> single source of truth; this file is a thin index over it.

## Binding standards (from the parent, do not weaken)

- Required gates (lint, typecheck, test, build) green on `master`.
- No first-party TypeScript `any` (`as any`, `: any`, `any[]`, `<any>`).
- Tests deterministic; tests never touch prod serving resources; force
  test-only config (no `??=` fallback to ambient prod env).
- No disabled/weakened gates (`--no-verify`, `ts-ignore`, `.skip` /
  `.only`, commented-out checks) without an equal-or-stronger replacement.
- Verify in a fresh ephemeral checkout; heavy commands under
  `large-action-lock`. Attach an Agent Gate Record per commit / issue
  update.

## Scope owned by this repo

### Phase A — `helios/` client typecheck debt

1. **Fix the ~13 real client type errors** so
   `tsc -p tsconfig.client.json --noEmit` passes:
   - `Pill` `children` typed `string` but passed `string[]`;
   - `number` → `string` prop mismatches;
   - maplibre `Geometry` / `LngLatLike` casts.
2. **`tsconfig.client.json` hygiene** — stop pulling `*.test.ts` and
   node-using `shared/` modules into the *client* typecheck; they belong
   to the server/node typecheck, not the browser bundle. (Doing this
   first may shrink the error list in step 1.)
3. **Re-enable the client typecheck** in `.githooks/pre-commit`
   (`tsc -p tsconfig.client.json --noEmit`) and remove the
   "disabled, ~9 errors" note. The re-enabled hook must match CI.

### Phase B — `helios/` `any` + test-config debt

4. **Remove the ~31 first-party `any`** in `helios/src` (give each a
   real type; no blanket `unknown` cast-through that re-hides it).
5. **Force test-only config** in smoke/tests — replace
   `DATABASE_URL ??= ...` and any sibling ambient-prod fallbacks with an
   explicit ephemeral test resource, GC'd on every exit path. No test
   may reach a prod DB / live server / prod credential.

### Phase C — `ads/`

6. **Remove first-party `any`** (≈14 files).
7. **Ensure a typecheck/test gate exists for `ads/`** and is green
   (if `ads/` has no gate wired today, add one).

### Phase D — scaffolding to stay green (do once for this repo)

8. **Required-status CI** on `master` / PRs running the full gate set
   (lint, typecheck — server *and* client, test, build).
9. **no-explicit-`any` scanner** — ESLint
   `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: error` where ESLint exists, else
   a grep gate over first-party `src`.
10. **disabled-gate scanner** — flag `--no-verify` recipes,
    commented-out checks, `ts-ignore`, and `.skip` / `.only` in
    committed tests.
11. **test-resource scanner** — flag prod URLs / credentials and
    ambient-env `??=` fallbacks in tests.
12. **Pre-commit hooks installed and matching CI** — no client-typecheck
    carve-out.

## Acceptance

Fresh ephemeral checkout; full gate set (server + client typecheck,
lint, test, build) run and **recorded green** under `large-action-lock`;
scanners (Phase D) added and passing; pre-commit hooks match CI with no
carve-outs; Agent Gate Record attached. Sole exception to green is an
active prod incident, repaired to green immediately after.
slots.delegationNote: FreshlyBakedNYC/automation (Helios monorepo) slice of the fleet-green epic. helios: re-enable client typecheck in .githooks/pre-commit (tsc -p tsconfig.client.json --noEmit), fix ~13 real client errors (Pill children string vs string[]; number->string props; maplibre Geometry/LngLatLike casts), fix tsconfig.client.json hygiene (drop *.test.ts and node-using shared/ modules), remove ~31 first-party any in helios/src, force test-only config in smoke/tests (replace DATABASE_URL ??= ...). ads: remove ~14 first-party any, ensure typecheck/test gate exists and is green. Plus stay-green scaffolding (required-status CI, no-explicit-any scanner, disabled-gate scanner, test-resource scanner, pre-commit matching CI). Verify in a fresh ephemeral checkout; heavy cmds under large-action-lock. Every satisfying commit carries Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#20.

# Amp cost reduction — `github-worker` child epic **P3**: `bin/rg` guardrail wrapper + hit logging

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality."
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> — **Lever C = §4**, phased plan = §10 (Phase 3).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 now has **several**
> `github-worker` child epics, the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO
> carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so
> the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal (Lever C, design §4)

Tool away the single most-recurring agent footgun: passing a value to
ripgrep's short `-r` thinking it means "recursive" (rg recurses by default;
`-r` is `--replace`), which silently rewrites output and corrupts the agent's
own next input. Replace *any prose warning about it* with a deterministic
wrapper that **rejects only the provably-footgun form**, prints the fix, and
records a structured telemetry event. The wrapper lives in the prepared
workspace's `bin/` (first on `PATH`) and logs every hit (Lever D / Phase 4).

## 2. Detection rules (the subtle part)

`-r` consumes the remainder of a bundled short cluster (or the next argv) as
its replacement value, so `-rn` means `--replace=n`, not `-r -n`. The wrapper
MUST:

- **Stop at `--`**: anything after a bare `--` is a pattern/path and MUST never
  trigger rejection (e.g. `rg -- -rfoo` is legitimate).
- **Parse short clusters left-to-right** against the set of value-taking rg
  short flags (`-A -B -C -E -M -d -e -f -g -j -m -r -t -T`): boolean shorts
  consume one char and continue; the **first value-taking short** consumes the
  rest of the cluster (or the next argv) as its value and ends parsing of that
  token.
- **Reject iff `r` is reached in *flag* position**: `-r`, `-r foo`, `-rn` (the
  canonical `--replace=n` corruption), `-nr`, `-inr`.
- **Never reject `r` in *value* position**: `-er` (pattern `r`), `-gr` (glob
  `r`), `-tr`, etc. are legitimate.
- **Pass `--replace` / `--replace=…` through untouched** — that IS the escape
  hatch; no env-var backdoor is added.
- **Fail OPEN on any parse uncertainty**: if a token doesn't match a known
  shape, `exec` the real `rg` unmodified. The guardrail fires only on the
  provably-footgun form; it must never block legitimate expert use.

## 3. Rejection behaviour

- Print a short stderr message with the fix, e.g.: *"`rg -r` rejected: ripgrep
  recurses by default; `-r` is `--replace`. Use `-n`/`-l` to search, or
  explicit `--replace` if you really mean to rewrite."*
- Exit non-zero. **Reject — never silently rewrite argv** (silent rewriting
  recreates the corrupted-output problem in reverse).

## 4. PATH blast radius (wraps `rg` for EVERY agent command)

- Resolve the **real** `rg` by removing the wrapper's own directory from `PATH`
  (or bake the absolute real-rg path in at workspace-prep time). MUST be
  recursion-proof (the wrapper must never invoke itself).
- `exec` the real binary; byte-exact stdout/stderr passthrough and **exact
  exit-code passthrough** (agents rely on rg's `exit 1` = no match, `2` =
  error).
- Pure bash, no per-arg subshells — `rg` is a hot path.
- If the real `rg` cannot be resolved, **fail loud** (do not silently swallow)
  — a missing rg is a workspace-prep bug, not a footgun.

## 5. Workspace / manifest / contract wiring

The prepared workspace currently creates **no** `bin/` dir and adds **nothing**
to `PATH`. This phase adds:

- Create `<bundle>/bin/`, install the `rg` wrapper there, and prepend
  `<bundle>/bin` to the **amp process's** `PATH` (worker-loop export).
- Record `bin_path` and the active guardrail list in `manifest.json`. **This is
  a manifest schema change** → bump `schema_version` and update
  [`PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/PREPARED_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT.md)
  (schema doc + validation list) **and** the workspace `--validate` **in
  lockstep**. This needs the canon §3 Oracle critical-infra diff review.
- **Green-master sequencing:** land the wrapper + tests first (or in one commit
  with tests); make worker-loop and `--validate` tolerate bundles **without**
  `bin/` so no in-flight dispatch breaks during rollout.

## 6. Hit logging → shared waste-telemetry store (Phase-4 contract)

No hard dependency on Phase 4 code. This phase **freezes** the event schema +
path as the P3↔P4 contract; P4 builds ranking on the same file.

- On each rejection, append a design-§5.1 structured NDJSON event:
  ```json
  { "time":"<iso8601>", "repo":"<work repo>", "task_sha":"<sha>",
    "kind":"tool_footgun", "id":"rg-short-r-rejected",
    "severity":"low", "estimated_wasted_tokens":0,
    "estimated_wasted_seconds":0 }
  ```
- Write via `flock -n` (non-blocking) + `O_APPEND` to the designated store
  path. **Operator open question (design §12 Q1):** proposed default
  `~/.local/state/github-worker/agent-waste.ndjson` (single prod host today);
  confirm, or choose a git-ref-mirrored location.
- Logging is **strictly best-effort**: attempt `mkdir -p`; never block on the
  lock; **any** failure is swallowed and MUST NOT alter the wrapper's
  stdout/stderr or exit code.

## 7. Promotion ladder

There is currently **no** `rg -r` advisory in the injected base worker prompt.
So the acceptance criterion is: the wrapper hit-logs, **and** no `rg -r` prose
entry is ever added to the (Phase-4) live advisory budget — the guardrail is
the permanent replacement for that prose. (Retiring any historical KB
"inject-this" flag is tracked by the Phase-3 promotion-ladder task on #34.)

## 8. Tests (deterministic, no prod resources)

- **Parser table** — reject: `-r`, `-rn`, `-nr`, `-inr`, `-r foo`; pass
  through: `--replace x`, `-er`, `-gr`, tokens after `--`, no args,
  `--version`.
- **Recursion safety** — wrapper dir first on `PATH`; wrapper must not call
  itself.
- **Exit-code passthrough** — real rg exit `0`/`1`/`2` preserved.
- **Logging-failure-is-invisible** — read-only state dir must not change the
  wrapper's output or exit code.

## 9. Acceptance

- `rg -r`/`-rn`/etc. rejected with a fix message + structured telemetry event
  logged; `--replace` and all legitimate forms pass through byte- and
  exit-code-exact; workspace/manifest/contract wiring landed with the schema
  bump; master stays green throughout rollout; canon §3 Oracle critical-infra
  diff review recorded for the PATH/manifest change.
- Each implementation attaches an Agent Gate Record (canon §3), and the final
  satisfying commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34` **and** this
  issue's `Issue:`/`URL:` trailer.

## 10. Production safety / rollback

- The wrapper is inert until the workspace installs it and worker-loop prepends
  `bin/` to `PATH`; until then nothing changes.
- Fail-open detection + best-effort logging mean the worst realistic regression
  is a legitimate `rg` invocation wrongly rejected — mitigated by rejecting
  only the provably-footgun form and keeping `--replace`.
- Rollback = stop prepending `bin/` (revert the worker-loop/manifest change);
  the wrapper script alone is harmless.
- The manifest schema bump must land with the contract + `--validate` update so
  no in-flight dispatch fails validation.
slots.delegationNote: Lever C / design §4 + §5.1 hit-logging + §10 Phase 3; installs into the Phase-1 prepared workspace, logs to the Phase-4 waste store.
slots.title: Amp cost reduction P3: bin/rg guardrail wrapper + hit logging

# Helios "Business & Performance Metrics" page tree — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/business-metrics/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo; this child epic scope is **strictly the
> `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` slice of that design**, which is the
> whole thing in v1 — no other peer repo is on the critical path.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation` master that
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>`
> trailer so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post the
> per-phase progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

Everything described in the parent EPIC_PLAN.md, broken out by phase
below. Re-read the parent before starting — the section here is
deliberately a thin index over the parent rather than a re-statement
of the design (the parent is the single source of truth).

### P0 — schema + API contract

- DB migration adding `metric_annotations` per the schema in the
  parent plan (postgres; uses `gen_random_uuid()` and `timestamptz`).
- TypeScript `MetricDef` type + auto-discovering registry under
  `server/src/metrics/**`.
- HTTP endpoints:
  - `GET  /api/metrics`                          → list of `MetricDef` (sans `query`)
  - `GET  /api/metrics/<id>`                     → execute the metric's query
                                                  (query params: `sites`, `from`, `to`, `agg`)
  - `GET    /api/metric-annotations?from=&to=&scope=` → list visible annotations
  - `POST   /api/metric-annotations`              → create (returns full row)
  - `PATCH  /api/metric-annotations/<id>`         → update title/body/tag/scope/t_*
  - `DELETE /api/metric-annotations/<id>`         → soft delete
- Two trivial `MetricDef`s checked in (e.g. `_demo.flat_line` and
  `_demo.random_walk`) so P0 can be exercised end-to-end without
  waiting on real-data SQL.

### P1 — shared chart wrapper + page shell

- React `<MetricChart/>` per the parent design:
  - subscribes to a page-level `TimeAxisContext` (locked by default);
  - 🔒/🔓 toggle to opt the chart out of the shared axis;
  - pan + wheel-zoom that round-trip through the context when locked;
  - "annotate mode" toggle → click (point) or click-drag (range) to
    author a `metric_annotations` row via the P0 API;
  - renders existing annotations in the visible window as 4-px
    vertical ticks at the bottom of the plot, colour-coded by
    `tag`, with hover tooltip;
  - inline edit/delete on the tooltip.
- `/metrics` layout page:
  - left-nav grouped by `metric.group` (auto-built from the registry);
  - global controls bar across the top: **site filter** (multi-select),
    **aggregation** dropdown, **time range / zoom** picker;
  - renders the P0 demo metrics through `<MetricChart/>` end-to-end.

### P2 — Customer acquisition + Margins

Implements these four `MetricDef`s exactly per the parent plan:

- `acquisition.first_vs_returning`
- `margins.effective_gm_pct`
- `margins.gross_margin_dollars`
- `margins.stack_new_vs_returning`

This phase validates the SQL aggregation pattern against real Sweed
order data. Pin the "first-time vs returning" definition to: a
customer is "first-time on order O" iff there is no prior completed
order in our system for the same `customer_id` (Sweed identity). If
Sweed identity isn't stable across the time window, the child-epic
owner documents the fallback in the runbook (P7) and pages the
parent issue with the chosen definition for sign-off **before**
shipping P2.

### P3 — Basket / category / fulfillment / payment

Implements the eight `MetricDef`s in the parent plan's "Basket size",
"Category distribution", and "Fulfillment & payment breakdown"
groups. Includes the category-expand interaction (click a category
in the stack → re-render with the clicked category split into
subcategories).

### P4 — Inventory / slow movers / running low

Implements `inventory.cost_distribution`, `inventory.misalignment`,
`slowmovers.cost_at_risk`, `lowstock.upcoming_outs`. The two
"as-table" panels (slow movers, running low) ship inside the same
`<MetricChart/>` wrapper rendered in table mode — same site filter,
same aggregation (where meaningful), same annotation support — so
that the operator never has to context-switch between table and
chart UX. Expected-margin-loss column for running-low uses the
trailing-21-day daily-margin run-rate for the SKU.

### P5 — Cashier throughput + weather correlation + delivery sub-line

- `cashier.transactions_per_hour` — joins order timestamps against
  the Sweed Shifts RPC's Cashier-role logins; non-manager filter
  applied at the role level.
- `weather.scatter_margin_vs_{high_temp,low_temp,precip}` — adds a
  daily NOAA-pull ingest. Station list lives in a per-site config
  (default mappings: NYC sites → KLGA primary / KJFK fallback;
  child-epic owner picks defaults for other sites and documents them
  in the runbook). If station-selection ergonomics turn out to need
  operator-level edits without a redeploy, the owner files a
  follow-on child epic against `helios-parser-configs` — do **not**
  pre-emptively move it there in v1.
- `delivery.order_count_by_zone` + `delivery.margin_pct`.

### P6 — Customer origin map (static v1)

- OSM-tile base layer (use Helios's existing map tile provider /
  config — do not add a new dependency on a tile vendor for this
  epic).
- Choropleth + heatmap per delivery zip, intensity = order count in
  the selected window. "First-time customers only" toggle. Diff
  overlay vs. a user-selectable prior window ("change since 6 months
  ago"). **No playback.** The playback v2 follow-on is filed as a
  separate issue at the end of this phase but is explicitly not part
  of #7's acceptance criteria.

### P7 — Operator runbook

`docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md` covering:

- "I want a new metric X" — file path, `MetricDef` template,
  picking `defaultAggregation`, registering the metric group, SQL
  idioms (when to use `time_bucket()`, when to fall back to
  DuckDB, how to keep the site filter param SQL-injection-safe).
- Annotation model (point vs range, `scope=global|metric:<id>`,
  soft-delete semantics).
- Sanity checks to run after a Sweed backfill (cross-check totals
  against the existing Helios `/pricing` daily summary).
- Closure-comment template: at P7 land time, post the comment per
  the parent epic's acceptance criteria #6 on `virusdave/top-level#7`.

## Out of scope for v1 (filed as follow-ons at P7 close)

- `cashier.upsell_lift` (statistical-significance per-cashier).
- `promos.{summary,detail}`.
- `customers.origin_playback` (animated timeline scrub of the map).
- Threshold-based alerting on any metric.
- Mobile-optimised layout.

## Validation per phase

Each phase MUST:

1. Land green on `automation`'s existing CI (typecheck, unit, e2e
   if applicable).
2. Be visible on `vps-nixos-3` after the standard
   `systemctl restart helios-{prep,server,worker}` bounce
   (per `AGENTS.md` of `automation`).
3. Carry both `Phase: P<n>` and `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7`
   trailers on the master-landing commit (or the final commit of a
   multi-commit phase).
4. For P2 and beyond: include at least one screenshot link (in the
   commit message or a docs PR) demonstrating the new panel
   rendering against live data on `vps-nixos-3`. Helios is
   operator-only so the screenshot link is for the operator's
   review, not for the public.

## Completion signal for the child

This child epic is done when:

- P0–P7 are landed per the trailer convention above.
- The acceptance criteria 1–6 in the parent epic plan are
  demonstrated on `vps-nixos-3`.
- A closure comment is posted on `virusdave/top-level#7` per the
  P7 runbook section above, including:
  - the live `/metrics` URL on `vps-nixos-3`;
  - the per-phase commit links;
  - a one-line note for each deferred v2 item with the follow-on
    issue number(s) filed against this repo.
slots.delegationNote: Helios /metrics page tree — shared time-axis chart wrapper (pan/zoom/lock/unlock), metric_annotations table+API, global site filter + aggregation selector, v1 metric panels (acquisition, margins, basket, category, inventory, slow movers, running-low, cashier throughput, fulfillment breakdown, weather scatter, delivery sub-line, customer origin map static-v1), plus operator runbook.

# Tooling `--help` safety — `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc` child epic (safety-critical)

> Parent epic: [virusdave/top-level#47](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/47)
>
> The implementation commit on this repo's master MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47
> ```
>
> That trailer triggers the cross-repo completion flow back to the parent
> issue.

## Why this is safety-critical

Our `self-deploy*` deploy wrappers are the single sanctioned way to roll
production services. They currently do **no flag parsing** and barge
straight into their effectful core, so an agent invoking one with
`--help` — expecting only usage text — can trigger a real production
rollout (`nixos-rebuild switch`, traffic flips, unit restarts, SSH to the
peer host). Canon now forbids this.

## Step 0 — read canon first

Read the rule before touching anything (ephemeral checkout of top-level
master):

- [`docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md) "Code standards" — the normative `--help` rule.
- [`docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md) "Serving services" — the deploy-safety face of it.

## The requirement

Every invocable tool must accept `-h` and `--help`, print usage to
stdout, and exit `0` **before any effect** — for these deploy tools,
before any `nixos-rebuild`, traffic/mirror flip, `systemctl`
restart/drain, deploy-lock acquisition, SSH to a peer, secret read, or
file write. Handle `--help` first, ahead of all other option parsing and
required-env checks.

## Known violators (audit for more — this list is a starting point)

- `self-deploy` — inline bash in `hosts/vps/amp-local.nix` (the
  whole-host `nixos-rebuild switch` package).
- `self-deploy-helios` — inline bash in `modules/helios.nix` (traffic
  flip + `helios-prep`/`helios-server` restart + `/healthzz` poll).
- `self-deploy-{site}` — generated by the `mkSelfDeployScript` factory in
  `hosts/vps/sites-mirror.nix` (per-site MSS rollout). Fix the factory
  once so every generated package inherits `--help` handling.
- `scripts/helios-deploy` — orchestrates `self-deploy-helios` across
  primary/mirror; begins Phase 1 SSH immediately.
- Any other scripts in `scripts/` and any other nix-packaged CLIs you
  find during the audit.

Note: `scripts/update-amp-local-version.sh` and
`update-amp-local-version-everywhere.sh` already handle `-h`/`--help`
correctly — mirror their pattern (a `usage()` that exits 0, parsed
first).

## Verifying without deploying

**Do not run an actual deploy to test.** For each nix-packaged tool,
`nix build` the package and run the built script with `--help`, asserting
it prints usage and exits 0 with zero side effects. Landing on
`nixos-sbc` master does not auto-deploy (deploy stays manual via
`self-deploy`), and adding an early `--help` exit ahead of all effects is
a low-risk, easily-reverted change. Keep a clean revert path.

## Finalize

Commit with a plain imperative subject (no `feat:`/`fix:` prefix) and the
`Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47` trailer; push to this repo's default
branch.
slots.delegationNote: Safety-critical; self-deploy*/helios-deploy must print usage and exit 0 before any nixos-rebuild, traffic flip, restart, lock, or SSH.
slots.title: Add innocuous --help to self-deploy* and deploy tooling

# github-worker child epic: strict dispatcher freshness and recovery

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#64`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/64)
· Binding design:
[`durable-dispatch-input-recovery.md`](../../../../designs/durable-dispatch-input-recovery.md)

## Goal

Keep dispatcher inputs observably current and recover from prolonged local
mirror or event-delivery failures without ever authorizing work from stale
state.

## Required implementation

1. **Verified mirror success evidence**
   - Fetch task refs plus default history atomically under the existing
     per-repository lock, verify `HEAD`, then atomically publish repository,
     remote fingerprint, completion time, `HEAD` SHA, and task-ref snapshot
     hash.
   - Store attempts/errors separately. Failure, malformed/future metadata, or
     remote changes do not advance success.
   - Continue roughly minute-scale polling. A failed current fetch always
     skips that repository for the cycle; the last-good mirror is never a
     dispatch authorization source.

2. **Strict prolonged-failure fallback**
   - After the configurable default 180-second success-age threshold, create
     at most one host-wide, per-repository-locked, full-history temporary bare
     clone with cooldown/backoff.
   - Strictly fetch and verify before canonical task-dag
     `frontier --no-fetch` / `roots --no-fetch`. Any uncertainty produces no
     candidate or claim.
   - Strictly refresh and recompute again before spawn.
   - Trap-own a selected fallback through claim, agent handoff,
     block/release/retirement, signals, and exit. Remove unselected fallbacks
     after scanning. Never copy fallback state to the primary mirror.

3. **Managed task-dag CLI mode fix**
   - At module source, distinguish a non-empty explicit `TASK_DAG_BIN`
     override from managed mode. A bad explicit override fails with no network
     fallback; a valid one stays pinned.
   - Managed exports never become overrides. Track attempt/success and
     backoff, build and validate a coherent checkout, then publish/export an
     exact immutable `versions/<commit>/` path.
   - Keep last-good on failure. Retain all versions initially; do not delete by
     age. Any future GC needs invocation leases and separate review.
   - Log mode, commit, success age, attempt/error, and backoff.

4. **Independent comment watchdog**
   - Under one host lease, invoke task-dag's canonical reconciler for every
     registry repo approximately every two minutes with a 15-minute overlap.
   - Run a complete audit daily and at startup when its success heartbeat is
     stale.
   - Configure per-repository `ingestion_start_at` and explicit reviewed
     historical allowlist; first full run is dry-run and bounded.
   - Monitor heartbeat independently from GitHub Actions. Bound duration,
     pagination, concurrent repos, and rate use. Never replace task-dag's
     classifier or receipt semantics in github-worker.

5. **Configuration and operations**
   - Ship fallback and watchdog disabled, with documented flags, thresholds,
     metrics, alerts, and rollback.
   - Keep existing origin claim compare-and-swap and pre-spawn verification.
   - Use the canonical task-dag checkout, never a vendored fallback.

## Required tests

- Successful atomic fetch advances success metadata; partial/failing fetch
  changes neither verified snapshot nor success time.
- A block added after last success can never spawn during later fetch failures.
- Under-threshold failure skips; over-threshold concurrent workers construct
  one fallback; fallback fetch failure produces no claim.
- Selected fallback survives pre-spawn reverify, release, retirement, signal,
  and cleanup paths. Primary recovery resumes without copying fallback state.
- Remote URL change, malformed/future timestamp, and concurrent claims fail
  safely.
- Valid explicit CLI override performs zero network; invalid override fails;
  managed first clone, pre-TTL call, successful/failed post-TTL refresh,
  backoff, candidate validation, concurrency, immutable publication, and logs
  are deterministic.
- Watchdog recent/full cadence, stale heartbeat startup, host lease, dry-run,
  bounded apply, task-dag failure, and rate-limit behavior are covered without
  production resources.
- Repository light checks and full final presubmit pass.

## Rollout and rollback

After the task-dag child is live, deploy this code disabled. Review first-audit
dry-run counts per repository, enable recent reconciliation, then bounded full
audits, and enable mirror fallback last. Roll only via github-worker's
canonical deployment path.

Production verification deliberately suppresses a test event and injects
isolated git-remote failures; it does not touch serving services or databases.
Rollback disables watchdog/fallback and selects the previous immutable CLI
version while preserving additive receipts.

This is critical infrastructure. Obtain Oracle design review before coding and
Oracle diff review after implementation; iterate to APPROVE before commit.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#64
```
slots.delegationNote: Implement verified minute-scale mirror success, bounded strict full-clone fallback, managed task-dag CLI refresh, the independent reconciliation watchdog, deterministic tests, and operator-visible telemetry.
slots.title: Make dispatcher inputs fresh, observable, and fail-closed

# Helios build hygiene — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#22](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/22)
> ("codebase cleanup & hygiene"). The authoritative design is
> [`docs/designs/codebase-cleanup-and-hygiene.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/codebase-cleanup-and-hygiene.md)
> in the top-level repo (§1 verified findings, §3.2 build design, §4
> Phase 3, §6 resolved decisions 4 & 5).
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`
> `master` and satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#22
> ```
>
> This is **Phase 3** only: small, low-risk build-setup changes that help
> even on the current shared production build box and need no off-prod
> infrastructure. The heavier "move build off prod / off-prod CI"
> work is **Phase 4**, tracked separately and parked in
> [virusdave/top-level#23](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/23).

## Verified starting state (read directly from `automation`)

- Helios build = plain `tsc` + `vite` over npm (`helios/package.json`):
  `build` = `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` (+ asset copy) then `vite
  build`. No turbo/nx, no build cache, no build/test CI.
- `helios/package.json` has **no** `typecheck` / `test` / `lint` scripts
  (so "build & test always pass on master" is currently unenforceable).
  `vitest` is a dependency but unscripted.
- `tsconfig.server.json` names a `tsBuildInfoFile` but does **not** set
  `incremental` / `composite`, so the file is inert and every server
  build re-typechecks from scratch. `skipLibCheck: true` is already set.
- No `flake.nix` / devShell — toolchain (node/tsc/vite) is whatever the
  host provides.

> Re-verify all of the above in a **fresh ephemeral checkout** before
> editing; do not trust this snapshot blindly. Run any heavy command
> (`npm ci`, `tsc`, `vite build`, `vitest`) under `large-action-lock` —
> the build host is the 2 vCPU / ~2 GiB production box.

## Scope owned by this repo (Helios) — Phase 3

### H1 — Turn on incremental TypeScript (near-zero risk, behavior-preserving)
- Set `"incremental": true` in `tsconfig.server.json` so the existing
  `tsBuildInfoFile` actually caches and warm `build:server` stops
  re-typechecking from scratch. Consider `composite` + project
  references for the client/server split if it's a clean win; don't
  force it.
- Persist the `.tsbuildinfo` between runs (on-box now; graduates to
  `actions/*` cache when an off-prod builder exists — that's Phase 4 / #23).
- Ensure `tsc` `include` does **not** pick up `dist`/build outputs as
  source (`exclude` them) so outputs are never re-consumed as input.

### H2 — Add the missing check scripts + make `check` the required pre-push gate
- Add to `helios/package.json`:
  - `typecheck` → `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit` (and the client
    tsconfig if applicable),
  - `test` → `vitest run`,
  - `check` → runs `typecheck` + `test` (+ a fast build sanity if cheap).
- Wire `check` as the **required pre-push gate** each agent runs before
  `git push` (the decided "master always green" mechanism for now;
  design decision 5). A GitHub-hosted/self-hosted CI backstop +
  branch-protection is Phase 4 (#23), not this epic.

### H3 — Idempotent, self-prerequisite build env (#22 problem 1)
- Add an `ensure-build-env` step the build owns and that is safe cold or
  warm:
  - `npm ci` (lockfile-pinned) when `node_modules` is absent/stale,
    using the on-box `~/.npm` cache;
  - `mkdir -p` every output dir the scripts assume (generalise the
    existing `mkdir -p dist/server/...` so no step fails on a
    missing-or-already-present dir);
  - never assume — and never fail merely because — `node_modules`/`dist`
    already exist.
- Wire `build` / `test` / `check` to call `ensure-build-env` first.
- Add an **idempotence matrix** test (cold checkout; warm `node_modules`;
  stale `dist`; post `git clean -xfd`; run `check` twice) so artifact
  flakiness can't regress.

### H4 — Reproducible toolchain via Nix devShell (operator suggestion D)
- Add a `flake.nix` (or `shell.nix`) devShell pinning node + npm (+ any
  system libs) so `nix develop` / `nix-shell` gives an identical,
  declarative build environment locally and on the box. Additive; pairs
  with `ensure-build-env` (devShell = toolchain, script = project
  prereqs).

## Out of scope (Phase 4 — see #23)
- Moving heavy build/test off the production box onto a builder host.
- Off-prod build/test CI + `actions/*` caches + branch-protection
  required checks.
- Nix **binary cache** / Nix-closure deploy.

## Acceptance
- `helios` has working `typecheck` / `test` / `check` scripts; `check`
  is green on `master` and is the documented required pre-push gate.
- Server build is incremental (warm builds measurably faster) and never
  consumes build outputs as source.
- A cold checkout and a warm checkout both `check` successfully (the
  idempotence matrix passes); the build sets up its own prerequisites.
- A `flake.nix` devShell pins the toolchain.
- Every satisfying commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#22`.
slots.delegationNote: Phase 3 of the codebase-cleanup epic. In helios/: set "incremental":true in tsconfig.server.json (the tsBuildInfoFile is currently inert) and exclude dist from tsc include; add typecheck (tsc --noEmit), test (vitest run), and check npm scripts and make check the required pre-push gate; add an idempotent ensure-build-env (npm ci against ~/.npm, mkdir -p output dirs, never assume/fail on existing node_modules/dist) wired into build/test/check plus a cold/warm idempotence matrix test; add a flake.nix devShell pinning node/npm. Re-verify state in a fresh ephemeral checkout; run any heavy cmd (npm ci/tsc/vite/vitest) under large-action-lock since the build host is the 2vCPU/2GiB prod box. Out of scope (Phase 4, see top-level#23): moving build off-prod, off-prod CI/caches, branch protection, Nix binary cache. Every satisfying commit carries Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#22.
slots.title: Helios build hygiene — tsc incremental, check gate, idempotent build env, flake devShell (top-level#22)

# GAds → Landing-pages analytics (V1) — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#18](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/18).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/gads-landing-analytics/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in the top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the
> `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (Helios) slice of that design**, which in
> V1 is the whole thing — no other peer repo is on the critical path.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation@master` that
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#18
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>` trailer
> (`P0`..`P5`) so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post the
> per-phase progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

Everything in the parent `EPIC_PLAN.md`, broken out by phase below.
**Re-read the parent before starting** — the parent is the single source
of truth; this file is a thin phase index over it.

## Binding constraints (from the parent, do not weaken)

- **Confidential, per-site access.** Three grants `gads-bronx`,
  `gads-midtown`, `gads-all`. `gads-all` is its own grant, never
  synthesised from the per-site grants. The server derives the site
  predicate from the authenticated route/grant and MUST NOT accept a
  client `site`/`sites` param that widens scope.
- **Cheap DB, by operator decree.** One small rollup table refreshed
  out-of-band; **no** per-assignment fact table, **no** hourly+daily
  rollup pair, **no** always-on derivation worker, **no** CAGGs /
  hypertable conversion / compression / HLL in V1. Each of those, if
  ever proposed, needs its own Oracle DB review. Do not fight epic #11.
- **Serving never touches raw `lp_events`.** Dashboard reads hit only
  `gads_lp_rollup` (+ the refresh-state row). A test asserts this.
- **Observed performance, not accounting.** No causal claims. Revenue
  and ROAS render "Unavailable" (no fake numbers). Cost is allocated and
  badged. Hide variant rows < 25 assignments behind a toggle.
- **Canon gates at implementation time:** the DB migration + refresh
  query ship with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` plans and a payload
  byte-size measurement (canon DB gate); the UI gets the mandatory
  Oracle UI review before it ships; record the Agent Gate Record on each
  commit / issue update.

---

### P0 — Audit + lock semantics (do this first)

No schema change yet; produce a short design note (committed or linked).

- Verify the live `lp_events` columns + existing indexes match the
  parent's assumptions (`assignment_id`, event types, `site`, `family`,
  `cluster_slug`, `experiment_id`, `policy_id`, `policy_rule_id`,
  `branch_id`, `served_probability_bps`, `assignment_key_type`,
  `gclid_hash`, `traffic_flags`, `event_ts`). Confirm `assignment_id`
  presence per stage and whether `branch_id` is whole-page vs per-slot.
- **Define + test the GAds traffic predicate** (biggest correctness
  risk): which `assignment_key_type` / `traffic_flags` count as paid.
  Decide handling of `cookie`/`session`/`default` (default: exclude
  from cost/CPA, badge "GAds-detected traffic only").
- Pick the **reporting timezone** (America/New_York / Ads business
  zone) for `assignment_day`; document it.
- Lock the exact metric formulas: assignment-level-unique funnel counts;
  `conversions_7d/30d/90d` semantics; right-censoring of immature
  cohorts; sample threshold (25); allocated-cost basis (must sum back to
  the aggregate snapshot total per day/site/campaign bucket).
- `EXPLAIN` the candidate refresh query over a realistic date range on
  current data volume; decide whether the one partial `lp_events` index
  is needed.
- Pick the initial refresh cadence (30-60 min; default to the slower
  end).

Deliverable: design note + the confirmed predicate/timezone/formulas.

### P1 — Grants, routes, access enforcement

Files: `shared/contracts/domain/auth.ts` (grant enum),
`helios/src/client/routes/metrics/MetricsLayoutPage.tsx`
(`MetricsTabId`, `METRICS_TABS`, `METRICS_TAB_ALIASES`), server auth
middleware/route guard.

- Add `MetricGrantKey` values `gads-bronx`, `gads-midtown`, `gads-all`.
- Add the three tab ids + aliases so
  `/metrics/gads-<site>` -> `/metrics/gads-<site>/landing-pages`.
- Add the typed `GADS_METRIC_SCOPES` registry (grant -> site scope).
- Server-side grant + scope enforcement; `gads-all` requires its own
  grant explicitly.
- Regression tests: Bronx user cannot read Midtown or all; Midtown
  cannot read Bronx or all; holding both site grants does **not** grant
  all; unauthorized responses leak no site list / no cross-site data.

### P2 — Rollup storage + refresh job

Files: new migration under `helios/...migrations`, new worker job under
`helios/src/worker/jobs/`, query helper under
`helios/src/server/db/queries/`.

- Migration: `gads_lp_rollup` (grain + measures per parent §3),
  `gads_lp_rollup_refresh_state`, and (only if P0 proved it needed) the
  one partial `lp_events` index.
- Idempotent refresh job on the P0 cadence: recompute a **bounded 90-day
  assignment-day horizon** (so late `lp_conversion`s update the correct
  older bucket), dedupe duplicate event posts, apply the GAds traffic
  predicate, compute counts in the reporting timezone, join allocated
  GAds cost conservatively, write the refresh-state row.
- Ship `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` for the refresh query in the commit
  body.
- Tests/fixtures: duplicate events deduped; late conversion updates the
  right assignment-day bucket; 7/30/90d counts correct; allocated cost
  sums back to the snapshot total.

### P3 — Serving endpoint

Files: `shared/contracts/api/gadsLandingPages.ts`,
`server/db/queries/gadsLandingPagesQueries.ts`, the route handler.

- `GET /api/gads/<site-scope>/landing-pages` returns hero KPIs + funnel
  + variant table (top N, 25-50) + per-site breakdown (for `gads-all`) +
  freshness/badging metadata, in **one** compact payload.
- Site predicate derived from the grant, never widened by client input.
- Reads **only** `gads_lp_rollup` + the refresh-state row; a test
  asserts no raw `lp_events` query on the serving path.
- Ship the full-fetch payload byte-size measurement (canon DB gate).

### P4 — UI (Landing pages sub-page)

Files: `helios/src/client/routes/metrics/gads/` (new `GAdsTab`,
`GAdsLandingPagesTab`), reuse `MetricsAccessGate`, range presets +
`RangeNudgeRow`, `ControlsSection`, metrics CSS; extract shared
`MetricRangeControls`.

- Sub-page nav: Landing pages active; Campaigns / Creative / Keywords /
  Policy health / Experiments / Evolution / Iteration as disabled
  "Coming soon" stubs.
- First screen order per parent §5: freshness+attribution strip -> KPI
  strip -> next-action card (top 3 review candidates, each with a direct
  action) -> funnel waterfall (biggest drop-off inline) -> variant table
  (mobile-first, sticky action column, low-sample toggle).
- Revenue/ROAS rendered "Unavailable" with explanatory copy; cost
  badged "allocated"; right-censored cohorts badged. No em-dashes.
- **Mandatory canon Oracle UI review before it ships** (record the link
  on the peer issue).

### P5 — Docs, observability, rollout

- Runbook notes: refresh cadence, how to inspect the last refresh, how
  to manually rebuild the rollup.
- Lightweight job logging/metrics for the refresh.
- Document the deferred V2 items (mss enrichment, revenue/ROAS, Timescale
  features, future sub-pages).
- Deploy via the canonical `self-deploy-helios` path (no manual service
  surgery).

---

## Out of scope (V2 / later epics)

mss event-schema enrichment (order id / revenue / device class /
page-load-failure event on `lp_conversion`); exact Sweed revenue
attribution + ROAS/CPA + cancellation/refund handling; gclid-level cost;
bandit-aware off-policy stats; the reserved sub-pages; Timescale
CAGGs/hypertable/HLL. Each gets its own design + Oracle review when it
lands.

BINDING: three per-site confidential grants gads-bronx/gads-midtown/gads-all (gads-all is its own grant, never synthesised; server derives site scope from the grant, never from a client param); cheapest DB (one small periodically-refreshed gads_lp_rollup, no fact table/hourly+daily/derivation worker/CAGGs/hypertable/HLL - do not fight epic #11); serving never reads raw lp_events; observed performance not accounting (revenue/ROAS Unavailable, cost allocated+badged, hide rows <25 assignments, no causal claims, no auto-disable). P0 first: define+test the GAds traffic predicate, pick reporting timezone, lock formulas. Phases P0-P5.
