# Helios signed readonly access — `automation` child epic

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#62](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/62)
> — "Need a means for local agents to access helios in trusted fashion".
> **Resolved design:** [`docs/epics/helios-agent-readonly-access/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](../../RESOLVED_DESIGN.md).
> **Delegated because:** the verifier, auth/session contracts, route gates,
> response caps, and audit logging live in `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` under
> `helios/`. Do not implement the NixOS key/config rollout or the agent-side
> browser helper in this child epic.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` for this epic MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#62`, plus
> this child epic's own `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer
> so the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to this delegated child.

## 1. Goal

Implement the **Helios-native** half of temporary, non-mutating, auditable live
verification for local agents. A local `amp-local` verifier will sign each
request with an Ed25519 private key; Helios verifies the request with configured
public keys, checks a narrow expiring allowlist, and then exposes only a
synthetic `agent_readonly` viewer principal.

This is not a general machine-to-machine API, not a write path, not a normal
operator login, and not a reason to weaken OAuth for real users.

## 2. Current state to inspect first (all paths under `helios/`)

| Concern | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Global auth gate | `src/server/auth/authGate.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) | Currently allows health/login/session/public endpoints and valid signed session cookies; all other app/API/asset paths are session-gated. Integrate signed-agent verification before the unauthenticated response, without adding broad public endpoints. |
| Session envelope + role gates | `src/server/auth/requireSession.ts` | `buildSessionEnvelope()` reads a signed cookie and DB user; `requireSessionUser()`, `requireMetricsGrant()`, `requireConfidentialMetricsGrant()`, and `requireCashierDisplayUser()` enforce downstream authorization. Add the explicit `agent_readonly` principal here, not a fake DB user or cookie. |
| Session contract | `src/shared/contracts/api/session.ts`, `src/server/routes/session.ts` | `authMode` is currently `anonymous | session`. Add `agent_readonly` and ensure `/api/session` returns a synthetic viewer envelope only for accepted signed-agent requests. |
| Permission helpers | `src/shared/domain/permissions.ts`, `src/shared/contracts/domain/auth.ts`, `src/server/auth/permissions.ts` | Reuse existing viewer permission semantics and role ordering; do not add editor/admin shortcuts for the synthetic principal. |
| Runtime config/env | `src/server/config/env.ts` | Add env/config parsing for public verifier keys, active allowlist JSON/path, timestamp skew, nonce cache sizing/TTL if needed, and default response byte cap. Keep private signing keys out of Helios config. |
| Server assembly | `src/server/app/buildServer.ts`, `src/server/main.ts` | Wire verifier/allowlist initialization through the existing app lifecycle. Signed-agent access must fail closed when config is absent or malformed. |
| Route tests/patterns | `src/server/auth/authGate.test.ts`, focused route tests under `src/server/routes/*.test.ts` | Extend existing `server.inject` patterns for accepted/denied signed requests and downstream gate denial. |
| Metrics/admin/cashier gates | `src/server/routes/metrics.ts`, `src/server/routes/catalogAnalytics.ts`, `src/server/routes/budtenderAnalytics.ts`, admin/config routes, cashier-display route using `requireCashierDisplayUser()` | Add focused coverage that `agent_readonly` can satisfy only viewer routes explicitly allowed by rule, and is denied for metrics grants, admin/config, cashier-display, and mutating routes. |

## 3. Design decisions to preserve

1. **Ed25519, not HMAC.** Helios stores public verifier keys only. A Helios
   config leak must not grant signing power.
2. **GET/HEAD only.** `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, and `OPTIONS` are denied
   before route handling, even with a valid signature and allowlist rule.
3. **No mixed credentials.** Any signed-agent request carrying `Cookie` or
   `Authorization` is rejected before route handling. Do not allow a real user
   session and an agent signature to combine.
4. **Signature covers the exact authorization decision.** The canonical payload
   covers method, host, exact path + query, timestamp, nonce, key id, and rule
   id. Reject ambiguous path/query encodings rather than silently normalizing
   them into an authorization decision.
5. **Narrow, expiring allowlist.** No `/api/*`, `/api/admin/*`, or page-rule
   implies API-rule behavior. Every rule has `not_before`, `not_after`, owner,
   reason, path entries, safe-read notes, and a response byte cap.
6. **Explicit `agent_readonly` principal.** Do not mint a cookie and do not
   create a `users` row. Viewer-only route code may see a synthetic viewer;
   editor/approver/admin, metrics grants, confidential metrics, and cashier
   display still deny.
7. **Metadata audit only.** Log accepted and denied signed requests with
   outcome/reason, key id, rule id, method, path, status, response bytes,
   remote/forwarded metadata, timestamp, and nonce. Never log private keys,
   signatures, cookies, authorization headers, or response bodies.
8. **Response caps are enforced in code.** Deny or abort oversized responses;
   do not rely on route authors or downstream clients to self-limit.

## 4. Request contract

Use a small explicit header set (names may change if implementation finds an
existing naming convention, but the semantics must stay):

| Header | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `X-Helios-Agent-Key-Id` | Selects the configured public verifier key. |
| `X-Helios-Agent-Rule-Id` | Selects the allowlist rule claimed by the request. |
| `X-Helios-Agent-Timestamp` | RFC3339 or Unix timestamp; reject outside a short 60–120s skew window. |
| `X-Helios-Agent-Nonce` | Random per request; reject replay within the skew window. |
| `X-Helios-Agent-Signature` | Base64url Ed25519 signature over the canonical payload. |

Canonical payload shape:

```text
helios-agent-readonly-v1
method:GET
host:helios.freshlybaked.us
path:/config/agent-waste?tab=pending
key_id:amp-local-vps3-2026q3
rule_id:agent-waste-review-2026-07-10
timestamp:2026-07-10T05:30:00Z
nonce:<128-bit random base64url>
```

Replay protection can be an in-memory per-process `(keyId, nonce)` cache for
v1. Document cross-process/cross-host replay within the short skew window as a
residual risk; do not add a DB/shared nonce store unless the implementation
task obtains the required review and operator approval.

## 5. Allowlist contract

Read allowlist rules from Helios runtime config provisioned by the NixOS child.
Example shape:

```json
{
  "id": "agent-waste-review-2026-07-10",
  "owner": "virusdave/top-level#62 rollout",
  "reason": "Verify the agent-waste review page after deploy and collect Oracle UI evidence.",
  "not_before": "2026-07-10T00:00:00Z",
  "not_after": "2026-07-17T00:00:00Z",
  "max_response_bytes": 1048576,
  "paths": [
    { "method": "GET", "kind": "page", "match": "exact", "path": "/config/agent-waste", "safe_read_note": "SPA route only; no write action." },
    { "method": "GET", "kind": "api", "match": "exact", "path": "/api/agent-waste/backlog", "safe_read_note": "Read-only backlog endpoint; no promote/write path." },
    { "method": "GET", "kind": "asset", "match": "prefix", "path": "/assets/", "safe_read_note": "Hashed Vite static assets only; byte-capped." },
    { "method": "GET", "kind": "session", "match": "exact", "path": "/api/session", "safe_read_note": "Returns synthetic agent_readonly envelope only." }
  ]
}
```

Implementation requirements:

- Prefer exact path matches. Prefix matches require segment-boundary checks and
  should normally be limited to hashed static assets.
- Page rules do not imply API rules; list every SPA loader/API call separately.
- API rules require route-specific safe-read notes because a `GET` handler can
  still trigger refreshes, external calls, streams, costly DB scans, cache
  writes, or large downloads.
- Deny streaming/SSE/download responses by default. Any future CSV/ZIP/report
  route needs an explicit rule and cap.
- Fail closed if allowlist JSON is absent, invalid, inactive, expired, or has an
  unknown kind/match shape.

## 6. Suggested implementation leaves

Author these as the child epic's own frontier leaves when the automation epic
root is broken down:

### H1 — Verifier + allowlist parser (no auth bypass yet)

- Add a small signed-readonly module, e.g. `src/server/auth/agentReadonly.ts`,
  that parses headers, builds the canonical payload, verifies Ed25519
  signatures using configured public keys, checks timestamp skew, rejects nonce
  replay, evaluates allowlist method/path/rule activity, and returns a typed
  accept/deny result with an audit reason.
- Add env/config parsing in `src/server/config/env.ts` for public verifier keys,
  allowlist JSON/path, skew, and default/max response cap. Helios must never
  read private signing material.
- Tests: canonical payload bytes, signature success/failure, unknown key, bad
  base64, missing headers, timestamp too old/too new, nonce replay, inactive
  rule, exact/prefix path matching, method mismatch, broad/invalid rule denial,
  and ambiguous path/query rejection.

### H2 — Auth gate integration + audit + byte caps

- Integrate the verifier into `authGate.ts` before unauthenticated redirects or
  401s. Accepted signed-agent requests should attach an `agent_readonly`
  principal to the request for downstream session code; denied signed attempts
  should return a flat 401/403-style response and should not fall through to a
  cookie path.
- Reject `Cookie` or `Authorization` on signed-agent requests before route
  handling.
- Enforce allowlist `max_response_bytes` for accepted signed-agent responses;
  abort/deny and audit `too_large` if the cap is exceeded. Ensure `HEAD` does
  not accidentally require a body to count bytes.
- Add structured log entries for accepted and denied signed-agent attempts,
  metadata only.
- Tests: `authGate.test.ts` accepted GET/HEAD, POST denied, mixed credentials
  denied, non-allowlisted page/API/asset denied, oversized response denied, and
  no signatures/secrets/cookies in logs.

### H3 — Session/principal contract

- Extend the session contract to `authMode: 'anonymous' | 'session' |
  'agent_readonly'`.
- Update `buildSessionEnvelope()` / `requireSessionUser()` so an accepted
  `agent_readonly` request returns a synthetic active viewer such as
  `agent-readonly@local.helios`, with viewer permissions and an empty
  `metricGrants` list, only where the caller asks for `viewer`.
- Ensure `requireSessionUser(..., 'editor' | 'approver' | 'admin')` denies, and
  `requireMetricsGrant()`, `requireConfidentialMetricsGrant()`, and
  `requireCashierDisplayUser()` deny because the synthetic viewer has no grants
  and is not a cashier-display allowlisted email.
- Tests: `/api/session` envelope for accepted signed-agent request;
  viewer-route success when explicitly allowlisted; editor/admin denial;
  metrics and cashier-display denial.

### H4 — Route-author docs and focused safe-read examples

- Add Helios docs for route authors describing how to decide whether a GET route
  is safe to allowlist, including hazards: writes hidden behind GET, cache or
  external refreshes, expensive scans, streaming/SSE/downloads, PII-heavy pages,
  and required byte caps.
- Include example allowlist snippets for the intended first verification page
  (`/config/agent-waste` plus its necessary loader/API/session/static asset
  routes), but keep them inactive/example-only unless the NixOS child has
  provisioned the real production config.
- Tests/docs review: verify docs explicitly say page rules do not imply API
  rules and private signing keys never belong in Helios config.

## 7. Out of scope for this child

- NixOS secrets/config rollout, nginx header stripping, optional loopback vhost,
  vps2/vps3 parity, and rollback commands live in the `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`
  child epic.
- The agent-side `fetch`/`render` helper, Playwright no-cookie context,
  per-request signing, local evidence bundle, and Oracle attachment workflow live
  in the agent-helper owner child (likely `Nicponskis/github-worker`).
- Live rollout verification is a later cross-repo leaf after Helios and NixOS
  changes are deployed through sanctioned paths. Do not fake it from unit tests.
- DB-backed audit or nonce storage is not part of v1. If implementation finds a
  DB change is necessary, stop for Oracle DB review and explicit operator go.

## 8. Gates and safety

- Follow `automation/AGENTS.md` dev-loop gates. Expected local checks for this
  Helios server/shared change:
  - `cd helios && npm run typecheck`
  - `cd helios && npm run typecheck:client` when the shared session contract or
    client-visible envelope changes
  - Focused Vitest runs for touched auth/session/route tests, e.g.
    `cd helios && npm run test -- src/server/auth/authGate.test.ts` plus any new
    verifier/require-session tests.
- No serving service restarts. Deploy, if a later implementation leaf reaches
  deployment, only via `self-deploy-helios` after push and per canon.
- No production DB writes or migrations for v1.
- Rollback is a normal revert + redeploy, and the NixOS side can separately
  expire/remove allowlist rules and public keys. With config absent or invalid,
  signed-agent access must fail closed while normal OAuth sessions keep working.

## 9. Acceptance criteria

- Helios has Ed25519 signed-agent verification with canonical payload tests.
- Signed-agent requests are accepted only for GET/HEAD, no Cookie, no
  Authorization, fresh timestamp, non-replayed nonce, valid key/signature,
  active allowlist rule, exact allowed path/query, and route-specific safe-read
  entry.
- Accepted requests expose `authMode: 'agent_readonly'` and a synthetic viewer,
  not a cookie or DB user.
- Viewer-only allowed routes can be read; mutating routes, admin/config,
  editor/approver/admin gates, metrics grants, confidential metrics, and
  cashier-display gates deny.
- Response byte caps are enforced and audited.
- Structured audit logs include metadata and deny reasons, never secrets,
  signatures, credentials, or response bodies.
- Route-author docs explain safe-read allowlisting and the page/API/asset/session
  split.
slots.delegationNote: Implement the Helios-native signed readonly primitive from the resolved design: Ed25519 verifier, expiring narrow allowlist, explicit agent_readonly viewer principal/session envelope, GET/HEAD-only + no Cookie/Authorization, byte caps, metadata audit logs, route-author docs, and focused auth/session/metrics/admin/cashier denial tests. NixOS provisioning and agent helper are separate children.
slots.title: Helios signed readonly access for local agent verification

# Agent Canon — `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc` child epic

> Parent epic: [virusdave/top-level#10](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/10)
>
> The implementation commit on this repo's master MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10
> ```
>
> That trailer triggers the cross-repo completion flow back to the
> parent issue.

## What this epic does

Rewrites this repo's root `AGENTS.md` to consume **canonical agent
rules** from `virusdave/top-level` instead of duplicating them
locally. The canonical rules are short, imperative, and updated in one
place — so all our repos stay in sync without manual mirroring.

## Step 0 — fetch and read canon BEFORE doing anything

The canonical agent rules live in
`virusdave/top-level : docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md` on `master`. **Read
them first** (and use the same mechanism in your final AGENTS.md
header — see Step 2):

```sh
canon_ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
              /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$canon_ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … internalize the rules — they govern this rewrite …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$canon_ws"
```

Pay particular attention to: ephemeral checkouts for your own work,
the "Canon update interrupt" in §0, the operational-reality §5, and
the §6 contract for what peer `AGENTS.md` must contain.

## Step 1 — ephemeral checkout of THIS repo

```sh
ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
        /home/amp-local/src/nixos-sbc --label agent-canon)
cd "$ws"
```

Adjust the source path if `nixos-sbc` lives elsewhere on this host
(`/home/amp-local/src/nixos-sbc` is the standard).

## Step 2 — rewrite `AGENTS.md` to the pointer model

Open the existing root `AGENTS.md`, audit it for what to keep, then
replace its contents with this exact structure. Fill in the
repo-specific section from your audit.

```markdown
# Agent instructions for `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`

**MANDATORY FIRST READ — agent canon.** Before doing anything in this
repo, fetch and read the latest canonical agent rules:

```sh
ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
        /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … apply the rules …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$ws"
```

That file is authoritative across **all** our repos. Re-read on every
agent session — it changes. If anything in this file conflicts with
canon, **canon wins** — fix the stale prose here.

The rest of this file lists only **nixos-sbc-specific** instructions.

---

## Repo purpose

<one-paragraph summary: this repo holds the NixOS system closures
for our SBC fleet — vps-nixos-3 and any other managed hosts —
deployed via `self-deploy`.>

## Deploy

<the canonical deploy procedure: `self-deploy <host>` (or the
equivalent canonical wrapper). Per the operator's recurring
complaint, NEVER `nixos-rebuild switch` directly on a serving host,
NEVER restart user-facing services during the switch — the canonical
`self-deploy*` packages handle drain/mirror modes. Preserve any
nuance the old AGENTS.md had here.>

## Build / test

<repo-specific: `nix flake check`, `nix build .#<host>`, etc.>

## Host topology / paths

<exact paths agents need: which hosts this repo deploys, source
checkout location on each, where flake.nix and per-host configs
live, naming conventions for modules.>
```

## Step 3 — what to KEEP

From the existing AGENTS.md, **keep every operational fact** an agent
needs to work here: exact deploy commands, service names, log paths,
config locations, build/test invocations, architecture diagrams,
repo-specific cross-references, contact info.

## Step 4 — what to DELETE (canon covers it)

Delete and do NOT restate any of:

- "Never SSH to self" / "SSH port" rules
- "Use ephemeral checkout" / "do not edit shared `~/src`" rules
- "Default to `master`, no feature branches" rule
- Bash vs Python / shebang style / typed-code rules
- Performance budgets (UI ≤500ms, DB ≤125ms)
- "Use Oracle / painter / Bedrock LLMs" rules
- Group-writable file rule
- Generic task-dag CLI workflow (the
  `frontier → work → complete → push` loop)
- Generic cross-repo child-epic trailer flow

If you find any of those in the current `AGENTS.md`, **delete** the
prose and rely on canon. If a rule there contradicts canon, canon
wins — flag the conflict in your commit message.

## Step 5 — target size & sanity check

The rewritten file should be **≤ 120 lines**. If it's bigger, you're
probably restating canon — re-audit and trim. If it's much shorter
than the existing file but still has all operational facts, that's
the correct outcome.

Run a final read-through asking: "could a brand-new agent who has
just read canon do real work in this repo using only what's left
here?" If yes, done.

## Step 6 — commit, link, push

```sh
git add AGENTS.md
git commit -m "agents: adopt canon pointer model (Satisfies virusdave/top-level#10)

Replace duplicated cross-repo rules with a mandatory canon-fetch
header per docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md. Repo-specific content
(deploy, paths, services) preserved.

Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10"
git push origin HEAD:<this-repo-default-branch>
```

(Use this repo's default branch — usually `master` or `main`. Do not
open a PR; push directly per the canon working-workflow rule.)

The `Satisfies:` trailer fires the cross-repo completion flow back to
top-level#10.

## Acceptance

- Root `AGENTS.md` opens with the unignorable canon-fetch header.
- Zero duplication of canon content.
- All prior repo-specific operational facts preserved.
- File length ≤ 120 lines.
- Commit includes `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10`.
- Pushed to default branch.

## If you're blocked

- **App not installed / push refused**: stop. Report the exact error
  and your proposed diff to the parent issue
  ([virusdave/top-level#10](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/10)).
- **Repo doesn't have a root `AGENTS.md`**: create one using the same
  template. The acceptance criteria still apply.
- **Existing AGENTS.md has something you don't recognize**: assume
  it's an operator customization and preserve it. When in doubt, ask.
slots.delegationNote: Slice 2 of the agent-canon system. Receiving agent should fetch canon first, then rewrite root AGENTS.md to the inlined pointer-model template; preserve all repo-specific facts.

# agent-pain-points migration — github-worker child epic: dispatcher catalog/exporter retarget

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#40](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/40)
> — "Migrate the agent-waste canonical git storage to different repo".
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`virusdave/top-level` → `docs/epics/agent-pain-points-migration/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/agent-pain-points-migration/EPIC_PLAN.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit on
> [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#40`, and the **final** satisfying commit MUST
> also carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer.

## 1. Goal

Re-point the dispatcher's advisory-catalog resolution and pending-review backlog
export from `top-level` to `virusdave/agent-pain-points`, so agent-waste writes
stop bumping the `top-level` canon SHA — with a fail-safe fallback so advisory
injection never breaks during rollout.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Catalog resolution** | In [`worker-loop.sh`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/worker-loop.sh) (the `adv_catalog` block, currently resolving `manifest .canon.top_level_path/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`), resolve **first** from `manifest.repos["agent-pain-points"]/docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml`; fall back to the current top-level path if the new repo/catalog is absent (rollout + fail-safe). Because the exporter root is derived as `$(dirname adv_catalog)/../..`, this single change re-points **both** advisory selection and backlog export. |
| **Exporter default** | [`scripts/agent-waste-export`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/scripts/agent-waste-export): confirm the derived-root behavior writes to the `agent-pain-points` checkout; keep `AGENT_WASTE_BACKLOG_FILE` default relative path `docs/agent-runtime/agent-waste-backlog.ndjson`; ensure the push credential targets `agent-pain-points` (via the amp-local SSH alias from the nixos-sbc child). Branch stays `master`. |
| **Registry sync** | Add `agent-pain-points` to [`repos.conf`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/repos.conf) to keep it in sync with the canonical `top-level/scripts/ephemeral_checkout.d/repos.conf` (top-level leaf L2 lands the canonical copy first). |
| **CLI + docs** | Update the header/comments of [`bin/agent-waste`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/bin/agent-waste) (references to `virusdave/top-level : docs/agent-runtime/...`), the operator text in [`scripts/waste-page`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/scripts/waste-page) (tells the operator to commit to top-level + validate `advisories.yaml` — now `agent-pain-points`), and [`docs/AGENT_WASTE.md`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/docs/AGENT_WASTE.md). |
| **Tests** | Update `tests/agent-waste-export.sh`, `tests/agent-waste.sh`, `tests/prompt-capsule.sh`, `tests/waste-page.sh` to the new repo target; all against ephemeral temp repos, never prod. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants

- **Fail-safe fallback is mandatory** during rollout: if `agent-pain-points` is
  not yet in the manifest / not yet cloned, advisory injection and export must
  degrade gracefully (fall back to top-level, or skip), never crash a dispatch.
- The advisory allowlist safety invariant is unchanged: only reviewed catalog
  `text` is injected; `note` is never injected.
- The exporter stays idempotent (no-op when unchanged), pull-rebase-retry,
  best-effort + fail-safe (`|| true`).

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Depends on** the nixos-sbc child (dispatcher write deploy key for
  `agent-pain-points`) and on the repo being in the cohort (top-level leaf L2)
  so the manifest carries `.repos["agent-pain-points"]`.
- The fallback lets this land/deploy **before** the automation Helios cutover;
  final cutover is coordinated in parent epic §6 (avoid the split-brain window).

## 5. Acceptance

- On a prepared workspace with `agent-pain-points` cloned, `worker-loop.sh`
  selects the catalog from the `agent-pain-points` checkout and the exporter
  pushes the backlog to `agent-pain-points`, not `top-level`.
- With `agent-pain-points` absent, advisory injection/export still work (fallback
  path) — proven by a deterministic test.
- No `top-level` write on a normal worker completion once cut over.
- Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

Rollback = revert the resolution change (fallback returns behavior to
top-level). Best-effort export means a push failure never blocks dispatch. Tests
must target ephemeral temp repos only. No prod DB, no schema.
slots.title: agent-pain-points migration: dispatcher advisory-catalog + backlog-export retarget

# task-dag child epic — eliminate hand-built JSON (and YAML)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#44](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/44)
> — "Our critical tooling should NOT be constructing json by hand."
> **Parent epic plan:** [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md).
> **Governing rule:** canon `docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md` "Code
> standards" — *never hand-build / hand-parse / hand-validate JSON or YAML*.

## Scope

Replace every remaining hand-built JSON (and YAML) emitter/parser in the
task-dag runtime with proper serialization. The CLI already ships
jq-preferring primitives (`json_escape`, `json_str_or_null`,
`json_int_or_null`, `json_number_or_null`, `json_str_array`); the JSON fix
is to route the raw emitters through them (or through `jq -n --arg …`), not
to invent new machinery.

### Offenders (survey 2026-07-08; re-grep + expand before implementing)

1. **`scripts/task-dag` — raw-interpolation `echo "{…}"` emitters.**
   Many `--json` result lines interpolate shell variables straight into
   the JSON string, e.g.
   - `echo "{\"ok\":false,\"reason\":\"not-claimed\",\"sha\":\"$task_sha\"}"`
   - the `claim-root` / `release-root` result objects that interpolate
     `$claimer`, `$claimer_host`, `$existing_claimer`, `$existing_host`,
     `$existing_when` (untrusted strings from commit/ref metadata),
   - the `deps`/`allMet`/`blockedAncestor` object assembled with a series
     of `echo` lines,
   - the `validate` summary object,
   - the `breakdown` result object / per-task array entries,
   - the reap `printf '{…}'` object (`deadReason` can contain arbitrary
     text).
   Numeric fields (`issue`, `claimerPid`, `ttlHours`) must go through
   `json_int_or_null` / `json_number_or_null` (raw interpolation of a
   malformed `Issue: #41abc` is exactly the outage the helpers were added
   to prevent). String fields go through `json_escape` / `json_str_or_null`.

2. **The CI chain/repair module family** —
   `scripts/task-dag.d/ci-chains.sh` and `scripts/task-dag.d/ci-repair.sh`.
   `_cichain_jstr` is a private pure-bash escaper (no jq preference) and the
   CI-chain status/CAS-result objects plus `ci-repair.sh`'s classifier /
   tree-fix-outcome / verify report objects are assembled with
   `printf '{"…":"%s"}'`. Fold these onto the shared jq-preferring helpers
   (or `jq -n`); drop the duplicate escaper.

3. **JWT payloads** in `scripts/operator-blocked-dashboard-publish.sh`
   (and the mirrored `.github/scripts/materialise-child-epics.sh`) —
   `printf '{"iat":%d,"exp":%d,"iss":"%s"}' … "$APP_ID"`. Low risk
   (numeric/APP_ID) but still hand-built; emit with `jq -n` for
   consistency. The constant `{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT"}` header is a
   fixed literal and may stay.

4. **YAML: the `delegated_to` block** in
   `scripts/task-dag.d/cross-repo.sh` (`_xrepo_upsert_delegated_block` and
   its readers) is a bespoke, hand-rolled YAML parser/renderer. #44
   explicitly covers YAML, so convert this to `yq` (or a proper YAML
   library) for both emit and parse. Note the canon Bash-default / no-Python
   rule: prefer `yq`.

Re-grep before implementing — treat the list above as a starting point,
not an exhaustive census:

```sh
rg -n -e '\\"[a-zA-Z_]+\\":' -e "printf '\{" -e 'echo .*\{.*:.*\}' scripts/ .github/
```

## Constraints (critical infra)

- **Do not change the commit/ref format or the *shape* of any `--json`
  output** — only how the same bytes are produced. The dispatcher and
  golden fixtures depend on the exact keys/values. This is a correctness
  refactor, not a format change.
- **Oracle design + change review is mandatory** (canon
  `QUALITY_GATES.md` "Critical-infrastructure changes"): task-dag is the
  dispatch/claim core.
- Add/extend tests so a regression (an unescaped field) is caught: the
  existing `tests/task-dag/*-json.sh` harnesses should assert the output
  parses under `jq -e` for inputs containing quotes/backslashes/newlines.
- Keep `validate --strict` green; run the `tests/task-dag/run-all.sh`
  suite as the final gate.

## Acceptance

- No remaining hand-built JSON/YAML in `scripts/` or `.github/scripts/`
  (constant no-interpolation literals excepted).
- All existing tests plus new adversarial-value tests pass.
- The **final** commit on `virusdave/task-dag` `master` that demonstrates
  this child epic's acceptance criteria are met carries
  `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#44`. Intermediate commits MUST NOT carry
  that trailer unless the child epic is already fully satisfied. (task-dag's
  own `complete` adds the peer `Issue:`/`URL:` trailer for completion
  attribution.)
slots.delegationNote: Route --json emitters and the delegated_to YAML block through jq/yq or existing json_ helpers; do not change output shape.
slots.title: Eliminate hand-built JSON (and YAML) in the task-dag CLI and scripts

# Helios DB cost reduction — `automation` child epic > Owning child of > [virusdave/top-level#11](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/11). > The authoritative design is > [`docs/epics/helios-db-cost/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in > the top-level repo; this child epic's scope is **strictly the > `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (Helios + ingest monorepo) slice of > that design** (which is to say, all of it). > > Every implementation commit landing on `automation@master` that > satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer: > > ``` > Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#11 > ``` > > Phase-tagged commits MUST additionally carry a `Phase:

` > trailer (`A2`, `A3`, `A4`, `A5`, `B2`, `B4`, `C1`, `C2`, `C3`, > `D1`, `D2`, `E1`) so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can > post the per-phase progress comment on the parent issue. ## Scope owned by this repo Everything described in the parent EPIC_PLAN.md, broken out by phase below. Re-read the parent before starting — the section here is a thin index over the parent rather than a re-statement of the design. ## Hard constraint — live customer scans stay real-time This child epic inherits the hard constraint from the parent: the [`/visitors/scans`](https://helios.freshlybaked.us/visitors/scans) page and any other operator-facing "live during a shift" surface MUST keep their near-real-time freshness. If E1 would otherwise throttle one of those pages, the implementer's job is to **change the mechanism** (WebSocket / SSE push, `LISTEN/NOTIFY` fan-out, direct webhook → operator-UI event), not lower its refresh rate. Pages explicitly excluded from any throttle work in E1: - [`helios/src/client/routes/visitors/VisitorScansPage.tsx`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/client/routes/visitors/VisitorScansPage.tsx) — the live-scan operator surface. Existing `setInterval` cadence is 20 s; the E1 implementer MUST replace the polling loop with a push-driven mechanism rather than slow it down. Add any other "during-shift live feedback" page to this list as it's discovered, before throttling it. ## Already shipped (out of scope for this child epic) Commit [`abb0b6f`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/commit/abb0b6f) landed and is deployed on `vps-nixos-3`: - A1 — `sweed_package_snapshots` bulk upsert. - B1 — `loadAllConfigSchedules` in-process cache. - B3 — polynomial empty-poll backoff in the worker lease loop. The phases below are the remaining work. --- ### Phase A2 — `configWorkersStockRefreshJob` bulk upsert Files: `helios/src/worker/jobs/configWorkersStockRefreshJob.ts` (primary) plus any new query helper in `helios/src/server/db/queries/`. - Replace the per-row loop on `stock_variant_state` with a single `INSERT … SELECT FROM jsonb_to_recordset(...) … ON CONFLICT (...) DO UPDATE …` (one statement per dealer, chunked at `BULK_CHUNK_SIZE = 500` for safety — same shape as the A1 commit). - Replace the per-transitioning-variant guard SELECT against `pending_litalerts_refresh_queue` with a single `INSERT … FROM jsonb_to_recordset(...) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` that relies on the existing partial unique index. - Replace the per-brand upsert loop on `landingpage_brand_site_presence` with one bulk `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` per dealer. - All of the above inside the single existing per-dealer transaction. - Validation: - Before / after row count on `stock_snapshot_items`, `stock_variant_state`, `pending_litalerts_refresh_queue`, and `landingpage_brand_site_presence` for one full poll, posted in the commit body. - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` snippet for the new bulk statements. - Operator sign-off that the live VeriScan scans page still updates in real time post-deploy. Commits MUST carry `Phase: A2`. ### Phase A3 — `configWorkersSweedOrdersIngestJob` bulk upsert Files: `helios/src/worker/jobs/configWorkersSweedOrdersIngestJob.ts`. - Replace the per-invoice `SELECT EXISTS(...)` + `INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` loop with: - one bulk `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING … RETURNING` over the incoming batch via `jsonb_to_recordset`; - one set-based CTE that computes `first_time_for_customer` for the newly-inserted rows in a single pass against `sweed_orders` (uses the existing `sweed_orders_customer_pay_time_idx` partial index). - Highwater bump stays unchanged. - Validation: - Backfill-equivalence check: run the new path on a held-aside dealer for one full poll, diff resulting `sweed_orders` rows + `first_time_for_customer` column against the pre-deploy snapshot. - Operator sign-off as above. Commits MUST carry `Phase: A3`. ### Phase A4 — Litalerts batch + `enqueueMarketRefreshForProducts` bulk transactions Files: `helios/src/worker/runtime/configWorkersScheduler.ts` (scheduler batch path) and `helios/src/worker/litalerts/enqueueMarketRefresh.ts`. - Collapse `for (const row of pendingRows) { await withTransaction(...) }` into one transaction per batch: - one bulk insert into `job_queue` (the existing `enqueueJob` helper grows a `enqueueJobs` plural variant that takes an array and uses `INSERT … SELECT FROM jsonb_to_recordset`); - one bulk `appendAuditEvent` (likewise, a plural variant); - one `recordEnqueueAndPatchCache` call at the end of the batch. - Preserve the single-flight dedupe-key behaviour. - Validation: - Count of `job_queue` rows inserted per scheduler tick before / after. - Operator sign-off as above. Commits MUST carry `Phase: A4`. ### Phase A5 — `configWorkersLitalertsRefreshJob` round-trip compression Files: `helios/src/worker/jobs/configWorkersLitalertsRefreshJob.ts` plus index migration under `helios/src/server/db/migrations/`. - Combine the queue-row load, catalog-group containment search, brand-expiry lookup, and (when needed) prior-observation lookup into a **single CTE** that returns the assembled context in one round-trip. - Add a GIN index on `catalog_groups.live_state_json` (or a computed jsonb_path_ops index on `live_state_json -> 'products'`) so the existing `(... -> 'products') @> $1::jsonb` containment search stops doing a sequential scan. Verify via `EXPLAIN` before declaring done. - The observation insert + queue-row update + audit row stay in one transaction (already true) but use a single multi-statement pipeline rather than three sequential awaits where possible. - Validation: - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` showing the new containment index is used. - Throughput / round-trip count per job before / after. - Operator sign-off as above. Commits MUST carry `Phase: A5`. ### Phase B2 — Gate the expired-lease sweep Files: `helios/src/worker/runtime/leaseJobs.ts`. - Move the unconditional `UPDATE job_queue SET status='queued' … WHERE status='running' AND leased_until < now()` out of the per-poll path and behind a per-process timestamp guard (e.g. run at most once per minute per worker process). The guard MUST survive a process restart cleanly (i.e., default to "sweep on first tick post-startup" so we don't lose recovery semantics). - Validation: - Count of `job_queue` UPDATEs issued during a 5-minute idle window before / after. - Confirm by deliberately leaving a leased row past its deadline that the sweep still picks it up within one minute. Commits MUST carry `Phase: B2`. ### Phase B4 — `LISTEN/NOTIFY` wake-up + idle-cap raise Files: `helios/src/worker/runtime/workerLoop.ts`, `helios/src/server/jobs/enqueueJob.ts`, and any new `helios/src/server/db/notify.ts`. - `enqueueJob` (and the new `enqueueJobs` plural from A4) emits `NOTIFY helios_job_queue` after a successful commit. - The worker lease loop opens a dedicated `LISTEN` connection that races with the `delay(...)` in the idle-backoff path: whichever resolves first re-enters the lease loop. (Don't share the LISTEN connection with the lease-CTE client; a dedicated pool connection is cheap and avoids pg client-state weirdness.) - With LISTEN/NOTIFY in place, raise the empty-poll backoff cap from 15 s to 60 s. Live work paths now have sub-second wake-up latency, so the cap raise is free. - Validation: - End-to-end latency from `enqueueJob` returning to the worker actually leasing the row, before / after. Target: ≤ 200 ms in the post-B4 world. - Count of `leaseJobs` round-trips during a 5-minute idle window before / after. Commits MUST carry `Phase: B4`. ### Phase C1 — Hypertables + compression Files: new migrations under `helios/src/server/db/migrations/` (one per table), and probably a `helios/scripts/explain-coverage.ts` or equivalent EXPLAIN-diff helper to compare pre/post planner choices. Tables to convert (in order, smallest-first to validate the pattern): 1. `parsekit_reverse_shadow_events` — small, easy validator. 2. `sweed_auth_events`. 3. `audit_events`. 4. `litalerts_competitor_observations`. 5. `sweed_orders`. 6. `sweed_package_snapshots`. For each: - `create_hypertable(...)` with an appropriate `chunk_time_interval` (sized so each chunk is in the low-GB range under current write volume — start at 1 day for high-write tables, 7 days for diagnostics). - Re-create every existing index ON THE HYPERTABLE; verify via `EXPLAIN` that every production query path still uses the expected index post-conversion. - Add `add_compression_policy(..., interval ...)` with `compress_orderby` and `compress_segmentby` matching the table's access pattern (typically segment-by dealer_id and order-by the time column DESC). - Each migration MUST be reversible (drop the policy + decompress + drop the hypertable in a `down` migration) so we can back out cleanly if the planner regresses. Validation per table: post the size before/after compression, plus the EXPLAIN diff for the top 3 production queries hitting that table. Commits MUST carry `Phase: C1`. ### Phase C2 — Retention policies Files: migrations under `helios/src/server/db/migrations/`, plus a small `/config/workers` UI surface for the operator-tunable knobs. - Operator-tunable retention windows (in days, persisted in a new `db_retention_policies` table) for: - `parsekit_reverse_shadow_events` (default 30 d), - `sweed_auth_events` (default 90 d), - `audit_events` (default 365 d). - Each tunable read/write through a new `/api/config/db-retention` route + UI panel under `/config/workers` (operator can raise / lower the window per table). - The actual purge is `add_retention_policy` on the hypertable; changing the window via the UI invokes `alter_job(...) SET schedule_interval / config` on the existing retention job. - Validation: alter one window down to 1 day in staging-equivalent data and verify the next policy run removes the expected rows; raise back to default. Commits MUST carry `Phase: C2`. ### Phase C3 — Stop storing `raw_json` where it's redundant Files: schemas + ingest jobs across `helios/src/worker/jobs/` and `helios/src/server/db/schema/`. Per-table decision tree: - `sweed_package_snapshots`: every consumer reads typed columns; drop `raw_json` from the steady-state table and store it in a new `sweed_package_snapshots_raw` table with 30 d retention (so we still have a one-month rollback window for "re-derive a field we forgot"). - `sweed_orders`: catalog-analytics still unrolls `raw_json->'items'`; D1 removes that dependency. Once D1 lands, apply the same split here. - `litalerts_competitor_observations.evidence_json`: every read parses the same handful of fields. Project them into typed columns; move `evidence_json` to `_raw` with 30 d retention. - `parsekit_reverse_shadow_events`: 3 JSONB columns, all read on the diagnostics page. Project the per-page-needed fields, keep the rest in `_raw` with the C2 retention window. Validation: for each touched table, demonstrate (via the existing test suite + a one-shot sample query against staging-equivalent data) that no consumer path regresses. Commits MUST carry `Phase: C3`. ### Phase D1 — `sweed_order_line_items` Files: new migration, new query helper, modified ingest job. - New table: `sweed_order_line_items (dealer_id, invoice_id, line_seq, inventory_item_id, product_id, current_qty, subtotal_amount, wholesale_cost_dollars_as_of, …)` keyed by `(dealer_id, invoice_id, line_seq)` and indexed for the existing catalog-analytics joins. - `configWorkersSweedOrdersIngestJob` populates it incrementally alongside the `sweed_orders` insert (same transaction, same batch — bulk insert via `jsonb_to_recordset`). - One-time backfill script under `helios/scripts/backfill-sweed-order-line-items.ts` that walks `sweed_orders.raw_json -> 'items'` historically and populates the new table; idempotent via the PK so reruns are cheap. - Rewrite `helios/src/server/catalogAnalytics/catalogAnalyticsQueries.ts` to read from `sweed_order_line_items` instead of unrolling jsonb at request time. Validation: - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` before / after on the `/api/catalog-analytics` query at the default 90-day window; must hit the ≤ 500 ms p95 target. - Diff of the API response between the old and new query path on one site, demonstrating identical numbers. Commits MUST carry `Phase: D1`. ### Phase D2 — Continuous aggregates for `/metrics` Files: new migrations, route handlers under `helios/src/server/budtenderAnalytics/`, `helios/src/server/customerValueAnalytics/`, `helios/src/server/catalogAnalytics/`. - One Timescale continuous-aggregate per `(dealer_id, day, granularity)` rollup the metric pages currently compute at request time. - Route handlers read from the CAGG; "real-time" tail (the last few hours) is computed on-the-fly via the existing CTE and unioned in (Timescale's `materialized only` / real-time aggregation pattern). - Refresh policy: every 15 min during business hours, hourly overnight. Validation: - p95 server-side query time on every `/metrics` route after D2; ≤ 200 ms target. - Numeric equivalence sample on one site for the prior 7 days. Commits MUST carry `Phase: D2`. ### Phase E1 — Client auto-refresh audit + selective mechanism swap Files: `helios/src/client/routes/**/*.tsx`, plus the new push-mechanism plumbing (likely `helios/src/client/lib/realtime/visitorScans.ts` and a server-side SSE / WebSocket route). **Throttle bucket** (cadence raise, no mechanism change): - `TasksPage` (10 s → 60 s) - `TaskFrontierPage` (10 s → 60 s) - `EpicDagPage` (30 s → 300 s) - `JobsPage`, `JobDetailPage` (only between an operator-initiated state change; default cadence raise to 60 s; preserve the existing "tighter cadence while a run is pending" branch) - `SweedAuthLogPage` (raise to 60 s) - `PricingRunsPage` (raise to 60 s) - `SchedulingRunDetailPage` (raise to 30 s between runs; preserve the "tight cadence during a run" branch) - `AdsIngestPage` (raise to 60 s) - `PendingMigrationsBanner` (raise to 5 min) - `ConfigParsingPendingPurchasesPage` (raise to 60 s) - `CustomerReviewsDrawingPage` (the 5 s `setNowMs` is a display-clock tick, not a fetch — verify with grep before touching). **Mechanism-swap bucket** (must remain live, throttle forbidden): - `VisitorScansPage` — swap the 20 s `setInterval` for a server-pushed event stream: - server: `GET /api/visitors/scans/stream` SSE endpoint that emits a new event whenever the VeriScan webhook handler persists a row. Implementation: webhook handler calls `pgNotify('visitor_scans_new', JSON.stringify({ id, siteSlug, capturedAt }))` post-commit; the SSE route holds a long-lived LISTEN connection and pipes notifications back out. - client: open the SSE on mount; on each event, refetch only the head of the list (`/api/visitors/scans?since=`) and prepend the new rows. Reconnect with jittered exponential backoff on disconnect. - operator-visible behaviour: a scan at the door appears in the open browser tab in ≤ 2 s, indistinguishably from the current 20-s-poll worst case but at a fraction of the DB cost. - Add any other "during-shift live feedback" page surfaced during the audit to this bucket BEFORE applying any throttle. Validation: - For each touched page, post the before / after cadence + bucket classification in the commit body (parent epic's E1 description requires this). - Operator-visible smoke test of the live-scan SSE on `vps-nixos-3` after deploy. Commits MUST carry `Phase: E1`. --- ## Conventions - Every commit MUST carry both `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#11` and the appropriate `Phase:

` trailer. - Every commit MUST be deployable in isolation (the worker / server must boot and pass `self-deploy-helios` health checks after the commit alone). - Validation evidence (row counts, EXPLAIN diffs, operator sign-offs) goes in the commit body, not in a separate STATUS file — STATUS files in this epic's directory are reserved for "operator changed direction" events.
slots.delegationNote: Bulk-upsert the remaining per-row-txn ingest paths (A2-A5), gate the worker expired-lease sweep + add LISTEN/NOTIFY wake-up (B2/B4), convert append-only tables to Timescale hypertables with compression + retention (C1/C2) and stop storing redundant raw_json (C3), materialise sweed_order_line_items + continuous-aggregate the /metrics rollups (D1/D2), and audit/replace client-side auto-refresh cadences (E1) WITHOUT throttling the live VeriScan scans page (mechanism swap, not cadence drop).

# Trusted read-only Helios agent access — `nixos-sbc` child epic

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#62](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/62)
> — "Need a means for local agents to access helios in trusted fashion".
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`virusdave/top-level` → `docs/epics/helios-agent-readonly-access/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/helios-agent-readonly-access/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit on
> [`Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/nixos-sbc) `master`
> that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```text
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#62
> ```
>
> The final satisfying commit should also carry this child epic's own
> `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level
> completion aggregator can attribute the peer-repo completion to the delegated
> child issue.

## 1. Goal

Provision the production host wiring that lets local `amp-local` agents make
temporary, signed, read-only Helios verification requests after sanctioned
Helios deploys. This child owns only the NixOS / nginx / secret provisioning
slice of the resolved design; the Helios verifier and the agent-side helper
land in peer repos.

The result should make the Helios application receive enough configuration to
verify Ed25519-signed agent requests on both Helios-serving hosts, while keeping
private signing material restricted to the local agent user and making every
allowlist extension reviewable through `nixos-sbc` git history.

## 2. Why this is operator-gated

This work introduces a production signing key that can unlock OAuth-gated
read-only Helios pages when combined with a live allowlist rule. Workers may
prepare the Nix code, config shape, and verification commands, but generating,
installing, or rotating the private key material is security-sensitive and must
use the fleet secrets process with operator approval.

Do **not** commit private keys, plaintext secrets, or sample secrets. If secret
material is not already supplied through agenix or a host-local root action,
block the task and page the operator with the exact key names, intended owners,
and target hosts.

## 3. Scope owned by `nixos-sbc`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **`amp-local` signing private key** | Provision an Ed25519 private key only where local agents run today: vps-nixos-3. Materialise it as a real file owned by `amp-local`, group `agents` only if needed for operator inspection, mode `0400` or stricter. Prefer a stable path such as `/home/amp-local/.secret/helios-agent-readonly/signing-key` or another path exposed to the agent-helper child. It must not be readable by `helios`, must not appear in the Nix store, and must not be passed through systemd environment variables. Private signing keys do **not** need to exist on vps-nixos-2 unless agents are intentionally run there later. |
| **Public verifier key(s)** | Provision matching public verifier key metadata for the Helios server on **both** vps-nixos-3 (primary) and vps-nixos-2 (backend-only mirror). Public keys may live in Nix config or a non-secret environment/config file, but keep key IDs explicit, stable, and documented (for example `amp-local-vps3-2026q3`). |
| **Expiring allowlist** | Provision the active agent-readonly allowlist into the Helios server config on both vps-nixos-3 and vps-nixos-2. Every rule must include `id`, `owner`, `reason`, `not_before`, `not_after`, `max_response_bytes`, and route-specific safe-read notes. Prefer exact path entries; use prefix rules only for narrow static-asset paths with segment-boundary checks handled by Helios. No broad `/api/*`, admin, metric-grant, cashier-display, or indefinite rules. |
| **Helios env/config plumbing** | Add `services.helios` options or `extraEnvironment` entries (whichever best matches the Helios child implementation) for the public verifier-key config and allowlist config. Keep primary and backend-only mirror config in parity, because public traffic may be served by either backend during `self-deploy-helios` windows. |
| **Public nginx header stripping** | Ensure the public `helios.freshlybaked.us` nginx vhost strips inbound `X-Helios-Agent-*` headers before proxying to Helios unless the Helios implementation intentionally verifies raw client headers itself. The goal is that internet clients cannot smuggle trusted agent headers through nginx. Use explicit `proxy_set_header X-Helios-Agent-… "";` lines for the final header names from the Helios child. |
| **Optional loopback-only vhost** | If the implementation chooses a loopback-only agent vhost/port as defense-in-depth, expose it only on loopback, never publicly. Only that vhost may forward the `X-Helios-Agent-*` headers to Helios. Public nginx must still strip them. The loopback vhost is not the auth model; Helios signature, freshness, no-cookie/no-authorization, and allowlist checks remain mandatory. |
| **Backend bind/firewall verification** | Verify how `helios-server` binds on vps-nixos-3 and vps-nixos-2 and whether direct backend access is reachable outside loopback. Tighten bind/firewall behavior if the existing module permits unintended direct public/LAN access, but do not rely on bind tightening as the only protection. |
| **Permissions and comments** | Keep comments near every key/allowlist entry explaining parent `virusdave/top-level#62`, expiry, owner, and how to extend or remove access. Future extension must require a normal git review and deploy. |

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- Depends on the `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` child defining the exact Helios
  config contract: public-key env/config format, allowlist env/config format,
  and final `X-Helios-Agent-*` header names.
- Blocks live verification until the agent-helper child can sign requests using
  the provisioned private key path.
- The vps-nixos-2 mirror config must land before declaring rollout complete;
  vps3-only success is incomplete because self-deploy mirror windows can serve
  requests from vps2.

## 5. Suggested implementation shape

1. Add `services.helios.agentReadonly` options in `modules/helios.nix` if the
   Helios child expects structured config, or wire the agreed env vars through
   `services.helios.extraEnvironment` in `hosts/per-host/vps-nixos-{2,3}.nix` if
   that is smaller and clearer.
2. Register any required agenix secrets in `secrets.nix`:
   - private signing key secret for vps-nixos-3 only, owned by `amp-local`,
     mode `0400`;
   - only if the Helios implementation wants verifier/allowlist as secret-ish
     files, corresponding host-specific `.age` entries for both vps-nixos-3 and
     vps-nixos-2. Prefer non-secret Nix config for public verifier keys and
     allowlist metadata unless there is a concrete reason to hide them.
3. Materialise the vps3 private key through the existing per-host secret helper
   pattern in `hosts/per-host/vps-nixos-3.nix`, not through a systemd
   environment variable.
4. Add public-nginx header stripping in the Helios nginx vhost generated by
   `modules/helios.nix`. If adding an optional loopback-only vhost, keep its
   config adjacent and document that it is defense-in-depth only.
5. Add parity comments/checks so vps-nixos-2 receives the same public verifier
   keys and active allowlist rules as vps-nixos-3.

## 6. Acceptance

- `nix flake check` or the repo's equivalent targeted Nix eval/build gate is
  green for the touched hosts/modules, or any skipped heavy gate is justified in
  the Agent Gate Record.
- The `amp-local` private signing key exists on vps-nixos-3 at the documented
  path, is owned by `amp-local`, is mode `0400` or stricter, and is not readable
  by the `helios` service user.
- Helios on both vps-nixos-3 and vps-nixos-2 receives the same public verifier
  key ID(s) and the same active expiring allowlist rules.
- Public nginx strips the final `X-Helios-Agent-*` header set before proxying
  internet-originated traffic to Helios.
- If a loopback-only vhost is added, it binds only to loopback and is the only
  nginx path that forwards agent headers.
- Backend bind/firewall behavior is explicitly verified and recorded.
- After the Helios verifier and agent helper are deployed, live verification
  from `amp-local` proves:
  - a whitelisted page route renders;
  - a whitelisted loader/API route returns;
  - a non-whitelisted route denies;
  - `POST`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` deny even with a valid signature;
  - signed requests containing `Cookie` or `Authorization` deny;
  - vps-nixos-2 has the same public key/allowlist behavior during a mirror
    window or an equivalent controlled mirror-host probe;
  - logs contain metadata only, not signatures, cookies, private keys, or
    response bodies.

## 7. Safety / rollback

Apply production changes only through the sanctioned `nixos-sbc` deploy path
(`self-deploy` / `self-deploy-helios` as appropriate for the final change). Do
not manually restart `nginx`, `helios-server`, or `helios-worker`.

Rollback is deliberately simple and does not require DB cleanup:

1. expire or remove the allowlist rule(s);
2. remove the public verifier key config from both Helios hosts;
3. remove the vps3 `amp-local` private-key secret/materialisation if access is
   being fully retired;
4. redeploy via the sanctioned wrapper;
5. verify signed requests now fail closed while normal OAuth login and Helios
   health checks still pass.

The Nix change is additive until the allowlist becomes active. Reverting the
implementation commit and redeploying removes the access path; the Helios child
must still enforce its own fail-closed behavior when config is absent.

## 8. Out of scope

- Implementing the Helios Ed25519 verifier, request principal, allowlist parser,
  response byte caps, or audit logging — owned by `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`.
- Implementing the agent fetch/render helper — likely owned by
  `Nicponskis/github-worker` unless that child chooses a different existing home.
- Granting write access, creating real Helios users/cookies, broad API access,
  metric grants, cashier-display access, or operator impersonation.
- Publishing captured HTML/CSS/screenshots to public hosts.
- Any production DB write, schema migration, or Helios data backfill.
slots.delegationNote: Provision amp-local Ed25519 signing key, Helios public verifier keys and expiring allowlist on vps-nixos-3/vps-nixos-2, nginx agent-header handling, mirror parity, deployment verification, and rollback for trusted read-only Helios agent access.

# github-worker child epic: repair reconciler and watchdog

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Provide typed, bounded host orchestration for task-dag's canonical
`repair-reconcile` command and independently detect stale or failed convergence.
github-worker must not duplicate repair classification, desired state, or
ticket semantics.

## Required implementation

1. **Typed reconciler command**
   - Read top-level's current `master` and `repos.conf` through GitHub, accept
     only equal/descendant registry generations, and enumerate only explicitly
     enrolled repositories.
   - Run five-minute jittered sweeps with a bounded pool of four. Invoke one
     coherent canonical task-dag revision and its `repair-reconcile`; never
     reproduce classifier or projection logic in github-worker.
   - Mint short-lived single-repository GitHub App installation tokens with
     only the binding design's permissions, refresh at 80 percent of lifetime,
     and keep credentials out of config, disk, logs, and command lines.
   - Fail closed with named preflight errors for installation, label,
     permission, clone, policy, or token failures.

2. **Durable status and independent watchdog**
   - Atomically replace `status.json` after each repository with registry
     commit/blob, sweep state, per-repository success/error, active-red identity,
     projection age, counters, gauges, and bounded incident keys.
   - Add a separately supervised watchdog as the sole writer of
     `watchdog.json`. It reads status every five minutes, invokes the packaged
     `page-dave`, persists attempts/results/recoveries, and implements the
     exact stale observation, pending projection, lease, duplicate, and invalid
     policy thresholds from the design.
   - Prefer at-least-once incident notification across a crash; notification
     deduplication is never repair desired-state authority.
   - Emit structured journald events without credentials, check output, issue
     bodies, or one-off contents.

3. **Configuration and lifecycle**
   - Ship orchestration, projection, and paging controls disabled. Document
     cadence, concurrency, state files, preflight, metrics, alerts, dry-run,
     enablement, restart behavior, and rollback.
   - Keep all git and API operations bounded and cancellation-safe. A stopped
     process leaves only durable task-dag state for the next pass to resume.

## Deterministic tests

Use fake registry/GitHub/task-dag boundaries and temporary state directories.
Cover registry generation rollback, malformed enrollment, bounded concurrency,
token mint/refresh/failure and redaction, partial sweeps, restart at every
handoff, atomic status replacement, stale status, every incident threshold,
page attempt crash windows, recovery, task-dag nonzero/timeout, and disabled/
dry-run/enabled controls. No test may contact production.

## Rollout and rollback

The task-dag child must land first. Deploy this code disabled through
github-worker's canonical deployment path. Run credential preflight and the
24-hour dry-run, then support observe-only and the two-repository projection
canary. The nixos-sbc child owns production unit/credential provisioning; the
top-level child owns fleet enrollment and final stability evidence.

Rollback disables the sweep/watchdog controls while preserving status evidence
and task-dag chain history. Package/version selection belongs to nixos-sbc and
must retain a new-format-compatible task-dag until the chain compatibility gate
is satisfied. Do not manually restart or stop a serving service; use only
canonical rollout paths.

This is critical fleet infrastructure. The binding architecture already has
Oracle approval, but the implementation worker must get Oracle architecture
rereview for any design change and Oracle review of the actual final diff
before commit. Iterate to APPROVE.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```
slots.delegationNote: Orchestrate canonical task-dag reconciliation with least-privilege tokens, durable status, independent stale/failure paging, deterministic tests, and disabled-by-default controls.
slots.title: Add the bounded repair reconciler and independent watchdog

# Helios: cluster pending agent-waste reports with an advanced Bedrock LLM

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#51](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/51)
> — "Waste review page…".
> **Delegated because:** the agent-waste review page, its API routes, the
> backlog reader, the shared contracts, and the bedrock-mantle LLM client
> all live in `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` under `helios/`. `top-level` has
> no code to change.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` for this epic MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#51`, plus
> this child epic's own `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer
> so the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this* delegated
> child.

## 1. Goal

Add a **"Cluster similar reports"** action to the admin agent-waste review
page (`/config/agent-waste`). Pressing it sends the current pending backlog
to an **advanced** Bedrock model (via the existing bedrock-mantle
OpenAI-compatible gateway) which groups near-duplicate / highly-similar
observations. The page then renders the result as ranked **clusters**:

- a **primary** (representative) observation per cluster,
- a **total count** of members in that cluster,
- a **collapsed but expandable** list of the remaining members, and
- clusters **sorted by "likely aggregate agent waste"** so the operator can
  address the most common / most expensive problems first.

This lets the operator triage a noisy backlog by theme instead of scrolling
a flat, newest-first list.

## 2. Current state (all paths under `helios/`)

Read these first; the feature slots into the existing shapes.

| Concern | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Review page UI | `src/client/routes/config/AgentWasteReviewPage.tsx` | Admin-guarded page; fetches backlog, renders `ObservationCard`s, has Refresh + per-row Promote. Add the cluster button + clustered view here. |
| Client pure helpers | `src/client/routes/config/agentWasteReviewShared.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) | Fetch/parse/sort helpers are pure + unit-tested (no DOM harness). Put cluster fetch/parse/sort logic here. |
| Server routes | `src/server/routes/agentWaste.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) | `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` and `POST /api/agent-waste/promote`, both `requireSessionUser(request, reply, 'admin')`, structured 503-degrade via `handleAgentWasteError`. Add the cluster route here. |
| Backlog data layer | `src/server/agentWasteRepo.ts`, `src/server/agentWasteBacklogReader.ts` | `getBacklog()` / `getBacklogSourceStatus()`; `BacklogReader` reads the read-only agent-pain-points mirror. Reuse `getBacklog()` verbatim. |
| Shared contracts | `src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts` | `AgentWasteObservationSchema` (+ the display-only `note` rule) and the backlog/promote schemas. Add cluster request/response schemas here. |
| Bedrock env | `src/server/config/env.ts` | `bedrockMantleBaseUrl`, `bedrockMantleBearerToken`, `llmRequestTimeoutMs`. |
| Server LLM call pattern | `src/server/llm/reviewSentimentGate.ts`, `src/server/routes/configLitalertsParsing.ts` | Canonical shape: `fetch(`${baseUrl}/chat/completions`, { headers: Bearer, body: { model, messages, response_format: json_object, temperature }, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(llmRequestTimeoutMs) })`; errors returned structured, never thrown across the request boundary. |
| Model context registry | `src/shared/domain/bedrockModels.ts`, `src/server/llm/bedrockModelConfig.ts` | `BEDROCK_MODEL_CONTEXT_KEYS`, `resolveBedrockModel(db, key)`, operator overrides in `app_settings.bedrock_model_overrides`. Add an `agent_waste_clusterer` context key. |

**Backlog item identity gap (important).** `AgentWasteObservation.id` is a
*stable trigger id* (e.g. `rg-short-r-rejected`), **not** unique per event.
The client already synthesises a composite `observationKey(obs)` for local
dismiss. Clustering needs to map LLM output back to specific observations,
so **assign each observation a stable index/key server-side before sending
to the LLM** and have the model return those keys (see §4).

## 3. Design decisions (implement exactly)

1. **The server does the LLM call.** The Amp Oracle is agent-only; the live
   Helios server calls Bedrock directly through bedrock-mantle, exactly like
   `reviewSentimentGate.ts` / `configLitalertsParsing.ts`. New route:
   `POST /api/agent-waste/clusters`, `admin`-gated, reading `getBacklog()`.

2. **The LLM groups; the server ranks.** The model returns only the
   *grouping* (which observation keys belong together + a short human label /
   representative). "Likely aggregate agent waste" is computed
   **deterministically in Helios** from the members' real
   `estimated_wasted_tokens` / `estimated_wasted_seconds` — never taken from
   the model. Rationale: the ranking must be trustworthy and reproducible,
   and the numbers already exist on each observation. Define the aggregate
   explicitly (e.g. `sum(estimated_wasted_tokens over members)`, with
   `estimated_wasted_seconds` as a documented tiebreak/secondary); pick one
   and encode it in a pure, unit-tested helper. Sort clusters descending by
   that aggregate.

3. **Cluster output is display-only.** It is NOT injected into agents and
   does NOT auto-promote. Sending observation text (including `note`) to the
   *private* clustering model is read/analysis, not allowlist injection; the
   result only renders in the operator UI. The promote path and its
   `.strict()` "`note` can never be advisory text" contract are untouched.

4. **No persistence for v1.** Clusters are computed on demand when the
   operator presses the button and shown in the page; nothing is written to
   the DB or to git. (If the operator later wants shareable/persisted
   clusters, that is a follow-up; do NOT pull in the promote/applyConfig
   write-clone machinery for v1.)

5. **Advanced, operator-overridable model.** Add an `agent_waste_clusterer`
   context key so the model is configurable via the existing Bedrock
   model-override UI, and resolve it with `resolveBedrockModel(db,
   'agent_waste_clusterer')`. **Open question (§6):** the codebase has no
   confirmed-working *advanced* model id on the gateway — `google.gemma-3-27b-it`
   is the only proven model, and `anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-…` was rejected
   with "model not found". The whole point of #51 is a *more advanced* model,
   so the implementer must confirm a working advanced model id on
   bedrock-mantle (or have the operator set one via the override UI) rather
   than silently defaulting to the small model.

## 4. Contract sketch (`src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts`)

Add (names illustrative; keep zod + `.strict()` discipline):

```ts
// Request: no body needed beyond the action; server reads the live backlog.
// (An empty POST is fine, or accept an optional { } for forward-compat.)

// One clustered group, ready to render + already ranked server-side.
export const AgentWasteClusterSchema = z.object({
  label: z.string(),                       // short human theme from the model
  primary: AgentWasteObservationSchema,    // representative member
  members: z.array(AgentWasteObservationSchema), // includes primary; length = count
  count: z.number().int().nonnegative(),   // members.length
  aggregateWastedTokens: z.number().nonnegative(),
  aggregateWastedSeconds: z.number().nonnegative().optional(),
})

export const AgentWasteClustersResponseSchema = z.object({
  source: AgentWasteSourceStatusSchema,    // reuse backlog source status
  model: z.string(),                       // which model actually ran
  clusters: z.array(AgentWasteClusterSchema), // sorted desc by aggregate waste
  unclustered: z.array(AgentWasteObservationSchema).optional(), // items the model left ungrouped
})
```

- The server assigns each observation a stable key (reuse the same field set
  as the client's `observationKey`, or a simple 0-based index for the
  request round-trip) and instructs the model to return groups **by those
  keys**; the server then rehydrates full observations, drops/one-members any
  key the model hallucinated, and computes the aggregates.

## 5. Suggested leaf breakdown

Author these as the child epic's own frontier leaves (the automation
epic-root worker `task-dag breakdown`s this issue):

- **L1 — Server clustering endpoint + contract.**
  - Add cluster schemas to `contracts/api/agentWaste.ts`.
  - Add `agent_waste_clusterer` to `BEDROCK_MODEL_CONTEXT_KEYS` /
    `BEDROCK_MODEL_CONTEXTS`.
  - Add `POST /api/agent-waste/clusters` in `routes/agentWaste.ts`:
    `admin`-gated; `getBacklog()` (503-degrade via `handleAgentWasteError`);
    factor the Bedrock call into a **testable helper** (e.g.
    `src/server/agentWaste/clusterBacklog.ts`) that takes the observations +
    a model id and returns groups; compute aggregates + sort in a pure
    helper; map missing token to `503 bedrock_unconfigured` and gateway/parse
    errors to `502`, matching `configLitalertsParsing.ts`.
  - Tests: route tests via `server.inject` with mocked auth + injected
    backlog reader + stubbed `fetch` (see `agentWaste.test.ts` patterns);
    pure tests for aggregate-scoring + sort + LLM-output parsing/rehydration
    (incl. hallucinated/duplicate keys).

- **L2 — Client cluster button + clustered view.** (depends on L1)
  - Add a **"Cluster similar reports"** button near Refresh on
    `AgentWasteReviewPage.tsx`, with loading / error / unavailable states.
  - Put the fetch + response-parse + (defensive re-)sort logic in
    `agentWasteReviewShared.ts` as pure, unit-tested helpers.
  - Render clusters: a primary `ObservationCard` with a **count** pill and a
    collapsed `<details>`/`<summary>` (per `helios/AGENTS.md`) that expands to
    the member list; keep the existing flat list available (e.g. toggle
    between "flat" and "clustered" views, or show clusters above the list).
  - Pure client helper tests in `agentWasteReviewShared.test.ts`.

## 6. Open questions (resolve during implementation; not operator-blocking)

- **Which advanced model?** Confirm a working advanced model id on
  bedrock-mantle (§3.5). If none is confirmable, ship the endpoint +
  override plumbing and let the operator set the model via the existing
  Bedrock override UI, but surface (don't hide) that the default is not the
  "advanced" model the issue asked for.
- **Aggregate-waste formula.** Tokens-only vs tokens+seconds weighting, and
  how to rank clusters whose members lack `estimated_wasted_*` (treat
  missing as 0, but keep count as a secondary sort so a large all-unrated
  cluster still surfaces). Pick and document one.
- **Backlog size vs prompt budget.** The pending backlog is "tiny and rare"
  by design, so a single-shot cluster call should fit; still cap the number
  of observations / total prompt size sent and degrade clearly if exceeded.

## 7. Gates (canon `QUALITY_GATES.md`)

- `cd helios && npm run typecheck` (server) and `npm run typecheck:client`.
- Focused tests: `npm run test -- <file-or-pattern>` for the new server +
  client helper/route tests. Full `npm run check` is CI-owned.
- Client bundle build (if touched) with an enlarged heap:
  `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 npm run build:client`.
- **This adds a new LLM call on the live server request path** consuming
  agent-adjacent text (backlog notes). Even though the output is
  display-only, it is a new private-LLM surface: get an **Oracle design
  review** of the endpoint + prompt before implementing and a change review
  of the diff, and make the prompt strictly instruct the model to *only*
  cluster + return the fixed JSON shape (defend against injected instructions
  in `note`/observation text). No prompt-injection reachback exists because
  results never feed agents, but the review keeps that boundary explicit.

## 8. Out of scope for v1

- Persisting clusters (DB or git), sharing/linking to a cluster.
- Auto-promoting a cluster to an advisory (still the separate, per-row
  operator-approved promote path).
- Any change to the promote / draft-assist (L1–L3) flow or its `note`
  contract.
- Any `top-level` change beyond this delegation.
slots.delegationNote: Add an admin-gated POST /api/agent-waste/clusters that reads getBacklog() and calls an advanced bedrock-mantle model (LLM groups only; server computes+sorts aggregate waste), plus the client cluster button + collapsed/expandable clustered view. Display-only output; no persistence; no promote/advisory changes. New LLM-on-request-path surface: Oracle design+change review applies.
slots.title: Cluster pending agent-waste reports with an advanced Bedrock LLM
