# top-level child epic: enroll and verify durable repair convergence

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Own the authoritative fleet enrollment, per-repository policy rollout, staged
production enablement, stability evidence, and final closure decision after the
task-dag, github-worker, nixos-sbc, and mostly-static-sites implementations are
reviewed and available.

## Required implementation

1. Extend `scripts/ephemeral_checkout.d/repos.conf` to accept exactly two or
   four fields and document `<mode> <branch>` without breaking existing
   two-field consumers. Two fields mean `off`; reject three/trailing fields.
2. Add strict version-1 `.github/ci-repair-policy.json` files to each enrolled
   repository in its owning repo. Bind every required check to its exact name,
   GitHub App identity, accepted terminal conclusions, and explicit grace.
   Missing, empty, malformed, unsupported, or identity-mismatched policy is
   never green.
3. Update final-gate callers to invoke the canonical `repair-reconcile` only as
   a low-latency hint without weakening, replacing, or making correctness
   depend on the final gate. Coordinate peer-owned policy/caller edits through
   their own repository task trails and `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65`.
4. Keep all rows `off` until the three repair-infrastructure child epics have
   Oracle-approved diffs, landed code, disabled deployment, and successful
   credential preflight. Then execute the binding design's dry-run, observe,
   projection-canary, crash-drill, peer-by-peer, and fleetwide sequence.
5. Record durable evidence for aggregate parity, missed-run recovery, restart
   at every interruption boundary, exactly-one issue/task convergence under
   duplicate creators, authoritative-green closure, stale/failure telemetry,
   watchdog paging/recovery, cost bounds, and rollback readback.

## Required gates

- Every nontrivial critical-infrastructure diff gets Oracle architecture review
  before implementation and Oracle review of the actual diff before commit.
- Changes to canon or any `AGENTS.md` follow the canonical update protocol.
- Tests use fake APIs and temporary git origins; drills use isolated test
  evidence and never point tests at production resources.
- Deploy only through canonical paths. Never manually restart, stop, or kill a
  serving service. No database work is in scope.

## Rollout and rollback

Run credential preflight, then 24 hours of dry-run parity. Enroll task-dag and
top-level in observe mode, enable chain writes without projection, then enable
projection and inject missed-run/post-create-crash drills. Require 48 stable
hours before adding one peer at a time and enabling the fleet sweep. Keep
missing/invalid-policy paging disabled until that stability evidence is
complete; enabling it is the final rollout stage.

Rollback disables the host sweep and peer hints first. It then changes registry
modes to `off` through fenced cleanup and verifies projection readback.
Preserve all chain refs and issue/task audit history. If old task-dag code
cannot read an active new substate, use only the reviewed compare-and-set legacy
migration from the binding design; never delete refs or repair tickets. List
active red chains in the rollback record.

Issue #65 remains open until both systems are live and stable: durable repair
convergence is proven fleetwide, and mostly-static-sites has completed its
seven-day one-offs/index rollout, rendered-output Oracle approval, canaries,
two GC cycles, telemetry, and rollback verification.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```
slots.delegationNote: Own authoritative registry/policy enrollment, final-gate hints, staged observe/enforce rollout, exactly-once crash drills, telemetry, compatibility-gated rollback, and final closure evidence.

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#20](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/20).

# task-dag: infer owner/repo from the configured remote URL (aliased/ephemeral worktrees)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#41](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/41)
> — "Tooling design & functionality gaps causing various agent waste."
> **Delegated because:** the fix lives entirely in `virusdave/task-dag`,
> and the parent's leaf `12b6d98` (a top-level DAG task) cannot be
> `task-dag complete`d against a peer-repo implementation commit
> (`complete` links a *same-repo* commit as a git parent). Per operator
> instruction the work is **delegated** to task-dag so the cross-repo
> `Satisfies:` completion primitive tracks the actual code change.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** the implementation commit landing
> on [`virusdave/task-dag`](https://github.com/virusdave/task-dag) `master`
> MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#41`, plus this child epic's own
> `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level
> completion aggregator attributes it to *this* delegated child.

## 1. Goal

In a prepared/ephemeral worktree the `origin` remote is an **aliased SSH
host** that `ephemeral_checkout` configures — e.g.
`git@github-task-dag:virusdave/task-dag.git` or `git@github-top-level:...`
— which does **not** contain the literal string `github.com`. The
task-dag `comment` command and the automatic status-comment poster derived
`owner/repo` with a `github.com`-only regex, so they failed with
`could not determine owner/repo; pass --repo=owner/repo` in exactly the
worktrees the fleet runs in. Every issue op then had to be re-run with an
explicit `--repo`. Empirical waste
(`docs/agent-runtime/agent-waste-backlog.ndjson`, 5+ hits):
`task-dag-comment-needs-repo`, `task-dag-comment-missing-repo`,
`task-dag-comment-needs-repo-flag` (x3).

This is the classic epic-#41 pattern: a tool built for pattern **A** (a
plain `github.com` origin) should support the superset **B** (aliased SSH
host / scp-style / `ssh://` / non-`github.com` remotes) with no downside.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Shared resolver** | Add one helper (`parse_owner_repo_from_url`) that strips the leading scheme+host (`https://host/`, `http://host/`, `git@host:`, `ssh://[user@]host[:port]/`, `git://host/`) and the trailing `.git`/slash, then keeps the leading `owner/repo` pair (requiring exactly that shape). |
| **Wire the failing ops** | Route the `comment` command and the automatic status-comment poster through the helper instead of a `github.com`-only regex. |
| **De-dupe** | Route the two existing generic-sed call sites (retroactive-link paging, blocked-dispatch logging) through the same helper. |
| **`--repo` stays** | The explicit `--repo=owner/repo` remains the override for genuinely ambiguous / non-standard remotes; unparseable inputs (bare local fixture paths) resolve to nothing and still fail closed and demand `--repo`. |
| **Tests** | Extend `tests/task-dag/comment-cmd.sh` with the aliased SSH host, scp-style, `ssh://`(+port), `git://`, and no-`.git` HTTPS forms, plus a "bare local path fails closed" case. |
| **Gates** | `bash -n`, `shellcheck -S error`, and the full `tests/task-dag/run-all.sh` green. |

## 3. Non-goals

- No change to the `Satisfies:` / delegation / completion plumbing.
- No broadening beyond owner/repo resolution from a remote URL.

## 4. Completion

A single task-dag implementation commit on `master` carrying
`Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#41` and this child epic's `Issue:`/`URL:`
trailer satisfies this child epic; the top-level aggregator then records
the delegated-child completion against #41.
slots.delegationNote: Fix lands in virusdave/task-dag; a top-level DAG leaf cannot be task-dag complete'd against a peer-repo commit, so delegate + Satisfies tracks it.
slots.title: task-dag: infer owner/repo from the configured remote URL so comment/issue ops work in aliased/ephemeral worktrees without --repo

# Opaque `branding/` slugs — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Thin index over the authoritative parent plan
> [`docs/epics/branding-opaque-slugs/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in `virusdave/top-level`. Where this and the parent disagree, the parent
> wins — fix this doc. Tracking issue:
> [virusdave/top-level#19](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/19)
> (split from #15).
> **Operator-approved (2026-06-15); parent §6 decisions are RESOLVED and
> folded in below.** This peer issue materialises under top-level **#19**
> via the `Materialise-Child-Epic:` trailer flow — the work scope here is
> final.

## Scope (Helios control plane)

Make Helios speak the **same opaque `branding` ref** that
`mostly-static-sites` consumes, so the bandit/`NUM` emission, the signed
bundle, and any ad-URL producer reference branding rows **without the
literal brand name**.

**BINDING:** Helios still only decides **`NUM`** (the variant) and
publishes weights/kill-lists evaluated locally by the existing mss
middleware (parent §0, [#13 §6](../../../unified-landing-engine/EPIC_PLAN.md)).
This epic changes only the **`SLUG` representation** Helios emits for
`branding` — literal → opaque. No new route shapes, no schema change.

## First task: confirm the in-repo facts

The top-level repo cannot read automation source. Locate (parent names the
likely area, `helios/src/server/ads/…`):

- where the bandit / `NUM` emission and the signed bundle reference a
  branding row's `SLUG` (currently the literal brand id);
- any ad-final-URL / ValueTrack producer that builds `branding/` `/0`
  URLs;
- how `compare/`/`conquest/` already emit their opaque refs (reuse that
  exact path/helper-equivalent for parity with mss).

## Phase (parent §5)

- **P3 — emit the opaque branding ref.** Only after mss prod serves opaque
  and protects literal URLs (parent P0–P2). The bandit/`NUM` emission, the
  bundle, and any new-ad-URL producer reference branding rows by the
  **same** opaque ref mss uses. Add a **bundle-compile parity check**:
  every emitted branding ref must resolve in the mss registry (same spirit
  as the existing `MAX_VARIANT_BY_PURPOSE` / variant-id drift guard) so
  Helios can never publish an opaque ref mss cannot decode. The operator
  chose **migrate** (parent §6.2), so Helios additionally emits the
  **literal→opaque mapping** for every affected `branding/` `/0` final URL
  — the input the operator's one-off Ads-Editor CSV migration consumes.
  Agents do **not** touch the Ads account.
- **P4 (with operator/mss).** Staged rollout + deploy via
  `self-deploy-helios` under operator approval. The operator runs the
  one-off Ads-Editor CSV final-URL **migrate** (parent §6.2 — export →
  rewrite literal finals to opaque → re-import) using the mapping above
  for the already-approved ad final URLs; absorb the Google re-review on
  migrated ads. mss P1 `308` back-compat stays in place throughout.

## Verification

- Bundle-compile parity test: every emitted branding ref resolves in the
  mss registry; build/test green.
- Prove identical `brand-id → opaque-ref` output against the **shared
  contract** mss publishes (checked-in test vectors / generated manifest /
  importable package — parent §7), in CI.
- Each landing commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#19`.

## Coordination

P3 depends on the mss opaque scheme (parent P0–P2) landing first — agree
the shared output **contract** (not just "same code") before Helios emits
opaque branding refs.
slots.delegationNote: Helios emits the same opaque branding ref (bandit/NUM + bundle + ad-URL producer) only after mss P0-P2; bundle-compile parity check; emit literal->opaque mapping for the operator's Ads-Editor CSV migrate (parent §6.2). Shared contract/test-vectors, not "same code".

# Agent-waste review queue — Helios child epic: second top-level read-only mirror + wire `setBacklogReader()` (re-scope of leaf `0d07aed`)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality" (Lever D).
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md)
> ("Remaining work" #3; decisions **D1/D2** RESOLVED).
> **Re-scopes** the previously operator-blocked task-dag leaf `0d07aed`
> ("Wire Helios agent-waste backlog to the real store"), whose operator gate is
> now closed ([automation#57 comment #4891081664](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/57#issuecomment-4891081664));
> that leaf is parked `--downstream` awaiting this workstream, not
> operator-blocked.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 has **several** child epics,
> the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO carry this issue's own
> `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level completion
> aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal

Make `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` (admin-only) return **real** pending-review
items instead of the 503-degrade default, by having Helios read the backlog file
that github-worker exports into `top-level` (D1/D2). This is the **re-scope** of
leaf `0d07aed`: the operator resolved the transport to be a **git-backed file in
`top-level`, read via a second read-only mirror** — superseding the earlier
same-host-NDJSON sketch in that leaf's note.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Second read-only mirror** | Add a **second** git `--mirror` of `top-level` alongside the existing `automation` mirror, using the same proven pattern as [`helios/src/server/taskDagMirror.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/taskDagMirror.ts): bare `--mirror` clone, ~60s refresh, deploy key, **loud-but-non-fatal** (a fetch failure keeps the last-good copy + reports "stale", never 500s). Reads the D2 read-only deploy key provisioned in child epic #1 (same shape as `/run/agenix/helios-github-automation-deploy-key`). |
| **Wire `setBacklogReader()`** | Implement a `BacklogReader` (the `status()` / `readBacklog()` interface already defined in [`helios/src/server/agentWasteRepo.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/agentWasteRepo.ts)) that reads the exported backlog file from the top-level mirror, and install it via `setBacklogReader()`, replacing the default `unavailableBacklogReader`. Use the hardened `parseBacklogNdjson()` / the Zod contract [`helios/src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/shared/contracts/api/agentWaste.ts). |
| **Reuse the merged plumbing** | The route `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` (admin-only, 503-degrades when unwired: [`helios/src/server/routes/agentWaste.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/routes/agentWaste.ts)) already exists (issue #57 task 1). This child epic only supplies the reader + mirror. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants (carry forward)

- **Read path is loud-but-non-fatal** (taskDagMirror semantics): a `top-level`
  fetch failure shows stale/unavailable, never a 500.
- **`note` is display-only** — surface it in the admin UI, never inject it into
  any agent.
- **No prod DB dependency** — the whole point of D1 (git file) is to keep the
  producer decoupled from Helios's prod DB. Do not add a DB table for this.
- Deploy key is the **`helios` service user**'s agenix read key (D2), not the
  machine/`amp-local` credential.

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Depends on** child epic #1 (backlog file **format** + **D2 read key**) and,
  for live end-to-end data, child epic #2 (the exporter actually writing the
  file). The reader can be built against a fixture as soon as #1's format is
  fixed; live verification needs #2.
- **Closes out** the re-scoped leaf `0d07aed`.

## 5. Acceptance

- With the exporter running, `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` returns real
  pending-review items; with `top-level` unreachable it reports stale/unavailable
  and never 500s.
- Deterministic, prod-resource-free reader test (fixture backlog file, no prod
  resources), plus the live endpoint confirmed on prod **after** deploy via
  `self-deploy*` under lock. Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

Additive: a second read-only mirror + a reader install. Rollback is reverting
`setBacklogReader()` to the default (endpoint returns to 503-degrade) and
removing the mirror. Read-only credential; no writes to `top-level` from this
child epic (writes are child epic #4). Deploy follows canon (push →
`self-deploy*` under lock; never manually restart the serving Helios process).
slots.delegationNote: RESOLVED_DESIGN Remaining-work #3; depends on child epic 1 (format + read key) and 2 (live data). Re-scopes/closes blocked leaf 0d07aed.
slots.title: Agent-waste review queue — Helios: second top-level read-only mirror + wire setBacklogReader() (re-scope of 0d07aed)

# About-Us Unification — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#6](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/6).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/about-us-unify/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> the top-level repo. This child epic exists because the operator
> hoisted the "v2 staff strip" (with a 15-minute auto-refresh
> requirement) into v1 scope, and the staff-roster data lives in
> Helios.
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `automation` master and
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#6
> ```

## Scope owned by this repo (Helios)

### H1 — Public-roster export endpoint + approval workflow

1. **New GET endpoint: `/public/roster.json`** (path under the
   existing Helios HTTP surface; final route under
   `helios-server`'s decision).
   - **Auth:** none. The data emitted is the same first-names
     and approved-for-public headshots that are already destined
     to be public on the brand sites. Rate-limit to e.g.
     60 req/min per source IP via the existing reverse-proxy
     layer (or in-process if simpler).
   - **Response shape:** JSON array of rows, one per emitted
     employee:
     ```json
     [
       {
         "first_name": "Karon",
         "headshot_url": "https://helios.../public/headshots/<sha>.jpg",
         "headshot_approved_at": "2026-05-20T18:31:04Z"
       }
     ]
     ```
   - **Filter:** only rows where `headshot_approved_at IS NOT
     NULL` AND `public_excluded = false` AND `headshot_url IS
     NOT NULL`.
   - **Stability:** order alphabetically by `first_name` then by
     `headshot_approved_at` so the brand-site grid order is
     deterministic between revalidates.
   - **Caching:** server-side cache for ~60s (the brand sites
     revalidate every 15 min anyway — the 60s cache exists to
     soak up the cold-start spike when many static-site builds
     happen near the same revalidate boundary).

2. **Schema additions on the `employees` table** (or whatever
   the existing Helios employee model is named — verify in
   `helios-server`).
   - `public_excluded BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false` —
     per-employee opt-out. Admin-only writable.
   - `headshot_approved_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NULL` —
     stamped when an admin clicks "approve for public display".
     Null until then.
   - Indexed compound: `(headshot_approved_at IS NULL,
     public_excluded)` so the public-roster query filter is
     cheap.
   - Migration is additive (no backfill needed — default state
     is "not approved", which is the safe default).

3. **Admin UI: per-employee approval toggle.**
   - On the existing employee-detail view in the Helios admin
     pages (location: confirm in `helios-server`'s template /
     route inventory), add two controls beneath the headshot
     field:
     - **Toggle:** "Exclude from public roster" → writes
       `public_excluded`. Persistent across approvals.
     - **Button:** "Approve headshot for public display" →
       stamps `headshot_approved_at = NOW()`. If already
       approved, the button toggles to "Revoke public
       approval" → clears `headshot_approved_at = NULL`.
   - Both actions are admin-only (use the existing
     admin-auth middleware; no new auth model).
   - Action gets logged to the existing Helios audit log
     (operator-action style — "admin X approved employee Y's
     headshot at T").

4. **Headshot URL stability.**
   - `headshot_url` must be content-addressable so the brand
     site's ISR can rely on URL change to bust its image
     cache: serve from
     `helios.<host>/public/headshots/<sha256-of-bytes>.<ext>`.
     If today's headshots are stored at mutable URLs, add a
     thin re-publisher that copies the bytes to
     content-addressable storage on first approval (and on
     change).
   - Serve with a long `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000,
     immutable` because the URL changes when the bytes change.

## Out of scope

- Any brand-site rendering — that's M4 in the
  `mostly-static-sites` child epic.
- Any FBUS-specific image scrubbing — also lives in the
  `mostly-static-sites` child epic (on the FBUS build side).
  Helios serves the un-scrubbed headshot; FBUS scrubs locally.
- Any change to the existing employee data the parsers ingest.
  This epic only adds two columns + one read endpoint + a small
  admin UI.
- Any deploy automation — operator (Dave) handles
  `systemctl restart helios-server` per `automation`'s AGENTS.md.

## Phases (matches parent EPIC_PLAN.md)

- **H1.** Single phase. Schema migration + admin-UI controls +
  public-roster GET endpoint, all behind no feature flag (the
  endpoint returns `[]` until an admin approves the first
  headshot, so the brand-side render is a no-op until then).

## Cross-repo dependencies

- The brand-site M4 phase in `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites`
  consumes this endpoint, but it ships against a checked-in
  fixture in parallel so M4 isn't blocked on H1.
- No dependency on `helios-parser-configs` (this is a Helios
  server change, not a parser config).
- No dependency on `nixos-sbc` (Helios is already exposed
  publicly via the existing reverse-proxy chain; the new path
  rides on that).

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. H1 commits have landed on `automation` master with the
   `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#6` trailer.
2. `GET https://helios.<host>/public/roster.json` returns a
   valid JSON array on the deployed system (operator-verified
   after `systemctl restart helios-server`).
3. An admin can approve a headshot in the UI and the next
   `GET /public/roster.json` (within ≤60s server cache window)
   reflects the new row.
slots.delegationNote: Helios GET /public/roster.json (filtered by headshot_approved_at IS NOT NULL AND public_excluded = false), employees.public_excluded + headshot_approved_at columns, admin-UI approval toggle, content-addressable headshot URLs. Consumed by mostly-static-sites M4 on a 15-minute revalidate.
slots.title: About-Us unification — Helios public-roster export + per-employee approval workflow (H1)

# task-dag: parse Materialise-Child-Epic groups from the whole commit message, and fail loud

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#49](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/49)
> — "Materialise-Child-Epic trailers silently ignored when not in the
> final trailer block."
> **Delegated because:** the materialise trailer-scanning logic lives
> entirely in `virusdave/task-dag`
> ([`.github/scripts/materialise-child-epics.sh`](https://github.com/virusdave/task-dag/blob/master/.github/scripts/materialise-child-epics.sh)),
> and the reusable `materialise-child-epic.yml` workflow it drives is what
> every wired peer repo calls — so the fix is repo-local to task-dag and
> automatically protects all callers.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** the implementation commit landing
> on [`virusdave/task-dag`](https://github.com/virusdave/task-dag) `master`
> MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#49`, plus this child epic's own
> `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level
> completion aggregator attributes it to *this* delegated child.

## 1. Goal

`git interpret-trailers --parse` only recognises the **last contiguous
trailer paragraph** of a commit message. The materialise scanner pre-filters
each commit message through it:

```sh
trailers="$(printf '%s\n' "$msg" | git interpret-trailers --parse)"
[ -z "$trailers" ] && continue
```

so a `Materialise-Child-Epic:` group followed (after a blank line) by any
other trailer paragraph — `Related:`, or a task-dag
`Task-Commit:/Issue:/URL:/Status:` block — is dropped, and the job goes
green logging `No Materialise-Child-Epic trailers acted upon`. Silent no-op
on critical cross-repo delegation. Fix it two ways:

1. **Parse the whole body** (option 2): recognise `Materialise-Child-Epic:`
   groups anywhere in the message, delimited only by the next
   `Materialise-Child-Epic:` opener or EOF.
2. **Fail loud** (option 1): a commit that carries an explicit materialise
   directive but produces zero successful materialisations must exit
   non-zero with an `::error::` (and page where a parent issue is known),
   never a benign green summary.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Replace the pre-filter** | Remove the `git interpret-trailers --parse` pre-filter in the main scan of `materialise-child-epics.sh`. Add a purpose-built raw scanner (extracted into a helper so it is unit-testable under `MATERIALISE_LIB_ONLY=1` with no network/GitHub side effects). |
| **Parser contract** | See §3 — a group opens **only** on a column-1, case-insensitive `Materialise-Child-Epic:` / `Materialize-Child-Epic:` key line, and stays open until the next opener or EOF. Blank lines, prose, and unrelated trailer-like lines (`Related:`, `Task-Commit:`, `Issue:`, `URL:`, `Status:`, unknown keys) are **ignored, never group terminators**. |
| **Fail-loud accounting** | Track groups seen / created / already-materialised / failed and a `had_error` flag. Parser/validation failures in `flush_group` (bad peer, missing required keys, bad parent, bad slug, missing body file) set `had_error=1`. At end: benign no-op message **only** when no materialise opener-like line was seen; if an opener was seen but no group parsed, `::error::` + page; if `had_error`, exit non-zero. `::error::` annotations alone do **not** fail a step — an explicit non-zero exit is required. |
| **Tests** | Extend the `MATERIALISE_LIB_ONLY=1` unit tests: (a) group followed by blank line + `Related:` (the #44 regression); (b) group followed by an interleaved task-dag `Status:` block; (c) multiple groups separated by blank lines / unrelated trailers; (d) the plain contiguous-block case (regression); (e) blank line *inside* a group is accepted; (f) indented `Word: value` example lines do not open a group; (g) value containing a colon (`RFC: parser fix`) survives; (h) a malformed explicit group (missing required keys) reports failure, not benign no-op. |
| **Docs** | Remove the header-comment warning that all groups must live in a single final contiguous trailer block; document the new contract (parsed from the full message, delimited only by the next opener or EOF). Update `top-level` `AGENTS.md` / cross-repo-driver design doc references only if they restate the old rule (best-effort, may be a follow-up). |
| **Gates** | `bash -n`, `shellcheck -S error` (as task-dag already runs it), and the materialise unit-test script all green. Critical-infra Oracle design review **before** implementing and change review of the diff **after** (canon `QUALITY_GATES.md`). |

## 3. Parser contract (implement exactly)

1. A group starts **only** on a column-1, exact trailer-key line:
   `Materialise-Child-Epic: <owner/repo>` or `Materialize-Child-Epic:
   <owner/repo>` (key match case-insensitive).
2. Once opened, the group stays active until the next materialise opener or
   EOF.
3. Blank lines, prose, `Related:`, `Task-Commit:`, `Issue:`, `URL:`,
   `Status:`, and unknown trailer-like lines are ignored — **not** group
   terminators. (Closing a group on a blank line or prose would reintroduce
   the whitespace footgun.)
4. Only recognised child-epic keys at column 1 are collected into the open
   group: `Child-Epic-Title`, `Child-Epic-Body-File`, `Parent-Issue`,
   `Child-Epic-Slug`, `Delegation-Note`.
5. Keys before the first opener are ignored.
6. Values preserve existing behaviour: split on the **first** `:`, trim
   leading whitespace after it, preserve later colons in the value.
7. Require column-1 keys (`^[A-Za-z0-9-]+:` with no leading whitespace) so
   indented examples / code blocks in commit messages cannot trigger a
   group. Strip a trailing `\r` and handle a final line with no trailing
   newline (`while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]`).
8. Duplicate recognised keys: preserve existing last-wins behaviour (do not
   silently change semantics as part of this fix).

Suggested shape: an `extract_materialise_trailers_from_message` helper that
emits a normalised synthetic trailer stream, which the existing
`while read line; case "$key_lc"` group-flush loop then consumes with
minimal change. Keep marker-ref identity, ordering, and the
check→create-issue→push-marker→`delegate` sequence **unchanged** — this is a
parser fix only.

## 4. Non-goals

- No change to the `Materialise-Child-Epic:` trailer **format** or the set
  of recognised keys (this is a parser fix, not a format change — but note
  it still touches critical-infra behaviour, so the Oracle review and the
  script's own gates apply).
- No change to marker-ref namespaces, idempotency, App-token minting, or the
  `task-dag delegate` step.
- No pre-commit/pre-push hook (option 3), and no folded/multi-line trailer
  support.
- No change to the pre-existing marker-check → issue-create race (out of
  scope; the parser fix does not worsen it).

## 5. Completion

A single task-dag implementation commit on `master` carrying
`Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#49` and this child epic's `Issue:`/`URL:`
trailer satisfies this child epic; the top-level aggregator then records the
delegated-child completion against #49.
slots.delegationNote: Replace interpret-trailers --parse with a whole-message scanner (opt 2) plus fail-loud accounting (opt 1); drop the pre-commit-hook option; keep the marker/delegate flow unchanged. Critical infra: Oracle design+change review and the script bash -n/shellcheck/materialise tests apply.

# Helios GAds evolver introspection dashboard — automation child epic

> **Child epic of** [`virusdave/top-level#24`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/24)
> (`gads-evolver-introspection`). The **parent epic plan is authoritative**
> for design, philosophy, IA, data sources, and page content:
> [`virusdave/top-level:docs/epics/gads-evolver-introspection/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/gads-evolver-introspection/EPIC_PLAN.md).
> This child holds the Helios (`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`) implementation
> scope only.
>
> **Every implementation commit** that satisfies any part of this epic MUST
> carry the trailer `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#24`, and SHOULD also
> carry `Phase: P<n>` (`P1`..`P7`) so the cross-repo-completion-sync
> workflow posts a per-phase progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope (one-line)

Build the reserved **`Evolution`** and **`Iteration`** sub-pages under the
existing per-site, grant-gated `/metrics/gads-<site>/` GAds tab system
(IA + grants from [#18](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/18)),
reading the evolver's own decision/outcome data already in the Helios DB /
filesystem. An **introspection surface for how Helios reacted**, not a
re-implementation of Google's ad dashboards. Rapid hill-climb, **not**
audit-grade (decision
[0003](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-kb/decisions/0003-joint-gads-lp-optimization-not-audit-grade.md)).

## Binding constraints

- **Reuse #18's IA, grants (`gads-bronx` / `gads-midtown` / `gads-all`),
  scope registry, and serving model verbatim.** No new route shapes, no
  forked access model. `gads-all` is its own grant, never synthesised.
- **Server-derived site predicate.** Never trust a client-supplied
  site-widening param. Per-site pages must not leak cross-site rows.
- **Cheapest defensible DB use.** Bounded aggregate queries over the
  existing small purpose-built tables. **No** per-event fact table, no
  always-on derivation worker, no rollup/hypertable/CAGG/HLL in V1.
- **Honest approximations.** Every estimate badged; never a fabricated
  precise-looking number. Honest empty states where a write path is not
  yet confirmed.
- **Migrations do not auto-apply on deploy.** Any schema change is applied
  on prod by the agent only after Oracle DB review **and** explicit
  operator approval, then verified live (canon §3).

## Phases (detail in the parent plan §5–§7)

| Phase | Deliverable | Closure criteria |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Data audit + site-scope semantics | Confirm prod population of `gads_ad_attempts`, `landingpage_ad_outcomes`, bundle/L2/L3 artifacts. Decide per-attempt site-scope policy (preferred: add `site text null`, backfill best-effort, hide unknown-scope per-site, show under `gads-all` badged). No per-site page ships until scoping is safe. |
| **P2** | Minimal schema/index support | Add `site` to `gads_ad_attempts` if P1 confirms; cheap indexes only if justified; optional tiny `gads_evolver_runs` run-index table (no large JSON/prompts in DB). No rollup/hypertable/CAGG/HLL. Migration gated on Oracle DB review + operator approval. |
| **P3** | Backend contracts + grant-gated endpoints | Typed `GadsEvolutionResponse` / `GadsIterationRunsResponse` / `GadsIterationRunDetailResponse`; `GET /api/gads/evolution`, `/api/gads/iterations`, `/api/gads/iterations/:runId`; server-derived site predicate; per-site access tests (Bronx user cannot read Midtown/all; `gads-all` explicit; unknown-scope hidden per-site; payload bounded). |
| **P4** | Evolution UI | `/metrics/gads-<site>/evolution` (reserved stub → implemented): learning heartbeat, loop-health KPI strip, action/outcome matrix, hotspots, L3 adoption + LP-reaction panels. Honest empty states + badges. **Mandatory Oracle UI review before ship.** |
| **P5** | Iteration run browser | `/metrics/gads-<site>/iteration`: bounded run timeline + run-detail drilldown (DB-derived + badge when L2 JSON missing). No unbounded historical-file loads. |
| **P6** | L3 + LP enrichment | Latest L3 evaluation summaries; `l3-addenda.md` freshness/hash; whether a later L2 run consumed addenda; `landingpage_ad_outcomes` summary if populated. No approval-workflow / prompt-diff persistence invented here. |
| **P7** | Docs, tests, rollout readiness | Operator runbook; tests pass; UI reviewed; payload/query-cost notes recorded; epics updated; ready for **gated `self-deploy-helios`** (no deploy from the planning worker). |

## Out of scope (V1)

Causal lift / off-policy estimates, win probability, credible intervals,
regret; prompt/rule approval workflow + prompt-diff persistence; trial
monitoring until the trial check tables are real; per-click cost / revenue
/ ROAS; anomaly detection; heatmaps; any Timescale CAGG/hypertable/HLL.
slots.delegationNote: Helios Evolution + Iteration pages for GAds/LP evolver introspection; reuse #18 IA/grants; P1 per-attempt site-scoping gate before any per-site UI ships.

# Prospective Pending-Purchase Classifier — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#33](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/33).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md`](../../../../designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md)
> and the staged plan + the 8 operator decisions live in
> [`docs/epics/prospective-pending-purchase/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md),
> both in the top-level repo. This child epic exists because **all
> implementation lands in `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (the Helios app
> under `helios/`)**: the worker classifier, server routes, DB schema,
> review UI, and the inventory lifecycle are all Helios surfaces.
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `automation` master and
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#33
> ```

## Scope owned by this repo (Helios)

Two parallel tracks. The **classifier track** replaces the reactive
pending-purchase generator with a prospective Bedrock-driven one behind a
deterministic validator. The **pricing-safety lifecycle track** closes the
first-sale mispricing race for brand-new SKUs. They are independent and
meet only where catalog-apply creates the live product the lifecycle then
prices.

### Classifier track

- **C0 — Amp → `import_json` bridge runbook** (already operational; no
  code). Purchase 151113 packet #53 was built this way. Documents the
  manual escalation path that stays as the human-triggered escape hatch.
- **C1 — Refactor the generator into seams.** Carve
  `collectPendingPurchaseContext`, `buildPendingPurchasePacket`,
  `persistGeneratedPendingPurchasePacket` out of
  `worker/jobs/generatePendingPurchasePacketJob.ts`; no behavior change
  yet. Isolate the legacy rule-based row-builder behind ONE seam **so it
  can be deleted at cutover (C8)** — it is not a preserved path
  (decision 4: go direct).
- **C2 — Hint bundle storage + admin API.** New
  `pending_purchase_hint_bundles` / `pending_purchase_hint_documents`
  tables; admin endpoints; `hintBundleId` on the generate job + route.
  v1 = pasted arbitrary hint text only (decision 2).
- **C3 — Hint fact extraction + intent classification.**
  `extractPendingPurchaseHintFacts` (Bedrock JSON for menus; deterministic
  for Sweed PO JSON). First LLM-classify the hint for *how* it helps
  (canonical SKU list / ordered-items expectation / free-text description /
  line-item list — decision 2), then extract inert cited facts.
- **C4 — Prospective LLM classifier.**
  `classifyPendingPurchasePacketWithLlm`; event-level prompt over the full
  order + live catalog + hint facts; `PendingPurchaseLlmDraftRow` output
  contract (model proposes a reuse link, never authorizes it). Default
  model = the current "standard, most capable general reasoning model,"
  chosen dynamically + a below-the-fold Bedrock config page for rare
  per-context overrides (decision 1).
- **C5 — Deterministic validator / reconciler (the safety layer).**
  Validate every reuse candidate vs the live product; taxonomy/size/pack/
  house-brand guards; duplicate detection; Helios (not the model) computes
  deterministic fields + price + inline market evidence.
- **C6 — Review-UI surfacing.** Show confidence, rationale, hint
  citations, reuse candidates, and new-brand/new-group/no-comps warnings
  (all from the passthrough `raw_row_json`).
- **C7 — Apply-time drift guard + optional post-apply refresh.**
  Generated-reuse drift guard in the apply job; optional enqueue of created
  product ids after apply.
- **C8 — Direct cutover + legacy deletion.** Switch
  `catalog.pending_purchases.generate` to the LLM-prospective path and
  **delete the legacy rule-based classifier** (decision 4). A short
  dev-only shadow comparison during validation is fine, but it ships as the
  single path — no permanent `generationMode` toggle, no legacy fallback.

### Pricing-safety lifecycle track (independent; can ship first)

- **L1 — Lifecycle record + gates (no reverse move).**
  `purchase_inventory_lifecycle_runs` / `_items` tables keyed by
  `(dealer_id, po_id)`; start / verify-quarantine / purchase-market-refresh
  / purchase-reprice routes; market-completion (timestamp-based) +
  price-applied (live-price-equality) verifiers; reuse the existing pricing
  review UI. No release route yet.
- **L2 — Bulk quarantine repair + gated release.** Extract a shared
  stock-transfer service from the one-way move-to-inspection; purchase-
  scoped bulk move-to-inspection (repair); reverse + bulk **release** to a
  chosen FOR SALE room (dropdown, default "FOR SALE - Sales Floor" —
  decision 6) with immediate-before-transfer preflight (live price + live
  quarantine re-verify), post-transfer verification, and partial-failure
  recovery. Quarantine is **optional, not enforced** (decision 5): the UI
  offers bulk move-to-quarantine + full lifecycle OR reprice-in-place
  skipping the release/move-back. Repricing is SKU-level with a small badge
  when a SKU already has on-floor stock (decision 8).
- **L3 — Automation + monitoring.** `inventory.lifecycle.advance` job to
  poll/advance async gates; quarantine-breach monitor; alerts (lot in FOR
  SALE before priced, market timeout, price-apply failure, release partial
  failure).

## Dependency order (for task breakdown)

```
C0 (done) ─▶ C1 ─▶ C4 ─▶ C5 ─▶ (C6, C7) ─▶ C8
              C2 ─▶ C3 ─────────▲
L1 ─▶ L2 ─▶ L3        (lifecycle track, parallel to the classifier track)
```

- C1 unblocks C4; C2 unblocks C3; C3 feeds C4; C5 depends on C4; C6 & C7
  depend on C5; C8 depends on C5+C6+C7.
- L-track is fully parallel and independent of the classifier track.

## Out of scope (explicit)

- **FT-1** hint file uploads (CSV/PDF/manifests/POs/catalogs/scrapings) —
  near-term follow-up, separate task.
- **FT-2** auto-generated proposal packets — gated on FT-3.
- **FT-3** LitAlerts competitor-data redesign — its own future top-level
  epic (decision 7); not created here.
- **FT-4** broader pricing process/engine redesign — its own future epic.
- Any change to the human review + apply approval gate (kept as-is).

## Required gates (per canon)

- **Oracle critical-infra / DB review** for the validator (C5), the apply
  drift guard (C7), the hint tables + generate-job changes (C2), and the
  lifecycle tables + release safety (L1/L2). DB migrations apply on prod
  only after Oracle blessing **and** explicit operator approval, then
  live-sentinel verification.
- **Green tree** — repo-documented light/targeted lint/typecheck/test for
  touched Helios areas in the dev loop; full presubmit before merge. No
  first-party `any`; no bug-masking fallbacks.
- **Oracle UI review** for C6 review-UI changes, the L1 lifecycle panel,
  and any operator-facing copy.

## Completion signal

This child epic is complete when both tracks have landed on `automation`
master with `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#33` trailers: the legacy
classifier is deleted and `catalog.pending_purchases.generate` runs the
validated prospective path (C8), and the quarantine→reprice→release
lifecycle is operator-usable end-to-end with its hard release gates (L3).
slots.delegationNote: Implement classifier stages C0-C8 and lifecycle stages L1-L3 per docs/designs/prospective-pending-purchase-classifier.md. Each stage honors its canon Oracle critical-infra/DB + UI reviews and explicit operator approval before any prod DB migration or live-inventory write. Carry Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#33 on implementation commits.

# Helios `/catalog/review` perf & UX — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#16](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/16).
> The authoritative design (measurements, root-cause analysis, phase
> rationale, Oracle review) is
> [`docs/epics/review-page-performance/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in the top-level repo. Read it first. This file is the repo-local
> implementation breakdown.
>
> Every implementation commit that lands on `automation` master and
> satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#16
> Phase: <A|B|C|D|E>
> ```

## Where the code lives

- Slow endpoint query:
  `helios/src/server/db/queries/reviewFamilyQueueQueries.ts`
  (`listReviewFamilyQueue`).
- Route: `helios/src/server/routes/review.ts`
  (`GET /api/review/family-queue`).
- Contract: `helios/src/shared/contracts/api/review.ts`
  (`ReviewFamilyQueueQuerySchema`, `ReviewFamilyQueueResponseSchema`).
- Live-state writer (Phase B projection hook):
  `helios/src/worker/jobs/catalogGroupPersistence.ts`
  (`updateCatalogGroupLiveState`).
- Migration sentinels: `helios/src/server/db/pendingMigrations.ts`.
- Migrations: `helios/src/server/db/migrations/NNN_*.sql` (applied
  manually by an operator; idempotent `IF NOT EXISTS`).
- Client review page + the canonical pending-purchases review layout to
  reuse: `helios/src/client/routes/...` (pending-purchases review is the
  UI parity target — find and extend it, do not fork).

## Constraints (apply to every slice)

- **Typed TS only.** No untyped query/response shapes.
- **Measure before/after with a real full fetch**, not just
  `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` (canon: plans hide payload/detoast/serialization
  cost). Record server `exec_time`, wall time, payload bytes, and
  executor memory in the commit/issue.
- **Idempotent migrations** (`CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`,
  `CONCURRENTLY` where applicable) so they no-op on prod and stay
  recreate-safe. Add a matching sentinel to `pendingMigrations.ts`.
- **Do NOT add btree indexes to the join/filter path** — measured fast
  already.
- **Do not regress competitor-match correctness** (separate epic).
- **Reuse canonical UI** (pending-purchases review layout); no forked
  components.

## Slices

### R-A — Server family-aware pagination + minimal client paging *(ship together)*

Two-phase query in `listReviewFamilyQueue`:

1. Narrow family-page CTE/query over the indexed join only
   (`proposal_line_items ⋈ proposal_rows ⋈ proposal_batches ⋈
   catalog_groups`, projecting `brand/category/subcategory` columns
   only) → group → deterministic order → `LIMIT familyLimit+1`. **No**
   `jsonb_array_elements`, `regexp_replace`, `evidence_json`, or full
   `live_state_json` here.
2. Fetch full line items + reduced live state for the selected
   families' proposal rows, and observations only for that page's
   product ids.

- Add to `ReviewFamilyQueueQuerySchema`: `limit` (default 10, max 25)
  and `cursor`. Add `pageInfo { hasNextPage, endCursor }` to the
  response. Cursor encodes the sort tuple + filter state +
  `familyKeyVersion: 1`.
- Interim family key = `(brand, category, subcategory)`; multi-size
  families render `Mixed`/blank size. Keep individual actions.
- `maxItemsPerPage` safety cap; oversized family returned alone +
  logged.
- Minimal client change: request a single page; stop fetching/rendering
  the whole queue.
- **Acceptance:** payload ≪ 2.4 MB, no whole-queue
  `jsonb_array_elements`, executor memory ≪ 600 MB, DB interaction
  ≤125 ms; before/after numbers posted. Ships before R-B/R-C.

### R-B — `catalog_group_products` projection table

- Migration: `catalog_group_products(catalog_group_id, product_id,
  ordinal, name, tab, size_name, price numeric, updated_at, primary key
  (catalog_group_id, product_id))`; indexes `(product_id)`,
  `(catalog_group_id, ordinal)`. Idempotent + sentinel + idempotent
  backfill from `live_state_json`.
- Populate in `updateCatalogGroupLiveState`, write-on-change only
  (`WHERE … IS DISTINCT FROM`), inside the same transaction as the
  existing column projection.
- Size semantics: product-targeted → that product's `size_name`;
  single-size group → that size; multi-size group → `NULL`/`"Mixed"`.
- Rewrite R-A's narrow query to read `size_name` from the projection
  table (drop the lateral blob crack); upgrade the family key to
  include size; bump `familyKeyVersion → 2`.
- **Acceptance:** narrow page query has zero JSON cracking; multi-size
  groups grouped correctly; plan + timings posted.

### R-C — Client UX parity with pending-purchases review

- Lazy/virtualized mount of pricing ladders (mount on demand, not all
  at once).
- Reuse the pending-purchases review hierarchical layout: family groups
  with **group-level actions** + per-item actions.
- Group-aware pagination UI: never split a normal family across a page;
  massive family handled per R-A's guard.
- **Acceptance:** page interactive ≤500 ms after data; no all-ladders
  mount; layout matches pending-purchases review.

### R-D — Resolve dead MSO filter

- `msoOnly` is hardcoded `{ isMSOBrand: false }` → returns nothing.
  Either wire to a real brand-annotation source or remove the dead
  filter from contract + UI. Prefer removal if no source is ready.

### R-E — *(stretch)* precomputed preview columns

- Only if `regexp_replace` previews still measure material after R-A.
  Add `*_preview_text` (+ truncation flag) columns on
  `proposal_line_items`, maintained on insert/edit paths. Do not do
  pre-emptively.
slots.delegationNote: Implementation of top-level#16 in Helios. Start with Phase A (server pagination + minimal client paging) for the 9x+ win; do NOT add join-path indexes (measured fast).
slots.title: Helios /catalog/review performance & UX overhaul

# agent-pain-points migration — automation (Helios) child epic: mirror/reader/promote/client retarget

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#40](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/40)
> — "Migrate the agent-waste canonical git storage to different repo".
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`virusdave/top-level` → `docs/epics/agent-pain-points-migration/EPIC_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/epics/agent-pain-points-migration/EPIC_PLAN.md).
> **Lever-D design being amended:**
> [`docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md)
> (this migration reverses its decision **D1** storage location — it is the
> "dedicated advisories repo" option that was earlier considered and declined).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit on
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation)
> `master` that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#40`, and the **final** satisfying commit MUST
> also carry this issue's own `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer.

## 1. Goal

Re-point Helios' agent-waste review queue (backlog read) and promote button
(advisory write) from `top-level` to `virusdave/agent-pain-points`, and update
the operator-facing catalog links — preserving the admin gate, server-side
validation, audit trail, and `note`-never-becomes-`text` invariant.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Read mirror** | Add an `agent-pain-points` read-only bare mirror (model on [`helios/src/server/topLevelMirror.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/topLevelMirror.ts)). Introduce distinct, accurately-named env: `HELIOS_AGENT_PAIN_POINTS_REPO_URL`, `HELIOS_AGENT_PAIN_POINTS_MIRROR_DIR`, `HELIOS_AGENT_PAIN_POINTS_DEPLOY_KEY`, `HELIOS_AGENT_PAIN_POINTS_REFRESH_SECONDS`, `HELIOS_AGENT_PAIN_POINTS_DISABLE`. **Do not overload** `HELIOS_TOP_LEVEL_*` — the mirror dir is a *bare mirror* while promote wants a *working tree* (design §5 hazard). |
| **Backlog reader** | Re-point [`agentWasteBacklogReader.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/agentWasteBacklogReader.ts) at the new mirror; keep relative path `docs/agent-runtime/agent-waste-backlog.ndjson`; keep fail-closed (empty/unavailable → structured empty / 503). |
| **Promote** | Re-point [`agentWaste/promoteAdvisory.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/agentWaste/promoteAdvisory.ts) to commit `docs/agent-runtime/advisories.yaml` in `agent-pain-points` using a **separate write clone dir** (`HELIOS_AGENT_PAIN_POINTS_WRITE_DIR`) + write deploy key. Preserve validate→write→add→reject-no-op→commit→push→reset-on-failure + subprocess timeout + duplicate-id rejection + single-path staging. |
| **Client links** | Update the hard-coded `github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/agent-runtime/{advisories.yaml,ADVISORY_CATALOG.md}` links in [`agentWasteReviewShared.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/client/routes/config/agentWasteReviewShared.ts) to `agent-pain-points`. |
| **Startup** | Update [`main.ts`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/helios/src/server/main.ts) to init the new mirror + reader. Keep top-level mirror only if still needed for other purposes; otherwise retire it for agent-waste. |
| **Docs** | Amend `RESOLVED_DESIGN.md` (D1 storage location now `agent-pain-points`) and any contract comments referencing `top-level`. |
| **Tests** | Update `promoteAdvisory.test.ts`, `agentWasteBacklogReader.test.ts`, `routes/agentWaste.test.ts` to the new repo/env; all against temp repos, never prod `top-level` **or** prod `agent-pain-points`. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants

- **`note` never becomes advisory `text`** — the load-bearing allowlist safety
  boundary. Unchanged.
- Promote stays **admin-gated + server-validated + audited**; the admin action
  is the safety gate for a behavior-changing mutation.
- Read mirror is read-only; only promote uses the write key/clone.
- Deploy only via `self-deploy*` under `large-action-lock`; never manually
  restart Helios.

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Depends on** the nixos-sbc child (Helios read + write deploy keys + env for
  `agent-pain-points`).
- Cutover is coordinated with the github-worker child in parent epic §6 to avoid
  the split-brain window (promotions landing where the dispatcher isn't reading).

## 5. Acceptance

- `GET /api/agent-waste/backlog` reads the backlog from `agent-pain-points`;
  `POST /api/agent-waste/promote` commits `advisories.yaml` to
  `agent-pain-points`; both fail closed (structured 503) when unavailable.
- `note` provably cannot reach advisory `text`; invalid/duplicate promotions
  rejected before any write.
- Deterministic, prod-resource-free tests of validation + commit path against a
  temp repo; live path confirmed on prod **after** `self-deploy*` under lock.
- Client catalog links point at `agent-pain-points`.
- Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

Rollback = revert the retarget + redeploy; Helios fails closed (empty catalog =
inert injector, unavailable backlog = 503), never serves wrong data. A bad
advisory can be reverted in `agent-pain-points` git. Never point tests at prod.
No prod DB, no schema.

# Pilot: attested surface registry + drift guard, fixing the agent-waste notification

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#57](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/57)
> — "Implement operator-comms UX enforcement". Authoritative design:
> [`docs/designs/operator-comms-ux-enforcement.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/operator-comms-ux-enforcement.md).
>
> **Delegated because:** the agent-waste notification
> ([`scripts/waste-page`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/scripts/waste-page)),
> its formatting helpers, its tests, and the new
> `.well-known/operator-surfaces/` registry all live in
> [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker).
> `top-level` has no code to change for the pilot.
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing
> on [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` for this epic MUST carry `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#57`,
> plus this child epic's own `Issue: #<this-peer-issue-number>` (or `URL:`)
> trailer so the top-level completion aggregator attributes it to *this*
> delegated child.

## 1. Goal

Deliver the design's **pilot** (design §6): the first end-to-end slice of
the surface-enforcement mechanism, proving the shape on the operator's cited
concrete defect.

1. **Establish the registry format in-repo.** Add a `.well-known/operator-surfaces/`
   directory with one JSON entry per operator-facing surface (schema in
   design §4.1: `id`, `repo`, `channel`, `reviewed_input_closure`,
   `examples_dir`, `hash` canonicalization, `oracle_review{url,
   approved_hash, approved_at}`). Author the `agent-waste-page` entry.
2. **Build `operator-surface-guard`'s drift check** (design §4.2 check 1):
   recompute the content hash of the entry's reviewed **input closure**
   (renderer + helpers + fixtures + theme, not one file) plus the
   **CI-regenerated** representative examples, and fail if it differs from
   the recorded `approved_hash`. Two layers: a **pre-landing** run in the
   sanctioned completion path (real prevention) and a **post-push** CI
   backstop (design §4.2 "honest enforcement boundary"). **Never** gate on
   any registry host being at HEAD (design §8.2).
3. **Fix the notification template + register it.** Rework
   [`scripts/waste-page`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/scripts/waste-page)
   so the ~35-40% repeated boilerplate no longer truncates the actual waste
   explanation on mobile (design §1; canon `QUALITY_GATES.md`
   "do not let boilerplate crowd out or truncate the signal"). Get an
   **Oracle UI/UX review of the template plus representative rendered
   examples** (worst-case payloads, not one hand-picked instance) before
   first operator exposure, and record it in the `agent-waste-page` entry's
   `oracle_review`.

## 2. Current state (paths in this repo)

Read these first; the pilot slots into the existing shapes.

| Concern | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Notification builder | `scripts/waste-page` | Builds `title`/`body` (~L230-294) and the `page-dave` command; also builds a one-off detail page (`build_detail_md` ~L114-169, `publish_one_off` ~L171-211). The boilerplate defect is here. |
| Advisory catalog resolver | `lib/advisory-catalog.sh` | Resolves known advisory metadata. |
| Backlog exporter | `scripts/agent-waste-export` | Publishes the backlog NDJSON to `agent-pain-points`. |
| Tests | `tests/waste-page.sh` | Existing coverage; extend for the reworked template + representative-example regeneration. |

## 3. Scope (suggested leaves — the child-epic worker breaks this down)

1. Add the `.well-known/operator-surfaces/` registry schema + a small
   validator/loader; author the `agent-waste-page` entry (closure listing
   `scripts/waste-page`, its helpers, fixtures, any theme asset).
2. Add fixture-driven **representative example regeneration** for the
   agent-waste notification (worst-case payloads) so "what Oracle saw"
   cannot silently drift from what the code renders (design §4.1).
3. Implement `operator-surface-guard`'s drift check over the input closure +
   regenerated examples; wire the **pre-landing** layer into the completion
   path and the **post-push** CI backstop (reusable workflow shape so other
   repos can adopt it later). Include the registry-integrity check that a
   hash/closure change also updates `oracle_review` (design §4.1).
4. Rework the notification template to lead with the waste explanation and
   drop repeated boilerplate; extend `tests/waste-page.sh`; get the Oracle
   UI review; record `oracle_review` in the entry.

## 4. Non-goals (kept out of the pilot)

- The **emission-time lint + new-emitter detection** at the chokepoints is
  **Phase 2** (design §4.3), not here — except that the drift guard's
  new-emitter scan may land as a reusable piece if cheap.
- The **cross-repo fleet index** is **Phase 3** (design §8.2 layer 3).
- The **canon prune** is **Phase 4** (design §4.4), in `top-level`.
- Keep the lint **warn-only** where any lint appears (operator decision 3);
  do not hard-fail emission in the pilot.

## 5. Acceptance

- `.well-known/operator-surfaces/agent-waste-page.json` exists with a real
  `reviewed_input_closure`, CI-regenerated `examples_dir`, and a recorded
  `oracle_review` (URL + `approved_hash` + date).
- `operator-surface-guard` drift check runs **pre-landing and in CI**; a
  deliberate edit to any input-closure file fails it until the entry's
  review + hash are refreshed. No check requires any registry host at HEAD.
- The agent-waste notification leads with the waste explanation and fits the
  mobile-visible space without truncating it; `tests/waste-page.sh` covers
  the reworked template and passes; `master` stays green.
- An Agent Gate Record is attached, and every commit carries
  `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#57` + this child epic's `Issue:` trailer.
slots.delegationNote: Design §4.1/§4.2/§6 pilot; establishes .well-known/operator-surfaces/ + operator-surface-guard drift check and reworks scripts/waste-page as the first Oracle-reviewed surface. Keep any lint warn-only (operator decision 3).

# Helios-driven SEO widgets — `automation` (Helios control plane) child epic

> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md). **Re-read the parent before
> starting any phase** — this child epic is a **thin index** over the
> parent's design, not a re-statement of it. The parent is authoritative;
> if this file ever drifts from it, the parent wins.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#15
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>` trailer
> so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post per-phase progress
> on the parent issue.

## Role in the epic

Helios (`automation`) is the **SEO brain**: it owns content generation,
the editorial review/approve workflow, schedules/prompts, the SEO
control plane, the GA/GSC feedback loop, and the signed SEO-bundle
publisher. mss stays a thin, zero-DB renderer (its child epic is the
peer at `../mostly-static-sites/EPIC_PLAN.md`). **FB.nyc is NOT pulled
into Helios** — only widget *content* flows out as signed bundle data.
See parent [§2](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#2-what-moves-into-helios-answer-to-operator-question-a).

## ⚠️ Binding constraints (from the operator's decisions — parent §0)

- **IRONCLAD human-approval gate (canon §1).** Nothing this control plane
  produces — drafts, title/meta changes, FAQ/posts/images, social
  exports, recommendation-engine proposals — may become publicly visible
  or be posted to any external channel without a human approving that
  **specific** content first. The recommendation engine only *proposes*.
  The only override is explicit prior approval from Dave recorded in a
  GitHub ticket naming the exempted pipeline.
- **Separate SEO bundle**, reusing the unified-landing-engine (#13)
  publisher/signer/`/cloud` mount/validator/`lp_events` pipeline verbatim
  — not a parallel system and not merged into the LP bundle. Reuse
  whatever #13 has landed; specialize once it lands (parent §0.6, §12).
- **Stable, non-cloaked content.** Indexable content is deterministic per
  URL within a bundle; no UA/crawler-varying rendering; JSON-LD must
  match visible content (parent §4, §8).
- **GA/GSC already provisioned** — start from operator-supplied **batch
  data dumps**; direct API integration is a later, optional add-on
  (parent §0.4).
- **DB-cost discipline (canon §3).** The GA/GSC import jobs and the
  `lp_events` SEO extension are recurring/background DB workloads → each
  needs a written cost budget + an Oracle DB-efficiency review recorded on
  this issue **before deploy** (parent §9).

## Subtasks (see parent §11 for the authoritative list)

- SEO bundle schemas + compiler; `seo-bundle build`/`validate` CLI.
- Signed publisher to `/cloud` (atomic-rename pointer + ed25519), reusing
  #13's publisher.
- FAQ generator/editor/approval (raw + sanitized side-by-side).
- Blog source ingestion (`seo_source_items`) + bedrock draft generation
  (private Bedrock endpoints — canon §4).
- Prompt-schedule + topic-mix config; review/edit/schedule UI; image-gen
  metadata + **independent** image approval/rejection.
- Social/marketing export generator (**export-only first** — parent §0.3).
- GA4 + GSC **batch-dump** import (cost budget + Oracle DB review).
- SEO recommendations engine + dashboard (proposals only).
- `lp_events` batch-ingest SEO extensions + DB migrations/rollups.
- Alerting + runbooks.

## Phasing

Tracks the parent's 8-phase strangler-fig (parent §10): P0 contracts/
inventory → P1 publisher dry-run → (P2 is mss) → P3 FAQ MVP → P4
auto-blog MVP → P5 GA/GSC loop → P6 canary → P7 cleanup. The **FAQ MVP
(P3) is the smallest shippable slice**; do it first. Tag commits with
`Phase: P<n>`.

# Customer check-in → Sweed link, enriched admin view, cashier live view — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md). Re-read the parent
> before starting any phase — this child epic is a thin index over
> the parent's design, not a re-statement of it.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#12
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: B<n>`
> trailer so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post per-
> phase progress on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

Everything in the parent EPIC_PLAN.md §3, phases B1–B5:

- **B1.** Unblock the Sweed find-by-`documentNumber` RPC in
  `helios/src/worker/sweed/customers.ts`. Wire it into the existing
  visitor-scan link worker. Add the person-key-seen-before fast-path
  that lowers `next_probe_at` to `now()` for repeat visitors so the
  link populates sub-second. Retire the
  `NEEDS_OPERATOR_VERIFICATION` comment block.

- **B2.** Migration `041_sweed_customer_profile_snapshots.sql` per
  parent §3-B2 (table + indices). New worker job
  `refreshSweedCustomerProfileSnapshotJob` that computes #purchases
  / total / avg / favorite category / favorite product from the
  existing `sweed_orders` + `sweed_package_snapshots` tables. The
  `>= 3` repeat-count gate for favorites lives in the snapshot
  generator, not in the read path. Scheduled on (a) successful link
  in the link worker, (b) a daily cron tick for linked customers
  whose `snapshotted_at` is older than 24h.

- **B3.** Augment the existing `/admin/customers/check-ins` page
  (alias of `/admin/visitors/scans`) loader and table component
  with: `# Purchases`, `Avg $`, `Total $`, `Favorite Category`,
  `Favorite Product`. Single LEFT JOIN through `visitor_scan_links`
  → `sweed_customer_profile_snapshots`; NO N+1. Favorite columns
  blank when snapshot's repeat-count gate isn't met.

- **B4.** New cashier live view at
  `/admin/checkout-counter/check-ins` (final URL is operator's call
  — see parent §7). Components:
  - `CheckoutCounterPage.tsx` — landscape-tablet layout, reuses
    the visitor-scans table component in `privacyRedacted` mode.
  - `privacyRedacted` table mode: forces `expanded=off`, renders
    `FirstName L.` only, hides DOB / address / phone / email /
    id_num. Sweed aggregate columns (B3) stay visible (not PII).
  - New SSE route `GET /api/check-ins/stream` on the existing
    `helios-server` fastify app. In-process `EventEmitter`
    published-to by the existing webhook handler (after the link
    row is seeded) and by the link worker (after `linked` /
    `ambiguous` / `no_match` transitions). On connect: one bounded
    "last 20" query (no polling thereafter). See parent §0 — this
    is the DB-cost cap.
  - Two chime assets bundled at
    `helios/src/client/assets/audio/chime-first.ogg` and
    `chime-returning.ogg`. Click-to-enable overlay handles the
    browser autoplay policy + Notification permission in one
    gesture.
  - Browser Notification API on each event with the redacted name,
    first-vs-returning, last-visit date.

- **B5.** Auth gate on the cashier route + SSE endpoint that
  restricts to user `internal.shared_accounts@freshlybaked.nyc`.
  When that user lands on `/admin/customers/check-ins`, redirect
  to the cashier page so the un-redacted view is unreachable from
  their session. When they're on the admin check-ins page (e.g.
  via redirect race), apply the same name-redaction the cashier
  page uses — the operator was explicit about this:
  > the customer list should be like this as well on this
  > particular page, for enhanced privacy.

## Out of scope (deferred / other epics)

- Sweed CRM customer **creation** when there's no documentNumber
  match — owned by the existing customer-sentiment capture flow.
- Multi-tenant cashier RBAC beyond the one shared-account email.
- Host-level config (no `nixos-sbc` changes; nginx `proxy_buffering
  off` for the SSE location is an in-repo deploy concern, handled
  in `automation` alongside B4).

## Per-phase DB-cost statements (canon §3 — REQUIRED)

Every commit landing a phase MUST include, in the commit body:

```
DB-cost:
  per-request: <op count + index used>
  per-day:     <upper bound for steady-state>
  index:       <name(s) the path relies on>
  caching:     <TTL / pub-sub / materialisation>
```

Reviewers should reject phase commits missing this block.

## Phases — task-dag

Use the existing `scripts/task-dag` flow:

```
scripts/task-dag frontier --issue=<child-epic issue number>
# pick a leaf, do real work, then:
scripts/task-dag complete <task-sha>
git push origin HEAD:master
```

Never create empty tombstone commits for new work. Phase order is
strictly **B1 → B2 → B3 → B4 → B5**; B3 and B4 can be cut from the
same change set if both rely on B2 already being live (which they do).

## Operator pre-reqs (do not implement until done)

- Sweed session UUID pasted into the token pool at
  https://helios.freshlybaked.us/config/sweed/sessions. The new
  token supplied with the parent request is the one to paste.
  Without an active pool token, B1's Sweed RPC will return
  `Auth expired` and the worker will retire the env-fallback path.
slots.delegationNote: B1 unblocks A4 in FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#31; B2–B5 build the customer-facing UX. Phase order is strict: B1 → B2 → B3 → B4 → B5.

# task-dag child epic — eliminate hand-built JSON (and YAML)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#44](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/44)
> — "Our critical tooling should NOT be constructing json by hand."
> **Parent epic plan:** [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md).
> **Governing rule:** canon `docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md` "Code
> standards" — *never hand-build / hand-parse / hand-validate JSON or YAML*.

## Scope

Replace every remaining hand-built JSON (and YAML) emitter/parser in the
task-dag runtime with proper serialization. The CLI already ships
jq-preferring primitives (`json_escape`, `json_str_or_null`,
`json_int_or_null`, `json_number_or_null`, `json_str_array`); the JSON fix
is to route the raw emitters through them (or through `jq -n --arg …`), not
to invent new machinery.

### Offenders (survey 2026-07-08; re-grep + expand before implementing)

1. **`scripts/task-dag` — raw-interpolation `echo "{…}"` emitters.**
   Many `--json` result lines interpolate shell variables straight into
   the JSON string, e.g.
   - `echo "{\"ok\":false,\"reason\":\"not-claimed\",\"sha\":\"$task_sha\"}"`
   - the `claim-root` / `release-root` result objects that interpolate
     `$claimer`, `$claimer_host`, `$existing_claimer`, `$existing_host`,
     `$existing_when` (untrusted strings from commit/ref metadata),
   - the `deps`/`allMet`/`blockedAncestor` object assembled with a series
     of `echo` lines,
   - the `validate` summary object,
   - the `breakdown` result object / per-task array entries,
   - the reap `printf '{…}'` object (`deadReason` can contain arbitrary
     text).
   Numeric fields (`issue`, `claimerPid`, `ttlHours`) must go through
   `json_int_or_null` / `json_number_or_null` (raw interpolation of a
   malformed `Issue: #41abc` is exactly the outage the helpers were added
   to prevent). String fields go through `json_escape` / `json_str_or_null`.

2. **The CI chain/repair module family** —
   `scripts/task-dag.d/ci-chains.sh` and `scripts/task-dag.d/ci-repair.sh`.
   `_cichain_jstr` is a private pure-bash escaper (no jq preference) and the
   CI-chain status/CAS-result objects plus `ci-repair.sh`'s classifier /
   tree-fix-outcome / verify report objects are assembled with
   `printf '{"…":"%s"}'`. Fold these onto the shared jq-preferring helpers
   (or `jq -n`); drop the duplicate escaper.

3. **JWT payloads** in `scripts/operator-blocked-dashboard-publish.sh`
   (and the mirrored `.github/scripts/materialise-child-epics.sh`) —
   `printf '{"iat":%d,"exp":%d,"iss":"%s"}' … "$APP_ID"`. Low risk
   (numeric/APP_ID) but still hand-built; emit with `jq -n` for
   consistency. The constant `{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT"}` header is a
   fixed literal and may stay.

4. **YAML: the `delegated_to` block** in
   `scripts/task-dag.d/cross-repo.sh` (`_xrepo_upsert_delegated_block` and
   its readers) is a bespoke, hand-rolled YAML parser/renderer. #44
   explicitly covers YAML, so convert this to `yq` (or a proper YAML
   library) for both emit and parse. Note the canon Bash-default / no-Python
   rule: prefer `yq`.

Re-grep before implementing — treat the list above as a starting point,
not an exhaustive census:

```sh
rg -n -e '\\"[a-zA-Z_]+\\":' -e "printf '\{" -e 'echo .*\{.*:.*\}' scripts/ .github/
```

## Constraints (critical infra)

- **Do not change the commit/ref format or the *shape* of any `--json`
  output** — only how the same bytes are produced. The dispatcher and
  golden fixtures depend on the exact keys/values. This is a correctness
  refactor, not a format change.
- **Oracle design + change review is mandatory** (canon
  `QUALITY_GATES.md` "Critical-infrastructure changes"): task-dag is the
  dispatch/claim core.
- Add/extend tests so a regression (an unescaped field) is caught: the
  existing `tests/task-dag/*-json.sh` harnesses should assert the output
  parses under `jq -e` for inputs containing quotes/backslashes/newlines.
- Keep `validate --strict` green; run the `tests/task-dag/run-all.sh`
  suite as the final gate.

## Acceptance

- No remaining hand-built JSON/YAML in `scripts/` or `.github/scripts/`
  (constant no-interpolation literals excepted).
- All existing tests plus new adversarial-value tests pass.
- The **final** commit on `virusdave/task-dag` `master` that demonstrates
  this child epic's acceptance criteria are met carries
  `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#44`. Intermediate commits MUST NOT carry
  that trailer unless the child epic is already fully satisfied. (task-dag's
  own `complete` adds the peer `Issue:`/`URL:` trailer for completion
  attribution.)
slots.delegationNote: Route all --json emitters and the delegated_to YAML block through jq/yq or the CLI's existing json_* helpers; do not change output shape.
slots.title: Eliminate hand-built JSON (and YAML) in the task-dag CLI and scripts
