# Low-inventory review page — `automation` (Helios) child epic

> Thin index over the authoritative parent plan
> [`docs/epics/low-inventory-review/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md) in
> `virusdave/top-level`. Where this and the parent disagree, the parent
> wins — fix this doc. Tracking issue:
> [virusdave/top-level#32](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/32).
> **APPROVED — parent [§6](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#6-blocking-decisions-operator)
> resolved by the operator 2026-07-06, then write model SIMPLIFIED
> 2026-07-09 (parent
> [§6.11](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#611-2026-07-09-operator-simplification-no-quantity-writes-move-to-a-configurable-not-for-sale-room)).**
> Materialises via the issue #32 decomposition (the
> `Materialise-Child-Epic: FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` trailer group under
> `Parent-Issue: #32`).
>
> **⚠️ 2026-07-09 supersede (parent §6.11).** Helios **never adjusts Sweed
> stock quantities** for this feature. Both short-count and zero-count
> perform the **same reversible action**: move the affected package(s) to a
> **UI-configurable NOT FOR SALE room** (default = per-site "Hold for Dave
> inspection"). This **retires** the set-quantity write, the METRC ceiling,
> the counted-more readback, the write-mode A/B model, and the mandatory
> two-stage `Inventory Count Verification` room. The operator's other answers
> still apply (per-package barcode/METRC-scan granularity, first-to-zero
> location verification, a universal 24h one-offs link, a barcode-scan mobile
> review queue on the roadmap). Building still proceeds phased, safest-first;
> **no write to live Sweed inventory** (now only a reversible room transfer)
> ships outside operator-approved, feature-flagged, single-site-pilot
> rollout.

## Scope (Helios only)

A new per-site Helios operator page that lists SKUs with **`1 <= combined
FOR-SALE stock <= N`** (`N` admin-configurable, default 2; combined-0
excluded), grouped by warehousing location, lets an operator enter the
**actual physical count per package** (barcode/METRC scan), and on an
operator-confirmed short/zero count reacts with a `page-dave` (short `-p 2`,
zero `-p 3`) and **moves the affected package(s) to a UI-configurable NOT FOR
SALE room** (parent §6.11; default = per-site "Hold for Dave inspection") via
the existing `move-package-to-inspection` / `stockTransferService` transfer.
**Helios does not adjust Sweed stock quantities** — short and zero count use
the same reversible transfer, differing only in page priority. Complementary
to Sweed cycle counting and to Helios' existing velocity-based reordering
analytics — do **not** duplicate them.

## First task: confirm the in-repo facts

The parent §1 cites likely files from a read-only audit; verify each before
coding (the top-level repo cannot build Helios):

- `src/server/db/schema/sweedPackageSnapshots.sql` + the
  `sweed_package_current` view — columns `available_qty`, `stock_location`,
  `internal_track_code`, `dealer_id`, `product_sku`, `inventory_item_id`.
- `src/server/metrics/_real/sweedPackageSnapshotsQueries.ts` — the shared
  `FOR SALE%` / `available_qty` low-stock query helpers to **reuse**.
- `src/server/routes/catalogMaintenance.ts` +
  `src/server/catalog/maintenance.ts` — the existing
  `move-package-to-inspection` write path (`store.inventory.item.transfer`
  into `NOT FOR SALE - Hold for Dave inspection`) to reuse for the
  zero-count action.
- `src/server/catalog/stockTransferService.ts` — the transfer primitive,
  now the **sole write path** (parent §6.11): used for both the short-count
  and the zero-count move into the configurable NOT FOR SALE room.
- **No trade-sample set-quantity spike needed (parent §6.11).** The former
  "FIND FIRST: locate & generalize the 'reduce trade sample to zero' write"
  task is **dropped** — Helios no longer adjusts Sweed quantities, so there
  is no set-quantity write, no METRC-ceiling handling, and no counted-more
  readback to build.
- `src/worker/runtime/pageDave.ts` + `src/server/routes/warehouseLocations.ts`
  — `pageDave({ priority })`; the resolved page levels are literal ntfy `-p`:
  short `-p 2`, zero `-p 3`, counted-0-but-held `-p 4` (parent §6.2/§6.8).
- `src/shared/contracts/domain/pendingPurchases.ts` — site→dealer resolution.
- `src/server/app/buildServer.ts` + `src/client/app/router.tsx` — route
  registration; mirror the Catalog Maintenance / Inventory Procurement
  pages.
- `src/client/routes/catalog/LiveBarcodeScanner.tsx` and
  `WarehouseLocationsPage.tsx` — reuse the canonical camera scanner and its
  manual/hardware-scanner fallback pattern; do not create a second scanner.
- **Confirm (parent §6.5/§6.11):** the configured NOT FOR SALE destination
  room per site — default `Hold for Dave inspection` (fuzzy name match, IDs
  differ). Wire the destination as an **admin/UI-configurable setting**
  (parent §6.11), not a hardcoded name; the operator will later create a
  dedicated NOT FOR SALE location and repoint it. No new `Inventory Count
  Verification` room is needed unless the operator opts into the optional
  second-confirm stage.
- **Confirm (parent §6.8):** `current_qty` vs `available_qty` as the
  reconciliation baseline, and the behavior of `transferReservedItems: false`
  when a counted-zero package still has `hold_qty > 0`.
- **Design (parent §6.10/§6.11):** the **24h one-offs link** on every page,
  the **first-transition-to-zero** verification (last-known location code +
  METRC-tag suffix), and — only if the operator opts in — an optional
  non-admin second-confirm stage (parent §6.11; not required for safety since
  the move is reversible). The actual representative **mobile/tablet UI and
  notification templates must be Oracle-reviewed before every
  operator-facing phase first lands, including P0.**

## Operator workflow acceptance (binding)

The page optimizes for a mobile operator walking one physical location at a
time. Keep the current item and likely next action visible; collapse
methodology/provenance; never make the operator return to a dashboard to find
the result of the action they just took.

1. **Queue:** one explicit site, grouped in practical shelf/room walking order;
   current and next unresolved package remain visible. Handle populated,
   empty, loading, error, stale, long-name, multi-location, and multi-package
   states without horizontal scrolling or explanatory clutter.
2. **Scan:** reuse `LiveBarcodeScanner` plus Warehouse Locations' camera,
   manual-entry, still-photo, and hardware-scanner patterns. Scanning never
   writes. Exactly one package becomes active; duplicate, unreadable, unknown,
   ambiguous, wrong-site, camera-denied, and camera-unavailable scans recover
   inline without losing queue position.
3. **Count:** enter/tally physical count, then show a distinct equal, short,
   zero, over, or held result. A captured discrepancy remains visibly
   unresolved as **count recorded, package still for sale, transfer pending**;
   do not suppress it or call it reconciled.
4. **Review:** inventory changes require a separate package-specific
   confirmation showing site, product, METRC suffix, Sweed and physical
   counts, source room, configured destination, and that the **whole package**
   leaves the customer menu. No bulk transfer and no fallback-all-lots
   behavior. A stale live package stops, refreshes, and requires reconfirmation.
5. **Recover and continue:** prevent double-submit; distinguish in-flight,
   conflict, timeout/unknown outcome, partial success, success, undo success,
   and undo failure. An unknown outcome is verified before retry. Success
   stays inline with destination, audit status, undo, 24h detail link, and the
   next package action.
6. **Accessibility:** no horizontal scrolling at 320/375px phone or
   768/1024px tablet widths; 44px minimum primary targets; labeled numeric
   input; keyboard/hardware-scanner completion; focus-managed dialogs,
   visible focus, `aria-live` status, and no color-only meaning.
7. **Oracle evidence before first exposure:** actual phone and tablet renders
   for every queue state in item 1; scanner idle/active/denied/unknown/
   ambiguous/matched; equal/short/zero/over/held and count-pending;
   confirmation/in-flight/conflict/unknown-outcome/success/undo; unavailable
   destination; first-to-zero verification; admin room configuration; each
   batched `page-dave` template; and active/expired 24h detail views. Oracle
   must return APPROVE for the relevant set before that surface lands.

## Phases (parent §5 — production-safety order)

- **P0 — read-only review page.** Per-site `1 <= combined FOR-SALE <= N`
  table (admin-configurable `N`, default 2; combined-0 excluded), grouped by
  warehousing location, from `sweed_package_current` (reuse the shared
  queries). No inputs/writes/pages. `viewer`/metrics-grant read. Safe to
  deploy under normal Helios deploy.
- **P1a — physical-count entry + audit record (no write, no page).**
  Per-package physical-count input (barcode/METRC scan, parent §6.3); write
  the reconciliation record (P3 table). Captured discrepancies remain pending
  and visible until resolved. `editor` grant.
- **P1b — configure and validate the NOT FOR SALE target (no inventory
  write).** Admin/UI setting per site (default = "Hold for Dave inspection").
  Resolve and display the exact site/room before transfer enablement; fail
  closed when unavailable. Optional second confirm only if the operator opts
  in.
- **P1c — short-count page + move-to-NOT-FOR-SALE (write-gated).** On
  operator-confirmed `0 < count < Sweed`: `page-dave -p 2` (parent §6.2) +
  **move the affected package(s) to the configurable NOT FOR SALE room**
  (parent §6.11, default = per-site "Hold for Dave inspection") via
  `move-package-to-inspection` / `stockTransferService`, capturing
  from-room/qty undo data in the audit row. **No Sweed quantity write** (the
  set-quantity path, METRC ceiling, write-mode A/B, and counted-more readback
  are all retired — parent §6.11). `editor` grant; write path
  operator-rollout-gated. Shares its primitive with P2.
- **P2 — zero-count action + first-to-zero verification.** On
  operator-confirmed `count == 0`: `page-dave -p 3` (§6.2) + move to the
  **same configurable NOT FOR SALE room** via `move-package-to-inspection`
  (parent §6.11, site-equivalent room, parent §6.5); the counted-0-but-held
  edge pages `-p 4` + 24h one-offs (parent §6.8); add the
  first-transition-to-zero verification (last-known location code + METRC
  suffix, parent §6.6). `editor` grant; operator-rollout-gated. Shares the
  P1c transfer primitive.
- **P3 — reconciliation audit + no-renag.** Helios table (site, SKU/package,
  Sweed-qty snapshot, operator count, action, actor, ts); suppress
  resolved lines for a configurable window; never suppress captured-but-
  unresolved discrepancies; per-SKU history. Its schema lands with P1a.
- **P4 — mobile review queue (roadmap, parent §6.10).** Non-admin
  barcode-scan re-confirmation queue on the P1a/P3 foundation.
- **Cross-cutting:** every page carries a **24h one-offs link** to an
  info-dense mobile/tablet-first operator view; that UI **must pass an Oracle
  review before first exposure, including P0** (parent §5.1/§6.10).

## Verification

- Build/lint/typecheck green.
- P0: unit test the `combined FOR-SALE <= N` query against seeded snapshot
  rows; grouping renders for both a parseable shelf code and a stock-room
  fallback.
- UI: focused interaction/accessibility tests cover the full binding workflow,
  including scan recovery, no-side-effect count capture, package-specific
  confirmation, stale and unknown-outcome handling, undo, and next-item
  continuation. Capture and Oracle-review the representative evidence set
  before first exposure.
- P1/P2: discrepancy-classification unit tests mapping short/zero count to
  the **shared move-to-NOT-FOR-SALE transfer** (parent §6.11) at the correct
  page priority; the transfer reuses the existing verify-live-item +
  restore-on-failure guarantees; the configurable destination room resolves
  per site (falls back to `Hold for Dave inspection`); `pageDave` asserted
  with the agreed priority (mocked — **never** a real page in tests, canon
  no-prod-resources-in-tests). No test performs a Sweed quantity write (that
  path is retired — parent §6.11).
- P3: audit row on every action; suppression within the window.
- Each landing commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#32`.
- P1/P2 prod rollout is operator-gated: `self-deploy-helios` under explicit
  approval, then a live probe on one known low-stock SKU per site.

## Coordination

Single repo — no cross-repo contract. The parent §6 decisions are
**resolved** (operator, 2026-07-06) and the write model was **simplified**
2026-07-09 (parent §6.11 — no quantity writes, move to a configurable NOT FOR
SALE room), so all phases are unblocked to build. The remaining gates are
operational, not decisional: (i) the mobile/tablet UI must pass an **Oracle
review** before each operator-facing surface first lands, including P0
(parent §5.1/§6.10);
(ii) every live-Sweed room-transfer phase (P1c/P2) ships only under
**operator rollout approval**, feature-flagged, single-site pilot first
(Midtown). One small confirm remains for build time: whether the operator
wants the optional non-admin second-confirm stage (parent §6.11) — it is not
required for safety.
slots.delegationNote: Build the phased per-site low-inventory queue, canonical barcode-scan count flow, audit trail, configurable reversible NOT-FOR-SALE transfer, batched mobile detail alerts, explicit rollout/stability verification, and Oracle-approved representative operator UI states defined by the parent and child plans.
slots.title: Helios low-inventory physical-count review and reconciliation

# Agent-waste review queue — `github-worker` child epic: export pending-review backlog to top-level (pull-rebase-retry)

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#34](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/34)
> — "Drastically reduce AMP agent costs while retaining quality" (Lever D).
> **Authoritative design:**
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` → `docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/blob/master/docs/helios/agent-waste-review/RESOLVED_DESIGN.md)
> ("Remaining work" #2) and
> [`docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/amp-cost-reduction.md)
> §5 (Lever D).
> **Producer schema (this repo):**
> [`docs/AGENT_WASTE.md`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker/blob/master/docs/AGENT_WASTE.md)
> (`agent-waste backlog --format json`).
>
> **Completion signalling (required):** every implementation commit landing on
> [`Nicponskis/github-worker`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/github-worker)
> `master` that satisfies part of this child epic MUST carry
> `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#34`. Because #34 has **several** child epics,
> the **final** satisfying commit MUST ALSO carry this issue's own
> `Issue: #<this-issue-number>` (or `URL:`) trailer so the top-level completion
> aggregator attributes it to *this* child epic.

## 1. Goal

Add a github-worker-side **exporter** that publishes the **pending-review**
agent-waste backlog (the tiny/rare unknown/free-form-`id` items needing a human
eye) to the committed backlog file in `top-level` defined by child epic #1, so
Helios can read it via its read-only mirror (D1/D2). The github-worker
dispatcher (OS user `amp-local`) already holds push creds to `top-level`, so this
reuses an existing, operator-blessed capability.

## 2. Scope

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Exporter** | A step (in the dispatcher / a scheduled hook — reuse the existing worker-loop plumbing) that reads the local pending-review backlog (`agent-waste backlog --format json`, from `docs/AGENT_WASTE.md`) and writes it to the `top-level` backlog file (format from child epic #1). |
| **Raw store stays local** | Only the **pending-review** stream is exported. The chatty raw NDJSON observation store stays **local** to the dispatcher under its state dir (design §5.1); it is never pushed. Do not conflate the two streams. |
| **Pull-rebase-retry on push** | The exporter commits + pushes to `top-level master` using **pull-rebase-retry** (operator-blessed, low volume) so it never leaves piled-up local commits when Helios's promote path lands adjacent commits. Reject no-op writes (nothing changed → no commit). |
| **Idempotent + fail-safe** | Re-running with an unchanged backlog is a no-op. Push/network failure is loud-but-non-fatal (log + retry next cycle); it never blocks dispatch or a serving path. |

## 3. Constraints / invariants (carry forward)

- **Never export the raw observation store**; only the pending-review backlog.
- **`note` is display-only** and never becomes advisory `text` anywhere in the
  pipeline (the promote path in child epic #4 enforces the write side; the
  exporter must not smuggle it into `advisories.yaml`).
- **Pull-rebase-retry** on every push; **reject no-op** commits; reset local
  commit on push failure and refetch/rebase before retry — the same discipline
  the applyConfig pattern uses.
- Runtime stays **PAT-free** — use the dispatcher's existing `top-level` push
  credential (the machine credential owned by `amp-local`), not a new PAT.

## 4. Dependencies / ordering

- **Depends on** child epic #1 (`top-level` backlog file format — the exporter's
  write target). Start after #1's format lands.
- **Feeds** child epic #3 (Helios reads the exported file).

## 5. Acceptance

- A pending-review backlog recorded locally is reflected in the `top-level`
  backlog file within one export cycle, via a pull-rebase-retry push, with no-op
  writes rejected and failures non-fatal.
- The raw observation store is verifiably **not** exported.
- Deterministic, prod-resource-free test of the exporter (fixture backlog → file
  content), no test points at prod resources. Attach an Agent Gate Record.

## 6. Safety / rollback

Additive: a new exporter path writing one committed file in `top-level`. Rollback
is disabling the exporter (a dispatcher flag) and/or reverting the file. No
serving service is restarted; pushes go to `master` normally (no `self-deploy`
needed for a data-file push). No prod DB, no schema.
slots.delegationNote: RESOLVED_DESIGN Remaining-work #2; depends on child epic 1 (backlog file format).

>

> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10

> parent issue.

## What this epic does

Rewrites this repo's root `AGENTS.md` to consume **canonical agent
rules** from `virusdave/top-level` instead of duplicating them
locally. The canonical rules are short, imperative, and updated in one
place — so all our repos stay in sync without manual mirroring.

## Step 0 — fetch and read canon BEFORE doing anything

The canonical agent rules live in
`virusdave/top-level : docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md` on `master`. **Read
them first** (and use the same mechanism in your final AGENTS.md
header — see Step 2):

```sh
canon_ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
              /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$canon_ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … internalize the rules — they govern this rewrite …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$canon_ws"
```

Pay particular attention to: ephemeral checkouts for your own work,
the "Canon update interrupt" in §0, the operational-reality §5, and
the §6 contract for what peer `AGENTS.md` must contain.

## Step 1 — ephemeral checkout of THIS repo

```sh
ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
        /home/amp-local/src/automation --label agent-canon)
cd "$ws"
```

Adjust the source path if `automation` lives elsewhere on this host
(`/home/amp-local/src/automation` is the standard).

## Step 2 — rewrite `AGENTS.md` to the pointer model

Open the existing root `AGENTS.md`, audit it for what to keep, then
replace its contents with this exact structure. Fill in the
repo-specific section from your audit.

```markdown

**MANDATORY FIRST READ — agent canon.** Before doing anything in this
repo, fetch and read the latest canonical agent rules:

```sh

        /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … apply the rules …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$ws"
```

That file is authoritative across **all** our repos. Re-read on every
agent session — it changes. If anything in this file conflicts with
canon, **canon wins** — fix the stale prose here.

The rest of this file lists only **automation-specific** instructions.

---

## Repo purpose

<one-paragraph summary: this repo is the Helios codebase + adjacent
ops tooling, deployed to vps-nixos-3>

<the canonical deploy procedure for this repo. Per the operator's
recurring complaint, the canonical mechanic is `self-deploy*` /

<repo-specific build & test commands, language versions, etc.>

<if this repo uses task-dag, any conventions specific to it; otherwise

needs to work here: exact deploy commands, service names, log paths,

repo-specific cross-references, contact info.

## Step 4 — what to DELETE (canon covers it)

Delete and do NOT restate any of:

- "Never SSH to self" / "SSH port" rules
- "Use ephemeral checkout" / "do not edit shared `~/src`" rules
- "Default to `master`, no feature branches" rule
- Bash vs Python / shebang style / typed-code rules
- Performance budgets (UI ≤500ms, DB ≤125ms)
- "Use Oracle / painter / Bedrock LLMs" rules
- Group-writable file rule

- Generic cross-repo child-epic trailer flow

If you find any of those in the current `AGENTS.md`, **delete** the
prose and rely on canon. If a rule there contradicts canon, canon
wins — flag the conflict in your commit message.

## Step 5 — target size & sanity check

The rewritten file should be **≤ 120 lines**. If it's bigger, you're
probably restating canon — re-audit and trim. If it's much shorter
than the existing file but still has all operational facts, that's
the correct outcome.

Run a final read-through asking: "could a brand-new agent who has

## Scope (FB-US thin runtime)

Make the `branding/` family's `SLUG` segment **opaque**, reusing the exact
`buildFreshlyBakedUsOpaquePublicRef` helper already powering
`compare/`/`conquest/`. The brand name must disappear from every
crawler-visible URL, with **zero 404s** for already-approved Google-Ads
`/0` final URLs.

**BINDING:** do **not** change the canonical `/SITE/PURPOSE/SLUG/NUM`
schema, the `/0` distributor, or the `utm_content=NUM:N` contract (parent
§0, [#13 §6.1](../../../unified-landing-engine/EPIC_PLAN.md)). Only the
`branding` `SLUG` representation changes.

## First task: confirm the in-repo facts

The top-level repo cannot read mss source. Begin by verifying the exact
symbols (the parent names the likely locations):

- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/lib/purpose-families.ts` — the brand registry,
  `MAX_VARIANT_BY_PURPOSE`, and `buildFreshlyBakedUsOpaquePublicRef`
  (signature, determinism, whether it is family-scoped or global).
- the `branding/` route segment — `generateStaticParams`, page param
  parse, and the registry/NUM guard.
- `apps/freshlybakedus-site/middleware.ts` — existing legacy-form `308`
  redirects (the pattern P1 extends) and the `/0` re-roll/rewrite.

## Phases (parent §5 — production-visible order)

- **P0 — dual-accept.** Route accepts **both** literal and opaque `SLUG`;
  reuse the opaque helper for `branding`; `generateStaticParams` builds
  opaque pages (+ transitional literal pages so nothing 404s yet). Page
  resolves opaque→row; the registry/NUM guard `notFound()`s unknown refs
  and out-of-range `NUM`. No emitted-surface flip yet.

  (operator chose `308`, parent §6.1 — **not** `noindex`+canonical),
  same-origin, full query preserved (`gclid`/`gbraid`/`wbraid` + UTMs +
  ValueTrack), `/0` redirect-chain handled intentionally (parent §5.1).

  the `branding/` sitemap entries emit **opaque only**, in the **same
  deploy** so the literal + opaque pages are never both indexable. (P1
  already protects literals.)

  (and FB-NYC's) URL `SLUG` source and confirm whether any literal
  brand/cannabis token can appear in a crawler-visible URL. Operator does
  not expect a leak but asked us to verify. Deliver the findings; only if
  a real leak is found does it expand into further opaque migration
  (re-scoped with the operator). Does **not** block the branding work.
- **P4 (with operator/Helios).** Operator runs the one-off Ads-Editor CSV
  final-URL **migrate** (parent §6.2) using the Helios-emitted
  literal→opaque mapping; canary one `SITE/branding` pair; monitor
  404s + Google-Ads disapprovals; deploy under operator approval. `308`
  back-compat stays in place through and after the migration.

## Verification

- Build green with opaque `generateStaticParams`.
- Redirect unit/e2e: literal→opaque preserves `gclid`/UTMs; redirect-chain
  (literal `/0` → opaque) is the intended single hop or the accepted
  two-hop `308`+`307`, correct statuses, `/0` re-roll stays `no-store`.
- **URL-emission audit test:** no literal brand name in any internal link
  / canonical / sitemap entry for `branding/`.
- **Opaque-ref stability test:** checked-in `brand-id → opaque-ref` test
  vectors (the cross-repo contract — see Coordination); ref derives from

- Each landing commit carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#19`.

## Coordination

The opaque scheme **must** match Helios (`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`)
output exactly. Don't rely on "same code in two repos" — publish a shared
**contract** (checked-in test vectors / generated manifest / importable
package) that both repos prove against in CI. Agree it before opaque ads
are emitted (parent P3 depends on this).

> Owning child of

## Scope owned by this repo

- **agenix secret** `secrets/veriscan-webhook-token.age` on
  `vps-nixos-3` whose plaintext is the 256-bit hex bearer token
  documented in the agent comment on
  [#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9).
- **`helios-server.service` wiring** — extend the existing systemd
  unit's `EnvironmentFile=` (or equivalent agenix-template
  generated file) to include `VERISCAN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN=<plaintext>`.
  No new unit; the existing helios-server reads it from env at
  startup.
- **Confirm nginx routing** — `helios.freshlybaked.us` already
  proxies to the helios-server backend; verify that the existing
  `location /` (or equivalent catch-all) covers `/wh/*` without
  needing a new server block.  If a path-specific block is needed
  (e.g. to bump body-size limits for VeriScan attachments), add it
  here.
- **Body-size headroom** — VeriScan envelopes can include base64
  payloads (the `PhotoBase64` field is obsolete but still possible);
  ensure nginx `client_max_body_size` on the helios vhost is ≥ 4MB.

## Out of scope

- Helios app code, DB migration, webhook handler, admin page,
  backfill CLI — `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`.
- VeriScan-side webhook configuration — operator.
- Rotation procedure for the bearer token — documented in the
  parent EPIC_PLAN.md §"Bearer token"; mechanical rotation is a
  follow-up if needed.

## Phases

- **N1.** Add the agenix secret and wire it into helios-server's
  environment.  Restart `helios-server` once the FreshlyBakedNYC/automation A1
  release is also live so the env var is consumed by code that
  reads it.  Until then, the env var simply sits unused.
- **N2.** (Conditional) nginx body-size or path-specific tweak if
  the smoke-test in `automation` A1 reveals a default-size
  limitation.  Likely a no-op on the existing config.

## Cross-repo dependencies

- N1 has no upstream dependency.  It unblocks `automation` A1's
  prod deployment (A1 code can be developed and unit-tested
  without N1).
- N2 is reactive — only land if A1 testing surfaces a need.

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. N1 has a landing commit on `nixos-sbc` master carrying
   `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9`.
2. `systemctl show helios-server -p Environment` on `vps-nixos-3`
   (or the equivalent inspection of the rendered agenix template)
   confirms `VERISCAN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` is present.
3. `curl -i -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H
   'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{}'
   https://helios.freshlybaked.us/wh/bx/veriscan/checkin`
   returns the response generated by the helios-server handler
   (post-N1 deployment of A1), not an nginx error.

# mostly-static-sites child epic: durable seven-day temporary pages

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`](../../../../designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md)

## Goal

Raise the one-offs service's bounded maximum lifetime from 24 hours to seven
days, make every serving/control surface agree on manifest-derived liveness,
bound storage growth, migrate publication to daemon-owned uploads, and make the
existing private `/one-offs/` index useful and accessible on phones.

## Required implementation

1. **One liveness contract**
   - Keep the two-hour default; set the daemon and NixOS hard maximum to
     604,800 seconds. Preserve each existing manifest's immutable 24-hour
     ceiling and every shorter caller-selected lifetime.
   - Define one `liveSlots(now)` selector used by direct serving, index, list,
     get, health, extension, boot, and garbage collection. At
     `now >= expiresAtMs`, all reads are absent and extension cannot revive the
     page, regardless of disk cleanup timing.
   - Keep validated manifests as the sole source of truth; never persist or
     cache a second index.

2. **Bounded daemon-owned storage**
   - Implement the binding design's defaults for live slots, files/bytes and
     submissions per slot, 10 GiB data-directory quota, 5 GiB free-space
     reserve, reservation accounting, error codes, and one async mutation
     mutex.
   - Add the streaming upload API and update `scripts/one-offs stage` before
     retiring group-writable `incoming`. Reject symlinks/special files and
     clean abandoned reservations. Publication must fail before visibility if
     any bound would be crossed.
   - Handlers are never daemon children. A socket-activated executor accepts
     only validated slot, submission, and configured-handler IDs over the
     root-owned Unix socket, derives every path itself, selects executables only
     from the fixed Nix allowlist, and runs separately unprivileged with the
     entire one-offs data directory bind-mounted read-only.
   - Fsync atomic manifest writes. Quarantine invalid/partial/orphaned state,
     omit it from serving, garbage-collect it after 24 hours, and expose
     bounded pressure/degraded diagnostics.

3. **Canonical private index**
   - Keep the bare `/one-offs/` route, render a bounded newest-first snapshot
     of live manifests, and preserve tailnet-only serving, Unix-socket control,
     `no-store`, and `noindex, nofollow`.
   - Implement the approved information architecture, privacy language,
     exact/relative expiry, accessible uniquely named actions, collapsed
     technical details, 320-pixel card layout, optional 21+-item progressive
     search, and populated/empty/degraded/error/direct-404 states.
   - Escape all caller labels. Do not add mutation controls or imply that a
     nonce authorizes a tailnet user.

## Tests and review

Use a fake clock and temporary data directory. Cover exact expiry across every
surface, old/new ceilings, restart recovery, partial manifests, upload/create/
submission/GC/index concurrency, reservation rollback, every admission bound,
quota/free-space failures, escaping, bounded 500-item output, 21-item search
and no-script fallback, mobile markup, all states, `HEAD`, headers, and
tailnet rejection. Integration tests must prove handler IDs cannot inject paths
or executables and handlers cannot write slot data. Accessibility coverage
includes landmarks, heading order, focus, unique actions, 44-pixel targets,
light/dark contrast, reduced motion, and 320-pixel width.

Before first exposure, Oracle must review representative rendered output for
populated, empty, expiring, degraded, error, and 404 states on desktop and
mobile and return APPROVE. The approved design review alone is not the final
render review. Before implementation, any nontrivial deviation from the binding
architecture requires a fresh Oracle architecture review; the actual final
critical-infrastructure diff also requires Oracle change review.

## Rollout and rollback

Follow the four-stage client-first migration in the binding design: add the
streaming API; deploy the packaged client everywhere and update canon/runbooks
through canon's update protocol; prove seven days with zero legacy claims plus
streaming canaries; only then remove legacy upload access and enable seven-day
lifetimes. Prove the backing filesystem quota before increasing the cap.

Roll out selectors/index first under the 24-hour maximum through the canonical
mostly-static-sites deployment path. Then enable bounds and seven-day creation,
verify two-hour and seven-day canaries, delete them, and observe two GC cycles.
Rollback first restores a packaged client compatible with the running server.
Before rolling the server behind the streaming API back, restore legacy
`incoming` permissions and the prior canon/runbook in one reviewed change and
pass a short-lived canary, preserving at least one supported publication path
throughout. Then restore 24-hour creation while grandfathering already-created
longer-lived manifests; list their latest expiry rather than deleting or
shortening them.

All satisfying master commits must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```
slots.delegationNote: Unify manifest-derived liveness, add daemon-owned bounded uploads and handler isolation, raise the maximum lifetime to seven days, deliver the approved mobile index, and complete rendered-output review and staged rollout.
slots.title: Ship bounded seven-day one-offs and the canonical live index

        /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … apply the rules …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$ws"
```

That file is authoritative across **all** our repos. Re-read on every
agent session — it changes. If anything in this file conflicts with
canon, **canon wins** — fix the stale prose here.

The rest of this file lists only **helios-parser-configs-specific**
instructions.

---

## Repo purpose

<one-paragraph summary: parser configs consumed by Helios. Helios
auto-refreshes from this repo's master roughly every 60s — meaning a
push is the deploy. There is NO restart step; do not attempt to
restart Helios after editing here.>

## Editing workflow

<authoritative format of the parser config files, validation
commands (whatever lints/round-trips configs before push), and the
"how do I know it took effect" path (Helios logs / dashboard / etc.).>

## Compatibility / breaking changes

<warnings about breaking changes that would break Helios on the next
60s pull — and how to stage them safely (feature flags? new file
alongside old? coordinate with the Helios repo?).>

## Host topology / paths

<deploy targets — the Helios instances that pull from this repo and
the polling interval / endpoint.>
```

## Step 3 — what to KEEP

From the existing AGENTS.md, **keep every operational fact** an agent
needs to work here: exact deploy commands, service names, log paths,
config locations, build/test invocations, architecture diagrams,
repo-specific cross-references, contact info.

## Step 4 — what to DELETE (canon covers it)

Delete and do NOT restate any of:

- "Never SSH to self" / "SSH port" rules
- "Use ephemeral checkout" / "do not edit shared `~/src`" rules
- "Default to `master`, no feature branches" rule
- Bash vs Python / shebang style / typed-code rules
- Performance budgets (UI ≤500ms, DB ≤125ms)
- "Use Oracle / painter / Bedrock LLMs" rules
- Group-writable file rule
- Generic task-dag CLI workflow (the
  `frontier → work → complete → push` loop)
- Generic cross-repo child-epic trailer flow

If you find any of those in the current `AGENTS.md`, **delete** the
prose and rely on canon. If a rule there contradicts canon, canon
wins — flag the conflict in your commit message.

## Step 5 — target size & sanity check

The rewritten file should be **≤ 120 lines**. If it's bigger, you're
probably restating canon — re-audit and trim. If it's much shorter
than the existing file but still has all operational facts, that's
the correct outcome.

Run a final read-through asking: "could a brand-new agent who has
just read canon do real work in this repo using only what's left
here?" If yes, done.

## Step 6 — commit, link, push

```sh
git add AGENTS.md
git commit -m "agents: adopt canon pointer model (Satisfies virusdave/top-level#10)

Replace duplicated cross-repo rules with a mandatory canon-fetch
header per docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md. Repo-specific content
(deploy, paths, services) preserved.

Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10"
git push origin HEAD:<this-repo-default-branch>
```

(Use this repo's default branch — usually `master` or `main`. Do not
open a PR; push directly per the canon working-workflow rule.)

The `Satisfies:` trailer fires the cross-repo completion flow back to
top-level#10.

## Acceptance

- Root `AGENTS.md` opens with the unignorable canon-fetch header.
- Zero duplication of canon content.
- All prior repo-specific operational facts preserved.
- File length ≤ 120 lines.
- Commit includes `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10`.
- Pushed to default branch.

## If you're blocked

- **App not installed / push refused**: stop. Report the exact error
  and your proposed diff to the parent issue
  ([virusdave/top-level#10](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/10)).
- **Repo doesn't have a root `AGENTS.md`**: create one using the same
  template. The acceptance criteria still apply.
- **Existing AGENTS.md has something you don't recognize**: assume
  it's an operator customization and preserve it. When in doubt, ask.
slots.delegationNote: Slice 2 of the agent-canon system, retry with corrected owner. Receiving agent should fetch canon first, then rewrite root AGENTS.md to the inlined pointer-model template; preserve all repo-specific facts.

# Tooling `--help` safety — `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites` child epic

> Parent epic: [virusdave/top-level#47](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/47)
>
> The implementation commit on this repo's master MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47
> ```

## Step 0 — read canon first

Ephemeral checkout of top-level master, then read
[`docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md)
"Code standards" (the `--help` rule) and
[`docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/canon/rules/SAFETY.md)
"Serving services".

## The requirement

Every invocable tool must accept `-h`/`--help`, print usage, and exit `0`
**before any effect** (env-var assertions, locks, network/API calls,
`git` fetch/push, file writes). Handle `--help` first, ahead of all other
option parsing and required-env checks. This applies to bash scripts
**and** to `.ts` entry-point scripts (parse `--help` at the top of the
entrypoint, before any side-effecting work).

## Known violators (audit for more — this list is a starting point)

- `scripts/commit-scan-report.sh`
- `scripts/*.ts` runnable entry-points (e.g. `review-proposals.ts` and
  any other `bun`/`ts-node`-invoked scripts).
- Any other invocable tooling you find during the audit (including the
  `bounce` deploy helper if present — a deploy helper with `--help` must
  not deploy).

## Verifying

Run each tool with `--help` and confirm it prints usage and exits 0 with
no side effects.

## Finalize

Commit with a plain imperative subject (no `feat:`/`fix:` prefix) and the
`Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#47` trailer; push to this repo's default
branch.
slots.delegationNote: Applies to bash and .ts entrypoints; parse --help before side effects.
slots.title: Add innocuous --help to mostly-static-sites build and report scripts

# FBUS FAQ — `automation` (Helios control plane) child epic

> **MATERIALISED 2026-06-15.** The four operator decisions are resolved
> in the parent
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md` §1](../../EPIC_PLAN.md#1-operator-decisions-resolved-2026-06-15)
> and folded into the phases below.
> Owning child of the top-level epic at
> [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md). **Re-read the parent (and the
> parent epic #15) before starting any phase** — this child epic is a
> **thin index** over the parent's design, not a re-statement of it. The
> parent wins on any drift.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#17
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: P<n>` trailer
> so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post per-phase progress
> on the parent issue.

## Role in the epic

Helios (`automation`) is the **FAQ brain**: it owns the FAQ content
source-of-truth, generation + the editorial review/approve workflow, the
sanitized-host denylist, the change-detection/sync loop, governance
checks, and the signed SEO-bundle publisher. mss stays a thin, zero-DB
renderer (peer child epic at `../mostly-static-sites/EPIC_PLAN.md`).

This builds **directly on the FB-NYC SEO FAQ control plane already
shipped under epic #15** (`helios/src/server/seo/faqGenerate.ts`,
`faqContent.ts`, signed bundle publisher). This child epic **extends**,
it does not rebuild.

## ⚠️ Binding constraints (parent §5–§6, canon §1)

- **IRONCLAD human-approval gate (canon §1).** No FAQ draft, sanitized
  variant, family content, or sync-detected change becomes publicly
  visible without a human approving that **specific** content first.
  Generation and the sync loop only ever produce **drafts**
  (`source='generated', approval_id=null`) + fire `page-dave`; they
  **never auto-publish**.
- **Zero `.nyc` / brand / cannabis-meta-term leak in sanitized content.**
  The FBUS sanitized-host denylist must be **stricter than the current
  `RAW_ONLY_TERMS`** (include `flower(s)`, `strain(s)`, etc. if the rule
  is truly zero meta-terms). Approval and bundle publish must both fail
  closed on any leak.
- **`content_sha256` must match the approval ledger** before publish.
- **No invented facts.** Generated answers are drafts; verify against real
  store data (hours, areas, payment, policies) before approval.
- **DB-cost discipline (canon §3).** The sync/change-detection job is a
  recurring background DB workload → written cost budget + Oracle
  DB-efficiency review recorded on the peer issue **before deploy**.

## Subtasks (authoritative list in parent §4 / issue Phases 1 & 5)

**P1 — FAQ source migration + sync loop:**
- One-time import the hardcoded FB-NYC FAQ
  (`mostly-static-sites: apps/freshlybaked-site/app/sites/all/loyalty-faq/page.tsx`)
  into Helios; generate sanitized variants; human review/approve; publish
  the bundle with FAQ sets + widgets.
- Add a **source-key** model (`fbus-global-faq`, `fbus-deliverance-faq`,
  … `fbus-dedicated-faq`).
- Add a **sync/change-detection job** with the **hybrid cadence the
  operator chose** (parent §1 Q3): **(a)** an *approval* of FAQ content
  (FB-NYC / Helios) **drives the bundle push** (event-driven publish of
  already-approved content); **(b)** an *observed* upstream/source change
  — or **creation/modification of content** such as a newly added or
  modified LP family — recomputes `content_sha256`, creates/updates a
  Helios **draft**, and fires **`page-dave`** for review. Path (b)
  **never auto-publishes**; only path (a)'s human approval does. **Guard:**
  path (a) may publish **only** the exact `content_sha256` / sanitized
  content that was approved — a raw/upstream approval that would change the
  FBUS *sanitized* output routes through path (b) (new draft + page), never
  an implicit sanitized publish.
- Coordinate with mss to remove/neutralize the hardcoded FB-NYC FAQ page
  (+ CI guard against reintroduction). FB-NYC then renders raw from the
  bundle.

**P5 — family-contextual generation + governance:**
- Generate per-family drafts (deliverance, conquest, tours, recurse,
  branding, compare — the operator-confirmed current set, parent §1 Q1)
  via the private Bedrock LLM, scoped via widget `route_patterns` that
  **consume the machine-readable LP-family registry artifact** mss P0
  exports (family id, canonical representative route, route patterns,
  sample routes, indexability policy, source SHA) — or, if a generated
  copy is unavoidable, record the exact mss source SHA for provenance.
  Do **not** maintain a second hand-edited family list here.
- Governance before review: item-count cap, answer-length cap,
  forbidden-term scan, duplicate-question check, near-duplicate-answer
  check (token/Jaccard/shingle overlap is fine to start).
- Review page shows: raw + sanitized + rendered FBUS preview + route
  patterns + approx impacted route count + diff vs previous + leak/dup
  warnings.

**P6 — rollout support / monitoring:**
- Provide approved-content status, disabled-content rollback, `page-dave`
  alerts, and any ads-policy lint / reporting needed for rollout
  decisions.
- Coordinate with the operator on the ads-disapproval baseline + window.

## CI gates owned here (parent §7)

(1) sanitized-content leak unit tests; (2) approval rejects any leaked
sanitized answer / shared question / `.nyc` URL; (3) bundle-validation
tests (`content_sha256` must match approval); (9) ads-policy lint.

## Phasing

P1 (source migration + sync) is the unblocking control-plane slice and
goes first; P5 (family content + governance) follows once mss can render.
Tag commits with `Phase: P<n>`.
slots.delegationNote: Helios FAQ brain. BINDING: IRONCLAD human-approval gate (canon section 1) - nothing auto-publishes; FBUS sanitized denylist stricter than RAW_ONLY_TERMS; hybrid sync (approval->publish, change/new-content->draft+page-dave); approval publishes only the approved content_sha256; consume mss P0 LP-family registry artifact. Phases P1, P5.
slots.title: FBUS SEO FAQ - Helios control plane (top-level#17)

# Helios `/metrics` v1.3 rework — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
> for the v1.3 iteration. Authoritative design:
> [`docs/epics/business-metrics/EPIC_PLAN_v1_3_REWORK.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN_v1_3_REWORK.md)
> in the top-level repo. Oracle-approved design thread:
> [T-019e654a-8d2f-74fb-9734-3588f512d8a2](https://ampcode.com/threads/T-019e654a-8d2f-74fb-9734-3588f512d8a2).
>
> The v1 child epic is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#21`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/21)
> (closed); the v1.1 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#28`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/28)
> (closed); the v1.2 rework child is
> [`FreshlyBakedNYC/automation#30`](https://github.com/FreshlyBakedNYC/automation/issues/30)
> (closed). This issue tracks the v1.3 rework only — please do
> not reopen the v1 / v1.1 / v1.2 children.
>
> Every implementation commit landing on `automation` master that
> satisfies any part of this rework MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#7
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: V3<n>`
> trailer (e.g. `Phase: V3'3`) — distinct from v1's `P<n>`,
> v1.1's `R<n>`, and v1.2's `V2<n>` — so per-phase progress
> comments on the parent issue are visually grouped per rework
> iteration.

## Scope owned by this repo

v1.3 lands the **Budtender Performance** tab at
`/metrics/budtenders` per the parent addendum:

1. `/metrics` top-level tab strip (Dashboard | Budtenders) +
   sibling-route shell at `/metrics/budtenders` with sticky
   Core / Advanced sub-tab strip.
2. Core sub-tab panels backed by real data:
   leaderboard, daily cashier-attributed sales trend,
   customer / fulfillment / payment mix, shift productivity,
   dollar-basket upsell lift (same-customer + similar-customer).
3. Advanced sub-tab one-dot-per-cashier scatter with
   axis / color / size / opacity switchers, peer-percentile
   encoding, highlight-subset search, optional quadrant
   reference lines.
4. MISSING DATA cards for the four (five, including basket-
   quantity upsell) operator-asked-for metrics that have no
   real data path today.
5. Consolidated `/api/budtender-analytics` endpoint behind a
   single CTE-chained prepared statement; supporting indexes;
   `compareTo=peer-cohort` extension.
6. Perf measurement, runbook refresh, validation evidence,
   oracle review pass, parent closure package.

Re-read the parent addendum before starting any phase. This
child plan is intentionally a thin index over the parent.

### V3'0 — Scope freeze + route shell + canonical update

- Re-confirm the v1.3-in-scope panel set against the canonical
  v1.2 list (Budtender panels are additive — no headline-
  dashboard panel is removed).
- Extend `MetricDef` types (additive):
  - `area?: 'dashboard' | 'budtenders'` discriminator
    (defaults to `'dashboard'`).
  - `supports.peerCohort?: boolean` (Budtender metrics
    declare `true`; headline metrics unchanged).
  - `blockedBy?: { ingestIssue?: string; column?: string;
    note: string }` on MISSING DATA registry entries.
- `/metrics` top-level tab strip: add a small tab strip below
  the controls bar with "Dashboard" (default; preserves the
  v1.2 entry URL) and "Budtenders" (routes to
  `/metrics/budtenders`). Sticky across scroll like the
  controls bar.
- `/metrics/budtenders` route shell:
  - Page header band with title + coverage badge placeholder
    (wired with live data in V3'1).
  - Sticky "Core | Advanced" sub-tab strip under the global
    controls bar.
  - Empty grid containers for Core (responsive 1/2/3 cols)
    and Advanced (single full-width).
  - Sub-tab choice persists in URL
    (`?sub=core` / `?sub=advanced`).
- Backend skeleton: `GET /api/budtender-analytics` returning a
  well-typed empty payload (`cashier_rows: []`,
  `daily_trend: []`, etc.) with `meta.sources` already
  populated correctly. The CTE chain is added in V3'1 / V3'3.
- Refresh `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics-v1_2-canonical.md` to a
  `…-v1_3-canonical.md` superset that adds an "area" column
  and the `supports.peerCohort` / `blockedBy` columns; update
  the runbook anchor on the parent issue's body.

**Exit criteria**: top-level tab strip renders on `/metrics`;
`/metrics/budtenders` route loads with Core / Advanced empty
grids; the backend endpoint returns a well-typed empty payload;
canonical metric list refreshed; `MetricDef` types extended
(no behavioural change yet).

### V3'1 — Core P0: Leaderboard + Daily Cashier-Attributed Sales Trend

- Backend: first cut of `/api/budtender-analytics` CTE chain
  covering `orders`, `cashier_agg`, and a per-day rollup feeding
  `daily_trend`. Filters honour the global controls (sites,
  range, agg for the trend). Excludes `cashier_user_id IS NULL`
  from `cashier_agg`; surfaces the same count under
  `meta.coverage.unattributed_transactions`. Implemented as a
  single prepared statement to minimise round-trip overhead.
- Frontend:
  - **Budtender Leaderboard** panel: sortable, paginated table
    of cashier rows; default sort `sales desc`. Inline
    horizontal bars per numeric cell; cell colour driven by
    peer-cohort percentile within the visible window; low-n
    rows (`transactions < 20` OR `shift_coverage_minutes <
    120`) dimmed with a "low n" chip. Pagination state lives
    in the URL.
  - **Daily Cashier-Attributed Sales Trend** panel: time
    series in the v1.2 `<MetricChart/>`. Primary = daily
    sales; togglable secondary series = transactions, AOV,
    discount fraction. `cashier_user_id IS NULL` daily totals
    render as a dimmed reference-style series. Tile-level
    annotation pip + hover popover from v1.2 R'5 reused.
  - Unattributed-transactions warning chip in the Leaderboard
    panel header.
- Per-row click on the Leaderboard in v1.3 emits a "single-
  cashier detail view forthcoming" toast and pre-fills
  `highlight=<cashier_id>` for the Advanced sub-tab.

**Exit criteria**: leaderboard + daily trend render with real
production data on `/metrics/budtenders?sub=core`; peer-
percentile colour coding visible; low-n dimming visible on
known-low-volume cashiers; unattributed-transactions chip
appears when `IS NULL` rows exist in the window.

### V3'2 — Core P1: Mix + Shift Productivity

- Extend the consolidated endpoint with the `shift_agg` CTE
  (`sweed_shifts ⋈ orders` on `(dealer_id, employee_id,
  pay_time BETWEEN shift_open_at AND shift_close_at)`) and the
  three mix breakdowns under `mix.customer_segment`,
  `mix.fulfillment`, `mix.payment`.
- Frontend:
  - **Customer / Fulfillment / Payment Mix** cards: three
    stacked percentage bar charts. Per-card toggle switches
    denominator between transactions and sales. Fleet-level
    by default; re-scope to a selected cashier (URL-persisted)
    via overlay over the fleet baseline.
  - **Shift Productivity** card: scatter or ranked bar of
    `transactions / shift_hour`. If
    `shift_agg.coverage_pct < 0.4` on the visible window,
    render the panel as a MISSING DATA card with explicit
    "shift attribution coverage too low" copy + a link to
    the shifts-ingest follow-on issue (see V3'5 for the
    `blockedBy` registry shape).

**Exit criteria**: mix cards render at fleet and per-cashier
levels; overlay-on-leaderboard-select works URL-persistently;
shift productivity card either renders real data or falls
through to a MISSING DATA card with honest copy.

### V3'3 — Core P1: Dollar-Basket Upsell Lift + `compareTo=peer-cohort`

- Extend the consolidated endpoint with the `baseline_lift`
  CTE:
  - Per-order `same_customer_baseline` = leave-one-out average
    of that customer's order totals in the window (filtered to
    known, non-guest, `count >= 2`).
  - Per-order `similar_customer_baseline` = leave-one-out
    average over cohort
    `(guest_flag, first_time_flag, fulfillment_type,
    payment_method)`.
  - Per-cashier rollup is the mean of per-order
    `(order_total - baseline)` with explicit sample-size
    counts.
- Frontend:
  - **Dollar-Basket Upsell Lift** card: diverging horizontal
    bars; toggle in header switches mode between
    `same-customer` and `similar-customer`. Sample-size chip
    per cashier; low-n dimming consistent with leaderboard.
    Colour driven by `desirableDirection: 'up'`.
- `compareTo=peer-cohort` API extension:
  - The Daily Cashier-Attributed Sales Trend panel adopts
    `peer-cohort` as its default `compareTo`.
  - The reference data is the peer-cohort P25 / median / P75
    aggregated within the visible window. Renders as a faint
    band (P25..P75) with the median as a dashed line.
  - Per-panel toggle still offers `prior-period` / `year-over-
    year` / `peer-cohort` / `off`; existing headline panels
    are unchanged.
- V3'0 guardrail tightens: any metric with `area:
  'budtenders'` MUST declare `supports.peerCohort: true`.

**Exit criteria**: dollar-basket lift card renders both modes
on real data; per-cashier sample-size chips and low-n dimming
visible; peer-cohort band renders on the Daily Trend; per-
panel `compareTo` toggle works; guardrail in enforcement.

### V3'4 — Advanced sub-tab: one-dot-per-cashier scatter

- Adapt the v1.2 catalog-style scatter renderer to plot one
  dot per cashier (data source = `cashier_rows` from the
  consolidated endpoint; no extra HTTP).
- **Axis pickers** (X + Y, independent): expose 15+ fields
  per the parent addendum's enumeration, including
  peer-percentile-suffixed (`__pct`) variants computed
  client-side from `cashier_rows`.
- **Color encoding picker** with sensible per-field defaults:
  - Diverging red→gray→green for signed-lift fields.
  - Diverging blue→gray→red for `discount_pct`.
  - Sequential low→high for everything else.
  - "Match X axis" / "Match Y axis" one-click shortcuts.
- **Size encoding picker**: sqrt-scaled by `transactions`
  (default), `sales`, `unique_customers`, or
  `shift_coverage_minutes`.
- **Opacity / confidence**: auto-dim per the rules in the
  parent addendum (lift axes < 10 samples; shift-productivity
  axes < 120 min; volume axes < 20 transactions). Combination
  dimming does not stack below 0.3.
- **Highlight subset**: text input filters by cashier name /
  id / status suffix; matching dots render on top with 2 px
  stroke + label; non-matching dots fade to 0.2 opacity;
  empty input = no highlight. Pre-fills from Leaderboard
  row-click (`?highlight=<cashier_id>`).
- **Reference lines / quadrants** (optional, off by default):
  axis median + P75 lines with quadrant labels.
- **Default first paint**: `X=transactions_per_shift_hour`,
  `Y=aov`, `Color=same_customer_lift`, `Size=transactions`.
- Keyboard: axis pickers reachable via Tab; highlight input
  focusable; quadrant toggle reachable; Escape clears
  highlight.

**Exit criteria**: Advanced scatter renders one-dot-per-cashier
with default encodings on first paint; all pickers work;
highlight-subset filters; pre-fill via `?highlight=` works
from the Leaderboard row-click handoff.

### V3'5 — MISSING DATA cards + summary chip

- Wire `blockedBy` registry entries for the five known-
  missing Budtender metrics:
  1. Product Subset Comparison & Category/Subcategory
     Distribution by Cashier (blocked by line-items ingest).
  2. Returns / Refunds Distribution by Cashier (blocked by
     `sweed_returns` ingest with cashier attribution).
  3. Cashier-Attributed Customer Reviews (blocked by
     invoice → review linkage in `review_submissions`).
  4. Shift Cash +/- (Drawer Reconciliation) (blocked by
     drawer-close actuals).
  5. Basket-Quantity Upsell (blocked by line-items ingest;
     dollar lift shipped in V3'3 as the v1.3 substitute).
- For each, register a MISSING DATA registry entry with:
  - Panel header copy describing what the panel would show.
  - "What's blocked / why / next step" body section with a
    link to the tracking ingest issue on the peer repo if
    one exists, or a "file ingest issue" helper that
    prefills the title + body.
- **MISSING DATA summary chip** at the top of the Core
  sub-tab: "N panels missing data: …" — clicking expands to a
  short list of blocked panels with their ingest links. Chip
  is hidden when N = 0.
- **CI guardrail extension**: extend v1.1 R0's stub-leak
  test to assert no `dataStatus: 'pending'` card on the
  Budtender sub-route ever renders with non-empty `series` —
  catches a future regression where stub data sneaks into a
  MISSING DATA card.

**Exit criteria**: five MISSING DATA cards render in the Core
grid with honest copy + ingest links; summary chip renders
when N > 0; guardrail green.

### V3'6 — Indexes + perf + closure package

- Land four `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` indexes on
  `vps-nixos-3` production DB:
  - `sweed_orders (dealer_id, pay_time)`
  - `sweed_orders (cashier_user_id, pay_time)`
  - `sweed_orders (customer_id, pay_time)` (verify presence
    from v1.1; create only if missing).
  - `sweed_shifts (dealer_id, employee_id, shift_open_at,
    shift_close_at)`
- Perf measurement of `/api/budtender-analytics`:
  - Capture `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` for the consolidated query on
    typical windows (1d / 7d / 28d / 12wk).
  - Endpoint timing (P50 / P95 cold / P95 warm).
  - Targets: P50 < 500 ms warm, P95 < 1.2 s cold on a 4-week
    window across all sites.
- Runbook refresh: `docs/runbooks/helios-metrics.md` extended
  with the v1.3 surface (Budtender sub-route, sub-tab
  semantics, `compareTo=peer-cohort`, `area` discriminator,
  `blockedBy` registry, MISSING DATA summary chip).
- Validation evidence committed under the runbook:
  - Leaderboard screenshot with peer-percentile colour coding.
  - Daily Trend screenshot with peer-cohort band rendered.
  - Mix cards in fleet mode and per-cashier overlay mode.
  - Shift Productivity card (real-data mode) + the MISSING
    DATA fallback shape (separate screenshot).
  - Dollar-basket lift card in both modes.
  - Advanced scatter at default first paint.
  - Advanced scatter at a non-default
    `(X, Y, color, size, highlight)` configuration.
  - Each of the five MISSING DATA cards.
  - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` + endpoint timing table.
- Oracle review pass: re-run an oracle review on
  `/metrics/budtenders` Core + Advanced + each MISSING DATA
  card. Capture the oracle's "fit for purpose — world class for
  this operator's stated needs?" verdict. If the oracle flags
  new gaps, address them in this phase before the closure
  commit, or file an explicit follow-on epic and call it out
  in the closure package.
- Closure package: a single comment on
  [virusdave/top-level#7](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/7)
  containing the live URL
  (`https://helios.freshlybaked.us/metrics/budtenders`), the
  V3'0–V3'6 per-phase commit table, the AC §1–9 sign-off
  (with one-line evidence per criterion), the refreshed
  canonical Budtender metric list, the validation evidence,
  and the oracle note. The close commit MUST carry
  `Closes-Epic: #7` per #8's policy so
  `close-completed-issues.yml` closes the issue.

**Exit criteria**: parent can close based on evidence, not
trust; v1.3 AC §1–9 demonstrably hold on production; v1.1
AC §1–10 and v1.2 AC §1–8 continue to hold (no regressions);
oracle confirms `/metrics/budtenders` is fit for the
operator's stated "world-class budtender performance
dashboard" purpose.

## Cross-repo dependencies

None hard. The five MISSING DATA cards represent ingest
dependencies that are *acknowledged* as out-of-v1.3-scope.
Each card carries a `blockedBy.ingestIssue` link to a peer-
repo ingest issue (file new ones if they don't exist; e.g.
`sweed_order_line_items` ingest, `sweed_returns` ingest,
review-invoice-linkage, drawer-close-actuals ingest). v1.3 does
not block on any of these landing — the MISSING DATA cards are
the deliverable for the unblocked-data path.

When an ingest unblocks in a future iteration (v1.4+), each
MISSING DATA registry entry's panel can be promoted to a real
panel in a follow-on epic. v1.3 just leaves the slots ready
and visible.

## Acceptance criteria (delegated from parent)

The full v1.3 acceptance criteria live in the parent rework
addendum §"Refreshed acceptance criteria". Reproduced here as
a checklist for the V3'6 owner:

- [ ] (1) `/metrics/budtenders` reachable via top-level tab
      strip on `/metrics`; sub-tab + highlight selection
      persist in URL; share-link reproduces.
- [ ] (2) Core P0: Leaderboard + Daily Trend land with real
      data; peer-percentile colouring; low-n dimming;
      unattributed-transactions chip.
- [ ] (3) Core P1: Mix + Shift Productivity + Upsell Lift
      land with real data (or honest MISSING DATA fallback
      for Shift Productivity at < 40% coverage); overlay-on-
      leaderboard-select works.
- [ ] (4) Advanced sub-tab one-dot-per-cashier scatter with
      all axis / color / size / opacity / highlight pickers;
      default first paint per spec.
- [ ] (5) Five MISSING DATA cards render with "what / why /
      next step" copy + ingest links; summary chip; CI
      guardrail green.
- [ ] (6) Consolidated `/api/budtender-analytics` + four
      `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` indexes; perf targets met
      (P50 < 500 ms warm; P95 < 1.2 s cold on 4-week window).
- [ ] (7) `compareTo=peer-cohort` extension works; default on
      Budtender Daily Trend; per-panel toggle still functional;
      headline panels unchanged.
- [ ] (8) v1.1 AC §1–10 and v1.2 AC §1–8 continue to hold on
      production; no regressions.
- [ ] (9) Oracle-approved closure evidence package — live URL,
      commit table, screenshots, perf table, canonical
      Budtender metric list, oracle note; close commit
      carries `Closes-Epic: #7`.
slots.delegationNote: Helios /metrics/budtenders tab — Core (leaderboard, daily cashier-attributed sales trend, dollar-basket upsell lift in same-customer + similar-customer modes, customer/fulfillment/payment mix, shift productivity) and Advanced (one-dot-per-cashier scatter with switchable axes / color / size / opacity, peer-percentile encoding, highlight-subset search) sub-tabs; explicit MISSING DATA cards for line-items / returns / cashier-attributed reviews / shift cash +/-; consolidated /api/budtender-analytics endpoint behind a single CTE chain with four CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY supporting indexes; compareTo=peer-cohort extension. V3'0..V3'6 phasing; oracle-approved evidence package required at V3'6 closure with Closes-Epic: #7 trailer.

# Seven-day temporary pages and canonical live index

Parent: [`virusdave/top-level#65`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65)
· Binding design:
[`durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md`, System 2](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/durable-red-master-and-one-offs.md#system-2-seven-day-one-offs-and-one-canonical-live-index)

## Goal

Extend the existing `mss-one-offs` service without creating another source of
truth. New temporary pages may last up to seven days, callers may still choose
any shorter lifetime, and the existing bare `/one-offs/` route becomes a
mobile-friendly view of every page that is live according to its manifest.

The binding design has Oracle architecture and template approval. Follow it
exactly. Any nontrivial design change needs fresh architecture review before
implementation. The actual rendered index and recovery states need Oracle UI
review before first operator exposure.

The durable top-level coordination point is the pending
[`Roll out and verify repair convergence and one-offs operations` leaf](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/commit/ba3ddc914238987ae3bfaebe4d259e30ffba0348).
It depends on this materialisation task, remains open across both peer
checkpoints, and owns caller migration plus production deployment, canaries,
cleanup-cycle observation, telemetry, stability, and rollback evidence.

## Existing implementation to extend

Keep ownership in the existing implementation:

- [`tools/one-offs-server/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/tools/one-offs-server/src/index.ts)
  owns manifests, the in-memory registry, request serving, expiry, garbage
  collection, control endpoints, submissions, and the current bare index;
- [`nix/modules/mss-one-offs.nix`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/nix/modules/mss-one-offs.nix)
  owns service configuration, users, storage, filesystem isolation,
  environment, and the tailnet-only listener;
- [`scripts/one-offs`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/scripts/one-offs)
  is the supported publishing client; and
- [`docs/HOW_ONE_OFFS_WORKS.md`](https://github.com/Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites/blob/master/docs/HOW_ONE_OFFS_WORKS.md)
  is the repository-local operational contract.

Do not persist an index, add a second registry, or place index-only
authentication in front of direct page URLs. A strictly validated manifest is
the sole authority.

## Implementation sequence

### 1. One live selector and reviewed index, with the 24-hour cap retained

- Introduce one `liveSlots(now)` selector used by direct serving, the HTML
  index, `GET /v1/slots`, `GET /v1/slots/<nonce>`, health counts, extension,
  startup, and garbage collection. A page is absent at `now >= expiresAtMs`;
  garbage collection only reclaims disk and can never define liveness.
- Snapshot live manifests under the mutation mutex using one captured clock
  value, then render outside the lock. Keep newest-first order and bounded
  O(live slots) rendering.
- Keep the bare `/one-offs/` route as the only index and render it directly
  from that snapshot. Preserve `Cache-Control: no-store`; add
  `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`.
- Implement the binding mobile and desktop information architecture: linked
  human note with an untitled fallback, prominent relative and exact UTC
  expiry, secondary creator metadata, a uniquely named direct action, and the
  short nonce only in collapsed technical details. Use one `<main>`, one H1,
  H2 item titles, 44-pixel targets, high-contrast focus rings, WCAG AA light
  and dark colors, and no horizontal scrolling at 320 pixels.
- Preserve the complete privacy boundary: serve only through `tailscale0` with
  daemon CIDR enforcement as defense in depth; keep the Unix control socket
  restricted to the `mss-one-offs` group; and expose nothing publicly. State
  that every live nonce is discoverable to any tailnet node that can reach the
  service and that a nonce is not authorization inside the tailnet. Require
  operator-safe `note` and `requestedBy` labels and content-free logs. Never
  expose delete or extend controls on the read-only TCP listener.
- At more than 20 live pages, add progressively enhanced search with the exact
  labels and announced result count from the design. Every page remains visible
  and usable without JavaScript.
- Implement the populated, empty, concurrent-expiry, degraded-load, plain 503,
  and indistinguishable direct-page 404 states from the binding design.
- Render representative populated, 21-item search, empty, degraded, 503, 404,
  concurrent-expiry, mobile, and dark-mode fixtures. Obtain Oracle UI approval
  of the actual output before any of it is exposed to the operator.

### 2. Bounded mutation, storage, and handler isolation

- Add one daemon-owned asynchronous mutation mutex covering capacity pruning,
  reservations, activation, extension, deletion, garbage-collection registry
  changes, and submission accounting.
- Enforce the binding configurable defaults: 500 live slots, 5,000 persisted
  files and 100 MiB per slot, 1,000 submissions per slot, a 10 GiB whole-data
  project quota, and a 5 GiB post-admission host free-space reserve.
- Count files and bytes during the existing tree-validation traversal, not in a
  second pass. Reserve capacity before mutation and release or reduce every
  reservation on every success, rejection, disconnect, timeout, and crash
  recovery path. Fail publication before a partial slot can become visible.
- Fsync atomic manifest writes and their parent directory. At startup,
  quarantine invalid, mismatched, manifest-less, and orphan temporary slot
  directories outside the serving registry; expire quarantine after 24 hours
  with bounded diagnostics. Never resurrect an expired manifest.
- Replace daemon-child submission handlers with the binding socket-activated,
  separately unprivileged `mss-one-offs-handler`. Accept only validated slot,
  submission, and configured-handler identifiers; derive paths in the executor;
  use a fixed Nix allowlist; and bind-mount the whole one-offs data directory
  read-only for the handler.
- Expose bounded disk-usage, rejected-publication, quarantine, degraded-load,
  and reservation metrics without logging page content.

### 3. Migrate publication to daemon-owned streaming uploads

Follow the client-first migration order. Do not combine or reorder these gates.

1. Add the daemon-owned streaming upload API from the binding design while
   preserving legacy `incoming/`. Update `scripts/one-offs stage` to walk the
   source, declare counts and bytes, stream only validated regular files, abort
   cleanly, and activate only a complete upload.
2. Package that exact client in every one-offs host's NixOS system path. Prove
   old and new publishing paths work before any caller migration.
3. Stop before retiring legacy `incoming/`. Post durable checkpoint evidence on
   [parent issue #65](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/65), but do
   not use a `Satisfies:` trailer yet. The
   [durable parent rollout leaf](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/commit/ba3ddc914238987ae3bfaebe4d259e30ffba0348)
   deploys this 24-hour-cap checkpoint and owns the dependent top-level canon,
   shared runbook, and known-caller migration to the packaged `stage` command.
4. After that migration lands, the parent rollout observes legacy claims for
   seven days. Continue only after the count is zero and streaming
   create/delete/rollback canaries pass.
5. Make upload storage daemon-only mode 0750, remove the legacy API and path,
   and land the seven-day maximum. Do not use a `Satisfies:` trailer yet; the
   parent must still deploy and verify this final runtime candidate.

The streaming API reserves declared capacity under the mutex, rejects
symlinks and special files, refuses count or byte overruns, expires abandoned
uploads, and leaves no group-writable path that can bypass admission or consume
cleanup headroom.

### 4. Raise the maximum only after capacity and migration gates pass

- Change the daemon fallback and NixOS `maxTtlSeconds` default from 86,400 to
  604,800 seconds. Keep `defaultTtlSeconds` at 7,200 seconds.
- Preserve each manifest's immutable `maxExpiresAtMs`. Existing 24-hour pages
  cannot be extended beyond their original ceiling. New pages can request any
  positive shorter lifetime, clamped only at seven days.
- Before enabling the longer cap, prove the backing filesystem enforces the
  10 GiB systemd state-directory project quota and admission preserves the
  5 GiB cleanup reserve. A missing proof blocks enablement.

## Required deterministic coverage

Use a fake clock and isolated temporary directories. Cover:

- seven-day clamping, shorter lifetimes, immutable extension ceilings, old
  24-hour manifests, and `now == expiresAtMs` across every route and API;
- restart with expired, invalid, partial, mismatched, and orphan state;
- create, extension, deletion, garbage collection, submissions, reservations,
  streaming uploads, and index snapshots under concurrency and injected
  interruption;
- rollback of every reservation and partial upload, all per-slot and global
  bounds, project-quota and free-space failures, and single-pass accounting;
- escaped labels, bounded 500-item rendering, 21-item search and no-script
  fallback, `HEAD`, no-store, noindex, and tailnet rejection;
- populated, empty, degraded, 503, indistinguishable 404, concurrent-expiry,
  light, dark, and 320-pixel output; and
- landmarks, heading order, visible exact times, unique action names, focus,
  44-pixel targets, contrast, and reduced-motion behavior.

Add a focused test path for the one-offs daemon if the package still lacks one,
then run the repository's documented targeted checks. CI owns the full
retrospective `pnpm check` gate.

## Rollout, rollback, and completion

Land code inertly and preserve the 24-hour cap until the parent rollout leaf.
The parent uses the normal `mostly-static-sites` deployment path, first exposes
the selector and Oracle-approved index, then performs the client migration and
capacity rollout, and only then enables seven-day lifetimes. It verifies one
two-hour and one seven-day canary, deletes both, and observes two garbage-
collection cycles.

Rollback restores a packaged client compatible with the running server before
rolling server behavior back. Restore legacy `incoming/`, canon, and runbook
together before reverting the streaming API. Reverting the configured cap to
86,400 seconds does not shorten or delete pages created under the seven-day
version; report those grandfathered pages and let their recorded manifests
expire normally.

Use this completion handshake so delegated completion cannot close the parent
functionality epic before rollout:

1. Land the inert 24-hour selector, reviewed UI, bounds, upload API, packaged
   client, tests, and documentation without a `Satisfies:` trailer.
2. Hand the checkpoint to the
   [durable parent rollout leaf](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/commit/ba3ddc914238987ae3bfaebe4d259e30ffba0348),
   which deploys it, migrates top-level canon/runbook/callers, and records seven
   days with zero legacy claims.
3. Land legacy-path removal and the seven-day maximum without a `Satisfies:`
   trailer.
4. Hand the final candidate back to that rollout leaf. It deploys through the
   canonical path, proves quota enforcement, verifies two-hour and seven-day
   canaries, observes cleanup, exercises rollback, records stability, and
   durably completes that rollout task.
5. Only then land one real peer evidence/operational-documentation commit with
   the completion trailer below. Intermediate commits must not carry it.

The child is complete only after deterministic tests and final gates pass,
Oracle approves the actual rendered output and any nontrivial
critical-infrastructure diff, every migration gate is met, and the parent has
durable rollout and stability evidence. The final peer commit must carry:

```text
Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#65
```
slots.delegationNote: Preserve manifests and the bare index as sole authority; coordinate both peer checkpoints with rollout task ba3ddc914238987ae3bfaebe4d259e30ffba0348.
slots.title: Seven-day temporary pages and canonical live index
