# Customer / Visitor Address Ingestion — `automation` child epic

> Owning child of
> [virusdave/top-level#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9).
> The authoritative design is
> [`docs/epics/visitor-address-ingestion/EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md)
> in the top-level repo; this child epic scope is **strictly the
> `FreshlyBakedNYC/automation` (Helios + ingest monorepo) slice of
> that design**.  Every implementation commit landing on `automation`
> master that satisfies any part of this child epic MUST carry the
> trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9
> ```
>
> Phase-tagged commits SHOULD additionally carry a `Phase: A<n>`
> trailer so the cross-repo-completion-sync workflow can post the
> per-phase progress comment on the parent issue.

## Scope owned by this repo

Everything described in the parent EPIC_PLAN.md, broken out by phase
below.  Re-read the parent before starting — the section here is a
thin index over the parent rather than a re-statement of the design.

### A1 — DB migration + webhook handler + bearer-token auth

- Alembic / golang-migrate / whatever-helios-uses migration adding
  the `visitor_scans` table with **exactly** the columns, indices,
  and unique constraint defined in the parent design.
- Two routes, mounted on the existing helios-server HTTP router:
  - `POST /wh/bx/veriscan/checkin`
  - `POST /wh/mh/veriscan/checkin`
- Both routes share a single handler whose only per-route input is
  the literal `site_slug` (`'bx'` or `'mh'`) passed by the route
  binding.  Unknown slugs MUST be impossible by construction
  (whitelist at mount time, not at runtime).
- Bearer-token auth middleware that:
  - reads `VERISCAN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` from env at process start;
  - rejects requests with no `Authorization` header (401);
  - parses `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (case-insensitive scheme);
  - compares constant-time against the env value;
  - on mismatch: 401 with no body and a `warn`-level structured
    log including remote IP + path (no token material).
- Envelope validation per parent design (Type, EventId, WebHookId,
  Data.HashId presence).  400 on missing.
- Insert with `ON CONFLICT (provider, hash_id) DO NOTHING`.
- `info`-level structured log of every accepted body keyed by
  `hash_id` (so we have a full audit trail outside the DB).
- Smoke-test: a `curl` example committed under `docs/runbooks/`
  that POSTs a synthetic VeriScan envelope at the local helios-server
  binary and asserts a 200 + row insert.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: A1`.

### A2 — Backfill CLI

- New subcommand on the existing `helios-prep` binary:

  ```
  helios-prep visitor-scans backfill \
      --site=<bx|mh> --provider=veriscan \
      --file=<path> [--dry-run]
  ```

- Accepts JSON array, NDJSON, or CSV (sniffed from extension first,
  content second).
- For each input record, reshapes columns into the VeriScan-envelope
  `Data` schema (the operator-supplied Drive export is a flat row
  dump, not a wire envelope), synthesises an envelope with:
  - `Type='CreateCard'`,
  - `WebHookId=0` and `EventId=<stable hash of HashId>` (so re-runs
    are idempotent and not just "no-op via unique constraint" but
    also produce identical `raw_envelope` JSONB),
  - `Created`/`Sent` set to the file's mtime,
- Calls into the **exact same** insert helper used by A1.
- Reports `inserted=`, `skipped_duplicate=`, `errored=` counts at
  the end; `--dry-run` prints the would-be inserts as JSON Lines.
- Unit tests cover: round-trip with the same file twice yields
  `inserted=N` then `skipped_duplicate=N`; malformed row yields
  `errored=1` and does not abort the run.

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: A2`.

### A3 — Admin page

- `/admin/visitors/scans` per parent design.  Sits behind the
  existing helios admin auth (oauth-reverse-proxy).
- Paginated table newest-first, columns + filters per parent.
- Row click → drawer with the full normalised row + a syntax-highlit
  JSON view of `raw_envelope`.
- CSV export of the current filter view (uses the same query the
  table renders, no second source of truth).

Commits in this phase MUST carry `Phase: A3`.

## Out of scope

- DNS / TLS / nginx / agenix / systemd unit changes —
  `Nicponskis/nixos-sbc`.
- VeriScan-side webhook configuration — operator.
- Downloading the Drive backfill file — operator hands the file to
  the backfill CLI via `--file=`.
- Any consumer of `visitor_scans` (marketing, segmentation,
  loyalty, geo-analyses).  Later epics will read this table.

## Phase dependencies

- A1 depends on `nixos-sbc` N1 (env var present at runtime).  A1
  code itself can be written and unit-tested without N1; only the
  deployed-to-prod step blocks.
- A2 depends on A1 landing (shared insert helper).
- A3 depends on A1 landing (table must exist).
- A2 and A3 can proceed in parallel.

## Completion signal

This child epic is considered complete when:

1. A1, A2, A3 each have at least one commit on `automation` master
   carrying `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#9` and the matching
   `Phase:` trailer.
2. The A1 smoke-test (`docs/runbooks/`) runs green against the
   deployed helios-server on `vps-nixos-3`.
3. The operator confirms (via a comment on
   [#9](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/9)) that
   VeriScan webhook configuration on bx + mh points at the
   correct URLs with the correct bearer token, and that at least
   one live check-in has produced a row visible in
   `/admin/visitors/scans`.
slots.delegationNote: Helios /wh/{bx,mh}/veriscan/checkin webhook handler with bearer-token auth, visitor_scans table + migration (idempotent on provider+hash_id), helios-prep visitor-scans backfill subcommand for the operator-supplied Drive export, and /admin/visitors/scans operator page.

# automation child epic — eliminate hand-built JSON

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#44](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/44)
> — "Our critical tooling should NOT be constructing json by hand."
> **Parent epic plan:** [`../../EPIC_PLAN.md`](../../EPIC_PLAN.md).
> **Governing rule:** canon `docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md` "Code
> standards" — *never hand-build / hand-parse / hand-validate JSON or YAML*.

## Scope

One offender found in the automation repo (survey 2026-07-08):

**`ads/google/scripts/run-cluster-sweep.sh`** builds `manifest.json`
structurally in shell — a sequence of `printf` lines that emit the object
braces, the `clusters` array, and the inter-element commas by hand. The
scalar *values* are already escaped via `jq -Rn`, so the escaping risk is
low, but the object/array/comma scaffolding is still hand-assembled and a
future edit (a new field, a reordered element) can easily desync a comma
and emit invalid JSON.

Convert the whole manifest to a single `jq -n` invocation that takes the
run id, timestamp, slug list, and the `strategic_context_present` boolean
as `--arg`/`--argjson` and builds the object/array natively. Re-grep the
repo before finishing to confirm nothing else was missed:

```sh
rg -n -e '\\"[a-zA-Z_]+\\":' -e "printf '\{" -e 'echo .*\{.*:.*\}' ads scripts
```

## Constraints

- The emitted `manifest.json` must be equivalent in *content* (same keys,
  same values, `schema_version: 0`, placeholder `kind`/`note`, per-slug
  `{ "slug": …, "files": ["verdict.md"] }` entries) — this is a correctness
  refactor, not a schema change. Formatting/whitespace may differ (it is
  machine-consumed); verify any downstream reader still parses it.
- Follow the repo's own `AGENTS.md` and task-dag workflow.

## Acceptance

- `run-cluster-sweep.sh` produces `manifest.json` via `jq -n` (no
  hand-assembled braces/commas); output parses under `jq -e` and matches
  the prior structure for a representative slug list.
- The **final** commit on the automation `master` that demonstrates this
  child epic's acceptance criteria are met carries
  `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#44`. Intermediate commits MUST NOT carry
  that trailer unless the child epic is already fully satisfied.
slots.delegationNote: Build manifest.json with a single jq -n; keep content/schema identical.
slots.title: Eliminate hand-built JSON in run-cluster-sweep.sh manifest construction

# Agent Canon — `Nicponskis/mostly-static-sites` child epic

> Parent epic: [virusdave/top-level#10](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/10)
>
> The implementation commit on this repo's master MUST carry the trailer:
>
> ```
> Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#10
> ```
>
> That trailer triggers the cross-repo completion flow back to the
> parent issue.

## What this epic does

Rewrites this repo's root `AGENTS.md` to consume **canonical agent
rules** from `virusdave/top-level` instead of duplicating them
locally. The canonical rules are short, imperative, and updated in one
place — so all our repos stay in sync without manual mirroring.

## Step 0 — fetch and read canon BEFORE doing anything

The canonical agent rules live in
`virusdave/top-level : docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md` on `master`. **Read
them first** (and use the same mechanism in your final AGENTS.md
header — see Step 2):

```sh
canon_ws=$(/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout \
              /home/amp-local/src/top-level --label canon-read)
cat "$canon_ws/docs/canon/AGENTS_CANON.md"
# … internalize the rules — they govern this rewrite …
/home/amp-local/src/github-worker/bin/ephemeral-checkout --remove "$canon_ws"
```

Pay particular attention to: ephemeral checkouts for your own work,
the "Canon update interrupt" in §0, the operational-reality §5, and
the §6 contract for what peer `AGENTS.md` must contain.

# task-dag child epic — `reconcile-closed-issue` command

> **Parent epic:** [virusdave/top-level#48](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/issues/48)
> — "There are a large number of incorrectly still open tasks".
> **Gating design (signed off):**
> [`docs/designs/closed-issue-task-reconciliation.md`](https://github.com/virusdave/top-level/blob/master/docs/designs/closed-issue-task-reconciliation.md)
> in `virusdave/top-level` — read §2 (disposition policy), §3 (CLI
> contract), §6 (rollback). The operator signed off the §2 policy on #48.
> **Governing rule:** canon `docs/canon/rules/QUALITY_GATES.md`
> "Critical-infrastructure changes" (task-dag is the dispatch/claim core)
> and "never hand-roll ref surgery — reusable, tested logic belongs in the
> CLI".

## Why this lives in task-dag

The task-dag CLI now has a single canonical home in `virusdave/task-dag`.
Closed-issue reconciliation is reusable, tested issue→task discovery plus
ref deletion — exactly the kind of logic canon forbids hand-rolling as
one-off workflow bash. It must be a first-class CLI subcommand so both the
automation (parent epic child 3) and the one-time backfill (child 4) call
one implementation, not two.

## Problem recap

The github-worker dispatcher gates every candidate task on **live** GitHub
issue state: when a task's issue is observed `CLOSED` it skips the task and
prunes only the **local** `refs/heads/tasks/*` ref. The authoritative
`tasks/frontier/<short>`, `tasks/active/<short>`,
`tasks/blocked/<full-sha>` (+ `tasks/blocked-meta/<full-sha>`) refs on
**origin** survive and re-materialise on every `git fetch`. Such a task is
never worked and never cleaned — it clutters the frontier and dashboards
forever. Issue #48 is the accumulated backlog of exactly these tasks.

The existing sweep
(`.github/scripts/cleanup-closed-issue-task-refs.sh`) only runs on the
sanctioned bot `Closes-Epic:` push path; manual/out-of-band closes (the
common case behind #48) only fire a pager and never reconcile the refs.

## Scope — implement `task-dag reconcile-closed-issue`

Add one subcommand (policy-named, not mechanism-named):

```
task-dag reconcile-closed-issue <issue> [--dry-run] [--json] [--yes]
```

### Behaviour (per design §3)

1. **Confirm the issue is CLOSED first.** Resolve the issue's live state
   via the same authority as the dispatcher (`gh issue view … --json
   state`). Undetermined or not-`CLOSED` ⇒ **no mutation**; report and
   exit `0` on a clean not-closed no-op, non-zero only on a genuine error.
2. **Enumerate** the non-completed, open task refs that resolve to this
   `(repo, issue)`: `tasks/frontier/<short>`, `tasks/blocked/<full-sha>`
   (+ `tasks/blocked-meta/<full-sha>`). Reuse the canonical resolution
   (the same `blocked --json` meta-overridden-issue + derived-repo
   semantics); a cross-repo `Repo:` block that is not *this* repo is **not**
   a match. Never re-parse commit bodies ad hoc.
3. **Delete only** refs that point at the expected task SHA, honouring the
   **frontier-first** invariant (delete `frontier` before `blocked` under a
   `--force-with-lease` on the observed SHA, so a concurrent breakdown that
   re-pointed a short-sha ref is never clobbered and no pickable window
   opens) — the exact discipline already proven in
   `cleanup-closed-issue-task-refs.sh`. **Absorb / share that logic so
   there is one implementation, not two** (ideally refactor
   `cleanup-closed-issue-task-refs.sh` to call the new subcommand).
4. **Never delete** `tasks/pending/<N>` (epic identity) or
   `gh/comments/<N>/<id>` (comment provenance). Leave `tasks/active/*`
   alone — a live claim's worker CAS-cleans it on `complete`; deleting it
   only makes that worker fail loud, and a stale active ref for a closed
   issue is harmless debris.
5. **`--dry-run`** reports exactly what *would* be removed and mutates
   nothing. Non-dry runs require `--yes` when stdin is not a TTY (matching
   `drop`'s guard).
6. **Output** is both human-readable and machine-readable (`--json`): the
   removed task SHAs and ref names, the skipped/undetermined items with
   reasons, and a summary count. **Idempotent**: a second run over an
   already-clean issue is a successful no-op. **Race-safe**: origin
   readback + `--force-with-lease`-style deletes.

### Fail-safe (per design §2.1)

No mutation unless the issue is **CONFIRMED CLOSED**. Any of the following
⇒ **no-op + report for manual review** (never assume closed):

- `gh` missing / unauthenticated for the repo, or any GitHub API failure
  (mirror `is_issue_closed`'s "undetermined ⇒ don't act", conservative
  direction = *don't delete*);
- ambiguous or unresolved task→issue association (e.g. a cross-repo
  `Repo:`/`Issue:` block not resolving to *this* repo + issue);
- issue state anything other than `CLOSED`.

## Constraints (critical infra)

- **No change to task commit/ref FORMAT and no new ref namespace.** This is
  a reconciliation command built on existing `drop`/ref-helper semantics.
  If implementation ends up needing a format change or a new archival
  namespace, that is critical-infra: **stop, get operator approval + an
  Oracle design review** before proceeding (the design does not anticipate
  this; child must re-check at implementation time).
- **Oracle change review** applies per canon "Critical-infrastructure
  changes" — task-dag is the dispatch/claim core.
- Reuse existing primitives (`drop`, ref helpers, `blocked --json`
  resolution, `is_issue_closed`); do not fork a parallel implementation.

## Tests + docs

- Unit/integration tests for: confirmed-closed happy path (frontier +
  blocked + blocked-meta dropped, pending + provenance kept, active left);
  not-closed ⇒ no-op; `gh` missing/unauth ⇒ no-op + report; ambiguous
  cross-repo association ⇒ skip + report; `--dry-run` mutates nothing;
  idempotent second run; `--json` shape parses under `jq -e`; frontier-first
  race safety (`--force-with-lease` refuses a re-pointed short-sha ref).
- An optional audit/report mode for `validate` that surfaces closed-issue
  lingering refs **WITHOUT** making normal offline `validate` depend on the
  live GitHub API (offline `validate` must stay offline).
- Update the task-dag CLI docs/help for the new subcommand.
- Keep `validate --strict` green; run `tests/task-dag/run-all.sh` as the
  final gate.

## Acceptance

- `task-dag reconcile-closed-issue <issue>` exists and behaves per the
  contract above, with `--dry-run`/`--json`/`--yes`.
- Fail-safe verified: no mutation on any uncertainty; only refs at the
  expected SHA deleted; `pending`/provenance refs preserved.
- `cleanup-closed-issue-task-refs.sh` shares the CLI's logic (single code
  path) or a follow-up to do so is filed.
- Tests (existing + new adversarial/fail-safe cases) and docs land.
- The **final** commit on `virusdave/task-dag` `master` demonstrating this
  child epic's acceptance carries `Satisfies: virusdave/top-level#48`.
  Intermediate commits MUST NOT carry that trailer unless the child epic is
  already fully satisfied. (task-dag's own `complete` adds the peer
  `Issue:`/`URL:` attribution trailer.)
slots.delegationNote: Implement `reconcile-closed-issue <issue>` per top-level docs/designs/closed-issue-task-reconciliation.md §3 (operator-signed-off policy §2). Default drop-with-audit; --dry-run/--json/--yes; fail-safe (no mutation unless issue CONFIRMED CLOSED); frontier-first --force-with-lease deletes of only refs at the expected SHA; never delete tasks/pending/<N> or gh/comments provenance; leave tasks/active/* alone. Reuse drop/ref-helper/blocked --json resolution and share logic with cleanup-closed-issue-task-refs.sh. Critical infra: Oracle change review; NO ref/commit FORMAT change or new namespace (stop + get operator+Oracle approval if one becomes necessary). Tests + docs; keep offline validate offline.
slots.title: Implement task-dag reconcile-closed-issue command for closed-issue task cleanup
